Also the fridge is stuffed with their bottles and is computerized, so I wasn't able to put MY beer in the fridge - sucks...
Otherwise - nice hotel.

title: “An island of comfort in Chicago”
text: Its so great to stay in a hotel that has the guest as their top priority. Its also great to have a hotel room that the bed doesnt take 90% of the space in the room. Its great to have a bathroom that when you streach your arms out, you dont touch the walls... All in all, the location is great - right off Michigan Ave, easy access to whatever you want to do. Take the elevator down, and you're in a high end shopping mall with a Nordstrom store as it's anchor. The staff is great and helpful. I'd come back here in a heartbeat.

title: “Great Hotel”
text: This old hotel has great character. I understand it is about to be remodeled. It does need updating, and I hope it retains its charm through the remodel. As it is now, our bathroom didn't have ventilation so it got very steamy during showers. Our water pressure was super strong, but a friend staying on the 3rd floor said hers was weak. As with most old and some new hotels, there needs to be more electrical outlets. We missed having a large flatscreen especially since the room was so big. Our reservations were for a standard room with two beds. Our room was HUGE. It had two king size four poster beds, a separate dressing area and closet. The beds were comfortable, but I like just a little more cush. The rooms do not have microwaves or refrigerators, but you can request them. Service was great when we made those requests. The location is very good. There is a park right accross the street and you are close to the riverwalk. I was there on business during the week, but because I had prior reservations made at the Menger hotel for a marathon that weekend we had to change hotels. I chose The Menger for the race because of its close proximity to the starting line of the race. I was not impressed with the Menger room or service after staying at the St. Anthony. I definitely preferred the St. Anthony.

title: “Yucky! Roach hotel!”
text: This was our first time staying at an Embassy Suites and it will be the last! The carpets were absolutly filthy. Our son's legs and feet were black from crawling on the floor. We requested a room change. The second room was no better. Both rooms smelled like mold and body odor. We found a live roach in the bathroom and by the door, made me not want to eat the free breakfast. We were extreamlly disappointed. Would not reccomend to anyone!

title: “Best Experience!”
text:
I planned a surprise trip to Chicago for my girlfriend to ask her to spend the rest of her life with me. I can not begin the explain how Eden, our conceirge, made our expience the best. Eden suggested great resteraunts on multiple days while offering to do so much more.
Eden went out of her way on one specific occasion and truly exemplified the "Whatever..Whenever" motto of the W Hotels. We asked if the hotel had a "white noise" machine to loan as we are use to one in our room at home. At the time, the hotel did not have one but they went to 5 different stores in the Chicago area to find one! I was so impressed and would never expect someone to go to such lengths to made our trip so special.

title: “Everything was great!”
text: My son and I stayed 5 nights for a recent golf tournament...The room was big...the front desk staff were very helpfull...the 5th floor housekeeping staff were the best..our room was spotless everyday...We would stay here again in a heartbeat...

title: “staff issues”
text: i use a website that reports cheap rates to be had on priceline called betterbidding dot com - so I got a rate I was pleased with for crown plaza. It was a throw down weekend get away that was decide in haste on Friday afternoon for a midnight arrival that same day.h I was beat when I got to the checkin counter at 12:30AM - just wanted a shower and a compfy bed. First room was un made on 10th floor (back to the lobby for a another) second room was un made on the 14th floor, again back t the lobby, third time the charm. it was large aging room, old tv and had new bath and carpet, king bed with nice pillow top and linens. The air worked but not needed in February. The room was on the freeway side with an office park that rev'ed diesel engines ALL-NIGHT-LONG (wife says I snore louder) - but the shower was hot and nice and I was offered a free breakfast, - I'd give it another try as long as my room was on the back side. The common areas were nice, perhaps a bet squeezed and the parking and guest internet was free.

title: “Charming Boston hotel!”
text: My boyfriend and I stayed in Boston over my birthday in conjunction with a trip to NYC. I had not been before, so I wasn't sure what to expect, but I was very impressed with the hotel and the city! I heard that the rooms were very small and cramped, so I booked a junior suite (joining the Omni's select guest program gets you a free upgrade coupon,) which was very spacious and comfortable. The rooms were renovated earlier in the year and looked great! The bathroom was very small and lacked counter space, which was my only complaint, but it's easy to put up with when you're staying in a historic hotel. The beds are very comfortable, allowing a great rest after exploring historic trails and walking up and down Newbury Street. We had my birthday dinner at Parker's Restaurant and met the most wonderful waiter, Francesco, who shared with us his favorite things about Boston (including the food!) and invited us to stay past closing to enjoy some Boston creme pie--complete with a little candle on top! Overall, the stay was great, and the few staff members we encountered were wonderful. We will be back!

title: “We loved it and will be back next year!”
text: Outstanding and friendly service! .

title: “Great hotel well located - Great View of Empire State Building”
text:
Just arrived back from a great stay at the Strand. First visit to NYC, with family children aged 17 and 15yrs, so was a little apprehensive when booking as there are so many hotels to choice from. Wasn't disappointed.
On arrival was greated by cheerful and friendly staff who informed us we were being upgraded to a Executive Kingsize, which I was pleased with as I thought they were treating me to the upgrade as we were there to celebrate my 50th birthday. We had booked a two double room. On arrival at the room on the 20th flloor was disappointed to see they had given us a kingsize bed and a bed settee, which was only big enough for one of the children to fit on. The room was wonderful with a walk in shower but unfortunately we couldn't sleep three in a kingsize. Informed reception who admitted they had no double rooms available. After a couple of minutes and lots of whispering we were allocated a double room on the 18th floor.
We were delighted with the new room overlooking the empire state building. Room was spacious enough for the four of us, beds really comfortable and the pillows were like marshmallows.
Breakfast was free and enough to start the day, pastries, cereal, cold meat, juice and tea/coffee. Gets really busy after 8.30 and the only negative was the four sliced small toaster really slow and inadequate.
Hotel ideally suited for sightseeing and shopping. One minutes to the East and you are at fifth avenue, ten minutes West and you are on broadway and Times Square. 
We eat in the hotel one evening and the food was really good although a little on the expensive side.
We have had a great trip and would highly recommend. Only four stars because of the toaster and mix up with room initally.

title: “More of a hostel”
text:
The location is great and the staff is friendly. However, those two points do not outweigh how uncomfortable it is to stay here.
I opted for a deluxe queen room with the private bath. The room is very small but that's ok, I knew that going in.
The bathroom is tiny as well, which would have been ok if it included a functional sink area to accomplish basic things like brushing one's teeth or shaving. The sink is the size of an office telephone, with a glass shelf directly above it. The shelf makes it impossible to lean down to rinse, etc without bumping your head into it. The height of the sink is also very low. Incredibly uncomfortable for a person of my height - and I'm not even that tall at 6'1. The bathroom sink i would say is the worst i've ever experienced in my business travels. Just a horribly uncomfortable experience.
With the exception of the bathroom window, the windows do not open in the room! I was there when the temps hit the 80s in San Francisco. There's no AC! The room got incredibly stuffy and humid. There is zero circulation of air going through the room making it very difficult to sleep.
The noise. Oh the noise. There is loud screeching noise, which lasts a full minute whenever someone their toilet. It's very, very loud and obnoxious. Like a tea kettle, which is not very pleasant. Also, God forbid you do open the bathroom window on the floor i was on - the 3rd. You hear the lovely sounds of construction, taxi whistles from neighboring hotels, corn horns. All sounding like they are in your room.
I rarely write reviews but really felt like i needed to warn potential visitors. This place was just horrible.

title: “We Loved Pier 5!”
text:
We spent 2 nights of a mini-vacation at Pier 5 in August. We were trying to save money and bid on a room for 4 people with Priceline. We were incredibly happy with what we got!
The location was very convenient - you could walk to everywhere in the Inner Harbor. Coming back at night to this beautiful hotel on the water just made our mini-vacation.
We were treated no differently than those who paid rack rate. We paid $75 per night (not including taxes, parking or Priceline fees) for a very lovely, very quiet room on the 3rd floor. There were 2 queen beds so the four of us shared. 
Our kids are 14 and 5 and they enjoyed attention from the very helpful desk staff, and they LOVED the over-the-top decor of the entire hotel. 
Overall I would say if you can get the wonderful rate we got, you will be extremely happy. A couple of little housekeeping issues (not enough pillows, not enough towels replaced by housekeeping, and a slight musty smell in the corrider) might bother you if you had to pay full rack rate.

title: “First class staff”
text: Stayed 3 nights 2-5 Jan. All staff v. helpful and amazingly friendly. Desk gave excellent recommendations for local restaurants, 3 of which we tried and enjoyed. Il Campanello restaurant was nearby and good. Room was large with free internet access. Beds comfortable. Room & bathroom clean, plenty of towels and toiletries. Our room was on 19th floor and sometimes we heard a bit of noise from the outside corridor (I think there was a supply room for bedlinen, towels nearby), but it didn't really bother us. We had an interesting view over city. Local area seems a little run-down, but close to all the central areas and subway and we never felt threatened or uneasy, even late at night. We walked everywhere, even up to East 54th. Hotel has cafe where you can get breakfast, but we didn't use it. There is a Mcdonalds on the corner, but instead turn left and go to American Gourmet on 29th, which does food and coffee (gourmet a bit of a misnomer, but cheap and cheerful and cooked to order). Reception booked me on a shuttle back to Newark Airport - $20, which turned up promptly outside the hotel and dropped me right outside departures for my airline - so no lugging cases. We enjoyed our stay at the Hilton Garden Inn Chelsea.

title: “Great place to stay when visiting San Diego”
text: We arrived at the hotel around 1am and were promptly checked in. There still were parking spots available even at that late hour. The room was very clean and adequately furnished. The dishes in the kitchen were very clean as well. The fridge was a bit noisy, but that is expected. Breakfast items were typical continental breakfast stuff - bagels, danishes, cereal, etc. Everything was extremely fresh and hotel staff was always present to make sure that everything is stocked and everyone got everything they wanted. The hotel is near the university, so expect some younger crowd and possibly some noise late at night. The hotel is also located within 15 minutes from the most popular destinations in town.

title: “Great hotel in a fantastic location”
text: The pros are many: the Eliot is right in Back Bay with easy access to Newbury & Boylston St, less than 2 blocks from Hynes Convention Center, and right before the on-ramp to the Masspike West. The room we stayed in (a premier suite king) was spacious and comfortable. The staff were all very attentive and polite. Even the free shoe shine was wonderful: you hang your shoes on the doorknob in a bag they provide before you go to bed and you wake up to find your shoes looking better than they have in years. My wife and I did the "Winter in the City" deal which provided free parking (a must in the Back Bay area of Boston) and a free breakfast in Clio. I'd highly recommend a breakfast package because for the cost of tax and tip, we had a complimentary $20 per person buffet with fresh fruit and some very delicious baked goods (if you want bacon or eggs and order a la carte, say goodbye to your wallet). The only cons are that the dresser was pretty small and probably could not accomodate 2 people if we stayed for several nights. Also, the shower is bizarre with a partition which only covers half the shower, so you feel like at any minute you'll flood the bathroom. I can't understand why they wouldn't have some kind of sliding door, if only to keep you from getting cold in the shower. But these are small items. Overall the Eliot is a really great hotel. You'll pay $300+ per night because of where you are in Boston, but you will get your money's worth.

title: “Great Hotel”
text: Staff was very Courteous and attentive. Room was quiet and Dinner was great !!!

title: “Great place to stay in Columbus”
text:
Our son lives in Victorian Village and we needed a place to stay for one night in December 2009. We had previously stayed in a hotel near Polaris Towne Center, but it was so dirty we could not stay there again! T
This Fairfield was clean, comfortable and the staff was SO helpful. There was a little mix-up on our reservation and the the staff went above and beyond to make us happy. One of the extra perks is that there is a Damon's restaurant right in front of the hotel.... about a 1 minute walk across the parking lot. The food there was good and the atmosphere relaxing. We had dinner there with our son and his girlfriend and we walked back to the hotel! It probably wasn't the best that Columbus offers in food, but we were pleased with the convenience. When we return to Columbus which we do every few weeks, we WILL stay there!

title: “Central location hotel with comfortable beds”
text:
First, the room was great with a nice view. Stayed in a king bed that was very comfortable and the bathroom was clean. These are the two things I care most about. The decor was decent. Since it is an older hotel, the technology side is a bit lacking e.g. few outlets, old tv, no free wifi.
The location is central to most of everything including 6th St.
The service is mixed. The doorman was very nice when I checked in. At the reception desk, I indicated that I will not need parking. Apparently, the guy did not pay attention and charged me $26 parking which I had to call and dispute several times which I do not like to do after a trip. They finally relented and took off the charge 2 months later. By the way, there are parking lots for about $8 around the corner and plenty of meter parking if staying on the weekends.

title: “Great Place to stay”
text: My husband daughter and I stayed here at the end of February.This was our 5th trip to NY and we would normally stay in the Quality Inn Times Sq, but that has been taken over and we found it too expensive. My daughter booked this hotel, based on reviews on TA, and as usual we weren't disappointed. Its all been said really by other reviewers, but I will add that we had a problem when we arrived, as we had to wait a while (2hours to be exact) for them to find two rooms on the same floor. We had booked 4mths in advance,one double and one single, on the same booking form, so I would have thought that would really have been sorted before we arrived. But maybe we should have specified this. When we did get the rooms one of them was room 18, room 18 on each floor has an ice machine and drinks dispenser directly outside. My daughter is a light sleeper and so she was disturbed by people using this during the night. We really wouldn't have minded if we were only staying a night or two, but we were there for 5nights. The following morning I spoke to the Manager on duty, Martin, and he couldn't have been more helpful. He immediately allocated us two rooms on the 11th floor. When we arrived back to the rooms that evening, there was a note of apology and a box of chocs in each room. I just thought that was a great touch. We really enjoyed our stay at the Hampton Inn and when we return to NY again, it will be our first choice.

title: “Quiet Suite hotel - good for large groups”
text:
A group of five girls + teenage son (ha!) stayed in this hotel in December last year. Its located in between Third and Lexington on 47th. Good location in Midtown but my personal preference would have been to have been a bit further West - around Fifth Ave. or Sixth. 
The hotel is quite near Grand Central and has a subway station two blocks away. [Get your 7 day unlimited $24 metro tickets here.] Its clean and really spacious - five girls, one boy and lots of shopping fit well into their 2 bedroom suite. The rooms did used to be private apartments and this is reflected in the design. 
The hotel provide cereal, muffins, milk, orange juice, etc... which is left in the fridge in the small kitchen each morning. There is a little bit of noise from the traffic outside but to be honest .. not enough to bother. The room was also really clean and the cleaners did a super job each day. 
There is a pizza place right next door which is handy.
We got the best rate from the Best Western site of $349 USD p/night for the two bedroom suite which worked out really well between five of us. 
I would prefer to stay in the Doubletree Suites Times Square but this has gotten really expensive. 
Overall a good hotel in an ok location. Would go back if I got another good deal.

title: “like we were family”
text: They took care of us, we took a motorcycle ride down there an we had a problem with our navigation and ended up at the wrong Country Inn and Suites ,the manager Sam seen that we were wore out and took control of the situation and called the other hotel to cancel our reservations an even got us a confirmation number.It happened to be rainging 2 of the 11 days we were there , Miss Connie at the front desk offered to let us use her car (how nice). The room was clean, the food was great the service was awesome the entire staff was friendly, we deffinitly felt like we were at home. Every time were in the Charlotte Nc. area this is deffinitly the first place we would choose to stay.

title: “Great hotel!”
text: I was in town for a conference but couldn't get the conference rate at that hotel. Found this gem and could not have been happier. Booked through hotels.com and paid less than I would have at the conference hotel. Room was a little small but very comfortable. Nice view out of the 13th story window of State Street and the Hancock Tower. Bathroom is slightly different with the glowing lips on the mirror, but I loved the shower! Great breakfast got me going. Staff was very helpful, let me check out a little late since the conference went over. I would not hesitate to stay at the Acme again!

title: “Busy family and school group hotel but great location”
text:
This hotel is very busy and had lots of families and school groups staying there. Breakfast is a feeding frenzy and the small room means you need to wait for tables at busy times. Our room was next to the lifts and was noisy. Room was very clean and staff excellent. Great location. 
Overall a good hotel for the money and NYC but be prepared for lots of people and kids, and using fire stairs instead of only 2 lifts in busy times.

title: “only stayed half an hour!”
text: a friend of mine booked this hotel for our girlie holiday to new york- a word of warning this is the worst hotel i've ever seen!!! the wallpaper was peeling off the walls, it smelled damp, looked dirty, there was a hole in the bathroom ceiling and had carpet on the walls in the hall- yuck!!! we stayed half an hour the time it took us to find a relatively cheap hotel elsewhere. i wouldn't recommend this to anyone. only plus point the staff were friendly- but they obvisiously didn't care about the state of the place...

title: “Great Location”
text: Loved the location of this hotel. It is pricey and if you aren't spending much time at your hotel I'm not sure it is worth the money. However, the room is comfortable and clean and you will be able to walk to many NYC attractions.

title: “Nice Getaway”
text: The Hotel was super clean, nice modern-retro design, We stayed in the Jr. Suite. Pretty roomy, and pretty pricey! We called the front desk for a mini fridge and had it delivered to our room in about 10 minutes. The view was great from room 915. The free continental breakfast is fruit, cereal and a few pastries. The location is great, in the middle of city center houston. Check out time is noon. Overall it was a great two night stay.

title: “Perfect location and great value”
text:
For a sightseeing vacation of L.A. area, you can't miss with this hotel. It's right on the beach and just around the corner from several great restaurants and bars. It doesn't offer much in way of services or extras but when your purpose is to enjoy the sights, it's not likely you'll be spending much time in the room anyway. There was coffee, juice and sweets for breakfast as well as internet access. The rooms were average in size, comfortable with flat screen TV and kitchen with small fridge.
There's only a few parking spots behind the hotel but we were fortunate not having any difficulty getting one. We were told, however, that there was free parking available a few blocks away.
We selected the cheaper rooms to the back. The only noises we heard were the garbage and delivery trucks. Of course, the hotel can't be held responsible for this.
There's also a patio right along the main walking path or on the roof to sit and have drinks while watching people go by or just looking out over the beach.
I loved Venice Beach and will definitely go back! Riding a tandem bike along the beach was great fun! It's also not far from Santa Monica pier to take in the amusement park or do some shopping on 3rd Street Promenade in Santa Monica.

title: “Wonderful room and location”
text: My husband and I stayed at this property from May 31- June 06. I was there on business, and he was there to relax and enjoy the city. I was very pleased with the hotel!! The rooms were spacious- large and comfortable bed, flat screen TV, big bathroom-for NY standards, the vanity had enough space for my toiletries, closet space, etc. In addition the view of our room was amazing- the lights at Times Square during the evening were incredibly romantic. I also loved that they hotel had an amazing gym!!! My husband and I took advantage of it on a daily basis: lap pool, exercise classes, weight room, aerobic equipment, etc. The gym staff was courteous and friendly- no charge for hotel guests. If you can, do the boxing class; it is a real killer. The hotel is centrally located, near shops, theater, restaurants, etc. I didn’t eat at the hotel restaurant, so I can’t comment on it. The hotel overall is very clean and well kept. We will definitely return to this property during our future visits to NY.

title: “Historic Dump on a Nasty section of Market St”
text:
This hotel appears to cater primarily to package or group tours and as such the lines at reception can be a long wait, while the the always lone counter clerk processes everyone. 
This property is ancient and while it has some lovely interior architectural details it desperately needs updating and renovation. The lobby furniture is ugly, worn and seriously uncomfortable. The general decor is depressing and outdated in every way.
It is located on a decrepit stretch of Market Street, very near many homeless shelters and is thus rather scary and creepy at night. 
The hotel is generally clean and my room had good linens but both mattresses were old and Very Saggy. I had to stuff two pillows under the mattress in order to keep from sliding off in the night. 
The free internet is so slow, both in the lobby and the rooms that is is basically worthless. Add to that the fact that there is no cell phone coverage in the lobby for some reason, meant that I could not reach my friend waiting hours there for me to arrive. There few restaurants of any quality within walking distance. The best thing is that there is a Starbucks just off the lobby where you can at least get a decent cup of coffee.

title: “Tiny room, clean, excellent service”
text: I found this hotel through the Hotel Tonight app. We stayed two nights. The room had a full bed and was tiny. We had a forth floor room wiith no view. Check in and out were fast. Cool retro decor. Doormen were all very nice and helpful when we needed a cab. Room was clean. Bathroom had a heated tile floor which was really nice! Complimentary New York Times paper each morning. Starbucks right next door and a Pinkberry frozen yogurt place not far away. Right next to central park. I would defiantly stay here again.

title: “Great Service, Great Location, Perfect for Meetings”
text:
Normally, I dread a trip to an airport hotel, however I have found the exception to that rule! I found this Hyatt to be a real gem - clean, quiet, great service -even good food (when do you see THAT at a business hotel?) and great Wi-Fi service!
There are two Hyatt hotels at DFW - the Gand Hyatt is closer to the runways, and the Hyatt Regency, where I stayed, is across the street and further from the runways (which I would assume makes it quieter). Free shuttle service makes the trip from any one of the numerous terminal buildings a snap.
My room was on the 9th floor facing the airport. It was clean and spacious. I was able to keep the room very cool, and found it to have a large work space that allowed me to be productive. While Wi-Fi service is often slow at hotels, I chose an option that allowed up to three devices to connect and all at a higher speed. Certainly the best Wi-Fi service I've had while traveling.
DFW is a large and isloated airport (thanks to crazy road construction surrounding the airport),and I was very happy to find great service and good food in the hotel restaurant for both lunch and breakfast. 
Finally, as other reviewers have mentioned, every staff member I encountered was pleasant, personable and helpful. All had a smile and a genuine approach that made me feel welcome. I'd stay here again without hesitation.

title: “We'll keep looking”
text:
I have to admit this Comfort Inn had all the necessities one could reasonably expect, but it's hard to be enthusiastic about it. The hallways were rather dark and had a musty smoky odor even in the non-smoking areas. Our room appeared to be lacking all its normal furniture- in looking at another open door, it seemed the desk unit in our room was gone and that open space had a rather crooked floor lamp awkwardly placed there. Still, the room had a coffeemaker, iron, ironing board and hair dryer. The bathroom though small and plain was clean- the sink was outside the bath proper which was handy for us. 
Parking seems to be an issue as they sell lots of "Park and fly" packages , so parking was at a premium and they sent us to the rear parking lot although the back door's security system which was supposed to open with our keycard didn't and we had to walk around to the front- except fro the times when the door was propped open by someone- not a real secure feeling.
Breakfast from 6-9 once again had several choices- but only corn flakes or fruit loops for cereal, hard boiled eggs one day but not the next and a rather bland display of mini mufins, bagels, and bread. One waffle iron seemed to result in a delay if you wanted a waffle. The seating area was very drab- can you say "school cafeteria?"
We got a nice AARP rate, but all in all, I'd try someplace else next time.
Oh, and when we checked in the young woman at the desk said."I'll have to see if any rooms are cleaned" and left me standing at the desk for quite a while. I could not imagine that there was not a better system for seeing what rooms were available than having her go up and down the hall opening doors- she returned after quite a while and said "I found one." What??? We usually have a better experience at Comfort Inn than we had here.

title: “An absolutely fabulous hotel, with wonderful Alicia at front desk and Kathy as concierge.”
text: Much more than we expected, this hotel is gracious in every way. Suites are large, well appointed, with fabulous bathrooms. The staff, including the front desk, and the concierge were so helpful. A lovely, quiet and accomodating hotel, one of the very best! The Parkers

title: “Location...Location... Location !!”
text:
This was my second trip to New York this year. Me and my GF stayed at the Roosevelt both times and loved the place. I really dont understand when people write bad reviews regarding this Hotel . The Hotel is rated a 3 star therefore people should expect to get a 3 star type of a hotel. 
People complain about the price of the lobby bar or restaurant . Well as an experienced traveler I have never found a cheap lobby bar or cheap hotel restaurant . People must realise that they are in NYC and if they walk outside for about 5 minutes , there are literally all kinds of restaurants,cafes. 
I recommend the room with a King Bed which is much larger than the regular room ( though still small compared to rooms in other countries , though decent size for NYC). King Bed is very comfortable. 
The greatest thing about this Hotel is the location . Everything is about walking distance. 5th avenue, Times Square , Grand Central, Rockefeller Center. If you're not the walking type , everything is about a 5-6$ cab ride.
Cons for this Hotel are the bathrooms which are a little retro and the TVS which are old and small. There is also no Free WiFi for the Hotel . 
I would recommend this Hotel for the experienced traveler who is going to NYC to visit the sites and is looking for a great room for a decent price. I do not recommend this Hotel to anyone looking for a 5 star ALL INCLUSIVE type of experience.

title: “Very good stay and bargain”
text: Stayed a couple nights (Thursday and Friday) for a job interview. The hotel's location to the job interview was close by. Easy access to the interstate. We had a room with a king size bed and a sleeper sofa. Enjoyed the breakfast buffet, which had eggs, waffles, sausage/bacon, cereal, pastries, toast, oatmeal, yogurt, milk, juice, coffee. The pool was nice. The spa (hot tub) was closed. Only problem we encountered was noise from kids on a swimming team who were staying at the hotel. You could hear noise coming from the room next door. The problem was resolved after contacting the hotel front desk. Will stay again if we are in Austin.

title: “Valentine's Day”
text: Great hotel. We've stayed in many, many New York hotels, and this ranks near the top, especially if you are looking for something small, friendly and good value for the money.

title: “Perfect place for families with children or just about anyone else!”
text:
We stayed at the Hotel Donatello for 4 nights and it was a perfect stay. I chose this place primarily for the location and also the fact their amenities included a microwave and a small fridge, so I could make simple breakfast and meals for my toddler. It turned out to be more than I asked for! 
First the location was great. It had the BART, MUNI, and the cable car that would take you up the hills to fisherman's wharf with in very close walking distances, with in a few blocks. It got a bit noisy one part of the night on Saturday but only for about 10 minutes. We were glad that we didn't book a hotel at the Fisherman's Wharf after visiting there... there were so many tourists, and just so congested in general. The Union Square area that Hotel Donatello is in was perfect. Not too far from any of the key places, and most places were very walkable.
The service was always prompt and friendly, by everyone including the porter and the concierge. We called the front desk for a taxi at the last minute to get to a wedding, and a limo service was waiting downstairs- and the price was better than what a cab fare would be. The cleaning ladies even washed the dishes I had brought and neatly laid them out to dry on the counter.
The rooms were kept clean and neat and they had plenty of closet space. I had read some reviews before the trip about how things look very worn-out, but in reality, there is some wear, but still maintained nicely. I think if you take flash photos of corners of a bathroom floor or walls in any hotels you'd probably see some worn-out areas. This is not a newly constructed hotel, but still up-kept nicely. The kitchenette has a small sink, a coffee maker, a microwave, and a small fridge (no freezer compartment, though). In a small drawer are metal utensils, and up on the shelves are mugs, glasses, bowls and plates.
The bed was a bit high but incredibly comfortable. We just had our son sleep in between us, but they do have cribs if you need one.
One extra note-- I had left my son's favorite DVD in the room and didn't realize until we got back to the east coast. I called the hotel and they promptly mailed it to me, packaged safely in a cd case and a bubble protected envelope!
Highly recommend!

title: “Very good deal and great stay”
text:
We just returned from a four night stay at the Langham Boston. We found an exceptional deal on Expedia during a time when there was a big conference in town; comparable -even lower tiered hotels- were significantly more expensive than the Langham and we actually wound up canceling at another property for significant savings (and I mean SIGNIFICANT savings). So we were THRILLED that we got such a great deal at a great hotel. 
Staff was top notch at check-in. The lobby renovations still had not been completed when we checked in, but, I didn't plan on hanging around much in the lobby anyway! It wasn't too much of an inconvenience. 
Our room wasn't available at check-in, but not a big deal. They took our luggage and held it for us.
When we finally did check-in, our room had a dusty smell to it; something to do with the filter in the air-conditioning duct I suspected. I noticed that the vent also looked a bit dirty. When we left that afternoon to go out, we let the front desk know about the dusty smell. They offered to put an air purifier in the room and let it run for about two hours which was the length of the time that we would be out. It did the trick, the dusty smell was gone by evening and we just kept that wonderful air purifier running the remainder of our stay!
Room was spotlessly clean otherwise. Furniture getting a bit dated in looks; still in good condition. 
Beds are comfortable; we slept great all nights. I got a stomach bug the second day we were there (from dining out elsewhere most likely; nothing to do with the hotel) and was bed ridden practically all day and night for 24 hours straight! Glad I was in a comfy hotel bed in a cozy room! 
Bathroom had a slight problem: the tub/shower had some issues (water pressure was just OK, not bad but not great) and the tub drained incredibly slowly; we'd have a nice pool of water to wade in after the end of each shower. Not a major issue at all just a bit annoying. Bathroom was spotlessly clean. 
All-in-all it is a really good property I think. Great staff, good location, clean rooms, easily walkable to the greenway, congress street, downtown crossing, quincy market, etc. 
We will definitely look at staying at the Langham the next time we roll into Boston!

title: “NIce location for shopping and enjoying the holidays”
text: The staff is very helpful, professional and courteous. Valet parking is a nice touch in such a poor parking location so there is no worries for your vehicle. Located close to the great shopping in the Galleria area, this is a nice albeit a little bit of a splurge to stay at during the Christmas holiday madness.

title: “Avoid - unless you can get a very very very good prize”
text:
we paid 160 ,- thorugh hotwire for a two star hotel with good location. The location is good. The hotel terrible. The room was a closet which looked like a flamingo with a love for Trinidad had exploded in it ( you will understand if you ever see it), queenseize 
 bed, holes in blankets and furniture, its view was a brickwall, no ac, a fan in the loft. It was ok clean but so depressing I felt like crying. Unfortunately it was late, we had our ten month old baby with us - so we stayed. The very sternlooking chinese man in the frontdesk ( manager I think) told us they hadn't a baby crip and declined our wish for room with a king bed, so it could fit the three of us.
The breakfast next morning was as depressing as the room. The only uplifting thing was to canadian women who complained over the bird droppings and the dirty carpet in their room and got a discount ( 140 ,- instead of 199,-).
If it had costed 70,- it would be all right - the canadian women called the hotel ' a scam'.
Poor woman this morning working the front desk and looking at all those discontent guests. We fled this morning. Staying at Cova down the road now - great place! Same price. I have written hotwire and asked them to remove a star from the hotelrating. If it had one star and costed 70 bucks it would be an ok solution for young travellers. Ohhh yeah ...the internet worked fine.

title: “Great Hotel”
text: Stayed in January February 2012"This hotel is situated across from the Beverly Centre which is a shopping centre. Bloomingdales Macey, and other named shops. The hotel is nice friendly staff. The restaraunt serve a beautiful dinner. You can then sit in there courtyard for after drinks very pleasant. Stayed 2 nights on arrival to LA then returned here for last night to catch our flight home. Returned to airport by taxi for $45.00 USD The hotel helped with arranging car hire delivered to the hotel and return to the hotel. Would definately recommend this hotel. A bus stop is a cross the road so you can catch it do a on off for site seeing and runs every 15 minutes.

title: “Loved this place!”
text: We had never been to Baltimore before and were to meet friends there for a long weekend. We had no idea where to begin for a hotel search. They were there on business so their room was already booked. We couldn't afford to stay where they were so I went to hotwire. We were set up at the Holiday Inn Express on North Gay St which is only a few blocks from the Inner Harbor area. We were close enough to walk to the Inner Harbor area within 10 minutes but far enough away to get away from the city distractions. This building is an old bank converted to a hotel. It is a lovely hotel with the original mail chutes still there. The main check-in desk, lobby area, lounge area, breakfast area are all in the huge downstairs with high ceilings and large pillars. Very attractively decorated. The continental breakfast area is spacious enough that you don't have to "wait in line" for anything. There is lots of seating areas from small tables to lounge type chairs. Our room was a corner room with windows facing 2 different streets. There were many windows that were quite large and gave us a beautiful view of the city from a couple of different angles. The room was perfect with the standard 2 beds, 2 easy chairs, table, large screen TV. It was much more spacious than most hotels we've stayed in. The bathroom had a large sinktop area with lots of room to put everything. All of the furniture was a dark cherry finish. There was also a small refrigerator and microwave between the bathroom and sleeping area. The ice machines were stationed at convenient locations on each floor. We didn't have to go up or down stairs to get ice like some other places. The hotel staff that we interacted with was all friendly, courteous, and knowledgeable about the area. This hotel also has its own parking lot and you get a pass to park free when you pay for your room. Our friends were staying in a hotel that was much more expensive but we all agreed that our room was much nicer than theirs. I would definately recommend this hotel to anyone and I would not hesitate to stay here again.

title: “Nice price and perfect location”
text:
Stayed in January together with a friend. Small rooms, pretty much 2 QS beds and a TV. But for us that was fine.
Clean room, bathroom OK but not great. 
Breakfast was ok, it was nice not to have to go out and pay +$20 every morning for some coffee and a sandwich!

title: “We had a great time and wish we could visit more often.”
text:
We really enjoyed the memorabilia throughout the hotel. That was really cool. The room was great the view from our room was pretty good. We could see the ballpark ( which we also got to see a game between the Padres and D-Backs ). First major league baseball game I've ever been to. All in all it was a great experience.
 Thanks,
 Mason

title: “Way better than most for price”
text: I stay here or business 2x/month. Much better than hilton garden inn or radisson martinique. The rooms are clean, service is good, and restaurant is very good. Free breakfast is delightful -real food, not doughnuts and yoghurt. Rooftop bar is a bonus but most nghts is booked for private functions. Rooms have robes, good hairdryer, but no bottled water.

title: “A Pleasant Surprise in DC”
text:
I was in DC for a training workshop for three nights, and the Comfort Inn was the only hotel I found within walking distance that was within my budget. Having had mixed results at various Comfort Inns, I was wary before I arrived.
The hotel is in a quaint old building, a block east of Thomas Circle, surrounded by mostly luxury residences. Just to the southwest is the edge of the bustling business district of DC. The room I was in faced the main street, and the occasional sirens of various types reminded me that I was, indeed, in the middle of a bustling metropolis. Otherwise, the room was relatively large for an urban hotel, with high ceilings, giving the illusion of even greater space.
The room was clean and neat, and the housekeeping staff did a consistent job keeping it that way. The mattress was the most comfortable I've slept on in a Comfort Inn, firm without being hard. As expected, toilet amenities were adequate--shampoo, conditioner, soap, lotion, mouthwash--and the high-speed internet access, while not blazing, was much faster than I have experienced at many other hotels.
The continental breakfast was predictable (belgian waffles was the one hot dish). My only complaint was there were only two yogurt flavors available all three mornings I was there: strawberry-banana and strawberry.
For most travelers, my chief complaint may not be important. Because of its location, there are only a few eateries within about three blocks of the hotel. Not a problem if you don't mind a short cab ride or find walking convenient. However, the weather happened to be rainy for two of my three evenings there, and there were no sit-down restaurants within a ten minute walk. Mercifully, the guest directory provides an extensive list of "local" eateries that delivery right to the hotel. So even though I generally ate dinner in my room, I had a variety of menus to choose from.
Overall, my stay at the Comfort Inn was a positive, and the value for the price was excellent!

title: “Good Location”
text: My wife and I stayed at the Westin Copley Place for 6 nights in July 2011. Having the directional sense of an under nourished gnat, I was initially confused by arrival at Level 1 and Check In at Level 2 but I got with the programme eventually! As we both have bad backs we appreciated the comfortable sleep the suuportive bed afforded us during our stay. The bedroom was was a good size and well furnished but we both thought the bathroom was too small for comfort. As we were on the 32nd or 33rd floor we enjoyed panormic views of the city and the summer sunsets. We ate out every night except one (easy to do given the location of the hotel) and on that night we only ate a snack in Bar 10 as the humidity had effected our appetites. The snack food was good though and delivered quickly and pleasantly. The only serious quibble we had with the hotel was that the bottled water in the room's fridge was vastly over priced and led us to buy bigger bottles for loss money in the CVS across the square.

title: “Great location”
text: Myself and my husband stayed at The Roosevelt between 1st and 5th December. It's in a great location close to major attractions, in particular The Chrysler Building and Grand Central Terminal. We were a little early for check-in but this wasn't even questioned when we arrived. There was no queue at the desk and we were quickly guided to our comfortable, clean and reasonably sized room on the 7th floor. We had a view onto Madison Ave which was great for watching people and traffic go by - you could hear the traffic but it didn't disturb us in the slightest. Our room service order was taken efficiently and delivered quickly by a very pleasant member of staff. There was a restaurant available but we didn't use it - we've been to NYC before so have our favourite places we go to eat. We did have soom food and drinks in the bar - again, the service was friendly and efficient and the food portions were huge! We can't fault The Roosevelt and wouldn't hesitate to stay there again.

title: “Good place at a good price with an exceptional breakfast”
text: Good place at a good price with an exceptional breakfast. As others have mentioned the breakfast is what sets this place apart from other hotels in the Choice chain, most of which serve junk breakfasts like ersatz egg and sausage disks and waffles and watery coffee. This place has abig Mexican buffet. Besides that, everything else was very good here plus the price was lower than most of the others.

title: “Hilton- it was ok”
text:
I was expecting good things from this Hotel, not only because i paid a fair bit for the room, but because the Hilton name usually suggests a certain standard. 
When I got there, the oracle convention was on and there were signs plastered all over the interior and exterior of the hotel, I had to confirm with the taxi driver that this was actually the Hilton because I genuinely couldn't tell. 
Not one person offered to help me with me two big bags (when checking in or out), no free wifi in rooms, the room had a nice view but the floors in the bathroom looked grubby and it looked a little run down. 
The location is ok if you are really keen on Union Square, but if you aren't, maybe look somewhere else. Also i didnt feel safe walking around this area after dark. 
When I come back to SF I won't be staying here.

title: “Definitely give this hotel a miss! AWFUL!”
text: I have been to NYC before and was fully aware that the hotels can be pretty basic but none the less ok for the short time you spend in the room. However, this hotel was AWFUL! I would not recommend anyone to stay here. As we arrived the man on reception didn’t even look up which was a bad start. When we got up to our room I was horrified, the smell was disgusting. I knew that the hotel was very old but that was a smell I will never forget. The first thing I did was to buy some glade to get rid of the terrible smell. We didn’t let this ruin our stay, we just made sure we spent as little time as possible in the hotel. As people have said it’s a great location, when you stand outside the hotel and look up you can see the Empire State building which was fantastic. It was an excellent price but next time I will pay a little bit extra to stay in a decent hotel and will definitely give the Wolcott a miss. The worst part of the trip was the last day when we had to use the “shower room” as we had an evening flight and had to check out at 12noon. We were given a key to a dirty shower, a stained toilet and a sink. We decided not to use the shower as it was so dirty and instead had to make do with having a quick wash. This was not ideal especially as we had a 7 hour flight and couldn’t have a shower as the facilities provided were not clean. This hasn’t put me off New York it’s a great City and my time there was fantastic. I did read the reviews on here before I went and noticed they were mixed but I would suggest you do not stay here.

title: “Horrible hotel, horrible staff even for a starwood preferred guest”
text:
I am a Starwood Preferred Guest, so I assume I always get a bit of TLC when I visit startwood properties- Not the case with the Parker NYC. This was my second time at this property and my last. First of all we enter reception and the guy at the front desk has a horrible cold. He is pale, coughing and sneezing. Just what I want to see on the first day of vacation, not to mention I have a child with me to be exposed to this. No upgrade available Im told. Ask for manager, he doesnt have a cold but proceeds to lie to me that they are booked at 100%. I take this standard room since its late stuff 3 of us in tiny quarters. Go to be at 2am, to be awaken at 7am by huge jackhammers and noises. NO ONE decided, even with my startwood status to tell me huge construction was going on at the hotel. We asked to be moved to a quieter room at 7am. At which point they moved me to a suite. I thought there were no more suites left? Liars! Still heard noise , rude manager told me she would not refund me. Called Starwood, got moved to W LEXINGTON, much better experience. W Lexington, front desk staff awesome, did everything they could to help me out.
PARKER NEW YORK sucks! Noisy, rude staff, liars, small rooms- dont go there. W Lexington rocks!

title: “not our definition of "luxury"”
text:
Clearly, the person who writes the copy for the promotional literature and website has never stayed here! We booked a studio suite (the next most expensive category), which was extremely small and barely furnished--a small side chair, as table too small to be useful. Virtually no storage--only a couple of drawers under the bed...which were on the wrong side of the bed and virtually inaccessible. Not even a throw rug on the bare floor!!!! Our room bore no relationship whatever to the photo of the Studio Suite on the website. Because no slippers were provided (nice hotels usually do), we had to wear our shoe bags to avoid walking on cold hard floors! Weird. Only one bathrobe in the room (we had to call for a second one); neither bathrobes nor the very small bath towels could ever be considered fluffy. And a person under 5'7" tall cannot see in the bathroom mirror.
Worst of all, our room had not been cleaned when we returned at 3 pm. When we called to inquire, the front desk said , "Well, you must have had your Do Not Disturb tag on your door." Not, "We're very sorry; we'll fix that right away." Needless to say, we did NOT have our Do Not Disturb tag out.
We ordered from room service 3 times--simple things--and it was never correct. And not very good quality--definitely minimalist. We did, however, haave an excellent meal of sushi, sahimi, etc in the restaurant on the first floor.
This place should present itself for what it really is: a very basic hotel in a good location.

title: “Easily accessible”
text:
Opportunity to staff in hotel that is easily accessible to San Francisco and all of the tourist venues with out paying exhorbitant prices offered by other well known hotel chains. Continental breakfast of fruit, eggs, toast, conserves, fruit juice and tea and coffee are refreshing and come as part of the priceàssa.
Ladies on reception are ready with a smile and a willingness to guide you in the right direction.
Good pick up location for tours such as Alcatraz and the Napa Valley

title: “Excellent Value for Money”
text:
Excellent value for money.
My partner and I stayed here for 3 nights. Rooms have air conditioning and are decorated to a good standard. The bathrooms are excellent. One of the cleanest hotels we've stayed in.
Great location. Easy access to the subway. Felt very safe. 
The staff on reception could do with being a little more friendly! But I think a lot of the people we came across in customer service positions in the city were kind of abrupt and not as helpful as they could be perhaps be! What I think people forget is a smile doesn't hurt and it goes an awful long way!

title: “Girls on tour December 2011 from Durham Uk”
text: Great location for getting around. Plenty of good restaurants on 9th avenue. Safe location. Remy in particular provided a really good service and is a well experienced member of staff x

title: “Superb B&B in NYC”
text:
Staying at the 414 Inn was a pleasant experience from the moment I made my reservations online. We received an e-mail as well as a courtesy phone call from the staff before our visit.
The hotel is located on 46th Street, a quiet respite from the hustle and bustle of Midtown Manhattan. Tucked away in the middle of 'Restaurant Row', it's just short walk to Times Square.
Rooms at the 414 Inn have a European flair and look similar to what you may find in a local NYC apartment. The room was clean, well appointed, and stylishly decorated. The bathroom was large, bright and had plenty of clean towels and hot water. 
414 Inn provides a wonderful continental breakfast of fresh muffins, danishes, coffee, fruit and cereal each morning. You have the option of eating in at tables in their comfy lobby, or in their lovely outdoor courtyard. The staff were kind, friendly and willing to provide guests with assistance. 
We enthusiastically recommend the 414. For what you get, for what you're paying, you'd be hard pressed to find a better bang for your buck anywhere else in NYC.

title: “Great hotel and location”
text:
Stayed here for two nights and the hotel was excellent, ideally located on Santana Row , the staff were friendly the breakfast was nice and the room was amazing, plus you get free wifi all over the hotel.
Parking is free if you self park in the big car park around the corner. Will definitely stay here again

title: “I was not impressed”
text: This was our first stay at the Carlton. We spent 2 nights for our anniversary. Check in was easy. The front desk employee was not friendly. The room was small, but clean. We were placed on the side of the building by the a.c. unit mentioned by other reviewers. I called to switch rooms, but was told that they were at capacity and can only move us to the unrenovated part of the hotel. So we decided to stay. The picture quality of the t.v. was horrible. No microwave and fridge is filled with overpriced drinks leaving little room for you own items. The corridors are quite dark and a little scary. I wouldn't feel comfortable walking them alone and I'm from NYC! Overall, we were not impressed. Their customer service needs improvement. Spend a little more money and stay somewhere else. On a positive note, the bed was extremely comfortable and it was quiet (aside from the outside noise).

title: “Great Location but Hotel disappointing”
text: Mixed views about the Marriott Marquis. On the plus side, the location on Times Square cannot be beaten. The elevators are great fun and my teenage son loved them. The hotel is mostly what you would expect from a modern, impersonal city hotel. There was a wait at the check in and the hotel was very busy. I booked a Times Square room, but was very disappointed to get the side of the hotel next to a construction site. A very tall crane dominated the view from our window and so spoilt our view of Times Square. As it was the weekend, so there was no work going on, but from our room it looked as if the crane could swing through our window. We should have been warned about this and offered an alternative. The room decor and the bathroom were somewhat tatty for a hotel of this class and I was suprised that there was no fridge or mini bar. We had a room with two queen beds. One of the beds was extremely soft and so uncomfortable that neither my husband or I could sleep. The other bed seemd OK. I asked if the matress could be changed - they refused saying they did not have a spare and could not swap with another room because the hotel was full. They only offered a board for the bed. My son ended up on the very soft bed- and we had the other, but that's not the point - we should have had two comfortable beds in the room.

title: “Great Hotel”
text: Spent a week staying at this hotel with husband and 2 teenagers, 19 & 17, had a great stay. The rooms we had were a good size,beds were very comfortable and the showers great, also had the best hairdryer I have ever had in a hotel. Found all the staff friendly, polite and helpful, the door staff were helpful in recommending places to eat. Hotel was in a good area, not to far from shopping malls, Newbury street and Boston Common. Food was good had dinner there on first night and breakfast each day, my sons could not believe the size and amount of pancakes served for breakfast, I enjoyed the fruit available and the unusual juice combinations that were sometimes served. We all enjoyed staying here and would definitely stay here again.

title: “Better than Expected”
text:
Before selecting the Marriott Indianapolis Downtown, I did some research on the web looking for reviews - both negative & positive. I found many of the reviews to be so widely varied, I thought it would be safe to book our 2-night getaway here. After all it is a Marriott and it couldn't be as bad as some have described.
I'm very glad that we did make our reservations here. It was a wonderful experience and I would willingly and cheerfully stay at the Marriott Indianapolis Downtown again. We arrived late in Indy (while Victory Stadium was unleashing its fans), but still found the hotel staff to be quite courteous and amazingly, we found parking in the hotel garage. All staff members from the beginning of check-in to the final check-out were extremely hospitality-oriented and very accommodating. 
The breakfast buffet @ Circle City Bar & Grille was delicious and satisfied our appetites quite well.
What I loved most about the hotel was the location -- right downtown next to all the convention center and sports activities; its proximity to Circle Centre and all that it has to offer visitors and locals alike; and a block away from White River State Park that offers something for everyone to explore.
Next time we stay in downtown Indy, we'll be sure to book with Marriott Indianapolis Downtown again!

title: “Decent compared to the reviews.”
text: I was quite reluctant when searching for a place to stay while in the NE Columbus area. I finally compromised and booked a room at Hawthorn Suites and expected the worst. Reservations went smooth. Checkin was awesome, in plain english, with a smile, no issues, etc. The room was typical of better Wyndham properties. Not plush or fancy but quite functional. The only thing that didn't work, was the button on the TV. The remote took care of that. The rooms were laid out in smaller condo like buidings with four rooms on the ground floor and four more above that. It was a little confusing as to where your room was, but once I found it, all was good. It wasn't super quiet in the evening, but after dark there was not much noise at all. The rooms had a full kitchen which would be great for a longer stay. I heard another person say that the hotels in the area (there were several) often had vehicles broken into, but other hotels were worse than Hawthorn. I didn't have any issues nor did I hear of any issues by others while I was there. The staff seemed helpful when I needed something or others asked for something. The grounds were clean. The pool area looked refreshing enough, but I did not use it. The breakfast was warm and fresh. The sausage and eggs were actually quite good. Check out was simple and again in plain english with a smile. I would go back again for the price paid and am considering the option when I go back to Columbus in October.

title: “Great hotel and fantastic location”
text:
This was our 3rd stay in LA and 2nd time at the Sofitel (1st stay at four seasons for honeymoon). We stayed in the opera suite and found the suite to be very spacious and clean.
We were travelling with our 1 year old and the staff went out there way to make sure we had everything we needed and felt very at home.
The location is excellent for both shopping and sight seeing.

title: “Terrible hotel experience”
text:
This hotel was probably one of the worst hotels I've ever stayed at. My family booked the hotel for us because it was a good price. But the price was simply not worth it. First getting into the hotel was a nightmare! We drove around in loops for about 25 minutes trying to get into the place. The signs that said "entrance here" with an arrow were after the actual entrance getting us disoriented only to have to loop around again. Once we got in we only learned that we had to go back out to the street to access the parking garage - which was $22 per night! And that was where the next problem set in. They told us it was good for 24 hours - don't believe them. It was only good until 12pm noon - because if you wanted to walk around after checking out like what we did - we got charged another day which was a complete rip off. There were four of us down to check in and we all got the same story - 24 hour parking fee - which is supposed to be a great deal and perk for staying at the hotel, according to them. So for my dad who was there for less than 24 hours he had to pay $44 to park. 
The location was okay. They say inner harbor but it is about a 7-8 block to the actual inner harbor. And it wasn't the safest location. As a female I refused to go anywhere without someone else in my party with me. And that was even if we were walking down to the corner bar a block away. 
The cleanliness was definitely subpar. The room size was decent. The tub was not draining properly and with four of us in a room we had to wait a half hour in between showers just to allow the tub to drain. A big inconvenience. 
The windows were definitely not sound proof. The first night I was kept up listening to sirens for about 2-3 hours and then the second night my brother-in-law was up half the night listening to the rain (that's bad when you can hear the rain and your up on the 6th floor)
The elevators were a disaster! We stayed at the hotel for 2 nights for a total of 36 hours and one of the two elevators was broken for at least 15 hours. The morning we were checking out there was a line for the elevator to go down of about 15 people on our floor alone! (the elevators were small and could only fit maybe 8-10 people and that was if they were sandwiched in which no one really wants. Plus there were 8-9 floors - so what if there were that many waiting on each floor?!?!) We decided not to wait because it took an average of 5-10 minutes to wait for the elevator normally when both were working and we didn't have a half hour to stand around and waste. So we had to take the stairs six flights down with our luggage. That was a joy...
All in all I would not recommend this hotel to anyone. The money it looks like you are saving you are not with the added taxes and then the expensive parking.

title: “Great experience--would definitely stay again!”
text:
After much researching, my wife and I decided to stay at the Belvedere. We decided to stay here mainly because of price, location, and the free continental breakfast! In addition, the reviews were excellent.
The only negative thing we can say, and everyone else seems to agree, is that the elevators were extremely slow! During the middle of the day, they were fine. But in the morning and evenings, when everyone was coming/going, they were slow!
Also, most people commented negatively about the A/C window units, but ours worked like a charm! The room was beautiful!
We would DEFINITELY recommend staying here and we will definitely attempt to stay at the Belvedere on our next stay!

title: “Good Hotel, Great Location, A Few Kinks”
text:
We spent the week of July 11-18 in New York City, staying at the Hotel Reserve. My sister booked two rooms back in February via Expedia, so we got a rather swell rate under $99 per night, per room.
When we arrived at the hotel very late on Saturday night (having driven up from Baltimore), there were supposed to be two rooms with two double beds. Well, the front desk clerk (none of those knuckleheads wore name tags, so you never knew who you were dealing with) informed us that they did not have a second room with two double beds so someone was going to have to use a blow up air mattress. I was very angry and they finally agreed to change our room. After the clerk convinced me that the air mattress would be “perfect” for our very petite mother, we went ahead and took the single bed room. Well, that air mattress sucked…sucked air, that is…that darn thing would not stay blown up. So, if they offer this to you…DO NOT ACCEPT!
The room was very small, but comfortable. The bathroom was very tiny. The bed was plush (way too many pillows for me!), but Mom couldn’t take the air mattress so we had to force one of our teenage nephews to come downstairs and sleep on it. When we asked for extra towels, the maids always left them, but they did forget to clean our room on one of the days. The free Internet service was great, and we did not experience a lot of street noise from our eighth and nine floor rooms.
The hotel is convenient to several different subway stations (only $27 per person to ride the subway for seven days!), and within walking distance to Wall Street, the Financial district, the World Trade Center and Battery Park. Overall, the location is great!
The restaurant connected to the hotel, The Federal Café, was THE ABSOLUTE WORST place we have ever eaten (check out my review on that dive!). Within walking distance is George’s Restaurant (awesome for breakfast & lunch) or Bobby Van’s Steakhouse for dinner.
I would have rated this hotel higher, but they really ticked me off by charging my credit card $8.68 for something that I did not use. When I called the hotel to complain, the front desk clerk kept telling me that I had stayed in Room 206 and that is where the charges originated. I informed him that he was quite wrong…we stayed in Room 801 the entire time we were there! He promised to call me back, but two months later I am still waiting.

title: “Great price/location”
text: We loved the location, it's centrally located, a minute away from the Common, across the street from the T, at a great price ($120/night for the smallest room). The said-small room was comfortable with the exception of the 2-feet wide shower (had to choose between banging elbows on the wall or sticking on curtain) and overheated bathroom (90 degrees ?) because of radiator that could not be controlled. Free wifi in Lobby was almost impossible to get at regular hours. Though, clean and quiet rooms, we'll return, it's a great deal if you spend your days and evening out in the city !

title: “Good value, Good location, Good Find - would stay again (just in a different room)”
text: Decided to add a few extra days to our trip and visit Baltimore while attending a local family event close by. Wanted to stay in the Inner Harbor area at a decent hotel for a reasonable price - the Days Inn seemed like a good choice. Glad we did – the location was great. Easy walk to Inner Harbor, Basilica, Camden yards, Museums and more. Staff were very pleasant and helpful. Parking convenient. Restaurant had good service and food (only tried Breakfast). Outside pool was quite refreshing. Only negative was the room layout was very odd – they had pushed the queen bed against the wall to the bathroom which made it difficult to get out bed if you were on the inside, leaving the rest of the room wide open. The foot of the bed was where the sink outside of the bathroom was, leaving very little space to maneuver. To watch TV in bed was awkward since it had to be turned so much. The microwave, refridge, coffee maker & free WI-FI all made up for the inconvenience and it was only for two nights. Would recommend to budget conscious travelers’ looking for a good central base close to the Inner Harbor.

title: “Enjoyed the stay”
text: I did not have a pet but enjoyed meeting all the pets that were staying here and the attention they received by the hotel. I loved having a goldfish in my room too! My room was small but clean and worked out ok. I was there 8 days so I would have liked a larger space. There was nowhere to sit except at the desk or on the bed and that was a pain for such a long stay. The bed was comfortable and the room was clean and in good shape. The evening 'reception' was always well attended and pleasant except there were always so many people that I never did get an appetizer the whole time I was there. The location is convenient to 16th St. Mall shopping and not too bad a walk to the Convention Center. The fitness center was very small but never crowded and the machines were in good shape and clean.

title: “I would stay nowhere else in Seatac”
text: I've been to this location twice as an extraordinarily well-designed business venue. Near the airport, easy to find, CRAZY good value, wonderful service, great food. If you can afford Doubletree or the Radisson or the Holiday Inn, you're in for a serious treat.

title: “Wonderful stay, beautiful hotel!”
text: Our experience was completely flawless and the only negative I can say is the self parking @ $18/night was a little much..... This hotel is beautiful and the rooms are really nice. The bed was very comfortable and the bathroom is a great size and really nice and clean. We ordered room service which was very good and the roof top pool is nice with a great view. We will definitely be back next time we are in Austin!

title: “No respect for time”
text:
1) Waited at airport for shuttle - 30 Minutes.
2) Waited in line for check in - 15 minutes
3) Came early - Waited for room - 2 Hours.
Then rooms are comfortable... stay was good later on...

title: “Wonderful hotel in a great location”
text:
Brief summary: I've stayed here before and was pleasantly surprised with the renovations and some changes. The location is always very good if you are interested in the theater, subway a short walk away, right in Times Square. I'd stay here again.
Our room was on the top floor, 4501 (or 03?) had a view of the Hudson and was billed as a "quiet room." Yes, it was quiet in general, but if you listened hard, you could hear some soft sqeeks of the service (not public) elevator that cut into some of the room space. I think that rooms with the number 53 (or 63?) might have a similar location on the other side of the elevator shafts. Still, this was a pretty quiet room and spacious enough, and probably the default location for people booking with award points.
The housekeeping was excellent and staff throughout the hotel was very friendly and professional. The concierges may be a little overworked, but they are helpful and can supply more tourist information, subway maps, etc.
The room has all of the amenities that one expects of a recently renovated business class hotel, i.e. ironing board, toiletries, duvet-style bedding (with a top sheet, thank goodness, so we didn't have to crank up the AC ro be comfortable,) etc. Good closet and drawer space. I really appreciated the oversize in-room safe that can accomodate a laptop as well as other valuables. The tub/shower is a traditional standard size, which was fine by me since I have tired of the jacuzzi-size tubs at inns where I;ve recently stayed, and that seem to take forever to fill. Lots of counterspace in the bathroom.
Check-in was fast, but it was not very busy. Similarly, the hotel was not empty, but I've seen it busier. The elevators handled any crowd very well with a new gizmo where you keyin the floor you want, and a code appears that shows where the next elevator to that destination will arrive. Unless you really don't like heights, everyone seems to enjoy the glass elevators that are their own entertainment.
I've been in the hotel's lobby many times, often before the theater for cocktails and a clean place to go to the bathroom before the show. It was nice to see the addition of a Starbuck's on the 8th floor lobby for a relatively inexpensive breakfast close by, as well as one at ground floor level. It seems that they don't mind your taking breakfast to the cocktail lounge area in the morning, but that area turns into a cocktail lounge later in the day.
We didn't use the gym facilities, but it looks pretty nice with a great view of the city.
Again, the irritation: in-room internet access requires a fee. It feels like nickle-and-diming.
So: this may not be one of those unique charming boutique hotels, but it has not failed to deliver a very good night's rest right in the center of things.

title: “Great Choice!”
text:
My family and I stayed here for 2 nights in July while visiting San Antonio. We were able to book a room at the OMNIZOO promotional rate of $89/night and received vouchers for the excellent breakfast buffet for 2 every morning as well as complimentary newspaper and breakfast drinks delivered to our room by joining the Omni club. Thank you to previous reviewers for the excellent tips.
The room was adequate in size and very clean. We had a wonderful view from our window and could even see the downtown area. The bathroom was clean and had nice toiletries. The turndown service in the evening and bathrobes were also a nice touch. We used the pool and workout room and both were well-maintained. The lobby area was very pretty. Parking was easy and getting to and from downtown was also hassle-free and only took about 15 minutes. Free wireless Internet service worked great in the room. The staff -- front desk, bellman, doorman, housekeeping, restaurant (omelet station chef was very efficient!), etc. -- were all courteous and professional.
A couple of minor complaints about the room were not enough plugs for charging laptops and cellphones and not having an in-room safe. But, all in all, a great value for a top-notch hotel.

title: “Excellent Service, Great Location...”
text: I was extremely nicely welcomed by the front office director Mr. Zalki... then went to my room and found a beautiful cozy bed to relax and have a nap after a long international flight... (I took a shower before obviously, with very good water pressure)... The breakfast buffet had everything one could wish for... Mr. Zalki checked up on me during my entire stay... it was a real pleasure staying at the Park Central. The location was just perfect... Check out the map on their website...

title: “It's the people who work there that need to be highlighted...”
text:
Stayed at the Park Central just last week and I have almost all great things to say.
Location: 2 blocks from Central Park South. Can't beat it if this is the area you're looking for. Stayed once across the street at the Wellington (similarly priced) and that was a dump in comparison.
Hotel itself: Like many older hotels in NYC you can see the age and the wear and tear on the rooms. Not bad... but just not 100% fresh and new like you see in other cities or at other NY hotels for twice the price. This was mostly true in the rooms. In the public areas I was quite impressed. Lobby restaurant was up to date and clean. Lobby itself was kept up. Even caught crew touch up painting on my last day.
But as I said, this place really shines by way of the staff. Never ran into an unfriendly person. They were mostly accommodating to every request. One negative is I did once come down to the front desk to ask for a courtesy razor to shave (can't bring em on the plane anymore and most hotels have a little kit they'll give you). The woman said they were out but she would have someone send one up later in the day to my room. That never happened... and I never had a message or anything explaining why.
Now... the real reason for me glowing about the staff. There was one young lady... Her name was Cynthia. She was part of the "front desk" staff but didn't actually work behind the front desk. She was more of the telephone arm of the front desk. 
She was phenomenal. I mean, there was nothing she wouldn't do to make the guests happy. She was charming, accommodating and friendly. If everything were equal with similarly priced hotels in that neighborhood, I would still stay there again even if just to know she was there helping make the stay pleasant for me. 
Other hotels need to heed this review: Staff your hotel with nice people then give them the freedom to go out of their way to impress the guests and you have a recipe for success!

title: “What a great location”
text: This was a find. We stayed here for a weekend and the location could not have been better. We found the hotel to be quite gilded, ie. gold, but the rooms were sufficently updated and clean, they were a good size, the gym was very nice, and the staff friendly. For the price, it was a great deal and we would stay here again. We had stayed at the Sofitel in the past in NYC but they do not have rooms large enough for our kids there. So, we looked around, came across this one after much research, and would stay here again.

title: “Needed a last minute place to stay, we lucked out!”
text:
I stayed here last minute along with my wife and mother in law while my father in law went through surgery at St. Luke's.
We stayed here 3 nights, and although the hotel is older than some others around, it is still a great place.
We had a room with two queens (3 of us staying), and the beds were comfortable and clean. The bathroom was pretty average, but hey, it had a sink, a toilet, and shower/bath, and a small counter to put your stuff.
There was a small table with two chairs outside, and a little area with a mirror (that also housed a coffee maker with some coffee samples) that one could use to get ready. We never felt cramped.
The front desk staff (which we encountered both nights and days due to going back and forth to St. Luke's) was phenomenal. Always greeted us as we walked in and out, and were very helpful on where to find certain things locally.
The Best Western is within walking distance to St. Luke's and the Childrens Hospital. You could walk outside, or walk into the hospital across the street (can't remember which one), and connect to overhead walkways that got you to St. Luke's.
The breakfast was above average in choices, and tasted good too. There was coffee, juices, a waffle maker, assorted pastries and bread, and hot sausages, eggs, biscuits and gravy. Cereal too, I believe. You could grab a free copy of the Houston Chronicle each morning as well.
