There was shuttle service, but we rarely used it. The shuttle runs from 7 am to 7 pm. Depending on visiting hours (assuming you have a relative or friend at one of the hospitals), this may or may not work for you. I personally found it easier to walk to where I needed to go.
We got a great rate, and they may have a rate specially for those visiting hospital patients (nearby hotels seem to offer this, so I'm assuming they do too, even though it wasn't explicit when we called to ask about vacancy and rate).
The parking was free and ample.
Not sure about the wifi, we didn't use it, and didn't inquire about it.
There is a laundry room on site.
I did not see it, but my wife said there was a small gym and pool too.

title: “Great location!”
text: We vacationed here for 6 days. We stayed in two adjoining rooms with our two children 12, and 8. the rooms were clean, comfortable, and quiet. The refrigerators were hard to open and close the freezers were small and did not keep the leftover ice cream frozen. It would have been nice to have a microwave in the room to reheat leftovers and reheat coffee. We tried to find one in the hotel bar but there wasn't one there either. The furniture is dated but in good shape. We were close to many great attractions and the metro bus stop is just outside the hotel. The trolley is just a couple blocks away. We had a great breakfast at the hotel and kids were free. Near the hotel there were other great breakfast places that were also very good. We would definately stay here again.

title: “Very Nice and Good Location!”
text: I have stayed at a lot of the other hotels close to LAX and this one seems to have more toffer than most. The location is convienent and the traffic is not bad at all. Close to the 405 freeway and only a few blocks from the beach. Most of the hotels are dead in the evenings, but this one is busy early to late. Nice bar and resturant is not bad other than being a little overpriced, but then it's a hotel restaurant. The rooms are clean and quiet especially for this close to the airport. Overall very enjoyable and Starwood points!

title: “Outstanding site”
text: Very nice in every aspect. Check in was a breeze. Our room contained a king size bed, sofa, desk, the standard options. The bed was outstanding-I don't usually sleep well the first night on the road, but I slept very well all three nights. The breakfast buffet was one of the best I have encountered in a motel, though it was $9.95 or so. My wife ordered from the menu; had a breakfast sandwich that was $7.50. She was satisfied. The waitress was excellent. We stayed three nights, and were completely satisfied. The next time we are in Charlotte, we will probably stay in the same place.

title: “Great service in a great location”
text: We spent the weekend overlooking the Water Tower and with a magnificent view of the Hancock building. The staff was eager to cater to our every desire. If you want to see downtown Chicago or spend time shopping the Magnificent Mile, this should be your home base for the trip.

title: “Wonderful place to stay”
text: I loved this place. It was clean, quiet, comfortable and convenient to all the New York has to offer. I plan on staying there every time I am in the city.

title: “The difference between hotels and extended stays.”
text:
I on the road for 2 weeks now and state is in very nice hotels best western and holiday inn express. I checked in at the Staybridge San Antonio Seaworld hotel yesterday and for the first time I felt like I was at home. The hotel, staff and amenities are awesome, but the room with it's kitchenette was the icing on the cake. 
I highly recommend if you're staying for more than 2 days that you check into this Staybridge during your travels.
Steve Lewis

title: “Loved our stay at the French Quarters”
text: It was the location that attracted us to this hotel and we were blown away with the customer service that we received. The staff were all very helpful and friendly and went out of their way to make our experience a good one. The location as I said was perfect as it was just a quick walk to Time Square. Would definitely return here.

title: “Great stay, fantastic service”
text:
Stayed twice now and both times had a great experience. Rooms were very clean and although two tour buses of pee-wee hockey were in the building, it was still quiet enough to not even know they were there. 
Also the cookies are fantastic. =D

title: “Loved Location - Hated Hall Noise”
text: Hotel location is excellent. Good access to all public transportation. Rooms are small, but nice. Short on drawer space. Stetsons food and service are excellent, but pricey (as expected). This Hotel has the WORST hallway noise in the room of any hotel I have ever stayed at. If they put you in a room next to the elevator, RUN to the nearest Motel 6.

title: “Great Hotel, well worth the money and time!!!”
text:
Was very sceptical about this hotel, after I read reviews about it on expedia and on tripadvisor but once I got into the lobby and saw the size of it to what is shown on expedia doesn’t do it justice. Check in/Check out was very swift. We had a concierge king room booked, located on floor 18 we got what we asked for...king size bed and 32inch LCD T.V with 50+ T.V channels. The room size was good, (easily fitted 3 big luggage bags, all my wife’s!) also very clean and comfortable. Housekeeping did a commendable job. Got all the simple ammenities, i.e...coffee, toiletries, extra towels. Every member of staff which I came into contact with were very friendly and polite. Reception and concierge service was fantastic, gave me tips about finding restuarants and broadway shows. We didn’t eat inside the hotel’s resturant, as we wanted to explore the city, but across the street on W 56, there’s a great place for breakfast...Teleon cafe. Breakfast for 2 for under $10. Times Square, Central Park & Broadway are literally 2 minutes from the hotel, 5th Avenue and Rockefeller Centre where about 5 mins from the hotel. All-in-all for first time NY visitors I was very pleased that I booked this hotel. At first I wasn’t too sure but I will surely book this hotel when-ever me and my wife visit NY again! 
For meals, trying eating out. Expecially when visting in the spring, as most deli’s and resturants are open early and close very late. Also to get in all of NY sites, try walking from your hotel. Many of the top attractions are within Midtown, around the hotel and 7th Avenue. For the very fit, walk straight down 7th Avenue, past Times Square and you will first come to Macy’s then MSG (Madison Square Garden) and then finally Ground Zero. This takes about 30 mins but its worth it!

title: “Great Location - Exactly What We Hoped For In A Hotel”
text:
If you are looking for a luxurious setting or rooms, not really the place for you. However, if you are looking for a centrally located "decent" hotel, with friendly staff, this is definitely the place.
Located 1 block away from Penn. Station (and therefore super convenient if arriving by train), this hotel is a fairly easy walk away from Central Park (1 mile north), the High Line Elevated Park (1/2 mile to the West), or Chelsea (1 mile south), as well as many other locations.
We were slightly dismayed on arrival, because: (a) the check-in line was a bit lengthy; and (b) the main elevators weren't working. However, we were upgraded (to a balcony room) just by asking nicely (balcony = absolutely worth it, even if paying!). And, the hotel staff worked very hard to direct folks to service elevators (this was only temporary and the problem was fixed within 1 hour) and were very polite and extremely apologetic about the (slight) inconvenience.
Rooms were a bit on the small side, but were always promptly cleaned and furnished with new towels.
While not really the highlight of the trip (hotel really isn't the point of visiting NYC, is it?), it was the perfect background for the trip. That is, we never experienced any really problems with the hotel, so we were free to enjoy our weekend. As far as I'm concerned, we got exactly what we hoped for in the New Yorker hotel.

title: “Free Upgrade - charged on check out ??”
text: I booked through Expedia (via TripAdvisor) for a standard room. I emailed the hotel directly afterwards requesting a room on a high floor if possible. I was surprising my fiance as we got engaged at christmas and he had never been to New York. They emailed me to say that they had upgraded us to a Park View which was very nice of them. When we arrived they charged us for the upgrade. Location of hotel was superb, very close to a number of subway stations. Roof pool was nice - had it to ourselves. No jacuzzi though and the sauna was down at the health club - gravity. Minibar could not be used as a fridge and we were told 'if we moved ANYTHING we would get charged as it was on a sensor device' No coffee making facilities. EVen a basic B&B in Ireland has tea/coffee making facilities. We loved New York - had a ball, found everyone to be very friendly, the staff were not as warm as everyone else, then again they probably looked at us and said ' leisure market'. Internet access was free but when we checked the price on the webtv it was charged ? It did not tell us it was free? Have stayed on business in a number of other Meridiens, Brussels, Barcelona, London, Dublin but not really sure if they are worth it.

title: “A delight as always.”
text:
I 've stayed at 6 Columbus before, and there is a reason why I come back. Friendly staff, clean and neat rooms, newspapers at the door, quick roomservice and not to forget; the location. With it's perfect spot on the south-western corner of Central Park there is a short way to engaging scenery such as the park, Times Square, Upper West Side, an the subway just across the street.
The hotel is by noe means a cheap B&B, but by my opinion you get what you pay for; a chic-boutique style hotel.
I have already booked my next stay here, and I am looking forward to come back!

title: “Home Pod Home”
text: This is a great little hotel, very conveniently located for both business and pleasure, very clean, affordable (by new york standards!) and stylish in an understated, functional way. I LOVED all the clever storage units (think IKEA but a little more sturdy), the furniture in the room, and the flat screen TV. It was a little noisy at times--especially when some (I'm guessing drunk) twenty-somethings were partying in the hallway one night...come ON you're in the big apple! Get out and do something instead of bothering your hotel neighbors!--but it was actually much more quiet than I thought it would be after reading the other reviews on this site. The customer service was great, very friendly and helpful staff, and it's a safe neighborhood with lots of restaurants, delis, and more upscale spots that are still somewhat affordable nearby. The free wifi was also excellent, as I was in town on business and needed to get some work done. I had a single/twin room and yes it's small, but really when you're in new york city are you really gonna be in your room all that much?

title: “Recent stay at DIA Baymont”
text: Not a bad place to stay. Two major problems. The pillows are the most uncomfortable I have ever experienced. Heard guests talking about it at breakfast the next morning, so I knew I wasn't the only one. Also, the staff isn't on the ball. Tried to print out my boarding pass and ended up spending 5 minutes cleaning up the printer log jam only to find out that the printer didn't work with the terminal I was using - although the printer control panel indicated that it was functional. The desk staff was right behind me at the front desk and never said a word until I asked them what as wrong with the printer. I stuck a note on the computer screen so the next person wouldn't suffer frustration as I had.

title: “Some nice things, but don't plan to sleep or get accurate bill!”
text: Well, the staff were nice and the gym/pool/spa were in good order. But don't plan to sleep here. The room next door was under construction during the day, and at night, the awful floral stench in the room combined with a high pitched whine/whistle coming from around the doorframe due to air pressure in the hallway was so loud it kept me awake all night. This, combined with an extra charge for internet use in my room when I didn't ask for it nor did I use it, made for a terrible experience. No coffee service in room--and none to be found anywhere in the hotel, at least not where I could find it. I was told they would send me an invoice via e-mail--yet I didn't get it and had to call the next day only to discover the excessive charge which I am disputing. Also no rubber mat for the tub--and I slipped and banged my shin but good. Their restaurant advertised a "breakfast to go" feature--but when I called, the person on the phone never heard of it. Overall, visit this hotel if you want to look "hip" in their bar--but stay and sleep at a better hotel where your comfort is assured over their yen for "hipness".

title: “A gorgeous new hotel let down by some Fawlty service”
text:
We stayed at the Cooper Square Hotel for a few nights in November. Like many in NYC that weekend we were there because of the marathon, to support our son and his colleagues who were all running. There was a buzz in NYC that whole weekend, a great experience to be there. The guy at JFK passport control told us that 40% of the people entering that day were there for the NY Marathon. Wow! 
Overall we loved The Cooper Square. We had a room on the 19th floor with a spectacular view over adjacent rooftops. One entire wall of the room was glazed. We didn't need to turn on the TV, the view out the window was far more interesting. The room, which we termed 19th Nervous Breakdown, was not at all large but it was the norm by contemporary NYC hotel standards. The bathroom was gorgeous, small but beautifully well planned and fitted. I defy anyone not to be able to sleep in that large comfortable, firm bed having walked the mean streets of NYC.
The lounge area on the ground floor was cosy and comfortable and the hotel generally worked seamlessly with a very informal check in and check out. This hotel has one really exceptionally nice touch and that is that there is no formal reception desk, just a small room off the lounge with a human being and a laptop. This creates a nice, informal atmosphere. Well done Cooper Square! What a difference to the oh so formal hotel reception desks of yore which resembled train station ticket booths.
Cooper Square also has a gorgeous bar with atmosphere. If you haven't tried warm olives put that right here! They sure do make a glass of wine go down much more easily...
One criticism however...They have a really nice dining room and we had breakfast there on two days. The breakfast is nothing to get excited about, only adequate and certainly not cheap. But when one of our party asked for her croissant to be warmed, her request was met with a huff and shrug by the waitress who obviously had far better things to do than accomodate a request from one of her guests. BTW, a guest is someone who comes to stay with you. Maybe she was an actress from New York's Stanislavsky School preparing for a stage version of Fawlty Towers? If so, she's got the part! 
Fortuitously, I ran into one of the hotel managers in the lift (oops elevator) and brought this Fawlty lapse to his attention. He seemed decidely disinterested. I would have thought that constructive feedback from a generally very satisfied guest about a team member who is letting the side down would have been welcome but sadly that was not the impression I got. I certainly heard no more from him.
Overall, a gorgeous, newly constructed hotel in a great part of town within walking distance of Soho with nice rooms, lounge and bar. Let down by an only OK breakfast and some Fawlty service.

title: “Location, Location, Location!”
text:
Location: less than 1/2 block from Beale Street but just enough to be away from the heavy traffic...PERFECT location. Directly across the street from the FedEx Forum. We'd stay here again just for the location...felt very safe too. 
Rooms: decent sized room and bathroom. Standard modern Westin decor but carpeting in rooms need updating (we had two rooms and both carpets seen better days). Air conditioning was "weak" in one of our rooms but cranking in the other (we did not have time to report to hotel).
Staff: very helpful and pleasant. I actually left my purse in the restaurant and it was returned to me with all the cash and credit cards within minutes. Thanks Michael! 
Price: a bit steep for the age and area in my opinion ($300 after taxes with $30 breakfast credit per room plus extra $30 for overnight valet parking).
Overall, would definitely stay again due to the location.

title: “Great hotel in a great location”
text:
We stayed here for five nights and were very happy with our stay. We got a great deal with an upgraded room (with a wonderful view of the Washington Monument) and free breakfast buffets. The room was spacious and came with a fridge...and a very comfortable king bed that was much appreciated after long days of sightseeing! The staff was friendly from check-in through check-out. The hotel is located right above a Metro stop (Green, Yellow, Blue & Orange lines, with just two stops from the transfer to the Red line), so all the sights are easily accessible. The only thing that was disappointing was the lack of food options in the area...although that will be soon remedied with the completion of major renovations to the food court in the office building just below the lobby.
We highly recommend this hotel to anyone who is visiting DC, for business or pleasure!

title: “Extremly awfull customer service”
text:
I stayed in this dump with my parents, when we made the
Check in the clerk desk employee was extremly rude , my mother asked this guy for a first floor room and he said NO in a very disrespectufull way , then the ice machine did not work, the hotel smelled awfull . I would recomend every one to stay away from this crapy hotel

title: “Exceptional service in a first class environment (albeit don't expect much from the tiny pool).”
text: I've been going to this property since it opened some 20 years ago. (Unfortunately, while the rest of the hotel shines with what one expects from a luxury Four Seasons, the tiny pool area remains from Day One and it can get painfully crowded -- not at all conducive to a relaxing five-star experience. Hopefully, they'll replace it.) The entire staff is exemplary. They truly understand what service is. And the legendary Sunday Brunch continues to be the best around.

title: “Excellent Stay right on the the Magnificient Mile”
text: The hotel upgraded unsolicited my reservation to a King suite upon arrival. The design, decor and comfort of the room are top notch: hardwood floors, marble bathroom, full size bath tub, rain shower. I have never experienced having a TV broadcast on the mirror of my bathroom! Beds are really comfortable and so are the couch in the sitting room. The staff was very friendly and professional. We received a welcome signature cookie from our room attendant just as we were settling in in our room. The Hotel is located just a block away from Michigan avenue and there is a Garrett pop corn just before you get on the Mile :). We have found our hotel in Chicago for all future visits!

title: “first time visit to Baltimore”
text:
just spent the weekend
Everything about this hotel was great
From the friendly staff to the large comfy rooms We also enjoyed the great view of the inner harbor while eating breakfast at the 5th floor restaurant ...
You can not beat the location.
Steps to the inner harbor and minuites to camden yards
we got a resl great price on our room, by using price line.
We plan to visit again next year to see a Yankee game

title: “Great, We liked it”
text: This hotel was great. The rooms were clean, the beds were comfortable, and the staff was friendly. We had no problems whatsoever. I would defiantly stay here again.

title: “Great Location”
text: Having stayed at quite a few types of hotels in SF in the past, the Hilton in Union Square was the first chain hotel that we have stayed in because of travel points. The location is perfect with easy access to everything and the rooms are standard & comfortable for a hotel chain (the boutique & small "mom & pop" places we've been in have been TINY). The elevators were super fast which was pretty key because we were up on the 19th floor. The continental & buffet breakfast items were not great, just ok, but the servers were very nice and attentive. All of the staff, from reservations to housekeeping, were very nice and accommodating. Just a couple of recommendations - ask for Tower 2 because these rooms have been renovated and pay to park across the street instead of using hotel parking. It was about $10 cheaper per day with in & out privileges and much easier to walk across the street then deal with the hotel parking. Also, there's a Starbucks inside the hotel but it always had a line of 15+ in it - go down 1/2 block to the other Starbucks and it'll be much faster. Overall, our experience was good.

title: “Clean, comfortable and totally adequate”
text:
Homewood Suites Liberty Station were well located for the start of our holiday given that they are so close to the airport and the hotel will arrange a free shuttle for you (call hotel upon arrival at the airport). The location is not so great in terms of reaching attractions (certainly not on foot), but there are amenities such as basic restaurants in the immediate area. We used local buses to reach attractions and the bus stops are easily reachable from the hotel, but the buses are not especially reliable (obviously not the hotel's fault, but worth considering).
We were upgraded from a one bedroom suite to a two bedroom suite, which sounded superfluous to our needs, but was actually a lovely plus because, after travelling from the UK, out jet lag meant we woke up at funny times so it was great to be able to retreat into the extra space at 6 in the morning when the other person was still asleep :-)
Everything was pretty clean but basic. The beds were not uncomfortable but not super comfy either. The air conditioning worked, but not very well. The full kitchen in the room was great - especially the full size fridge freezer.
There was no shower gel provided which we found very odd. We enquired with reception and they said they had found some and would get it to us, but when it arrived it turned out to be hair styling gel... so we got a bit lost in translation! Had to remember after that that in the US they always call it body wash and not shower gel!
Breakfast was fine - again very basic, but a helpful addition to our stay. 
We didn't have time to use the pool so I can't comment on that, but the grounds of the hotel are quite pleasant.
We didn't experience much in the way of service, but hotel staff were pleasant and friendly. I guess Homewood Suites are more like apartments rather than a hotel so you don't get hotel style service.
We booked with hilton points, but I think you can get some good deal at this hotel so for the right price I would recommend it, especially if space and self catering facilities are a priority for you.

title: “A "Gem" in Hollywood”
text: What a Blessing this Hotel was. Bailey and all the rest of the Staff were excellent in customer service, area knowldge and all smiled while they did their jobs. The Hotel is just a 1.5 blocks from Hollywood and Highland which is right in the middle of the Walk of Fame. After fighting traffic all day to get there we were so glad to pull in and escape the Hollywood/LA scene. Rooms are oversized and quite. Breakfast is served on 4th floor so you don't have all the Lobby business and bustle going on around you. Brekafast was more than just your typical HIE cinnamon rolls and eggs. The Ladies upstairs took care of the food like they were serving their family a Holiday meal. I want to go back to LA just to stay at this Hotel and maybe take a Studio Tour, which we did not do this trip. 20.00 Dollar a day for parking sounded steep but was worth it for the convenience.

title: “Great Hotel for the Price”
text: Traveling to downtown Boston for the first time. Had made a updated online reservation with another hotel who lost the new reservation and we were forced to find another place to stay. The original hotel recommended the Courtyard by Mariott. The Courtyard's price was over $100 less and the rooms were a nice. The only problem that I noticed was that the water pressure in our room was extremly low. Otherwise, I would recommend this hotel over more expensive hotels in downtown Boston.

title: “Beautiful and spacious room”
text: I stayed in room 316 and could not have been more satisfied by my room or my stay at Hotel George. I expected a small room since the hotel is in a city, but I had plenty of room even though I didn't stay in a suite. The room was also beautifully decorated and I really appreciated the fact that the tv was hidden behind a cabinet that you can pull open. Also--the room had a dvd player! I only wish I had known this ahead of time so I could have brought my yoga dvd. The bathroom was just as aesthetically-pleasing, with a deep, full tub and separate shower stall. Finally, the windows in the room opened--something I always value so that some fresh air can circulate around the room. Thanks, Kimpton!

title: “good value on Priceline”
text: my third stay here and all via Priceline. The most recent winning bid was $58 per night two nights. Valet parked because it was most convient. No mention of Priceline during checkin and it was rather fast. Assigned a double non smoking, asked for a king non smoking and that's what I got, away from the elevators. No use of the facilities, except valet and they were rather prompted. Still a small problem was the bathroom toilet, the seat did not fit under the counter, making putting up the seat impossible. Last time, it fit under the counter and I felt the counter every time, like a stick up man robbing me. I think I robbed them with the price.

title: “Great Location & Amenities”
text: Marriott always seems to get it right. Consistent quality and service whether I travel for business or pleasure. This was a pleasure visit. Love their snack area 24/7 in case you come in late or leave really early. I was there for a horse show and our hours were insane so great to grab a bottle of water, snack, etc. at midnight if I was too tired to go out. Great rooms. We were upgraded to a suite as we travel and stay at Marriott's a lot. Can't get better than this. Also, a restaurant the next property over (good for breakfast if you can handled the cranky woman in the morning)...close to lots of good restaurants as well. Close to Westworld!!

title: “Disappointing visit at a beautiful boutique hotel...”
text: We were so excited to come down to Boston to visit family and stay at this hotel. First off I must say that other than the room service people, the customer service was excellent. We had several issues and they promptly responded to our issues including the professional operations manager who was quite helpful. Our main complaint was the bathroom was not cleaned properly. I wont go into details, but for over $350.00 for our 2 bedroom suite...it should be clean! When we ordered room service, the person was very unprofessional. I called room service and they answered promptly and asked me to hold....for 2 minutes....why didn't he just let the phone ring for awhile if he wasn't able to help me? ANd, he just plopped the phone down instead of putting me on hold. I said I wanted the bread basket and asked what kind of pastries they had. He said "I don't know, I will check" and plopped the phone down again for 2 minutes. I finished my order. Ten minutes later, he calls to say that they don't have any pastries..........ok...I said. What do you have? He said, "I don't Know....let me check".......lol...........smart guy.....He comes back to the phone and says "we have muffins"....what kind I said............I'll check he says"........lol... He comes back and says "we have chocoate, bluberry and cranberry" I said I will have one of each. Well, what shows up at the door is cinammon, banana and blueberry. Also, our windows were so filthy we could hardly see out them which is kind of disappointing considering we were in Boston and wanted to look out the window! The bar was wonderful though. They had a wonderful staff and the drinks and bar food were great with fabulous ambience overlooking the street. They even have outdoor couches which we loved. The Manager appologized for the issues we had a gave us a good discount off our room service and hotel costs. So for that we were very thankful. Which is why we gave it 3 stars instead of 1. If they clean the bathrooms and windows better and educate their room service personnel, this will be a first rate boutique hotel.

title: “Wonderful Hotel!”
text: Every aspect of our stay at the Morgans was great! When we arrived, we checked our bags and relaxed in the Living Room before heading out to see the sights. After a long day of walking around New York, we checked in and were greeted with an upgrade to a suite!!!! Our room was very comfortable and clean - NO bed bugs!!! :-) We loved the decor of the room, as well as the comfortable bed. The shower was also exceptional. The complimentary continental breakfast was the perfect ending to a perfect weekend!

title: “beware of the size of the rooms”
text:
My wife and I stayed here for 5 nights in August and it was our first time in NYand were looking forward to staying here based on previous reviews we had read. We arrived about 3 and our room was ready. Our first impressions when we walked into the hotel was good as it appeared lively and trendy with a retro feel. Our good first impressions were abruptly sunk when we entered our room....we were not impressed....it was tiny! 
We were in NY for 5 nights as part of a 18 night trip to the states and we had 2 large cases and a 3rd smaller hand luggage size case.We literally had nowhere to put the cases so went down to reception to complain and see if we could get another room. We were informed that we had booked a mini room which sleeps 2 people (probably 2 kids in my opinion) and if we wanted a bigger room it would cost us $60 plus tax a night. The girl on the front desk was not understanding in anyway as I asked her how we could feasibly live in this room with our suitcases in the middle of the floor with no free floor space left to manouvre around the room. Her reply was to pay the extra and that was it.
The room itself looked more like a student room in a university campus, it had a unecessary large desk which took up most of the space not occupied by the small double bed. The bed was nowhere near big enough for 2 adults and there was 10 inches of clearence around the foot of the bed and side next to the window. My wife chose to sleep at that side as she had a better chance of actually not getting stuck while getting up to use the bathroom. Also in her way was a 10inch rail protruding from the wall for hanging your clothes on....we managed to get 2 items each hanging on this and that was all the hanging space....pathetic! After she manages to get out of the bed and avoid getting an metal rail in the face, she has to negotiate the wall mounted t.v. which is on a movable arm and protrudes over the corner of the bed at shoulder height...didn't realise the obstacle course was part of the deal!
The bathroom was ok nothing special and the shower had a curtain which had seen better days and made the bathroom look like something you would see in a run down public swimming pool. On the website the rooms look fabulous and very retro with smeg fullsize fridges and decks for playing vinyl records on with cool wall art....I don't doubt that they have those rooms but the websites are not explicitly clear about what type of room they are and what room you are booking and paying for. I can honestly say that we payed a sustantial amount of money for this hotel and actually went above our budget based on the photos and reviews, but was left bitterly dissapointed and it actually put a downer on our visit to NY as my wife wanted to spend as much time out of the room as possible. 
The only good thing to say was that we had a great view of the Empire State building from our window but because it is so close it is hard not to have a great view of it.
In summary it is a cool hotel for young people but the room we stayed in was just larger than the prison cells that we saw in alcatraz and is only functional for someone who travels light with hardly any luggage. I would not recommend this hotel for any of my friends as for the money they could get something much nicer.

title: “Sensational”
text:
Hotels around the world may have forgotten the basis of a good stay . . . . a comfortable bed. The Muse has wonderful, comfortable, luxurious beds. A perfect night's sleep in the Big Apple makes this THE place to stay.
We stayed visited New York to celebrate a 40th birthday and we could not have chosen better.
Friendly staff. Elegant hotel. Wonderful night's sleep. Fantastic location.
Would recommend highly.

title: “Bad area of town”
text: This was a budget hotel in all respects.No clock in the room,or coffeemaker.Was next to a junkyard.Its very industrial,near strip clubs and hookers.i wouldnt stay there again. The breakfast was bear bones. The shuttle was fine.

title: “very nice location just not impressed with the room”
text: We were in town for the Indy 500 so the hotel was full. Check in went well. Went to our room which was hot. So we adjusted the thermostat and left for an hour. It still was hot. The engineer came very promptly to address the issue. He moved us to another room 2 doors down. Unfortunantly it was not really any better. So they brought us a box fan which helped a bunch. I just dont think this should be the way a Hyatt is....... beyond the air problem we did enjoy the pool and fitness room. both were nice and well maintained.

title: “Excellent Hotel & Great Staff”
text: Stayed for 2 nights on a recent business trip to the Denver area and highly recommend this hotel. The hotel is new, clean and the staff is great. The early breakfast, evening cookies and small lounge for a night cap with colleagues (not to mention the great bar tender) will keep me coming back on future trips through Denver International.

title: “Great Hotel”
text:
Lovely hotel and great location.
I can recomend this hotel, the location is great for all tourist attractions and the airport.
Very friendly staff and worth every penny.

title: “Nice enough”
text: We stayed at this hotel for six nights. It is outdated, however our room was very clean and comfortable. The bathroom needs much better lighting. However, our room was on the 14th floor (the hotel only uses 11-15), and we had a panoramic view over the Potomac. I doubt I would have been able to afford that view at another hotel. It is close to the mall, which was nice. There is a shortage of restaurants in the area. The hotel has a restaurant with good, but expensive food. Good bar in the lobby as well as Starbucks. I found the staff friendly and helpful. I would probably stay there again but for the lack of restaurants in the immediate area.

title: “Probably the best budget-hotel in Manhattan”
text: Mother, father and daughter stayed in the Morningside Inn twice: in july 4 nights in a room with shared bathroom, and again in august in a room with private bathroom. Staff was very, very friendly and helpful. Hotel was clean, rooms had TV, AC, fan, fridge. Shared kitchenette with microwave was very handy. Excellent location near Broadway with everything you need, e.g. restaurants, banks, subway (don't miss the enourmous grocery/delicatesse around the corner!). You might think that the carpet in the hallway is a bit old, but then consider the price! It is everything I ask for a budget hotel.

title: “This hotel was perfect, not one complaint!”
text: The room was spotless, very comfortable bed, friendly staff, unbelievable breakfast..complete with an omelette bar! Great location, within walking distance to train station, museums, nightlife, etc! I work at a small family owned hotel on Cape Cod, MA and I'm very meticulous...this Hyatt exceeded my expectations! Would definitely stay here again!

title: “Mixed feelings this time”
text:
I've loved this hotel since it opened. Stayed here 3-4 times for a night or two. This time, came for almost a week and persuaded friends from L.A. who were also coming to NYC to stay at the City Club. The location can't be beat. The staff are friendly and always helpful. Housekeeping is excellent and thorough.
But.....the bloom is off the rose. There was the elevator that didn't work one day and no one seemed to know why not; then the bathroom door that was off its track and no one could figure out how to get it back, so it required brute force to open and close; then the toilet that needs a new flapper valve so that it closes each time; and room service who decided "you must have an old menu" but wouldn't bring a current one upstairs (!).
I still like this place. I like it a lot. But after the latest visit, I will check out other new places before automatically coming back here. The NYC hotel scene is highly competitive - at current rates, you've got to stay on top of your game! I hope the City Club management can kick it up a notch.

title: “Perfection in every way!”
text:
As a now multiple time guest of this beautiful hotel in trendy SoHo, I can truly say that this place is incredible in all aspects. From the warm and friendly front desk to the wonderful service, The Crosby is a small boutique hotel that is part of the Firmdale hotel group out of London that truly stands out! During our last visit, we arrived quite early and were immediately greeted and told that although my room was not ready, we would be upgraded since the hotel had some open rooms. A nice treat for a regular guest!! Our suitcases were secured and then we were off to explore the great surrounding areas. Visiting Balthazar, a fantastic and very popular french bistro, around the corner for a late breakfast was amazing. We then walked the great streets of SoHo (South of Houston) to just enjoy the sights and sounds of the city. We arrived back to the hotel to be rewarded with an upgrade to a spectacular suite for the evening. The suite was beyond belief and jaw-dropping....impeccable in all ways with enough room to entertain ten or twenty in luxury! Beautiful robes, high end bath materials and superb bedding are all part of the Crosby experience in all rooms! Although we have not eaten in the restaurant, we enjoyed the top-notch lively bar scene. The bar always seems to be hopping! The bartenders are quite imaginative and the atmosphere is cool!
This is a must go to hotel and one that you will not be disappointed in.

title: “Blue Moon, you're a great host”
text: Our family and friends gathered at the Blue Moon while in NYC for a wedding in March. The staff were friendly, the rooms were charming; we had a lovely experience. Thanks, Blue Moon, for helping make a special celebration even more special.

title: “Not worth the money and they humiliated me !”
text: I have just returned from a six week trip to the states , I stayed in hotels which varied from mom and pop outfits through to Days Inns and upwards to Sheratons and Hiltons . This was the most expensive hotel of the trip and I chose it because of the excellent reviews on this site - My initial experience was favourable as the young lady who checked me in was very pleasant and managed to put me in a room with a bath . It went downhill after that . The room was quite small for the price . A major disappointment was the fact that there was no tea/coffee making facilities in the room and this is where the trouble began - I need a cuppa first thing in the morning to get going so on the first morning I opted to go down and have the hotel breakfast rather than get dressed and go out in search of coffee or use the hotel coffee shop - Breakfast was not included in the extortionate price charged for the room . I'm a bit of a free spirit and went down to breakfast barefoot - the man who seated me glanced at my feet and I was aware that he realised I was not wearing shoes but he said nothing . I was seated and told that someone would come over to take my order , whereupon I was supplied with coffee by a waiter who clearly did not understand my British English very well as the waffles I requested never arrived. The rest of the breakfast was a buffet , which was adequate but quite disappointing and ruined by the fact that the restaurant manager chose to come over halfway through my meal and inform me that it was 'against health and safety regulations ' for me to not be wearing shoes ,admittedly they offered to get me some from my room but I was then further interrupted by them telling me that they did not want to go in to my room as I had left the do not disturb sign on the door - overall I felt this was a very embarrassing and humiliating experience and that they only wanted me to put shoes on as I was probably lowering the tone of their establishment - I wonder if I had been wearing my Rolex and jewellery if the attitude would have been different ? I feel at they should not have allowed me to be seated in the first place and if they had had a kettle in the room this would not have happened . I was massively disappointed with this hotel compared with the reviews given.The internet was free but slow , the fitness room was hardly bigger than my room . To be fair ,the location was excellent , the bed was comfortable , the towels large enough for my plus size frame and the toiletries supplied were nice quality but I cannot justify the cost of this hotel and would not recommend it to anyone and I would never stay there again as there are plenty of other hotels in that price point nearby .

title: “Great location, friendly staff, good value”
text:
I didn't think finding accommodation in Los Angeles would be so hard! Since my friend and I weren't travelling with a car, location was very important to us and we wanted to stay somewhere where it would be relatively easy to get around. Transport in LA isn't the best - hard to believe for such a modern city! I came across the Orchid Suites on a website, checked it out on Trip Advisor and it had pretty good reviews, so we booked the last room available for two people - a junior suite. I was expecting it to be small, but it was quite roomy, with two double beds, a kitchenette, a TV, nice bathroom, closet and safe, which came in very handy.
There are many positives about the hotel. They include:
* friendly hotel staff - I think the guy was called Marlo, he always had a friendly smile and was too happy to give advice and tips
* free internet!! which was so handy, it was great being able to check your email in the morning and at night and print out tickets to theme parks
* free continental breakfast every morning - we were so appreciate to have access to cereal, fresh fruit, muffins, bagels, tea, coffee every morning...it was simple but a great way to start the day of sightseeing
* location, location, location! Just a walk to Walk of Fame, Chinese Theatre (which is handy if you want to take a Starline Tour to any of the theme parks, around the city, etc), the metro is just down the street (which is just one stop away from Universal Studios)
* decent sized swimming pool (which we didnt use)
* free parking (which again, we didnt use but was a great option to guests who needed it)
* decent sized rooms - more than enough space to store your suitcases. I was happy to have a decent sized fridge to store drinks and fruit too
One tip if you're visiting LA and staying at the Orchid Suites - check out this website for details of upcoming premieres http://www.seeing-stars.com/Calendar/index.shtml#premieres 
Thanks to that website, I discovered that Angelina Jolie was having her premiere of "Salt" at the Chinese Theatre during our stay and since its just a walk away from the hotel, we was able to watch all the stars walk the red carpet and even had a moment with Angelina and Brad!

title: “Great location but not worth the money!”
text: Challenging time conversing with the front desk manager. If you need a crib you should bring your own . They only have two and they won't reserve one for you! They have a first come first serve rule regarding their cribs. The decor is CHEEZY! We paid over two hundred dollars a night for a QUEEN bed. The bed wasn't comfortable and the pillows were too soft. The room was clean and spacious. Be careful where your room is located. We were right across the street from the Baja Cantina and it was loud. They knew I had a toddler and this is where they put us. I requested a month in advance a quiet location. My request wasn't granted at all! They finally delivered a crib and the blanket inside the crib smelled of urine and body odor. I put it on the floor the next morning for the cleaning service to take it away and they folded it back up and put it on the bed. The sink made a VERY loud gargling sound every time the room above us had their shower on. Upon checkout I mentioned the sink noise and the response I got back was, "you need to jiggle it when you hear that sound." HELLO...I am paying to stay here and I have NO desire to be a plumber or fiddle around with a sink during my stay. I could hear conversations from the adjacent rooms. Overall, this hotel is located in a fantastic area. Decent breakfast with a nice terrace to enjoy the eats. I wouldn't go back or suggest this hotel to anyone I know. Overpriced and very disappointed.

title: “Great value - perfect location”
text: I stayed there for 2 nights and have now found the hotel to return to when on business in New York. The rooms are spacious and very clean, there is free internet and the staff is very helpful, professional and friendly. The location is great, a few steps from the subway at Lexington and 53rd - which takes you everywhere in the city. I will definitely come back. And of course you can reach many of the major sights and shopping in walking distance - not a bad thing either....

title: “Cool Hotel, Bad Bed”
text:
The hotel was very nice. They allowed our dogs to stay for 25$ extra. We were allowed to have our dogs on the patio downstairs while we had dinner from the hotel cafe. The food was very good but overpriced as most hotel cafes are. The staff was very nice and the hotel was also very nice. 
The only negative thing, and perhaps the most important part of the review, the mattress was awful. My wife and I tossed and turned all night. It was impossible to get any sleep.

title: “Wonderful”
text: Got a great offer to that hotel and didn´t think to long about taking that chance! When I got there I even got a complimentary upgrade to the Waldorf Towers and really loved it. Spacious room, wonderful lobby, great central location. Always again, but i doubt to get a similar offer!

title: “Great hotel, great location”
text: Pretty little hotel in the middle of Houston Downtown. Very close to theaters, bars, nightlife. Service was just amazing, lovely people! Room was actually quite big, clean and had a good working air-con (important in June!). No mini-bar though :(

title: “My regular hangout when in San Antonio, TX”
text: I stay here on a regular basis as my employer has an account with this property. Of the six local hotels we are allowed to stay at this one is my favorite. The place isn't perfect but I've had few complaints and these were quickly rectified. Very good staff, good location but not the best neighborhood. Unfortunately, many of my co-workers hanging out around the property often give the place a poor rep. Attentive staff but room cleaning is often spotty. I'll still recommend this property.

title: “Refurbished perfection”
text:
My latest visit to this grande dame hotel allowed me to see first hand how the renovations are coming along. I had a junior suite on one of the revovated floors, and the results are fabulous. Everything brand new, but the old flavor of the hotel still remains. Our room had two very large flat screen tv's, great bath, completely restored woodwork detailing, and a tremendous view of Lake Michigan. All of the old details of the hotel were perfectly restored, allowing none of the old character to be lost. I do not know why anybody would stay any place else other than this place. The Palm Court was absolutely hopping on the weekend with great jazz music and dancing, and the timeless feel and elegance are just so palpable.
They are redoing one floor at a time, so make sure you ask for a room on one of the renovated ones.

title: “One of the best Hilton Hotels”
text:
This is really one of the best Hilton Hotels we have ever stayed at. We have been to this hotel twice now and on both occasions the service was exceptional and the food, excellent. The staff seem extremely well trained and are very knowledgeable and friendly.
We are definitely looking for an excuse to visit Dallas again and pamper ourselves at the Hilton Dallas Lincoln Centre.

title: “really overpriced”
text: We are Canadians who stayed at the Sir Francis Drake Hotel this September and were really disappointed. This is an old hotel badly needing an update. Our room was so small it had only one small computer chair. We asked for another chair and received a metal meeting room chair. I think our view was fabulous but the windows were so dirty we couldn't see the view. The bathtub was slippery and had peeling paint. There were smokers in the adjoining room and smoke poured through the large opening under the door. We blocked the opening with towels. The hotel offered free coffee in the lobby- but only at 6:30a.m.! We paid $421.00 for a tiny room. Luckily we moved to the Sheraton at Fisherman's Wharf for a beautiful room at about half the price. The doorman in the beefeater outfit doesn't justify the outrageous prices charged by this hotel.

title: “Good but ...”
text:
Nice Hotel with room and service perfect for a business trip but boring with almost nothing around that ....
Zero choices in case you just want to have a meal or a drink not in the hotel!
Unless you are desperate for a cheese burger at McDonald

title: “Wonderful hotel!”
text: We stayed here in December 2011 and loved it! Staff is very friendly and so helpful! Rooms were nice and very clean. My only complaint is that the closet was small but that was pretty minor given all the other great things about the hotel. Location is great and the hotel bar and restaurant were very good and reasonable. Would definitely recommend!!

title: “Nice hotel in central location”
text: We chose this hotel becuase we were spending a few days at the zoo, Seaworld, and other sights around San Diego. This hotel was quite central to all of these locations, and was a fine place to crash during an active stay in the area. It is on the highway and you are car dependent if you stay here. The pros: very comfortable beds, clean, good sized room, friendly staff, easy freeway access to get anywhere in San Diego, many restaurants and malls within a few minute drive, nice pool. Cons: high parking fee for unsecured surface parking in front of the hotel, nothing in walking distance, not much charm and nothing unique (cookie cutter business hotel).

title: “Worst staff ever”
text:
She didn't have batteries for the remote tv broken dirty towels before we went to the room several chain smokers outside of our nonsmoking room.ask.to.switch.said we had the last room lied I went to the room and booked another room online 
Maybe she would of been more helpful if she didn't keep the phone in her ears and texting the whole time only coming up to say what she can't do . Last day on san Diego would of liked to had a good nights sleep coming from a great mission beach outing thanks a lot .:....

title: “They had me at "woof"”
text:
Just came back from a weekend stay with our family and dog. We stayed in the summer at both this hotel and also the Hotel Monaco in Baltimore. Both hotels are hip, fun and a beautiful mix of old architecture and new furnishings. But just like a house doesn’t make a home-a wonderful hotel isn’t just about the rooms or décor. It is about the people. Everyone from the doormen,bellhops, front desk, the managers really care about their guests. You feel like they have just welcomed you into their home. What a very strange feeling to get this in a chain hotel- kudos to top management since this doesn’t happen without the right people. 
Also a side note- pop culture and history are creatively combined in this hotel... even Ben Franklin is hip. He greets you atop the entrance and there are three colorful busts of him as you check-in... this hotel has Philly attitude- a very positive detailed and creative one-no wonder why they are the number one place to stay in Philly!

title: “Business travel”
text:
Stayed one night at the Westin Copley. Corporate rate but reasonable by Boston standards. 
Clean, up to date room. Only complaint was lack of plugs at desk area. Many electronics to plug in.
Breakfast at Hotel restaurant was good but pricey as most are. 
Would return on next trip to area.

title: “Overpriced, but very nice.”
text:
My wife and I went to a meeting at the hotel. The meeting facilities were very good, and the audiovisual equipment good. The facilities for this type of meeting are excellent and help to make the meeting successful. 
The lobby is very spacious as are the open areas near the ballrooms. These areas are very attractive, clean and well lit. The hallways of the hotel are also well lit, attractive and clean.
The room was somewhat small, but the size you expect in a large hotel in a metropolitan area. The bathroom was appropriate and the amenities generous. The room and bath were well furnished and clean. The heating and air conditioning system was good, and easily controllable. 
The internet service is pricey, but if you don't need to have it in your room, it is free in the lobby. The screens at the complimentary lobby computers are large, and the way things are programmed makes one comfortable with the system. Your browsing history is completely erased when you sign off. You may also use your laptop in the free computer area by Wi-Fi if you wish.
Our check in was uncomplicated. The check in clerk was very accommodating and the service with our bags was also very good and accommodating. 
Right across the street is an open mall with many dining places and upscale shops. We found a wide choice of dining at very reasonable prices so did not eat at the hotel.
Our experience with this hotel was first class, but you expect that for the price. We were not disappointed in our stay but there are hotels within a block or two for much less money.
Bottom line is that this hotel is definitely a five star hotel, but pricey.

title: “Ideal location, super ambience”
text:
We chose the hotel after lengthy deliberations and many visits to the TA website. We were not disappointed.
The hotel is ideally situated within walking, if you like walking, distance to all the major buildings and museums in central Washington. We even walked to Arlington cemetery (which is across the river) after visiting the Lincoln memorial, although we did take the metro back.
It is a lovely experience, well decorated and furnished. The bed is one of the nicest and most comfortable we have found on our travels. The room was spacious as was the bathroom. I have no complaints. A little pricey perhaps but this is in the heart of the business area. Maybe the price is right and it is me that doesn't usually pay that sort of rate.
My wife felt that the tiles in the shower hadn't been kept up to. To be honest I wouldn't have noticed but she pointed out that, whilst they appeared clean to me, they had a film on that does appear in showers and needs constant attention to keep under control. She is fastidious and I would suggest most wouldn't know what she was talking about.
Three very comfortable nights, restaurants close at hand, metro also but get the legs going and enjoy the visit. We arranged to pick up hire car after our DC visit so as not to incur hire / parking charges for three days / nights that were not necessary.

title: “I thought it was nice!”
text:
I think that this hotel has been remodled. I stayed here for CinEvent in May, and I thought it was a very nice hotel. Certainly not the Ritz, but the rooms were clean and certainly not disgusting as some other reviews posted.
The two negative things: the confusing and broken elevators and the barmaid who was more interested in flirting with a policeman than waiting on customers!

title: “Nice stay”
text: Stayed at the hotel the week between Christmas and New Years.The location is good to the show areas. There is a lot of coffee shops and place to eat near the hotel.

title: “Great but not amazing”
text: I don't have a bad thing to say about the Taj. Fantastic location is the best part. The room was nice, and service good enough...however house keeping knocking on our door after 10pm to offer a turn down service was too much...some people do like the occasional early night! Also heard them still hoovering at this time! Although I don't have anything bad to say, I don't feel it's worth what you pay...we stayed at several other hotels on the same trip which surpasses the Taj.

title: “Went back for a second time”
text: Had a great stay the first time- went back and had the same experience. We have stayed at the hotel two years in a row to watch the browns plays the colts. Perfect location. Not far from lots of restaurants and the stadium is your back door. Nice sized rooms with practically a fully furnished kitchen. My only complaint is that you have to pay to park, but what can you do!

title: “Not to Starwood standards”
text: We booked this hotel through the Starwood Hotels loyalty program, thinking that would guarantee a standard we are familiar with. Not so. Though described as "historic," it has none of the lovely time-worn patina we had expected--it is just tired, shabby and down-at-the-heels. Peeling wallpaper, damaged walls, cracked sink, missing grout and broken tiles in the shower all added up to a less than satisfactory experience. The room was clean enough, I guess, but it needs some updating NOW because the overall feel is one of dinginess. The seat in the one reading chair is long past its best-before date--it felt like you would fall through the bottom. And the television was about the same vintage as the hotel. Its one saving grace was the wonderful location, just a minute's walk to the mag mile. Really disappointed to find this under the Starwood banner.

title: “THE BEST HOTEL BY THE SAN ANTONIO AIRPORT”
text: When my family and I come to San Antonio, this is the only airport hotel that we stay at. This hotel and the JW San Antonio Hill Country are the only two hotels that I will stay at in San Antonio, period. Springhill Suites gives the best service, the cleanest and largest rooms, and it's convenient to everything. There are so many hotels by the airport and Northstar Mall that it can get nerve racking trying to find a great property. Take my advice: this is it!

title: “I Love This Place!”
text:
I found this hotel via my google search of many others in the area. I decided to call and spoke with Kim who was more than helpful in making my decision final to book my 5 day stay with my sister and 14 yr old grandson. We stayed in the King suite on the 2nd floor. Mary and Nicky who were our housekeepers (the most important people) have made this Holiday Inn worth coming back to! I LOVE knowing I am sleeping in a clean bed and can stand in a clean shower. They did not have a hair dryer attached to the wall, but we were by request brought one to us immediately. The kitchen w/ microwave and porta fridge (wish it was full size) just for length of stay, due to left overs from some restaurants we ate at. We made due. You do want to bring your paper plates and plastic wares, etc. if you stay with children. The pull out sofa was not at all comfortable for my grandson, but by request of a roll-a-way bed did the trick. You may want to reserve in advance just in case of availability. This is a newer hotel with a small work-out room 2 treadmills and 2 (I believe are elipticals) sp? off the indoor pool area and outdoor patio. We were told by other patrons that they open the roof for outdoor pool weather. Either way, it was immaculate and plenty of table, chair and lounge comfort. Toweling is shelved also. They have a restaurant with a full length stocked bar open at 3pm., closed at 10:00pm.
The restaurant serves breakfast for a $10.00 extra cost per day. My sister and grandson ate there...I believe opened 7-10 am. They brought me my hot coffee as I readied in the steady stream and perfect temperature of my hot shower. Ahhh! Towels are like new, the commode is in the same room as tub/shower, just outside of that is the beautiful granite counter space for toiletries with sink and dressing area which is protected by two entry ways w/ locked doors if needed, one off hall and one off bedroom. I was disappointed to find out that they don't have in room video gaming (for kids) nor pick of movie rentals available. They do have a variety of cable stations and one movie channel of what is showing for time slot. The young ladies at the front desk...I must add all their names as we dealt with them all and they were like being with my sisters. Friendly, informative and personable! Always a Smile and Hello! Kim, Brittany,Tiffany Ashley Amanda and manager Adrianne in the evening. Oh I do need to mention the custodian, Cornelius is always in sight. We had a family friend visit and left his lunch on the floor after a scare of choking on his gum after swimming and with a dramatically (was me) happy outcome along came Cornelius to the rescue of cleaning up the mess. Whew and yuck! There is a computer room available with complimentary high speed internet and a small shop filled with convenient last minute forgotten needs and variety of munchies and soft drinks. I saw they held a banquet for a wedding on Saturday, looked very nice. They have discount rates $7.00 per day for the YMCA not walking distance w/ young kids, but not far at all w/ car. My grandson needed his Basketball fix on their full court. Nice Place! Restaurants galore!! Anything you have at home they have in that area, many in walking distance. The Shopping Mall is right around the corner. Walking distance and again, everything you have at home and some. Lastly, when I ever hear the term Southern Hospitality again, I will always think of my stay here!!

title: “Loved the Sofitel Lafayette Square”
text: A wonderful weekend at this beautiful hotel. When we entered the hotel we loved the ethos from the very first minute. The staff were so friendly and warm and welcoming they could not do enough to help and assist. We were a party of four (2 double rooms) and we loved our rooms they were so big and the beds were the best we have ever experienced. The location was perfect only minutes away from monuments and parks. It was quiet at the weekend but cafes were close and souvenir shops too. Saturday night was excellent at the hotel bar but Sunday night was obviously the chefs night off and was poor (food). Very relaxing cocktails in the afternoon and a longing to return there soon!

title: “Great way to start a trip”
text:
I live an hour's drive from Boston's Logan Airport (make that two hours with traffic). I try to take this fact into account when making airline reservations for personal trips. But inevitably, I make reservations 10 months in advance to leave at 11:00 a.m. and the airline deletes my flight and rebooks me and my long-suffering spouse for 7:45 a.m. Since getting up at 4:45 a.m. is never my first choice for starting a leisurely vacation, I fire up the computer and make a reservation at the Logan Airport Hilton the night before we leave.
This hotel does a good job of maintaining Hilton quality standards for cleanliness and service. As in all the airport Hiltons that I've patronized, the rooms are small but well-appointed. The soundproofing is excellent such that I've always had a good night's sleep.
This Hilton has an HHonors lounge with a wonderful view of Boston and comfortable seating. The food and drink offerings are not as generous as some HHonors lounges, but it is still possible to consume a serious number of calories!
We used the indoor swimming pool once, but I found it awkward to walk through the lobby in my swimming attire (the only way to get to the pool). This placement was not the greatest design decision the architects ever made.
While the hotel does has a shuttle to the airport, it is possible to walk to at least Terminal C via some enclosed walkways and then through one of the central parking garages. After more than half a dozen stays, we have "cracked the code" and walk each time to our concourse.
We are very comfortable at this hotel and find it's a good way to start a trip the next morning.

title: “Lovely”
text:
Absolutely loved this hotel.
It wasn’t cheap but it really was lovely.
Check in: Very quick and super friendly. Everyone was lovely and wanting to help.
Breakfast: Again not cheap but nice. Not a massive variety but good enough. The one complaint was that pastries were not warm and seemed like they were out for a while.
Room: Lovely, had a clear view of the Hollywood sign. Everything in the room was in great condition, safe, fridge and the most TV channels of any place I have stayed.
Concierge: Was great, an aspiring actor who was very helpful and did a great job. They ordered us a car to go the airport and it ended up being a stretch limo, very happy about that.
Location: Great, right next to the Walk of Fame and a shopping centre and other Touristy things. 
I would definitely go back there again, but it really wasn’t cheap!!!
Tip: Ask for a view of the Hollywood sign and definitely ask for a NON adjourning room. We had people next to us one night and the doors are paper thin, they woke us up constantly with their noise.

title: “Style no Substance”
text:
Staff at check-in were apathetic and not well trained (taking 15 minutes to type in an already-reserved room to the system is not good, esp. for NY). 
Room was very small, even for NYC. Interior quality was dated and in need of a makeover -- furniture shopworn and walls needed painting/papering. A/C system was filthy and began squeaking loudly at 3:30am, waking me up. Bathroom large but had no ventilation execept for window which was difficult to open.
Upon checkout, was told that late departure would cost $25, then charged $75 for a three-hour period!!!! Charge was refunded, but I was not told that charge was PER HOUR! What is this, a flop-house?

title: “There are many better hotels”
text: Stayed one night on a business trip because most everything else was booked. Had a queen room at $199. It was TINY -- barely enough room to walk around the bed, and there was no way two people couild have used that room. Bed was comfortable but the plumbing was noisy all night long. Bathroom was roomy and well lighted -- quite nice. Only one chair, a straight back desk chair. Hi speed internet at $9.95/day. No newspaper in the morning, front desk was courteous but understaffed -- never more than one person on duty to handel checkins/checkouts, andswer phone, etc.

title: “Excellent Courtyard”
text: Very clean hotel and nicely decorated; Very clean room and nicely appointed; Very comfortable bed; Polite and professional staff with attentive service; A very relaxing and comfortable stop after a long day on the road; Our room was very quiet even though this hotel is next to I-10 freeway. Nice courtyard swimming pool area that was fun for the kids (and adults!).

title: “So so for its price”
text: The only reason I gave it an average rating is its location which is near most major landmarks in NYC. We paid more than $500 per night and stayednfor 4 nights and yet... There was no ref, minibar, slippers, bathrobe, coffee or tea making facilities in the room. Most of these things are already standard in 3 or 4 star hotels. To make it even worse, I was being charged by the bell service to store one small bag for an hour while waiting for my car pickup! I know NY is expensive but to make money on storing a guest's bag for an hour??? This is not the Hilton that I know and I have to agree with the 330+ people who rated this hotel as poor or terrible.

title: “This was a glorified Marriott”
text: The service was excellent. The clubroom lounge was very nice. Unfortunately, the rooms resembled a Marriott more than a Ritz. The worst part was the smell of trash near the elevator bank. Next time in Philadelphia, we will stay at the Four Seasons.

title: “Very spacious hotel”
text: The rooms at the Red Lion were extremely spacious. The were very helpful and friendly. The service was excellent and all requests were answered promptly.

title: “liked location”
text: We stayed at the Crowne Plaza for 3 nights on our honeymoon. We paid for an executive room but got a suite which was very large and quiet. The decor was perhaps a little tired and the bath small. The Wi Fi is not free here which was an issue for us.Breakfast is not included but is not expensive, the public areas of the hotel could do with updating. Service was fine. The best thing about the hotel is the location by Union square handy for everywhere. We tried to get in the Mark Hopkins initially and went to the wonderful bar whilst in san francisco, The mark hopkins appeared to be of a higher standard but is up a very steep hill.

title: “Memorable Anniversary Night”
text: The Hotel Teatro went out of their way to make our anniversary a memorable one. An added perk is The Oceanaire restaurant is right across the street, which made for a great night. The hotel staff was friendly and courteous. The hotel was quiet, the room was clean and the bathroom was amazing. Very upscale at an affordable rate. I would reccomend this hotel to my friends! A champagne toast ended our night. What a great memory. Thanks to the staff and the hotel.

title: “Highly Recommended!!!”
text: This was the first time our family stayed downtown Chicago. We usually stay in the suburbs. We did a lot of research prior to selecting this hotel and we were very pleased with our choice. The staff was very friendly and helpful and Ismeta, the breakfast host was outstanding! The rooms were very clean and comfortable and the view out our window was breathtaking and very relaxing. Every night I enjoyed the view and also woke early to watch the sun rise over the buildings. The hotel was very convenient to the orange CTA line (about 4 blocks) and to downtown, numerous restaurants, and attractions. Members of our family with small children enjoyed the nice pool and hot tub. Neat view from the 27th floor where pool is too. The evening reception was a nice way to relax and refreshments were great as was the staff. We arrived before our room was ready and were able to leave our bags (in locked room) and hit the city before we checked in. We stayed 7 nights and will definitely stay again. We had two families which included 4 adults and 4 children ranging from 6 to 17 years old. We have recommended this hotel to several friends planning trips to Chicago. Can't say enough about the staff and hotel!

title: “Ramada Gaslamp”
text: Noisy location on weekends, but convenient distance to everything. Elevators very slow. Rooms are small -- my room had sink outside bathroom, and only stand up shower.

title: “cheap basic accomodation”
text:
Stayed one night after a long flight from the UK.
The shuttle collected us from airport with no difficulty (there was only two of us) and check in went smoothly.
The room was a good size and clean. There was a notice about ants and we did see a couple in the shower but other than that the room was fine.
We did have to climb stairs to get to our room so ask for a ground floor room if this is a problem.
The pool looked nice although we didnt use it, the grounds were very tropical. The area the hotel was in was'nt the most up market.
Breakfast, a bit chaotic and very basic. There is a Dennys next door but we stuck with the free breakfast!
The shuttle also dropped us at our car rental place in the morning which was helpful.

title: “Fantastic 4 night stay”
text:
We've just returned from our New York trip and can not recommend The Eventi enough. We'd booked a corner deluxe suite and when we checked in had already been upgraded to a city view corner, then when we told them it was our Honeymoon upgraded us again to a suite overlooking Empire State Building, we also had complimentary Champagne and cupcakes, plus mini bar credit. Amazing! We were on 8th floor and traffic noise not an issue at all.
Staff are friendly and always helpful, couldn't do enough for us.
Perfect location, only 5 min walk to Macy's and 34th St subway which provides connection to anywhere in the city. Within walking distance of Times Square, Central Park and 5th Ave but after two days of walking everywhere resorted to subway to save our tired tired feet!! 
I only have a couple of cautions
- Do Not buy tickets from street vendors they will rip you off
- Do not bother with The View restaurant in Times Square - ridiculously expensive for poor food which gave my husband food poisoning!
- Be careful in taking Town Car back to airport. Told us would be $75 inc tip but when we arrived at JFK would not take any less than $95. Pay up front before you leave hotel.
We had a fantastic time in NY and would definitely stay t The Eventi again

title: “Convenient, Comfortable and Quaint”
text: The second we walked in the door, we were greeted by friendly hotel workers who immediately got us to our room. Although the room was somewhat small, it is an older hotel and most hotels in NYC have smaller rooms. The bathroom was a good size though, and everything worked just fine. The best parts of the hotel are the unique decor of the lobby, the classy chairs and sofas in the lounge area, and the fun New Yorker cartoons on the wallpaper. Also, the Algonquin is only a few blocks from Times Square, and it was unbelievably quiet! I recommend ordering a drink in the lounge. It's a little expensive, but well worth it! All in all, we had a very comfortable stay and we'd be happy to stay there again!

title: “Nice hotel- cool lifts!”
text:
We stayed here for three nights in a Corner King room. Check in was efficient and easy. The glass lifts are a tourist attraction in their own right! Super-fast and 45 floors high- if you suffer from vertigo or don't like heights, request a low room! 
The room was really spacious, comfortable (especially the huge bed), quiet and clean. The view from the 40th floor at the rear of the hotel is fantastic, overlooking the Hudson river- request a high room when booking if you want a view.
The bathroom was fairly standard but everything worked OK- nice touch to have downlighters under the sink so if you use the bathroom in the night you don't get blinded by the bright lights! There was a hairdryer- although it was not listed in the room amenities. 
The coffee machine was good but only comes with paper cups along with 4 filters of coffee, and all the time we were there we only had two powdered creamer sachets- a minor niggle but would expect a little more for £350 a night!
In-room internet is fairly cheap, fast and easy to set up.
The Broadway lounge is a great place to chill out and they do some wicked cocktails! You may have to wait for a table by the window overlooking Times Square though, but if you ask the waitress they may 'reserve' or 'grab' one for you when it becomes available.
The View restaurant is a must. Not too expensive and the food is out of this world. You must book this in advance though, as there is nearly always a queue of people waiting in the ground floor foyer, where the'check in desk' for the restaurant is. It has it's own express elevator only accessible from the foyer. If you want a seat by the window you should ask for this when you book, otherwise it's a great experience, but without the View! The same goes for the View Lounge, unless you have a reservation you can't just pop in for a cocktail before dinner!
Down sides:
The lifts don't always work at peak time (about 6-6.45 in the evening). You press your floor into the key pad and normally it tells you which elevator to go to (there are a lot) but at peak times it just shows 'xx' and nothing happens. Tip: if you're going down, get into the first elevator that stops on your floor, even if you have to go up to the top to go back down to the lobby.
Also it is expensive- but you pay for the size of the room, the fantastic views and the convenient location.
We found the concierge unhelpful

title: “Was made to feel at home...like a family member.”
text: I spent the entire three days of our visit in the hotel while my husband attended classes at Toyota. Crystal couldn't have done anymore to make our stay more comfortable and accomodating. She was warm and friendly and easy to talk to. She even found me a bite to eat one day for lunch when it was raining and I couldn't walk to get a bite to eat somewhere. She loaned me her umbrella when I went out to dinner that evening with my husband. She did all this and so much more. All the employees I came in contact with were quite friendly but she is the one I interacted with for three days...and was glad she was there. We will be coming back to Jacksonville three more times in the coming months and had originally planned to try three different hotels for the next three visits but I told my husband I prefer staying here. If it ain't broke...why fix it?! :)

title: “Good Choice”
text: The Sofitel is a very nice hotel in a good location for shopping along Michigan Avenue. Staff could not be better. We stayed in a suite, which had a living room, hallway with bathroom, and a bedroom (long and narrow versus feeling expansive, but worked fine). The bathroom has a separate shower and tub. Doors to shower and toilet were clear, meaning that unless you don't care at all about your privacy, only one person can use the bathroom at a time despite the fact that it is quite large. My other minor complaint is that it has a mini-bar but no fridge. Would have been nice not to have to remove extremely overpriced cans of beer in order to keep anything of ours cold. Very convenient to food: Tempo Cafe just down the street - fabulous for breakfast and easy for takeout instead of waiting for a table. A nice takeout place; a small grocery and a Walgreens also very near.

title: “We had one of the nicest stays ever”
text: The General Manager, Amy, and her entire staff were incredible! They even had a bottle of champagne waiting in their rooftop garden for us. Room service was fantastic and they were unbelievably fast.

title: “Would have rathered stayed at Motel 6”
text:
Well it all started when trying to get checked in and it was pretty much the same from there on out. I get it, they are trying to be trendy, but after a long flight and day of traveling I just want to get to my room and relax. Upon walking into the lobby on a Wednesday evening, all I could here was obnoxiously loud house music coming from the bar just down the stairs.
