It was hard conversing at the front desk trying to get checked in, the young man working didn't seem to care if I stayed at their hotel or not.
The room was ok, nothing special. You could tell a lot of time was spent to make sure everything was in its place, but you had the feeling that if housekeeping had to vacuum they would charge you for it. Turned out to be pretty much true, random charges for the in room mini bar(that I never touched), $.75/day for a newspaper I didn't want. The room and bathroom were pretty poorly lit. I'm surprised I was not charged for using the soap and shampoo.
The customer service was the same at the front desk throughout my stay as the first night I checked in. I'm sorry the conference I was attending happened to be stationed in the hotel(the only reason I stayed there). This place has great potential, but to be honest I've been to Motel 6's with better class.

title: “Great place to stay!”
text:
The customer service at this hotel is beyond excellent! The breakfast bar was terrific. The value, compared to nearby hotels, was great. 
There were a couple problems with our room, however: 
 The A/C unit was mounted high on the wall above the door to the bathroom, almost directly over one of the two queen beds. This created a chilling problem for the people sleeping in that bed. 
 The bathroom door also hit the side of one of the beds and would not fully open. A king-size bed would be better for the room.

title: “Pleasantly surprised..loved it”
text: Having read a view negative reviews, we were pleasantly surprised & loved our stay here. Assigned to this hotel while in town attending the NCAA women's basketball tournament, and so read reviews before arriving. We ended up on the 11th floor and yes, faced railroad tracks, but slept soundly at night & expect some noise while staying in any downtown hotel (chicago area hotels much worse with sirens, etc); hotel is within walking distance of many museums (6th Floor Museum, the great Dallas Aquariam, the West End restaurant area); and when we got tired from walking, can walk underground to Union Station & for $4.00 for a day pass, could take the DART system trains anywhere. Easy to get to the Dallas zoo using the train system. When coming back to hotel late Sun evening, restaurant and bar staffs on 2nd level very accomodating to the large groups coming back for a late meal after our game. Front desk & concierge staff always helpful.. we did get a great group rate which we appreciated and so overall, happier there than we thought we'd be after reading other reviews. If we ge the opportunity to return to Dallas would definitely check this hotel out again. (oh & received complimentary internet service in our rooms which was greatly appreciated just for checking attractions, etc..thank you)

title: “Terrible Room”
text:
I just stayed in this hotel on a business trip. The room was in a terrible shape. The carpet was heavily stained; there was a hole in the wall; the walls, window sills, molding were dusty, and there was mold growing around the vent in the ceiling.
I got into the room so late, that I just went straight to bed and decided to call to change rooms in the morning. I had an early breakfast with 3 other people, with rooms in similar conditions. Two had try to change rooms unsuccessfully. Since I was just staying for two nights, I didn't try.
Needless to say NONE of us will stay here again (we all went back to our companies and sent out email warning others to avoid this hotel and notified (in group) the company organizing the event we were attending - however, their staff was staying here and had the same experience so they already knew!).
I was upset with myself for not checking TripAdvisor to see how this hotel was rated. Now, I guess it wouldn't have mattered since there were so many postive ratings, I would have stayed in this hotel.

title: “It was going well until....”
text:
I spent there the night of my birthday. 
The hotel was in an excellent location, it's in walking distance to the Boston Common building and the park. The room was cosy and the bed super comfy. I was extremely happy as I was travelling from Chicago to Boston and I honestly wanted to relax in a nice hotel. I checked out the following morning regenerated and ready to face my whales watching tour that I planned for my birthday... 
the disappointing about the Back Bay experience was simply that my partner from England got in touch with the Back Bay Hotel to deliver me a birthday message with a surprise (a room service) for my birthday that I simply didn't get... and finally I had to handle my disappointed partner who was expecting a thank you message or something... for the surprise... Honestly... Birthday was simply spoiled because of the inefficiency of the Back Bay hotel concierge. PS. They had my details as well and I was honestly hoping for an apology... which of course I never received. Sorry guys, this is definitely not 5 or 4 stars service to me!
Do you have swimming pool and SPA? Lol If I only was told about it when I checked in... I might have been able to rate it!

title: “Great Location”
text:
I was in town attending a convention and booked this hotel through the convention's website. I looked at TripAdvisor reviews and I was a little apprehensive about what to expect.
I have to say that I was very pleased with my stay at this hotel. I split a room with a colleague and the room was very spacious. THe little balcony was a great way to get some fresh air. 
The bathroom and room was very clean.
We ordered room service one night and the food and service was very good.
We loved THE LOCATION...right beside the convention center, walking distance to Alamo, mall, shops, restaurants, nightlife, You name it! 
There is a fabulous Irish Pub called Durty Nelly's that is down on the riverwalk and attached to the hotel. Highly recommended for a real "pub" feel complete with peanut shells on the floor, piano player, and bar crowd that sings along to the tunes streaming from his keys. 
Also, Bark at the MOon dueling piano bar on the Riverwalk was another fun spot within walking distance.
Hit up the Lone star cafe for the BEST chicken fried steak. Very reasonable.
I have no complaints about the hotel. They even split the bill for us which was very convienient. 
We took a shuttle from the airport that cost $32 ROUNDTRIP...cheaper than a taxi which would run you around that for one way.

title: “A disappointing place”
text: We had an awful experience here. The front desk checked us in under a different person's name and then sent us to the wrong room. We got a call at about 9:00 in the evening when the real person showed up, yet I still had to make two trips to the front desk to make sure that I was not being charged for the other person's room--which had originally happened. The hotel is in disarray with dirty carpets and exposed wiring in the hallways. I would not recommend this place to anyone. I can say that after my initial email complaint to Doubletree, I was refunded one night's stay for my troubles, but all in all, I would not recommend this place again, partly due to the awful condition of the facility.

title: “Good service, nice clean rooms”
text: I was very pleased with my stay at this hotel. Rooms were nicely decorated and clean. Faye at the front reception was very helpful. Breakfast spread was one of the better ones For a hotel of it's category. Location was convenient enough, and takes about 10 minutes to downtown.

title: “Great price great hotel”
text: Close to georgetown. The only negative is the parking. You are forced to pay $30 for valet. Also they have limited tv channels. Bring something to do if you plan on staying in hotel for awhile. And don't forget anything in your car. Valet is not on site. We had express check in. hot cookies. Clean rooms. Full kitchen. Crabtree evelyn toiletries. 24Hr fitness center and business center. Will stay here again for $120 in dc.

title: “Great Bargain at a very central location”
text:
Spent a long weekend here in a triple room with my boyfriend, his sister and their mutual friend. Finding affordable triples in NYC is no mean feat. We were glad we landed this place.
The front desk staff was fabulously friendly, even helped us play practical jokes on one another.
The decor was gloriously cheesy in an over the top "Big Lots" special sort of way, but well-maintained and the room was very clean and HUGE by NYC budget hotel standards.
The bathroom was gigantic (could have slept 3 more people), very clean, if a little short on towels and towel hooks, so the place looked like a bit of a laundry when all four of us were done showering. However, the water pressure was great, and the room/towels clean and fresh.
No view, other than the fire escape and air conditioner, but there was a large safe and a small fridge for those so concerned.
Huge television, but the most amusing entertainment came from the couple staying next door. Although we had the constant humming of the air system to cover the sounds of traffic, the walls are rather thin, and the headboards line up on the connecting walls. Must have been their honeymoon next door. Amazing...

title: “Great Hotel!”
text: I recently stayed at the Hotel Palomar for business and I was pleasantly surprised by the experience as I've never stayed at a Kimpton before. The rooms are decorated very nicely and the bed is super comfy. I loved the bathrobe and the toiletries provided. The staff when checking in was incredibly efficient and even gave me free wifi, a mini bar credit and a glass of wine - couldn't have asked for more after a long day of meetings. The location is very central and has proximity to a large number of great restaurants. Only complaint is shortly after check in I got a knock on the door asking who I was by a hotel staff member - not sure what that was about, getting our car in the morning took about 20 minutes and check-out in the morning was also slow - unclear if this was because of staff or other guests.

title: “Very Nice Stay for the Price”
text:
I booked 10 rooms and with the group discount the price beat most other hotels in the area. The room was clean and modern. Nice bathroom although the door didn't close all the way. I had my own room since this was a business trip, but if I was vacationing and sharing a room that door being an inch open would have made me uncomfortable. 
The continental breakfast is ok, cerel, fruit, yogurt, bagels and pastries. If you want eggs or anything you'll have to order it from the menu. 
Wi-Fi connection was good. 
All in all this was a nice hotel for business travelers.

title: “Thanks Priceline for this hotel. It was fantastic!!!”
text: Fantastic hotel in an unbelievable location. We had tickets to Padres game and were able to enter stadium via skywalk on 4th floor of hotel. After the game, simply show your room card and exit stadium to hotel via skywalk. Amenities in room were fantastic, i.e. bedding, view, bathroom robes, etc. Pool / hot tub area was very nice. Staff was extremely friendly. If you sign up for Omni's free Select Guest Program, free wireless internet is included. This hotel was an unbelievable value through Priceline bid for $100/night.

title: “waterside quiet otherwise quite noisy”
text: The massive buildings is a bit difficult to be reached by foot from the downtown. The busy highway and other roads nearby make a noise that is heard in rooms facing them. I was kindly replaced to a quiet room by the waterside facing NJ and the vessels, including one military boat. Staff is helpful. A bit expensive breakfast available downstairs and the nearest Starbucks is about 15 mins walk away. Despite booked through Bookings no King Size bed was available but the room was otherwise convenient, Expensive WiFi available.

title: “Nice Hotel, Cold Pool”
text: My family stayed at the Drury West Houston for one night. We were traveling home after Thanksgiving and this was the only hotel on our route that accepted pets and had an indoor pool, so we booked it. I called the hotel directly was offered a discounted weekend rate on a suite. The hotel was easy to locate from I-10 and there were several restaurants within close driving distance. Everything was very clean and the room was large. Their slogan is the "extras aren't extra" and that was true. The hot breakfast was good, though very crowded. For us the only drawback was that the indoor pool is NOT HEATED- it was freezing. This was a huge disappointment to my kids as it was just too cold to swim. There is a hot tub but it is small and not appropriate for small children anyway. So if you are looking for a nice place with perks on the west side of Houston, I would recommend this hotel, but don't plan on swimming if it's cold outside.

title: “Great Value and Wonderful Staff”
text:
First time staying at this hotel and everything has been GREAT! The staff is very friendly and professional and it feels like home staying here. The free meals are a nice perk and the folks in the kitchen work hard feeding everyone. I’ve been here for three days and will be here another week. I would definitely stay here again anytime my business travel brings me to San Diego. 
There are a lot of nice restaurants in walking distance along with many nice parks and walking trails. This hotel is a hit since you get nice meals in the evening Mon-Tue, free internet, nice rooms, free parking, and just an overall great place to stay. The walls are a little thin but it isn’t a big deal.

title: “Cosy little busy place”
text:
If you're looking for something cost-effective right off Market Street, there's no better place than the Mosser.
The room might be a little small, but the convenience and the cost saving will be worth it.
Be sure to check out the morning coffee and muffins. It's better than the ones they serve at Peet's in my opinion.

title: “A really great place to stay”
text: I have just spent four nights staying at the State Plaza Hotel with my adult daughter. We booked this hotel because of Trip Advisor reviews and we feel that it was a great choice. Our room, which was in the building which fronts F Street, was very large. It included a good-size kitchen (with a cook top only and unfortunately no microwave oven) a lovely bathroom and a dressing room. The windows open, which is essential for me because I need fresh air to be able to sleep. The room was quiet and extremely clean and the beds were very comfortable. I found the retro-design bathroom very attractive. The water pressure from the shower was excellent. I tended to shower at night and had no problems at all with getting hot water. However, my daughter told me that the hot water tended to run out in the mornings. The kitchen facilities were adequate. A microwave oven would have been a very welcome addition, but we managed to heat up soup on the cook top provided. One disadvantage was the lack of wifi in the rooms. There is an internet connection, but I didn't have an appropriate connection cable, so I couldn't use my laptop. A wifi connection is available in the lobby, but it only seemed to work properly in the E Street lobby. We couldn't get it to work in the F Street lobby. We worked around this by going to Starbucks or using the widely available free public wifi available in a number of locations, including the various Smithsonian museums. Hotel staff were very courteous and helpful. We only ate breakfast in the bistro on the last morning of our stay. The buffet selection was adequate, but not impressive. The location was great for us, being within walking distance of the Kennedy Center, the Lincoln Monument and the White House. After staying in New York City with a subway line at each end of the block, having to walk for about seven blocks to get to the Metro was a bit of a shock to the system, but it was really not a problem. Overall, we found the State Plaza to be excellent value for money. We loved our few days in Washington and would love to go back. If we do, we will definitely stay at the State Plaza.

title: “Highly Recommended!”
text: We just got back from NYC and loved the Belvedere. It was extremely clean, updated and close to everything. I read comments about the small bathroom and was preparing for the worst -- but the size wasn't bad at all. It might be cramped it you were to have 4 people, but what hotel wouldn't? We also recommend the Brazialian Cafe on the corner a half a block away -- wonderful!!

title: “Stayed here before and will stay again.”
text: Super location. Large comfortable rooms. Coffee maker, mini frige, microwave, lots of storage. Very friendly and helpful staff.

title: “Great Value”
text: After reading other reviews, we had some concerns, but we had a great time. Not the Hilton, but a great value for travelers who want to spend travel budget monies on something besides the room. The room was clean, seemed recently remodeled, bathroom was beautiful. Complimentary soaps, shampoo, etc, which I did not expect for the price. Complimentary continental breakfast was not much, but saved us time and money. Location was great, on the same corner as subway stop, and only a $4.90 cab ride back from Times Square. Probably walking distance to Times Square for those who like to walk. Front desk staff was friendly, and had our reservation at the quoted price, no suprizes. They were unable to extend check out, but did not kick us out when we were still packing at official check out time. Definately will recommend.

title: “No car needed”
text:
Great location with access to restaurants, Pikes Place Market, and shopping by foot or hotel shuttle. Outstanding yoga studio across plaza with hotel discount. I wish we did not rent a car as parking was expensive and we barely used it. 
Service attentive and friendly. Lobby and rooms very elegant. 
I will be back.

title: “This historic guest house on a quaint cobblestone street adjacent to Morris-Jumel mansion is a hidden gem in NYC!”
text:
A great place to stay if you need something within walking distance of New York Presbyterian Hospital/Columbia Medical School.
Has very large living room/kitchenette/dining area and two bedrooms. Nicely furnished in African motif and kitchen stocked with all essentials. Grocery store adjacent. Very quiet historic street. Never felt unsafe at all here. Easy access to subway. Owner extremely accommodating, pleasant and helpful.

title: “Sub par hotel in a great locale”
text:
55th and 7th Ave. 3 blocks from Central Park south. 2 blocks from Carnegie Hall. A few minutes walk to the Letterman Show...'nuff said. The physical location of The Wellington Hotel is terrific.
Now, for the physical condition of the Wellington: Hit or Miss.
We arrived out front (one way street) and an easy off load. We had an attentive door man. There are 4 or 5 steps up into the lobby. There is no permanent ramp, but I eventally saw a temporary ramp they can slap over the steps.
The lobby was pretty nice. An older style, but what you'd expect of Manhattan in an earlier time (say, 1940's).
We got our room assignment and a bellman. No one could break a $20 for me at the desk, which meant I was going to have to get change from the bellman after he got our stuff to the room. Awkward...A hotel in NYC oughta have some singles and fives on hand.
The elevator was small, so my wife and I went up separately. The bellman would meet us there with the cart and bags.
The hallways were pretty old and oft-painted. We got to the room which overlooked 7th ave. However, the room was tiny. I'd say less than 10' by 10'. We thought we'd booked a room with two beds. (We hadn't). But the bed provided was a double...for the both of us. 
My wife called downstairs as the bellman arrived who waited patiently. As she called to change rooms, I began looking around...the carpet was filthy. I don't mean a spot or two here and there...I mean dirty. As if you had an open bag of Kingsford charcoal and dragged it around. I never got to see the bathroom or closet. Overall, the room looked like a small, college dormitory circa 1925.
Granted, we "only" paid about $150 per night for the place, but cleanliness and bed size is non negotiable at any cost.
The woman at the desk was none too cheerful about it, but we got an immediate room change. She seemed to sneer at the fact that we'd booked the room online via Travelocity. With a room that dirty, she shouldn't sneer at ANYTHING. We had arrived around 5 pm...I wonder if we'd have gotten a new room if we'd come much later.
We went all the way back down to the lobby, got a new set of keys, and went over to a separate set of elevators (apparently a different tower) and went up.
The hallway was somewhat better than the previous, but the room was a pretty decent change. Everything had probably been redecorated in the past 5 years or so. Tan and beige. The room was somewhat bigger and the bed was acceptable (queen).
I got change back from the bellman (ugh) and we unpacked. The closet was an OK size. The bathroom was definitely for one person at a time. Weirdly configured: No mirror directly over the sink, but one over the toilet. The toilet bowl was jammed against the tile wall, so you'd have to sit at a 45* angle when taking care of business. But, it was clean and reasonably new.
There was no view, except of the brick wall across the way. I could barely tell if it was day or night, raining or sunny. No matter...the room was a big improvement in cleanliness, and a decent improvement in size.
The television worked fine, the lights were fine, the carpet was clean. I could walk in bare feet. Not so the first room.
There is no bar or any kind of hangout in the lobby. There is a breakfast place next door, and it is attached to a Greek restaurant if that's your bag. We didnt try either, tho they were both very busy. Immediately outside is a subway stop which we used to great advantage.
I suppose to sum up, the Wellington is an OK deal ($150) if you're trying to save some money, are only travelling with 2 people, max of 3, and want to be near a lot of sights.
I probably won't run back there anytime soon, and would prefer to spend somewhat more on a better place.
If you choose the Wellington, get there early and FIGHT for a good room. There are decent ones and awful ones.

title: “Nice location”
text:
We stayed at the Holiday Inn-Government Center on June 18, 2005 when we went up for a Red Sox game. We got the hotel on Hotwire, so we weren't sure where we would end up but I've had good luck with 3 star hotels on priceline and for $87 a night it was just what were we looking for. I have noticed prices for hotels have increased significantly in Boston over the past two years so this was a good deal. 
The hotel was about 2-3 blocks from Government Center and Fanueil Hall. There are definitely closer hotels, but it was still a nice location and if you don't mind walking a little bit the T stops aren't far. 
The room it self was nice, we were able to check in 2 hours earlier than the stated arrival time and got a King Size bed on the 10th floor, which said it was a "preferred" level but we didn't do anything extra to get that. Probably just that we got there early and it was available. Parking, like everywhere in Boston, was an additional $32 for the day. You can skip the valet and park right in the garage, which is attached to the hotel and there was plenty of parking on the first level. 
I had no complaints and would be happy to stay there again if the price was right.

title: “Remarkable Stay”
text: The History And Architeture Of This Hotel Is Amazing

title: “Gotta Say Happy for SD”
text: A very busy weekend - nice place to stay. For this area and hotel the people are crazy at least when I was there, I don't know anywhere that wouldn't be in SD? But I was happy for the price I paid and the service I got. The hotel - while it may be due for some updates, it provided me with a nice stay in SD. I think the staff really cared. It was packed in the lobby, but the staff was doing their best, that matters to me. I slept great. The place was so perfectly located, we were able to see all the attractions we wanted to. Enjoyed the pool even after a day at the beach with a little bbq action made our room experience fun. People just got to spice up their trip and have fun - like me!

title: “Historic properties should be measured by different criteria”
text: Having read mixed reviews about this property, we decided to give it a try nonetheless, and were delighted with our stay! True, some of the rooms could use refreshing; ours was dark and a little tired, but the bathroom was spotless and the bed comfy. Our traveling companions asked for a different room after they were given one with an extremely noisy air conditioner; their replacement was light and airy and appeared to have been recently redecorated. The public rooms and gardens are impressive and well-maintained, and all the staff we encountered were pleasant and helpful. The dining room has a genteel atmosphere reminiscent of more refined days, and the food is good and mostly reasonable (just don't use room service - VERY pricey!). Remember, this place is OLD, with a long history; it can't be compared to a Marriott or Hilton, but the atmosphere and sense of place more than make up for that. In addition, it's centrally located for walking to all the tourist attractions in the area. We give our experience two thumbs up!

title: “Lots of Amenities at a Very Affordable Price!”
text:
We were staying a night in Jacksonville before going to Europe for a month vacation. We had picked the Jacksonville Plaza Hotel. They let us park our car for a month giving us 7 days free parking and charge us only $3.00 per day on succeeding days. I think this was a great deal!
The hotel was very nice, very clean. Our room has 2 queen size beds with pillow top mattress, down pillows, with a microwave and fridge, desk and a chair set up for wireless internet access.
The Queen size bed was very comfortable.
The bathroom was very clean and nice. Nice selection of boutique items in the bathroom, like a shower cap, body lotion, etc. in addition to shampoo and soap. I like the jade shower curtain as well. It matches the green blanket and light green linens in the bedroom. 
We didn't use the gym but it looked clean and well equipped.
The Office where you can use their computer/printer/fax was nice and clean. No problems connecting to the internet to check email.
There is 24 hour coffee available in the dining area.
Breakfast was good, plenty to choose from. There were muffins, cereals, fruits, danishes, etc.
I would reccommend the Jacksonsonville Plaza as a nice place to stay. We will definitely come back and stay here again.

title: “Great Hotel & Great Location!”
text: We're seasoned NYC travelers and usually stay in Midtown but love Hotel Indigo Chelsea. Stayed for 4 nights and really enjoyed the big comfy bed with crisp linens and soft comforter. Room size is nice (remember it's NYC) with good sized rain shower in the bathroom. Room service was VERY fast and courteous. In fact the entire staff was wonderful and very gracious. What amazed us the most was how quiet the hotel was at night - perfect for a good sleep. You're withing walking distance of just about everything and we did enjoy a great lunch one day at the restaurant. The rooftop bar is a great meet-up place and appreciated the security card swipe in order to get off on our floor.

title: “Ouch -- My conscience hurts”
text:
I stayed here for a conference, meaning I didn't pay for it (that kind of money belongs in my kids' college account, not a hotel chain). Staff are delightful, from room service to housekeeping to front desk. Really great room: large, super comfortable bed, small but okay bathroom. THANK YOU for covering the unhygenic bedspread with a freshly laundered duvet cover. I wish every 4-star hotel was doing this by now (just stayed at Omni-CNN Atlanta, and they still don't). I appreciated the makeup mirror, but found the hotel toiletries to be too strongly scented for my taste (some of us have fragrance allergies, hello people!). Cute balcony overlooking the bank building across the street, but after five minutes the Santa Anna winds sent me inside with an allergy attack, so not much use to anybody.
The real kicker (and my kids really laughed at me later) was that I was starving on arrival and couldn't find a restaurant in my price range in the hotel (there is a mall nearby, I just didn't know about it yet). So I ordered a $19 room service pizza which came with another $10 of taxes, service fees, and other charges. So I ate a $30 pizza. Will never hear the end of it from my kids. And will probably never stay here again, but it was nice while it lasted.

title: “The accommodations were great, and the service even better.”
text: I had the pleasure of staying at the Bryant Park Hotel just last week, and was delighted both by the lovely room/accommodations, and the friendly, accommodating service. I am a frequent business traveler with pretty high standards, and they exceeded my expectations. The room was spectacular: the sheets and pillows, perfect, and I really loved the small touches (especially the white noise machine in the room, as I rely on the sound of a fan to sleep). It was nice not having to battle with the HVAC system to get the sound. The best part of my stay was the service. Every person I interacted with: the front desk staff, restaurant crew, bellman, and doorman, were just delightful, warm and welcoming. I will absolutely stay again, and will recommend it to my friends.

title: “Run....fast”
text:
I should have known not to stay at this property when it took me calling three times to make a reservation. The hold time was absolutely ridiculous. 
When I checked into the hotel the front clerk Pam was not accommodating at all. She was very short with me when I asked her questions.
My guest room was very below average for $174 per night. I could of gotten a better room at Motel 6. The bathroom was disgusting. Their was rust in the bathtub and mildew in the caulking not to mention the fine pieces of hair on the bathroom floor. We layered the floor with towels to ensure we wouldn't step on it.
The only positive thing I could say was the manager in the restaurant was very polite and he checked to see how our dinner was. If you are smart run, run fast...... Go to Cherry Valley Lodge or Great Wolf Lodge. Don't waste your money!

title: “THE BIGGEST THANK YOU EVER!”
text:
This was the first time I ever stayed at the Park Plaza hotel, and wow, what a place!! The room was beautiful, everyone was so kind, and all the food in the executive lounge was delish. This is definitely my Boston overnight go-to. 
Huge props to your concierge, Alyssa. She was so kind when I came up to the desk. Greeted me with a great smile, helped me figure out my reservation, gave me TWO keys, and sent me on my happy way. I was shocked for how cool she kept it. There were SO MANY people waiting in line, but she made sure to give each and every single people a genuine "hello and welcome." Someone should make her CEO, stat.

title: “Impeccable, and well worth the expense.”
text: From the moment we entered the hotel Giraffe, we were welcomed, treated kindly, and made to feel important. The room was spacious and clean, and it was kept at a comfortable temperature. The bedding was clean and comfortable. There were plenty of amenities - including (but not limited to) an iphone dock alarm clock, a flat screen TV with cable and DVD player, an automated privacy/darkness shade, a fully stocked mini-bar, and complimentary wifi internet access. Oh, I almost forgot - there's a FREE wine and cheese bar every evening, and free breakfast every morning. They even have late (1:00 pm) check out. I cannot say enough good things about the quality and value of the rooms at this hotel.

title: “Family Road Trip”
text: We stayed in two rooms for 5 nights at the Carlyle Suites during a recent family road trip after a great deal of research on the internet. The staff was very busy when we arrived but were extremely friendly and helpful. We travelled with our four children and needed rooms next to each other (we requested this a month early when we made our reservations). Unfortunately they did not offer us rooms together for the first night, but made a change on the second night. The small kitchens were very convenient for breakfast, though one of the rooms had a strong smell of cooking spices from a previous guest. The neighborhood is very nice with several embassies you will pass on New Hampshire Avenue on your short walk to the DuPont Circle metro station. Fortunately there was a parking spot for our car which we kept parked for the first four nights. We took the car vs. metro on the last day and there was no longer a space. The staff recommended we park on the street but there are not spots available on the street so I parked at the Hilton (several blocks away) for $36 (parking rates in DC are very high) Overall we were pleased with our stay at the Carlysle. We made use of the laundry facilities one night, and noticed many people with families staying. I recommend the Carlyle.

title: “Great hotel!”
text:
My friends and I stayed here for 2 nights. Location is great, right near times square and Rock. center, Bryant park, Hells Kitchen etc. So if you are sightseeing its a good place to stay. They just opened a few days ago so you could tell they were still getting things completely organized and running smoothly, but I think that's to be expected. There looks like there is a restaurant and bar however it wasn't really open for anything but breakfast when we were there? Not really sure since we were not awake for breakfast hours but it was pretty big. There's a computer in the lobby you can use. The rooms were pretty huge by NYC standards, and the beds were amazing! stylish modern decor. In addition, the hotel staff was so great. They were very helpful with all kind of requests, from the normal directions and food recs and subway maps to hangover cures at the local market and clubbing recs and ice buckets at 6am when we stumbled in not wanting our night to end...we were pretty respectful and tried to be quiet and in return they did not seem to judge us for our frequently intoxicated state of mind. In fact, they seemed pretty entertained by our enthusiasm for the city. 
We didn't really see or hear any of the other people staying at our hotel, since we pretty much only slept there for a few off hours...but it was never noisy or anything. I saw a normal mix of tourists and ages. 
I would definitely recommend staying here!

title: “A fabulous hotel”
text:
My mother and I have just returned from spending 3 nights at The Bryant Park Hotel in room 2003. The visit was our annual mother/daughter break and a birthday treat for my mother. Therefore, I was very appreciative of the room upgrade given and we were both extremely delighted with our room. The view of the City was sensational and we simply loved the Molton Brown products. I was also very pleased with the goodies in the room including cup cakes to acknowledge my mother's celebration. We also had a balcony overlooking Bryant Park. We thoroughly enjoyed relaxing here after a long day of sight seeing with a drink, just taking in the magnificence of the City. The view and ambience was truly amazing!
The location is faultless - for walking, shopping and the subway - which helped us to make the most of our time in New York and having Bryant Park across the street is priceless! My only regret is that we we missed having dinner at Koi.
I have stayed in many hotels in NY and I must say that this is my favourite. Initially, I was concerned that this hotel might be too trendy for my mother, however, there were guest of all ages and the staff treated everyone with genuine care, attention and respect. 
Last year, my husband and I stayed at Gansevoort Park and I must say that The Bryant Park Hotel was much better in every way. Gansevoort was more style over substance, whereas the Bryant Park hotel effortlessly combined, style, high levels of service and sophistication with a hotel that is run to a very high standard. Every member of the team provided exceptional service and did everything possible to ensure that our stay was perfect. The personal touch demonstrated by Darren and the team truly sets this NY hotel apart. As a result, I will be taking my husband to experience this wonderful hotel - hopefully in December, if not early 2013 - and will certainly be recommending this superb hotel to family, friends and colleagues.

title: “Great Hotel”
text: Stayed here while seeing family in Dallas. Easy location to get to all parts of town. Nice new rooms. Great staff that helped us out. They even have this computer in the lobby that gives us flight times. Will stay here next time we visit Big D.

title: “What a awesome hotel!”
text: It was very cool walking into the Ace Hotel the lobby was filled with all kinds of people just hanging out and relaxing. It's a very dimly lit place but don't like that put you off it really sets the mood. There are all sorts of quirky decorations including taxidermy animals. The rooms where incredible very homely and welcoming. I would stay here again no questions asked.

title: “A gem”
text: 11 women stayed on this trip (we had Oprah tickets). Awesome location. Rates were excellent for this class of hotel. Concierge, desk and bell staff took care of our transportation and other needs. Room lighting a little dim was my only complaint. Great combo of room selections - it was perfect for 2 (unrelated) people to share a room. Best shopping and restaurants just a few steps in high heels away and right next to Hancock Tower so if you have trouble with direction, you can find your way back.

title: “My favorite place to stay in LA”
text: I love visiting Venice Beach and The Venice on the Beach Hotel has become a particular favorite of mine. Cozy and adorable, it is the perfect place for short or long-term stays. Nestled right between Marina Del Rey and Santa Monica, the hotel is fresh and fun and full of interesting wayfayers who are easy to chat with in the open beachfront setting. Right outside, Ocean Front Walk beckons with easy beach access, nearby restaurants and great people watching. The hotel -- always cheery, clean and very capably managed -- never fails me. I always feel relaxed and happy when there to get my beach fix and to mix it up with all the glamour of LA.

title: “Business traveler - sorely disappointed”
text:
The Good:
The lobby of the hotel is nicely appointed. The staff seemed competent and cordial.
The Bad:
The hallway outside of my room was littered with food and crumbs. Down the hall from the elevator, there was a wine bottle and other room service detritus that stayed in the hall for nearly 18 hours. The room was poorly lit--very hard to work at the desk. My bathroom tiles were moldy.
There was zero service done to my room in the two nights I was there. No one remade the bed, folded a towel, brought another washcloth, etc. However, someone did open the door to move the USAToday inside of the room--so I know that staff exists.
My clock radio was set to the right time--12 hours off.
Water pressure in my room was fine. My colleague two floors up could barely get the shower to dribble.
The internet connection in my room didn't work. The hotel said it was a problem with the Wayport. Wayport said it was a problem with the hotel.
Such a disappointment.

title: “Okay, but not 4 diamond”
text: An okay place - clean, comfortable, convenient to shopping, restaurants, highway, and downtown. Not, however, worthy of 4 diamond rating. This is your standard run-of-the-mill business hotel at best. Plain hotel, boring furniture, no decor, no extra touches, old TV, staff consistently apathetic at best. I can't think of a single thing that makes this property stand out, or makes it worthy of a 4 diamond rating. It's just plain, ordinary, and boring. If you want to stay in this exact area, just pick one of the other 2 properties near the Polaris Mall - my guess is that they are about the same, and much less expensive.

title: “My daughter is an MD Anderson Patient & the staff treats us like family!”
text: My family has had to travel from New Orleans to Texas once a week for my daughter to get her chemo. The hotel staff is very accommodating & courteous. We never know when we need a last minute reservation. I have called while the rodeo was taking place in the Reliant Stadium & got my reservation changed for that day with no problem, we stayed that entire week of the Rodeo for medical purposes. On some weeks my daughter & her husband travel without me & stay at the Holiday Inn Houston South Loop & I don't worry about them, I know they are safe, the staff at the hotel treats us like family. The rooms are very clean & we get a discounted rates for the room & restaurant because my daughter is an MD Anderson Patient. We have been staying at this hotel since December 2010. Some weeks we stay for a day or two & sometimes we have had to stay for a month. I make changes to our reservations all the time depending on my daughter's condition. I love that I can call the day I need a hotel in Texas & I know this hotel will always make me a last minute reservation. Everyone there is very friendly & they always allow me to stay longer if we needed without a prior reservation.

title: “Dismayingly Disappointed”
text: As both an Intercontinental Ambassador Member and a Platinum IHG Member, was unfortunately dismayingly disappointed with our recent stay. We stayed here for 2 nights to celebrate my wife's birthday, for which we were extremely excited and for which we were willing to spend for (Our other hotels for the rest of our vacation were in much cheaper hotels). After having had countless fond memories in IHG properties we've stay at in different countries, most especially with the Intercontinental Brand, we chose this new property despite the relatively more expensive price, understandably due to its excellent location, to celebrate the special occasion. Our experience however from the first moment upon check-in was simply far from what we'd expect from an Intercontinental. We could not check-in even by the standard 3pm check-in time. The service was outright stone cold, not to mention unapologetic. By the time when we did check-in, the water from the sink, was leaking all over the bathroom due to the pipes below. Upon calling the guest service to provide the feedback regarding the sink and the check-in experience (Since we received this paper that as Ambassadors, if at any point in time during our stay, we felt it was not "Excellent", all we needed to do was call the guest service number), unfortunately the guest service was once again unapologetic while at the same time took the effort of justifying our check-in experience. I'm just simply so disappointed that I'm hardly angry, it was a sincerely sad experience to have celebrated my wife's birthday in this property.

title: “Would give it a 3.5 if I could”
text:
I arrived late and was greeted by a panhandler - not the best beginning to my stay. I think a better run hotel would have either bribed the panhandler to go elsewhere, or at the very least, had the doorman/porter observant enough to greet me as I exited the taxi, as opposed to after I had checked in. 
The room was as others have described it - slick and modern - and had just about everything you could ask for. My only issue with the room was that the television reception was pretty fuzzy for a couple of the network stations (NBC and I think CBS). I know this can be an issue in a city, but I would have enjoyed my early morning routine with less static on the TV. 
Speaking of mornings, one morning there were 2 elevators out of service. After waiting for 20 minutes, and I'm not exagerating, I decided that I would have to walk down, rather than risk being late for my customer meeting. Fortunately, I was only on the 7th floor. I lugged my laptop down a couple of flights, only to be greeted by guests and a hotel employee heading back up. It seems we had all chosen the staircase to no where, and had to get to a floor with the correct access, and then were guided to the basement, and finally to an exit. Kudos for the employee, who did lug my laptop for me.
Normally, I wouldn't even mention this last point, but I think it is indicative of the lack of attention paid to details. That was the erratic nature of newpaper delivery. One morning, the Wall Street Journal was outside my door. The next three mornings, no paper at my door, but copies of the San Francisco Chronicle near the elevator. The last morning, USA outside my door. As I say, this was no big deal, but highlights a lack of consistency in the hotel.

title: “Small but fits needs”
text:
I got this hotel on hotwire. Check in was not an easy process. My card was swiped several times and odd charges showed up. I am sure they will fall off after a week or so but I could see where this could be annoying to some. It took about fifteen minutes to find my reservation but they did and I got to my room.
I walk into any hotel I book on a discount site with a lowered expectation. I walked into my room and for the price I paid...the room exceeded my expectations. They make excellent use of the small space. The rooms are very clean and very bright. I thought that the bed was extremely comfortable and I really have no complaints.
Check out was different than check in. The young lady working the front desk was EXTREMELY friendly and you could tell she liked her job. 
Overall...yes the rooms are small. But with the location...you shouldn't be hanging out in your room. There is so much to do right outside the hotel. Its off the beaten path...but just a few blocks away from restaurants, shopping and entertainment. 
I would stay at this hotel again. I would also recommend it to friends and family.

title: “Perfect Location”
text: My mom, sister and I stayed here in a King Suite with 2 queens. It was the perfect size for all 3 girls. I had problems when I booked the room through Travelocity choosing 2 queens and when I called reservations, they told me that they couldn't accomodate either but to ask at Check-in. There was no problem at all and we were granted the room. It did overlook Lex which made for a perfect location as neither my mom or sister had every been to NYC before. The subway is only 2 blocks up and several great places to shop and eat nearby. There was also an incredible street fair the Sunday we were there. They closed off Lex for several blocks for merchants to sell their goods. What a treat! The beds were comfortable and the shower was hot and had great pressure. The room was hot the first night but after a call downstairs the adjustment was made. The street below is just too loud to have the windows open. The fridge in the "mini" kitchen was perfect to put water in for when we came back from our long days of shopping. When we come back I would not hesitate to stay here again.

title: “Perfect home base for family vacation”
text: My husband and children and I spent two nights at Eventi over school vacation. We arrived via train at Penn Station just a few blocks away and were warmly greeted when we dropped our bags there in the morning. That evening, when we arrived back from dinner, we found milk and cookies waiting for the kids. They felt so special and ate them wearing the "fancy robes". The room was clean and nicely decorated. If your kids are good walkers, you can reach Times Square, Bryant Park, Rockfeller Center, the Empire State Building, and the High Line on foot. Thank you, Eventi, for making our kids' first visit to NYC so wonderful.

title: “Large Rooms”
text:
This hotel was great! really close to grand central station and access to all the subway lines! lots of food and shops nearby to buy water, snacks, etc. The room was also huge for a NYC hotel. Clean modern rooms and bathroom. I would definitely stay here again! Also check out aroma cafe near by for their croissants and coffee!
The service was excellent as well. They let us check in super early and check our luggage the day we left!

title: “Excellent service!”
text:
We booked this hotel by chance through Priceline. I should have called the hotel right after booking to request a room with two beds, but I forgot. Fortunately, they were able to find an available room for us while we were out in the city during our first day. The morning/afternoon doorman, Daniel, was incredibly helpful; he gave us great information about where to eat nearby, when to visit the Empire State Building ('If you can't see the top, don't go"), etc.
My wife has Multiple Chemical Sensitivity, so she's extremely sensitive to scents from certain chemicals and perfumes. Most of the world doesn't have to worry about this, and many hotels, including The Marcel, will use Febreze or other scented deodorizers on their linens. We had to ask the staff to change our bed linens with unscented ones, which they did expediently, and they even lent us a table fan to help circulate the air out the window. When bedtime came, the scent from our children's bed linens began to bother my wife, but our children were already asleep. I went down to the front desk to ask for help. The night desk manager quickly lent us an ionizer to remove the scent from our room, and left a voicemail with the housekeeping manager to ensure that our room received only unscented linens for the duration of our stay. He also was very understanding of our problem, and went out of his way to make my wife feel better about her condition.
Rooms were nice and clean but on the small side. The beds were super comfortable though a tad short. I'm 5'10" and my feet hung off the edge if I weren't careful. The shower was refreshing; it had two shower heads, one on the ceiling and a handheld on the wall. One or both could be used.
Our biggest problem with the hotel is it's location; there weren't many sit down restaurants nearby, and eating out is our favorite activity in New York. The corner restaurant next to The Marcel, Inoteca, was low on flavor and high on pretentiousness, but had a huge wine selection.

title: “Great location. Good service”
text:
I stayed at the Westin St Francis for a week. The location was fabulous. Everything was within walking distance - shopping, Chinatown, the Bay area, etc. When needed to, bus and taxi was easily available. 
The staff were helpful and friendly. When me little girl cannot decide on what she muffin she wants, the staff patiently waited for her to make her choice. The concierge was very helpful and never fail to give us good recommendation of restaurant and places to shop, giving precise walking route (when required). They also promptly helped with reservations. Excellent service!
The room was spacious and bed very comfortable. 
Will definitely stay here again!

title: “GOOD VALUE IN A VERY EXPENSIVE TOWN!”
text: If you want to take a family/couples/friends vacation to Boston and don't want to pay a ton for the hotel room because you want to see all the sights- then stay here! The location is good if you have a car. With a car, it is 4 minutes to Highway 93 and 1 minute to the a Stop & Shop Supermarket. We didn't take the T from there but there is the Red Line stop within a 10 minute walk. The rooms were standard and the check-in was easy. There are 2 computers in the lobby for free internet and printing. It was also a real plus having FREE HOTEL PARKING which is about $30-40 a day for most Boston hotels. The immediate surrounding area was ok, not the super high rent district but not completely unsafe either (Yes of course, you get what you pay for.) But with Boston Hotels being $225-$400 a night, stay here and spend your $$ having fun with all this great city has to offer. The hotel is labeled as "Boston South". It is not technically in South Boston, but very close so worth taking a stroll around Castle Island and having dinner at traditional Southie restaurant Anhreims.

title: “Nice hotel but cannot recommend”
text: Recently spent two nights at the San Diego Marriott Gaslamp quarter due to an accident which resulted in a total loss of my car. Check-in was quick and efficient and the front desk associate skipped the "hotel talk-through tour" as I had already explained the wreck situation and it was quite obvious that I was just ready to go to my room. So for that I give kudos to this hotel, however, having worked in the hotel industry before, for a situation as serious as a totalled car, I half expected a complimentary amenity or upgrade, neither of which was offered (can't really fault the hotel for this, however, many other hotels would have offered one or the other). Room was a large corner room, however was a handicap accessible room (no mention of this at check-in) and did not have a tub, but instead had a roll in shower. Had I been notified of this at check-in (it is standard procedure to notify a guest if they are being placed in a handicap accessible room and have not requested such) I would have been asked to be moved to another room. Had requested extra towels, a microwave, and a refrigerator prior in my reservation. Was told at check-in these items were already placed in the room. They were not there when I arrived so had to call back down (after being told that they WERE there) to have them delivered. Hotel loses points for this. Overall my two night stay was good however, on the first night (the night of my accident) a group of drunk women exited the elevator on my floor and proceeded to converse quite loudly in hallway at 2:30 in the morning. I called down and requested that Loss Prevention (Security) be sent up to take care of the noise. Not quite sure if anyone was sent, but my assumption is no as the conversations continued until around 4:00 AM. Housekeeping began their rounds around 7 AM, once again awakening me due to the rather large gap between the bottom of the door and the floor. Second night went uneventful. At this point, my opinion of the hotel was still rather high, with a few key points that needed to be worked on. However, check-out was a disaster. I asked to speak with a manager regarding my inconveniences and the manager which responded just kind of looked at me with the attitude of why was I even bringing this to her attention (no writing down the problems [Marriott encourages a log of all guest complaints] and a general sense of apathy). I was then told that since I was staying on a discounted corporate rate, that my complaints don't really matter and that I would just have to deal with it. I was also told that had I called back with the noise complaint, I could have been moved to another room (moving at 4AM, when I'm sore and can barely move anyways due to whiplash among other accident related pains, which would include moving of the refrigerator, microwave, and other towels). Unsatisfied with the response received from the manager, I proceeded to call the president of Marriott Intl (I am acquainted with him as he is a graduate of my university) and left him a voicemail stating my concern. At this point, the manager's attitude still remained one of apathy and arrogance, as if noone above her (not even the president of the company) can overrule her decisions. I must say, I am quite dissatisfied and this is the worst service I have ever received from ANY level of hotel, select, limited, or full service. I will not be returning except maybe as a full paying customer solely so that I can receive a guest satisfaction survey and let the company know just how poorly managed this property is.

title: “Rittenhouse 1715, a gem in central Philadelphia”
text: An excellent small hotel just half a block from Rittenhouse Square. Comfortable rooms, very accomodating staff, good breakfast. A real find for those who prefer smaller hotels with excellent amenities.

title: “You can't get everything!”
text: This hotel reminds you that you cannot get everything in life. Whereas the location of this hotel is a dream come true - few blocks from Times Square and right next to the Rockefeller Centre, it is living right in the heart of the world's awesomest city; once you enter the hotel, there is nothing but disappointment. It looks like a cheap shady motel where space is scarce and ambience is laughed at. The gym has a single treadmill and a vending machine - laughable sight! The food isn't that great either. But the whole point is, you might not need to be indoors except for sleeping when you are in a place like that!

title: “cheap and clise by denver airport”
text:
Just ok for a one night sleep before or after a flight, but nothing more than this. 
The area is quite nasty
Ac very noisy and not working properly: the room was incredibly hot even if the temperature outside was pleasant.
The remodeled room looks old even if it's not and the sheet could have been cleaner.

title: “Lovely location, service was great”
text: My husband and I typically stay at The Lowell when in NY, but for a girl's weekend, I opted to try the RC Central Park. The location across from CP, and access to great shopping was perfect for us. We had four rooms on the 12th floor. The rooms were very nicely done, with all of the amenities you would expect for $750/night. The rooms were spacious by any standard. All of the rooms looked over a grungy water tower, but frankly we weren't there for the view. From check in with Robinson, to the bar where we ended most of our evenings, to room service, all was very well done. Look, the Ritz Carlton is a chain hotel, albeit a very nice one. You can expect a spacious, well-appointed room, beautiful public areas and great service. I will take that any day, and am returning in two weeks on a solo trip to the city.

title: “Great Location Especially for Foodies”
text:
A lovely boutique hotel in a great location. It's surrounded by fantastic restaurants - about 5 Tom Douglas establishments within 300 ft. of the hotel's front door. Pike Place Market and Westlake Center (the monorail) are within walking distance. Taxis are usually outside the hotel but the staff is always on hand to hail one for you if needed. 
The standard king room I booked was on par with hotels in large metropolitan cities. WiFi is free and the common areas are a great place to just read a book or entertain friends.
The staff is professional and had wonderful suggestions for things to do in Seattle. Room service was quick, even at peak hours, and Lola's menu is phenomenal. At this price point, I would recommend the Andra for a Seattle home base.

title: “Great location in New York!”
text: We stayed here for a week and were extremely confortable. The hotel is new and very clean. The rooms and bathroom were spacious. We were on 27th floor and noise wasn't an issue up that high. It's 3 blocks from Penn Station which worked great for using trains from JFK and not having to spend money on taxis. And we had friends to visit in New Jersey so it was very convenient for us. Its also was close to the Empire State Building. Its about a 15 min train ride to the lower east side, greenwich village. We didn't get a chance to eat at the hotels reastaurant but we did run down to the small market/cafe that served a variety of food for breakfast, lunch & dinner. All hotel staff were extremely nice and helpful. I would definitely stay here next time I'm in New York.

title: “Great location & nicely fit out, but small rooms, noisy and VERY hot”
text:
This hotel is difficult to rate overall as it's a bit of a mixed bag, so please bear with me and consider my comments.
Good points: 1) Great location - right in the thick of things in the city. Great restaurants and bars nearby and near the shops. 2) Great decor - this hotel is fitted-out very nicely. It's contemporary, yet sympathetic to its age. 3) The front desk service is very good - the guys are keen to help and to make you feel at home.
Bad points: 1) The rooms get SO hot it's unbelievable. I'd just come from Vegas and the rooms felt hotter than it was outside there! There's no air-conditioning and the hotel seems to conduct heat like crazy! 2) It's very noisy. Now this would be less of a problem if there was air conditioning as you could shut the windows. Nevertheless, there is a lot of road noise and then there are deliveries throughout the night - the result is the worst night sleep I have EVER had. 3) The rooms are WAY smaller than they appear on the internet! There wasn't even enough room for me to lay my suitcase on the stand! Overall very cramped - this may not be a huge problem if the website was more clear about this and you could get a good night's sleep. 4) Toiletries not replaced. Although the room was well cleaned and linen changed each day, there was no replacement of shower gel, shampoo or soap each day - I don't think that's good enough.
Overall I don't think I'd recommend this hotel to anyone as there are better competitors at the same or lower price. If they sorted the air conditioning, I may change my mind.

title: “A fabulous city break”
text: We stayed here for 2 nights with our two young daughters (2 and 5 months). I was a little worried prior to the trip as it's obvious this hotel is mainly inhabited by business travellers, as it is in the heart of the financial district. I didn't see another child in the hotel for the entire trip - but the staff and facilities were fantastic and we didn't struggle with the girls at all. Our room on the 27th floor had a double aspet view out over the water, and on our 1st night we were given complimentary access to the concierge lounge, which had a stunning view of the statue of liberty. Out room was fairly spacious and had two king sized beds, plus they'd added a cot for us (a real cot, not a travel cot which hotels often provide) We drove in to the city from Boston and the hotel was easy to find. We also had valet parking until 5.30pm the day we left, so the car was taken care of completely by the hotel. The hotel was a short stroll to Battery Park, which is where you pick up the Ellis Island ferry (big queues tho). It is also immediately next to Ground Zero and you could see the work going on from out of the elevator lobby windows. We took cabs into the centre of city, Times Square, Blue Circle ferry pier for trip around Manhatten, also to Broadway to the theatre. Grabbing a cab was easy as there are plenty around. Central Park is right over the other side of the city so that was the longest cab ride we took. I don't think this hotel would be right if you wanted to be more in the heart of the city, but that didn't bother us at all. As you'd imagine, 100% clean and excellent service. Friendly waiters at breakfast waived any charge for our toddler and just offered her the buffet without charge. Waitress on our last day also offered take away cartons for us to take whatever food we wanted to the journey - which was great. Front desk gave our children a bag of goodies, a lovely teddy, toys and activity bits too. I couldn't fault this hotel at all.

title: “Great Service”
text:
Good Evening
Once again the SpringHill Suites by Marriott, with Naomi Herring, Asst. General Manager, her staff and host of housekeepers made our stay a pleasure. They were always willing and ready to accommodate us with whatever we needed. The rooms were furnished with a refrigerator, microwave, sink, desk and queen sofa sleeper. The rooms were clean and updated. 
 Special Thanks to Billy, Cassandra, Tonya and Donna (housekeeping) and the rest of the staff for greeting us with a smile each time our paths crossed. The coffee and breakfast was fresh and hot at all times. 
The location was great and close to all the attractions were we interested in. (shopping, food)
In the future, when selecting a hotel we will consider SpringHill Suites by Marriott our host hotel. 
Thank You for quality service.

title: “Excellent choice for Boston Symphony”
text:
Spacious rooms and immaculate. Charming small boutique historic hotel and service very attentive. Excellent comfortable beds. Good value for Boston. Would definitely return when in Boston and would recommend hotel to friends and family. 
Marilyn

title: “Would Stay There Again In A Heart Beat”
text:
My husband and I stayed here this Labor Day weekend. (2006) We drove in from Illinois. It was such a joy to park the car - with no parking fees - and just use the city transportation.
We took several tours, and were picked up at the hotel for most of them. . It is about a $10 cab ride to the bay. The staff was extremely pleasant and helpful
There is a cheese store on the corner which serves great sandwiches. Suggest you split one if you are not a big eater. Great place to check out snacks too.
The rooms were clean ,spacious,and well appointed. The price for the great room and free parking was the best I could find (on line )in the city, and believe me I did my homework.

title: “The Best Hotel next to Westside Oil Companies”
text:
It was my 4th stay here in the hotel. Rooms are spacious and the bed is very good. The hotel staff is very helpful and always friendly. I really liked the same day delivery of laundry and a free WiFi.
Fresh fruits and a nicely prepared omelet makes a great breakfast. The hotel also serves one of the best "Club Sandwiches" and the fries are very tasty.
Try to stand on some of the bridges in the lobby and you will see, that fishes are coming to see you and asking for some food.

title: “Noisy”
text:
Went for buisness so happy i didnt pay out of pocket. Relatively clean and food is good. However all rooms have paper thin walls and and plumbing is quite noisy. Reception/bar is often busy with people making it noisy as well. 
Really annoying, the way to the restaurant through hotel is blockef off so hotel guests are forced to go outside in the cold and take street entrance to have breakfast... Not cool.
Internet is 14.00 dollars for 24hrs which i personally find to be a ripoff..
The SPA was closed down, the so-called pool is more like a tub, and the "beach" bar on roof was maybe cool a long time ago, but now resembles an adult sandbox....
Anyway, think there are enough choice of hotels in San Diego to avoid this one.....

title: “Great location and great service”
text:
This was our second stay at the Marina Inn and again - we were happy to stay there.
The Marina Inn is a well priced, nice little hotel in the Marina District. You can easily get to downtown, the piers and other nice places. There are a lot of restaurants and bars just a short walk away. The front desk was always helpful (thank you so much Yolanda - you made our stay great again) and made really good recommendations on food and trips. The rooms are small but ok - if you go to SF you just need a bed to sleep and that is what is offered. For breakfast - ok - continental breakfast in the US means you have to find a nicer place but there are good opportunities around the Marina Inn. To be true - of course there are some "negative" things: The rooms are not always so clean (but give the usual tip to the chambermaid and it will get better) and the Lombard street is really loud. Hence, you should try to get a room that is not located on first or second floor. The breakfast is not so amazing but most hotels in the US do not have a real breakfast. 
Overall, because of the great people in this hotel, the fantastic location and the "ok" rooms we will definitely come back. We love this city and enjoyed our stay there once again.

title: “Perfect New York boutique hotel”
text: Found out about this hotel on Tripadvisor and want to add to the list of those who sing its praises. The hotel is lovely- the exceptionally clean rooms were more spacious than expected. The wonderful breakfast is such a bonus -it is so convenient to leave your room and breeze into their second floor hospitality room instead of dealing with a restaurant. The breakfast included large bowls of fresh fruit salad (which were constantly replenished),yogurt,cereal, bagels, pasteries, etc. A complimentary wine cocktail hour is also provided which we would have happily attended if we didn't alreay have plans. The staff is courteous, professional and always available to help. When the doorman saw us attempting to hail a cab during a raging rain/snow/sleet Nor'easter, he shooed us inside and stood outside for quite some time until he was successful! In additon, the manager thoughtfully sent Prosesso and chocolates to our room in honor of our anniversay.We are so pleased to have found this well-run small boutique hotel and can't wait to return the next time we travel to New York!

title: “Great location,great city great Hotel”
text:
Stayed at this hotel through the Disney Vacation Club and what a great hotel it was with plenty of nice touches including chocolate covered strawberries in our room upon arrival.
Very elegant , staff were very good indeed checking with us after we arrived that we were satisfied with our room.
Would definietly stay again, only way they could improve is to have tea and coffee making facilities in room and keep the residents bar open after 10:30 pm.

title: “Great hotel!”
text:
The hotel is great. I hinghly recommend it!
It's very clean, the service y really good and has a great fitness area.
Great location: steps from Madison Ave.
It has an amazing lobby and a nice bar . The room service is really good, and the staff is always ready to help.
I do recommend the Roosevelt Hotel.

title: “Excellent Stay, Friendly Staff, Great Location”
text:
Over the past 2 to 3 years - I have come to love the city of Philadelphia. This is my 1st stay at the Meridien and boy did it meet my expectations. Just like the previous reviewer - I got the exact same deal through priceline and stayed here over the long weekend.My girlfriend and I drove down from Toronto for the long weekend and since this was her first time in Philadelphia she we both had high expectations.
The hotel was beautiful. The lobby was modern and very comfortable - I felt like I was staying in a condo rather than a hotel. There was a bar and a restaurant in the lobby, and the check in staff were extremely friendly. As I mentioned before, I booked the hotel through priceline but called in to make a request for a king bed. The staff took my SPG number and gladly put me up on the 10th floor (which is the highest floor) with a great view of the city. 
The room was clean, modern, and had all the amenities we needed. There was a LCD TV, a safe, and a minibar. The washroom was really clean, and my girlfriend and I really liked the shower (with a glass door) which is different from other hotels. The bed was really comfortable and the pillows were so soft - I felt like I was at home. The cleaning staff always had a smile on their face and were extremely accomodating. 
I used the gym all 3 nights I was here and like previous reviewers mentioned - it is very basic and I would have expected a lot more from a 4 star hotel. However the weights and treadmills were enough to help keep my exercise routine.
The biggest positive of this hotel is the location. It is smack in the middle of city hall and close to everything. The majority of the tourist attractions are within a walking distance and there are many restaurants within a few minutes. There is a Mcdonalds right next door for breakfast or late night snacks and the hotel is right across from JFK plaza.
A few negatives of the hotel include: no free internet in the rooms, expensive parking (you can park overnight at any of the parking garages in the area and will cost you less than $17 a night), no fridge in the room just a mini bar. The staff in general were exceptional - except for one staff at the front her name was Hannah. She seemed sad and was upset when I asked her for a late checkout.
In all this hotel made our visit to Philadelphia a trip to remember. It is on the expensive side but if the hotel gave me a better rate or I got the same rate as I did on priceline - I will definitely be back.

title: “the difference between good and 'outstanding'”
text: we arrived late with the dreaded news that our room had been inadvertantly double-booked and with an apology and a promise of true compensation, we were chauferred off to the nearby Hilton for the night. The next day upon early check in, the hotel manager himself came to greet and personally escort us to our 'upgrade' - a 3-room luxury suite accompanied by chilled champagne, flowers, a letter of apology , free drinks voucher in their incredible Redwood bar and free breakfasts for the duration of our stay. For the next four days we were treated like royalty in one of the finest hotels I have ever stayed in. The Asia de Cuba restaurant is superb, the Redwood Bar an experience and our whole stay perfectly memorable. What a difference a great hotel manager can make. Thank you Steven - we will be back!

title: “Fantastic Stay”
text:
We stayed in this hotel for 6 nights in March. We booked from Ireland on the Travel Republic website and got an excellent rate. Our room was on the 4th floor, room 444 in fact. Even though room was on a lower level we did not hear traffic noise.
Room was great, there was a huge bed which was very comfortable, a 42 inch widescreen HD TV! and a computer which we actually did not use. There was also a mini bar. Bathroom was well equipped with a rain drop shower. The rooms were spotless and no sign of bed bugs here.
We did not eat at the hotel, breakfast was expensive but then everyone goes out for breakfast in NY.
Location is the best thing about this hotel, 2 minutes walk from Times Square, 5 minutes from Macys and Madison Square Garden.
I hope to return in the future.

title: “Cool Little Place”
text: Had a nice time with the wife and kids. Had booked another property through Expedia with was a dirtbag place, so left and moved to Magnolia. Cute little lobby and nice suite-type rooms. We spent a couple of nights and liked the location fine, though it's not downtown Denver's best area for activities and restaurants, but good if you're a banker (I'm not)

title: “Another Travel Lodge Broken Ice Machine!!”
text: Again, after checking in we find out that this Travel Lodge has a broken ice machine. No one bothered to offer that information as we checked in. This is getting to be a trend since the last two Travel Lodges we stayed at also had broken ice machines. This is really a reflection of poor management and the motel owners willingness to accept full advertised price when they know that part of their value is not available. I can live with that if I am informed ahead of time. Apparently, that is not Travel Lodge policy - but it should be. We also placed the "DO NOT DISTURB" sign on our door when went out and staff ignored that.

title: “Because they care”
text:
I happen to meet the the room service manager Serge Belanger and I relayed to him a problem that I had with room service. Well this man knows that it is not necessarily the problem that matters but the way you deal with it. 
 A personal note of apology and impeccable room service ( complimentary ) went above and beyond my expectation. I have always liked this hotel, but now I like it even more. 
 Great service Serge, thank you.

title: “Good Value”
text: Not luxury, but clean, pleasant, well-maintained. The area feels safe and is extremely easy to get to if you are flying in and renting a car. It appears to attract many business people, and we were allowed check-in with no hesitation when we arrived early. The desk was quick and efficient, and we would definitely stay there again.

title: “Great location, but watch out for the parking charge.”
text:
We stayed a couple of nights here as part of a tour round California. Hotel was good and staff very helpful with directions and suggestions for restaurants etc. Location is great for wlaking down to the pier area and seeing the sights or going out to Alcatraz. Room was clean and quiet for a restful night.
Only negative points are that there is no pool and the charge for parking your car is $36 a night.
PS if you travelling with a family into downtown, don't bother with the trams - theyre slow, packed and expensive, just use a taxi - quicker and cheaper.

title: “A Classy Establishment”
text: I am a bit late in my review but I felt my opinion might matter to somebody anyway. My first introduction to the United States was spending 2 nights in this uniquely shaped hotel! I spent Two nights here and found my stay very pleasant. My room was not as spacious as I'd anticipated but never the less it was very clean and welcoming. The staff were friendly enough but the friendliest staff members were those that pointed me towards the correct elevator to use! That was impressive and fun! The gift shop lady was nice too.

title: “Roaches on the Park”
text:
Stayed at this hotel for our summer vacation. Location is good (Just in front of Central Park and 3 blocks from subway station) but rooms are tiny and the second night we found a huge roach in the room.
If you're traveling on a budget I guess it's ok, but otherwise stay some place else!

title: “Friendly Staff!”
text: Stayed at this hotel due to its proximity to USC, where we were dropping off my freshman. Definitely convenient and easy to get to. From the moment we checked in, we were impressed by how friendly and accommodating the staff was. The room was small but the bed was incredibly comfortable. Not a lot of amenities I am used to---but we were in and out of the hotel anyway. We frequented LA Live for dinner and entertainment with friends----again, very, very close to the hotel so that made up for the lack of good restaurants in the hotel. We just might make this our regular hotel when we visit my son at USC.

title: “Comfortable beds!!”
text: They've put some bucks into refurbishing and the beds are high quality and very comfortable. I just want a clean comfortable bed and hot shower and don't care much about amenities since I spend very little time in a hotel room, but there are great amenities here like free wireless, free parking and free coffee. The room is very clean, small but comfortable. Word must be getting out about this place because there were no vacancies the three days we were there.

title: “We love the Belvedere”
text: We stayed at the Belvedere for 5 nights first week in May – 3 women cousins. This was our 2nd time staying here, the first being back in 2008. Our experience then is what brought us back. All went smoothly from check-in to check-out. We ate breakfast in the restaurant every morning – nice variety and super-friendly staff. Location is handy to everything. Grayline office/tour stops just a short distance away. Food Emporium a couple blocks away – very convenient for snacks, deli food or beverages. We had tickets for “Live with Kelly” one morning and needed to depart early. There were taxis waiting on the street out front, so we were able to get one promptly. We never had to contact the staff regarding any issues, and would definitely stay here again.

title: “Location and Value”
text:
The Hotel was the standard Holiday Inn. clean, good size room and
standard features for a comfortable stay. There was enough room for a family of five in a room with two double beds and a roll away. We
arrived early 10:30 am expecting to check our bags and return later
to get our room. We were surprised when the clerk verified our reservation and put us in a room right away, even though check-in wasn't until late afternoon. There is a pool, a bar, a summer cafe near the pool, a gift shop, room service, restuarant, valet parking, bag/bell
