service and tourist info all for under $200 a night which is a bargin in NYC.
The location is away from times square, but only about 5 minutes to
Broadway and another 10 minutes or so to get down to the square. It
is not a plush Hotel, but it is perfect for a family looking for a comfortable
stay at a reasonable price.

title: “Pleasant Stay, Friendly Staff”
text: Each summer we stay in Philadelphia for a weekend without our children to enjoy the restaurants, museums and a show without having to rush home. The Westin is in a great location for many of Philadelphia's attractions. The staff also couldn't have been more friendly or accommodating. The front desk made sure we could check-in to our room as soon as one was available by calling us on our cell phone. The doormen made sure we knew where we were going and supplied us with cold bottles of water as we explored the city during the heat. As expected the rooms were spacious, well kept and a lovely respite from the heat.

title: “About what you would expect for a hotel airport”
text: This hotel is very close to Hobby and has a free shuttle. The room was a bit dirty and the caroet was actually sticky. I'd be shocked if anyone every stays at this hotel more than one night nor would they want to. The rooms on the airport side are a bit loud due to the planes landing and taking off.

title: “Beautiful hotel”
text: My mom and I stayed here for the weekend when we came to Indy to see the DCI World Championships. What a beautiful hotel! I expected as much being a part of the JW series. I loved the underground parking and also how the parking garage was color coded to let you know where you needed to go. Check-in was super easy & the young woman at the front desk walked us to the elevator and explained all the hotel restaurants & other details we might want to know. Our room was perfect! It was clean, well-stocked, & had everything we possibly could want in a hotel room. We did however hit a snafu with ordering room service. It took us about an hour & a half at about 1:00 a.m. to get our room service order, but the hotel was great in making it up to us by deducting our room service bill by 50% since the food was delivered warm & was actually very tasty. This by no means hurt my rating on this hotel! We had breakfast in Osterio Pronto, and it was pretty good. The hotel overall was very nice, clean, the staff was very accomodating, and the decor was just gorgeous! I highly recommend this hotel!

title: “Great Place to Stay Downtown”
text:
We had a great stay at the Courtyard, Downtown Indianapolis in October 2007. The location was perfect for our desire to explore downtown on foot. The capitol building was gorgeous! The walk on the canal is beautiful and relaxing. Our room was spacious, clean, comfortable, and attractive. The wonderful bed and pillows provided a great night's sleep! The public areas are clean and well-maintained.
The parking was $12 a day. The only thing free in the morning was the coffee and a piece of fruit. I generally like to stay where a free breakfast is provided but didn't think that would be an issue for a city the size of Indianapolis; however, we did not find many places to have breakfast nearby, and what we found was as pricey as the Courtyard's buffet. Next time, we will either pay for the buffet or price compare with the Residence Inn across the parking lot which charges more for a room but does provide a free breakfast.
All in all, the Couryard is a great find. Many of the other downtown hotels charge much more, and comparatively speaking, we received good value for our money. We will probably return.

title: “Fantastic hotel, wonderful stay- will be back!”
text:
I stayed at the Swissotel as part of a business meeting for five nights. This was the selected conference hotel, but I was very happy to become acquainted with it because I will definitely plan on using it again for my next trip to Chicago. I loved the location- very central off Wacker. I love to walk when I come to Chicago so this facilitated my walking sprees down The Magnificent Mile, to Millenium Park, and to the Navy Pier. You could even watch the fabulous fireworks over the Navy Pier from the hotel. 
The hotel staff were very friendly and helpful. The check-in was prompt without issue. The elevators are modern and you select the floor and the panel indicates which elevator will take you there. For some reason, I had not seen this before, but it seems efficient. The rooms are a generous size with very nice views and nice sized bathrooms. The bed and pillows were super comfy and the turn-down service left chocolates. I used room service once and they were on time....the food was fine but did not blow me away with taste or value (but, that is typical). The conference rooms were nice and well taken care of during the meetings. The penthouse level gym was nicely outfitted and the hot tub was clean and large enough to share comfortably with strangers. I enjoyed using the facilities greatly at the end of my stay and wished I had used them the whole time. Wifi capabilities in the room were good and were included in my stay (as was the gym). The bar downstairs is not large but has some friendly staff that are probably a bit overworked depending on how busy the hotel becomes.
As far as restaurants, I did go to the Palm. I had never been before. Some people seem to love this restaurant and I just don't quite get it. I feel like the menu is priced pretty high for what I received. Granted, I did not order the steak and lobster...maybe I should have. I got the cesar salad which was good followed by the crab cakes which were suprisingly not good. The flourless chocolate cake was tasty. The waitstaff was fine. Perhaps this was not a place to eat solo. I just did not care for it overall and the value simply wasn't there for me.
As for restaurants within walking distance, I would suggest Volare for Italian, The Purple Pig for shared plates/drinks, and The Gage for a tavern feel with creative takes on American cuisine and great beer options.
The overall takeaway for me is that this hotel was not lacking in any way and I really enjoyed my stay. I have stayed in about 10 different downtown Chicago hotels and this one ranks #1 for me. I will look to stay here again next time.

title: “an ok stay but overpriced; well, it's new york”
text: Went to ny a week prior christmas 2007; I booked the hotel through priceline but giving the high season I got the room for $330 before taxes and fees; which is a lot for what the hotel has to offer. I read the reviews on priceline and trip advisor and I knew the room was going to be small and indeed everybody was right! It is true, you don’t spend ur time in the room but I think you could use a little bit more space when u try to relax; The lounge/club is nice, the restaurant is nice and good food, the personnel is helpful. If you get the room for under 200 go for it, otherwise look somewhere else.

title: “Would avoid if possible. Quite old with very small rooms.”
text:
Rarely ever speak poorly about a hotel, however I would recommend staying elsewhere if availability exists. 
The rooms was exceptionally small, as was the bathroom (where only one person could actually stand in). You could not fit a desk in the room even if you wanted to (let alone a chair) and I found myself using the old radiator as a 'desk' for my laptop. 
I received a charge on my credit card 2 months after my stay. After calling multiple times to the front desk, they were not able to identify the charge. I have since had to contact my credit card company to determine what it is for (still pending). All and all, you can find better in boston for the same or lower price.

title: “Nice and clean!”
text: My family of 4 consisted of my husband and 2 sons ages 8 and 10 recently stayed here for a week of vacation. We requested two adjoining rms however they were not able to accomadate us. We were upgraded to luxury rms and about 8 rms . We never used any of the hotel ammenties since we were out sightseeing from the morning til the evening so i can't comment on any of those but any hotel staff we dealt with were very friendly and helpful. The rooms themselves could use a bit of a remodel but were spacious for NYC standards. Added note Beware of that mini bar in room items are very pricey! All in all we were satisfied with our rooms and service and have already told friends to try this place out.

title: “If you are a person who values life you...”
text: If you are a person who values life you will pay a few extra dollars for a different hotel. Outside doors remain unlocked for anybody to walk in. First walked in to 2 homeless men in the lobby. 1st rooms tv didn't work, 2nd room key didn't work cuz it was a storage room... not a guest room, 3rd room was HOT and had no remote. I was not about to request yet another room. After going back twice I noticed a sign that read no refunds. Ha, I wonder why. The amenities are very worn, stains on sheets, bed has dip in center from being so old, fridge made loud sound do to fan, door had dents and appeared to have chain replaced from somebody kicking it in, the elevator looked like it had 2 bullet holes. Its next to what appears to be a bad bar if you know what I mean. I made the mistake of being stuck here, I travel all the time for work and in 3 years this is by far the worst I've ever seen. Make the smart choice and don't stay here.

title: “the BEST!”
text:
I'd like to give my advice about this Hotel! I've been there 2 years ago . It was my first time in the US! Anyway I really loved it. The people were so nice and the sevices were all working! It's a vvery big building , above the central station. The room was very clean aand nothing misses in it! u have a big flat tv and a big HUGE wonderfull GREAT bed!!!!! I was the best bed i've ever slept in! the bathroom was clean and the wadrobe was very wise. the breakfast buffet was very full of any kind of international food! i really loved it. It's pretty close to times square and to the empire state building! i really appreciated this hotel! i reccommend it to you ! 
thanks for you attention!
best reguards,

title: “Great location but not outstanding hotel”
text:
Location was perfect for my trip. Easy to walk most places that I had to be. 
The hotel is new so it is fresh and beautiful. But at the prices they charge it should be. 
Gym is huge, well equipped and world class. 
Restaurant has a stunning and unique view but breakfast can be $40+ per person and the coffee is nespresso and the bread is supermarket variety. 
Service is Asian style which probably impresses many. But it also isn't quite right. My room had a sofa bed which was set up 2 nights in a row despite me traveling alone and telling reception. 
Excellent just not outstanding

title: “No Rooms - ----- Service”
text: Had reservations, but there were no rooms. They told us they would book us at the Penn, which is a third rate fleabag hotel accross the street from Madison Square Garden, not even in the Times Square Area. The room was like a coffin, filthy. A $300.00 a night hotel offers to put us up in a room in a hotel that costs $89.00 a night. Worse, the hotel lied to us and told us the hotel we were being booked at was a $250.00 a night hotel. Needless to say, we are beyond disappointed with the Mariot corporation.

title: “Top of the hill! Expensive valet”
text:
Top of Nob Hill is the Fairmont with its impressive entrance and a warm welcome from the reception and valet parking staff.
Yes, the place is a "little tired" but that's the whole point of it. The history (and relevant pictures) is quite rightly proudly displayed in the hallways off the opulent entrance. It is a bit of a conference type hotel and as a result you can find yourself walking down a few long corridors and the "walk to the tower" where the rooms are can be a trek. But the rooms are large, the bathrooms are luxurious and covered in marble.
Worth a mention was Tom Wolf, the concierge and his team, who got us some great seats to see the Giants. 
The Tonga restaurant was a lot of fun and very qwerky as they've decided to convert their indoor swimming pool into a Hawaiin/Asian fusion style restaurant that has a boat on the water that the band floats on. Bit wacky and if you dont mind missing out on that swim, then it works.
Only poor point was the valet charges that at $61/day were comfortably the most expensive on our recent drive through California.

title: “Almost Perfect”
text:
We loved almost everything about the Omni Hotel - check-in was easy even with 200 other meeting attendees arriving almost at the same time. We loved our room - very spacious with tasteful modern amenities - bed and bedding very luxurious - our room on the 21st floor was quiet even next to Petco Park. Everyone in the hotel was extremely helpful, friendly and professional except the one server on duty at the pool. She was the only one on duty - pool was full and should have been staffed more appropriately which probably explains her bad attitute. However after waiting close to an hour to get her attention we actually summoned her over and requested service...she flatly refused to take our order saying she was too busy. We watched her service other hotel guests who had been at the pool for several hours - she was continually running food and beverage for her "regulars" and wasn't interested in taking on anyone new. This was our only bad experience which is unfortunate because the Omni was perfect in every other way - 
The Omni is conveniently located around the corner and walking distance to the Historic Gaslamp Quarters which is a fabulous area to visit day or night. We loved the Omni - service around the pool needs improvement.

title: “as if I was staying at a friend's apartment (a nice apartment)”
text: As if I was staying at a friend's apartment (a nice apartment). The area is residential (for NYC) and a nice contrast to the normal tourist areas. The room was a one bedroom suite and quite large (for NYC). The hotel is an extended stay facility so plan on a trip to the local food store for snacks and drink as none to be found in the hotel. Don't underestimate the value of a nice retreat after the a day in NYC. The Falafel place down the street is great.

title: “One of the best hotels I have ever stayed in.”
text: I really loved this hotel for a lot of reasons. I had read reviews prior to staying here and had seen a few scattered negative reviews mixed in with a lot of positive ones. I decided to check it out just because it was so cheap and close to the places I was planning on visiting. All the staff (especially Francis) there were super nice and very accommodating. The first night I had one of the few rooms that pointed towards the street, which gave a great view but was kind of noisy. I asked to see if they had a different room for the next night and they were super nice about switching me. I think one of my favorite things was the free alcohol and snacks in the evening during the weekdays. Can't beat that! Also the location was fabulous. Great neighborhood and close to everything. I went with a few friends and they all said they would stay again. Rooms were a bit small, but for San Francisco at a great price in a great area, I was definitely blown away by everything I got! Thanks!!! :)

title: “Good business hotel”
text: This property is clean, well located, and the staff was very efficient.

title: “Bulk standard US 4 star”
text: Good confortable hotel downtown Boston. Rooms are spacious with the Heavenly Beds which always make a stay at the Westin worth your while. Had no problem with internet, room service was great - no glitch. Exactly what you expect from this kind of hotel. The breakfast buffet was nice but I have seen better in other hotels in downtown Boston. Do not look for anything funky here, it is just very functional and convenient. Direct access to the mall is a great plus as well.

title: “Very clean!”
text: Happy with our stay! Rooms were spacious, bathroom was roomy and very clean. Loved the shower head and water pressure. Good location. Ralph's across the street was convient. Parking isnt great. The breakfast was ok. Troy at the front desk was very polite and helpful

title: “LOVELY hotel and excellent staff so it pains me to report....”
text: ....thin walls! There is absolutely nothing that the staff could do on this one, but unfortuntately to me, sleeping is the most important part of the hotel experience. I am confident that the staff would have moved me to as many rooms as necessary to please me, but the trouble is that I was settled in bed, very tired and not willing to go through moving rooms at that point. The people in the room next door were not exceptionally noisy, but merely in a festive mood and there was a child also. I'm not even a 'light sleeper'. In the average hotel, I would not have been bothered by the noise, but I could hear the conversations next door...word for word...clearly...not muffled! The room was gorgeous, spacious, very clean,had free internet and the very kind staff had set me up in a room with a beautiful view of the Golden Gate Bridge. And my rate was under $150.00 per night including tax! Therefore, I will definitely stay there again if it is possible to select an end room with an empty room next door or perhaps a solo person. I hate to complain about this very lovely hotel, but since I lost a couple hours of sleep, I thought it would be helpful for readers to know this so that they can request quiet rooms if possible.

title: “Reliable and Convenient”
text:
I have stayed at this hotel over 30 times over the last 5 years and it is very reliable. The rooms are clean, albeit some are very small with very unusual bathroom configurations, but I guess that since I stay at corporate rates, I tend to get the smaller rooms. The hotel floors are gigantic and you can sometimes feel like you walk a mile to get to your room, but it is fairly priced and a minor inconvenience. The rooms are fully-equiped (iron, hair dryer, etc) and I can only remember one time when something didn't work. 
The lobby is to die for and is a glorious place. No matter how many times you stay here, look up at the ceiling and you will be wowed yet once again. The location is great, right in the heart of everything. I recommend this hotel.

title: “Okay but some problems”
text:
The hotel location is good, 10 minutes walk from the Metro.
Close and cosy supermarket "Giant" with tables for breakfast ( No breakfast at the hotel ) . Reasonable price.
The problems are : Small rooms with poor view , the hot water in the bath were cold and got warm only after 20 minutes waiting each time, The internet in the room didn't work even after I complained at the reception desk , and the staff at the reception are not helpful and not friendly.

title: “Wonderful place to rest in the city!”
text:
In a nutshell, the holidays were here and I was faced with the prospect of finding affordable accomodations for four adults ... needless to say I was not looking forward to my search after some initial searching! 
After a few hours, I wished there were cheaper places in downtown SF. I stumbled across this motor inn that seemed to have to have some pretty good reviews. I gave them a call and found a solution that fit our needs. Upon arrival, we were extremely pleased. My boyfriend and I had a large room with a king bed, a pullout sofa, small kitchen with microwave, mini-fridge, coffee maker (or cocoa if that is what you fancied), and a heating/air con unit. Our friends had an adjoining room with two queen beds also with a heating/air con unit. There was an iron and board also with a nicely appointed bathroom (good hot shower and plenty of extra towels.)Perks:1. Free parking - there were other places in SF under consideration until I learned about the nightly fee. Our Ford Escape rental fit snugly but to be honest, some of the spaces were a bit narrow on the nights that we got in late. We learned if there is a full house, they will park your car for you and move it accordingly if necessary.2. Free continental breakfast - translates to free coffee, cocoa, Tang, danishes (cheese, fruit or cinnamon). Nothing fancy but a nice a.m. snack to get you going.3. Free wireless Internet in our room. 
I believe they were making it available throughout so check before you making reservations if this is really important to you. There may be a deposit for the wireless card but I am unsure because we have an AirPort card in our laptop.4. Color television with HBO + basic cable. 
Our room and the adjoining one had a television for convenience. 5. The entire hotel is 100% non-smoking. There is a small area in the courtyard for smokers because there are notices posted prohibited smoking on the walkways between rooms.6. Frank and Judy. They are the managers of the property and they were some of the nicest people we ever met in the hospitality industry. Alex was also helpful in answering our questions so during our stay we had no difficulties with any of the desk staff. Off the top of my head, I can only think of one drawback.Unless you have the top floor, we noticed mid-stay that we could really hear the family above us. We had second floor accomodations so next time, we will definitely request the uppermost floor.Other than that, this place is a good value for the money. It is clean, safe, and the price is definitely right for long term stay in SF. It is not the top of accomodations but after all, do you plan to spend all day and night there? No. One's hotel room is a place to shower and sleep til your next day of fun in whatever city.

title: “Anniversary Weekend”
text: My husband and I came to celebrate our one year anniversary. We got a great price through Hotwire. The outside of the hotel and the lobby are beautiful. The room, however, was much smaller than I thought it would be. Renovations are being completed, so I hope the rooms will be updated. It was very quiet for us. Our room was on the 21st floor, and they are currently working on the 14th floor. They were a little slow to check us in. After working all day, catching a flight and arriving at 9pm, we just wanted to go to our room. Everyone was really friendly. The hotel was very close to the Taste of Chicago that is going on this week, and 2 blocks from Michigan Avenue.

title: “Not bad, not great either”
text: Not a bad price at $80 for one night on the AAA rate booked online through the Ramada website. The room was pretty small and no breakfast to be found, not even a continental breakfast. On the plus side, the staff were very attentive and prompt with the service at check-in. Tight parking outside and seemingly very full hotel for a Wednesday night. Didn't find it to be very noisy, however. We like the Hotel Circle area, as there are a few nice family restaurants for breakfast/dinner nearby.

title: “Awesome Place to stay...”
text:
After reading all of the reviews on here i was a bit pessimistic about the hotel....we found on their website a room for only $135 a night which is an amazing price for anywhere especially that close to times square (100 ft.) The rooms were clean and surprisingly bigger than what i expected and the staff was very nice...the bar and restaurant seemed dead but all in all i would definitely stay there again.....oh and watch out when you are looking in the mini bar, its electronic and charges the room when you take something our, even the $50 bottle of moet champagne that i took out to look at.
Stay there

title: “Not as high class as expected!”
text: We were recommended this hotel based on location, excellent service and comfort. We were informed by friends to request the new tower rooms as they are larger and more modern. Upon arrival I did just that, at the check-in counter I kindly requested a room in the new tower, the request was well received and we were on our way to the elevator banks. During our stay they were doing maintenance on the elevators banks but we thought this would not be an issue seeing as there were 5 elevators to choose from, little did we know. Our room was on the 5th floor (one of the lowest floors for guest rooms) and right next to the elevator banks! The room itself was spacious and clean and comfortable, no complaints there, but we could definitely hear the noise from the running elevators. During our stay it took up to 15 minutes (I am not kidding here!) after pressing the button for the elevators for one to arrive, and when it opened it was usually packed with people, so many we could not at times even squeeze into one! We also had a problem with our shower curtain rod, it was loose and coming off the wall. I had contacted guest services and nobody showed up the first day, the 2nd day I complained again and someone did "tighten" the fixtures, but the rod was still hanging off the wall! We also ate at the accompanying steakhouse at the hotel (which shall remain nameless) and the service was abysmal ! The waiter service was horrible! I must say that I had high expectations of such a prestigeous hotel chain, but this particular stay was very poor indeed.

title: “Excellant Hotel”
text: I am in the hotel business, no I am not with this hotel. This hotel offers excellant customer service, my room was very clean and the breakfast hostess was great. I just wanted to commend the General Manager, who did i not meet on this trip. Thank you for taking me while I was away from home.

title: “Renaissance LAX = Nice”
text:
I recently stayed at this hotel on a return trip to Los Angeles. I needed to stay near LAX for a quick overnight trip. In October I stayed at the nearby Marriott LAX which was very expensive and they didn't have their act together. This hotel, on the other hand, is very nice and much cheaper too. It also seemed much more relaxed and less convention like. The lobby wasn't noisy or too busy. The restaurant had a well above average wine list - much to my surprise. The hotel is a little gem at LAX. 
My stay was over a Friday night so I had a $99 (the Marriott was $119) weekend rate which is very reasonable price. The room was very spacious and had a large bathroom and the new-Marriott beds. The room also offered a Ipod radio as well as cd player, plus free bottles of water. Very nice touch. 
Being a Marriott Rewards member I was granted access to the concierge lounge which, I must say, was fantastic. This place offered well above the average appetizers including poached salmon, various cheeses, meatballs, etc. 
The hotel also has a cute-little gift shop and great gym (also outdoor pool if you have the time). 
I was on the 5:30 am airport shuttle and the shuttle (which also picks up people at the Marriott) was right on time and was a short 10 minute ride to my airline at LAX. 
This hotel is very nice an I highly recommend it if you need to stay near LAX airport.

title: “Extremely basic”
text:
The place looked promising from the approach… it’s right on the river, facing the beautiful River North area. The building, built way back when, is charming from the outside. And the lobby, while not grand, is also appealing. Once I got into my room, though… ho hum.
It isn’t terrible, but there just is not one thing about it that makes it the least bit special. I had a small room, which was fine, but it was just very bland. The bed covering is one of those bad synthetic things, there were only two limp pillows on the bed… stuff like that. There wasn’t even an iron or board in the room. The place just felt very cheap and kind of sad. My rate was $200, which was less than other properties the weekend I stayed. But in retrospect, I should have paid an extra $30 to stay at a place that felt more upbeat. 
My only plusses were: its location, the fact that I was able to check in early, and free internet. Those aren’t strong enough factors, though… next time I’m in Chicago, I’ll stay somewhere else. C-minus.

title: “Good upgrade from the Rhiga”
text:
Stayed for one night after dining at GR.
The hotel looks ten times better than the old Rhiga, some parts of the renovation still to come, especially the fitness room, but work is underway and temperary room is functional
Room design is different but functional, desk space is awesome, wireless internet worked great, two lcd tvs one in living area and small one in bedroom
we were taken aback by sofa at first - it was hard and a weird purpley color - but eventually we warned up to it, not fun to lay about on but worked for eating and watching tv.
No art on teh walls was a bit odd as well, dont know if it is coming or they are going for a bare wall look.
Bathroom was great, awesome shower not tub and that is fine by me, I love a big standup shower with multiple heads
was in an -02 room, private w/ 2 different rooms at end of hallbut smaller than the others on teh floor
service was ok, room was turned down at 4 pm, before we got bcak from work and cahnged for dinner, pretty bad
ordered room service breakfast and attendant insisted they only had cheddar chees to go on my eggs, I told him I would go next door to teh deli and gte him some swiss to put on my eggs and he put me on hold for a minute and cam eback and said ok they could give me a different cheese, really weird
asked for a usa today newspaper an dthey delivered me one that had allready been read, no charge though
sam the doorman is a hoot, real character that adds some fun to teh property
restaurant and bar scene are great, GR one of the best in NYC
Overall I like this hotel and if you dont want to pay for teh St regis, 4 Seasons or Peninsula it is a good alternative, not great lik ethose others but good....

title: “Nice hotel, convenient location!”
text: The hotel is very nice, rooms are accomodating--ours had a mini-fridge which was handy for our 6 night stay. We realized after our first night there that there are a bunch of restaurants on the Metro level (below the lobby) which the front desk didn't tell us about--that is also where you can catch the Metro and you don't ever have to go outside. Very convenient! Wifi is not free, but that's about typical. Pool is nice, rooftop and even though they say it's heated, it is still not very warm. It is about 3/4 mile walk to the Washington Monument--we actually had a beautiful view from our room of the monument. The Smithsonian Musuems are not far, along with the National Mall. I would not recommend driving, just because of lack of parking and ease of access to the Metro. Our cab ride was $16 from DCA airport. We also walked to the "Wharf" and had dinner..very nice!

title: “Beautiful, quiet, relaxing, peaceful!”
text: We had a wonderful stay at the Town and Country. Everything was clean, quiet and comfortable. The grounds are gorgeous. The staff is extremely friendly and helpful. Each day at the breakfast buffet we were greeted by Mary Mejia. She treated us like family or honored guests. Her hospitality set the tone for the entire day.

title: “Quick, enjoyable stay”
text:
We got a pretty amazing deal on Priceline for our double queen room of $89 + tax / fees for our one night stay, and were very pleased.
Check-in was a breeze, and the lobby of the hotel is quite elegant.
The room itself was very nice, but did smell a tiny bit of stale cigarette smoke, (however not enough for us to complain about.) Our room faced the back of the building - we could still hear the train, but it was not disruptive. The color scheme of the room / furniture was all very warm and inviting, the beds were very comfortable, and we heard nary a peep from other hotel guests which goes a long way towards happiness in my book. 
Our only (minor) gripe is about the parking situation. The valet is $35 a day, which seems a bit high, and there didn't seem to be any other options but granted, we didn't try terribly hard to find alternate parking.
The hotel has a very nice bar / restaurant off of the lobby, and the bartender was excellent. The location of the hotel is wonderful, and within easy walking distance of all kinds of bars / restaurants. We had dinner down the street a few blocks at Cafe Sevilla which was lovely, albeit very loud.
In all, the Hilton Gaslamp would have been a bargain at twice the price. We would definitely recommend!

title: “Lovely place - would stay again”
text: Thought outside looked a bit shabby on arrival but got a room facing marina and it was lovely - towels and robes provided, fridge, microwave, coffee machine. Extended family's room was the same. Booked bed and breakfast and was given thirty dollars to spend in the restaurant for breakfast - it had a great choice and couldnt fault the breakfasts - we spent that for three people with a little bit more added. Very calm - would have liked to have gone in the hot tub but thought it was a bit chilly at night but there were plenty of people using the pool and hot tub area. Sat outside the firefly restaurant drinking and was warm enough under the patio heaters. Really liked the Dana and would definitely stay again. Reception staff were really helpful we expected to pay for parking the car but this wasnt added on at the end so must have paid it already. We paid approx £30ppn (three in a room) so we thought good value.

title: “Enjoyed Our Stay at JW Marriott”
text: We had a nice stay at the JW Marriott. I'll be honest, it was a bit of a let down, because I had just come to expect the highest standards from the JWs. In many ways, this just seemed like a new Marriott, with better-than-normal service. Rooms were smaller than I was expecting. Bathroom was wonderful, complete with glass shower AND tub. View of Denver skyline was very nice. Of course, Marriott beds are great! Dinner in main restaurant was excellent, as was breakfast. You cannot beat the location. Plenty of great restaurants and shopping right out the front door. Breakfast food in concierge level was very good. Dessert service was pitiful - I swear they put out the same cake 3 nights in a row! Concierge level service was a little hit-or-miss. Several of the staff told us that they had just started working there and their inexperience in working with guests showed. All in all, this was a very comfortable home for our 4 day stay.

title: “Remodeled, downtown and average.”
text: Nice downtown location. Staff friendly. Elevators didnt work, confusing floor plan and vending machines were always empty. Just average hotel. Would probably choose another place the next time I'm in the area.

title: “Excellent hotel”
text:
I stayed at the Omni Houston for 4 nights in March. First of all, I got an excellent rate though travelzoo (75 dollars a night). I had a great stay. The hotel is spotless, service is great. There is a lot to do close to the hotel (good restaurants, great shopping) but you need a car (we had one so we were fine).
There's free wireless internet and complimentary morning beverage (you can choose 1 cold and one hot drink, plus a bottle of water). The swimming pool looked great but I didn't use it. Our room was very spacious, good bathroom too. The beds were very comfortable.
Parking is expensive but since we got such a great rate anyway, it wasn't a problem.
I found the hotel to be pretty quiet except for one night when the was a party going on and I could hear loud voices until after midnight. There were no problems on the other nights however. 
I had one minor (very minor lol) complaint: they didn't have Comedy Central and I missed my daily dose of Jon Stewart and Colbert.
Overall, I was very satisfied with this hotel, especially considering the price I paid.

title: “Great stay at the Holiday Inn Express”
text:
We arrived on Wednesday night. We had two cars with us, one went into the garage adjacent to the hotel and the other street parking. I had read that on Thanksgiving, the metered parking was free, so I left my car on the street for the evening and following day. Free metered parking holds true for Sat. 11am-12am, for the holidays. Check on twitter, I love Philly or PPA website they give current information.
Check in went in smoothly with Jared, he assisted me and explained in detail any possible holds or charges. While checking in, my daughter shared she forgot her toothbrush, and Jared promptly handed my daughter a toothbrush. We were pleased with this gesture, as my response to my daughter, was she was out of luck. 
The room was spacious, sort of narrowed a bit by the desk, and windows. Room was clean and all toiletries were available. Remote seemed to have needed a new battery. We all slept well, sheets were soft, and beds were comfortable.
What we did notice was that the walls were awfully thin, or it could have been that the guest were very loud. It sounded like they were in the room with us. However, it really didn't bother us, because we were up late as well. 
I do agree that with another, the air conditioning was sort of loud, and the bathroom fan kept going all night long. But I am not particularly picky. The t.v. was high def. , very nice. We actually had a very nice view in the evening, with the city lights. 
Breakfast had a variety, including a to go bag and tray that you can take back up to the room with some food items. Staff was very pleasant and healthful at breakfast. 
The hotel is centrally located to everything. There is an Ihop and dunkin donuts across the street. The hotel is located near to several bars and restaurant. We walked to Reading market terminal, the convention ctr was nearby, and even went to Chinatown. There were Wawa, and 7-11 all within walking distance. 
Only thing I would question is the need to get the parking through the hotel, rather than directly with the company. You pay 21.00 for parking through the hotel, daily and you can go in an out. But depending on your needs, paying the company directly may be cheaper. 
All in all, was a good stay, and did not have any issues with the quality, or service at the hotel. If your looking for luxury, this is not the place. If you looking for value, this is the place.
Thanks again to the staff, they were great.

title: “Great Location”
text: We stayed 3 nights and enjoyed our stay. The hotel was beautiful and the staff friendly and helpful. Even though we liked our stay, I would recommend avioding room 304. The room was spacious and clean BUT had no view as it was blocked by awnings above and below the windows. It also had a window unit that would not be very helpful in the heat of the summer. The bathroom was clean and had all the amenities that you need however it was very hot and became unbearable after a shower. The location was perfect. It is across the street from the Museum of Natural History (3 minute walk), less than a 5 minute walk to Central Park. Starbucks is around the corner but we enjoyed World Coffee each morning. 10 minutes away you have tons of resturants on Amsterdam Ave. to choose from. Time Square is about a $10 cab ride and there is a Metro station at the end of the block. I loved the neighborhood feel and would stay again..

title: “Showing it's age despite the great location!”
text:
I stayed here during late Nov on mix of Business and Pleasure from the UK. The access from the street is muddled as there is the Union Square access (pass Victoria Secrets) or from the Garage/car offload ramp which can be busy at most times. 
However once inside the check-in was fairly smooth but reputation in my view is of an hotel that is 'past it's best' and has lived on it past glories to much. The room I had was close to the lift and not away from the lift as requested in my Starwood account, I asked to be moved but was told that there was nothing else available. The bed was comfortable but took up almost 70% of the room space, there was only a small window and overall the furnishings and decor was poor and needed a much needed makeover. There was no tea/coffee make in my roomand I had to request it, also I requested my own refridgerator as the minibar costs are prohibitive. The Bathroom was small and tolietries were poor in comparsion with other Westins in the US and Europe.
The Oak Room is used for Breakfeast and at $21.50 for a full Breakfeast is not cheap and you could certainly find better down the street. You do not need to use this place for Dinner as there are many better and varied restaraunts in SF/Union Square area as well as Chinatown which is only 5 blocks/10 mins walk away, the doorman will direct you.
SUMMARY
This is an 'Grand old Dame' of hotels in SF and sticks to it's authentic attention to detail and historical association to the past, not to mention playing on it's location on Union Square, however that should not preclude it from providing a better and more up to date product. The staff are attentative and helpful and resourcful; but it seems that they are continously trying to plug gaps in a creaking and somewhat aged system in the hotel.
Would I stay here again?........probably not, there are superior hotels close by including the Omni, W, Hilton etc. So unless Westin/Starwood improve the product they may lose more people to those and other locations in future

title: “Great Experience”
text: I was definitely not expecting to find such a wonderful hotel experience at Magnolia, exceeded my expectation by all means. FREE wireless, downtown shuttle service, breakfast, happy hour drinks and cookies coupled by great location and very courteous staff (and very reasonable prices considering all this). You can't go wrong with Magnolia Hotel!

title: “Superb!”
text: Throughout the years, i have traveled to Washington often for business. This is my first stay at Sofitel and it has exceeded all expectations. From the moment i walked up to the front desk to register it has been all about making my stay better. Anna's recommendations of where to eat have been amazing. Overheard other staff saying Anna knew best places to eat in Washington and they are right! Sofitel is now my home away from home in Washington.

title: “Nice modern hotel, nice staff”
text: I got stranded by my airline in Denver, and put up for the night at the Red Lion Central. (It's way out east, far from "central" downtown, so is misnamed.) I found the place clean, comfortable, modern, and appreciated the courteous and efficient staff who checked in our busload of stranded, grouchy passengers late at night. Found the breakfast buffet the next a.m. quite good, fresh fruit, good coffee, very acceptable, but not remarkable. It has an outdoor pool and lounging deck. Did not hear or notice the trains going by at all but it is near tracks; a huge, long freight train did delay my bus back to Denver Intl Airport the next day. The neighborhood is unattractive, industrial but there are cafes nearby. There are worse hotels to be stranded in, in my opinion.

title: “Beware - they charge you more then they are allowed”
text:
If you think you have every stayed in a Hotel where greed rules, you have not been to the top of it.
I choose the hotel only as every suite has a balcony and I don't wanna stay in a locked room. For many other reasons my co-contributors have referenced in detail (breakfast, elevators, Check-Inn Staff, Management, non-existing green Policy) I cannot recommend this place.
But what experienced to me last time has pushed the envelope - they have charged me more (439.95 + Tax) then the displayed max. price (419.00 + Tax) in the room.
To be honest, I'm not upset about the price itself - I'm more upset that you display a maximum price in the room (and all my fellow travelers know that you have never paid the one) but this time I have been asked to pay even more.
We have then canceled the booking, went back to Hilton.com the next day, booked a new room (for 239.USD) and kept the same room - the girls at the reception did not help and the Managing Director just does not care.
Have a look at the Image from the Room and the invoice and make yourself the judgement if you wanna stay there!

title: “Fantastic Location”
text: We stayed here for 4 nights at the end of 2010. Fantastic Location! Rooms are small but good value for the location. This was out second time staying here and would definately stay here again.

title: “Excellent desk and breakfast staff!”
text: Upon arrival we were greeted very warmly by the front desk staff that was on duty. I did request a first floor room for my 80 year old mom whom was staying with us and was not accomodated but offered two single rooms at an inflated price that was declined. Breakfast service was outstanding and the food was identical both days we stayed here. Our room did not have a hair dryer, corkscrew or can opener in it. The hair dryer that was delivered 40 minutes after request was brand new in the box. The master room closet had trim missing from the ceiling as someone had gone in the access panel to perform some work and insulation all over the shelf in the closet. The toaster had crumbs and stuff all over and in it and hadn't been cleaned in who knows how long. The stove surface had swirl marks all over it and appeared to have spread whatever grease was on its surface rather than it having been cleaned. Room service never entered our room the morning after our first night. I'm not sure if they did after we checked out. This was truly a disappointing stay at a Wyndham faclilty and far less than we ever expected. The room items are the type of thing you would expect from a motel property, definitely not a Wyndham property. Not sure that I would stay here again after this past experience.

title: “Feels like a motel”
text: It's a Four Points, but worn, stained and musty. Workout room and bar were ok and the rooms were a good size. Some staff were super friendly and helpful, some were bratty and unprofessional. Location is on the edge of downtown in the dated touristy area, but you can walk to some interesting bars and restaurants within 5 to ten minutes.

title: “Great Location - Very Pricy - Not friendly”
text: Room was average size - bathroom needed updating. Location is great - 2 blocks from the air & space museum. Restaraunt was EXTREMELY expensive, the food wasn't great and the service sucked (Quizno's is just down one block). If location is important but the room isn't - stay here!!

title: “A fine hotel if you're not spending much time in the room.”
text:
I booked this hotel for an overnight in the city. I only needed the room to get ready for a graduation ceremony and sleep a few hours before checking out in the morning.
The location of the hotel is fine for getting around the city. I was able to walk to St. Patrick's Cathedral in just a few minutes. So if you're interested in the major mid-town attractions, this hotel would be great. My only issue upon being dropped off was the large number of people sitting and standing out front of the hotel smoking. You had to walk through a deep wave of smoke just to get to the revolving door. Of course, there's little a hotel can do about guests smoking out front, but it wasn't very welcoming.
The check-in was very smooth and the staff at the reception desk were very professional and friendly. A+
The room itself was TINY. The bed was comfortable and there was little noise from the street below. The bathroom could use an update. The grout was discolored, the tiles were coming away from the wall, etc. It just looked like it got a half-renovation a number of years ago, and then they forgot about it.
Overall, it's OK if your plan is to sleep, but it's not the sort of place I'd want to spend much time.

title: “Location is great!”
text: Very close to fishermans wharf. Everything is in walking distance. Even a trader joes and Safeway across the street.

title: “Fabulous Hotel”
text: From checkin to checkout, our stay was fabulous. The staff's professional, spirited attitude--be they reservationist, valet, front desk, or housekeeper--deserves 5 stars. For instance, mention in passing by one of us about an allergy to down brought an instant change of linens. The hotel's evening wine hour and morning's biscotti hour also distinguish the property as a cut above, and our group, which has stayed at many a biz hotel, had no problem whatsoever; in fact, a courtesy upgrade got us a fine meeting space with free internet, which even impressed our boss. And while we weren't expecting to dine at their restaurant, given how many fine ones there are to choose from in this neighborhood, as it turns out we relished the food, both dinner and breakfast. We're already planning our next stay.

title: “Great location, excellent value.”
text: Our stay at the Suites at Fisherman's Wharf was wonderful. The location right on the Cable Car line and near the bus line was phenomenal. The helpful staff at the relatively small hotel provided excellent, personalized service. Furthermore, the Suites were spacious and well-equipped with a kitchen and dining area. I had no complaints about this hotel, the only mild drawback might have been that it could be a little noisy in the morning, but I have found that in pretty much all hotels in large cities. The hotel also had a nice rooftop terrace to get a nice view of the city.

title: “Underwhelmed”
text:
I had one of those moments at The Marcel that I thought only happened in movies--I opened the door to my room, almost hit the queen bed with the door and then noticed that the one small window was almost entirely taken up by an air conditioning unit (room 203).
I've stayed in a wide array of hotels for business and thus am pretty forgiving about minor things that pop up--I know things aren't always perfect. But this particular room did not match up to anything I had seen on the hotel website, or on the Jetsetter website, from whom I booked my room. I knew I was booking a deal, but this seemed like a bit of a boondoggle. When I went to the front desk, the hotel staff did their best to accommodate my request for another room; while something on a higher floor (with perhaps more light) wasn't available, they were able to give me a larger room with a full size bed on the second floor. I'm still pondering why the smaller room had the larger bed...
The new room was much bigger and (relatively) brighter, thanks to a large window at the front of the building. The bed and linens were great and the bathroom was comparatively spacious with a full tub. On the downside, I thought the room looked a bit rundown and it smelled like something had been used to cover the odor of a smoker. Even with the window and all the lights, the room was still pretty dark. The floor also felt a bit unsturdy, which was pretty bizarre. 
All in all, I think The Marcel is really close to being a nice (and affordable) boutique hotel, but there are just some details that need to be addressed before I'd want to stay there again. The staff I interacted with, however, are a great asset to the establishment.

title: “Beacon Hotel is home away from home”
text: This was our second trip to NYC where we stayed at the Beacon. Great facility--clean and well maintained. Staff services are quick, polite and competent. Easy access to subway and bus lines. Fairway Market across the street. Many restaurants within easy walking distance. Laundry room is a great help. We will stay there on our next trip to the City.

title: “Great property, but...”
text: I've stayed at the Warwick twice. The first stay was great, the second a mixed bag. Although the room was fabulous, there was a funky smell in the bathroom and mold in the shower. The staff was very responsive and sent someone to look into the smell (which never entirely went away), but no help on the mold). Conveyed it to the front desk at checkout and in my review. I'd definitely stay at the Warwick again, but was a little disappointed that they couldn't resolve what should have been simple issues.

title: “Great value in NYC”
text: Just spent 4 days at this hotel, first time. I was really impressed. It is modern, well maintained and the efficiency and friendliness of the staff is outstanding. Although the location, next to the Port Authority terminal may not be great, it is convenient to the theatre district and other midtown attractions. The staff went out of their way to make the visit pleasant. It was my birthday and on arrival there was a cupcake in my room. When I checked out four days later the desk clerk remembered and said she hoped I had a great birthday! The hotel is quiet and the beds really comfortable. Will plan to stay there on my next visit to NYC

title: “Good hotel, a little different, but fun”
text: Room was clean, comfortable and had all of the necessary amenities. I had a corner room that was very bright with a nice city view. Location could be better as it is a little too far west, but not terrible as it is in midtown. Some sketchy blocks between the hotel and Times Square, I would not walk that route after 9 or 10pm. Service was very good.

title: “Horrible!!”
text:
This place was horrible! I stayed here with a friend and the first time she used the toilet, the water came back out of the toilet -discusting!! We tried to change hotels but seeing as though we booked with another agency it just proved to be too difficult....
The only good thing is the location - nothing else!!!

title: “Good Staff, Average rooms, costly internet”
text:
Stayed at the Grand Hyatt for a conference/trade show. The location is very good and the conference/trade show accommodations are excellent. Excellent access to the River Walk and River Center shopping as well as scores of great restaurants. The staff was very accommodating, especially the Concierge Service. (Thank you Melissa for all of your help!) However, the rooms were just average. The AC functioned less than effective as the return vent is right below the outlet. Basically, the air stays over on one side of the room making for a stuffy environment. They is no air vent in the rest room nor exhaust fan for the shower. More like a 2 star hotel. 
While this is a very nice business center hotel, the charges for the internet service are high and the service I paid for was spotty and extremely slow. I had much better service at "free wifi" hotels. I found this very unacceptable the primary reason for the average rating.

title: “Great stay. Great staff!”
text: I would say I'm an average consumer when it comes to critiqueing hotels. I'm reasonable and rationale. I was really happy & comfy in this hotel. No problems. It was clean everywhere. The hotel layout was great and just what we needed for 4 ppl in 1 room. The pool was good and the free breakfast. Best of all the staff were ALL pleasant & smiling the whole time even nightshift. Some hotel ppl act like they couldnt care less what u r saying, but i felt really accomodated here. Absolutely no complaints. I stayed here Sat - Mon for a High School hockey Tournament. They r pet friendly, so i brought my dog too for $25 xtra dollars. In the elevator there was a sign that said if your not happy w your stay here call the manager on his cell & it gave his #. That was really nice to see.

title: “Excellent location and service!”
text:
The hotel was was nothing but conventient and affordable. Just down the street from all the downtown shopping, dining and attractions such as the space needle, pikes place market and some shopping malls.
The service at the hotel was verry efficient and friendly. The food at the sushi bar was very memorable. The only down side are the small rooms and elevators. But oh well, didn't spend much time in the room anyway. Overall very clean and comfortable.

title: “Great Place for New York stay”
text:
We came to New York to be tourists and tourists we were. Steps from shopping, subway and food. What could be better! The room was a little small but perfectly adequate for two people. Always clean and well supplied. The a/c worked great and we loved the fact that we could actually open the windows. The continental breakfast was more than adequate to send us on our way each day and wine/champagne were wonderful to find after a day of touring.
The club room was great to use for just relaxing and to review the days tours.
The best thing was the staff. The front desk staff was impressive with their daily help for us. They printed maps and gave us detailed directions to the places we were touring. The staff at breakfast and cocktail hour were charming, helpful and efficient. We enjoyed it all. Probably lacks some of the things a large chain offers but when on vacation, who wants to be just another room number!

title: “wonderful experience”
text: I would definitely return to the Intercontinental Times Square. It was convenient to everything on our agenda. The hotel was beautiful and the rooms were contemporary and extremely clean. Every staff member was pleasant, smiling, very helpful and professional. I am in NYC quite often and can say that this was the best experience by far. The lounge is very comfortable and inviting.

title: “Right across the street from Universal Studios”
text: When visiting Universal Studios this is the right place to stay. The hotel is the usual good Hilton standard (the seafood buffet in the restaurant is five star with crab legs, oysters, sushi, sashimi, lobster, carvery and crepe stations etc.). It is clean, modern and a bit boring to look at but the location is a blast. Our room was on a low floor (actually under lobby level) and handicap friendly. we had the view of the hotel's outdoor pool but the high rooms have probably got more interesting views. Parking was not too expensive for Los Angeles and the staff was helpful. Tickets to the Universal Studios are sold at the hotel and from there it is a five minute walk to get to the park. I do not like when wifi is not included (you don't pay extra for aircondition or tap water, do you?) but it was at least not too expensive.

title: “Very nice, kid friendly”
text:
We finished a road trip from mammoth cave, ky with a stop in Indy. The omni was a welcome luxury after staying at roadside motels in rural areas. We entered into a beautiful lobby and staff was friendly and welcoming. I just booked a regular room with two queen beds and after I received my room, the front desk handed me these two backpacks with toys and crayons for the kids. They loved it!!! 
The room was clean, bright and felt new. Beds were comfy with down bedding. Large flat screen, mini bar and dry snacks - good bath toiletries. Typical 4 star. One neg may be the bathroom was small and warm, I didn't see a vent. We were only staying one night so it didn't really effect us.
My girls were playing in the lobby, pretending to be princesses and ballerinas and a security stopped and started chatting with us and gave us the history of the room and the hotel. He also took the girls and us to see the grand ballroom. We were impressed.
This hotel is connected to nordstroms.

title: “Great hotel, fair location”
text: The hotel was very nice, well maintained, clean. Staff was friendly and helpful. The baths were beautiful, although as others have commented, if the glass wall had been built a foot wider there wouldn't be any splash problems. However, only a tiny amount of water escaped. The rooms on the back (west) side were very quiet, although you just have a view of the wall of the adjoining property. Overall I'd probably have given the hotel five stars, but it's location was only fair. It's a good walk to most attractions--20-30 minutes to the Field, another five to the Shedd and another five to the Adler Planetarium. The Art Institute is probably the closest, about 15 minutes away at a brisk pace. Navy Pier and the shopping on N. Michigan are at least 30 minutes walk away. I don't mind a lot of walking, but most will spend some cab money, especially going out for dinner in the evening. The red line subway at the nearby Jackson stop on State Street is the quickest, most reasonable way to get to N. Michigan.

title: “Trying hard, nice location”
text: Nice, but small rooms. Attendant and friendly staff...very service oriented and helpful. Their parking during the week is close to $50/day!!! Suggest parking across the street at Bank of America. Didn't appreciate the tall doorman ogling my daughter as we walked out. Overall, a nice place, but nothing spectacular.

title: “Run away”
text: After leaving this hotel without staying overnight I mentioned to another visitor at my new hotel where this hotel is located and he started laughing, and I will quote him, "Oh Man! You were in the hood!" California Suites was shady to say the least. First entering the hotel requires two keys. One to open the cage that lets you into the main "compound" and then next to open your door. First thing I noticed is various individuals lerking in doorways. It was uncomfortable to be watched as you are making your way to your room. Upon entering the room I find right away that I have been lied too. A small microwave and a tiny fridge does NOT equal a kitchenette. We packed food and booked this location specifically so that we would save money by cooking in our room. I could have lived with this but the beds were the breaking point. First I pulled back the blanket to check the beds and the sheets were wrinkled so badly I had no question that they had been slept in. There was also hair on the pillow. When I sat down on the bed it made a distinct "Boing" sound. I felt unsafe in this room. When our friends arrived to join us and saw their room they also wanted to leave. They were a family of 5 and were given a small room with one double bed. When they complained they were told that the entire place was booked and that was all they had. Needless to say we sought and found another place to stay. We contacted our booking agent through Kayak and got a full refund. Kayak reports that they will no longer be representing this hotel (according to our representitive). Cheers to Kayak for their excellent customer service.

title: “Good way to end a holiday”
text:
Booked a night at this hotel based on (mainly)positive reviews on this website. More expensive than other hotels in the area, but my family were at the end of a road trip and wanted to dump the rental car and have 24 hours lazing in the room and by the pool. Shuttle from hotel was fine, but be careful about getting a pick up form the airport - they tell you to go to zone 4, but EVERY terminal has a zone 4, so make sure you specify exactly which terminal you are at.
Room was big and comfy. A/C was efficient and very quiet, blackout curtains allowed us a very welcome lie in.
Tried to have evening meal in the Courtyard Cafe in the lobby. Waited 15 mins to get order taken, then 40 mins for meal and when it arrived it was wrong. The waitress complained that they were busy with room service too, but would not eat there again in a hurry, especially as Ruby Tuesdays a block down the road does such WONDERFUL food. Other posters have made comment about its busyness - just try to eat at off-peak times. It is well worth the trip.
Pool and jacuzzi were clean and welcome part of the stay - courtyard area outside too for drying off in the sun.
Our flight did not leave PHL until 9pm, so we arranged to stay in the room until 5pm for an extra $99. Was quite a lot (for us) but defintely worth it to avoid hanging around the airport.
All staff were very friendly and helpful. Freshly baked cookies on the reception counter during the day were an added bonus. Would definitely return here if the need arose.

title: “Would give 6 stars if I could”
text:
This was my 4th visit to NYC and my partners 1st, we both work in hotels back home and I must say if the hotel we work in was to operate like this hotel work would be perfect. After a delay flight we arrived in the hotel to such a friendly gentleman (who seemed to work all the evening shifts) and were told where the facilities in the hotel were and where our room was (room 2201), check in was speedy, efficient and friendly (and being a reception supervisor of a hotel I should know)
When we got to our room (a kingsize room) we were so impressed, considering all the moaning reviews on here, the room was comfortably large the bathroom was fabulous and it was all so spotlessly clean. The free bottles of water were more then welcome after being awake and travelling for just short of 20 hours due to a delay......now I must say the bed, oh my god the beds and the hotel are like butter, and after a long day of walking and travelling round NYC this is just what you need, never in my life have I had such a wonderful nights sleep, they were so difficult to leave in the morning-and hello we were in NYC!!!!
The view from our room was over a rooftop car park but that was no bother to us, we were only going to sleep in it, and past the car park you could see the start of times square. Which brings me to the location.......couldn't ask for a better location. Just roughly 2 blocks always from times square, 6 blocks away from Macy's and Madison square gardens, 2 avenues from Bryant park and the New York library and the empire state building, out it this way the main attractions everyone would want to see in New York are in perfect walking distance so we saved a lot of money not having to pay for travelling around (although our feet are suffering now).
Few recommendations for anyone who hasn't been before you MUST dine at Tony DiNapolis just off time square the most amazing food you can eat and the cheapest place we at, a helicopter ride around Manhattan is amazing and.......wake up early one day (were talking like 530am to be out for 6am) times square is so quiet and you will get the most perfect un-hustled and un-bustled pictures you can imagine.
Put it this way we have come home back to England and everybody we work with now knows this hotel and the fab time we had in NYC so thank you very much for everything !

title: “Don't book this hotel if you are travelling as a family”
text:
Please read carefully all the other traveller reviews.
This is not a hotel - it is a conference centre.
We stayed for 1 week and had only 1 day that was not disrupted by conferences. The first was a 3 day "remax" conference that took over large parts of the hotel and closed of many of the communal areas.... The second was a 3 day party organised by playboy for 400 guests and, this meant that the pool and outdoor area were off limits to regular guests - totally unacceptable when travelling as I was with small children.
None of this was mentioned by my travel agent and I was not offered any satisfactory form of compensation.
Otherwise the hotel is good, but please check with the hotel prior to booking that you won't suffer a similar disappointment / inconvenience.

title: “Great location, facilities, helpful staff.”
text:
We stayed here for a few days before continuing a road trip around California. It was perfectly located for the main areas of San Francisco and for transport links, and we found a deal so we got one night for free.
The room was very clean and modern, with great views over the city on all sides, and the daily cleaning was performed excellently. I was sleeping in the pull-out sofa-bed in a suite room since there were three of us. It was very springy but still comfortable. We didn’t eat in the hotel except for a sandwich one day which was very good. The breakfast did look good and they offered complimentary hot drinks which were great before we needed to rush off after checking out. It definitely can’t be described as a family friendly hotel although there were a few staying. The gym looked great although we didn’t use it because of the age restrictions.
The staff were very helpful especially at the concierge where they all the nearby sites and stores and exactly how to get to them by public transport. We didn’t use the car park except for about an hour before leaving when we collected a hire car, and they were very prompt bringing it up from the car park. We found the hotel easily after coming off the BART train from the airport, which was very quick and great value. The location also meant that trains, trams and the cable car were very close to take you anywhere in the city.
The TV had a good selection of channels, although the picture quality of some of the channels was poor, while others seemed to be HD. The TV guide didn’t work on the main TV in our room which was disappointing. The hotel offered free wifi in the lobby by picking up a code from the staff there, which did also work in the room, however each code was limited to 3 hours. The mini-bar was very expensive like most hotels, however it would have been appreciated if some room had been left in the fridge for drinks which we had bought elsewhere.
Overall, the hotel was very good and we would definately recommend it to friends and family, although we might not have stayed there if we hadn’t received the offer that we did.

title: “Location, location, location”
text:
I stayed at this hotel one night for an executive business meeting. The location is fantastic. It's right on the water and I was on the 11th floor of the high-rise looking out over the pacific ocean. The room was spotless and nicely appointed. The amenities in the bathroom were nice. Each room had a little deck with two chairs where you can sit and read or look out over the view. The TV picture wasn't great but you're not there to watch TV. Also the mattress was a bit mushy and probably needed to be upgraded. 
We had a meeting reception at the hotel restaurant and clearly the restaurant didn't know how to handle a group like ours. Little appetizer dishes came out one at a time which doesn't really work for a group. It was also pretty pricey for what you got.
Overall I would recommend it for a family vacation, girls weekend or other personal trip. Not sure I would recommend this for business meetings.

title: “Reviews made me nervous,turned out fine”
text:
I knew the location was great,but reviews had me a bit nervous.Check out many web sites,found a good deal on NYC Tourist web site for club 5000 room for $157 night for 4 nights.
 Arrived at 11:30am after overnight flight,lobby a madhouse,but club 5000 has seperate check in area,no line,given keys and room right away,king and not 2 double I reserved but it worked out.
 Room was small,old,but clean enough.Bathroom older,smallish,but also clean enough and functional.Asked maid for extra towels,she gave and had in extra in room rest of visit.A/C worked just enough to keep room comfortable.View of other wing of hotel,but didn't care.TV in cabinet with 3 drawers,which is what you get..Brown carpet,a bit worn,but no ill effects on white socks.Never heard sound from nieghbors.Also in the room is a desk and a office chair and small lounge chair.I was happy with housekeepings service.
 Club 5000 offersbreakfast,bagels,muffins,danish,numerous coffees and tea's and apples or oranges.Two computors with printer also available on floor in club room.I would look to go at least with Club 5000 as some I met didn't seem to be satisfied with their situations at the Hotel.Would stay again

title: “Good Value for Money”
text:
I booked directly through the hotel website, and stayed 2 nights with my wife. The room was very clean and recently renovated, although the building looked old. Staffs were very friendly. Location is also good: silent and convenient, close to 2 subway stations and Central Park.
It's not a very gorgeous hotel, but certainly good value for money. We will stay again.

title: “Another great trip to the Biltmore”
text: I havent been back to the Biltmore in a few years. The renovations they have done to the resort are great! Loved Frank and Alberts and if you are going to try the spa I reccommend the sugar scrub. I have always loved this resort and it seems to get better each year.

title: “Professional service of old hotel, decor of new hotel”
text: Excellent hotel. Great location off of 5th avenue, close to everything including metro nearby. The hotel service was excellent, what's expected of brand hotel like Omni. The decor was also excellent, recently renovated, apparently. It has a great combination of modern room and classic service, something lacking in those "boutique" hotel whose decor lasts only for a few years and service utterly lacking. The room was really really big for NYC standard. Clean and classy appearance. Free internet if you register to their website. Only surprise - no tooth brush and shampoo/conditioner were not that great (not bad, but weren't cool like in some hotels this level). We didn't use, but the gym appeared quite awesome. Overall, it was a great stay - one of the few hotels that I would stay again out of more than 20+ hotels I've stayed in NYC around similar price range.

title: “Great location, expensive parking, very slow valet”
text: Booked this hotel via Hotwire for $125/night which is a great value. The hotel is a nice 4 star hotel with large rooms, new furnishings and a large marble bathroom. The hotel appears new both inside and out. Although the pool area is small, the pool was heated and enjoyable. The gym is not as big as other Westin gyms but it does have enough equipment for a long weekend. A very nice touch is every afternoon the hotel has music and free coffee/fruit juices along with snacks in the lobby. There are a few drawbacks to the hotel. Valet parking is a nightmare and extemely expensive, $25 per night. If you don't need your car during your stay park accross the street for 15.50per night. We waited over 1/2 hour for our valet car since the hotel is large but the car port is very limited. (Save yourself the hassle and park across the street). Checking in and out can be very very very slow because there is only 3 check in/out desks and it often has a very long line, allow yourself extra time. The hotel safe in the room is very small and remember to request a key for it at check in. The hotel is in a great location so enjoy your vacation.

title: “Clean, Efficient Value”
text: This was one of the few places in mid town available for $200/night after a long day at the US Open. No frills, but as advertised; clean, compact room, desk, chair, small but clean newish bath. No surprises. Wholefoods market across street on 7th avenue.

title: “Most Outstanding Sevice & Value in Chicago”
text: I have stayed at many hotels in Chicago over the years and the experience at "The Crowne Plaza" is the best I've ever had. The staff always remembers you by name, how impessive is that. The Managers reception is always a very friendly enviroment that makes people feel welcome. We have used their conference room facilities and the sevice and facility is equally outstanding. When ever you are in the Chicago area make "The Crowne Plaza" your hotel of choice.

title: “Excellent Location, Good Amenities”
text:
I chose to stay at the Boston Park Plaza Hotel & Towers for one night due to it's location (and a deal I found on a website). It is located one block away from the Boston Common & Public Gardens, 2 blocks from Emerson College and one block from the beginning of Newbury & Boylston Streets (ie, walking distance to Copley Square, Prudential Center, etc). It is also close to the T (subway), one block away from the Arlington stop.
The hotel lobby is nicely furnished and looks swanky. Reception was efficient and we received vouchers for a continental breakfast (which we didn't end up using). While the lobby is attractive and upscale, the hotel itself appears a bit old. This is probably because the hotel IS old (1920s!) The floor hallways are redone and are clean, no odd smells. The rooms themselves are on the smaller side; our room had a tiny bathroom (think: door swinging right past toilet, pedestal sink right next to the shower). The bathroom fixtures were updated for the most part, so the only downside was not being able to manuever around or have a lot of room to put toiletries.
The bed in the room was very comfortable; there was a flat-screen tv, black-out shades and a pod coffee machine. 
All in all, it was a good stay. I would choose this hotel if visiting Boston for the first time and intending to be walking around, visiting sites, etc.

title: “Good for Business”
text:
We used the Hollywood Hotel for a unit and crew base while filming a documentary in LA. The staff were very helpful and the facilities more than served our purpose while staying in the good sized and well equipped rooms.
The location was ideal for accessing all the studios and attractions LA has to offer.
Jason Shepherd - Producer

title: “great service and rooms”
text: Exceptional stay with incredible service. From check-in to check-out was very happy with service. Given an automatic upgrade to alamo view room. Room was terrific with the most comfortable beds. Hyatt chain must really be emphasizing customer service with their staff because they could not have been more helpful and attentive. The only downside was the pool was small and parking expensive. It was a very convenient location. Ground floor has exits to the alamo and riverwalk.

title: “Nice views and luxury feel”
text:
I like the location, the views and the stylish interior.
Service was good.
Decent value for money overall.

title: “Great location”
text:
I have stayed in many hotels around Union Square, and this is pretty good. The amenities are nice and the location is awesome. But honestly, for the price, I think I could've done better in the area.
The room was spacious and clean, and the view was amazing from the 26th floor (we had been upgraded because we are a Starwood member). The room was clean, but a little worn. Also, we had used a few items from the mini-bar the night we stayed; the next morning at 10:00 am the maid knocked on the door to refill the mini-bar, when I asked her to come back after check-out she got sorta pushy with me and wanted to come in right then. I was just glad I wasn't in the shower when she knocked!
Next time, given the money spent, I would go somewhere else. Like the Nikko or Parc 55.

title: “Nice new hotel, staff needs to get their act together”
text:
We spent 4 nights at the new Courtyard Liberty Station (Aug 8-12 2008). 
The good stuff: 
This hotel is brand new, and the facilities are gorgeous. It smells like new carpet when you walk into the loby (we're not used to that).
All rooms have a small (very small) refrigerator, huge flat panel TV, a pretty cool coffee maker, a good amount of space, and a large bathroom. The rooms on one side of the hotel are waterfront. The swimming pool is a decent size and it is heated so that you can even swim at night in San Diego without freezing in the cool air. The hot tub was very hot and big enough for six adults. 
There are plenty of tables outside and it was easy to find a spot by the pool.
The not-so good stuff:
Many of the rooms do not have a view. The first room that we were given, which we were told by the front desk was a water front room, had a tiny balcony (maybe 18 inches wide) and it overlooked a terra cotta roof on the second floor -- no water view. We called the front desk and were immediately moved to a better room, with a view, and a much larger balcony. The bigger balcony had no furniture - which I found strange.
We were there for four nights and our room was only cleaned by the maid only twice. One of the two times the maid came was because we asked the front desk that day to make sure that our room was cleaned.
When the maid cleaned the room, the small bottles of shampoo were not refilled. The coffee cannisters that can make one cup each in the room were not replaced after they was used. We actually ran out of toilet tissue on one of the days without maid service.
The hotel ran out of towels by the pool on three occasions during our stay.
