At checkout, I told management about our issues and no appologies were made. I was told by the manager that she had been "off" for the last few days. When I told her about the coffee she told me that the hotel may be out of the in-room coffee, but that complementary coffee is available to all guests in the loby and that I should have known that from reading information left in the room.
Anyway, we did like the hotel, regardless of our small problems. The location is pretty central. We were able to get to Old Town for dinner in about 10 minutes, Ocean Beach is about 15 minutes away, and La Jolla Cove was about 25 minutes away. 
Our kids really enjoyed the pool and the firepit is a nice touch at night. I rated this hotel above average, because I think that the hotel has great potential and it opened for business only very recently.

title: “Very Nice Hotel”
text:
Recently stayed at this hotel. The room was small but beautifully decorated and clean. Lobby is also very beautiful. The hotel is at 42nd and 2nd which is a bit out of the way of but I discovered you could take the "7" train down from Grand Central to Times Square if you didn't want to walk.
I would highly recommend this hotel to anyone!

title: “Awesome location and fantastic value for NYC”
text: Grandparents, parents and two boys aged 10 and 12 stayed here for 5 nights over the Xmas period, in a 'suite' - essentially 2 small connecting bedrooms (1 with QB and other 2 x DBs) with one bathroom. Very neat, clean but compact rooms. The heating was out of order but a reverse cycle aircon provided warmth (if a bit noisy!). Breakfast was included in the very reasonable price but was nothing special - loads of carbs on polystyrene. Staff were very friendly and helpful. Location was fantastic - very close to subway station. The one thing we found sad - not a Christmas decoration in sight! Not even a HINT that it was Xmas time - the main reason we visited NYC at this time of year. Oh well ... the city didn't disappoint!

title: “Large Room”
text: We tacked on a day to our vacation in Philly and ended up at the Raddison. We had come from the Marriott where we stayed 5 nights. On the plus side, the room was a double and it was one of the largest I have seen recently. The staff informed us upon checking in that we would have to have a king room as no doubles were available ( we were on a girls' weekend.) We checked again when we returned from shopping and asked if a double room had become available...it had, and they moved us. I did appreciate that. The location was nice...but I liked the downtown location of the Marriott better. This is a smaller, quaint hotel. There is a nice little lounge for cocktails..we did not eat in the restaurant. The room was okay.....lighting was poor and the outlet situation was lacking. Two girls with blow dryers , hair appliances ,and cell phones to charge was like playing musical chairs with the plugs! The carpet was in need of a good steam clean as well as the furniture pieces. Overall, this would be a good place if you want a big room and are not concerned with the little details, if you are super picky....look elsewhere.

title: “Econo lodge review”
text:
What you pay is what you get. The rooms are clean, but the hotel is located nearby a busy road and a bar. It is a 20 min walk from downtown. Wifi internet is available, but the connection is very poor in some romos.
Breakfast is minimal, and often finished am. Fine for a night or two, but not for a longer stay.

title: “The " Ugly Sister" of the Catamaran Resort.”
text: We do not care for this hotel. While it is located in a beautiful location, the rooms are old and the reservation staff misleading. This property is associated with the Catamaran Resort across Mission Bay which is much nicer although more pricy. We don't have anything bad to say about the place other than it is a "depreciated" property...well worn and on the older side.

title: “Just okay stay”
text:
We just stayed at the Days Inn Graceland and it was average. The location was great and I recommend walking down to Graceland so you don't have to pay $6 to park at Graceland (what's up with that?). The breakfast was decent and they had a number of tables in the lobby to sit at. The room itself was decent. I could tell the furnishings (comforters, throw pillows, counter top in bathroom, lamps) were new. The blankets on the bed and were really worn out. The bathroom was clean and it even had the new shower curtain rods that give you more room in the shower.
I would recommend this Days Inn to people who want the convenience of staying right next to Graceland, but if I went back to Memphis I would probably choose a different location.

title: “Great location and very reasonable”
text: Me and my son were on a father son trip and some how we stumbled on to this Geat little hotel.....the room and bathroom were small but very clean.....the beds were comfortable and the linens nice and fresh......we were busy running around for 5 days and this little Hotel was perfect!!!!!!!!

title: “Short Visit but everything was Nice.”
text:
We arrived on the airport shuttle pretty late at night around 9:30 PM. The check in process was pretty long, almost 30 minutes as there was a line, but with only one clerk, she was working as fast as she could and was pleasant thru the whole process and helpful. 
We went straight to bed, had a wonderful hot deluxe breakfast and caught the 7 AM shuttle back to the airport. 
So I used the business center to print out boarding passes and everything there was nice. Lobby was very nice and pretty. Rooms were adequate but not fancy. Nice bedding and everything we needed including enough towels. 
Shuttle was quick and handy. Checkout was very fast and efficient. The lobby was so nice that I thought the rooms were interior but all the rooms I saw were exterior doors and I did not find a way to the lobby with cover. In the morning it was raining and we had to run thru the rain with 4 pieces of luggage to get back to the lobby for breakfast and the shuttle. I did not see an elevator also and had to lug 4 pieces of luggage up the stairs. Other than that, it was a nice experience and would stay again.

title: “Great Place to Stay in San Diego”
text:
I stayed at the W with my husband and four-year-old son. No one, guest or staff, gave us a sideways glace for having a child there, and for such an upscale hotel, that was welcome. I found the hotel, rooms and bar very chic, but comfortable. The cabanas near the pool were a fabulous place to lounge, very fun experience. The rooms were quiet, elegant and comfortable. And you can't beat the proximity to the Gaslamp District. 
We ate at the hotel restaurant for breakfast - it was great, the service was prompt and courteous.
We lucked out and got a great rate - so sign up for their specials by e-mail.
So many of the hotels in San Diego are tired and in desperate need of rennovation (this is about our 20th stay in the area), but the W is an exception. Highly recommended.

title: “Very nice and conveniently located”
text: I recently stayed here for a business conference. No complaints other than the restaurant at the hotel was overpriced. The place was clean and the staff were professional. It is conveniently located. A little expensive but it's NYC.

title: “I had a totally different experience here from the ones described.”
text:
I was naturally a little perturbed by the other reviews about this hotel and my prejudices were given more credence when I saw our hotel lobby was effectively a door between a Chinese restaurant and an internet café. However, there was an extremely friendly and pretty girl in reception who upgraded us to a 3 bedroom suite (between two of us) and gave us all the information we needed about Manhattan. Our room was very spacious with a glass divider in the middle allowing a couple of blokes a bit of privacy and distance from each other and I think we paid about 60 dollars between us for it. The bathroom was fine, I don't remember any particularly noxious smells and the only problem was the slightly rusty windows.
It is in a great area, extremely cheap and although I can see how one more accustomed to smug grandeur wouldn't enjoy their stay here I found it better than suitable. Perhaps it would have been a different review if the room had been a box with a bunkbed and shared bathrooms (as we had at the Pickwick Arms hotel) but it was a large enough room to chill out in and not be on top of one another and actually bigger than 4* hotels I've visited. I've stayed at many hotels and this is the only one I've ever been sufficiantly motivated to write a positive review for. I can't guarentee you'll enjoy your stay here, but my own experience was far better than the others I've seen described.

title: “staff and management terrible”
text: I checked in, everything was fine I had a nice sleep and the next day I went out to get breakfast. When I came back my fridge was gone. I knew I had a fridge to begin with because I put my drink in there. There was only an empty space. I went downstairs and said my fridge was missing. They said they took it becuase it wasn't included in the reservation. I told them they can't give someone a room with a fridge an then take it out the next day while I'm gone, shady people. I told them that the reservation doesn't say I get an iron, coffee maker, hot water, air conditioning and internet. But nonetheless all of those are included and no one took those out. It's becuase I booked for a lower price than most when I checked out the rates the day of. Never go to a hotel that changes its mind on what amenities they give you one day and then take it when you're gone.

title: “Good experience”
text: The hotel was as described but when reservations were made, there was no mention of a shared bathroom. I found out before we got there by calling about something else and asking. Not much of a problem and it appeared clean. The room was small but we knew to expect that, but it was clean and the beds were very comfortable. Yes, the elevator was slow but we managed to take the stairs to the fourth floor most of the time (exercise!). The walls must be thin so it is a bit noisy. The staff was very friendly and helpful. Although parking is promised, we had to go to 3 parking lots associated with the hotel (which were full) and finally got them to find us one but was $55/day plus $12/day extra for oversize (Yukon). The other lots were $30/day. The location is great and there is a little Amsterdam Deli on the corner of 79th and Amsterdam that was perfect for us. The subway is close and very easy to get to Time Square -first time users and we felt very safe. Nice residential neighbourhood. I suggest taking the Gray Line Hop on Hop off bus tour. Great way to get around and see the sights with informative guides. For shopping, I suggest Canal Street for purses and pashminas and we had good luck with Macy's and K-Mart, both on 34th Street. Would love to go back ...not enough time to explore Central Park and Rockefeller Square.

title: “I liked this place - stellar NYC location”
text:
I booked the Room Mate Grace hotel for one night, as we had a wedding in NYC. Booked through Hotwire for $249/night, when everything else was well over $300/night, so definitely a savings.
Location, right off of Times Square on W 45th Street was great. Lobby is super-small and not impressive at all. We got there at 11 am and our room wasn't ready (check-in isn't until 3 pm), but they graciously held our bags so that we could explore the city. At the front desk they offer, for purchase, all sorts of things you can stock the mini-fridge in your room with - beer, soda, wine, snacks, etc...nice convenience.
Our room was ready at 1 pm and sure, it was small, but very well designed for its size. We were in Room 509 and faced W 45th Street, but noise was not an issue at all - double insulated windows - so we thankfully didn't hear a thing as we slept. Bed was very comfortable, linens are of fairly high quality. There is a small plasma TV right in front of the bed which was perfectly adequate. The bathroom is a bit odd, with a sliding door between the shower and toilet area, so you can't have the shower door and the door to the toilet closed at the same time, because there's only one door, but it was clean and functional (and hey, this was only for one night.) Shower pressure was decent and liked the rain-forest shower head. Mini-fridge, iron and ironing board, as well as a hair dryer are all provided. The only thing I didn't like was a cheap set of plastic drawers for your clothes next to the sink/fridge set-up. I think they could do better than that, looks like something for about $10 from Wal-mart. There is no room service, but they do provide menus for ordering in from local restaurants.
Breakfast in the am, which is included in the room price, was very decent, continental style, on the 2nd floor. Muffins, toast, crossiants, bagels, fresh fruit, cereal, hard-boiled eggs, yogurt, juice and coffee were offered. Great coffee, by the way. The staff was constantly replenshing, which was great. 
The indoor pool is something else. Located right in the lobby, and accessible by the 2nd floor, it is small, with a swim-up bar that opens at 5 pm. This is not a pool for small kids. There are a couple of steam rooms and a gym as well within close proximity of the pool. It turns into a club at night with young (think under 30's) splashing in their suits, drinking martinis and grooving to the DJ. Only in NYC! It seemed to be quite the scene. When we got back from our wedding at 1:30 am, it was still going strong. We were tired, but thankfully, we could not hear the downstairs noise at that time. 
I'd stay at the Room Mate Grace again without question. It is not a fancy hotel, so if you are looking for a grand hotel experience with a sprawling lobby and extra amenities, this isn't your place. But for a well-located, boutique-style, solid 3-star hotel with clean, quiet rooms and comfortable beds in NYC at a "decent" NYC price, you can't go wrong.

title: “Nice hotel but needs some upgrades”
text: I am a Diamond HH member and was upgraded to an Ambassdor suite. Room was spacious but carpeting was threadbare and ripping in places. Pool area was nice and lazy river is great for relaxation. We like to play tennis but tennis courts here are ful of bumps and cracks. After a multi-million dollar renovation, I would have expected much better in these areas!

title: “Disapointing and going down hill fast...”
text:
This was the second time weve stayed at this hotel, dissapointed with the room this time.
We stayed in room 206, you could hear EVERY movement the people in room 306 above made, even all their bathroom visits!! When they used the water it was practially impossible to hear anything in our room for the noise.
Our shower head was 4 feet off the floor, we had to sit down in the show stall to shower! the sink was in the bedroom not the bathroom! very poor water pressure aswell.
Patio door wouldnt open, kept jamming. Poor TV reception.
The only saving grace is the Location, however there are others we will use next time in just as good a Location for very little more money.
The restraunt underneath the hotel however is FANTASTIC, World Famous offers fantastic food and views while dining. Even the Cafe" Be Curious" on the boardwalk next to the hotel is excellent value for money, both of these are highly recomended, however the hotel isnt.

title: “Great Hotel”
text: My wife and I stayed here recently for four nights while I was in town for a conference. We absolutely loved the hotel. I booked a junior suite because Expedia was having a great deal. Very roomy, clean, and comfortable beds. Great view of the John Hancock building. The staff was very friendly and helpful. The location, a block off of Michigan Avenue, is excellent. We ate a half-block away at Coco Pazzo Cafe, and would highly recommend it. We also liked Bistro 110, which is a couple of blocks away. For something convenient and casual, Gino's East is right next door. Although temperatures were a little cold when we were there, we hung out a little at the outdoor rooftop bar, which is nice. Drinks are overpriced, but that's a big city hotel bar for you. We would definitely stay here again.

title: “Best trainer ever!”
text: When I went to use the gym, Sam Guiragossian offered to work with me on weight training, as well as core abdominal work. He was thorough and patient. He went above and beyond by scanning the routine and emailing it to me. What fabulous treatment.

title: “New York stay 2 nights”
text: Good location for Battery park and Financial district. Our room looked straight out onto ground zero. Modern clean hotel with modern comfortable rooms. Our door key failed to work one night and the staff were most helpful. Would stay there again.

title: “Fantastic hotel!”
text: We only had one evening in San Francisco and this was a fantastic location to be in. They hotel was very impressive. The rooms were comfortable and clean. I wish we had more time to enjoy the room and hotel.

title: “One of my fav H Inn in NYC”
text: I've stayed here several times for business and pleasure. The rooms are large as a NYC standard, and breakfast is pretty good. Hotel stuff friendly, conveniently located although not the greatest (I don't mind staying in the West side). I've heard the noise from next door once, but that was the only time. I'd come back here and this is one of my fav H Inn in NYC!

title: “I loved this hotel.”
text: It was convenient to everything. The staff were very helpful and polite. The rooms well decorated, clean and quiet. Overall a great experience. Planning to stay there again. P.S. loved the cookies!!!!

title: “Great location for exploring Washington”
text:
Overall this hotel was OK. The rooms are clean and the beds are super comfortable. Internet is fast and free. There is a decent small gym in the basement. It is walking distance to Union Station. There is also a nice view of the Capitol.
I had a room on a lower floor. I suspect that the bigger (upgradable) rooms are a better choice. My air-condition unit was old and noisy (with a few missing buttons). I had the main big hulking air-conditioning unit for the hotel right outside my window. Because my room had an interior view, it was rather dark. And the noise from the outside air-con unit drove me insane. One thing this hotel needs to look at is soundproofing. I could hear the late-night conversation in the adjoining room (up to 2 o'clock one morning). On my last day I woke up at 5:30 am. The person next door's alarm clock was going crazy, and clearly my neighbor is a sound sleeper. That alarm clock rang for at least 20 minutes! You can also hear the garbage trucks when they start picking up stuff at 6 am every morning. The rooms are also just a bit cramped, and I bumped into stuff over and over. The decor might be whimsical to some, I am not a big fan of floral patterns and that "old" hotel feel. But this is really just personal taste. I am sure other people love it.
Service at the hotel is great - friendly, efficient staff and welcoming doormen. There is a great space for breakfast just around the corner. The bed is really amazing. But with all the noise disturbances I did not get a great night's sleep. I would recommend higher floor rooms.

title: “Mediocre”
text: Average hotel. Well located. Room was large but decor is tired and needs updating. Service was slow and staff was not helpful.

title: “Great hotel!”
text: Stayed one nite. Very nice room with a fantastic view. Very clean. Great service. Doorman was very helpful in getting us cabs. Great location.

title: “Rooftop Party at High”
text: Hotel Erwin hosted the perfect party on Saturday. Everyone had an amazing time due to the set up, fantastic service, and yummy drinks and food. Our server was so on top of everything, sweet, and fun! It was crowded and with a reservation they gave us the 5 star treatment!

title: “Accessible, and functional”
text: Stayed here for two nights in early November. Hotels further up the valley were sold out so I ended up down here in San Jose, further from Palo Alto than I wanted to be. That said, this was quite functional. It's laid out a bit more like a motel in the sense that you can park near an entrance to the hotel that takes you straight to your room. I was on the third floor and the room was perfectly functional, with internet access etc. It was clean and safe. There were several nearby quick serve restaurants (Vietnamese, Mexican) and it's really convenient for getting onto 101 and close to San Jose airport. Overall nothing to write home about, but certainly more than adequate for a mid-priced business stay.

title: “New York isn't for the hotel anyway”
text: We stayed at the Tudor from the 8-12th of Oct. Nothing fancy. Booked on Priceline for a reasonable price. The room with one bed was TINY, but the room with 2 double was OK. It didn't matter, we didn't come for the hotel, anyway. We came to see New York City! The rooms were clean and there was an in room coffee maker and hairdryer. There is a bar and restaurant downstairs, altho, a bit pricey and we didn't use it. There is a restaurant a couple blocks away called PAX. Great breakfast at a reasonable price. We were only a short walk from Grand Central Terminal and probably about 20 minutes walk from Times Square. Would stay there again, but not at full price, only if I was booked there by Priceline. Didn't find staff overly friendly, but neither was the rest of New York City staff.

title: “Best Hotel Ever!!!!!!!!”
text:
Our Park Hyatt whotel stay was the best in our travel experience, which is extensive. As mentioned in other reviews, the staff was beyond phenomenal. You were greeted in a pleasant manner by every member of the staff regardless of where they worked in the hotel. The desk staff and door attendants were more than helpful; each person went out of their way to ensure we had an enjoyable stay in Washington DC. 
The hotel had complimentary bicycles, which were new, and included helmets and locks. We were able to bike around to monuments and memorials instead of walking (which you could do). When distance was an issue we used the metro, which is a short walk from the hotel, to get to other places.
The room was wonderful for a 4 day/3 night stay. It had an extremely comfortable bed, large rain shower, and soaking tub, flat screen rotating television, large sitting, and wonderful décor. The restaurant was pricey, but the hotel is in Georgetown and within short walking distance of many restaurants and cafés. I highly recommend Furinos of Georgetown for breakfast. We ate there daily for breakfast and met some wonderful people while dining outside. The Guards, a few doors down, was a nice, pub that had a good lunch menu (very lean corned beef).
The fitness room has all you could want for a workout, including aerobic balls, medicine balls, free weights, weight machines, ample treadmills, and some elliptical machines. The pool and workout room are in a strange location.
Fabulous stay all around!!!!!!!!

title: “Good location, nice staff”
text:
This hotel worked well for our family during our trip to Philadelphia. Its proximity to buses, the underground trolley, and the trains that go to the suburbs can't be beat. Independence Hall was a bit of a long walk (perhaps b/c it was so cold). We had a nice selection of restaurants w/in walking distance. All the staff were friendly and the concierge was helpful. If you don't have a car, choose this hotel. 
We had a less-than-wow experience with room service the first night. They were out of a number of dishes b/c of a recent snowstorm and delayed deliveries. After that I could not convince the kids to eat at the pub, which is probably deserved a chance. The room was fine, nothing special.

title: “remodel is nice. Doesn't have wifi”
text:
For a business hotel of this size to not have wifi is pathetic. They have high speed internet but in order to use it you have to sit at the desk in the room. The cord is 1 foot long. On top of that you have to pay 13 dollars to use it. I don't mind paying for wifi but not for wired. 
 No mini-bar, which I guess is a mixed blessing if you, like me, eat the whole mini bar by the time you leave.
The rooms are fine. Nicely remodeled. Small tub in the bathroom. Everything is very clean and new looking though.

title: “A great NYC experience”
text:
When my wife turned 50, I wanted to show her a special weekend in NYC. I originally chose Eventi because of the midtown location, and because of the reputation of the spa. We got more than we had hoped for. Omar at the front desk checked me in. When I told him about my desire for a special weekend, he helped direct me to a luxurious 1 bedroom suite on the 19th floor with a fantastic view towards the east and the Empire State Building. The marble bathroom with jacuzzi was functioning artwork. The lighting was adjustable to create the desired mood in any of the rooms. Omar even sent up a complimentary bottle of wine for the birthday girl. The following morning, my wife was pampered at the spa. The spa treatment was excellent. 
It's easy to spend a lot of money in NYC, it's nice to get something special at the same time.

title: “For Tight Budget Travel”
text:
This was a nice clean little place. Can't say enough about the fine staff. Rooms were small - (I'm quite tall so factor that in). One of the two elevators broke down making for looong waits for the remaining one. A lot of noise in the corridors - woke us up a couple of times. The location is a bit dreary, need to walk a few blocks to get to most attractions or take cabs - although there is a great flea market in the Garage across the street on the weekends. The breakfast corner was a nice touch and their coffee was excellent. I did miss room service in the morning though, but thats me.
Conclusion: If my budget was tight I'd go back - but I'd probably choose a higher end mid-town joint next time.

title: “Perfection...but expensive”
text: We have a Marriott rewards card, so it was wonderful to see a special check in/check out line just for rewards members. The view from our room was AMAZING. The elevators are so much fun. The location was smack in the middle of Times Square. Great places to eat all around. Room was quite large, very clean, and very QUIET (which is rare in NY!) Beds were incredibly comfortable too. Would highly recommend it if you want to treat yourself to a nice place to stay. My only complaint is how expensive it is! But if you put it in perspective of where you are, and how nice the place is, it's right on par with all the other hotels right around there.

title: “Amazing!”
text:
We stayed at Hotel Sorella before and after a cruise out of Galveston... It was AMAZING! We would highly recommend it! The City Centre area was fun, there is a mall nearby as well. The hotel was great, very cool decorations and set up! Our room overlooked the pool and the main City Centre square. Breakfast in the morning was one of the best ever! Fresh fruit, cereals, etc. They also made cappuccino / espresso / etc upon request! We will definitely stay here again!
We have already booked their sister hotel (Hotel Valencia) in San Antonio, just on the strength of Hotel Sorella

title: “The Loft Tours Suites are incredible”
text: My wife and i recently stayed at the Hilton Gaslamp Quarter Loft Towers and i have to say it was an amazing night. Great location close to all the good clubs and bars. Clean rooms and great room service.This is a location we will stay at again some time soon.

title: “"Excellent Stay in an Excellent Hotel"”
text:
Just returned from a weekend stay at the Omni Los Angeles @ California Plaza....and I must say that I was hoping for the best, but was so pleasantly surprised that this hotel met all my expectations and surpassed them. I was traveling with 13 other ladies for a weekend get-away/shopping/relaxation trip and I was responsible for making the accommodations, so I was a little nervous and my hopes were that everyone would be comfortable. I am "very" particular about where I lay my head and I wanted to have the best for our getaway without breaking the bank. The Omni was magnificent, the service was grand, the rooms were beautiful with a neutral decor, marble baths with separate shower and bathtub, large closet space and larger than average room. The beds, well, let's just say that some of us wanted to stay just to sleep in the "heavenly" bed just one more time. The beds are big, fluffy with lots of pillows and ultra comfortable. 
The room service was excellent and very timely. A few of us ate at the Noe Restaurant in the Hotel on the first night, granted it is "very" pricey, but you get what you pay for. The service was par excellent and the food was wonderful. The swimming pool is a little small and there is no jacuzzi...I did not get an opportunity to visit the Spa, but the prices were quite high. The next day some of us ate in the Cafe, which was very nice and the food had a really nice flare to it. The location was perfect for us as we planned to go shopping at the Garment District which was a few blocks away. There aren't many places open around the Hotel during the weekend, but right outside the door of the hotel, there is a Day Spa where some of us went and had manicures and pedicures and there is also a Starbuck's that stays open on the weekends. In the same area right outside the Hotel in a Plaza there is nightly entertainment, i.e. bands, etc. And of course, you have the Museums and Disney Concert Music Hall right near the Hotel that is also open on the weekend. 
The Hotel is close to the freeways and Saturday evening some of us went to the Universal City Walk for dinner and fun, which was about 20 minutes away. The Hotel has a courtesy Town Car to take you and pick you up from anywhere within a 3 mile radius. The Valet was steep at $28/night, but there is no other place to park, oh well.....All in all, this is a great place to stay and the only place that I will stay when in downtown Los Angeles....I have stayied in downtown L.A. several times in the past and the other Hotels cannot hold a candle to the Omni....I have already booked another stay with them next month. My hat goes off to the Omni Hotel and Staff and a very much deserved "Thank You" for making our weekend so wonderful!

title: “STAY AWAY!!!! Not worth it... dirty, run down, smelly, and bad location.”
text: Wanted to stay in the downtown area; am a member of the Best Western Gold Club, and decided to add some points to my balance and stay here. We are not super picky - we just need a bed after all, since we will be out and about most of the day anyway. It was difficult to find rest and comfort at this location. Besides the horrible noise pollution going on outside, the guests in the hotel do not care about being quiet at 2am either - and the staff could care less. The room was dingy, if not out right dirty, smelled like mildew, and had stains on the carpet. Tiny bathroom, not big enough to turn around in. Bad TV reception just to add insult to injury. Walls and lines felt damp (humid area, but why would that matter indoors?) Location is much to be desired, homeless people sleeping next to the hotel, and I think I actually witness a drug deal going on outside my window.... pay a few extra $$ and stay somewhere safer, cleaner and more comfortable!

title: “Very nice stay with the exception of....”
text:
HOT WATER! 
The room is clean, fresh, and in great shape. The bed experience, yes experience, is awesome. Everything was absolutely perfect except the water temperature in the shower. 
No matter what you did, the water was lukewarm at best. Not sure if they were having boiler issues, or what because no explanation was given by staff members. 
This hotel is attached to the Houston Galleria, so many restaurants, shopping, offices are close by. They have a new elevator system which is brilliant! You enter the floor you are going to on a keypad on the wall, and it tells you what car to queue up for. Then, that car goes only to the specified floors. It completely eliminates the "stopping at every floor", or the always annoying kid who presses every button. GREAT idea. 
All in all, a good stay at the nice Westin Oaks. One last thought..... $15.00 a day for internet is criminal. But when you force guests to pay, and the internet service is painfully slow.... shame on you.

title: “Close to all....great gym”
text: tagged along with my husband on a business trip since i had never been to Denver - loved it (other than all the homeless all over the streets downtown) but Hyatt was great. walking distance to everything, rented a car 1 day to go to Pike's Peak. the gym here is the best hotel gym i've ever seen - even better than fitness clubs. if you work out its worth staying here just fo that! the regency club which was part of our room package, was great. Tip: the Aveda Spa training school is literally around the corner = had the best facial there i've ever had and at a fraction of the cost - book early though!

title: “This place is very nice (and a little advice to the hotel)”
text:
We spent a terrific week here in April. I loved most things about this hotel and we plan to return to stay here again. Most of all I liked the friendly staff. When you travel with two children you can always tell if the staff is trained to be kind and helpful to children. This staff has had top training and are wonderful. 
The rooms are very nice despite the decor which is fake Italian (i.e. mirrors made to look worn and distressed and lights made to look like dripping candles). It is true that you have to walk down endless hallways to get to them but they are nice. I asked not to have any air fresheners placed in our room and they listened. We had a little porch with two chairs facing a golf course. My father had a porch (facing a pretty garden) that was too small for even one chair. A big plus would be an addition of screened doors for the porch because it would be nice to have the fresh air without getting mosquitos in the room.
The family pool is not huge but is large enough when the hotel is not too busy. We had it almost to ourselves in April. The landscaping is attractive. The staff is helpful with towels, etc. The first time we used the pool the staff started to clean with a loud smelly machine and we left. I thought they might have waited until it was empty. Also, there was a bit of a mold problem around the pool drain areas that needed to be attended to.
The Amaya restaurant is a great place for breakfast and we tried to go there every morning. We liked to sit on their outdoor terrace. The waiters give top notch service and are super friendly. My kids loved the pancakes and the adults liked the salmon bagels. All were happy with the fresh squeezed orange juice. Once the gardner came around just as we sat down and kept mowing the same patch of grass in front of the restaurant. After several of our requests to make him stop a staff person finally went over to ask him to leave. The hotel should arrange that gardeners come after breakfast and before lunch to work in that area. 
At night the hotel provides a variety of musical entertainers. We stayed up one night to listen to an older guy with a great voice play piano and sing standards. He even obliged us with a request for Billy Joel's "Piano Man" complete with harmonica. 
The hotel has several walks on it's property and the surrounding area. We were lead by one of the staff to the beginning of two trails that started past the horse stables. We walked on the one that turned right (the less traveled one) and soon noticed that there were ticks crawling all over every one of us! Disgusting. We felt that the hotel should warn the guests that they have a tick problem on these paths and told them so when we returned to shower and change. 
We took a stroll around the hotel property and were surprised when a dog came barking out of a ground floor room. The owners stopped it before it reached us. It made me think that I would not be very pleased to have a dog barking in a room near me. Not relaxing.
The spa is good one. My daughter and I went for a massage at the same time. She liked hers (my only complaint with hers was that the lady had a cold) and I liked mine. 
For Easter the hotel made it fun for kids by having an egg hunt and other activities.
Advice to fellow travelers: stay at this place if you want a relaxed and upscale hotel with great service.
Advice for the hotel:
Get rid of that awful scented candle that is in the lobby area. It smells very artificial. Also, please get rid of all the fake books and yard sale non-English books that are glued together in the "library" area. Instead, get real books in English that guests can read while visiting you and leave for others. So much more refined and useful!

title: “Great location - air conditioning NOT required~!”
text: We are well seasoned Canadian travellers, age 48. Booked this hotel through the hotel website, after checking numerous review sites on the web. We LOVED this hotel and have no hesitation recommending it to others. Like a previous poster, we had the good fortune of visiting this beautiful city during a heat wave. Not having air conditioning was a non issue for us, and the lack of morning fog was a bonus! The overhead ceiling fan did a more than adequate job cooling our room. We had requested a top floor (7th) non smoking room on the "back" side of the building, and we had a lovely room. No view mind you, but we spent so little time in the room this was also a non issue. The bathroom was small but spotless, the bed very comfortable. The rooms are a bit small, but ample room for 2 adults and their luggage. The location is great for shopping and theatres, which we didn't do; and convenient to public transportation for sight seeing, which we did. A bit of an aerobic excercise walking up Nob Hill and over the top down to Fisherman's wharf, but well worth the effort. Slow down and admire the architechture and interesting sights both up and down the hills in every direction! Lots of restaurants and coffee shops in the area, we enjoyed Foley's Irish pub a couple of blocks away on O"Farrell. The hotel's continental breakfast of coffee, juice, fresh fruit salad, croissants/pastries, yoghurt and cereal was more than adequate to fill us up and tide us over before take away crab cocktails at lunch! We hope to back for another stay at this gem of a hotel.

title: “Charming but cramped.”
text: The Hotel California is located in a historic building a few blocks from Union Square. Its age shows, with a dusty lobby, slow-moving antique elevator, and small, bare-bones rooms. It's charming, but there are comparably priced hotels in the area that appeared to be much nicer, judging by walk-bys. Free breakfast is nice, but it is vegan. Wine and cheese reception not really worth your time. We did however find the Union Square area to be perfectly central to the city.

title: “Great Service”
text: It's not fancy, but it's clean, the location is great, and the service is really good. Vicki, who checked us in, went out of her way to accommodate our requests. She is really terrific and we'll definitely be back.

title: “Great Room, But Don't Eat There”
text: Stayed in an Executive King Suite and wasvery impressed with the corner room, large marble bathroom, and view of the city skyline through the floor to ceiling windows. Awesome beds, pillows, and executive lounge access. We were in town for a concert at Joe Louise Arena. We're not gamblers but we do love great food. The mall-like "food court" had a strange feel to it, not to mention the endless cigarette smoke wafting through all the restaurants from the casino. Food service staff are generally uninterested in guests. My "homemade" mac & cheese came out of a box. Two bites and I was done. Stay for the rooms, but eat elsewhere.

title: “High five for Revere Hotel”
text:
This place is funky, energetic and brimming with feel-good vibes as soon as you enter the foyer. There is edgy artwork everywhere, smiley staff, a gushing concierge (who became our newest best friend, thanks to helpful advice) and the best toiletries ( with a peppermint zing). The beds are comfortable, with millions of pillows and Shakespearean quotes on the wall. It also had location, location location in its favour.
It was way beyond our normal budget, but I am glad that we had a splurge. I am ready to move in forever...

title: “great stay”
text:
My wife and babe stayed the weekend at the Dupont while in town for a wedding. I had stayed previously (in the jurys hotel days), and I was surprised by the changes. The place is now aggressively modern and hip, with chill-out music and high design aspirations. It's all a little over-the-top, but the staff is super-nice and the location is as good as it ever was. The noisy Irish bar has been replaced with a lounge-y place (great for working during the day). The room was nice -- fancy tv, a walk-in shower, kiehls toiletries, comfy bed, decent free wifi, etc. 
No complaints on noise from neighbors or the street (we were on the 5th floor, in a corner). 
I'd go back.

title: “Great stay at The Roosevelt!!”
text: My family and I just returend from a vacation to New York City where we stayed at The Roosevelt Hotel. It was such a great location!! Only one block to 5th Avenue and the fabulous shops. Just a few more blocks to Times Square and Rockefeller Center. (Came in very handy when we walked to The Today Show at 4 a.m.) We even walked to Central Park one evening, only about a 30 minute walk that goes very fast with the scenery on 5th Ave. Hotel staff was great, no complaints there. The room wasn't the largest but was certainly clean and updated. For the price and location we most definitely recommend staying at The Roosevelt!!!!

title: “Very cool hotel let down by 1 member of staff”
text:
The royalton is a very slick hotel, great location, just up from Bryant Park between 5th & 6th. Very easy to miss as there is no sign outside just a big imposing door. Communal areas are a design statement that will not be to everyone's taste, it is dark and feels more like an upmarket private members club than a hotel lobby. Rooms are of a good standard and size. The bar "44" is excellent, the function of cocktail making is turned into an art form with exceptionally good bar staff.
Breakfast is a bit of a let down for the price but not a major issue. The only thing that spoilt our trip was the attitude and knowledge ( incorrect directions, then total disinterest when we asked for some help with reservations) of the concierge, really poor for a hotel of that standard. We did complain and received an apology but it just didn't feel the same after our interaction.
Will we be back, not sure, probably will but make sure we don't need help again.

title: “Great location, friendly staff and great comfort.”
text: We have stayed at the Paramount in Portland several times but this was our first visit to the Seattle location. We were in town to watch the Mariners vs. Dodgers games. Location to the link transit to get to the stadium was awesome. Staff was friendly and helpful especially the valets! Room was very comfortable and we enjoyed every minute of our weekend in Seattle.

title: “Nice stay”
text: The location was a little out of the way, but this was a very nice place. They must have gotten a special on flat screen tv's because they are everywhere! Breakfast not that great. Staff very friendly and helpful. Room was very nice with comfortable bed. 6 pillows on the bed, granite in the bathroom, large flat screen tv. Location makes it possible to hit the main roads and freeways with little trouble.

title: “excellent mid-town location/rooms clean, quiet and comfortable”
text:
stayed for four nights in August, room was small but fine for two people in NYC, queen bed was comfortable and there was a new flatscreen tv, 14th floor window view was back alley but good background of gothic building across alley, room was quiet and cleaned properly,
staff in lobby were very helpful and polite, dj's spun relaxed beats in the lounge on some nights and bar was quite popular, very centrally located for walking city and very close to 6th line subway

title: “Wonderful week in NY at the Affinia Manhattan”
text: We had enjoyable stay at the Affina Manhattan, we had a studio suite with very spacious bathroom, it was ideal, as our Daugher's wedding was on, and we had lots of room for the occasion. The location was also ideal, very close to Penn Station, Macey's and the Empire State Building. The staff were very friendly and the bar and diningroom were fab, very modern. It was a little noisy at night, but we were in the centre of NY, the city that never sleeps. We had air conditioning in the room and comfortable beds.

title: “Fantastic location at a great price”
text:
Hotel service was brilliant, clean and friendly. Rooms aren't the largest, but you go to NYC to explore, not stay in!! Very close to the number 6 subway at 33rd and Park (takes you up the east side to the Bronx and downtown to Brooklyn Bridge), loads of coffee places and resturants nearby. Pick up the little cards in the lobby as they can give you discounts to places and products. 5-10 minute walk to the Empire State Building, Times Square etc.... Recommend taking the bus tours that go from Times Sq, brilliant way to see places and its a hop on-hop off service. Had a fantastic time, can't wait to go back.
ENJOY!!!!!!!!

title: “PERFECT location and modern decor - yummy breakfast!”
text:
This place was a steal!!!! 
Located in one of the BEST neighborhoods - Chelsea. Only a block from the 1 train that can take you all the way uptown or downtown in a straight shot. A couple blocks from the fabulous Chelsea market and all of the best restaurants on 8th ave.
Room was a nice size, bed was sooooo comfy and everything seemed brand new and remodeled. Modern/contemporary decor is especially to my liking:)
The breakfast was awesome! The oatmeal was perfect, they have yogurt, croissants, muffins, eggs, usually a meat, fruit, juice, cereal, waffles made to order, etc. Really, this breakfast will save you TONS by sticking with you all day long. Cookies hot and fresh at 3:30pm daily and hot coffee and teas available all day for free in the lobby. 
I will definitely consider this place again in the future.

title: “Nice Staff - Shabby and Dated Facility”
text: Stayed because all other downtown & airport hotels full for convention. Positives: (1) The desk, restaurant, and housekeeping staff all helpful, cheerful, and very pleasant except doorman who upon being asked for cab pointed outside and said I would find one (only doorman I ever met who did not want to earn a tip by helping out with bags or cab). (2) Beds are comfortable. (3) Food in restaurant ok though room is dark. Negatives: Hotel is dated and dark 1970's drab brown and beige with little lighting. Clean but shabby in lobby and on "Executive" floor to which I was assigned. Alas, the advertised "Executive Lounge" on the floor was unavailable because it was rented out to some construction company as field office. The electronic keys did not work and required one to repeat insert process 10-20 times each time one entered room. Room was drab, clean, smelled slightly of a stale locker room, with "Sleep Comfort Bed", flat screen TV, and old floral paintings. Bathroom is small with standard amenities and odd shower curtain that barely reached tub rim and therefore leaky. Staff advised that six floors were used as USC dorm until this Spring - maybe why lobby and elevators look so beaten up. Gym is adequate although TVs on treadmills broken. Overall: Hotel needs to be renovated and room rates lowered until then. Probably ok for visiting USC and one night stay for a tired traveler, but not one I would recommend to anyone looking for a nice stay at a hotel.

title: “We got what we paid for.”
text: Hotel is dismal. Bed is old and hard! Smells. The AC is on but doesn't cool the room. Pool area was nice. Tv is nice. Brkfst served at 7 am. We leave at 5:30 am so we'll miss it. Free wifi. Not fast enough to load my episodes of LOST. Eager to check out! Front desk was friendly but not very professional. The reception counter was built for tall people in mind. If you're short, they can't see you. I wouldn't reccommend this hotel.

title: “WOW! I didn't want to leave this Hotel!”
text:
5 Star ++ Hotel.. Another hidden gem in NYC...(Quick walk to Time's Square & Hell's Kitchen area) 
Amenities and Services provided at this hotel including the SPA... can only compare to Heaven! Ink48 Hotel Spa was fantastic.. Friendly staff and incredible atmosphere!
Also the hotel room was huge (for NYC standards)...
This made my stay in NYC one to remember :)

title: “Great location. Excellent staff”
text: Our family of four stayed at the Grand Hyatt for 5 days during our vacation to Washington DC. The hotel is centrally located and a great spot to take in all the sites including the White House, monuments, Fords Theatre, etc. Our reservation included breakfast daily in the Grand Cafe'. The buffet was AMAZING! Wonderful food and variety offered daily. If you go, request Phillip to be your server. He will exceed your expectations in meeting your every need. Martha also makes fantastic omelets. Rooms were very clean and QUIET! The hotel was 100% booked our first two nights, and I never heard a noise from our room. Staff was always friendly and accommodating to any need we had. Highly recommend.

title: “Nice rooms, nice people, great courtesy and a piano bar/lounge at is very civilized”
text: When we travel to D.C. and don't need to stay near the Capitol, we love to book a room at the Fairmont near Georgetown. It is an easy trip from Reagan National, in fact easier than to downtown, there are many restaurants within very short walks, Georgetown is just over the bridge 5 blocks away and the happy hour in the lounge is affordable and most refreshing. But, the special touch is Derrick, the piano player in the lounge on week nights. He remembers us when we arrive, even if we have not seen him in 12 months, he plays wonderful riffs on standards, and, you can talk with your company and not have to shout.

title: “THE Park and Cruise Choice for Long Cruises & SeaWorld combination.”
text:
We found an excellent park and cruise deal here - with a fantastic 5 star room. Here's what we did: we reserved one of the newer rooms in the buildings called "Bayside". It came with free shuttle to and from the cruise ports and FREE parking for the duration of our 12 day cruise. The Dana at Mission Bay is adjacent to Sea World and a 15 minute shuttle ride to the cruise terminal, but most hotels near the ports either jack up the price of a park and cruise or start charging your parking after 7 days, and they mostly have poor reviews and shoddy rooms for the price.
If you were to need a day or two at SeaWorld before or after your longer cruise this would absolutely be the perfect choice - and Mom's and Dad's will feel like heroes for this selection if this is the situation you are in. In our situation the cost of parking nearer to the cruise terminal for our 12 day cruise would nearly pay for the room. If your cruise is short, or you flew in, there is that much less incentive to stay here. It might still be my choice if I flew in because the shuttle does the airport, the cruise terminal and Seaworld.
We read all the reviews - they are so mixed I was sort of worried, but here's exactly what you need to know. 
Older rooms are rooms 101 to 829 - we didn't see any of them but understand they are older but remodeled. For under 100 dollars I'd guess they may be just fine, most overlook a parking lot and will feel much more like any older motel.
The new very nice rooms are in two adjacent curved buildings, each 3 floors tall. Again, they call these "Bayside".The first building (rooms 1100-1320 are more pointed towards a park with the bay being to the left and beyond that, a distant overpass. I would probably avoid these rooms as well. The second new building (rooms 2100 to 2320) are where you want to be, and I'd especially request a third story room as they overlook a lovely bay. The room number would then start with 23XX (second building third floor)
The first floor does not have private balconies, but the second and third floors do. There is a nice elevator. The rooms are exquisite, really they are, and along the lines of any 5 star resort. You can read about all the amenities at their web site but we didn't really use any of them. I feel certain that cars are safe here - hotel parking is gated but the long term is not, still, it's location makes it seem safe.
People were friendly, the shuttle clean, the directions clear, the lobby beautiful, the room exquisite, and I got the free parking in writing due to some other reviews here but it was never questioned. 
No bad surprises - and isn't that what you love about TripAdvisor?

title: “Bring Your own Ice Box LOL”
text: The room didnt have a refridgerator nor microwave which I felt it should .Other then that It was a very neat and clean hotel and the room was nice ..I put my sign on the door stating I wanted me time and the cleaning lady came in anyway ........maybe she wanted to see something I dont know but she said sorry and left...When I got home and got my credit card statement I had a charge from the room for $2.50 ..I called because my room was prepaid and the hotel shouldn't have touch my card so the lady asked me about the bottel of water in the room......SO Bring Your own Water.........LOL

title: “Best hotel we have ever experienced!!”
text:
Anybody who stays at this hotel and does not enjoy the experience has an issue with life.
Great location, walk out the door and you are virtually in Time Square. As such you are in the heart of New York.
Nothing is a problem for the staff at Casablanca. Little wonder they have the number 1 rating on Trip Advisor
We had a Premium Room with King Size Bed that was tastefully furnished and very comfortable. The bathroom was fantastic.
The healthy continental style breakfast at Rick's Cafe was great and made all the better as a result of the friendly service provided by the two young ladies working there. I am normally keen to have a fully cooked breakfast when on holidays, but Casablanca's presentation of fresh fruit, bagels, cereal, yogurt, juice etc etc more than satisfied my breakfast needs and has nearly converted me to a healthier breakfast regime.
Happy hour at Rick's Cafe from 1700 to 2000 was fantastic. It is an opportunity to meet other guests, share a wine and nibbles and generally relax after hard day exploring the wonders of New York or as a prelude to attending one of the many shows that are in very close proximity to the Casablanca.
We stayed at the Casablanca for 5 nights and could not fault any aspect of the hotel. It was a wonderful experience and we will be back.

title: “Was ok”
text: Needs to get coffee machines in the rooms. New carpet would be nice. Great staff. Awesome views and location is fantastic. Great hotel for pets. Dog park close by. However, the homeless and drug peddlers on the boadwalk takes away from this hotel.

title: “Great hotel and location”
text: This was a good hotel with pleasant staff on the front desk. The room was a good size and quiet. As a HHonors gold member I had access to the Executive Lounge. The breakfast was good. The only criticism I had was the lack of courtesy by the staff over the weekend. The reception was on the phone the entire time I was in the lounge and did not acknowledge you on entry or leaving. Otherwise I would recommend this hotel in terms of room standards and especially location as you werer close to so much within in easy walking distances.

title: “Beautiful hotel in a fantastic location!”
text:
This hotel is perfect for explorating San Francisco. It's only aprox 100 metres from Market Street, where you can either walk or catch busses, trams, trains and cable cars.
Our room was on the 30th floor so the views were fantastic (even during the fog!). Don't worry about being up high, the lifts only took about 5 seconds to get up to the 30th. You're more likely to have your ears pop than for it to take to long! The room was spottless and really comfortable. The coffee maker in the room with Starbucks coffee was a great touch and very much appreciated after a long day exploring. The staff in the hotel were brilliant and really helpful. 
Our only complaint about the hotel is the prices in the restaurant. We only ate there once but I think $60 for a small breakfast for 2 people is just too high (2 eggs and a sausage and a glass of juice). I'd recommend the Italian restaurant across the road for great food and fun atmosphere. There's free wifi in the lobby but it's not a strong signal. The wifi in the rooms I'm sure is of a better quality but it cost $14.99 a day!

title: “New York's Best!”
text:
The Palace is by far the best hotel that we have stayed at in NYC. Rooms
were very clean and spacious and the staff could not be more accommodating. Took my daughters for their birthdays and the last night there they delivered a beautiful cake for them. Have stayed at a lot of hotels in NY and this one is by far the best. We will return.

title: “Wow.. Great Location..”
text:
Stayed here in may 2005 for 3 nights. 
Didn't want to Leave!!
Hotel is central to all shopping and attractions.
Shopping mall across the street.
Plenty of dining options within two blocks.
Walked to Safeco and Qwest Field(Seahawks), took about 20 minutes.
Was only a $8 cab ride to the stadiums.
Only a $35 cab ride from Airport.
Staff was awesome, room service great, view from room outstanding.
I will be staying here again in November and look forward to it!!!
Great value due to location and room quality.

title: “By Far the Best in Venice, if not LA Altogether”
text:
From the moment I booked my reservation on the phone to the time we left, we were treated like VIP's by some of the kindest staff I have ever dealt with in an American hotel. Kind and courteous isn't enough to describe each staff member. When you stay at a "hip" or "trendy" hotel you almost expect to be given the cold shoulder; it's the exact opposite here. 
In addition to the staff going above and beyond, the hotel is awesome. The roof deck is incredible and the pictures do not do it justice. The food in Barlo is really good and fairly priced. If you want Venice, look no further because it's the number one location in all of Venice-literally the center of all things Venice. 
I will absolutely stay here again and highly recommend it to anyone. The target market is the hipster, younger crowd but it's not overly rowdy and everyone is welcome, from what I saw. I will go out of my way to stay here the next time I'm in Los Angeles even if I'm doing business in another section of town. It's really that good.

title: “beautiful hotel close to everything”
text: I spent 8 nights here recently, this hotel is very very nice, very spacious, the staff is very courteous and friendly. The Hotel itself is very nice, not overly modern, not overly classic, just a very straight forward hotel. The room was very spacious and comfortable with a huge bathroom and awesome shower. Very close to tons of restaurants on 8th and obviously, times square is right around the corner. Overall I was very pleased with this hotel and would stay there gladly for a trip to NYC.

title: “Great Hotel. Beautiful!”
text: Great Rooms, Friendly Staff, Love the 2 free drinks you get and cookies and milk at bedtime. Breakfast was free also. You get a lot for what you pay. Great price.

title: “Enough room to share and be happy”
text: Room were clean. Beds comfortable. Easy to use A/C controls. Two sinks is heaven and there are not even next to each other which is much better - for privacy purposes. Rooms are large - we shared with another couple at the last minute and all 4 of us were very comfortable. Neutrogena brand toiletries were nice. Pool cushions are awesome. I would definitely stay there again should I need a local hotel. WARM Cookies provided at check-in is a treat.

title: “Great Hotel, Great Location”
text: My sister and I stayed here for 7 nights, Saturday to Saturday. We had a one bedroom suite with 2 comfortable double beds. The room was clean and spacious. It was nice to have the 2 rooms as you could relax on the couch and chairs without having to sit on the beds. Each room had a nice tv. Bathroom was a good size too with the sink area being outside of the shower and toilet area. This is a better arrangement for 2 women trying to get ready for the day. As advertised, there was a small kitchen area with a 2 burner cooktop, a full size refrigerator with ice maker, a microwave and a dishwasher. We didn’t really use the kitchen though. Just the refrigerator to store drinks and the microwave to heat water for tea. This hotel is conveniently located. It’s about a 10 minute walk to the McPherson Sq metro stop and about 15 minutes to the Dupont Circle stop. It was also about a 25 minute walk to the mall area. The hotel serves a nice hot breakfast in the morning. Usually this consisted of scrambled eggs, bacon or sausage, and sometimes potatoes or biscuits. You could also make Belgian waffles. They had donuts, English muffins, bagels and bread for toast. They also alternated between toaster waffles and premade pancakes. You also had a selection of cereal, yogurt, milk and fruit. The hotel also served a dinner on Monday through Thursday from 5pm to 7pm. You wouldn’t call these gourmet meals but they were good for buffet style meals. The week we were here, we had fried chicken with mac cheese, pepper steak with rice, salmon with wild rice, hamburgers and fries. The menu for the month is posted on the refrigerator so you know if you want to make it back for dinner. There was always salad available. Also free wine, beer and soda. Not bad and saved us money by not having to buy lunch and dinner. At the end of a long day it was nice to have a meal ready for us to come back to. The hotel has a business center that had a copy machine and 2 computers for guest use. One computer was connected to the printer. There was also free connected internet and wifi in the rooms. We didn’t interact too much with the desk staff but when we did they were always nice and helpful. All in all we had a good stay and would recommend this hotel.

title: “All you need in the heart of NYC”
text:
My husband and I spent a glorious 5 nights in NYC with the Edison Hotel as our base. We have stayed at this hotel once before 5 years ago and were pleased to experience the same great service. We were able to check in early and our room, though small and basic - had every amenity one would need and was spotless. 
The location of this hotel is a huge draw card, a couple of paces away from Times Square and located in Hell's Kitchen - with Restaurant Row one street down. The hotel was so central that we only used the subway once and a cab once - and we walked everywhere else! 
Concierge was fantastic, and the shuttle offered at the transportation desk more than worth the money (to and from all airports every 1.5hours)

title: “Great breakfast bar! Friendly atmosphere!”
text: Great hotel! Denise, Harise, and Daniel always greet you with a warm friendly smile! Paulette does an exceptional job at the breakfast bar! Very clean with excellent food and service with sincere friendliness that makes every guest feel welcomed and comfortable. A+++++

title: “Fantastic Hotel”
text:
We stayed here for 6 nights ( May 20 thru 26) and the hotel is fantastic. All of the staff are very very helpful and always greeted us on our way in or out.
Our bedroom was superb and room service was great. The bathroom had a nice shower and the room was very well appointed with TV, aircon, fridge, internet and a very comfortable king sized bed.
Matching this wonderful hotel is its position. One block from Times Square ... you cannot get a better hotel closer to the heart of NYC.
We would recommend the hotel to everybody ... great value ... great position ... great people ... great hotel

title: “The most unfriendly Holiday Inn Express I've ever stayed at.”
text: I'm being nice by giving it a "poor" rating. The staff was very unfriendly. Whenever we went in and out, they never even bothered to look up from their computers or personal devices to greet us or even give us a smile in the lobby. We didn't get our priority club member box of goodies when we arrived either. The breakfast was not up to par. When they came to service the room, they threw our extra blankets on the floor and even forgot to refill the toilet paper. When we are back to the Seattle area next year, we will definitely find a better place to stay.

title: “Romantic getaway”
text: We stayed here one night. We had a lovely time. The management gave us a free upgrade! THANKS!!!!! Extremely clean, rooms a bit on the small side, but since we were on a budget & just the two of us, it was plenty comfy cozy. NO BED BUGS (we checked). The room is fully appointed. There was a white noise machine (which was great!), a small fridge, a closet with a safe, hangers, iron, small ironing board, smallish TV with the basic channels (I think), a writing desk, chair and last but not the least - an alarm clock with an iPhone dock. The toilet is separate from the bath area (awesome idea!). The bath soaps, shampoo etc were top of the line. It is LGBT friendly and I loved the atmosphere. The breakfast spread was great (fresh corn bread anyone?). Upon check in we were provided with a list of places to eat. We went to their recommended restaurant called Bill's Burgers a quick walk away. Great food. It was central to many bars, a CVS is around the corner and a Duane Reade a few blocks away. When we got back that night, their very friendly cat Charlie accompanied us to our room :) The next morning, we headed to the High Line for a walk before check out. All in all, an awesome, stress free, romantic stay for tired parents of toddlers :) Highly recommended.

title: “A pool to die for”
text:
Stayed for three nights with two young children. There was plenty of space in the room for both a roll away bed and a crib. The roll away bed isn't a camping cot either like you get at some hotels, but a real bed with mattress that was much appreciated by our son. Our first room didn't have a bathtub, making bathing the baby difficult but we were quickly moved to another room with a bathtub.
The 65' salt water pool is excellent as are the changing facilities. We couldn't keep the kids out. 
All the staff were extremely helpful and friendly. The concierge was excellent, directing us without hassles to everything from take out chinese food to a laundromat. 
Although on the edge of the downtown area, the location is great. Seattle's downtown isn't so large. The valet parking is actually an excellent value for the area with its unlimited in and out.

title: “Good Motel and San Fernando Valley Location”
text: This is a large, well located and maintained motel at the Burbank Bl. offramp of the 405 Freeway in Sherman Oaks. The motel is clean and I believe the walls must be sound proofed because we did not hear the traffic or freeway noise in the room. I am not sure, though, if all rooms would be as quiet due to it's close proximity to the freeway and street. The motel has a decent Denny's Coffee Shop on the premises and there are numerous restaurants, gas stations and stores nearby. The motel has a large parking lot plus there is additional parking along Sepulveda Bl.

title: “Perfect! Can't wait to return.”
text: Just returned from a repeat visit to the hip yet surprisingly comfortable Gansevoort Hotel. The hotel is surrounded by fine restaurants, unbeatable shopping and a happening nightlife. The beauty of the Gansevoort is that you have the option to do all of the above or simply hang in your comfortable, luxurious and quiet room. The bathrooms are surprisingly spacious and extremely well finished and the beds have those fluffy soft duvets that make you never want to leave. There will no doubt be more visits. Don't hesitate! You'll love it.

title: “Two Words: Wine Hour.”
text: I stayed here for a business trip for 3 days and I cannot praise this hotel enough. This ranks as one of my top 3 hotel stays ever in any city ever. The staff was friendly and accommodating. But the building...that is the star of the show. It has been beautifully maintained and really is breathtaking. The location is excellent and right in the middle the loop. As if that wasn't enough, there is a wine hour every night. My first day was a VERY long training and the concierge met me in the lobby with a glass of white sangria (delish). There was a glass of wine in the lobby waiting for me every day during my stay which really made coming back to the room a pleasure. From the wrought iron covered elevators, to the marble stairs and even the small touches like the traditional keys and plush robes in the room this hotel is definitely worth checking out. I just hate that I didn't take pictures!

title: “My Great Escape to the Desert”
text:
The Mid-Atlantic was hit with a barrage of snowstorms just before the holiday season when I decided to escape. By chance, I stumbled on the Pointe Hilton Tapatio Cliffs Resort, where I was greeted with courtesy, kindness and a grasp for customer service second to none.
Dining options include room service, casual dining and the ultimate in fine dining. Other amenities include High-speed internet (for a daily fee), a heated pool and hot tub steps away, USA Today on your doorstep and daily housekeeping. Lookout Mountain is a not-very-long, yet extremely challenging golf course.
If there’s one thing I would change, it would be having an in-room security safe. Instead, they offer a key, which accesses a safe behind the front desk.
p.s. I’m returning for the third time in less than 40 days

title: “Clean, Close to T and downtown, Friendly Staff”
text:
Stayed for 2 nights at the end of Feb 2010 to visit colleges in Boston with my daughter. Used Hilton points. The hotel was convenient to subway transportation (100 ft or so) and within walking distance of downtown, Newbury St, South End. 
Continental breakfast was tasty and plentiful. We had no need to upgrade to the full breakfast. Cookies were yummy, as always. Wait staff and bartenders, especially Jill, were very helpful and friendly.
Room was very clean and showers had good flow.
Enjoyed our stay.

title: “Clean and Comfortable”
text: The location of this hotel is about a 15-20 min walk to Fishermans Wharf AND so much cheaper than staying at hotel in that area. This hotel is clean and safe and the room is comfortable for the price. There is wireless and a small refrigerator in the room which was great. My only complaint is the breakfast. They only offer you a cup of coffee and a muffin and when I told them I was allergic to the muffin and asked for a banana they wouldn't accommodate me or offer me anything else. Other than that this hotel is a good hotel for single, couples and travelers. I wouldn't suggest it for families with young children.

title: “Hotel Diva was great.”
text: Customer service was very accommodating to our needs and wants. The rooms are cozy and trendy. I highly recommend this hotel for a wallet friendly night in the city.

title: “Four Points Sheraton Midtown, good value for money”
text:
Although located in a not too fancy neighbourhood, Four Points by Sheraton Midtown is a pleasant, clean hotel and really good value for money. If you prefer using your feet, you’re in walking distance from Times Square, the theatre district and shopping at Fifth Avenue. Close to the Metro, if that’s your preference. The staff is friendly and helpful, the breakfast adequate and reasonable.
All in all, we had a very enjoyable and recommendable stay.

title: “Great place”
text:
Booked one night here in Sept almost by accident but loved the place. Vast room, really clean, great bed with lovely cotton linen and plump pillows.
Variety of public rooms, our favourites were the Presidents' Bar and the small library snug area.

title: “Fantastic Hotel”
text:
Just spent 3 nights in the Millenium Hilton 23rd-26th April, what a fantastic hotel and great value for money.
After reading all the reviews about the Millenium Hilton on this website I decided to book 3 nights for my girlfriend and I through the Hilton website. We managed to get a city view room on the 41st floor including breakfast for £93 per night. We booked this about a month in advance and if you do your homework like I did that is a very good price for a 4* hotel b&b in NYC.
The room was modern and spacious with great plasma tv, internet, cd player, pay per view movies and floor to ceiling windows with an excellent view of the New York skyline and directly overlooking World Trade Centre site.
The hotel is situated in downtown Manhattan so you do have to get the subway or taxis to most of the sites and attractions, but for me this was'nt a problem at all. The subway station is right outside the hotel ($2 for one trip or $10 for 7 trips) and I never spent more than $8.00 on a taxi from the hotel. 
Still loads to do close to the hotel anyway. The fantastic Century 21 dept store is next door, Wall St around the corner, Ground Zero opposite, Statue of Liberty, Chinatown, and Soho only 5 minutes away.
All in all a great hotel, great value and friendly informative staff made this hotel a great place to stay and I'd definatley stay again.

title: “Stayed in many Manhatten Hotels - San Carlos is the Best!”
text:
My sister and I took our Mother to New York for a five day girls/birthday trip and had researched hotels on many sites. We are so grateful we found the San Carlos! For one, the service is so friendly, from the desk clerks to the doormen (Hi Matthew and Robert!) and even the housekeeping staff, who greeted us cheerfully every morning. But the real star was the room size. Having stayed in several other four star hotels in Manhattan, I was prepared to be disappointed by the room size. Not this time. Room 1505 was delightful. I've never had a kitchenette/diner AND living room in a hotel before, but it was heaven. After long stays of sightseeing, our favourite time of day was coming home for happy hour in our room.
If you stay at the San Carlos, don't forget to walk down to 2nd Ave. and enjoy some of the quaint neighbourhood Pubs and Restaurants. Thumbs up San Carlos, I hope you'll have a room available next time we're lucky enough to be in NYC.

title: “The Pluses Outweigh the Minuses, Stay Here!”
text:
Stayed here for a few nights mid-week and had a wonderful experience. The staff was friendly and helpful, the facilities spotlessly clean, and the location convenient even though it is on a seedy section of 40th St. It is sandwiched between two other nice hotels, though, so there are quite a few travelers walking that way so its not deserted. But, the area still might turn some people off as you have to walk by a sketchy liquor store and some peep shops to get to the hotel. But just look the other way because once you are in the hotel that disappears. The lobby is really slick with white marble floors and banquettes and chairs upholstered with a glam metallic sheen fabric. And there is a nice fireplace in the lobby too! The breakfast area in the back is also very nicely appointed and converts to a friendly bar at 5PM; lots of TV's to watch sports and news. We enjoyed the free wine and beer on the Tues. and Wed. nights we were there, and they put out food too. Granite counters in the bar and bathrooms are a nice updated touch. The breakfast in the morning was very busy but had everything you'd want; eggs, sausage, breakfast sandwiches, fruits, yogurts, juices, baked goods...the staff running it was really on the ball with the refills too. There is free coffee/tea/hot chocolate down there 24/7 too and everyone makes good use of that throughout the day. 
My overall impression of the way this hotel is run is that they know you might not stay there again if they don't get things right, (so many options!) so the staff are going out of their way to accommodate people. Great attitude! Our room was small but as I mentioned, very clean, and had a great view on the 27th floor. N
ow here is a curious thing. On the top floor of the hotel there is a rooftop nightclub. So starting at 6PM one of the elevators is commandeered by serious looking bouncers and a velvet rope goes up cordoning off a section of the lobby as a coatroom and security check area for nightclub goers. This did not present a problem to us, it was just unusual. One night we did drop our teen off in our room and go up for a drink to check it out (no cover charge on Tuesday night!). It was not crowded at that time but still the folks at the club were very different that the businessman/tourist crowd who stays at the hotel! Being 50-somethings we felt a bit out of place but enjoyed our martinis (don't even want to know what they cost, my friend expensed them, but judging by the fact that in the casual "breakfast area bar" downstairs a martini is $21, I shudder to think). If you are staying there on a night when there is no cover charge and you can go up early before there's a line, I would definitely check this place out for the views are breathtaking with floor to ceiling glass in some areas. It is something to see. And if you are a club-goer type then this is really a great hotel for you to stay at because you'll be right there!
But I digress from the hotel. I will absolutely stay there again. It is great value, great location, clean, near fun things, nice people. A favorite for the Times Square area., Though we took public transportation to the city, this hotel is also right across the street from Port Authority with the best deal on parking I've found in NYC so if you drive in check that out. I was torn about whether to give 4 or 5 stars because nothing is perfect and the location and tiny room thing are a bit of a drag. But because the price is so good, the location so convenient, and it is so clean and well-run, I gave it a 5.

title: “Great vacation hotel with the family”
text: I'm used to staying at a Homewood for business, but just finished a 7 night stay with the family and it was fantastic. Hotel was a perfect location right on the Riverwalk, but not too close to the busiest sections and crowds...very nice room, good breakfast (we never got back in time for the reception though). Pool is very small, but being on the roof was exciting. I didn't realize that the only option was valet parking....when I reserved it said that there was a self parking option, but that isn't the case. I'm hoping the new parking manager will make that run more smoothly because you need to plan around getting your car out, especially in the busy am. Overall, I would definitely stay there again and would highly recommend. Note to manager, Laura was particularly helpful and one of the most friendly staff..she's a keeper!

title: “Good and ok hotel, lovely near Central Park”
text:
Clean hotel, rooms small but ok. It is an old storey building and has changed into a hotel, which means narrow corridors and staircases, but is functional. The location is ideal, especially when one becomes accustomed to Subway system, which are indispensable as there is a bit of traveling to the Midt Town vibrant life.
maybe its a bit to pricy considering the standard
