title: “Real Americana - I definately had a nice day”
text: I came across this place from reviews on Trip Advisor and loved it. I booked directly and had a great email and phone conversation with the owners. The room was great, a big room with plenty of space for three motorcyclists. The hotel is built around a parking area, so free parking too. The place was very clean, furnished well and did not suffer from noisy guests or traffic. The owners were superbly helpful, giving great advice about trams, buses and diners and there is a host of maps and guides there too. The help were very friendly as well and the price was out of this world. A basic buffet breakfast allowed us to fill our bike jackets with muffins and fruit and then be on our way. Far better than Fisherman's Wharf which we found to be seedy and dirty. Two blocks from the tram and then a $5 dollar ride down to the Wharf, cab fare back was around $8.

title: “A Home Away From Home”
text:
My partner and I stayed at the Affinia Manattan for 6 nights in mid-November and we can't help but sing it's praises.
Our trip was split up into two halves, so we were able to try the one-bed and two-bed rooms on separate occasions. While both were nice and included a fully functional kitchenette (ie. microwave, stove, fridge), I would definately request the two-bed room as it's more spacious overall. Also, ask if they have a room with a view of the Empire State Building as it's not far away at all.
All staff were friendly and helpful. There is a free gym on one of the lower floors and a variety of vending machines in the basement.
Perhaps the best part of the experience was the close proximity to central New York. Being on 31st street, most areas were within walking distance and for anything further away, Penn Station and the subway are diagonally opposite to the hotel (below Madison Square Garden). You can literally walk across the street and catch an Amtrak train to Washington DC or the subway to Central Park. I couldn't imagine a better location.
Overall, we'd highly recommend the hotel to anyone to anyone looking for a "home away from home" while staying in one of the most amazing cities in the world.

title: “Fabulous room, great view, excellent service!”
text: We had a wonderful time at the Watergate. I was worried about the price versus value, but once we arrived and were greeted, I worried no more. The service was outstanding that responded to our every request and the facility was spotless. The public areas were opulent but not overstated. Our room on the 5th floor was a very spacious suite with a veranda that had the same view as Forrest Gump's when he called to alert that the electricity must be out and we got a kick out of that! We also had a great view of the Potomac. It was great! The huge bathroom was all black and white marble with separate tub from shower. Really pretty and spotlessly clean. Our only disappointment was that it was Mother's Day weekend and the dining hours were off, and we were sleeping in (vacation), so we were unable to eat at the restaurant when we wanted to. We had to watch the hours. But when we did, the food was absolutely wonderful and fresh, fresh, fresh. Yes, the Watergate is an older facility, but it is very well preserved, updated, and the service can't be beat. We will highly recommend it.

title: “Best hotel I have ever stayed at”
text: This hotel is in a good position. The room was large with a kitchen and fridge. All staff were accommodating and polite. Everything was excellent with The Benjamin.

title: “Great Location!”
text: My two visitors and I just spent two nights here. The location couldn't have been better. It is within walking distance of the Mall and the White House and right next to a metro station. We ate breakfasts in the hotel and one lunch and the food was quite good and service great. My room was $135 per night, Senior Discount and my guests at $151, AAA rate.

title: “The BEST Hotel in Boston!!!”
text:
My stay in this hotel lasted 3 days and the rate I had to pay was not as expensive as in other hotels and it was worth it! 
The location was great for us because we had to visit BU, BC, and had a sightseeing of the city. The public transportation is really close to the hotel, it is very convenient.
Our rooms were very clean and the staff is professional and friendly. 
I would definitely like to stay there again, if I have the chance to go back to Boston!

title: “Uncomfortable bed”
text:
I've been to Austin many times and this is the 2nd time my bf and I stayed at the Hilton Garden Inn Arboretum. We had no plans to go downtown this time so this worked just fine for a weekend getaway. We
checked in around 11 pm, and we asked the front desk to switch the name of the reservation to my bf's so the credit for the stay would be on his Hilton number. He was an old guy who was slow to type though
we didn’t take that against him. I did think that he was a bit rude though. He couldn’t look up my bf's Hilton number by entering his name at first. Eventually he did, but all he managed to do correctly was change the reservation to his name. Everything else was incorrect,
his address and Hilton number. We got the key card and went up to the room. The key card wouldn't work. Not a big deal, so he went downstairs and the guy gave him another key card which finally worked.
Once we were settled in, he called customer service and we were right that that was a faster way to get this all straightened out rather than explaining things to the front desk guy. 
The bed was so uncomfortable! I remember we complained about this the first time we stayed here. The Doubletrees and Hampton Inns have way better beds.
What I did like about this hotel is the free wireless internet and the hookup for my MP3 player on the clock radio. They did have Neutrogena toiletries which is nice, but I don’t really care too much for these things as I rarely use hotel-provided shampoo and lotion.
We cut our stay short (after only 1 night) and decided to move to a Hampton Inn for the next 2 nights.
It's fine if all you need is a clean hotel and you don't plan to stay much in the room. We're not coming back unless the rate is really cheap (we got this for $80/night with AAA discount).

title: “Fabulous hotel!!”
text: Just stayed in The Peabody for a one night stay on a brief stopover in Memphis on my way from NH to Dallas. The hotel was our splurge and well worth it!! The room was more than satisfactory. Beds extremely comfortable, air conditioning quiet, bathrooms well appointed. Rooms were also very very clean.. which is top notch to me. Loved the ambience of the entire place. We did miss the march of the ducks as it was too crowded. Overall I would stay here again in a heart beat.. really want to come back to Memphis with an extra day or two and to stay again at The Peabody.

title: “Prime Place”
text: I have been to the Hotel Pennsylvania three times in the last 2 1/2 years and I will be going back again in May. The rooms and bathrooms are kept up daily by the housekeeping staff. I have had no problem with rusty water, dirty floors, filthy sheets or unmade beds (try leaving a couple of bucks on the bed for housekeeping and you might see a difference!!!) Check in time is 3:00pm. The people who are complaining that they get there at noon and have to wait 3 hours should check the hotel policy. (By the way most hotels are 3:00pm check in time.) The hotel is in a prime location, Madison Square Garden is right across the street, Macy's department store is 2 blocks north, Times Square is 7 blocks north, the Empire State building in 4 blocks east and the world famous Blarney Stone Authentic Irish Bar and Grill is just a 1/2 a block away on W. 32nd st. You should stop in and ask for Martin at night. Anyway, I am more than pleased with the Pennsylvania and get wait to go back in May.

title: “Great Hotel”
text: I stayed at the Courtyard New York Manhattan / Midtown East September 6-9. This hotel is in a great location. We walked all over. There is no need to take a subway or taxi. After reading the reviews on here, I did double check to see if we had sheets on the sofa bed, and we did not. I was able to ask the bell man before he left our room. Other than that, everything was great. The extra towels we had requested prior to our stay were there and no complaints about anything.

title: “greatly, perfectly located for out of town guests”
text:
how can you go wrong? The W Hotel is located by Penn Ave and view of all the monuments on the rooftop. Service is impeccable and foods at the hotel are simple yet elegant.
I recommend to out of town need to be impressed guests.

title: “They treat you better than family”
text: We recently had to travel to Baltimore for a visit to Johns Hopkins. Going to another state to see a bunch of doctors is not typically a good experience but our stay at Admiral Fell turned our trip into a great experience. The staff was so helpful and friendly. They treated us special and like we were old friends. The hotel itself is so beautiful and clean. The location could not be better......right off the water and in the middle of Fells Point with shops and cafe's and pubs. You can spend a day just walking the area. From the valet to the cleaning staff to the front desk clerk.......we LOVED this Inn. We will happily stay there every time we visit Baltimore.

title: “Good value”
text:
The hotel is conveniently located - 2 blocks from metro and there is a circulator bus stop across the street which takes you to Georgetown.
The bellboys/elevator operators were very friendly. However, the lady at the front desk who checked us in did not come across as welcoming. A smile would help. The room was bigger than I expected - there was a living area plus a separate bedroom with a king-size bed. The bellboys kept telling us that we got a great room. It was only afterwards when I checked the hotel website that I realized I was upgraded to a suite. Interesting that the lady at the front desk didn't mention anything.
Negatives: There is no in-room safe. Also, upon check-out, I was asked by the bellboy if I needed a cab (to the Reagan airport) to which I said yes. He tried for 2 minutes and then told me to get in one of those black lincoln sedans. I questioned the bellboy saying that it wasn't what I asked for but he said "It's OK. He works for us and he charges the same as a cab." It was raining hard at the time so I got in the car. I asked the driver how he was going to charge me and he said the flat rate is $25, same as a cab. I did take a cab from the airport to the hotel and it costed me under $20 including tips. I also recall reading the rates posted inside the cab and there was something about a ceiling rate of $25 between the airport and the hotel area. I told the driver that it costed me under $20 and there was no "flat rate" and he mumbled something about the $25 included luggage which wasn't true as my luggage was small and the cab didn't charge me luggage fee. As I was enroute to the airport, I didn't want any delays so I didn't fight with him.
Lesson being don't let the bellboys flag you one of "his cars", make sure you get a cab.

title: “A Nice Little Gem”
text: I love this small hotel! Everyone is super friendly and helpful from the time you set foot on the property. My husband and I arrived after a long day and upon check-in our FD agent welcomed us back and made us feel right at home. She offered us free movies to watch in our room, Free Wi-Fi, coffee & tea, made sure we knew about breakfast the next morning and because we were here to cheer our family @ the SD Marathon when asked she was able to give us a late check out. Truly a magnificent stay. We stayed in the old bldg and the rooms although small are comfortable, neat and immaculately cleaned. We have and will continue to recommend this hotel to everyone that visits San Diego.

title: “A really terrible place to stay”
text:
We had used 1800hotels who recommended this hotel for 2 single travels. Instead on the 2 beds reserved we were given a tiny room with one bed and no room for a cot (which they didn't have anyway). Fortunately I could stay with a friend in New Jersey! There is no doorman, no concierge, no amenities except mouthwash were provided. The staff were sullen and told us they couldn't accomodate us because we had booked through a third party - even though they had a room with 2 beds in their SoHO property. The next day when a room with 2 beds was 'found,' we were charged $20.00 to make the switch even though our reservation through 1800hotels was for 2 beds. 1800hotels gave no assistance and I would never use them as a booking agent again.
Oh yes, the neighborhood is dangerous after dark.

title: “Best Place I've every stayed!!! Cannot be beat.”
text:
I've been to New York several times and have stayed at some great hotels but nothing compares to this one. It was soooo beautiful and comfortable with the perfect location. The staff always were friendly and helpful and went way beyond the normal expectations. We spoke to about 6 different staff members during our stay and each one of them was a delight to deal with.
The room was absolutely stunning and roomy and so comfortable. I loved this place and will tell everyone I know to stay there. IT's very close to times square and is located on what they call 'restaurant row' ....tons of adorble, quaint restaurants with live music and great food.
Stay here and you will not be disappointed. We just loved it.

title: “Nickel and dime”
text: Rooms dated and old, then they nickel and dime you to death. Fee for gym, fee for internet but a free newspaper! Friendly helpful people at the front desk. Free printing for the boarding pass...but watch the fees!

title: “Great Urban Retreat”
text:
We're San Francisco locals and stayed at the new St. Regis for Thanksgiving as a special treat. It was well worth it!
The room was wonderful, large, comfortable and beautifully furnished, great view of Yerba Buena Gardens and the Metreon (we were on the 18th floor). Shades, phone, music, lights, and climate are all controlled by a touch screen panel by the bed. A large, flat panel HDTV sits facing the bed (and sadly blocking some of the best view).
The bathroom is cozy but well designed. Deep soaking tub and separate (powerful) shower, but just one sink - which I always think is a shame. Double doors on one side of the tub open up into the bedroom allowing you to stare out at views, or just enjoy the spacious room while you soak.
Closet space is adequate for a short stay but would benefit from nearby seating. The bar was well stocked with wine, but other drinks were poorly catered for, no snacks were included, and their was no price list. Also, bottled water was distinctly lacking in the room. But these were minor inconveniences and we spent a lot of time in the room and thoroughly enjoyed it!
We tried out the spa and gym (the pool had not been finished). The Spa service was exquisite, but the rooms felt a little unfinished and the area, especially the waiting rooms were cramped and lacking natural light. The locker room was very stylish and well designed. The sauna, whirlpool and steam room had not been finished, they looked adequate but not particularly noteworthy. The locker room would have benefited from refreshments - especially water. 
The gym was on a different floor and not connected to the spa, which didn't suit my plans but probably isn't much of a problem for most people. Service at the gym was attentive (a little too attentive for me - unusual at a place this good). There were plenty of machines, mainly TechnoGym cardio, though a good selection of weight machines too. Very little space for stretching or free weights. I passed a door marked Yoga Studio but didn't go in. The gym has no locker rooms, shower, sauna, etc.
Public spaces are beautiful. Grand but modern. I love the fireplace between the bar and foyer.
The bar pours very generous whisky and makes a fantastic French 75. More of a scene bar than an intimate meeting place.
We ate at Ame for Thanksgiving Dinner. The food was incredible. Seafood is the specialty, with a Japanese flair. Had some of the best food I've eaten in the city (and there's a lot of good food here!). Thoroughly recommend. I expect we'll come back to the bar and restaurant even if we can’t justify staying in the rooms again!
Room service for breakfast the next day was excellent if a little slow (45 minutes from ordering - which they warned us about). Eggs benedict and an omelet. Both perfectly cooked. Good coffee.
Service was good, though there are still a few kinks to be worked out. Staff weren't as familiar with the hotel as you might want (spa staff weren't sure where the gym was or what it was like, reception staff had trouble with the computers, it took people a while to answer questions). Nothing that a few months of experience won’t sort out. Everyone was helpful without being intrusive (except at the gym!), and very professional. 
We left feeling very relaxed and pampered, and wishing we didn't have to head home. We're looking for our next excuse to go back!

title: “No they can't help you and don't want to.”
text:
Checked in about 3 Pm. Paid full price. They gave us the room next to the elevator. All night. 4 nights. 
 When we got to the room and realized the noice, 3 min. We went down to get a different room. They said the had no other rooms. There where 5-6 people standing in back of us. Yet, they had no rooms. We ask repeatedly to be moved. Never was. Oh yah. Room was above kitchen, nice smell. 
 I wrote Hilton and complained. Never heard back.

title: “Met my expectations”
text:
My husband and I stayed at the Inn from July 19-24. We were very content with the hotel. The staff was excellent. Wayne, Omar and Ann were exceptionally great. Loved the rooms. Did not need air conditioning as San Francisco was cool that week. The location could not have been better. It was centrally located. The breakfast was more than adequate. There was food for all palates. The evening wine and cheese was an additional perk. It was great to sit and chat with others from all ove the world in a relaxed atmosphere. The nighttime cookies topped it all off. 
All in all we would return again and would highly recommend this hotel.

title: “It was okay.”
text: The hotel was clean and comfortable. It was quiet using the A/C despite the busy traffic outside. The staff was helpful with directions and any questions we had. The breakfast had beverages, cereal, fruit and bagels...it was average. There were busy times when one could not find a place to sit because there were only 6-7 small tables. The hotel was very close to Old Town San DIego and about 10-15 minutes from the Zoo and downtown. There were many restaurants and places to shop, but it was a highly trafficed area. The hotel was good for the price, but I think I would like to be closer to the downtown atmosphere next time.

title: “Great hotel in great location.”
text: Originaly had a room on the 4th floor and the very friendly clerk upgraded me to the 12th floor with no extra charge. The room was very clean and the veiw was awwesome. The bed and pillows were very comfortable and smelled very clean. The only problems I had were thata the remote needed new batteries and the shower head was more like water coming out of a hose than a shower. Other than that the stay was great.

title: “Great Hotel!!”
text:
We went to Indy for a Colts game so we wanted somewhere close to the downtown area, but not in the thick of everything (with all the craziness of game day, we weren't sure what traffic would be like, etc.) We were also looking for something with free parking and free wifi (which most of the downtown hotels near the stadium didn't offer.) 
La Quinta Indy South was easily accessible from the interstate (which is great for me since I'm directionally challenged!) and it only took us about 10 minutes to get downtown. 
The hotel itself was great--great service, very clean and neat, several breakfast options, etc. The only "complaints" I had were personal ones--our AC wasn't pumping out as much cold air as we liked, but we didn't think it was serious enough to call the staff (I'm sure if we would have mentioned it then someone would have fixed it asap.) And the other thing was the pillows--if you're not into super fluffy plumped up pillows then you might want to bring one from home. I slept great, but I'm not used to something so fluffy so my neck hurt a bit in the morning. But like I said, that was ALL personal preference--none of that really has to do with La Quinta's overall quality. 
Anyways, overall, great hotel, great location, I would highly recommend it to anyone going to Indy for the weekend!

title: “warm welcome to a wonderful hotel”
text: I stayed here because of its proximity to my daughter's apartment and couldn't have been happier. When I arrived there was a happy hour in the lobby (where everyone looked very happy) and I received a warm welcome from the front desk. The check-in was smooth, the room immaculate, the bed comfortable. All the staff greeted me whenever I met them--in the lobby and in the elevator. The only fault was that the internet connection was rather slow.

title: “Great service and location.”
text: I stayed here the Wednesday before Hurricane Irene and got caught during the storm. The location was the best. Right across the street from Penn Station. I arrived ahead of my room being ready and was given access to hospitality suite to rest. Having a leg injury, they were very accomodating to my comfort. The accessible room was large, modern decor and roomy, the bathroom clean and kitchenette a plus. I have my own internet connection which was a plus as the hotel does not have free wifi and their per day costs is a bit pricey at $15. The restaurant was good and stayed open throught the storm. My only issue, which is not the hotel's fault was the noise from construction taking place next door. And as you are on 7th Ave, you do have the noise from the street. As a native NY'er, it didnt bother me and I spent a lot of time out of the room. All staff were friendly and customer service focused. Any issues I had were addressed immediately and they were accomodating in extending my stay at the same rate that I had booked during the hurricane. I will definitely stay here again.

title: “Great hotel!”
text:
Having read so many positive reveiws about the Pearl on TA, my partner and I decided to book here. We were in New York for 4 nights and the hotel is in a great location just off Broadway - very close to Times Square, theatres, restaurants and shops. 
I've never stayed in NY before but this hotel was fantastic - very stylish and clean reception area and the receptionists/concierge were very helpful/polite. Our room was large and included a terrace area with chairs and table. The bed was big and there was plenty of drawer/cupboard space for clothes. Safe, microwave, coffee maker, hairdryer, iron and board were also in the room. NY is constantly noisy but we were never disturbed during the night - the glass in the windows must be thick!
Breakfast was included in the price and we were really impressed with it - fresh fruit salad, yogurts, bread, variety of bagels, cereals and pastries - certainly enough to start off the day. Yes, we had to use plastic plates and cutlery but it didn't make it any less enjoyable.
I don't have any complaints about this hotel and would definitely stay here again if visiting NY.

title: “Clean, comfortable, very nice staff”
text:
This was my first trip to Phoenix and I don't have any major complaints about this hotel. Very good air conditioning--you immediately tell the difference when you walk in (or out! I went in July!). The staff was very hospitable and professional. Everything was clean. The dining... I wish there were more frills to it. It's a nice restaurant but a limited menu. Oh well, you can't have everything, and besides I got a great deal on the price. I lost several dollars because the vending machine gave out the wrong drink and I wish the staff could have warned me I wouldn't like one of the taxi companies they recommended.
I think this hotel would be great for a family vacation, especially if you rent a car. It's right next to a highway out (like to go to the Grand Canyon?), there's a decent budget amusement park with a nice charm and an EXCELLENT (and generally inexpensive) arcade right across the highway that I went to every day, and there's an indoor mall pretty close by, too. They had activities and movies by the pool. But best if you drive to get where you need to go. I mostly did tours that picked me up from the hotel, but otherwise I walked or took public transit everywhere. Walking was tough in the heat, and the public transit system has very bad hours. So in some respects a downtown hotel would have been better for me.

title: “If Apple owned a hotel, it would be yotel...”
text:
Perfectly efficient, meticulously clean, smart, and modern.
When the purpose of your visit involves minimal time in your room, but when you want to trust that your room has all that you need. Fun, and the future.

title: “Great value hotel”
text:
Stayed here in May.
Location could not be better! Generally friendly service, clean rooms, free internet and value for money.
Highly recommended if you're looking for a midrange hotel.

title: “Loved the Sofitel !!!!”
text:
Sofitel is a beautiful hotel in a very central location on W. 44th Street. It is walking distance to Times Square (about 3 blocks), to Rockefeller Center,Bryant Park,5th Ave and close to the subway. The staff was excellent, very friendly and always helpful. Our room was beautiful, very quiet and had a nice view on the 17th floor. Ask for the highest floor possible. The lower floors don't have much of a view. The bathroom was very nice, mostly marble and had a separate shower, with a candle and fresh flower. Housekeeping kept everything very clean and they even have turn down service with free bottled Avian water at night. The bed was almost too comfortable. The heavy duvet was too warm at night. The only complaint I have is that there was no top sheet to use in place of the duvet. The concierge knows everything about New York and was eager to help and very friendly. The doormen were always friendly and opening doors when we came and went. Drinks at the hotel restaurant bar were good (but expensive). Order the hummus as an appetizer. It was awesome! 
We just LOVED the Sofitel and will definitely stay there on our next visit to New York. 
**Tip- If you want to avoid the expensive breakfasts at the hotel restaurant, there is a diner very close to the hotel called the Red Flame. The food is great, inexpensive, and the service is excellent. We ate breakfast there all 4 days while visiting. As you exit the hotel, take a right and the Red Flame is just a short distance down the street on the right.

title: “Great Place Near the Bay”
text: This is the third time over the last 16 months that we have stayed at the Vagabond Inn. It is in a wonderful location on Gaffey Street which is the main street entering San Pedro from Route 110-S. It is just a few blocks from the bay and is quite convenient to all of San Pedro's attractions. The inn is clean and well maintained with very comfortable beds. We've found the staff to be consistently friendly and helpful. We'll always stay at the Vagabond when in the area and in fact we'll be there later this summer.

title: “central location”
text:
The Salisbury Hotel is situated in a convenient location enabling travellers to reach any part of New York with ease.
We found the room to be very clean. The maid came in every day. We were on the 17th floor overlooking 57th Street. It was noisy but after a long day sightseeing and shopping we all fell fast asleep without any trouble.
The hotel staff were always polite and helpful when we spoke to them.
Loved the Statue of Liberty. The only fault was that we were under the impression that the first boat left at 8.30a.m. so arrived at 8.00a.m. but didnt actually leave until 9.30a.m. It was worth the wait though.
The Empire State was also a sight to behold. The views both day and night were incredible.
Would definitely go back and stay at the Salisbury Hotel.

title: “Excellent Stay”
text: This hotel, is exactly why i continue to be a faithful marriot customer. the hotel was very nice, exceeded all my expectations, people were ALL friendly. Would definitely recoomend for EVERYON.. will be back next time in charlotte.

title: “Great central location for a business trip to Boston”
text: I stayed at the Omni Parker house for a business trip from Jan 13th - 19th 2012. Was looking for a reasonably priced hotel in the downtown area, that was convenient for public transportation as I needed to travel on the T to Newton each day. Check in was extremely quick and efficient and was told about a free loyalty program I could sign up for which would give me wifi in my room for free during my duration. I had booked a jr bedroom...which I was expecting to be really small. However, either I was upgraded or the jr bedroom wasn't that JR. The room was pleasantly a decent size and the bathroom was huge. Outside of that, the room was clean and had all the things you'd expect a hotel of that caliber to have. The one not so great thing was the food offered. They had a nicer restaurant called Parkers or something like that that was a little too expensive for what I could expense on the company. The other food option in the hotel was at the bar/pub...and I must admit that the choices didn't look that appealing. That being said, you're in Boston and there are plenty of other great restaurants within walking distance. Overall, great value for the money (I got a room for around $100/night); really close to public transportation; nice, attentive staff; and clean. What more could you ask. Would definitely stay there again.

title: “Great Value!”
text: The hotel was great! For what we were paying we were expecting something older or less up-to-date. It was clean, roomy (walk-in closet with chest of drawers), and luxurious. Comfortable beds, clean updated bath and the floor-to-ceiling windows provided a stunning view of west Houston. One of the nicest hotels I've stayed in. Only drawback was a parking area without clearance for my Suburban (6'-0"). There was however parking in the adjacent building within the complex. A mere 100 ft walk from the underground entrance from the hotel. I will stay there again.

title: “Great place, would stay here again!”
text: I was impressed with this hotel after reading some of the poor reviews. The beds were very comfortable, the staff was very nice and helpful when needed.It is within walking distance of shopping areas but you do have to cross major streets with lights. I would happily stay here again.

title: “Been awhile and I was very pleased”
text:
Just returned from a stay at the Paramount. I used to stay here frequently when I was quite younger but over the past 10 years decided I outgrew it and stayed in places like The Soho Grand, or Royalton, etc. but this week conferences, etc. had pushed four star NYC prices to the $400's so I stayed at the Paramount - first time in 12 years. 
It was great! I walked in, the staff was very friendly, the lobby looks great, and they upgraded my room. They have clearly refurbished the place. There are plenty of lifts for the 19 or 20 floors they have so waiting was never a problem. The room was nice and clean and they had a free electrical outlet by the head of the bed - I typically do some work in the evenings on my laptop and it drives me MAD that other hotels haven't figured this out - the only free outlets are by the little desk across the room. The Paramount has clearly solved this. It was a bit hot outside but the air con worked instantly and cooled down the room. Bathroom was clean and the shower was easy to figure out - another issue I have - all the strange approaches to hot and cold water, shower vs bath. Anyway, everything was clean, worked well and the location is fantastic - a nice 1 block stroll to Times Square. The WIFI was $9.95 vs $15 per day at most hotels and it was quite fast - I streamed an episode of "V" no problem. 
I thought the all you can eat breakfast was too high priced at $28, so I walked to the Blue Fin, and spent $26. Big savings! 
Paramount - I underestimated you. I will stay here again even when the rates of other NYC hotels are down.

title: “great little gem”
text: I was desperately looking for a hotel since our favorite, the Michaelangelo was very pricey, but still wanting the same amenities. Found this, and decided to give it a try. What a great find. It is nice, clean and newly redone. We took a red eye there and were beyond exhausted when we arrived at 7am. Got a great recommendation for breakfast and when we returned at 9:30, waited for less than an hour for our room to be ready. It was a large room, with microwave, coffee, and fridge. Utilized the fridge for water. Great location, only two blocks to subway and walking distance to most everything. Staff were always helpful. Noticed that quite a few people did have their dogs staying with them. It is a great location, great hotel, great price.

title: “Enjoyed our stay! Great location, good value and close to everything!”
text:
My girlfriend and I stayed at this hotel on February 19, 2010 and thoroughly enjoyed our stayed. We had used airmiles to pay for this trip so we can't complain about the value or price paid. The rooms were very clean, contemporary, well furnished and quite large by San Francisco standards. The hotel itself is centrally located to do great shopping along Market Street and even close enough to walk down to the Saturday market at the Ferry Building. We did not eat at any of the hotel's restaurants since there are so many places to dine in the immediate vicinity. The nearby Westfield Center has great shopping and affordable food places on the lower floor. The Metreon in down the street to grab a movie in the evening and to do some light shopping. All in all we had a wonderful time and would recommend this hotel. We have stayed many many times in SF and would say this is one of our favorites. The staff are friendly and willing to help when needed. The hotel was quiet except for some late night noice from fire trucks - which seemed louder than you would expect being 10 floors up and in a newer hotel. Also, the Westin beds are some of the comfiest in the hotel industry!
One suggestion would be to park down the street at Mission and 4th Street in the covered municipal parking lot. The daily maximum is $32 compared with the outragious $55 (including tax) at the hotel. It is only a 3 minute walk from it to the hotel's front door.

title: “Denise went above and beyond to turn around an unhappy guest.”
text:
A situation arouse that was not brought on by Denise. However, she felt the full wrath of my emotions. This trip was planned to attend our son's BMT Graduation Weekend. With very little sleep and a very emotinal day, I was at the end of my rope. Someone else had promised something that was not delieverd. This issue was going to cause even more problems but Denise saved the day. It is hard to find someone willing to help solve a problem when it was not their problem to solve. Here is a shout out to good customer service. Thank you!
Sincerely,
The emotional lady on 7-26-12

title: “A Luxury Hotel by Hyatt”
text:
Had a great stay at the Hyatt 48Lex.
Check-in was easy and an upgraded room was offered even though I wasn't an elite level loyalty guest.
Nice !
The room was clean, crisp and with the wall to ceiling windows it had a real New York feeling.
Nice !
The whole hotel has access to the "club level" on the second floor with snacks, beverages, computer work station and lounge chairs.
Nice !
My Business plan rate included free breakfast and Internet. 
Nice!
My free breakfast in the restaurant was just ok.....the lunch I had at the restaurant was bland and not that fresh. Unless you have free food skip this place. Hang out on the "club level" on the second floor or take in another restaurant in the neighborhood. 
Not so nice !
Hey Hyatt....fix the restaurant !

title: “Great Value”
text: The Moore Hotel is a great value for the money: fantastic location, great staff, free wifi in the lobby. It's nothing fancy but if you are looking for basic accommodations in downtown Seattle, this is the place for you.

title: “Very, very nice hotel & nicely maintained!”
text: I was a bit hesitant to stay at this hotel as some of the previous reviews were not favorable. However, we had a fantastic weekend. Our room was clean & very cool (considering it was 100+ degrees that weekend). I am a picky traveler & this hotel exceeded my expectations. The staff was courteous & quick to respond. I arrived & could not get the tv to turn on. I called the front desk & there was a repair person in my room in about 5 minutes (the back cable wire had come loose). Room service was fabulous & served at the time requested (by 6:15 am!). We even enjoyed a delicious cake & ice cream snack one evening. Location is great and convenient to several major highways. There are 2 pools (1 inside & 1 outside) that both looked delightful but we were not able to take advantage of them this visit. We will be back!

title: “A Pilar for all that is good in Detroit”
text:
I stayed in the Marriot Ren Cen during the National Tour Association Convention at the beginning of November. 
I could sing the praises of this hotel all day long. The housekeeping was immaculate. The beds beyond comfortable (What to do with all the pillows). Bathroom Amenities were top notch.
Customer Service within the hotel was perfect. Only blip came in the lobby bar were a server who wouldn't split our bar tab to different rooms. (Cost her a VERY large gratuity).
The internet at first seems pricey at $13 a day but when you find that all your long distance and local calling is included for that price, your expense account start smiling.
Only issue I had was feeling motion sick on the 45th floor as the 65 MPH winds outside rocked our hotel. I know it's built that way but what a crazy feeling.
If you have a chance to visit detroit, this hotel is in a great area (yes, it's alright to walk around), convenient to Greektown, the Convention Center, Windsor Tunnel and Comerica Field.

title: “Basic but good for the price”
text: In need of a refit but did what was needed. Ruby Tuesdays to eat at close by. If you've hired a car it's easy to get into the city. The hotel breakfast though simple is useful & is included in the price. We didn't use the train though the station is only a short walk with trains every 30 minutes into the city.

title: “Great Location in Capitol Hill”
text:
We were here for two nights as a weekend getaway. We picked the location because of its proximity to Capitol Hil and the Mall. The location is great and the room was average size for a hotel of this age. We were disappointed by a couple of things. We stay at a lot of Kimpton properties but this one was very tame. The halls are a sea of brown, carpet & walls, with no art hanging anywhere to brighten things up. On the wekeend they do not have the nightly happy hour nor do they provide any complimentary coffee in the lobby like most other Kimptons. 
There is construction going on next door and work commenced very early on Monday morning.
Overall this is a nice enough property but this was not a "fun" property at all. Next time we will likely stay at the Monaco or another Kimpton in the District.

title: “Great Value”
text: From the first greeting at check-in to the good-bye at check-out, the Front Desk was terrific. The staff of the hotel is exceptional, and I would be remiss if I didn't mention the wonderful Sabrina in the breakfast room. This lady has you feeling like Mom just cooked a huge breakfast for you and sends you out to have a great day. BTW, the breakfast is included. The location of the hotel is excellent. It sits atop a hill which affords great views, even though the building is only three stories high. It is between the Gaslamp District and Balboa Park. TIP: If you have any trouble negotiating the very steep sidewalk up to the main entrance, just enter the parking garage on Sixth Ave., and take the the elevator up. The free shuttle service is a tremendous amenity and will take you most anywhere downtown, as well as to the airport. Saves a bundle in cab fees. The hotel is older and the room is a bit dated and small. Not to worry, though. All the modern amenities are there. Free wi-fi, refrigerator, in-room safe. Very clean and comfortable. Bed was just the right firmness for me. You also have both soft and firm pillows. TV not flat-panel, but in San Diego who watches TV with such beautiful weather? You want to be outdoors all the time. ODDITIES: The bar is open only on Mondays and Thursdays. Also, when you call the hotel you have to leave a message, then they return your call. Quite odd, but just not enough of an inconvenience to dwell on. One elevator is out of service, leaving a bit of a wait for the one that is working. If you're fit, taking the stairs is no problem, which I did most of the time. There is a pool and a terrace with a great view of the city. All in all, my 5 nights here was a very nice experience and if I'm in San Diego again I will certainly stay here.

title: “Bleh...”
text:
Pros:
Nice decor and atmosphere. Most of the staff is accommodating and friendly. Dohyo restaurant was pretty tasty (key lime pie and beef ramen thingy especially). Was freezing out so having a descent restaurant and club indoors was a major plus.
Cons:
Overbooked our premium corner room and "upgraded" our room (had a balcony but no use in 20 degree weather) without a phone call or email (we wanted the view dang it!). Bar on Four was pricier that most bars in the city. Music that night was bleh (dont know what event was actually taking place) but there was a large turn out (not uncomfortably large) to keep it lively. Valet was a bad experience.
Overall:
Considering it was our anniversary, and it was me doing the planning, it was a frustrating experience, but for her it was okay. Management did try to rectify the situation so that earns some points.

title: “Bad location, GPS listed few difference suburbs!”
text: GPS did list a couple of properties under the same add! of course we went to the long one. Driving in Boston did not help either. Everything except talking to the receptionist and Newspaper and Ice are free. Net cost extra...no hotel charge anymore! we stay in Days Inn, which is so budget compare to the 'luxury' doubletree but continental breakfast and WIFI are free. so how can they justified being a valuable choice!

title: “Just fine!”
text: This was our second time staying at The Barclay. We were well aware of the quality of the rooms and the ideal location. The service is pretty good too. Those things have not changed. But, checking in on this Friday afternoon was a little ridiculous. The hotel should adequately staff for peak times, since we received indication that this was typical. Also, we didn't have to park a car the last time, but given the price the hotel charges, I would advise checking around the block for a rate less than the $60/day they charge.

title: “EXCELLENT”
text:
The Kawada is FANTASTIC! I stayed there with my Mum and my Brother, who's 6'3, for 7 nights and we found it comfortable, a great location and the staff were very helpful. 
The rooms are small, we got a bit of a shock but after we settled in it was fine, we had 2 single beds then a rollaway. We actually took the matress off and my brother just slept on it on the floor and we rolled it up in the morning.. 
The hotel is less then 100m away from the subway from which you can get to Hollywood, Universal City and Long Beach. We got a day ticket which was $5. When we wanted to get to Santa Monica we asked the front desk and they directed us to a bus stop 3 blocks away that cost us $1.25 each and got us all the way to the Pier..
The Downtown area iitself was great, there was a convienience store about 2min away, there was an amazing Italian Restaurant 2 blocks away and a very good cafe right next to the hotel.
I really can't praise it enough, I will definately be staying there again!

title: “Great room good views”
text:
I wanted to stay in my room all day. Stayed in a Jr Suite - #3148 - with views of the City, parts of the Bay Bridge, and the South Bay. It was much larger than I expected and looked renovated. It had two beds in a room separated by a wall, living room with couch and coffee table, large desk and nice chair. The shower if my 6 foot 5 inch frame with room to spare.
I prefer this hotel due to its proximity to the Powell Street Bart Station, which has direct service from SFO Airport. Market Street is just a 1/2 block away. The Concierge lounge (18th floor) level continental breakfasts included eggs, hot and cold cereals, fruit, breads, juices, etc. The lounge was small for the amount of people coming in. Many just took food to their rooms. Not enough tables or room to move about. Needs renovations I feel. 
This is my 5th stay at this hotel over the years and I will be coming back for sure.

title: “Comfortable and Well-Located”
text:
We spent three nights at the Eventi and overall, we were very happy with our stay. The staff were courteous and the room large and well-appointed. A minor concern was that our water (both shower and bathroom sink) took at least 2 minutes to warm up after turning on the taps. I felt that there was little to be gained by mentioning it until we checked out, but I did mention it then. I suppose there may be some plumbing issues that may take some time to resolve. We'd already been in the room almost a full day before discovering the issue, so we really didn't want to move.
We also saw room service dishes outside a room next to ours that were uncollected for more than 24 hours, which was a bit odd.
We ate breakfast one morning at the second floor restaurant and although the food was good, it was pretty pricey. $5.50 for a cup of coffee is crazy, and I wasn't even offered a refill.
One nice surprise was the large television screen on the wall outside of our sixth floor room. Much more fun watching the Euro 2012 tournament that way!
Overall, I'd gladly stay here again, if only to take advantage of the free wine hour (which we missed). I'd also recommend joining the Kimpton loyalty program, which gets you free wifi (essential these days). Staff were friendly and the neighbourhood, though not that interesting on its own, is close to the subway and a short walk from good shopping.

title: “Dated property, but classic four seasons experience”
text:
First and foremost this is a business hotel through and through. It's located in the downtown area, great for meetings but very quiet in the evenings.
The hotel feels like its getting a bit older, but upkeep is good as you would expect, and service and rooms are of the four seasons quality you would look for. I didn't eat in the restaurant, but the room service was good and the dry cleaning service was fast and efficient.
All in all a great choice when in Houston for business.

title: “Make memories that will last a lifetime.”
text: The Brown Palace is the only place to go when you want to make memories that will last a lifetime. It is elegant and the staff are exceptional. We absolutely love it! We have been going to the Brown Palace for Afternoon Tea for several years and everytime is different and always wonderful.

title: “Happy with the Wellington”
text: Just back from New York two days ago and felt I had to write a review on the Wellington as I had read so many critical one's online. The hotel was absolutely fine. We had a very clean, spacious room with two very clean bathrooms. The room was cleaned everyday. We had a problem with the toilet and the t.v on two separate occasions and we rang the front desk to let them know. Within five minutes someone was up to fix it. Staff were helpful although they should expand the reception desk as two members of staff is not enough on reception. The location is perfect, with central park so close and times square just a few minutes walk away. I would definitely stay at the Wellington. It's a great hotel in an amazing city.

title: “Nice but nothing special”
text: W Boston is well appointed and the service is good. It was actually one of the better deals in town and the location was good but I did not leave there thinking that I had to stay there the next time I was in town. Work out facility was lacking a bit!

title: “Hope to stay here again”
text: I was in town for the first time for a mini-convention organized by my co. Most of my co-workers were booked at another hotel. I got lucky and got to say at the Conrad. Beautiful, comfortable, friendly, professional...Attached to the hotel there's The Capital Grille restaurant (that I did not get to try) and a wine bar called Tastings that was phenomenal. My only complaint is that the Internet access was not free.

title: “NO working television + double charge=Bad Experience!”
text: My husband and I got married in Maryland, and stayed at the Renaissance Harborplace on our wedding night. Imagine my dismay when, first, the concierge informed us that our room had "two twin beds!" (this after we specifically requested a room with a king or queen bed). They managed to correct this, and we were given a room with a nice harbor view (one of the few impressive points in our experience overall). However, we found that we could not watch a single television program or even a movie due to problems with Marriott's Direct TV feed. The hotel staff attempted to compensate for this by giving us a free breakfast---which, admittedly, was excellent---but did not rectify the television problem at all. Furthermore, and what's worse, we were CHARGED DOUBLE THE FARE! A total of $632 for one night's stay! Absolutely appalling. When I contacted customer service about this, they promised they would refund the charge, which they have not done (it's now six days later). I cannot understand a $350-night hotel not having a working TV; I cannot understand the hotel not at least compensating us some portion of the hotel charge for this; and I certainly cannot understand being charged twice for an overall annoying and disappointing stay. THUMBS DOWN in every sense.

title: “Contemporary and Comfortable”
text: I loved this hotel. Reasonable rate and a nice change from the Hilton/Marriotts. Comfortable bed and friendly staff. An upscale feel like the W, but half the rate. I'd stay here again for business or at the Valencia Hotel(another new and modern boutique).

title: “Positive Experience W/ Friendly Staff”
text: I recnetly had the opportunity to stay at the Residence Inn on N Lamar and it was a exactly what I needed. The rooms was extremely Clean and when I entered it the little radio was set on classical music. That set the tone for the stay. I was there on business and the staff was very knowledgable about their corporate partners and worked hard to make a business travel experience as pleasent as possible. A business partner recomended a restaurant and the Girl behind the front desk google mapped it and printed the directions for me.

title: “BEWARE THIS HOTEL IS DOING MAJOR WORK ON GUEST ROOMS”
text: We stayed the night of December 22, 2011. We were there for a party in the hotel that was slated to finish at 2am. The party was magnificent and the hotel is perfect for any grand party. After all Queen Elizabeth had a dinner for 7000 people here during her tour of America in 1951, who could resist- it is a magnificent room and the stairs and the halls around the ballroom are perfect for any dramatic event. BUT the hotel knowing that we would probably get to bed very late put us on the 15th floor- BEWARE the four floors below us were under serious construction and at 7:30!!! AM the jack hammering, sawing and banging began. WOW if this were a New York apartment building the workmen wouldn't be allowed in the door before 9:30. What are they thinking? The hotel manager, after my calling at 7:30, 8:30 and 9:30 did take off all the room charges and the room service charges which I feel was fair. But be warned: do ask all about the construction and where it is and WHY it starts at 7:30AM!! before you book a room here. Now that being said. We had tea in the Irish pub and it was probably the only time in the US that I have had a proper cup of tea rather than a pot- they actually put the teabag into the cup before the boiling water! The breakfast was also wonderful. Not a prepackaged piece of butter or jam in sight- both in their own individual small container and delicious jam it was. A lovely breakfast. Our room service dinner was very good too. So top marks for the catering. We also had a charming view of the lake. Fantastic location next to the lake. So on every other level this was a wonderful hotel. Just beware and I hope the construction ends before your stay.

title: “There Are Deals to Be Had!”
text: I've stayed here several times for the Blues Festival, which is always the first weekend of June. At least 3 times, I've been able to get a room for $70. through Priceline. It was worth every penny - 10 years ago a Motel 6 downtown was $100. Our room was always clean. One year we had 2 queen sized beds and 2 bathrooms, which was heavenly! Another year we had a very small room. I'm guessing it is just luck of the draw.

title: “Great location and staff; average property”
text: Although the property is for "extended stays," I got a great rate so I stayed here for two nights as I attended a conference at Denver University. The main reason I chose the Towneplace Suites Southeast is its location - right on the RTD lightrail. It was easy to get to the lightrail and take it to DU each day. The front desk staff was very helpful and friendly. The room itself was only "average" in terms of cleanliness. There was a stale odor in the room (possibly smoke even though I had requested a non-smoking room). There was hair on the bathroom floor and in the shower. The location is desirable due to its proximity to lightrail, but it is also right next to the interstate so you hear some traffic noise from your room. There is a Chilis restaurant and United Artist movie theater adjacent - just across the parking lot.

title: “Loved it”
text: Had a very nice room on the second to top floor. Fantastic view, very very large space, with a separate livingroom and bedroom and 1.5 baths. Everything was in new shape. Would definitely stay there again.

title: “The hotel staff was wonderful, the room very small but clean”
text:
I have been to NYC many times in the past, but this was the first time I stayed in the WJ hotel. I was on a strict budget on this trip and I paid a total of $301.00 per night (250.00 for the room and then a bunch of taxes). 
The room was extremely small, and the bathroom was even smaller. I think it iss about the size of your average cruise ship room with the bathroom on ships larger than this bathroom. Also the heat and air are controlled by the hotel and if you are too hot or too cold you have to call them to come and adjust the temperature which they will.
The hotel was in a good location for shows, shopping, eating and central park. We felt safe. It is 2 blocks from the E train which takes you to Queens so that you can ride the Q33 bus to LaGuardia Airport. (It cost about $ 3 to 4.00 each way vs a taxi. The trip took us about 50 minutes total from hotel steps to terminal )
The staff was excellent, helpful and just plain nice. All of them were that way. The rooms were very clean and the bed comfortable and firm. I would stay there again. Once you get over the "small room" shock, it is a wonderful place to stay if you are on a budget.

title: “The housekeeping was exceptional”
text: My experience at the W was greatly enhanced by Joy Runy. She was the housekeeper on my floor (12) for the last two weeks. She greeted me in the hall everyday with a smile. One morning, I was running late for work and left my door open by mistake. She closed it for me as well as let me know what had happened so that I could check my belongings for everything. She took the time to talk to me durning my stay and truly cared about my New York and W experience.

title: “Comfortable hotel with friendly staff and great location”
text:
Pros: comfortable, well-appointed rooms. convenient location - many tours start around the corner. friendly staff. free wine-tasting in the evenings. noise proof windows.
Cons: touristy area. room window faced another hotel room.

title: “Internet rippoff”
text:
The milford plaza hotel charged me $14.10 per device connected to the Internet per day. That's $42.30 per day for 1 person in a single room with an ipad, laptop and iphone. 
The connection was so slow that i had to connect my ipad to read mails while i was waiting for mails on my laptop to send. I also connected my phone once per evening to skype my family which was a waste of time as it kept cutting out. What a disgusting blatent rippoff. I'm furious. I expressed my discust at reception and the best they would do is remove a total of $28.20 from my bill. 
While i fought my corner at reception a guy beside me that stayed 2 nights was being charged for 4 days internet connection. The manager would not come to the desk to speak to us despite our continued requests and instead left the girl on reception to deal with all of the unhappy customers that were waiting.
They need to be exposed for this blatent and criminal rippoff!!
Ps: the rooms are tiny and grubby with hair all over the sheets and toilet floor.

title: “Great overnight stay at the Hampton Inn in Charlotte”
text: We selected this hotel because of the special package that included a gas card. We were very pleased with the staff when they upgraded our room when they learned that we had an additional traveler, our granddaughter. They gave us the same rate and the same gas card package. The room was very clean and we had plenty of towels and toiletries and bedding for the couch. The hot breakfast was unique. They offered a variety of breakfast items that could be warmed up in a microwave that provided pictures of the food to get the correct heating time. Since we changed rooms at the last minute at arrival, they gladly provided the water that we normally receive as a platinum Hilton member upon request the next day. The staff was friendly and helpful. They had a small outdoor pool, but we did not use it because it was crowded due to a family reunion being hosted on the premises. We were also pleased with the wireless internet service.

title: “Great Location-Great Staff”
text:
My wife and I and another couple stayed here during NIOSA. Location cannot be beat-walking distance to everything in the downtown core. A nice bar lounge with big Bay windows overlooking the river and wonderful for people watching.
The room we had with a King Bed isn't huge but it is OK. The bathroom and closet share a sliding door-If you want the bathroom closed, the closet must be open and visa-versa. Also if the safe in the closet happens to be open and you want to open the door to the bathroom-CRASH!. It was obviously a space saving design but it is inconvenient - the refrigerator was also behind the sliding door in the closet-quite inconvenient.
The other annoyance was the thin walls and lack of soundproofing-we are not usually extremely light sleepers but hearing the telephone ring in the next room and jumping up to answer our own room phone might give you our impression.
Apparently the hotel was built in 1968 and was of modular construction-that is the room modules were built on the ground and lifted into place and stacked together like building blocks and I guess noise insulation was not high on their list. The hotel was completed in 202 days which is remarkable!
We heard rumors that the hotel was going to go through renovation so if so hopefully they will address those issues. 
Would we stay there again-yes- the hotel is well run, the staff are great, the rooms are clean and the location is terrific.Those other idiosyncracies we just accepted.

title: “Mostly good”
text:
This is my second time staying at this Hyatt location, and this time it cost half as much. Perhaps due to the economy and big discounts?
The location is fabulous - right on the waterfront, walking distance to the gaslamp district and museums. 
The hotel is huge and the front desk & concierge staff are helpful. Concierge suggested a couple non-touristy restaurants and the one we chose was excellent. 
The room size was adequate with a king bed, louge chair, desk, and mini-fridge. Good mattress and linens, with extra pillows and blankets. Our room was quiet - which is a huge deal for me, I can't stand hearing the people upstairs walking around.
The decor and bathroom fixtures need updating. Decor doesn't bother me, but drippy tub faucet and shower temperature variations are annoying. We let them know on the way out. For the price, I don't mind putting up with these things. 
All in all, it worked out well for what I wanted.

title: “One problem after another with our reservation - handicapped travelers beware!”
text: Stayed with several family members at the Marriott over Memorial Day weekend. Booked three rooms (two handicapped) directly with Marriott reservations and fortunately printed and brought copies of the reservations. There was one problem after another with the rooms (correct room types not available, unable to provide any adjoining or connecting rooms, arrival and departure dates incorrect-not matching the reservation). Each person at the front desk seemed to try to fix one problem, then screw something up with the reservation and cause another problem. In total ended up spending about two hours dealing with various front desk personnel. I travel quite regularly with business and have never had such a problem at any hotel I've stayed in. The fact that we paid over $400 per night for such a bad experience just makes it worse. Find another hotel.

title: “Service needs an overhaul!”
text: My boyfriend and I stayed at the Soho Grand for one night. The service is HORRIBLE. When we checked in the room was not ready, so we decided to go and have lunch at one of the restaurants in the area. We arrive back at the hotel, and our room is finally ready. We checked our bags with the bell hop, and they said they would send them up immediately. It took two and a half hours for our bags to arrive. We spoke to the manager Osacar and he said he would get right on it. After three phone calls the bags finally arrived. Room service was average. We had drinks in the lobby bar and the waitress was extreamly rude. The service at this hotel really needs improvement. The room itself is a little small for my liking. I wouldn't stay at the Soho Grand in the future. Choose another hotel.

title: “Never Again”
text: This hotel gives all Sheratons a bad name. At first our room looked clean until we came back from swimming at their pool and wanted to give the kids a bath, we noticed all the hair left in the shower and the beds. After we waited a hour and a half for them to clean the room again, we noticed the next morning the cups left in the corner of the room and the club wrist bands on the floor left by the previous attendents. When we went to complain and had to wait in line behind five other guest that were complaining.....

title: “Excellent location, value, and employees that care.”
text: Spent a night in Seattle at the Westin... everything here was great but rather pricey. We noticed the SIxth Avenue Inn as it was nearby. We decided to swing through Seattle again at the end of our vacation and called the Sixth Avenue Inn. On the phone, I totally appreciated the tone and helpfulness of the gentleman who answered. He represented the property well. He offered two queen beds, vs. two double beds and suggested we might qualify for a discount? We got the Facebook discount... yep. The room was clean, and everything we needed. The beds were comfy, there was free wi-fi. The location of the hotel is ideal if you wish to be in walking distance to Pike's Place Market, Nordstrom (1 block away), a mall..., walking or monorail to the Space Needle, and lots of shops and restaurants. There was also a fridge and microwave in our room which was a nice surprise. We typically stay in 4 or 5 star properties and found the Sixth Avenue Inn to be very nice.

title: “Great service, comfy beds = perfect after a long trip”
text: After a tiring 10 days of travels it was nice to greeted so warmly at check in. Check in took only around 5 minutes which was perfect. Our room was clean and the beds were very comfortable. The free shuttle to and from the airport is a bonus and very convenient with my flight coming in late. I have already recommended this hotel to our Kiwi's travelling in & out of LA Airport. Keep up the great service I will be staying again for sure.

title: “What a disappointment!!!”
text: My daughter and I booked a 2 night stay at the "DIVA" and when we got there the young lady who checked us in was very nice. The concierge guy was not pleasant at all especially when I tried to ask a question about a place that I had reservations for dinner that night. When we got to our room on the "Salon Floor" what a MAJOR disappointment!! Our room looked out onto a alley that was full of garbage cans and it REEKED like hell of garbage if we tried to open the windows and the other window looked out onto a brick building don't get me wrong you can't control a lot of things like that but good lord . The carpets were dirty in the hallway, the full length mirror in our room was leaning against the wall and not attached and we were told that there was free bottled water in the rooms on the "Salon Floor" but no there was not. When I called down to the front desk to let them know, they had done a shift change and the guys kept asking me what I want him to do about it and about 2 hours passed still no water or maintenance to be seen. I went down to the front desk and a housekeeper finally came out and handed me 2 bottles of water but not the kind that was advertised that was suppose to be in the room and the young man said all he had was a suite left on that floor and he was not going to give it to me and he did ask me if I would like at all, MAYBE I had the money for the room and he and the concierge guy made us feel like we were really nothing. The concierge finally showed me a room that was 3 floors down and it was exactly like the one that I paid more for. I have tried to call before but was placed on hold for a long period of time and then the phone just hung up. We came for my daughters spring break and we were stoked about coming but ended up feeling like we were not worth the time for some consideration of politeness and common decency. So we ended up leaving early the next morning and drove to Oakland to stay at a nicer hotel.

title: “Friendly and very central for all the sights !”
text: Just wanted to say that we have had a great stay in NY in this hotel. ALL of the staff were very friendly and helpful, and nothing was too much trouble. It was ideally located for all the major sights, and within easy walking distance of Times Square, and the underground if you needed to use it. The suite was spacious with loads of cupboards and well equipped kitchen - our only one complaint was the heat !!! We felt a bit like we were in a sauna! The breakfast was ample and we were evenly pleasantly surprised by the sofa bed - not half as uncomfortable as previous reviews had made it out to be! Thanks for making our trip so enjoyable, and especially to Sam who made us feel welcome from the outset.

title: “Not the best but not bad either”
text: Stayed her for total of 2 nights. The hotel is pretty much road touch. A place seemed a bit over noisy during weekend. The rooms were okay. Breakfast definitely need some improving. The parking lot was dated quite a bit. Staff was friendly enough. The internet kept on disconnecting for some reason, it may have been something with my pc but I had used it a few days earlier at some other hotel. Overall stay was okay.

title: “Wouldn't stay here again...”
text: Service was very good, location is good, however, hotel is a bit on the seedy side. Wouldn't stay there again, it was actually kind of creepy...

title: “Central, friendly, lots of extras”
text:
Second time staying there, and it will be our base in NYC from now on. Sure, it's in a great location - but so are lots of other hotels, some priced as well. What distinguishes Staybridge Suites is the experience itself - from the friendly staff, to the completely equipped rooms (full fridge, stovetop, micro, dishwasher, and fully stocked to enjoy anything you can imagine), to the full, tasty breakfast, to complete focus on customer service. Need to print out tickets? Go to their bank of computers, call up your email, hit 'print', and walk to the desk. No charge, and it's instant. Wifi is free. Rooms are kept clean and are very comfortable. Lobby is lively, with lots of international travellers. There's a complimentary 'light buffet', with wine and beer, Tuesday thru Thursday. 
Special mention: Jamie is the guy who pushed it over the top in both friendliness and helpfulness the first time we stayed, and we were delighted to see him again this visit. Have him teach you the special hand-bump routine.

title: “compact & cozy”
text:
I am really impressed with the other reviews of this property. They pretty much hit the mark. 
Don't be put off by the somewhat garrish apearance of the red marquee with some missing letters which give the look of a 
"No-tell Motel". This is a well maintained property, with a courteous and efficient staff. The rooms are compact but comfortable, though the bathrooms are rather a bit too "abbreviated", read very small. The bed was very comfortable and the linens were very fresh. The AC was working in Oct!!! however, it was not silent when cycling on and off. Other than this, my room was quiet. The breakfasts consist of small and unvaried selection pastries, crusty bread, cheese, prosciutto, granola and good coffee. The addition of some fresh fuit would be very nice.
The location is convenient for Met Museum visits, the Neue Galerie, and the Guggenheim Museum, etc. The metro station is just around the corner on Lexington.
My family lives in the neighborhood, so I will probably stay at the Franklin in the future if I come alone; though, I think my husband might find the rooms too compact for his comfort. 
However, dear traveler, be aware that there is a "sevice charge" added to your bill. When I asked about this, I was told it was for ...
basically the amenities - the NY Times every morning, the internet access, the breakfasts, the robes, slippers, toiletries, etc. Nope, there's no "free" lunch Virginia! Let's have some truth in advertising, please.

title: “Disregard All other Reviews”
text: I was on the phone with Jeff several times about the poor reviews. I was promised a pleasant stay because the hotel had been purchased by a new owner. The pict on the web site are as promised, clean and very comfortable beds. Jeff and Paten (?) were VERY helpful in assisting us with the better restaurants, tips on where to ride the underground train to get to Hollywood Walk of Stars and grocery stores. They were always available at the desk if needed. Breakfast was pretty good and since it fed a family of 4 much worth the price. The hotel includes parking and breakfast - not many do around there. I was VERY happy with our stay here. Parking not an issue and we rarely saw guests in the hotel, very quiet. Thank you for making our stay wonderful! I appreciate you keeping the promise.

title: “Convenient but not clean”
text: This place has a friendly staff, but the rooms are small, noisy and not very clean. Close to Union Square, but this is a bare bones place. Good restaurant down stairs. Mold and crud in the shower. Noise from the street, so stay on upper floors. Had an incident where the cleaning staff threw out a bag of wine glasses and cork screws. They said it was on the trash can. The hotel did send it to me, but charged me for the postage.

title: “A superb hotel which fully lived up to its high reputation!”
text: We chose the Casablanca Hotel because of its high ratings on TF, and we were not disappointed. Only 100 yds from Times Sq, its location is perfect and although I expected to pay the price with noise at night, excellent sound proofing meant a quiet night's sleep! Service was impeccable, food superb and the Moroccan motif added character and a touch of fun! A firm favourite for us now, and we will be back!

title: “Worth overlooking the shortcomings”
text:
The exteriors of the buildings are showing their age. Tile throughout the grounds are dirty and cracked, the floor mats in front of room doors are often dirty and glasses from room service (not ours) were not picked up in front of our room for 3 days. 
The room we stayed in was quite large with two queen beds. Apparently they upgraded us from the normal garden view room to one that was 25% bigger. If you can afford the extra few dollars get this bigger room rather than the cheaper smaller ones. The smaller rooms had their patios right outside their front doors on commonly used walkways rather than on the oppossite end of the room the way ours was. While we could see other people from our location we at least didn't have to worry about people tripping over our feet while they walked by.
The room was updated with new carpeting, bedding etc... Beds were comfortable but not as nice as some I've stayed on. The bathroom was loud, you could even hear when neighbors took showers, but had nice towels.
The pool and grounds around it were above average, even better than I had hoped based on the rest of the exterior condition of the hotel. There were lots of kids on the weekend however so I wouldn't recommend for someone looking for a quiet get away. The weekdays we were there were very quiet. 
Some rooms have fire pits outside. I personally did not like this as I don't want to smell smoke when I'm sleeping. We had a family move in below us who liked a good fire so that prevented us from leaving the sliding glass door open in the evenings.
The beach that is right outside of the hotel is really nothing special at all compared to the other excellent San Diego area beaches we visited. Still it gave our 3 year old a chance to play in the sand which is all she really cared about.
We had lunch and dinner at the hotel multiple times. It is very expensive but was of a high enough quality that we weren't dissapointed. One tip. Ask for the lunch menu if nothing on the dinner menu looks appealing. I could only have steak so many times and discovered that they'll server lunch during the dinner hour. The turkey wrap I ordered while still expensive was excellent.
I'm giving the hotel 4 stars simply because I enjoyed myself. For that reason alone I believe it deserves more than 3. It makes it easy to overlook the shortcomings.

title: “Great Staff!”
text:
All of the staff members were very pleasant and friendly. The concierge desk goes out of their way to accomodate the guest. The bell/valet gentlemen were exceptional at making suggestions and offering tips to get around the city. 
Our room had an exceptional view of the river and surrounding area. It was very clean, quiet and comfortable. The only drawback to the hotel is that it is not close to any of of the major attractions or restaurants. It is a great location when on business, but may be a problem with families with children since moving around the city is a challenge. It is almost impossible to find parking around the city. It is imperative to use public transportation or the cabs. Walking back to the hotel one afternoon, I noticed a couple of cars wheel locked. Be careful parking!
The hotel does have a $25 - $35 a day charge, but the car was secure and I felt very comfortable with the parking facility. I think that is reasonable considering the level of security for the vehicle. If you check with any of the major hotels, or try to park at the Phila. airport, you will see that the charges at the Hyatt are acceptable.
The restaurant was expensive and the food was average. Not a good situation for families since there are no family friendly restaurants close by. The bar and bar menu was very good and more reasonably priced. The morning breakfast bar was very nice and reasonably priced for those of us in a hurry.
I felt safe in the hotel and the area around the hotel. I'm not sure that I would recommend the location for families with young children or teenagers.

title: “Average hotel”
text: We stayed at the Hilton Chicago for 2 nights in April. Although the hotel itself was beautiful, the rooms were rather small. Literally, there was barely enough room to move around the bed. As others have stated, the bed was very comfortable though. The location was okay - quite a way down Michigan Avenue.

title: “Nice, recently renovated room”
text: My room was in tower 3 and had been recently renovated. The room decor was modern, quiet and very comfortable. The only complaint about the room itself was the poor space design in the bath in which the toilet was placed too close to the wall. Otherwise, a nice room in a convenient location. The staff, particularly the housekeeping staff, were some of the friendliest that I have encountered. I do agree with some previous reviewers, the wifi was slower than expected. However, it was usable. Overall, a good experience.

title: “great airport hotel”
text:
Prepaid rate on hilton.com $84 a night. Excellent rate for 2 people 2 beds.
Free shuttle from rental car drop off location.
Decent wireless internet access.
All staff extremely helpful: front desk, housekeeping, shuttle driver, bell person.
Front desk let me use their printer to print some business docs, for free at 9pm.
Prompt and free shuttle for early AM flight.
Quiet and odor free room. 
Too many feather products, but the housekeeping staff was prompt at bringing replacements without feathers for the bed.
Good in room coffee.

title: “Great Hotel - Excellent facilities, service & location”
text:
My family and I (2 children under 2) had the pleasure of spending two weeks at this hotel as I was working in San Francisco. We were upgraded from a Junior suite to an executive suite due to our extended stay. The rooms are well appointed and the bathrooms are large and well decorated. The pool and gym and both excellent. 
The location is first rate close to Union Square and Westfield shopping centre. 
The staff are excellent, knowledgable, friendly and helpful. 
Overall I would recommend this hotel to business travellers as well as families and holidaymakers.

title: “We loved this hotel!!”
text:
This hotel was perfect for our family. 
The highlights:
-Amazing esplanade trail with park along the trail that our kids loved, and mom loved jogging along every morning
-Balcony overlooking pool was very relaxing and great views
-Staff were all very friendly
-Pool and outdoor fireplace area were great
-Trader Joe's and Von's grocery stores super-close for beach supplies and groceries
-Starbucks and restaurants right in the adjoining retail area
-breakfast buffet was also delicious with friendly service. Omlettes made to order, waffles made to order, oatmeal with all the fixings, and fresh scrambled eggs and bacon etc...
