- the bar area was also very nice. 
-close to all the attractions, as far as freeway access and main street access. 
Cons: 
- maybe the airplanes were a little noisy, it didn't bothder us at all... But it is close to the Airport
-the elevator was slow. We ended up taking the stairs most of the time which isnt a bad choice. 
Overall a really friendly, convenient, nice hotel GREAT for families and other travelers. By far the nicest Courtyard I've ever stayed at. Stay here!!!!!

title: “Nice Hotel”
text: This is a very upscale property. The staff was knowledgeable, kind and considerate. The rooms were large and the bathrooms were great. The restaurant was one of the best we have enjoyed. Spa services were outstanding. We highly recommend the hot stone massage. Only two things keep it from being a 5-star review. The property lists having a hotel car available for transport in a 3-mile radius, but it was never available during our stay. We had to take cabs everywhere. Not that expensive, but just a little annoying. The other thing was the supposedly $85 credit for lunch. The fine print stated that the credit did not include the brunch. However, brunch is the only meal served at noon on Saturday and Sunday. Just something to be aware of for the weekend traveler.

title: “Hotel was nice right during construction”
text: We stayed here during a conference . The hotel was ok . The good part was it is next to a mall and movie theatres and restaurants galore. The problem was there was majror construction going on in front of the hotel so going anywhere became very difficult. The staff were very friendly and helpful but the bar is in a atrium and closes at 11pm . The rooms were old but clean. Since the bar is open the sound travels. All and all it was a descent trip . Probably would stay a little closer to Seattle next time .

title: “Average W - High Price”
text:
The W - Union Square is in a great location. It is within walking distance of many dining options and shopping. It is a skip away from Time Square and only a few stops from down town. It is hard to find a better spot. 
The rooms: we were on the 7th floor King Bed Mega Room. Supposely we were upgraded, but its hard to tell the difference b/t Spectacular, Wonderful, or Mega rooms at this hotel. So I really wouldn't splurge to upgrade here. The bathroom are standard in size and a little bit dirty. The corners need scrubing and several fixtures need changing (cracked lights), dirty shower curtain. The beds are comfortable but the duvet cover are a bit on the dirty side. They really should change those or disgard them when they are dirty. There were not sound from the room next door and the sound of the street is minimal. 
The rooms are modern but a bit tired and old. the hallway to the rooms are very very dirty and needs replacing. Lots of stains and water marks all over. Good thing they keep the lights dimmed. 
The front desk morning staffs are superb. But the evening staffs are too cool to pay attention to you. There's a night and day difference b/t the shifts. the morning crew are helpful and professional, while the night staffs are standoff ish.
In room dining were very quick. They cam prompty but hte price for a pot of coffee and apple crisp came out to be $28!
Overrall this is a nice hotel in a GREAT location. The rooms are a bit tired and the service average. It is not a clean hotel by any means. For the rate I paid of $450 per night, it was not worth it. Perhaps $280 is more like it...

title: “loved it .... book a suite ..”
text:
We recently traveled to Chicago for six nights and I stressed over where to stay. I am so thrilled that we booked the Hampton Inn & Suites, Downtown, what an absolute gem!
We booked a suite (there are about 5 on each floor) directly through the hampton site and got a variable rate (from a low of $101 for a night to a high of $150 for 3 nights) and the front desk clerk even commented on what a great deal I'd gotten! Our suite featured a living area with desk, TV, and queen size sleeper sofa (perfect for our two kids at night!) and also had a fullsize refrigerator (trader joe's is only a few blocks away on Ontario), dishwasher, microwave and cooktop (no oven). It was a breeze for snacks and leftovers and comes complete with plates & utensils! The best part was that this was a true "suite" room: the doors closed to the living area and it was like having two hotel rooms!
Check-in was a smooth process; if you have a car, there is an area to pull in and unload your luggage with very attentive bellboys / valet attendees. (note, parking is an additional $38/night through the hotel, but there is also a lot right next door that "only" charges $25/night)
The 2nd floor hosts the swimming pool/sauna/exercise room/whirlpool (plenty of towels available + water in the exercise area) as well as the breakfast room & there is also coffee/tea and hot cocoa available at all times. The breakfast room is very large, with plenty of seating (tables as well as couches) and the buffet itself featured two hot items daily (eggs, sausage, sausage gravy, etc.). There was also a nice selection of breads (bagels, toast, muffins, danish, biscuits), cereals, yogurt, fresh fruit (oranges, bananas, berries, apples, citrus fruit salad), oatmeal (in packets) as well as coffee,tea and juices. The employees re-freshed the foods constantly and even when there were a lot of people present, it was not difficult to get food/find a seat.
There are also laundry machines available for guest use on the 3rd floor; two washers and dryers that cost $1.50/load (quarters available at the front desk). 
All in all, we loved our stay at the Hampton Inn & Suites, downtown. The location was perfect for all of our site-seeing needs: walking distance to the Mag Mile, the free trolley runs to Navy Pier right out front of the hotel, there are plenty of restaurant options within walking distance (weber grill, rock bottom brewery, gino's east, lou malnati's, rainforest cafe, hard rock, etc..!). A cab ride south to Shedd Aquarium/Field Museum will run you about $10 and was about the same up to Lincoln Park Zoo.

title: “Not what we had hoped...”
text: I stayed at the belvedere a few weeks ago and unfortunately, I was not informed that there would be extensive construction going on at the time. They first put us in a room that was so loud and actually vibrated from all the work happening on the floor below. The rooms are small, the elevators even smaller and the bed are uncomfortable. The internet connection is extremely slow and good luck with the elevators. Overall, I was hoping this hotel would be a clean, comfortable place to stay based upon reviews, but I was really disappointed!

title: “Great loacation and bargain”
text:
I have stayed here in the past and staff is wonderful. You just can't beat the price for the location. I walked down to union square and over to Chinatown had a great lunch in Chinatown. 
I highly recommend this place for a budget traveler like myself.

title: “Second visit- still underwhelmed”
text:
The previous visit at the W in May left me a little uncertain as it took almost an hour to get into a room after I had checked in (room wasn't ready, was redirected to another room that was occupied). Staff seemed young, disinterested in customer service, more interested in looking cool.
This last visit was better- but the staff is still pretty inconsistent with requests. The bell staff is great but the "whenever" staff is not reliable and the concierge not helpful at all. For example, I called on Monday to cancel a Wed spa appt. Was transferred to the spa, no one answered. Asked the "whenever" staff to relay the message to cancel the appt....never happened.
Rooms are great, always clean. Great bathrooms, water pressure, deep tubs. Housekeeping seems to be on top of everything.
I would suggest moving the wall sconces to each side of the windows so that the wooden shades could be opened all the way.
If I go to SF on business, I'll probably stay at the W but couldn't justify spending the $$ to stay their otherwise.

title: “Very nice Hotel”
text:
Very nice hotel, all the staff were very friendly and helpful. We did not have any problems at all, our room over looked the courtyard which had pleasent music playing in the evening until 10pm. We only ate at the hotel once - clam chowder which was very tasty. For breakfast we went to the restaurant across the road - i recommend this as it was delicious (especially the omlettes!)
The tram line was just across the road - which takes you into the central shopping area. There were loads of restaurants, coffee shops and bars within walking distance too.

title: “Great little hotel in a fantastic location”
text: Just returned from a four-day stay in Seattle and would definitely recommend this hotel to anyone. As others have said, there is no AC, but we didn't need it. Just got a wee bit loud in the morning with the windows open (which you will definitely need to do, it gets stuffy, if nothing else). A terriffic location, close to the monorail and Space Needle/Chihuly, and it was really easy to catch a bus to downtown. They seemed to run about every two minutes! Also, there were some superb restaurants in the area, so no need to go back downtown in the evenings. And the view from the roof is top notch. Will definitely stay here again, especially for the rate.

title: “The Hotel Commonwealth is a "no frills" experience, but their service is impeccable.”
text:
I was at the Hotel Commonwealth for a little less than a week for my brother's wedding. As best man, I had to run back an forth handling minor but important tasks for the groom (my brother) and the wedding party. The front desk at the hotel did everything they could to provide me even the most bizarre requests. Also, I left several important gifts in my hotel room. The lost and found department quickly found the items and we worked out a way for me to have them delivered.
At first glance, the rooms are simple with few amenities. For instance, there is no coffee machine. I do guarantee that if you wanted one in your room, all you need do is ask. I had a small refrigerator delivered to the room. The truth about the Hotel Commonwealth is that it prides itself on its customer service. The beds are wonderful. The location is perfect. Even the restaurant is fantastic. I've visited many hotel sponsored restaurants and this one is probably the best, especially for the price. the drink specials are amazing. I recommend the Bloody Mary.
The only thing if at all I would want changed is the silly cordless phone in between the beds. It would be best to switch that with the more traditional phone that sits on the office desk because it is much simpler to operate. Also, the complimentary internet was incredibly slow.

title: “Nice place to stay and will go back again!”
text: We stayed 5 nights and really enjoyed the property. Courtney at the front desk is awesome, very helpful and enjoys her job. The pool was great, never crowed and very clean. The room was clean and fresh daily. Loved the front porch with chairs to enjoy my morning coffee. There was four staying in this room and we were not crowded. The AC is a little noisy cycling on and off during the night, got use to it after the second night. Here are the problems....Road construction, not their fault. Once you figure out the traffic flow it's not bad. For some reason the cleaning staff would only leave one wash cloth each day, just asking they will give you more. DO NOT LEAVE anything in the room after you check out! I left my bathing suit hanging on the back of the bathroom door, realized it when I got to Dallas, called to tell the hotel, they checked but said it wasn't there, don't believe them, someone is enjoying my brand new bathing suit I wore 4 times. I will stay with them again but I will be careful when I check out.

title: “Exceeded Expectations”
text: I was hesitant because this is an extended stay. I expected lots of noise and mediocre conditions. I was greatly surprised at how well maintained the entire hotel was. The beds were comfy. The rooms were modern. The counter tops were granite. It was very quiet. There was microwave popcorn, tea, and coffee in the room. The breakfast buffet was not spectacular but there were lots of choices. The staff was friendly. I would definitley stay again and recommend to anyone looking for a resonably priced awesome hotel.

title: “Not the best choice”
text:
As they know they are in a good location, they dont do their best.
To my surprise the refrigerator in the room was empty and the bathroom had one savon, shampoing and condicioner. We were in two and these was not sufficient. Not else in the bathroom. For a $300 hotel I throught that they will provide better experience. Looks like a bed and breakfast hotel without breakfast. Definetly was a wrong choice with high price.

title: “Great value in a great location”
text: I was in town for a conference and selected this hotel based on reviews here. I was looking for convenience, quiet, well maintained property. GW Inn did not disappoint. The location is a long block from the Metro, on the Blue line from Reagan National Airport. Rooms are clean, quiet. Staff is pleasant, helpful. As mentioned by others, it is a block or two to the Watergate, Kennedy Center, and the harbor entertainment district below Georgetown.

title: “Stay Here At Your Own Risk”
text: I stayed at The Quincy with my significant other for the New Year’s 2010 weekend and the experience was terrible, however the management’s customer service in handling our problems were great. I’ll start off with all the bad aspects of the hotel. The door customer service was not that great, the receptionist decided it wasn’t important to greet me or offer the Bally’s gym cards they are supposed to offer guests. First off, the décor and infrastructure is not identical to the website’s pictures and descriptions. This is an old boutique hotel that has been remodeled, however a lot seemed skipped during the renovation. The two elevators are only large enough for maybe four people without large luggage, and on the second floor there was a slight rank of an older building. The view from our room was of the central air conditioner, it was this huge disgusting contraption. We closed the blinds so that we didn’t have to suffer with the view. Second, the heating system is a bit odd. There is a thermostat in the middle of the room that I adjusted, only to later see in small print that “if” it didn’t work, to adjust the main HVAC unit behind the couch. This is a college-style heater that sucks to see in a hotel that boasts rooms over $100 a night. Thirdly, looking around the room we find a fridge and microwave that look to be from the 1980s. The bathroom was absolutely disgusting and the closet doors were rickety and old. The carpet around the bathroom and closet area was unevenly cut and the carpet itself seemed very lumpy. I think the only thing in the room that matched the website’s description was the desk. The desk is quite large for those who need to get work done. The rooms are indeed spacious, as other people have noted, however I wonder what good a large room does with crappy equipment. I kept my slippers on, there was no way I’d be walking on that carpet bare-foot. The big doozy came at midnight. Our toilet flooded (this was not due to us), the toilet had barely been utilized. However water spilled all over the floor making the room not really suitable to spend the night in. When I called the front desk, to make a long story shorter, the men were nonchalant, and said all other rooms were sold out, and finally sent us off to a partner hotel that they assumed the costs for (that hotel was not much better…). The main part that hurt and upset me was the lack of care they had. Here is a paying guest looking for proper, dry accommodations after midnight on what is supposed to be the best night of the year, and we’re being shuffled around in the cold trying to find a cab to take us to the new hotel. After this hellish nightmare, I wrote a letter to management and was really impressed by the response. A manager called me back with sincere apologies, and they seemed like they were going to take serious steps to make sure this type of thing never happened again. I got a refund, and was reassured that the men on staff that night were going to catch up on their customer service classes. I was also told that the room I stayed in was being taken off the market to be re-analyzed for further improvements. You can’t find good customer service these days. I was very taken aback and satisfied with the timeliness of response and the actions taken to remedy what had happened. I should also mention that this hotel is connected to a nightclub; the walls must be quite thin, because my room sounded like the dance floor itself. All in all, if you don’t need many fancy bells and whistles to your room and just need a bed to sleep in; this hotel might work for you. If you want a clean and modern facility, this may not be it. Stay here at your own risk!

title: “RUN, far far away”
text:
I was required to stay in this facility for more than a month due to work committments. If I would have had a choice, I would have left after the first few days,. I stayed in the south tower. Everything you read about the housekeeping is true. I had difficulty keeping supplies stocked such as toilet paper and tissues. We would repeatedly go to the front desk for these suppplies, but it never changed. The housekeepers did not appear to know how to run a vacuum, as the carpet was rarely cleaned,even in the halls. 
One Saturday I was called and told I had to evacuate my room due to a flood. Somebody had knocked a sprinkler head off the ceiling. This was approximately 15 floors BELOW my room. I asked why I had to leave and was given no answer except that I had to. I started packing my belongings (a months worth) and received a phone call 30 minutes later and told that was a mistake, I did not have to evacuate. It consistently appeared that there was very poor communication between all of the staff. 
I parked my car there, and got inconsistent information about the rate, the parking priveliges, whether there was an in and out pass and who to go see. I dont have a problem with rules or processes, but everybody working should know what they are. WHen I complained one day to the front desk, the response given was "duly noted". Of course there was no change at all
 My room was a corner room and larger than most with two walls of windows. This allowed all of the street noise and homeless fights to be heard clearly every night. Though the hotel cannot control the environment, it was disturbing that the valet people allowed panhandlers to solicit from guests at the entrance. They did nothing to send these people on their way and frequently allowed them to pace back in forth in front of the entrance. We notified Juan the manager about another potential safety issue, which was the back door. It does not latch on its own. It is a door into the south tower, and unfortunately the homeless population like to sleep there in the evenings. There is a camera there, but the hotel staff was never seen out there or keeping the patio area clean. I dont know if the camera worked, but the potential for anybody walking into the hotel back there was disconcerting at the least. Though it was mentioned to Juan, this problem was never addressed. 
The workout room rarely had clean towels and water early in the morning. This was also mentioned and never corrected, a few times we went in there early and the music was blasting so loud we could not stay in there. When we called the front desk, the only answer was "we dont know how loud it is, we cant hear it". You would think that there would be an established level to set the music. Housekeeping was a nightmare, one day my room was left open. When I returned in the evening it was propped open with the safety latch. I did get an apology, but that is inexcusable. Another day the cleaning materials and chemicals were left on my counter. (How did they clean the rest of the rooms?) Finally, the restaurant. The breakfast is very expensive, but the servers are long term employees and are great. Food is mediocre. We finally tried dinner one night and ordered something at the recommendation of Howard the server. It was a ribeye and crab cake with mashed potatoes and broccolini. It was very good. The next week we returned on our last night in town since it was so good, and lo and behold, what a disappointment. When seated, there was silverware on the floor under the table and rolled up remnants of straw paper and napkins next to the sugar container....Was this table cleaned? We ordered the same thing, and was also disappointed. It did not appear to even have the same cut of meat. One of our dinners did not get ordered. So one person had to wait until everybody else was almost done and she finally got her dinner. The mashed potatoes were thin, the brocollini was cool and the steak was slightly tough and chewy.....did not even compare. This inconsistent service was a hallmark of our stay.

title: “Great Price Great Service”
text: We didn't have a problem with anything on our stay. We arrived about 1 AM. The guy that helped us even gave us the internet rate without me asking. Everything was extremely clean and everyone was courteous. We left some jewelry and cash out on the dresser, the room was cleaned as we were at Schlitterbahn, and nothing was stolen. Towels were easily accessible with a call. The only problem was one of the people staying in the room with us was snoring like an 18-wheeler in second but theres nothing the staff could do about that.

title: “Awesome location, polite service, clean room”
text: Located near the subway, just a coin's toss from Union Square, this small hotel had clean rooms, decent linens and simple - if a bit dated - furnishings. We were lucky enough to get a room with a private bath and two single beds. Bring your own soap. Staff were helpful and didn't mind us storing our luggage there at no extra cost before and after official check-out times. I'd definately stay there again.

title: “Great location, room size, helpful staff, dominico's restaurant - will be back”
text: 6 of us stayed in 2 tower suites. Very spacious rooms, fridge, microwave & coffee machine were great to have. Nellie & Jasmine @ reception couldn't do enough for us - ordered personalised city tour, booked cars, limo's etc. Dominico's restaurant served excellent food - mid-priced. Nice bar there too where Laura remembered our drinks each day. We had stayed there for St. Patrick's Day earlier this year and were not disappointed with our stay again @ Hallowe'en. Right beside Grand Central, 5 blocks from Macy's & Empire State Bldg, 1 block from Chrysler Bldg. Great location, great deli's too - Gourmet Deli turn right out of Hotel and left @ traffic lights - on opposite side, 2 minutes from hotel - really good for breakfast and buffet all day. This is an older hotel but definitely worth a visit. Well done and thanks to the staff.

title: “LOved the pool and the professional reception”
text:
I have been enthusiastic about my recent stay at the Intercontinental Chicago, convenientely located on the "Magnificent Mile".
 I have really appreciated the warm and professional reception, with the staff always ready to assist you.
 Try the "old style" swimming pool next to the convenient gym facilities.
 And, after dinner, don't forget to drop by the new "Wine and cheese bar" , a pleasant and tasty experience in beautiful surroundings.

title: “Excellent Choice!”
text: My husband had heard of the Kitano from a comment made from a Professional Tennis Player. After reading other positive reviews, we decided to try it on our recent visit. We could not have been happier. The Kitano was situated a few blocks up from Grand Central right over Park Avenue. With the windows shut, there was absolutely no outside noise. It is a Japanese hotel and had traditional Japenese accents throughout the hotel. The exterior was well kept and had doormen that were always very friendly. The front desk staff were very friendly as well. They were very quick at check in and we had even arrived quite early before check in. They had a room available so they allowed us to go ahead and check in. We went up to our room, which was a bit small (but remember-NY rooms are usually a bit small) but was very nice. The bed was very comfortable and the view was right over Park Avenue. They had a nice flat screen tv. They even had a complimentary umbrella to use during your stay..which we did one afternoon. That was very nice little detail that we appreciated. They had a tea maker in the room with very nice tea cups. They also had stem glassware. You could call the front desk and they delivered a container of ice at no additional charge. There was not an ironing board in the room. The shower was nice as well as the HEATED towel rack! They offered High speed internet but we didn't use it. Some tips we have is to definitely travel in the early am for the quickest transportation between airport and hotel. The worst time is 5pm...takes at least an hour to get from manhatten to LaGuardia. Also, don't buy a snow globe unless you plan on packing it on your checked luggage-can't take it on the plane. Loved Little Italy, China town was interesting-right on the edge is a store I just fell in love with called Peony Red, Times Square-well,it is just crazy busy-Rockfeller Center was so much fun and had a Wimbledon set up which was awesome! They even had a grass court set up. I would definitely recommend the Kitano hotel. It is clean and friendly and you feel safe. Close enough to everything-either by walking or subway!

title: “The Ultimate Hotel”
text:
There's one hotel in Washington DC that captures everything a stay in our Capitol should be, and it's the incomparable Hay Adams Hotel. By its name it tells you of our leaders that have and do stay there, and the atmosphere reflects the care and consideration shown to the world leaders that have come and gone from here. 
Do you want some of the best food in DC? Do you also want a varied menu with artistic presentation yet comfortable to eat?
Do you like a small hotel, intimate, a staff that treats each guest as a VIP but is respectful of your privacy? Do you long to have your coffee/tea and breakfast in a restaurant with shafts of sunlight coming into the room that sets you up for the best of days? 
The Hay Adams has all this!
Do you want to have a cocktail or small supper available when you don't feel like "going out?" This hotel has a low lite room fitting your needs and it also is a place to meet and greet when that feels right. 
Your room or suite envelops you with luxury and warmth, the services are immediate and discreet. The hotel's elegant simplicity calms and centers the busiest traveler. Picture a small wood paneled lobby with comfy chairs and a huge bouquet on a table to greet you. You're there and yet home.
Speaking of home, our national home, the White House, can be viewed from many of the rooms. The Hay Adams is the ultimate location. On the top floor is a dining room used for holidays and special occasions. From there is the most magnificent sight ... the White House is almost your next-door neighbor, all lit up at night with the Washington monument directly behind.
Do treat yourself to this hotel. You'll remember the experience for the rest of your life!

title: “Great place for a getaway”
text: My husband and I were treated wonderfully. The rooms were clean and the employees were so friendly and helpful. This was our first visit to California and we had a wonderful experience. I would recommend the Paradise Point Resort and Spa to my friends and family.

title: “Magic in Manhattan”
text:
We stayed in the Hampton inn in December for 4 nights and we had a fantastic time. The location is perfect. We booked to see Hairspray on Broadway and it was only one block from the Hotel.The Hotel itself is very nice, the rooms spotless clean and a decent size especially for New York. We had plenty of room for the 4 of us including storage of our luggage and more importantly our shopping. I have stayed in the Ramada New Yorker in the past and their room sizes are very small in comparison. The beds are to die for at the Hampton and after shopping 10 hours a day they were a welcome sight every evening. Breakfast was great and a full choice for all. It set us before a long day shopping.
The location of the Hotel is perfect for food and drink and entertainment. The Cosmic diner across the road is very nice and recommended by chef Ainsley Harriott. Rays pizza next door serves fantastic pizza and well worth a visit. The house of Brews bar around the corner is great although the cocktails are a bit pricey at $10.00 but it did not stop us having a taste of them all anyway.
Overall a fantastic place to stay and looking forward staying there again when we return,

title: “Ghastly, Terminally Hip...kind of sleezy...”
text: If you like sleeping surrounded by the color of metal, then this is your place. This place is like a porn set in space or a gay brothel in a Woody Allen movie. Some idiot also got cute with the light switches which are impossible to figure out. Stay away unless you are 25 and work in the fashion industry, and that case go go go to the FAAAAABULOUS Dream Downtown Hotel!

title: “Absolutely FANTASTIC ! NO reason at all NOT to stay at this hotel !!”
text:
Absolutely FANTASTIC ! 
NO reason at all NOT to stay at this hotel.
NOTHING "wrong" AT ALL.
We had the N.W. CORNER room on the 14th floor (rm 1425). The ROOM was 15'x 14', the ENTRYWAY was 4'x 6.5' (with a place to hang clothes).
The bathroom that everyone talks about being "SO SMALL" was not THAT small... It was 5'x 6.5'.
It DID have a pedestal sink in it and below it is mentioned by the hotel that they are/were replacing the old sinks with pedestal sinks, 
so maybe we got a newer room ?
There was also an 32" LG Flat Panel TV.
Looking at the floorplan card in the room it looks like there are 5 corner rooms on each floor that are this same size, 
(room numbers xx01, xx02, xx05, xx25, xx26), and one that is HUGE corner room suite (room number xx14 ). Yes, 6 corners not 4...
The REST of the rooms look smaller on the floorplan... 
SO just ask for one of the "corner" room numbers that I listed above !! (they may all be KING rooms, ours was)
The room and bathroom were very clean. 
The location of course was AMAZING !
PARKING: The CHEAPEST parking in a 5 block radius is only 2 blocks EAST at 330 E Ohio St. 
It is the McClurg Court Parking garage. [---] $30/24 hours
GROCERY: One block SOUTH and 1/2 block EAST (255 E Grand) is a FULL SIZE Dominick's grocery store.
It is REALLY nice, with a huge Wine selection, decent beer selection and lots of produce, bagels, muffins, etc. plus all other regular grocery items and
a full drug store.
QUICK-FOOD: Within the 1 block around the hotel is Chipotle, Subway, Dunkin Donuts, Potbelly, Pockets, and several other places to grab something quick.
I am SURE going to check rates at this hotel EVERY time my family and I go to Chicago !! JUST G-R-E-A-T !!
I cannot understand what anyone was complaining about with this hotel...

title: “Nice room, brewpub in lobby, sweet!”
text: My room was nice and quiet and clean. I had lunch and dinner at the Gordon Biersch brewpub located in the lobby - absolutely wonderful German wheat beer. I was able to easily walk to the Whitehouse, actually saw President Obama as he drove in with motorcade - would be cool if I liked him.

title: “Bed Bugs”
text: As a former property manager I know that bed bugs are very hard to get rid of. Once you take them home you will have an infestation.

title: “Tale of two visits....”
text:
We stayed here two consecutive weekends this month and had two radically different experiences. Our first trip we simply took a cab the short distance to the hotel, checked in smoothly (and VERY early after a red eye) to a new, quiet room with strong internet and a great view (the sunset was spectacular). We used the shuttle to get to the T and the airport with no complaints.
The following weekend was a completely different hotel. First, we were left stranded at the airport in 6 degree temperatures waiting for the shuttle -- despite multiple calls -- before taking a cab. We were given a room on a floor that reeked of smoke and had partiers roaming the halls and shouting from rooms. We were booked into another room on a different floor that clearly had walls made of tissue paper. We were woken early by a crying baby several rooms away and could here every ablution by our neighbor the next morning.
To be fair, Joe and Max were extremely apologetic, did all they could and comped a few things. Apparently our story made its way around the hotel because we were treated extremely well the following days.

title: “Great location, friendly staff, rooms lacking”
text:
Having just written a lengthy review and having my computer crash, I will just touch on the highlights (or lowlights) instead.
* Staff are amongst the friendliest people I encountered anywhere in the US, the shuttle drivers especially. They also allowed us to store our mountain of luggage pre check in and post checkout.
* Lobby is lovely.
* Basic rooms are ordinary. Old so feel unclean but may be as clean as they can get. Facilities antiquated. Not very comfortable at all, despite the fact we were extremely tired so could have slept anywhere. AC not very good.
* Airport shuttle service runs all day, unlike Days Inn who advertise limited hours. Very hand if you are arriving and leaving in the middle of the day as we were.
* Area is seedy and a little run down. Not really an issue but if you know no better, you kind of expect Elvis Presley Blvd to be beautiful and tree lined, especially with the regular tourist pilgramage that occurs there. Maybe this reflects Elvis's down to earth side. We did have an approach for money in a nearby carpark at night and we did give over the money as we felt intimidated being so isolated in a darkened area, despite not being threatened. Just be wary venturing out in small numbers looking for food. There is food available in the bar area at the hotel I believe and shuttles will take you into Beale Street where food and frivolity are in abundance.

title: “Practical hotel, excellent rate”
text: Stayed in the hotel for 4 nights spanning a weekend mid-September. Weekend rate was an unbeatable $109 per night for a twin room. For value the place was unbeatable. Yes, the rooms are functional and practical but for sightseeing trips to NY city, how long do you want to spend in the room? The bathroom was compact, but again everything needed was there (shower, hairdryer, coffee machine - a strange thing to find that in the bathroom!). As two females travelling alone we found the hotel safe (room cards are needed to operate the elevators so minimises the risk of anyone wandering in off the street, someone was behind the desk at all times) and quiet. I would recommend the hotel and will certainly use again and rate as above average for sheer value for money, safety and location.

title: “On the Ave”
text:
Staff and service would definitely be a reason to return to On the Ave. From the doormen to the front desk clerks, everyone was extremely polite and helpful. They even got me into a room a couple hours earlier than check-in time. Since the weather was nice they even recommended I visit the 16th floor for a drink. I wish I had had more time!
The three star review comes from several other angles, none of which were all that big of a deal, but when compounded, left an impression. 1) I was emailed a voucher for a room upgrade--which was only valid for the day I checked in--but even after calling ahead and telling them specifically I was planning on using the voucher, the front desk clerk said that the rooms had been sold out and I wouldn't be able to use the voucher. I had read that on previous reviews as well, so it wasn't as much of a surprise than a disappointment. 2) I had originally asked for a King bed, but I was given a Queen bed--and the bed was hard! 3) The toilet in my bathroom made dripping noises all night (although to their credit, I didn't notify anyone of the problem because I didn't return to my room until late in the evening) and could have been cleaner. 4) I was given only hand towels, no full sized towels (although again, I didn't notice this until after my shower in the morning, so I didn't notify anyone to rectify the situation). 5) The hallways were a bit dim, but smelled heavily of cigarette smoke. Thank goodness I didn't notice it in the room itself, since I'm allergic and asked for a non-smoking room. 6) The restaurant downstairs (Serafina) wasn't finished, and didn't look like it would be soon. 
The area is nice, walking distance to Central Park, the subway, a Starbucks, and several shops, grocery stores and drug stores.

title: “The Best In Jacksonville”
text: Ok I mean it. I have been staying at the Indigo since April at least 3 to 4 times a month. I am a professional photographer. The location is great the staff is awesome and the rooms are wow. The food is top notch and if you do decided to go out to get something to eat you do not have to travel far. In fact I am booink the stuite today... GREAT SPOT THE BEST IN JACKSONVILL MJ IMAGES PHOTOGRAPHY & GRAPHIC DESIGN

title: “Nice hotel with great location”
text:
Very nice hotel. The staff was very service minded and helpful. It's located very close to shopping, cafés, pubs and public transportation. Only downside was that my room was right next to the elevator which makes a beep sound every time is passes a floor. This can be heard through the walls all night. The plusside of this was of course, that my room wasn't facing the street, and I was therefore not disturbed by the cable cars etc.
If I go to San Francisco again, I will definitely consider this hotel again.

title: “Excellent family friendly hotel, great location”
text:
We recently spent a week at this hotel and were impressed with the friendly service, child friendly service at this hotel. Our children revelled in the swimming pool and the excellent view of the airport, freeway and trainsform the upper floor balcony. (Not to everyones taste!) The decor is dated, but who looks at the inside of a hotel room on a tourist holiday. There was free parking across the road from the hotel which could be useful as parking is tight ($6-12/day/room). Easy access to freeways and public transport.
Only down side is the limited dining opportunities in the Old Town. There is mexican, mexican or poor mexican cuisine. No problem if you have a car.

title: “Pleasant surprise!”
text:
I was pleasantly surprised by the Hilton Manhattan East. While not a luxury hotel by any means, the hotel was just fine for an individual or family planning to spend most of their time away from their hotel room. 
Frankly, my spouse and I booked this room since we were having trouble finding anything under $300 in Manhattan. We wanted something safe and clean and felt confident that a Hilton could satisfy these requirements. Aside from that, we had no demands or expectations.
We were very surprised to a find a well-appointed room with a very comfortable bed, flat-screen TV, large bathtub and nice bathroom toiletries. Even more surprisingly, I could not hear street traffic even though we were on the second floor! The room was definitely tight- you better like your travel companion- but this is to be expected in NYC. I liked the layout of the floor; I never heard passerby in the halls or noise from the elevators. The gym is free and is open 24 hours, accessible with your room key. There are 2 treadmills, an eliptical machine, weights and water/towels. I appreciated the perfect temperature in the gym!
Minor complaints include housekeeping coming despite our request that our room not be serviced and TVs not working on the gym treadmills. For $190 a night, I am willing to put up with those deficiencies. 
The hotel is just a few blocks from the Grand Central subway station, making to travel to both uptown and downtown very convenient.

title: “Delightful Honeymoon Hotel”
text: Ten years ago this week my husband and I stayed at the Beresford Arms on our honeymoon to San Fran from L.A. We were on a tight budget, but wanted to stay somewhere memorable. The Beresford Arms was priced within our range, but what a surprise to find that it was so nice! Very clean and roomy, yet it had a nice, old-style charm to it. We would stay there again, and hope to make it back to the city sometime.

title: “BILLED TWICE!!!”
text: We stayed 1 night and paid in advance through Expedia. Upon arrival at Chicago Crowne Metro, I asked them to be sure not to charge me AGAIN for the room since it was already paid and taken out of my checking account. I was assure I would NOT be charged again. The next day, I am charged again by the hotel - it is now 5 days later and I still do not have my refund. The hotel is OK, I guess, but certainly not worth $278 a night! This included a breakfast but we had to leave long before they started serving! Parking was extra. Not many restaurants in the area (other than Greek) and the hotel actually looks rather old to me. We will certainly NOT be staying again.

title: “Outdated rooms, shabby service, WAY WAY overpriced.”
text: Front desk aloof and slow, not responsive to needs. When asked a question over the phone, transferred 3 times to different people with same results - nothing! Took 4 calls and 3 hrs to get a crib when told at check in its on its way. Rooms are outdated, kitchen looks like its from the Yogi-bear era. Bathrooms with rot and grout. Carpet smells. And we had a dexluxe garden bungalow-whatever that means. Pool rarely stocked with fresh towels. Food is below average and the worst thing is the price they charge. Only nice thing to say is the grounds, but of alot of it is roadways, and taking walks can be a lesson in traffic avoidance. This one is way way overpriced, and really only worth it if the room is <150 a night.

title: “The best location in NY”
text:
+fantastic location
+very trendy
+comfy bed
+iphone speakers for playing music
+nice food in the hotel restaurant
-it's very big hotel and doen't feel very friendly.

title: “Ruined Wedding Night”
text:
After booking our Wedding Night several months in advance. Two attempts were made to check in the day of the ceremony. Only to be told the room was not ready.Flowers and Champagne were delivered by friends,and assured by the front desk, to be put in the room. At 10:15 p.m.
following our reception, we tried to check in. Only to be told our room had been given away. No rooms, no sympathy. No help. Because our luggage was to be delivered later, we could not leave and go on to a new hotel. So we sat and waited. By this time we were so exhausted and frustrated,we just went home. No appology on behalf of the Hotel. IRREPLACEABLE!!!

title: “Perfect in every way”
text: Wonderful staff, excellent location, pleasant stay! Needed a quiet hotel for the night and was welcomed by an accommodating staff. Will definitely stay again.

title: “Great Hotel Exceeded Expectaions”
text: Booked this after reading reviews from other travellers and we were not disappointed. The hotel was excellent value for money as breakfast, happy hour, internet and long distance. were included. The staff were friendly and helpful. Breakfast and happy hour were crowded but no problem with service or food. Would stay here again.

title: “Wonderful location, wonderful staff!”
text:
We stayed at the Orchid Suites for 4 nights in December 2008..the location is amazing! You can't get much closer to the centre of things, and for us this was perfect. You literally walk round the corner to the metro, restaurants, the Chinese theatre, etc etc. The rooms are not the most modern, and probably a bit old-fashioned, but extremely clean. Our room was fortunately at the back, as I think the front rooms can be noisy.
The staff on reception are fantastic - friendly, helpful, and efficient as well. They got tickets for us, booked a transfer, told us the way to places . . . what more do you want?

title: “Wonderful accomodations and service”
text: This hotel was just what we were looking for - economical, clean, cheerful service, quiet, great beds, frig and microwave. We couldn't have been more pleased with our stay at this hotel. It is a quick and simple trip to downtown Indy. Anytime we need to spend the night in Indianapolis, this is where we will stay. The staff was exceptionally cheerful and helpful. Everything was neat as a pin and the beds were extremely comfortable. The breakfast was an added bonus. I really can't think of anything I would change. I did notice that some guests brought their pets. My only question would be as to whether they assign people with pets to particular rooms or whether they clean extensively so as to insure that people with allergies who stay in rooms previously occupied by pets won't be adversely affected. I highly recommend this hotel, probably, by far, the best hotel we've ever stayed in.

title: “Top Notch”
text: I just spent two days in Dallas and had a great experience at the hotel. Certainly the room decor could be a little fresher and the food was not upto their reputation-but the service and staff are top notch.

title: “Small, Efficient, GREAT PUB downstairs!!”
text:
My husband and I travelled to San Francisco for the Nike Women's Marathon Oct 22-24 and stayed at the CQ for 2 nights. We had two rooms, and although I requested adjoining rooms when I made the reservation, when we checked in, we were unable to get them. Instead, we were given rooms that were sort of across the hall from each other. 
The hotel is located across from the embarcadero center, so we spent a lot of time walking through the shops and just enjoying the sights and sounds.
The hotel is clean and nice. The front desk was friendly and check in/out was a breeze.
The rooms were definitely small. They weren't as tiny as I'd feared, but the smaller of the two rooms we had was not something I would choose to stay in again. There are either two twin beds in the room or one queen- much smaller than most of us are used to.
The door to the bathroom was odd- even fully shut, it had a noticeable gap that you could see through, or worse, smell through... sorry to be graphic, but this is a terrible feature of this hotel. This hotel is definitely geared toward the business crowd, with high speed internet free in the rooms, as well as internet on tv for a fee. I would think if a businessperson had a co-worker/client/etc to their room the bathroom door would be a real inconvenience. did i mention the bathroom doors need to be replaced?!
I also was disappointed in the walls. They were very thin, and when the person in the next room didn't shut off his alarm clock for 30 seconds at 4:50am, I got the pleasure of lying awake listening to him get up, take his shower, and get ready for his day. I had my 18mo son in the room with me, and I can only imagine his crying in the night must've interrupted our neighbors' sleep as well. Also, the hotel is literally around the corner from the fire station, so although this is a nice safety feature, be prepared for sirens at all hours-- more sirens than normal, anyway.
The bathrooms/bedrooms were very clean, and the showerheads were wonderful. 
Overall, I'd recommend this hotel if you're travelling on business. Otherwise, I'd suggest something a little more comfortable for a vacation.

title: “Disappointing AGAIN!!”
text:
I stayed here a year ago. It wasn't good. Sometimes when you give a property a year to regroup they can improve problems. Not the case here.
We had a business meeting and one of the bathrooms didn't have any soap leading one person to say "doesn't anything work around here!"
Here are the problems I encountered:
>ice machine didn't work - I had to go to the next floor for ice several times. I pointed this out to the front desk and they said they were aware of it for awhile.
>the bathroom sink's hot water came out like a trickle 
>I was hungry and downstairs the only vending machne was out of order
>the comfort sleep/select for the bed was broken
>the phone indicated I had a message - when I called it just kept ringing so I guess I didn't have a message?
>no glasses to drink out of in my bathroom
>the bed was as hard as a rock.
The front desk didn't ask if my two night stay went well. I was prepared to tell them I didn't know where to start. At least I didn't find a bed bug this year. I guess if you want to pay $118.00 per night for a hotel that is worth about $60.00 - go ahead. At least it is close to the airport and has a shuttle.

title: “Decent option and value”
text:
My husband and I were visiting family for the holidays, and we stayed at this property for several nights. This hotel is right off the highway and across the street from Hewlett Packard. It's a convenient option for business travellers and for families. The room was standard and clean. Service was good, and I appreciated knowing in advance that housekeeping services would be minimal on Christmas Day (this did not bother me in the least, but had I not been told, I would have been upset).
I was a little disappointed that the rooms did not have refrigerators as a standard ammenity (unlike many other hotels I've stayed in recently). The beds were a little soft and uncomfortable. I was greeted as a Marriott rewards member but was not offered any special ammenity as a result. Also, free breakfast is not provided by this brand, but free internet service is.
The lobby area looked recently remodeled and had contemporary furnishings. The hotel was very quiet. We would consider staying here again in the future due to the convenient location.

title: “Honest Review--Worst in Mission Valley”
text: I have stayed in many doubletree hotels. This is by far and away the worst one out there. The rooms are not that clean. It is noisy as anything as it is right on the highway and the staff is as close to incompetant as is possible. Generally this is due to the General Manager of a property, whom I ran into while I was there. When I asked him about certain problems I had he was not only rude but seemed not to care at all. I should only hope those who are planning a trip to san diego read this review, and if you really want to stay at a Doubletree, stay at the one across the street on Hazard Drive.

title: “Would stay again...”
text: I booked this hotel on priceline when I bid $50 and I was very pleased. We had a two room, 1 bathroom suite. The beds were full size and not queen but they were very comfortable. Nice thick bath towels. Clean. Didn't eat at restuarant in hotel but it looked nice. Lots of restaurants within walking distance. Great location. Close to the airport without all the airport noise. Hotel had open floor concept. Staff was friendly.

title: “A perfect location for traveling with teenagers”
text: Located in Fisherman's Wharf and near North Beach, this hotel was terrific for our family traveling with 4 teenagers. Close enough so the older teens could go off by themselves to Ghiardellis and the fun wharf and yet quiet enough for us to get some rest after a long drive. Had everything the kids were looking for except a pool. Many restaurants nearby from fast food to Little Italy, Chinatown, Seafood! Trolley not far. Beds were super comfy, nice bathrooms ( kids loved the bathroom amenities) All in all a place I will return to!

title: “convenient when displaying at McCormick Place”
text:
Just got done with displaying at an Expo in McCormick Place. Staying at Hyatt Regency McCormick made the logistics so much easier. No parking or grabbing taxis morning and night. No having to go outside unless I wanted to. And especially having a close walking distance from my room to the Expo area! Previous years our company had us staying at other hotels and the logistics of parking or cabs and timing was a real pain.
Besides that, the room at the Hyatt was well appointed and generally well kept, with the carpet starting to show some serious wear in our room. The staff was absolutely the best - excellent guest service. On-site parking quite spendy at $30/day if I remember correctly. We will definitely stay here the next time we're displaying at McCormick Place.

title: “I can accept a tired and outdated hotel...but, not dirty”
text:
This hotel is located in Union Square - so the location is the only reason why it received more than a one star. The hallway that leads to the bathroom and closet is painted a garish dark purple as well as the doors to the closet and bathroom - paint all chipped up. The worst part was the grime that caked the door handles to the bathroom. Absolutely disgusting! The wall paper was peeling and had bubbles in numerous spots along with areas what appeared to be mold...or dirt. The room had dust and dirt in corners and table tops. 
The general public areas are much better maintained than the rooms. 
I ordered room service and paid $37 for under ripe fruit, a small container of yoplait yogurt, and a cup of coffee. 
Would never stay here again....even for free.

title: “Great staff! Very clean & modern”
text: Wow, what a suprise! I booked on Hotwire and only paid $77 a night and didn't expect much for that price in NYC. Rooms are very modern and comfortable. They're a bit on the small side but it's NYC so that's expected. We didn't experience the noise issues that the previous reviewer did. The staff was fabulous! Friendly and very accomodating. Chad welcomed us warmly and set all of our bags up in the room while giving us directions to the nearest destinations. Breakfast was ok, could have been warmer but hey, it's free! Eggs, sausage, pastries, bagels, fruit etc. I much prefer staying in this district over Times Square, it's just not quite so crazy and you can get anywhere quickly. There are lots of restaurants that deliver to the room - even sushi - if you choose to stay in and of course many nearby. Macy's is a hop skip and a jump away. Theaters and Times Square are within walking distance. Parking is across the street and very convenient. Make sure your emergency brake works though! The entrance is a very steep ramp!

title: “Very Nice Room and Good Service”
text:
I had a modern very comfortable room. This is a huge hotel with an onsite restaurant and lots of ballrooms. It's in an excellent location and the price was great. I would definitely stay here again. 
Some areas of the hotel did have a mild damp smell but that's the only negative I have...

title: “OK, but neighborhood not so great.”
text: We chose this hotel because it is the closest to Illinois Institute of Technology. However the hotel was still at a premium price in a not so great neighborhood. I did like the fact you could park in a courtyard surrounded by the hotel for no charge. Much safer than being on the street in this neighborhood. The room was fairly nice, but felt cheaply decorated. Staff was not all that friendly. I would only stay there again if I needed to be close to the University again.

title: “Fun Hotel in the Middle of It All”
text:
My wife and I stayed at the Hilton Suites on the latter part of our Chicago honeymoon. We checked in on a Sunday after a mile walk from our previous hotel on the river. Walking in was impressive. I did not realize when I booked on Priceline how great the location was. The block that the hotel was on is in a little quieter neighborhood, but so close to Michigan Avenue and everything else.
One thing I want to emphasize is USE PUBLIC TRANSPORTATION TO GET HERE. I have heard that parking is outrageously priced, and thankfully we had a limo drive us in, and we are taking the train to our car in the suburbs--much more economical.
The lobby is beautiful. We were kindly greeted by the staff, who promptly and politely gave us our room keys, and up the elevators we went. The elevators are efficient and quick, and there seems to always have been an elevator waiting in the lobby. The pool and workout room on the 30th floor are a nice side attraction, especially if a guest were to have kids.
When we came to our room at first, however, we found it to still be occupied at 2:00p!!! How embarrassing! Apparently, they had not checked out when they were supposed to, but still--I think there should have been better communication between the cleaning maids and the front desk on that one. The issue was quickly resolved, and we were given a new room.
It kind of stinks that you have to pay for internet (which I refused, since there was a weak network I could connect to from elsewhere). Other than that, our room was kept clean, there were always friendly greeters at the front, and we had an overall comfortable stay in a beautiful city.

title: “Dysfunctional Organization”
text:
I love the James in Chicago and was excited when one opened in New York. My wife and I stayed there recently and had an ok experience . The hotel was still being completed, the restaurant remained unopened and we had to hold our opinion because so much was unfinished. Clearly not worth the price we paid for the room, but the General Manager at the time, gave us a letter for a complimentary stay any day through March. 
When I called to book a room on Monday, I was passed from person to person and finally told that they would check and get me a confirmation about my selected date later that day. Four days went by with no response, so I called back and was finally told that there was no availability on the date in question. Plenty of rooms available at rack rates, just none available for their comp letter. Of course it was subject to availability, but that meant, I was told, not availability of the hotel, but availability of rooms suitable for fulfilling their comp letter obligations. 
This struck me as total BS. I was then told that the general manager and at least one other position has turned over / they've been fired in the last few days. The revenue manager (who makes these decisions) could only be reached by email because she only owns a cell phone and didn't have a hotel number. (Absurd, and not believable.)
It seems the management of the hotel has lost sight of how to keep RETURN CUSTOMERS happy and the organization generally, in New York, is in a state of chaos.

title: “OK- BUT NOT A FULL PRICE”
text:
FYI- These rooms are small! Four women sharing one room, was no problem when we stayed at The W Union Square, but here we were cramped! There is no way those are double beds. One false room and someone would have fallen out. Also, our room got really hot and they suggested we open the window instead of them fixing the freaking air conditioning... So we really had a chance to experience the sounds of NYC.
I have to admit the staff were great! We arrived to all of our shows in style because the doorman had a nice Cadillac Escalade take us to our show...for FREE! We just made sure to tip him handsomely.
Finally, were able to eat at the Bodega next door really cheap. We had breakfast there everyday for less than $5.

title: “New Hotel in Great Location at a VERY Reasonable Price”
text:
I found this hotel after extensive research via TripAdvisor (which proved to be invaluable for all aspects of this trip). 
I typically look for a clean, newer hotel in a good location that is under $200/night. I don't care that much about having people park my car or turn down my bed. If this is what you need, look no further. 
This appears to be a brand new hotel. It smells like new lumber; kind of how my house smelled when it was newly built. The interior design is contemporary, interesting, and bright. It has many amenities. The pool is smallish, but OK for kids. They have a coffee kiosk (it is after all Seattle) that is inexpensive but not overwhelming in terms of quality. The rooms are great; very plush and comfortable. Fully equipped with flatscreen TV, microwave, fridge, etc. Beds are very comfortable. Floors are wood and tile. No tub, but I never use one anyway. It has a large tiled shower. 
Staff members are casual but polite. Only one glitch: I left some smoked salmon in the fridge and wanted to come back to pick it up. I called them right after checking out and they said they would check it out and get back to me. They didn't return my call and when I called back later they said it had been thrown out. Kind of frustrating although they were nice about it. Didn't offer to adjust the rate. 
The location is very good. It is close to the complex where the Space Needle and other attractions are. You can walk to several restaurants, but it takes a few minutes to do so. The area is safe for walking. They have free parking which is obviously a huge plus. 
All in all, this is a fantastic bargain. You won't find anything else in this area for under $150. My advice is go go for it before they raise their prices up with the rest.

title: “The Pier 5 Hotel was absolutely the best hotel I have stayed at!!!!!”
text: My boyfriend and I stayed in the Mystic Suite for a weekend and I could not be happier with the room, hotel, and service provided. As soon as you enter the hotel the staff makes you feel welcome and comfortable. Benjamin (who was working at the front desk), was very helpful with everything. He was also very knowledgeable about the hotel as well as the places to go in Baltimore. I recommend this hotel!

title: “Help!”
text:
When I was younger 'bout 2 weeks younger than today
I was going to Austin and needed a place to stay
But now I'm home again and writing a review
Now I avow, everything I say, is absolutley true
Help me if you can I'm going down
And I do appreciate the close walk to town
Help me the dollar drinks are making me drown
Won't you please, please hear me
And now the hotel happy hour is oh so very dear
You get free munchies, water, wine and beer
But the morning comes and it's a great breakfast 
Free wifi, comfortable bed, and a pleasant staff
Trust me if you can I'm gettin' down
If you want good bbq Salt Lick is north of town
Believe me when I say here you should stay
Won't you please, please here pay
here pay, here pay, oooohhh

title: “Great location”
text: The rooms were a little small. The service was excellent, the staff made us feel welcome Loved the location with easy access to the subway, museums, times square. We stayed for four nights and the breakfast was different not the same.

title: “Redone. Sets the standard for Courtyard by Marriott”
text: Great team. Check in was so pleasant. Like I was visiting home. Newly remodeled property. Suite was great great location. Definitely returning. The location is close to everything. The staff makes the difference here.

title: “Disregard bad reviews”
text: We stayed on Monday 9/5/11. Disregard all the bad reviews. We did have to wait a bit for our room but it was ready right at 3pm like they said. Yes, they should open the bar area earlier like 12:00pm (nnon) would be good. The room was great, bathroom was small but nice. Bed and pillows were great and we slept very well. Had a room on the back side on the 15th floor, smoking room and it did not smell like smoke at all. There was laundry in the hall but it is to be expected. The cleaning crew had it all gone by 5:00pm. They only have one house keeper per floor, 19 floors, so they did a good job considering. Not sure if I would call this a 4 star hotel closer to a 3 or 3.5. Great location and a great deal for the money. If you want a 4 or 5 star spend the $500.00 plus and stop bad mouthing a good place! We would stay again for sure.

title: “The Palomar didn't disappoint...even though the cherry blossoms did :(”
text:
I really, really love Kimpton hotels. I have had such great, consistent experiences with them in every city (San Diego and Chicago so far). When a conference came up in DC I was thrilled to see a Kimpton spot - especially in Dupont Circle. 
Highlights:
Clean and spacious rooms.
Warm and welcoming staff - we were there for five nights and staff was attentive and became familiar with our routine.
Great location
I also really appreciate the InTouch program and the effort that the staff makes to not only meet my preferences, but go above and beyond to make my visit outstanding. For example, this trip also coincided with my mother's birthday, so I brought her along to see the sights. I mentioned in my reservation notes that it was her birthday and the Palomar staff had champagne, chocolates, and a birthday card waiting in our room!
It's off to Seattle in a couple months and can't wait to see what the Monaco has in store!

title: “Nice, but should have been better”
text:
Don't get me wrong - this omni is a great hotel, but I definitely expected a bit better. 
Rooms were nice and spacious - we were lucky to be on the top floor with a view of Rock Creek Park. Beds and linens are extremely comfortable. The bathroom is updated, but layout is poor and there isn't a lot of room to put your "things" around the sink. Walls are a bit thin, but this was only a problem our last night when the room next to us came in at 4am and make quite a bit of noise - otherwise was pretty quiet.
The gym is top notch and was never too crowded in the mornings - lots of cardio equipment and various free weights and machines.
Our biggest complaint would have to be service. First, my husband traveled with me on this trip and despite having his name on the room, one day when his key became demagnetized, he went through quite a bit of hassle to get back in. They demanded he know the billing address on my work credit card in order to get in. After quite a bit of back and forth, they did let him in, but wouldn't give him another key. Very strange.
We also experienced subpar housekeeping service. If you had the privacy on in the morning, good luck getting housekeeping to come back at all. At one point, we asked them to come back in just 20 minutes (around 1pm) and when we arrived back late that night, still no service. They also failed to empty the trash can on several days.
Room service and the bar and restaurant were all great - decent food and great service. 
We got a great deal on the room - $90 a night, so for that price, I would absolutely go back - just glad we weren't paying what some colleagues were, which was over $200!

title: “Great accommodation with a personal touch.”
text:
We spent 6 nights at the Chelsea Pines and it was everything we had hoped for: a great location, minutes from the subway and on to the famous sights of Manhattan and walking distance to the tranquillity of the Highline Walk, Chelsea Market and Greenwich Village. The rooms at the Inn were cleaned and tidied to a high standard every day (quite a task in our room with 3 females and all the shoes, toiletries etc that go with them!) and there were plenty of fresh towels, and hot water. Breakfast is served in the kitchen/conservatory which is compact but works really well - you just help yourself along with other guests; there’s plenty of fresh fruit, bagels, yoghurt, cereal and a speciality bread of the day (what we would call cake) and of course plenty of coffee, tea and juice. We were spoilt for great places to eat: The Good Stuff Diner was fantastic – a classic New York diner – just a few blocks away; Bill’s Burgers were the best we’ve ever eaten and Two Boots Pizza was great for a slice ‘on the hoof’; then there’s numerous restaurants ‘on the doorstep’ serving food from around the globe. 
This was a first visit to New York for 4 out of the 5 of us, and there was a lot we wanted to do (and did). It was great coming back (nearly said home – that’s how nice it felt!) to the Chelsea Pines at the end of a busy day sightseeing. The guys working there were friendly and helpful and seemed genuinely interested in our days. When we enquired about seeing a show on Broadway, a list was provided and our chosen show booked for us; they also booked us a table at a local Italian restaurant, which was really helpful on a busy Friday night. We had two birthdays in our family whilst we were there and on each occasion a beautiful vase of flowers and a card was left in the room for the girls. A newsletter posted under the door every morning gave a weather report, the speciality bread of the day and some interesting suggestions for things to do, that you would never find in a guide book. Sadly we ran out of time so we’ll just have to return to New York and when we do we’d definitely like to stay at the Chelsea Pines Inn. Highly recommended.

title: “Lovely little hotel”
text:
Myself and a friend stayed at the 414 hotel for 5 nights in January and it was lovely! The hotel is very cosy and warm and our twin room was nice and spacious with really comfortable beds. The ensuite bathroom was also large and clean with a large mirror and they changed our towels every day. There was also a large mirror in the room, along with an ironing board, safe, TV etc. We had to ask for a hairdryer but they provided one with no questions asked. 
The hotel is in a great location, 2 blocks from Time square and just off restaurant row where it was easy to jump in a cab to go up or downtown. The subway at time square is pretty close too! The hotel also provided a nice breakfast of coffee, juice, bagels, croissants etc which was lovely and there were also some great diners to go for breakfast close by as well as some great restaurants. Becco was our favourite. 
The staff were all really friendly especially the owner and Jessica and made us feel very welcome!
We loved New York and would defintely go back to the 414 - its not luxury but its all you need and great if you are on a budget! 
PS Top of the rock at the rockafeller centre is amazing and in our opinion better views than the empire state building!

title: “Great location, but could use some slight improvements”
text:
I usually stay at another Hilton property while in Chicago, but The Drake came as a recommendation from a friend. The location is wonderful and the view from my room spectacular (see photo). It has a lot of charm and the service is great. I worked with two concierge personnel who were knowledgeable, accommodating and very cheerful. The housekeeping staff was great.
My only criticism would be two minor incidences and one major faux paz: 1) our waiter at the COQ d'OR - when asked about a wine selection, he had no idea, 2) while the business center offers shipping for FedEx and UPS accounts (I have an account with UPS), there are no UPS supplies and it was slightly painful to get UPS to retrieve my package (why offer the service, if you can't deliver) and 3) the major faux paz - our breakfast at the Drake Bros' was good once we got it. We felt like we were putting the wait staff out with ordering milk with our tea and asking for basic necessities. Then when our waiter took our order, he was a bit overwhelmed and didn't take good notes. Everyone's order was completely wrong. The manager had to retake our order. Once it came out, it was good. When it was time for the bill the waiter said "my boss took care of it, thanks." Instead, he should have apologized at the very least - he basically was turning his back when he told us the bill was taken care of.
It is a very charming hotel, but does have some basic service drawbacks.

title: “Great room, confortable”
text: Confortable and huge room, great room service. Definitely worth the price. At breakfast, try continental - great option for foreign people who want to enjoy fresh SF food. And great location - near Embarcadero and China Town.

title: “the most beautiful hotel we have ever stayed at!”
text: Hotel is beautiful, clean with very relaxing atmosphere! Staff was very polite and would go out of their way to help us out. Location was perfect as trasportation, shopping, eatting is all within 5 minute walk.

title: “overall a very good deal”
text:
close to lax and not at all noisy. good rooms and service.
only criticism is they really need to get faster internet.

title: “Gorgeous boutique hotel!”
text: We got an incredible last-minute rate at the Indigo Hotel, but I'd definitely stay here on another occasion (even without the discount.) The hotel was impeccably clean, with a beautiful, modern look. The room was quite large and had a nice view of the downtown skyline. I only wish I'd had more time to enjoy the amenities!

title: “good for the money”
text: I stayed here with my parents several times as a child and decided to try it as an adult with my husband. We stayed for 3 nights. I liked the size of the room and the the bedroom is completely seperate. The pool area is nice but we didn't use it because there were a ton of kids around. Breakfast and cocktail hour were very busy but worth it since it's free (breakfast is good for a free hotel breakfast-pancakes or omletes and bacon or sausage). Our room was very clean and comfortable. The bathroom was spacious with a nice tub. We got a good rate of $109 a night. I would stay here again but probably not during the summer. it was mostly families with little kids and they were running around everywhere, riding the elevators, etc. I would recommend this place for a family or for couples during the week or during the school year. Our cab fare to downtown was about $20 or so one way so if you're looking for convenience to downtown, I would try and get a little closer. Bu there are several good restaurants close by.

title: “Four Seasons Hotel Chicago”
text: A five star review is earned. Not patronized. One or two stays may impress me. However, for me, what defines a five star review is a constant level of attentiveness and service. I stay at the Four Seasons Hotel Chicago several weeks a year on business and pleasure. The reason I keep coming back? I always feel at home when I visit. The personalization and presentation from the entire staff is superior. The Four Seasons Hotel Chicago is an absolute personal favorite. Pure excellence.

title: “Run from this hotel Braxton now the District Hotel”
text: Do yourself a favor and stay away from this hotel. I've had the same problem others have reported. Poor service and having to change rooms because of non-function heater. The heater would shut-off about every 2 hours and I was told to just unplug it for 15 min when it stops working. I was afraid to plug anything into the electric outlets out of fear of starting a fire.

title: “Neat little place to stay -- full of charm”
text:
We stayed here for a couple nights while in San Francisco. It was so convenient to so much, and far less expensive than places close to the wharf. Next door to museums, the opera, performing arts center, city hall, and more. Walk a few blocks and catch the cable car to the wharf and chinatown and such -- only $2. It's close to Hayes Valley area -- a must to visit for the outstanding food and shops. Stelline's is a very genuine small Italian restaurant with GREAT food and GREAT value. Also, the Boxing Room was super. Would eat at both of them again without pause. Too many places to list. And it's only two blocks away!
The Inn at the Opera was wonderful - small charming rooms, but with enough space to relax. It was a bit of stepping back in time, with a charming little elevator that somehow is never slow. Old time open staircase all the way to the 7th floor. Nice complimentary breakfast in the morning. Excellent, friendly, warm, and attentive staff. More than the usual amount of coffee available in the room, in a standard-size coffee maker. Frig. We will undoubtedly return.

title: “Brand new and clean : nice place to stay”
text:
This hotel is brand new and spotless and the staff were very friendly and helpful. Also, the hotel is in a fairly convenient location : less than 5 minutes walk from Gallaudet U Metro Stop and from the Greyhound terminal. It's also only a 15 minute walk to Union Station and relatively convenient to walk to downtown, if you are a good walker. A taxi ride here in the evening from just about anywhere is quite reasonable too. 
There's also a Harris Teeter Grocery and Pharmacy right next door + a microwave and bar fridge in the rooms so that can provide some cheap meal options.
That said, the immediate neighbourhood is obviously only recently being gentrified and so the streets are kinda deserted at night and there isn't much to do right nearby in terms of restaurants or shops. Another issue is the noise from the big nightclub across the street (only an issue on Friday and Saturday nights from 10pm to 2am). If you are planning to stay here on one of those nights and want to sleep before 2am then try to get a room away from the nightclub. In my case the staff were super helpful and moved me to a different room before the second week-end.

title: “Filthy”
text: I've since demoted my friend from booking hotels. Hotel Pennsylvania was TERRIBLE. The lobby looks great. I walked off the elevator onto the second floor and I immediately noticed the poor bldg. management. The carpet was visibly dirty, there was spackle all over the walls, the doors were filthy, I could go on. Upon entering the room, more filth. The shower curtain had old toothpaste on it from a previous guest, the walls were dirty, the furniture in the room looked like the original furniture from centuries ago. The bathroom as a whole was dirty; there was rust around the toilet on the floor, the windows did not have a screen, no fan in the bathroom. It was horrible. The room was big and spacious however. I wouldn't recommend anyone booking this hotel. It's super expensive (probably due to the location) and it's not worth the price. If you do not care about cleanliness and cost, you might be ok staying there. If you do choose to book a room there and have to request a roll in bed, DON'T. Lindy's (a restaurant) is connected to the hotel and it's super expensive. The Statler Grill is also connected and the service there was horrible. Aside from it being in a great location right across from Penn Station, the hotel is in major need of updating. The 7th floor looked better than the 2nd but I do not know about the room condition. The basement is in shambles and I suspect there is asbestos in that place. It's something you have to see to believe. We spoke to people upon the end of our stay and they knew the poor condition of this hotel. Run, don't walk away from this place.

title: “Would definitely stay here again!”
text:
Stayed here last week on Business for 5 nights. Was very impressed with my stay at this hotel. The room was large, lovely bed. The only downside was the lighting in the room, but I find this the same problem with most hotels. 
The staff were friendly and helpful. Great lobby bar and breakfast was excellent.
The location is also good, easy walking distance to a lot of different sights in Boston. Great Indian restaurant (Tantric) across the road...we ate their twice!
I would definitely stay here again if I was in Boston.

title: “Not sure why one would choose to stay here...”
text: With so many hotel choices, I'm not sure why one would choose to stay here. A family member booked our stay otherwise I would not have. The rooms are very dark and dated so they don't feel very clean which is a big deal to me And the only reason I would not go back. The staff was nice, the pool was big (though the pool towels were tiny and scratchy), the grounds we grassy and well maintained and the hot breakfast included was a hit. I just really did not like the old look ad feel of the rooms.

title: “Ok hotel, needs better housecleaning”
text:
