Check-in was quick and guy on the desk was friendly. They only had room on the 3rd floor available when I was checking in at 6 pm but they said they´d have higher floor available if I would wait for 45 mins. I agreed and got a drink coupon for the hotel bar. That was a nice gesture.
My room with twin bed was on 27th floor. Room was actually quite spacious, and has two windows with lot of light. Bathroom was very small but adequate. AC worked fine. Room was a little rundown with paint chipping etc. but I didn´t come to New York to spend time in the hotel room so I didn´t care.
Fitness center was a nice surprise. I expected couple of treadmills and some weights, but there´s 5 treadmills, crosstrainer, bike and enough equipment to do a whole workout. 
Although I had a nice stay at the hotel, I feel they could really do better on cleaning and housekeeping. Room looked clean at first, clean sheets and towels etc. But when you look closer you can see it needs a thorough cleaning. There´s quite a lot of dust and during my 6 nights stay I don´t think the bathroom floor was cleaned even once. 
There was some noice from the elevators and from the street but not disturbing as I wore earplugs during the nights. Housekeeping seemed to do a lot of cleaning in the evening, lots of vacuuming going on 10 pm which I found a bit odd.
Location of the hotel is ok, it´s a nice area with a lot of other hotels and places to snack and eat. Closest subway is 3 blocks from the hotel. Although the subway is close I did find it a little bit unconvenient going to the west side of downtown, always taking 3 different subways.
Overall the hotel was good and with the right price I can recommend it.

title: “An okay place to stay.....”
text:
I came here with my family to explore Memphis for a week and see what the city had to offer. Upon arriving to my room, the room hadn't been clean (if it had, someone must've came back in and went to sleep) and there was a dirty sock on the floor and hair all in the bathroom. The cleaning crew cleaned it up quickly, but the hair problem was never solved. Other than the initial issues, the room was clean and sufficient. The bed on the other had was hard as a board and felt nothing like the usual Marriott beds. I stayed in a room with a view of the bridge and the river which was nice. There was not any noise issues even with the trolley running all day. 
The staff at this location is just average. They don't do anything terribly bad, but they don't do anything exceptional either. It seems like they are afraid to speak and will duck away before trying to make eye contact. 
The location of this hotel is great. They have a restaurant across the street called Allanahs and a market right beside there. There is a restaurant called Local and the food there is great. 
Overall, this hotel is just okay. It's a place to stay in a great location for a reasonable price.

title: “Decent Hotel”
text: Location was really good, Lobby was welcoming, rooms were dated, and a bit natty. Excellent bathroom. I had a junior suite with plenty of room to move around though the decore left much to be desired .. think grandma's house. My room had a great view of down town with a balcony however that more than made up for the inside decoration. Staff were wonderful .. room service was over the top expensive. and the gift shop hours were a bit off. All in all a decent stay.. and value for the price for sure. Just don't order breakfast as 47.00 for bacon and eggs was really over the top.

title: “Ticks all the boxes!”
text:
We got a very good deal on four nights at the Courtyard and we couldn’t really fault it. 
The positives: 
The staff really stood out for us. They were exceptionally knowledgeable, friendly and helpful. Checking in and out was a complete breeze (no more than 5 minutes total). We were considering taking public transport back to the airport which the front desk advised against (we had large bags and it was very hot for October) instead they were able to book a town car for $65 (inc tolls) which turned out to be money well spent. 
The location: you are right in the heart of SoHo and are no more than a 10-20 minute walk away from Chelsea, Greenwich and Chinatown. We actually walked downtown one day (this took about 40 mins). If walking is not your thing, the subway line no. 1 (Houston Station) is literally a stone’s throw away and this will take you both downtown or uptown in only few stops. 
The rooms: the hotel is relatively new so the furniture and finishes are modern and fresh. We had a king size room on the 8th floor and the bed was one of the most comfortable beds I have ever slept on. The room has a flatscreen tv with loads of channels, ipod doc, free wifi, coffee/tea maker, desk area and a mini fridge. 
The lobby: there are a couple of PCs in the lobby area for using the internet, as well as a couple of PCs especially allocated for printing off boarding passes so you don’t have to bug reception. There are also big sofa areas for waiting around, a bar and a small ‘market’ where you can buy snacks for the day ahead. You can also order hot snacks from the bar. 
The negatives: 
I can’t stress how minor these are but annoying nonetheless.
Our room was on the 8th floor but you can still hear street noise (this might be a problem on the lower floors so take earplugs if you are a light sleeper). 
We bought a couple of beers in the downstairs bar that were $9 each! I had to sit down when I heard how much they cost but this seems to be standard for hotels - there is a supermarket not too far away where you can buy six for $9 so do that instead (there is a pizzeria across the road too). 
The aircon in our room was so loud that we couldn’t sleep comfortably through it so we just left it on full before we went to bed and then shut it off. 
The water pressure in the shower wasn’t great, again, very minor and not serious as the shower was huge and clean! 
All in all, we had a fabulous trip and wouldn't hesitate to stay here again! Thanks again to the fantastic staff who made our stay stress-free.

title: “Served its purpose”
text: We were going to San Francisco on the Amtrak via Union Station. Since our train was leaving early in the morning we wanted to stay down in LA overnite. The Dragon Gate Inn served its purpose. It was close to Union Station, it was relatively clean and the staff was nice. The parking lot attendant on duty the day we were there was a gem, he parked our car for us and was very helpful with information we needed. I would stay here again if we were leaving out of Union Station.

title: “A wonderful hotel in the middle of the city.”
text: We stayed at the Mayflower with our 11-year-old grandson. The rooms are clean, comfortable, and the price is great. The location is perfect for walking to almost everyplace in the city. Buses are convenient to the location too. The staff is fabulous. Our grandson left his new wireless mouse there. I called, they found it and are mailing it back to us. That is fantastic service. I'll stay there on every trip.

title: “Great Place to Stay!”
text: The hotel has a great location. Walking distances to the Central Park, Broadway, restaurants. The concierge´s services were VERY helpful for restaurant´s reservations (they got us a table on Babbo´s for Mother´s Day evening, in a very short notice from us!). We looked at the reviews for this hotel before booking in, and most peaple complain about the elevators (slow). We didn´t think they were so slow and it didn´t bother us at all. We will definetly come back!

title: “Great Stay...no matter what anyone else said”
text:
The Millennium UN Plaza is located on the East side of Midtown. It is roughly 1 block from the United Nations. When you first arrive at this hotel, you must have your bags checked at the door by security. This is standard. From here you enter the beautiful lobby. The lobby is adorned with reflective glass and lighting. With it being the holiday season, there was a beautiful Christmas tree in the center. Once checked in, we made our way to the 38th floor and our room. The room was small but not bad for NYC standards. Since there were 3 of us, we had an extra cot brought in and still had plenty of room to move around. The room itself seemed to have a modern Asian flair. It had a closet for hanging our clothing and storing our luggage. It also had a spacious bathroom and shower. The only complaint about the shower would be that the showerhead could have been a few inches higher. 
The view from the panoramic windows were breath taking. We had a view of the Queensburo bridge and of the old Pepsi Co. sign--which can be seen best at night. 
The staff at the hotel was great. The concierge, Shawn, was awesome. He was a great help in setting up our car service to the airport. The doormen, Edward and Robert, were knowledgeable and helpful. And the front desk accommodated any request we made. Overall, I would highly recommend this hotel.

title: “Comfortable and calm stay”
text:
As expected from Hilton, this is a nice property. My stay was very comfortable. Rooms were very good, hotel staff were helping. Location was very convenient.
Pool was small though.

title: “Not bad, but:”
text:
It's rather dated. The room I was in on the 12th floor was a bit ratty in details: paint, caulk in bathroom, wastebaskets, tv and remote. The all needed replacement. Little things, but added up, they gave the room a slightly squalid feel.The room was also somewhat noisy, but I found it helpful to stuff a towel at the bottom of the door to reduse noise floating up through the atrium.
The good: great location, the staff was helpful, the bed comfy. Walking out the back of the hotel right onto the Lady Bird trail was wonderful!

title: “Nice Stop Over, But A Few Issues”
text:
The last time I'd visited this hotel, it was old and dated. Imagine my surprise when I saw that it had been entirely renovated into a very engaging modern style. 
I was using points and upgraded to the Executive Level, however, after 3 failed attempts to get up to the 10th floor, my husband and I had to engage one of the desk managers who attempted to blame the issue on us. Once finally arriving at the 10th floor, a fantastic woman named Babbette explained to the manager what he, and all the other desk attendants, were doing wrong. 40 minutes after arriving, we finally got to the room.
Despite this hiccup, our stay was lovely. The room and bed were comfortable, the shower pressure was fantastic, and the food and drinks were very nice. Never got the internet to work, but that wasn't a particular hindrance, and ended up saving us $13. The desk chair was awkward, though, and tipped back too far to really be of any use. I had to sit there for 4 hours doing work, and my back really paid the price.
Overall, I did enjoy my stay, and would stay again in order to give the place another shot. I have high hopes for Hilton, and unfortunately, a few too many unfortunate things happened at the same time.

title: “Great experience, great accomodattions & great location.”
text: I went to L.A. for the first time in Nov. 05, 2008 to see Madonna in the Dodger Stadium. We picked this Hotel because it looked nice on the Holiday Inn website, and becuase I read the reviews here and everyone was talking about the location were it was. I was not dissapointed at all, we picked the "2 QUEEN BED, NONSMOKING". The staff was educated and helped with every thing that I needed, specially Anthony (front desk). The rooms were always kept clean, no funky smells, the hotel smelled clean, like a new hotel. The room service always was on time and left us clean towels every day on the bathroom, the bed were so comfortable. The early brekfast, (I thin it was from 6AM to 9AM) saves you allot of money, just the basics, but it gives you a kick start in the day. And the best of all, was the location, is really near the Hollywood & Highland were there is a train station, allot of bus stops, Hooters, H&M, Urban Outfitters, Gap, Virgin Megastore, The Chinese Theatre, Kodak Theatre and in the Hollywood and Highland there are allot of stores and placest to eat. If I go back to Hollywood, I would go back to the Holiday Inn Express, you save allot because is not an expensive hotel, and because overall, it was a comfortable experience.

title: “Great for Wings or Tigers Game!”
text:
Stayed recently for a Wings playoff game, it was easy to find and the valet parking went well. Check in was very smooth and efficient. Our room was on the 8th floor and looked out towards the GM headquarters and the river. The room was clean but a bit dated in terms of carpets and drapery. We stayed at the Doubletree the week before for about $30 more and really enjoyed their suite.
We had payed for breakfast as part of the package and it was really excellent. There is a cook there to make you eggs to order, omelets or waffles. Plus, a nice buffet of bacon, fresh fruit etc. 
The front desk was very accomdating - when we checked out the stored our bags for us as we headed to the game. They could not have been nicer about this. Speaking of the game, the People Mover stops right inside the hotel; really convenient! Worked perfectly for us ~ as an aside, while on the People Mover the night before the game, a gentleman spoke with us who is a lifelong Detroiter. We did not know just how to find the restaurant we were looking for but he knew right where it was and walked us to it. He was as kind and polite as could be.

title: “Friendly staff and very modern Hotel”
text: We have just returned from a 3 night stay at the Conrad, Indianapolis and overall this is a lovely modern hotel with friendly staff. We picked the rate which included Continental breakfast which was very good value. The rooms were clean and nicely decorated and the bathroom was excellent. Even had a TV in it. We ate at the Capital Grille in the Hotel. The food was good if not a bit overpriced but we found the waiter a bit standoffish. Perhaps it was because we had a 6 year old with us and this is mainly a business hotel. The hotel has access to the shopping Mall via an indoor skywalk which was a great plus as it rained on our first day. This is a lovely hotel but be careful when parking your car. When we asked for our car on our departure morning we were told we needed a new battery as the car would not start. There has never been a problem with the battery in this car. The staff said they tried jump leads but could not get the car going and they could organise a new battery. I was not sure whether this was genuine or they were looking to make a fast buck. Turned out they had left the lights on overnight and this drained the batterry. The car was restarted after my sister went to check out the car and the valet eventually got a car with a bigger house power to connect the jump leads too. As we were rushing to make an appointment this delayed us and we ended up being late for the appointment.

title: “Great location, great price”
text: Great central hotel, great price. We booked online and got the parking package, stayed in room 1230 and had the window ajar the whole time we stayed. No noisy nights meant a great night sleep. Used the hotels recommended parking garage, very easy to get to and from. Safe central location, clean room, comfortable bed, quiet peaceful sleep..what else do you need?

title: “Not as bad as they say................................................”
text:
Greetings Fellow Travelers!
I just came back from a weekened shopping trip to NYC and chose to stay at the Carter because I wanted to stay in a central area (Times Square) and most importantly... I had a budget of $150.00 per night including tax for my hotel stay. The Carter Hotel fit the bill. I went to their website and found that it was $10.00 cheaper a night then when I had phoned them earlier. I paid $105.00 a night including tax. this meant more money for shopping YEAH!
Here are the Pros: Big bed that was strangely one of the most comfortable beds i have slept on. Strong Powerful water in the shower. Air Conditioning was good for the heat wave that went through the city. Amazing view from the 21st floor.
Concierge was very knowlegable and helped me map out my shopping trip, and also gave me some great coupons to macys and bloomingdales.
Here are the cons: There was no hair dryer in the room and when I went down to the lobby and asked for one.. i had to be put on a waiting list. they called me while i was asleep at 11:00 pm and told me to pick up the hair dryer in the lobby or it would go to another guest! 
overall assesment: If you want to stay in a good location and do not have much money to spend and you dont need amenities in the room such as a hair dryer, coffee maker, or iron, then the hotel carter is a great choice. and if the negative reviews are true, then trust me they are taking your advice and they are showing some improvement. they now have Card Keys instead of Metal Keys, and they have marble bathrooms, instead of old tiles. oh, and the elevators are pretty fast and modernized. i did not have to wait a long time to get to and from my 21st floor room.
If you want to stay in a good location and have some extra money to burn, or better yet, an expense account stay elsewhere. but dont forget that you get what you pay for. 
I wish you great travels!!

title: “the best hotel in the world!!”
text:
i stayed at the st. regis in New york in October 2011.
it was by far the best hotel i have ever stayed at! checking in at this landmark of NYC, escorted by the butler to your suite and enjoy a a complimentary coffee upon arrival ..is spoiling.
the bar is a must (thats where the bloody mary was invented), restaurant is simply amazing and what is there to say for the best concierge in the city!! restaurant, theatre , broadway, museum tickets was never a problem for those guys!

title: “Wish we could have stayed longer”
text:
We stayed at this hotel for two nights. This is very much a conference hotel, but we found it was fine for tourists as well. 
The Frank Lloyd Wright inspired cast block lobby and buildings are very formal and monolithic compared to some places we've stayed, and the interior spaces are a little darker than some hotels. But it's comfortable and relaxing.
We found the staff here to be friendly.
The gardens, fountains, pools and landscaping are georgous. The hotel terrace in the late afternoon has a fabulous view of the mountains and is a marvelous place to sink into the comfy rattan chairs and have a drink - they light the fire pits when it gets cool out. The prices are a bit on the high side but the ambience is worth it.
We ate breakfast and dinner at the Grill. The food was delicious, atmosphere pleasant, and there wasn't a wait to sit down. The wait staff was great - well trained, knowledgeable, polite, friendly, attentive but not intrusive.
This was our first stay and they upgraded us to a room with a private balcony and a mountain view - nice! It had rained a few days prior and the balcony was filled with water. We considered asking for another room, but we liked the room so we decided to call the front desk to ask if someone could just squeegee the water. We went to get our luggage and by the time we returned, the water was gone. Someone came by a little later to give it a second sweep to make sure it was done to our satisfaction. We were very impressed with the speed with which this request was handled.
The rooms are large, the furniture is big and heavy (craftsman style oak). The plant in the room was a nice touch. The bathroom was huge w/great shower and toiletries, plenty of towels, two sinks, separate area for the commode, make-up counter with a chair, and closet with full height mirror. 
The only complaint about the room is that the closet for the room is inside the bathroom. 
There are plenty of outlets in the room to charge your electronics (phone, camera, etc.) We liked that they not only have glasses in the bathroom but wine glasses and tall glasses.
We liked this hotel so much that we considered canceling our next hotel so we could stay here an extra day or two.

title: “Beware!! Worst stay EVER, Charged 3 times for a prepaid stay!”
text:
An absolute NIGHTMARE!
Prepaid for 3 nights booked through AOL America Online Travel Services using travelocity. The hotel and travelocity have NO communication network. The hotel failed to resolve the issue, inept staff and manager. Hotel charged $546.58 dollars for a 3 night stay AFTER I had already PREPAID $321.52 to AOL/Travelocity 3 weeks in advance. Hotel blames travelocity, travelocity blames hotel, hotel blames customer, customer gets a bunch of headaches and triple billed for stay. Keep your money and your sanity.....book and stay elswhere.

title: “Must suck to be me”
text: Elevator was dirty and smelled - the bed had cigarette holes or moth holes in the blankets. The Real BIG Surprise was @ 5 a.m. when I went to take a shower, there was NO shower head and what was there had absolutely no pressure. Now wherever I travel, that is the 1st thing I look for, so there are no early morning surprises. I called 3 wks ahead & was guaranteed ground floor near parking lot - when I arrived, I got 2nd floor at the street - front desk said take it or leave it - an overall horrible experience!

title: “BORING,DEPRESSING AND CONFUSING”
text: Well, to start upon checking in i was told i did not have a reservation, but i had a confirmation # . They asked for my I.D.which i gave the clerk in a hawaiian shirt and shorts (NO UNIFORMS?) and he told me my room was already paid for but I knew it was not. He then tells me Erica right? with my i.d. in hand without even looking at my i.d.... UH, DUH? Turned out they had given my room to someone else without verifying names. NOT GOOD NOR PROFESSIONAL. Took 30 minutes to finally get in my room, but was not pleased with the room either. Their pictures on line show very luxurious and peaceful rooms but were not. They were hot and smelly, the shower still had soap scum and used soap on the ledge, hair in the sink, no pillow cases on two of the pillows, which i refused to use. Called the front desk and they told me me they had no more extra pillows or blankets. So tired i didn't care. Thought i would wake up for a somewhat continental breakfast but not even, very sad food. Coffee was warm and all they had was powder cream? WTF? you need a good cup of coffee in the morning, the orange juice was warm and the bread(WHICH IS ALL THEY HAD)was hard and did not look fresh. still had to go but breakfast outside even after after all the money i paid. Regardless of everything i would not ever stay here again, unless it's for free. They have a lot of work to do if they want to be considered how they advertise themselves. To me it is false advertising...NEVER AGAIN.

title: “Everything was great!”
text:
We almost did not book this hotel because of some negative reviews. We are glad we did and we are thinking of coming back soon. 
The location is very nice: right on the water, in a quiet area. We had a room with view of the water and could have spent the whole day inside by the window! The neighbourhood is very pretty. We had trouble finding the hotel, as the GPS did not recognize the "Battery Wharf" address. We phoned the hotel and got instructions.
The room is beautiful, with a comfortable bed, large washroom with toilet and rain shower each with its own door.
Service was prompt and helpful, not at all intrusive. Breakfast was delicious!
Thank you for a wonderful stay!

title: “Opera -and A Bed and Breakfast”
text:
This hotel is sooo very close to the Opera House.
You can catch a cab to anywhere-they are always going by.
There are plenty of places to eat that are with in walking distance - with many being local. Delish!
The breakfast that comes with your stay here is good.
At breakfast we met others who had attended the Opera...then who should appear for breakfast but the director of the opera.
It was fun to hear the director's take of how the opera was interpreted....a bonus.
There is parking! Off street! 
Security.
An elevator- which we used.
Help with your luggage -if needed.
TV in the rooms.
 We asked for 2 double beds ... they have rooms with 2 doubles.
This place is MUCH larger than expected.
And we drove to the airport in 15 minutes.

title: “This could work well for some people...”
text:
I'm torn on this one, since there were definite pluses and minuses here.
On the good side: the location is excellent, the price is reasonable, the room is huge, the room contains a full kitchen (and with Trader Joe's nearby, this was a real money saver), the towels are big and fluffy, the staff is friendly, and housekeeping does their best to keep the place clean.
On the bad side: I say housekeeping "does their best to keep the place clean," because there comes a time when a place is so worn that it is grotty, not matter how hard it is scrubbed and vacuumed. One Washington Circle is old and under-renovated. I can put up with some wear and tear, but the rug was badly worn and stained (though vacuumed well), the curtain was torn, the desk chair arms were worn through to the foam beneath, the bed was sagging and uncomfortable, and the bedding was pretty gross (ripped/safety-pinned duvet cover, ancient/pill-covered blanket, etc.). Since the primary purpose of a hotel room is to provide a place to sleep, I draw the line at a gross bed.
So this place could work well for some - people who don't mind a youth hostel kind of wear and tear, and especially people who want to self-cater in an expensive city. I've reached a point in my life where I'm no longer willing to put up with grottiness, so next time I'll pay more for less space, sleep comfortably, and make do with takeout food!

title: “It was a great hotel!!!”
text: My Fiance and I stayed at the Heartbreak Hotel, and LOVED IT!!! I am a huge Elvis fan, and I must say that this was THE hotel to stay at if you're going to check out Graceland. THey have a television channel with only ELVIS MOVIES!!!! They play his music in the lobby, and outside of the building as well.

title: “pleasant surprise”
text:
i had to fly to seattle last minute for an emergency and stayed at the alexis because it was the only place that had availability. i was pleasantly surprised with how nice it was.
the hotel bar is so cute and very seattle - it looks like an old library and has all sorts of hipster-y cocktails on the menu.
my room the first night was quite small, but for my second through fourth nights i got upgraded to an enormous suite. the room was great overall, although the bathroom seemed a little outdated with one of those showers that bizarrely soaks the entire room even though the curtain seems to be tightly closed. there was a little TV nook near the hotel room door instead of having a TV across from the bed, which was a little weird, but it was kind of fun to hang out and watch a movie in the "movie room" as my husband referred to it.
no late night room service, and the front desk only had one pizza place menu, which at first seemed quite lame, except that the pizza was actually superb, so maybe they knew that and threw away all of the other menus on purpose!
my one serious complaint with this hotel is that there are homeless people hanging out right at the hotel entrance. not just one person - literally every time i exited or entered there was someone panhandling or sleeping. this was awkward insofar as the alexis operates its valet parking at that entrance, and i felt uneasy about parking my car in front of a bunch of homeless people and just leaving my keys there while the valet people dealt with someone else. i live in NYC, so i see homeless people everyday and i am not just being a snob. i just think that for the standard of hotel that the alexis claims to be, security and management should try to keep the hotel looking as nice as possible and making sure that their guests feel safe when coming and going. otherwise, the surrounding neighborhood is pretty cool - just make sure you take a left when exiting - to the left are cute shops and great gelato (don't remember the name of the gelato place but it is about 3 blocks away) and to the right is a quizno's, a creepy drugstore and not much else (other than more homeless people).

title: “Decent convention hotel, nothing special”
text:
I stayed at this hotel for a three day conference this past May. The location is also very good, right on the Embarcadero, adjacent to Petco Park, the Convention Center, and the Gaslamp Quarter. Be aware that there is a lot of construction in the area as of my review, so there is no real direct route to the Gaslamp Quarter and Petco park even though they are across the street. I saw a walkway being constructed, but as of now, it would entail walking a couple of crosswalks and a walk across the railroad tracks. 
The hotel itself is incredibly modern and stylish, with a design more akin to the "W" chain than run-of-the-mill Hiltons. The lobby is bright and airy, decorated with bold colors and modern furniture. The rooms are also of similar aesthetics, with comfortable modern furniture and sleek design. The rooms are sizeable enough, but I was disappointed to find that my room only had a shower, and no bath. At first I thought it was may have been an accessible room assignment, but noticed to grab bars in the bathroom.
The hallways on the room floors, however, showed for any lack of design. Where one would expect to see simple prints or plants spread about to decorate the long corridors, there was no added decor in sight. This gave the interiors the feeling of a Holiday Inn.
Service was friendly, but spotty at times. Upon check-in I was assigned a room that was already occupied. Although this was easily resolved, I'm sure this was an unpleasant experience for the guest whose room I tried to enter. Likewise, housekeeping was spotty, as one day I noticed that although the bathroom had been tidied, the toilet bowl was not cleaned.
And like most hotel chains, and as others had complained previously, there are "nickel-and-dime" charges everywhere - $13.95 for internet, $21 daily for self parking, fees for fitness center use. I can understand the need to generate revenue, but these types of things would not garner customer loyalty in my opinion.
Overall the stay was pleasant but not extraordinary. The design of the hotel appears that Hilton is trying to appeal to a more upscale clientele, but upon closer inspection, it still is a basic Hilton. Time will tell whether the design will age well or if the hotel will need a major overhaul in the next three years.

title: “Functional and Pretty”
text:
I booked our room months in advanced and got a mid-week rate of $149. Location, it is 5 minutes from the Metro and adjacent restaurants and shops. A starbuck's is on the corner as well as a few bars. 
As a Kimpton Hotel, a premium has been placed on design, but this tries just a little too hard. The bathroom is excellent, but the purple throw--maybe not. Room sizes are large, especially the double queens, but check room location and size. You can imagine that this was a 1950's-60s hotel in a former life. If you want light, push for a front king double on the high floors give you floor to ceiling windows. You will have a great view of P Street and and great light--if you plan to stay in your room. Note that this hotel has weddings and attracts "romantic weekend" baby-boomers that enjoy the 5-6pm complimentary wine bar. 
If you run outdoors, the hotel is adjacent to the Rock Creek Parkway. Two evenings, I ran from the Hotel, past the Watergate Hotel, Kennedy Center and Lincoln Memorial--quite thrilling. The on-site gym is well equipped.

title: “Adequate”
text: Outdated, small rooms, but clean, convenient and quiet. If you just need a place to sleep, this hotel is fine.

title: “I loved the Hotel Tomo!”
text:
I stayed at the Hotel Tomo in October 2009. The location was great - just a short walk to Fillmore street and shops and restaurants. 
The decor is fun- Japanese pop art meets Ikea. This was probably the cleanest hotel I have ever stayed in. The murals on the walls are awesome. The beds and pillows are super comfortable. 
The front desk staff were very helpful. I would definitely stay there again.

title: “Just okay”
text: This is an old hotel, and it is not near a beach, unlike the information given by Hilton. It is on top of a parking garage and the lobby is on the 11th floor or something. The rooms are really small. The beds are old, the breakfast is okay, but expensive. Hilton rates this a Level 5 hotel, and we had a talk with them about it. They say it is so rated due to the location. I say atmost, this is a Level 3 hotel.

title: “GREAT SERVICE !!!”
text:
Wow, I had a great experience in ths hotel, It is wonderful.
People at front desk were very professional, efficient and friendly.
Charlie at the coffe station, Outstanding !!!
Our room was great and clean. The location just perfect!
Everything was great !
Thank you

title: “The hotel Nice for a weekend stay”
text: The hotel overall was nice. The lobby was small but the front desk was very helpful when it came to checking in and out. They even let us keep our suitcases there until we left for the airport. A few things i didn't like were the small rooms, shower and the wait for the elevator. It seemed like we waited for 10 mins before it got to our floor which was the 11th. I also requested a queen bed but since i checked in a little early i got stuck with a double. So it was a little uncomfortable sleeping wise but nothing to complain about. I went with my boyfriend and had a amazing time, it was walking distance to everywhere, we went to the Top of the Rock which was amazing also. I would recommend this hotel only for a weekend stay though. I can't wait to come back!

title: “Excellent hotel excellent location”
text: This was our first visit to Chicago. The staff, to a person, was most friendly & courteous. Everyone went out of their way to answer questions, give directions, etc. Stephanie of Guest Services helped us with tour reservations & recommended local restaurants for Chicago cuisine, like deep-dish pizza & hot dogs!! We had a room on the 15th floor & it was very quiet. Everything we wanted to see was easily accessible via the EL, bus or on foot. I would definitely stay here again if the opportunity arose. Thank you.

title: “A good choice for Fishermans Wharf”
text:
This hotel is very well located - just around the corner from Fishernans Wharf. 
The breakfast being included in the price is a bonus - it is a bit of a bun fight but the food was fine and plentiful - cereals, yoghurt, toast, muffins etc, cinnamon buns, bananas as well as some hot options - scrambled eggs, sausages/bacon.
Also you get the bonus of being able to use the pool next door at the main Holiday Inn Fishermans Wharf. The laundry also is over there.
Our room had no outlook at all - just a window into an internal lightwell, but it was comfortable and quiet.
There is a Denny's on site and Internet access terminals in the foyer.
Basically everything we needed was there.

title: “you must be kidding”
text: The room was very very very very small and nothing like the photos on line. Two people could not be standing up at the same time getting dressed. It's like a big closet. A bit run down looking. Housekeeping carts were ALWAYS in the hallway, blocking the narrow hallways. Cleaning woman tried to open my door at 8:30 am on a sunday morning without knocking and I was still in bed sleeping. She was rude and her only explanation was that she was looking for vacant rooms. After I got dressed, the same woman was in the hallway complaining about having to work there. The manager is named Steve and was polite but no real help. Location is good. Price is way TOO HIGH for that kind of abuse. Lots of noise in the hallways. Don't go there. Not worth it.

title: “Cheap, Close and Clean”
text: My fiance and I stayed here recently based solely on it's location (within a mile of where we were visiting for a friend's birthday party). I was surprised at how clean it was. Clearly it has recently been renovated and the staff were very nice. The parking out front is very limited but I think there's a larger lot out back. Lots of families with small kids were taking advantage of the free pastries and juice in the morning. It's not in the part of The Valley or LA that you would call touristy or even remotely interesting but it was perfect for what we needed.

title: “Stayed in a single, left with company: bedbugs!”
text: I stayed at Pod hotel for a weekend workshop in the city and came home with bedbugs! I had to have the entire house exterminated - how awful.

title: “The W San Diego is Fantastic”
text: Love the W in SanDiego ... I had a very quick stay but the staff was fantastic from check in, where I recieved great service from the lovely Melissa Humble ... rooms were very cool and comfortable ... the lobby and common areas are welcoming -- was an oasis of calm in an otherwise frenetic trip

title: “disappointing return visit”
text:
i stayed at this hotel about 14 years ago and at the time it was a refreshing change from the typical new york hotel of the era. having read that its overhaul was to be completed in september i thought i'd give it a try again. no big changes really , new furnishings but a similar feel. but now 14 years later it seems more typical and run of the mill new york and so you just notice how small the rooms are and how uncomfortably dark the overall ambience is. 
the beds are very nice but thats about all i can think of that i liked.
its a shame that asia de cuba the restaurant , didn't get a make over, the food is mediocre at best and during the cold hard light of breakfast it's dirty, beat up and tired looking. 
over all , a disappointing stay at a hotel that used to be reasonably priced, funky and fun, but is now expensive and dull.

title: “Fantastic hotel in a great location”
text:
I stayed at the Affinia Dumont for 5 nights over Thanksgiving with 2 friends. The rooms are spacious and the kitchen is really handy for having breakfast in your room. There is a convenience store on the corner next to the Hotel. We were on the 30th floor and had a great view down town. The staff were all very knowledgeable and only too happy to help. 
The hotel is in a great location. Only 1 block from a subway station, loads of cafe's and restaurants near by. Loads of attractions within walking distance. 
I would definitely stay here again!

title: “Super stylish hotel”
text: Wonderful room, attentive staff and perfect location, stayed for two nights, hope to return one day....

title: “Not bad”
text:
Courtyard (by Marriott) is located just north of the Moscone convention centre. It is still a distance to walk compared to other hotels such as Intercontinental, Marriott and W Hotel.
It is near to the financial district but further to Union Square compared to many other hotels but it is within walking distance to Market Street where you can take streetcars, trains, buses etc. It is possible to walk to Union Square and chinatown though.
The hotel is near offices and it is quiet unlike hotels near union square where you can hear cable cars and sirens etc. 
The rooms are simple. You don't get a fridge but they do have a nice flat screen TV. Internet is part of the room rate (at least for me, which is good for business travellers)
I was staying at the Hotel Nikko. I thought it was cheaper and clearly better. Having said that, Courtyard by all means is a decent hotel too.
The beds are comfortable with good pillows.
I didnt try any restaurants in the hotel. So cannot comment on the food.
Front desk provides prompt and acceptable services.

title: “Best place in downtown Seattle”
text: I stay at the Mayflower Park Hotel every December when I go into downtown Seattle for a concert. It is an old, wonderful hotel in great condition. It is located right in the heart of the shopping area and you can go into Westlake Center for shopping and restaurants without going out side. From Westlake Center you can access Nordstroms, Pacific Place and Macy's all without going outside. The bar is the greatest atmosphere and the restaurant is also. Great service, friendly staff. Everything you can possibly want and more.

title: “Very dissappointed!”
text: We visited this hotel for the Indianapolis 500 weekend and spent $250 per night for our room. The first time we used the toilet paper holder, it fell apart. An easyfix with a small screw driver. Yet, despite 7 interactions with the staff and even a visit to their maintenance room to look for a screwdriver to fix it myself, it still has not been fixed as they did not have a screwdriver small enough and apparently are not willing to purchase one. The entire situation should have been quickly resolved. Their lack of attention to detail in getting this fixed is very unprofessional.

title: “Very nice”
text: I've only stayed at The Drake once, but I was very happy with the hotel. The hotel is older, and it has that feel. However, they have done a nice job of keeping it up. The room was an average sized room, and it was very comfortable. The bathroom was small, but it served my needs (it's a bathroom, after all). I stayed on the Executive Floor, and my room rate included a continental breakfast in the Executive Lounge. I was impressed with the breakfast. It included a variety of bagels/breads/cerals and also included lox with capers, hard boiled eggs, and a variety of fruit. The staff members were very friendly, and the location is excellent for any activity in that part of downtown. Finally, the price was very reasonable for downtown Chicago. I'll be happy to stay here again.

title: “Highly recommended”
text: I went to New York with my sister in mid august and stayed six nights at the Shelburne Murray Hill near Grand Central Station. When we arrived we were told that the room we had booked was not available. However the friendly staff swiftly offered us an upgrade to a deluxe suite with a kingsize bed instead two seperate beds. The room was located on the fifteenth floor with a great view of the skyline and the East River and plenty of space. The living room was huge. The kitchen had a minibar oven and fridge freezer and both the living room and the bedroom were equipped with flatscreen tv. The airconditioned suite was very tastefully decorated in a modern style and was clean throughout. Also the staff were extremely friendly during our entire stay. The main attraction of this hotel however is the huge rooftop terrace on the sixteenth floor which guest are free to use anytime. Until midnight there is also a bar which is open to the general public. From the rooftop you can enjoy panoramic views of the skyline including nearby Empire State Building and Chrysler Building. Absolutely stunning. I would not hesitate to recommend this hotel to first time visitors as well as seasoned travellers who are looking for a nice mid sized Manhattan hotel in a great location.

title: “It's been lovely since I was a little girl and hasn't changed!”
text:
Growing up in Jackson, Mississippi there were two choices for back to school shopping- New Orleans and Memphis (Jackson lies directly between the two cities). It was customary for my mother to take me to Memphis in the fall and New Orleans in the spring for shopping trips. We always stayed to the Peabody and indulged in mother/ daughter mani/ pedis, enjoyed brunch and enjoyed the ducks. 
Fast forward 20 years... I'm now married to a wonderful man and, as we were moving across the country (alas, one of the downfalls of being an army wife) I suggested we take a few extra days to explore Memphis and stay at the Peabody. It was precisely as I remembered it.- after all these years it is still an oasis of luxury nestled in downtown. It's nice to know some things never change...

title: “Very nice. Excellent value. Convenient location.”
text:
Our family of 4 stayed at the Residence Inn Central for 7 nights, and it was very nice, and we have no complaints at all. We booked a bi-level suite, with the fireplace. The beds were King and Queen. My children loved having their own upstairs bedroom with the queen bed, as well as their own bathroom. There was tons of storage everywhere, with lots of closets. We cooked a little one night. We even lit the fireplace one night and I baked cookies. 
The pool was heated, a little small, but was fine. We also liked the two jacuzzis. The breakfast was pretty good, and we liked the make your own waffle machine. We came back a few nights for the complimentary appetizers/manager dinner (Mon-Thurs only) and that was really nice. They have theme nights where one night, it could be deli, and the next can be BBQ, or italian. They also had free wine and beer, too. Awesome. 
The rooms were very clean, the beds were comfortable. We had 3 tvs which were awesome. The location was good - right off of the highway, and there were lots of restaurants nearby (driving distance). On Conway Street, we discovered some great Asian restaurants (Vietnamese, Korean) that our kids loved! We were about 10-15 minutes from SD ZOO, and 25 minutes from Legoland. The hotel provides preprinted cards with driving directions. So convenient!
The lobby has free newspapers, and a computer for guests to use to send an email, etc... And parking was free and plentiful. We felt very safe. We would definitely stay here again.

title: “Location location location”
text: Chicago 1st timer. Went for Chicago Marathon weekend. Spent 6 nights at the Avenue. Really enjoyed staying there. Wanted a high floor room. They gave me a high floor room. Room 3706 is just 3 floors from the top. Two-room suite with a pull out bed, a kinda walk-in closet and king bed. They brought a crib up for my toddler within minutes of asking for one. Concierge services were very helpful and knowledgeable of good local spots, not necessarily the trendy but the good. Bell service was courteous and efficient. Got us cabs quickly and arranged an early morning van cab for all our stuff when leaving for the airport. Really had no problems with the Avenue. Elephant & Castle Bar and Restaurant on the lobby works up a nice meal and has a great selection of beer by the bottle and on tap. Try the club sandwich. But best of all...the hotel is kinda tucked away just off Michigan Avenue. Not too far north, not too far south. Just perfect, perfect location. Plenty to see and do close by within walking distance. Apple Store, Brooks Brothers, Niketown and a whole bunch of other stores along Michigan Ave. John Hancock Building and Water Tower just a few blocks away. It's an easy walk to downtown and the river, and a close walk to Lakeshore Drive and the lakefront. Adnd you can walk north to the Gold Coast neighborhood. Plenty to eat too close by. Visited West Egg Cafe and Volare Italian Restaurant. Coco Pazzo Cafe is also close by. The hotel definitely served as a home away from home. We could stop in for a quick clothes change, shower or an afternoon recharge, and it never felt out of the way. Plus it has a rooftop pool, which is very cool.

title: “Not Quite As Good As We Remembered”
text:
A decade ago we spent several nights each year at this charming hotel. It was one of our most favorite places to stay, and even though it was above our budget we always found the money to indulge in the delights of this lovely hotel. We returned to San Diego recently after having not been in the town for more than ten years. We know that ten years is a long time in the life of a hotel, but we made reservations hoping things had not changed for the worse.
The good news: The hotel has attempted to keep up with the times by adding small refrigerators and microwaves as well as internet access. Drapes and spreads were fairly up-to-date, and the old Spanish-style furniture still looked good. Our room was fairly large, with a decent-sized bathroom. Service is still a high-priority. A problem in the bathroom was fixed within minutes of our report.
The bad news: Internet access is via cable so only one of us could work on a computer, which was a huge inconvenience for us. We were surprised that wireless was not available. In the past our rooms were always located under shady roofs surrounded by luxurious bougainvillea, over-looking interesting little gardens. This year we were placed in a building that overlooked a parking lot which did not even belong to the hotel. No special feelings from this view unless you want to compare it to a motor court of the 1950's. The absolutely fantastic restaurant in the hotel is under different management and a new menu and we will probably never taste lime-roasted chicken again. What a pity!
The first quoted price of $159/night would have been totally outrageous for this hotel, even though it does enjoy a good location. Our negotiated price of $120/night was still excessive for what we received.
Two random thoughts: It is silly to include a parking charge with a hotel room for which 90% of guests will have reached via automobile. Just add the charge to the room cost.
This hotel had the cheapest toilet paper I have ever used, and that includes some not very nice places in third world nations. I did not understand why they "skimped" on something like this.

title: “Great all around hotel”
text: We stayed at the Fairfax during a family vacation to Washington. The hotel was extremely clean and the staff very nice and helpful. The concierge Quatina was instructional in getting us directions and tips on where to eat and the best mode of transportation to wherever we were going. The location is excellent with a Starbucks around the corner. Also, there is a Tangy Sweet yogurt shop just at the end of the block that is a must for red velvet cupcakes. They are divine. We felt very safe in this neighborhood. We had a suite with a king bed and two pull out sofas. The room was spacious and extremely clean and well taken care of. The turn-down service was a nice touch. We had room service one night for dinner and it was okay. The service part of it was fine but the food was just status quo. All in all, it is a great find and stay for the value and service. We will stay there again in the future.

title: “Pricy but convenient location”
text: We made a quick trip to San Francisco and were looking for accommodations near the financial district. The room rate was, as expected, fairly high. It is San Francisco, after all. But on top of that, the almost $50.00 a night to park our car really didn't sit well. I did try to find a cheaper option to park, however, since I was traveling with my daughter, I opted for safety and convenience over parking in a lesser priced lot about a mile away. The hotel has a limited-hours restaurant. The breakfast buffet was around $18.00 (there were no cook to order items on the menu.) There are many other meal options just a short walk from the hotel, which I would advise. The staff was friendly and the rooms were clean and comfortable. The two positives about this hotel is the free wi-fi and its location. But they do come at a price.

title: “A nightmare”
text: The hotel is old, dirty, and people are not friendly, exceptly for two girls that work during the day in the front desk. There are lots of loud parties in the night that will make you wish to go back anywhere besides the hotel. It does not matter if you are tired or not. You will not sleep or rest. Do not eat at the restaurant aside because they are so confused that they charged you wrong bills to your room.

title: “Over-rated”
text: I don't know why TripAdvisor loves this place. I selected it based on the high ratings. I was expecting a truly classy hotel but it was average. Checkin service was average- I wasn't greeted by name at any point. I wasn't offered bellhop assistance with my luggage. The room heater didn't seem to be working. The lodge/den was not refreshed with the free snacks so when they were gone, they were gone. The refrigerators were so loud "lounging in the lodge/den" was impossible. My closet had a blood-stained robe in the closet. People speak of the hotel like it's an escape but I could see and hear street traffic when walking between the hotel room to the main building. I had a better stay the previous night at a much cheaper hotel.

title: “Excellent Service, Location and Space”
text:
Travelling with small children can always be difficult especially when it comes to eating. Not only do the separate rooms allow for some privacy at night, but the small kitchen proves to be a godsend. You can stock up on the some food for the kids at the local Wholefoods and save yourself a whole load of aggro.
Rooms are spacious, the views are amazing and the rates appear to be a lot more attractive than they used to be.
Recommended.

title: “Very nice hotel- would recommend”
text:
Stayed two nights- due to the unplanned winter storm.
Very nice room- nice/competent people on staff.
Pleasantly surprised at the level of service and room maintenance.

title: “All We Wanted”
text: Free breakfast buffet and free light dinner, great location, capable friendly staff, cheapest rates.

title: “Excellent value!”
text: We came to the LA area for a weekend (wedding) and chose to stay here for its proximity to our destinations, as well as the reasonable price. Honestly I was hesitant to stay at a Super 8 as I haven't heard great stories in the past, and I didn't know anything about the neighborhood. We were pleasantly surprised about the cleanliness of the rooms, and the immaculate parking lot, and the safe area. I would stay here again in a heartbeat.

title: “We really enjoyed our week at Millenium Hilton NYC”
text:
I stayed here on a trip to NYC with my mother for Xmas 2011. We stayed here for 8 nights. This is a pretty fabulous hotel. The views, are really spectacular, especially from the higher floors. I stayed in a Junior Suite on level 49, and my Mum was staying in a room on the smoking floor, which was on a corner and also had a very lovely outlook of the old church and the Woolworth Building. Both rooms were very comfortable and well presented, with very large wall like windows.
The location is great for exploring Lower Manhattan - and the subway is just on the corner near the hotel, so it is quite quick and easy to get up to midtown also. The impact of the WTC rebuild is felt while staying in the hotel, as it really is directly across the road from the construction. My mother and I found this quite powerful and moving, and also meeting some of the staff that were still working in the hotel from the time of 9/11, and hearing there stories was a very moving experience. 
There was 24 hour construction that was occurred during our stay, and there was some noise, but it wasn't overbearing. One nice thing is all rooms have windows that open slightly, so even on a very high floor one can get fresh air.
The lobby bar here is really great. Great bar tenders that make lovely drinks, and provide a really nice 'local' bar feel. I really enjoyed being able to come back and relax at the bar in the evenings after sight seeing and enjoy the ambience there.
There is quite a nice relaxed and second home feel about this Hilton, which I really enjoyed. Not being right in the centre of NYC, and also probably being a business hotel catering to many return guests, gave it a really nice feeling. We both felt very comfortable and secure in our stay.
The housekeeping dept. were fantastic. We really noticed their professionalism and attention to detail. It was a nice touch that the ice was placed in our ice buckets at turn down time. Very lovely staff we encountered there.
Overall, I wouldn't have any hesitations to recommend this hotel. It is a really comfortable, and well appointed property, and we enjoyed the food and drinks we had here. We had room service several times, and dined in the restaurant also, everything was lovely.
That said, even though I like the relaxed and not so uptight atmosphere here, there were some moments were the service of the front desk, operator, and concierge could have been a little tighter. The staff were always professional, though I did feel a few times the service standard wasn't quite as attentive or experienced as what I am used to experiencing at Hilton hotels, which was a surprise in NYC! The service at Hilton Times Square in these front office departments was definitely noticeably better. I think that this could be improved - a more service orientated outlook, without being to intrusive or forceful, and this hotel would be really fantastic. The breakfast sort of suffered a little from this hit and miss service quality too unfortunately. The dinner waiters were great, as were the bar staff in the lobby as mentioned.
Anyway, thanks to all the staff at this hotel. The service was overall good, and we really felt at home here on the other side of the world from Australia over xmas. A special thanks to the Housekeeping and Lobby Bar staff for looking after the 'Molony's' : )
Try Andy's Afternoon - a cocktail in Liquid Assets Lobby Bar, and a must - is Century 21 across the road for unbelievable discounted shopping. Definitely by all your I Love NYC souvenir items here-- it is so much cheaper than anywhere else!

title: “Disappointed”
text:
My wife & I often stayed at this quaint little hotel in the city before the change in ownership. Since coming under the corprate umbrella of a "hospitality" company, it has lost the charm and personal service that made it so refreshing. Our last stay was marked by a reduction in quality: food service and offerings for breakfast; room not clean, old carpet, dust, etc.; lack of friendly staff.
I only write now because the Petite Auberge recently sent a postcard seeking our consideration of a promotion at the property. The answer is no. We do not intend to return. Anyone who recalls the former Petite Auberge will likely have the same answer. Sadly, it's the large hotel on Union Square for us now.

title: “Fabulous Hotel!”
text:
Considering that I grew up in Houston, I never knew what a fabulous "vacation" I could have in my hometown, thanks to Hotel ZaZa. Since I live/work overseas, I wanted to book a nice hotel for my visit to Houston, and I was very lucky to have come across this hotel before it even opened. From the initial booking, the service was impeccable! Originally, I booked for a petit King, but due to change of plans I needed a bigger room. When I contacted the hotel through email, not only did they graciously oblige, they also gave it to me for the same rate as the petit King. 
From the moment we arrived, the staff was more than accommodating. They went above and beyond most 5 star hotels in getting us what we needed. The hotel was extremely stylish, the rooms beautiful, and the amenities were also a perfect touch. We loved the unique small pillows, the Bulgari bathroom sets, the 42" screen plasma TV! 
We spent the last day at the pool after we had already checked out, and the atmosphere and surroundings are like you are in some vacation hot spot. The pool is a bit small, but the surrounding more than makes up for it. The pool area also has private outdoor bungalows that are beautifully decorated.
My experience at Hotel ZaZa was one of my best stays in a hotel. 
The only thing I think they could work on is the service at their bar/lounge. The service was extremely slow. We must have waited about 30 minutes for someone to even come to our table. Other than that, I thought their overall staff and service were magnificent!

title: “Good Hotel in Great Location”
text:
This hotel is in the BEST location ever. The hotel staff was very nice, friendly, and helpful. Check-in was quick and they even gave me a choice of 2 full beds or 1 King bed. The common areas are very art deco style and cool looking, especially the elevators. Marble galore and immense paintings grace the lobby, and make the place look super fancy, but the furnishings in the waiting area in the lobby are more than a bit worn. The room itself was very clean and in good shape. The dresser and nighstand were scuffed up, but not in a major way. The bathroom was very clean and the tile and marble was all in perfect shape. We had a pretty good view from our room on floor 21. 
I can't say enough about the location. It is right next to the Times Square ToysRUs, on 44th St. 
This hotel was a bargain on Hotwire for around $188. Loved it!
To sum up:
PROS: 1. GREAT LOCATION- 2.Friendly & efficient employees- 3. Clean, comfortable rooms- 4. Price
Con: 1. A few areas in need of refurb.

title: “The Best Hotel in Indy”
text: Every year we stay at this hotel for Gencon and every year we have a fantastic time. The hotel rooms are always very clean and comfortable. The hotel staff is always extremely friendly and helpful. They show appreciation for our business and that makes us feel very welcome. The parking attendants are always great. They take care of our car, help us with our bags and give us directions with a smile every time. The lounge and breakfast is always terriffic! Coffee in the lounge is always available for free at all times during the day or night. The lounge is one of my favorite parts of this hotel. The location of this hotel is right downtown so everything is within walking distance. I am never concerned with security at this hotel since you need your keycard to get into the hotel and elevators at night. I love this hotel and I wouldn't want to stay anywhere else in Indy. This is probably the most comfortable I have ever been in a hotel. I hope this hotel never changes!

title: “Great find in a great neighborhood”
text: I had the chance to stay at the Normandy with my fiancee for one night this past weekend and we really enjoyed our brief time there. The hotel is located on a quiet street about a ten minute walk from the DuPont Circle metro station. I think you could also walk to the Woodley Park station as well if you were so inclined. The rooms are very impressive and the toile walls definitely give it a boutique feel. The rooms might feel a bit small if you were there for a really extended stay, but this is D.C. and the whole city can be a bit cramped, so I wouldn't "take off points" so to speak for that. The staff was very kind and courteous in our few interactions with them. One thing that people staying here should be aware of is that you cannot adjust the temperature in your room through the thermostat. Since it was still early spring, the heat was on in full force. We woke up at 5:00 AM both drenched in sweat and tried to turn the thermostat down. When that did not do anything we called downstairs and were informed by the person at the desk that rooms were on a central unit and that you could not change the temperature in individual rooms. We could crack the window, and after doing that things cooled off considerably and we were able to go back to sleep. This seems to be an older building that has been renovated (quite well I might add) so you should be willing to accept these idiosyncrasies in exchange for the added character of a boutique hotel. All in all it was a great stay and we were sorry to leave. We definitely plan on staying here again when we return to the city (especially if we can get another great deal on Priceline like we did this time)!

title: “No Shampoo”
text:
The property was better than antiicipated being recently renovated.
The grounds and pool are expansive. However, it must not be hotel policy to leave shampoo for guests, only lotion. This was quite strange to this veteran traveller. The roar from I 35 can also be irritating when trying to sleep.But, it's location is very convenient to Downtown Austin and Roundrock.

title: “Cancellation”
text: Their cancellation policy is not practial for the business traveler. If you do not cancel by noon the day before your arrival, they will charge the full amount for your room. Due to business deadlines and meeting cancellations, plans can change abruptly. I have stayed there many times but may need to change to a hotel with the usual cancellation policy of before 6pm the day of arrival.

title: “A Fabulous Hotel!”
text: We stayed just one night but thoroughly enjoyed this hotel. Our room was on the 37th floor with amazing eastward views of the bridges over the East River and northerly views of beautiful Midtown (loved the remote drape operation)! Staff was wonderful as was the amazing bed -- extremely comfortable! Room service for breakfast was quick and delicious! Highly recommend this hotel and looking forward to returning!

title: “Great Hotel”
text: Although in September 2005, the rates are no longer as inexpensive as they were in August, we thoroughly enjoyed our stay at the Hampton Inn. The room was very nicely furnished with a flat screen TV, nice modern furniture and was quite large for NYC. The bathroom had marble counters but was small. The bed was extremely comfortable. The room was quiet with no street noise or noise from other guests. The staff was pleasant and efficient. The free breakfast was very impressive with scrambled eggs, bacon, fresh fruit, as well as the usual continental offerings. It was nice to grab a quick breakfast and be off for a day of sightseeing. The location is good. You're a few short blocks from the heart of Times Square. The concierge recommended Ciro Trattoria for dinner. It was excellent. Would recommend this hotel to anyone.

title: “Fabulous value on priceline”
text: Spent a couple days in DC after the New Year, and got this hotel for two nights for a steal on Priceline. Very clean, spacious rooms. The kitchenettes would be terrific for anyone on an extended staff. The staff was courteous, and it was just a few minutes' walk from the DC metro and the eatries/shopping of Dupont Circle. Would love to stay there again!

title: “COMPLIMENTARY BREAKFAST WAS AWESOME! !!!”
text: Let me first start with the location near a lot of places n right on the side of amajor highway so that's a plus (easy access anywhere ) second rooms r decent n clean... my favorite of all is the quantity of different choices for breakfast n all included best ever caint go wrong but my only complaint is the smell of the hallways they stink nothing but cigarettes smoke smell. ( not good) n u can also smells in the rooms (non smoking rooms ) I travel with two kids n one is asthmatic so that wasn't good .. if only they did something about that this hotel for the price location and food will b a 5 star even though is a older building the rooms r kept decent ..

title: “Fun and Modern Hotel in Great Location”
text:
Check in was so quick and easy, it's all computerised. Bags were then taken to our room so that we knew where to go etc. 
Rooms are quite small if you were going to stay for more than a couple of days. But the rooms are really new and modern and perfectly designed to make the most of the space. It's very original and fun! Very nice flat screen TV on the wall and ipod docking station. Immaculately clean and good bathroom, although again fairly compact. As it's open plan (only glass and a curtain to separate bedroom and bathroom) you would probably want to ensure you were close to whoever you were sharing a room with. Complimentary muffins and coffee in the morning is a nice touch. 
We didn't eat in the restaurant but it looked very nice. We had cocktails on the rooftop terrace which was lovely. Nice space. 
Whole hotel was lovely and will definitely stay again and recommend it to people.

title: “Great stock standard Marriott- NO WIFI IN ROOMS!”
text: Enjoyed my stay, hotel covered all bases except the Wifi issue. They have free wifi on the first and second floors but that didn't suit my needs as i needed to work. paid about $12 to get internet in my room which i thought was abit steep, oh and worth mentioning (....seems to be the norm in Boston hotels... but worth mentioning) parking I paid $35per 24hrs (not the valet service that was more I believe) Just something to remember when working out cost of hotels in Boston.

title: “Fantastic hotel let down by silly thing!”
text:
Fantastic hotel, excellent service but parking is EXTORTIONATE at $48 a night!!! and internet service at $19 a day!!
Apart from the above the rooms, hotel, staff were fantastic. Hotel was clean comfortable and i would 100% stay here again in a heartbeat!! i just wouldt take the car!

title: “Exceptional Hotel”
text: Awesome Hotel!! After months of researching (I'm very fussy), reading several reviews & calling several 4+ star hotels with downright rude reservation clerks, I called The Benjamin & spoke with Avis who would guarantee me a high floor suite with a terrace unlike the other hotels I called. When we arrived she called me to make certain everything was alright. It was more than alright! The view was spectacular, room service was prompt & delicious but a bit pricey, so the kitchen came in handy with a refrigerator to store our food and a microwave to cook it, double-paned windows provided a quiet room in spite of the outside noise, when we returned after our hectic days the turn-down service was exceptional with scented dried herbs, soft music from the Bose radio, a pillow menu, great mattress and linens for a heavenly sleep, an office desk area with ample room to work, 2 large TV's so no one fought over what to watch, spacious rooms even with the sofa bed pulled out & closet space galore. The Benjamin is centrally located so you can walk to most major sites or take a taxi for about $5.00. Last but not least, every employee we met (and we met quite a few during our stay) had smiles and were very courteous and helpful. We never did take advantage of the Spa, but there is always next time. Now we know first hand why The Benjamin is rated #1 on several of the hotel review websites. It is the best!!!!

title: “Nice Budget Hotel”
text: We were in town for the Macy's Parade and selected this hotel based on the fact that it was the best deal we could find. That should be your selection criteria too. If you are looking for a clean, simple room, this is it. My husband and I have have stayed in every hotel price range imaginable, but for this trip, we were trying to stay on the cheap, as we knew we would never be in the room. The room was clean and small. All NYC hotels are small, so brace yourself. Beds were comfy and bathrooms clean. Lobby area was nice and they provide a complimentary breakfast of coffee, juice, bagels, and do-nuts. The location is great for exploring and the subway is around the corner and down one block. My only complaint is that our AC banged and roared all night (EVEN WHEN OFF, yes, I know, but it's true). I did let the front desk know, and while he was polite, nothing was fixed. Other than the strange window unti banging, we never heard our neighbors or the street. The staff was polite, but older and not exactly "hip" on cool places to eat or have a drink. You are on your own for that advice. I would probably not stay here again, only because I am personally not a fan of the neighborhood or being that close to Times Square, but for many visitors, the location is perfect.

title: “Hotel is ok, service is TERRIBLE!”
text: The manager and the assistant manager have ZERO customer service skills. The service at the bar is horrible. Bar closes at 7 pm and there is no way to get drinks thereafter. Very expensive, might as well go to Cancun for the weekend to get great service and lots of fun! Totally disappointed!

title: “Enjoyed it, a great central location for San Francisco”
text: The hotel had nostalgic looks. Needed double windows to reduce noise polution. Had a great conceirge, Jewel. He was exceptional helping us plan our daily tours and recommended great restaurants. He went above and beyond his duty, worked with us several weeks in advance of our stay.

title: “Interesting”
text:
This hotel does appear to be getting a bit of a bad reputation! I am not going to tell you that this hotel is amazing but what you get is what you pay for!
The room is interesting! You walk in and can almost touch both walls with your arms out stretched. The only furniture is a bunk bed and TV. 
The bunk bed is not the most comfortable but is adequate. The bed is quite noisy especially when moving around at night!
The TV quite suprisingly has cable and has a majority of the decent channels!
The shared bathroom always seemed clean and the shower provided was powerful enough to have a decent shower! Although the toilet did block up on one day!
The staff seem friendly at reception and my favourite part of the hotel is the lift which appears to be marble until you get near it and the marble effect is little more than stuck on panels!
The location appears to be pleasent with many shops around. The subway is a 5 minute walk away, you can either join the Number 1 line at 103rd or 110th.
The pictures are slightly misleading as they make the hotel look like a quaint Paris style hotel, this is not the case.
Please do not have high expectations of this place because you will be bitterly disapointed! It is basic but you should only be paying roughly $60 - $70 a night for two!

title: “We'll be back!”
text: My boatracing team was well taken care of during our stay at the Best Western Seven Seas when we stayed there for San Diego's Bayfair and I wanted to pass along my thanks. We had 18 rooms and they were all clean and well equipped. We're hoping that Bayfair will become an annual event again for the Unlimited hydroplanes and if it is, we'll be back!

title: “Location is the only thing for this place!”
text:
We stayed here for 4 nights on a business trip. The only thing going for this Holiday Inn is the location right next to the stadiums. We called for a courtesy van from the airport, and after 40 minutes, nothing showed up. After we called back, we found out the manager cancelled our pickup, since our bookings were done via our corporate travel department. It was a $20 taxi ride from the airport to the hotel, and after we found the manager, he stuck to his belief that if someone books their reservations via any other site than Holiday Inn, they will not provide courtesy transportation from the airport to the hotel. 
This hotel is dated, the staff at the check in desk seem to have a low morale, and it takes forever for the air conditioner to cool the room.
The good news is that a competitor will be building a new hotel about a block away soon, so a better choice will be available for this prime sports location.

title: “Crowne Plaza, my first choice”
text: I stayed at 2 New York hotels over total of 6 days. The other was considered a luxury boutique hotel that cost more. However, I thought the Crowne Plaza represented a better value -- location was central to Times Square and the theatre district, the room was larger, and service was good.

title: “don't stay here”
text:
I have been to other W properties and stay at the W in Miami all the time. the staff there are amazing and the manager (Dennis) is the best! 
However the W in DC I cannot even believe it's owned by the the same group. Th staff is so unfriendly beyond rude! the place looks cheap. the only thing positive is the roof top bar and BEWARE: Oh my they are abusive. there are lines. They I.D. some and not others. RUDE. believe me its not worth it. nothing that great to see better off walking around and seeing the sights or staying at another hotel. there are so many great hotels by the white house where you get treated amazing. I stayed at the Hay adams -top notch with a great bar called "off the record at least your not getting pushed around there, standing in lines, and having security pick and choose who they harass. also another great place to stay is in georgetown four seasons is great... ritz carlton.. georgetown inn. and as I mentioned hay adams by white house. stay away from the W. I travel all the time. believe me the staff is RUDE and security to get to the rooftop are racist. they will pick and choose. who needs it.. It will ruin your vacation.

title: “Small, but certainly suitable”
text:
My 2 daughters and I (from The Netherlands) enjoyed our 4-night stay at the Comfort Inn Times Square. The location was perfect, near to Times Square, Broadway, the open-top tour buses, a Starbucks and the subway. We came in on the Airtrain and Subway from JFK which was easy and the hotel is next to the Port Authority. Don't be put off by the exterior (building work and rubbish on the street), inside all is fine (remember this is a 2-3* hotel). The whole hotel is a bit on the small side from the lobby to the rooms, but these are modern and clean smelling and the bathroom in our room was very clean with a daily change of towels. We did have a problem understanding how to work the shower though!
We had read about the small breakfast room, but it was adequate and the bagels, toast, cereals and muffins were good and made an easy start to the day. 
As for the service, we are Europeans so our expectations are generally lower. (Americans expect more, we have got used to putting up with less!). For us there was nothing at all to complain about at all. The desk staff were polite, I was immediately informed about the free wireless internet for my iphone which was perfect (most business hotels I have stayed in recently charged EUR 12 a day) and the hotel stored our luggage (lots of it) for free on the last day.
For our mother and daughter trip to New York this hotel was certainly suitable and I would recommend it to anyone who is planning to spend most of their time in New York seeing the signts and not staying in their room.

title: “Top location for sightseeing”
text: Stayed two nights at the Hotel Monaco, the rooms are a decent size and the decor was good it looked like it had been recently refurbished, though the leopard print bathrobes were interesting. We were placed on the 1st floor, which is below street level, they advised us it was the quiet area, it was a long walk from the elevators, unfortunately they put families next door with young kids, so much for the quiet area! It is located almost across the road from the Verizon Center, a great spot for sports fans attending games! Overall we enjoyed it, as the location and reasonable price outweighed the flaws of the room location and noise of room's nearby!

title: “good experience, great location”
text:
my boyfriend and I stayed at the Allerton for one night while on vacation in Chicago. We hotwired the hotel and got a GREAT deal. Paid only $110 for the night whereas if we had booked it regularly it would have been $170 (which would have been too much for what our room was)
Reception is on the second floor. Hallways and elevators are both narrow.. you can tell that the hotel is old. Nice decor though. Our room was very tiny (it was the petite) but very clean. The hotels location itself was fabulous.. right in the middle of magnificint mile. 
We really didnt spend a lot of time there so the size of the room didnt bother us. Perfect for a hotel just to sleep in with a great location. If you are driving keep in mind that parking is $50 per day. Allow some time to pick up your baggage if you are leaving it with the bell boy to go and explore a bit more after checking out or before checking into your room.. they are very busy. 
All in all it was a nice hotel, with a good price due to hotwire. If we got the same price again we might consider staying here again.

title: “Pleasant stay, would recommend”
text: Room (Queen) was spacious, clean and neutrally decorated. Good views.
