Bathroom old, but clean and well maintained.Hotel is excellently located for sightseeing, shopping and evenings out.Staff friendly and helpful.Excellent variety of onsite restaurants, including Ben and Jerry's and the highly commended McCormack and Schmicks.Would go back.

title: “Great for the rate!”
text:
My husband, 5 year old son and I stayed here on the evening of 8/14/04. We booked through priceline for the rate of $55 per night so I have to say the price was right. We checked in and they vey nicely accomodated our request for a double room which had a nice view on the 8th floor. The room was a "standard business" layout. It was nice but not over the top deluxe. It did not have an in room safe.
The hotel is well located in downtown and is about a two minute walk to the Disney Concert Hall/Dorothy Chandler/Ahmanson, etc.. It would be ideal for dinner and an evening at the theater concert.
We went to Olivera Street for Mexican food on saturday night and ate at Los Golondrinas, a classic but touristy destination. Dinner for the three of us (with a couple Margaritas and tip) was about $60. The little shopping area on Olivera Street is alot of fun, especially for children, with lots of toys for under $5.
The pool at the hotel was well heated but did not get direct sun because of all of the tall buildings near by. It is also a small lap pool but was not at all crowded on the weekend. The three of us had the pool to ourselves for pretty much all of Saturday afternoon between 3:30pm to 5:00pm.
All in all, Downtown LA is pretty dead on the weekend and if this is your "Big Vacation" you could well be disappointed. However, if you get it for the right price and have the right expectations it is quite a find.

title: “Thus far in my 34 years of life I have...”
text: Thus far in my 34 years of life I have yet to stay in a hotel as disgusting and unsanitary as the Hotel Pennsylvania !! They should change the name to the flop house motel ,.. Dirty , loud , crazy people running the halls day and night ! The rooms were dirty , the beds made noise and were not stable , the sheets had stains and so did the bathroom walls ! The toilet was filthy and had been left without flushing and the tile in the shower was coming up all over the floor !! Thank God we only had one night here but we changed rooms 3 times and they were all disgraceful !!

title: “consistency”
text: great location. excellent service. makes everyone feel important from the moment you check in (front desk is above the norm) to the restaurant and bar staff to room service and the concierge. I stay in this hotel frequently because I know what I typed previously will be consistent with every stay.

title: “Very Comfortable Hotel”
text:
I stayed at this hotel for one night in May while traveling for business. I was only there for one night however it didn’t seem like there was much around this hotel as far as restaurants or shopping. There was a Denny’s nearby but that was all I saw. A co-worker was staying at a different Hilton and we went over to her hotel where there were tons of restaurants to choose from.
When we arrived check-in was quick and easy and everyone was very friendly. When I got to my room I was extremely disappointed as the strong stench of cigarette smoke hit me as soon as I opened the door. I called down to the front desk and asked for a non-smoking room and was told that they were completely booked for the night. I guess the person at the front desk could tell how upsetting this was to me because he said he’d see what he could do. Five minutes later he called back and said he did some “rearranging” and found a non-smoking room. He personally came up to my smoking room and walked with me down to the non-smoking room. It was so much better and I was so grateful that he was able to accommodate me with a non-smoking room.
Once my room was changed I was very happy with it. The bed was extremely comfortable. There was a card on the bed that said it could be adjusted to make it soft or firm however I wasn’t able to find the dial to do this adjusting. There was also a chair, footstool and a desk. There was a nice flat screen TV as well. 
Toiletries were really nice and consisted of Neutragena lotion, shampoo, conditioner and mouthwash. The bathroom was a nice size and very clean.
When we came back from diner the front desk had fresh cookies available which was a nice touch. I did not eat at the onsite restaurant but the breakfast looked good. They do not offer a continental breakfast.
When I arrived home I realized I left the cord for my cell phone in my room. I called the hotel and sure enough they found it. They said they could ship it to me. I asked them to ship it the cheapest way possible. Well, I guess they didn’t hear the word cheap because they shipped it next day air, which cost more than the cord was even worth. But, it was nice that they took the time to ship it to me, and I was glad to get it back.
I would recommend this hotel for its service, cleanliness and comfort however I’m not sure it’s in the most convenient location.

title: “Excellent value for you and your pets!”
text: I often stay at Red Roof hotels because they always accept pets, and they are a great value for the money. This Red Roof is in a very convenient location to both the interstate and restaurants, and, it was clean, quiet and the staff was excellent. While I did not in this case make a reservation, the staff quickly found a place for me to stay that was ideal for my needs. My cat, my 15 year old son and I had a restful night.

title: “Fantastic!”
text:
I stayed at The Greenwich for my Birthday recently & had an amazing stay! The hotel is located in Tribeca, a lovely, calm neighborhood in NYC, set on a cobblestoned st. I arrived early around 11am, & my room was ready. I had never stayed at the hotel before, & while the Front Desk Agent who checked me in was nice, I wasn't given an info. on the hotel, etc. I'm quite familiar w/ the property, so this wasn't necessary for me, but just something to mention. To access the elevator, you must use your key, which I wasn't aware of until I figured this out (this is something that should have been mentioned...again, just a note) My room (#503) was on the 5th fl. & incredibly quiet, lovely & super in terms of design, colors, etc. I loved my room! The pale yellow walls, clean hard wood floors, amazing Duxiana bed, soft sheets, & amazing bathroom done in beautiful Orange & White tiles were all great! The mini-bar was extremely well-stocked & all items were complimentary, with the exception of the wine & liquor. Everything was provided from Mexican Coca Cola, Fiji Water, Pineapple Juice, Ginger Ale, to a lovely basket of snacks, including Kettle Chips, Cookies, Nuts, Swedish Fish, etc....I thoroughly enjoyed the mini-bar & it was so nice to have it all included! nice touch guys!
The Desk area was spacious with outlets, & nice bookshelves w/ a cool selection of books, objects, & a little jar of candy! so nice! The Flat screen T.V. had clear reception, the sitting area had a comfy sofa, the windows opened which was great, the A/C made the room incredibly cold, which I love, & the closet was spacious, with a safe, slippers, padded hangers, etc. The bathroom had an absolutely amazing waterfall Rain Shower that was truly the best I've had in a hotel!!! I never wanted to get out.....the deep-soaking tub was also pure bliss! The Red Flower products have a lovely masculine scent & I also loved the soap. The towels were super great, the Frette robes were cool for the Summer & the light fixtures above the sink were amazing! The WC is in a seperate alcove which is nice. The pressure in the shower & tub were 100% flawless! 
I just loved the overall feeling of my room....light, airy, cool & beautifully unique in terms of design & colors! The rug was also great....so many unique, special touches in the room! I was celebrating my birthday, so the hotel sent a lovely card w/ Champagne(which I don't drink, so they sent a cupcake-thanks alot!) A welcome note from the hotel w/ 2 Oatmeal Sandwich cookies were awesome!!! The lobby & drawing room w/ outdoor courtyard were great & my meals from Room service were amazing! great food & arrived very quick. 
Everything was absolutely perfect during my stay! All bellmen were very nice & charming, Matt at the front desk granted me a late 1:30pm check-out that was much appreciated & Lauren & Jonathan were very nice, as well at the Front Desk. I loved the hotel & will def. be back soon! 
Best,
Patrick 
NYC

title: “Clean Rooms, Nice Staff... But Horrible Neighbors and Bad Area”
text:
I love the Motel 6 brand. When you're traveling just for the weekend, for some purpose other than a fancy vacation, it's absolutely the way to go.
Rooms were spartan and industrial, but VERY clean and comfortable. A/C worked very good... which is a big plus in the middle of July in Austin, Texas. Staff was extremely helpful and nice. I would stay again... if it weren't for the other guests and the REALLY ROUGH part of town where this motel is located!!!
Pool area was a perpetual party from the time it opened to the time it closed... people boozing, swimming, and screaming all day long. When the pool closed, people lined the sidewalks drinking every night. I would wake up in the morning to garbage sacks full of beer cans along the sidewalks. Very sordid groups of people walking around all night long, including ladies that I suspect were prostitutes. I am a smoker... I go outside each time I want a cigarette... I really didn't even feel safe doing that.
If motel would step up security patrol, it would be a decent place to stay. As it stands, it served its purpose, but I would not stay there again. The sad part is... the staff is great and the rooms are a good value. It would be a hidden gem if only it were in a better part of town and attracted better guests.
My suggestion... keep driving on I-35 southbound for about 2 more miles. There is a cluster of much nicer-looking hotels/motels (including another M6) near the I-35/HWY183 interchange.

title: “Had a really bad stay...”
text: Rooms were really small, location is great if its your first time in ny, but not the best hotel to stay if its your first time... you will end up hating ny...staff were really rude.. No hot water whole of Sunday.... And all they can offer you is breakfast.... I will never stay there again....

title: “Always my first choice in Seattle”
text:
I have stayed at the Moore Hotel three times now and it has always been a great experience. Its location is great if you are in town for shopping or just seeing the sights. Only a few blocks from Pike Place Market and a few more to Alaskan Way. Go east a few blocks and you are at Macy's and the downtown mall area.
Moore is a budget hotel, but not too budget-y (if you get me). The furnishings are dated, television only has a few channels and elevator is slow and tiny, still the bed is nicely firm and bedding clean and well taken care of. Some of the rooms have a toilet and shower, while others are shared (only stayed in one of those once; either get up early or sleep in as it is hard to in the shower right on time).
There is a little bar downstairs where you can get food, but I would suggest you head over to Virginia st. and eat at the wonderful Argentinian steak house (tango demonstrations on the weekend). They recently added a coffee bar too (this IS Seattle after all), and that I do highly recommend. Amazing lattes and the pastries are wonderful.
If I am ever in Seattle again you can be sure I'll be back at the Moore.
Fun fact: hotel is rumoured to be haunted though I have yet to see anything paranormal.

title: “Old elegance with niggling issues”
text: The grand atrium is a visual spectacle, but large events while I was there caused a great deal of noise, some of which leaked into my room until midnight one night. It is a beautiful place to have breakfast, but $72 + tip for two "american breakfasts" with juice and coffee is exorbitant. So, for that matter, is the charge for internet usage, which inexplicably in our case was deducted from the bill - if so, why the charade of charging? In fact, in such a hotel, why charge at all? Otherwise, all was comfortable old elegance, including a slow-to-react HVAC. The bed was great and the Pied Piper Bar a nice place to hang out.

title: “Nice, but not worth 4-Star Prices”
text:
We had a reservation at the Holiday Inn on the Hill 3* across the street for $89, then got a $65/night priceline deal for this hotel, a 4* hotel. So we were very happy! Had we actually paid the regular rates, this review would not be as good, but for the price we paid, we can't complain too much!
First, the good stuff:
-- Room looked nice and modern, clean
-- Hyatt's "grand bed" was great, my wife was 8 months pregnant, and she slept great!
-- breakfast service excellent!
-- atmosphere was classy, Christmas music playing, nicely lit and decorated lobby/lounging area
-- location was great, easy walk to Union Station Metro
-- Staff was very helpful
Now the not-so-good:
-- no fridge/microwave available, would expect more amenities in a 4* hotel
-- can't understand how they can be considered 4* and not include wifi for free....or make you pay extra for gym/pool...the Jefferson in Richmond has free Wifi everywhere and includes the gym/pool
-- Located next to fire station, at first hearing so many fire engines go by, we just thought DC was like that, then we walked out one day and saw the station across the street!
-- slow draining sink
-- the hot breakfast food was overly greasy, stick to the continental (still must pay extra $20 to "upgrade" to business plan)
-- parking is $33/day, overpriced

title: “Almost like home”
text:
Over the years I have done a lot of traveling , both business and leisure. I always look for 
the Jameson Inn first. I must say the one I like the best is in Jacksonville, Florida.at 7030 Bonneval Rd. These people have gone out of their way to make my stay a very plesant one. Everyone here treats you like one of the family, and since I am staying for 8 weeks, 
this is very important to me. I would like to think I was the only one that received this 
special treatment, however I soon found out they treated everyone like this. So, if you need a good place to stay that is clean and friendly, check out the Jameson Inn.

title: “Romance at the Radisson!”
text: My husband and I planned our own Babymoon and booked the Radisson as our hotel. The staff was SUPER friendly. I had requested a King Size Bed and when we walked in our room, there were two beds. We immediately notified the front desk, they apologized and got us into our King Suite right then. We also had Breakfast in Bed one morning. I, being pregnant, had so many off-the-wall requests. They did everything I asked for and everything was yummy! The room was just so clean and nice. The hotel is right across from Dave & Busters and we walked over our first night and had a great time. It is also in a great location and close to most everything in Jax. Oh, and the SleepNumber beds are amazing. I will DEFINITELY be staying here again!

title: “two stars at best”
text: Well I've never had a Caesar Salad with powdered parmesan out of a packet before! And all other aspects of the hotel were in every respect similar to the quality of my salad. Need I say more?

title: “Loved the Ritz Carlton”
text: We stayed at the Ritz-Carlton for a few days after Christmas and loved it. There aren't many hotels that I'm reluctant to leave but this was one. The room and the bathroom were both very spacious and we had a walk in closet/dressing room, which hid all our suitcases and clothes. The furnishings were beautiful and the bed linens were from Frette. There was a DVD player with the flat panel TV, so we brought up a movie to watch one evening. As we were celebrating two birthdays in two days, my husband ordered champagne and cake and the cakes were delicious, beautifully presented with fresh flowers and fresh fruit. The hotel staff were perhaps a little distracted as it was such a busy week - they took our used wine and water glasses on the first morning we were there and didn't replace them (ever! - we ended up using the paper coffee cups because we kept forgetting to call and ask for them to be replaced). We asked for four plates/forks for the birthday cake and only got two. But overall it was a great stay - the location was ideal; we walked out to dinner in Chinatown and North Beach on two of our nights there. The staff were friendly - and very nice to our young daughters too.

title: “Great Hotel!!!”
text: Just recently visited this hotel in October 2011. Beautiful property with great views of Pacific Beach. Get a room on the 2nd or 3rd floor oceanfront....you won't be disappointed.

title: “Great facilities - but service lacklustre”
text:
Good things about this property - unlike most of the luxury hotels in NYC, the facilities are new, and the rooms are not tired. Because of the location of the hotel, the entire hotel is quiet - no real street noise. Bathrooms are great.
Bad things - it is very expensive, and the service is simply not up to snuff for the type of property it pretends to be. Get ready for clumsy checkin, botched reservations (in the hotel's own restaurants ?) and generally blah service (even worse that what you would normally expect for high end NYC hotels). 
I've now stayed here a few times, and on each occasion, the experience has been the same. So, caveat emptor - you will pay dearly for a beautiful room, but if you are expecting service commensurate with the facilities, you will be disappointed - for that, try the FS instead.

title: “Nice stop over hotel”
text:
A very nice hotel and handy for stop overs for next day flights, just a walk away from flight book in.
Good food and friendly staff.
Why do they put a limit to the amount of characters for adding to a review. Maybe just a few words are enough for most people and having to add rubbish just makes you want to stop doing reviews!!

title: “great”
text: very nice hotel for the price, hotel staff is very helpfull and friendly. will stay again

title: “Excellent but Lacking in Some Things”
text: We're a family of five with three demanding teenagers. We checked in on Aug. 2 and out on Aug. 6. This hotel is conveniently located near the Metro (Federal Center SW station) but not much else unless you like to walk till your feet come off. The U.S. Capitol is close enough to walk to, along with some other tourist stops. In the evening, only pizza is available next door, while anything else is a Metro-ride away. We had a suite with two rooms and two TVs! The morning breakfast is fabulous. The room did look a bit dated with scratches on walls and doors that you'd think would be painted over quickly. The kitchenette proved valuable. The staff is generally very good, especially the front desk. The pool is very small and not worth the effort to swim in unless you have toddlers. Ice is only available on the 2nd floor, but your fridge has an icemaker. Although this hotel is ideal for families with over 2 children, the location makes it more suitable for a single business traveller, which is the irony here. However, I'd still come back if I were travelling with my family because you do get a lot of space for a reasonable price.

title: “Charming And Centrally-Located”
text:
I stayed at the Cornell for four nights in August. I found the service to be extremely friendly, and the breakfast was good, too. Much more than expected, actually, as it wasn't just continental. As an example of the great service, I can provide the following: for the first two nights a friend stayed with me whose flight was delayed. We went to the pizza place across the street to order, and was planning to drink one of the bottles of wine we had obtained from a place in Sonoma. When Claude, one of the owners, saw us, he offered us a table in the as-yet-unfinished cafe near reception. While he kindly refused when we offered him a glass, he stayed to chat with us for a bit, and remembered us the following day as well. The hotel also will arrange an airport shuttle for you, if needed.
My room was on the 4th floor, and the window faced a shaft open to the sky, so it was very quiet in the room while still being quite sunny during the day. The room was small, but the bed was very comfortable. If I were to stay there again with a boyfriend I'd probably get a larger room, because it was quite tight with the luggage of two people, even though we didn't have a lot. For the second two nights, when I was there on my own, the room was the perfect size. I'm only marking it down a little bit because the shower was pretty tight, even though I'm a pretty small person, the maids had missed a bit of dusting, and there was no cable TV. Aside from those pretty minor things I was very happy with the hotel. 
The hotel itself is near Union Square, and also near Market St. It's also within a longish walk to the Marina. There are many bus lines close by, and of course the Muni Rail and BART on Market St. The California and Powell cable car lines are also nearby. There are also a lot of restaurant and cafe options. I will definitely stay here again the next time I'm in San Francisco and need a hotel room. I wish I could give this hotel a 4.5 star rating.

title: “Avoid it if possible”
text:
Don't be fooled by the low price. The rooms have a nice set-up, but service is lame, especially if you need something. A BIG negative is the internet service-very poor signal if you could get it at all. The staff gave a variety of lame excuses-said they had ordered sme new parts that would be installed tomorrow, then 'my manager said' you should call the 800 # on the card. I didn't have one-she said she'd call her manager again and get it.
Still haven't heard back form her at this point!
The TV remote did not work; was told someone would come reprogram it. After awhile I went downstairs, and they gave me a new one to try. Still would not work, so I asked them to fix it this morning. They said someone would come to my room and reprogram it.
Didn't happen.
My room had soap but no shampoo-was told to come down to the desk to get some. I travel alot and can put up with quite a bit-this is definite a 'never again' location for me.

title: “Great Comfort and Value”
text: We stayed for one night to go to a Saturday Husky Game. The rooms were modern, clean and comfortable with competive pricing. I would definitely stay there again.

title: “Beautiful Hotel”
text:
Do not listen to the negative reviews of this hotel. 
My boyfriend and I are from New York City-home to the pickiest people in the country, and we LOVED this hotel. I've stayed at tons of hotels in my time, and this was by far one of the nicest. I booked the room last minute, and paid $179. All my requests that I stated on the online reservation form were kindly met by the man at the front desk: a non-smoking room, king size bed, away from the elevator. I had also requested a high floor and I was given a room on 17- which is not only the highest floor, but also the concierge level. The bed was very comfortable, with many pillows and a down comforter (my favorite). The bathroom was immaculate, and the shower even had a "rain" shower head. To our surprise there was even a couch and coffee table in the room. The balcony overlooked the pool- yet another pleasant surprise. The pool area was spacious and and the pool itself was huge. There was also a hot tub big enough for about 10 people, and a fountain on the opposite side. The grounds around the pool area, as well as the rest of the hotel, were beautifully manicured. The restaurant has indoor and outdoor seating.
The only drawback was the service was a little slow and food pretty average (although we only ate breakfast there). 
I would highly reccommend this hotel, and I intend to stay here again the next time I am in San Diego.

title: “Nice sized room but worn carpet and non-working coffee maker.”
text: I stayed here on business. The room was nicely sized and comfortable although the bath was tiny. The carpet seemed worn and stained. In the morning, I was disappointed to find that the coffee maker did not work. I called the service number (inaptly named something like Instant Service) twice but it was busy both times.

title: “Well priced, central location, nice pool”
text: Good price and comfortable for children. Fun pool and jacuzzi. Ease of breakfast buffet great for kids. Cris at front desk was very helpful.

title: “Beautiful Hotel - Incredible Service”
text:
A beutiful hotel - great rooms/beds (very comfortable)/well appointed, great amenities, very clean - but that's not rare - there are a lot of hotels that do these things well - create the right environment and have good service. This hotel has GREAT service - friendly, well-informed, helpful, excellent problem solving, responsive...I could go on. Beds are super comfortable, you even have a choice of pillows. The restaurant and bar are great as well, delicious, creative, well-executed food. Wish there were a few more appetizer options. Also wish that there was a fitness center - but as a whole - this place is top-notch.
I was traveling for business, but this makes a great tourist hotel as well!

title: “almost a 4 star”
text:
The biggest issue in the reviews seems to be centered around the star rating for this hotel. I truly believe that if it had a recognised brand name attached to it there would be little debate over this being rated 4 star based on its amenities. A large lobby welcoming you with fruit-infused water and fresh fruit, beautifully furnished and decorated, friendly and knowledgeable desk clerks, a concierge and valet parking. The room was large, extremely clean, well appointed with a desk and ergonomic chair, bedside tables, dresser, reading chair- and though the furnishings may have been slightly dated, they were quality pieces. Flat panel TV. Bed linens were clean and crisp, large fluffy towels and spa quality soap, shampoo, conditioner, and lotion provided in single use dispensers. Gormet coffee and teas with an in-room coffee maker. Iron/board and hairdryer in working order. Room service was available and there was a restaurant on site. The bar was very inviting, lively, not overpriced. These are the things that I feel classify a hotel in the four star range. There were a few areas that needed refreshed- the carpet and wallpaper in the hallways of some floors had seen better days; there was some rust around the drain in the shower; minor chips in the vanity, but I find that to be just normal wear and tear in a busy hotel.
Self-parking in a connected garage was $18, an average parking fee for the city. The location is not in the center of downtown, but It certainly is within a mile or so walking distance to Mass Ave, the zoo, the canal and some downtown attractions, without having the central downtown price tag. (example, from hotel to Murat Theatre was a pleasant 20 min walk.) I would stay at this hotel again and recommend it to others.

title: “Great Stay”
text: Best Western Sunset Suites is a great place to stay when in San Antonio. The room was clean, location great and Ashley upfront helped us with trolley passes, and finding all there was to do in SA.

title: “Fun place to stay on girls trip!”
text: We stayed at The W Hotel Times Square during the US Open in September 2010 and again in September 2011. Although the rooms are small, we weren't in them very much, but they were spacious enough for two women. Room was fully equipped with anything we needed. We ordered room service one night and their menu was easy and service was fast! Receptionists were very cordial - and we thought the price was great the first time we stayed in 2010 - thus the reason we stayed there again in 2011. If you're going to the US Open, it's an easy walk to Times Square, then catch the train to the courts. Also very close to Broadway and to shows and to amazing restaurants. No complaints here..... I'm sure we'll be staying at the W Hotel again for the US Open 2012!

title: “Peabody was beautiful!”
text:
Our overall stay was lovely in this historic hotel of the South. Others have commented on how small the rooms were, but please remember this building is over 75 yrs old and back then beds and people were smaller. The renovation done in 2002 has made the Peabody a wonderful place to stay. The beds were sumptuous and the bathroom was nicer than mine at home. Albeit small, the Kohler sink and granite countertop were beautiful. The towels were thick and soft. Shower pressure is great! 
 My husband and I had two problems: a) Check-in: room was not ready when we arrived at 6pm and b) Concierge: this person changed frequently and upon asking for a good seafood restaurant, she directed us to a suburban stripmall and said, "I personally would not recommend anything." We're from Chicago and get great seafood, the Peabody is on the Mississippi and I found it difficult to believe not one restaurant had good fish on the menu.

title: “Great First Night”
text: This was a pleasant surprise for an airport hotel. The facilities were first class and the breakfast was fantastic. Service and staff were very professional.

title: “Very good hotel”
text:
This is a small and cosy hotel. The staff was welcoming and smiling, the bed was amazing, the address in Upper east - I guess that's an individual thing (I prefer to be situated on the lower manhattan), but it's new york city .. use the Subway. stayed in room 42, going on to the street - no real noise to speak of.. great! and no overwhelming view either.. :/
With all the positive words I have to say, I must mention that I got this for $130 a day at quickbook. If I'd had to pay total price I'd gone somewhere else :)

title: “Quiet resort with perfect grounds”
text:
I was here for a convention and the best part of this hotel is the Griffin Club! It is well worth it - I ate breakfast there every morning, lunch most of the days and drinks and snacks at night. I only went out to dinner once on property and it just didn't compare to the food at the Griffin Club. They have an awesome coffee machine that makes all sorts of coffee - black, cappuccino, lattes, hot chocolate, etc. All of the other convention attendees were in line at Starbucks and I had my to-go cup from the Griffin Club!
The grounds are pretty - I was on east coast time so it was easy to get up before sunrise and walk around the golf course before the first tee time. I saw a coyote one morning when I was walking and then you see lots of rabbits all over. The water is an odd turquoise/artificial blue and that was weird to me - but you are in the desert!
The hotel is way out of town - it was a $70 cab ride. But on my way back into town I stopped at Hertz to rent a car (I was staying a few extra days in town for fun at a different hotel) and I returned the car to the Phoenix airport. I did visit Taliesin West and the tour was great - but I am a huge Frank Lloyd Wright Fan. 
Also part of the Griffin Club was daily use of the spa pool. It was very quiet and the padded chairs are wonderful. They are constantly coming around to refill your water. I ate two snack meals here as well as some of the juice and smoothie items. They were great! There is a women only outdoor shower right by the outside entrance to the ladies locker room. I would go back to this hotel just to stay at this pool for a few days!
The room was average and quiet. It was a little dirty when I checked in - I found a comb and hairs on the floor in the bathroom.

title: “well maintained, clean, and everything I expected”
text: The staff was also friendly and helpful in addition to the entire facility being very well maintained and spotlessly clean,

title: “Loved it”
text: I'll make it short. Loved the hotel, the rooms the restaurants and the location. A bit costly but it's worth it.

title: “jewel of a hotel in the middle of hollywood”
text: We stayed at the Hollywood Celebrity Hotel for 8 days and found it to be absolutely wonderful. It's a small hotel, only 38 total rooms, but the ammenities were perfect for us. Comfortable room with small kitchen area and dressing area. The location of this hotel was fantastic, right behind the Kodak and Grauman Chinese theaters - just one block from Hollywood boulevard. Right next to the Hollywood Highland Center which has lots of restaurants and shopping. Also very close to the major highways - so getting around was very easy. They even have a small parking lot behind the building which is FREE (a rarity in this area). We felt completely safe walking around day and night. You will NOT find a cleaner, more comfortable hotel with the most amazingly wonderful staff at these reasonable rates in this area!!

title: “Beautiful location, however mixed review..”
text: We stayed in a nice room overlooking the beautiful green grass the the bay. On a positive note, it was just a one minute stroll to the beautiful bay and the rooms were nice and comfortable. However, only got one tea bag. When I called for more milk and sugar, they took 45 minutes to deliver some more. Note - they will charge you for everything here - $28 to park your car yourself per night (not even valet parking!!) and the food is waaay overpriced for what it was. Also, the business centre is expensive to use.

title: “Hipster hotel in a terrific neighborhood”
text: What was once obviously an old hotel is seeing new life as a cool, hip, boutique hotel. The rooms are appointed with funky furnishings - no closet and a big red lip nightlight built in to the bathroom mirror. There is no coffee maker in the room, rather it is delivered in a thermos stapled inside a brown paper bag. That said, the coffee is good -- strong and hot. And the room is comfortable. Breakfast, served in the lobby, includes a nice assortment of breads, scones, hard boiled eggs, fruit and yogurt. The service is top notch. We asked the front desk to move us when we realized we were located next to a bachelorette party. They did so without hesitation. We had no issues with noise thereafter. All in all, our experience was positive. With the deal we got on parking, the level of service, the fun room and fhe decent breakfast, this place was a value.

title: “Hotel Metro - fabulous hotel”
text:
I just wanted to email you to thank all the staff at the Hotel Metro for making our holiday so wonderful. It was so kind of you to leave the water and chocolates for Victoria to celebrate her birthday – she really enjoyed them and it was a lovely touch.
It was our first visit to New York and we couldn’t have stayed anywhere nicer!
We will definitely be returning and will be recommending your hotel to anyone we know who is travelling to New York.
Kindest Regards and many thanks (special thanks to Matthew – font of all knowledge!!)

title: “Nice, but pretentious”
text:
This was our second stop in Memphis; we had booked for two nights.
You usually know what to expect with Westin hotels, but this time I have to say I was quite disappointed.
Location is great, just one block from Beale street - although do make sure to get a room on the other side of the building if you plan to get some sleep!
The hotel itself looks great, brand new, very clean. The rooms are very nice, too, pretty spacious, and beds are comfortable.
You can pretty much hear anything going on in the corridors though, and we were awakened a couple of times by people coming back to their room late, loud, after a few drinks on Beale Street.
The big let-down was service / attitude of the staff / hotel policies.
First, the person who checked us in wasn't nice at all. No smile, no welcome look. We didn't feel welcome at all, and had the same feeling all along our stay.
What to say about the mini-bar policy? 
All the items are on a scale, and if you touch something, it will be charged to your room directly. 
From a customer perspective, either the hotel thinks I'm a thief and I'll try to take stuff from the mini bar without telling them (which feels pretty insulting) or they're trying to charge me for services / products I'm not using (i.e if something falls from the scale, you'll be charged even though you haven't used it).
I've never seen anything like this, and I hope not to see it again!
Service wasn't really good: we would see trays of food left in the corridors, that would stay there all day. 
Everytime we tried to get the car out of the parking, we had to wait several minutes, because you need to show your hotel parking ticket to someone... but no one is ever there. People wouldn't even say hi or thank you.
When you add this to the fact that everything is extra at Westin hotels (i.e parking not included, breakfast not included, internet access not included, even bottles of water in the room are not free), the whole experience comes out quite overpriced for what you get.
The only smile we got from anyone in the hotel was upon check-out.
Overall, this is a hotel trying really hard to make you feel like it's a privilege for you to be here, when it's normally the other way round. Being high-end is not about looking down on your own customers. 
I think there's a big management issue here.
I will personally not stay there again, and do recommend other hotels in Memphis instead of this one (i.e River Inn in Harbor town, much better value and service)

title: “OK with a few problems”
text:
We just got back from 4 days and 3 nights at the Renaissance Washington DC and was a little disapointed in our stay. The hotel is OK... but only OK. I think the hotel would be good for business travelers, traveling alone. We went as a family and experienced several problems. First, when we checked in only one room was ready and we were told that the other room would be ready in a few minutes and we would be called when it was complete. We were never called. After a couple of hours we checked with the front desk and the room was still not ready. Again, we were told that it would be just a few minutes. One hour later, I stopped by the front desk and was able to get a key. This was at 6:30 in the evening. The valets were a consistent problem throughout our stay. It took close to an hour to get our car when they were not that busy. Also, the staff in the fitness area were very rude and not welcoming to myself and my children. The Concierge staff was not very helpful. I asked about the Cherry Blossom festival and was told that it had been going on for a month, (even though it actually started that weekend) and the staff had NO information. Kind of suprised that a Concierge staff for such a large hotel would not have written information about events associated with the festival. It was reported that several thousand visitors came to Washington for the event. Also, I asked the Concierge for dining recommendations and was told that Tony & Joes was a great place for a family. How wrong they were. They had no childrens menu. We were forced to pay between 20 & 30 dollars a piece for a 7 and 10 year old. Not so bad but the food was sub par. I would definately not recommend Tony and Joes for ANYBODY and especially not a family. 
I would recomend that the hotel purchase a computer for the Concierge desk and allow for quick printing of directions and recomendations. 
We chose this hotel from previous reviews of service. Unfortunately we did not receive such service. It was a busy weekend but the staff was not interested in our satisfaction. 
On the good side,... the breakfast buffet was great and reasonably priced. The maid service was always friendly and competent. The rooms were very clean... just small. The Starbucks was very convenient. 
All in all the trip was great as DC is a great place to spend a few days seeing the sites and having fun with the family. However, we will not be going back to the Renaissance Washington DC. Not a terrible place but not worth spending hard earned money on.

title: “No Problems”
text:
No complaints! Our room (which we spent very little time in - too much to do!) was pleasant, clean and spacious and only a little bit dated. Aircon worked fine and ceiling fan. Iron and ironing board handy in each room. Room was well serviced each day. Bed was huge with giant pillows which i found a bit uncomfortable but usually so tired slept ok anyway! Jacuzzi good but only had time to use once. Step over into shower may prove problem for older/disabled people.
Lobby/staff of hotel pleasant, friendly and helpful. Free use of computer and internet in lobby very useful.
Breakfast good - lots of choice and best of all free. Also free dinner which we werent around for but good option if budget conscious. Supermarket next door very handy and has EVERYTHING! Ice maker great for evening tipple!
We found location good - pretty central to everything we wanted to see. Taxis seemed reasonable and drivers friendly. Parking wasnt a problem at hotel.

title: “Excellent breakfast”
text:
I was very pleased with this hotel. The reception was cordially, the room was very clean and confortable, the parking was OK and the breakfast was great.
No complaints.

title: “Hidden Gem”
text: Wanted something close to Chase Field without spending alot - We arrived early, we were able to check in - staff was friendly and even gave us a cold bottle of water. Room was clean and spacious - bed was comfortable. Outstanding value.

title: “Second Stay.”
text:
This is the second time that my family has stayed here in the last 8 months and I will still recommend this hotel.
Here are the pros: Courteous, helpful staff; clean accommodations; very good breakfast; comfortable dining area; convenient downtown location; reasonable price; just an overall quality place.
A few cons: There is still a large construction project going on on the north side of the hotel and still many months from completion. If your room is on that side of the building the noise cranks up early in the morning and it can be very annoying. If you book a room be sure to book one with odd numbers (Riverwalk side). Also, the parking garage is nice to have but beware of your vehicle height because the overhead clearance is only 6'6". The parking spaces are also very narrow and the garage itself is simply very cramped. Not necessarily a deal-breaker, but something you should know.

title: “Take the METRO, room to spread out!”
text: Traveling with 2 teens and a pre-teen was no problem when we were able to spread out and relax in our large suite after a long day sightseeing. We took the metro to Foggy Bottom from Reagan airport and walked the 5-7 blocks to the hotel and never had to worry about a car or parking. The hotel is 10-12 minute walk from either Foggy Bottom or Dupont Circle metro. We preferred Dupont Circle because walk was more residential. Many brick townhomes and trees line street, felt safe! Hotel also within 15 minute walk of Georgetown shopping and restaurants, a plus! Hotel was very clean, staff friendly and hard working, pool nice and clean but a bit on the small side. Free breakfast was convenient albeit the long lines. Only negative is mattresses were very hard and some in our party had stiff backs or necks a few mornings. If hotel could change this, it would be an A+++ experience!

title: “Great hotel right outside downtown.”
text: We stayed here for two nights to celebrate our anniversary. While the hotel decor and amenities are nothing too special, the rooms were very nice, clean, and comfortable. We were very happy with our stay for the price we paid. Also, we used the shuttle 5 or 6 times in two days... it was very prompt and the drivers were very friendly. They even picked us up at the market and took us to the Underground Tour location. Saved us a lot of headache from trying to find parking! I would definitely recommend this hotel and would likely stay here again.

title: “Le Parker Meridien Very Niuce”
text: Great property .. great location ... the Burger Joint at Le Parker Meridien,just off the Lobby, is Killer !!! When you see 30 people standing in line to get a Cheeseburger and Fries ... it's GOOOD !!! So easy to get to anything in NYC from Le Parker Meridien ... location, location, location

title: “Great Business Hotel”
text:
Great Location just off Union Square - with the cable cars (Powell Street) just steps away from the front door. There are two sections - the Old section with smaller - older rooms, and the new section with very up to date - well decorated rooms. I stayed in the new section. Only weird thing is that the two halves don't interface well. To get to the new section - you go down two long hallways - up stairs or a platform lift - to the pool, then into the new building with elevators. The Lobby is in the old section - on the first floor. The new section elevators go to the 2nd floor if you wish to backtrack to the lobby, or the parking garage is on the first floor of the new building. It will make sense when you navigate it a couple of times. The new rooms are excellent - new, and well decorated. Coffee maker & Ironing board - Flat screen TV - Internet service is good.
Many of the reviews refer to the EXCELLENT Breakfast in the "Daily Grill." Some guests get free vouchers for breakfast there. The breakfast was good - although most options were 3 egg - and I'm not always that hungery. So my rating is: EXCELLENT if you got it free - GOOD if you didn't. Staff is good. New Area had good business type desk/chair in the room. WILL stay here again.

title: “Absolutely fabulous!”
text:
We loved the room, the view, and everything about our stay (except perhaps the price : )
It made our mother's day stay with my young daughters perfect!
There is a rotating restaurant on top. Again really cool, but quite pricey. this is a great location to stay and feel like you really are "doing" New York city. Within walking distance to the Rockefeller, American girl, etc.
We loved our view facing south looking down at the downtown financial disctrict, particularly at night. We even had a glimpse of the river. It was so pretty, we left the drapes open all night to admire the view from our bed.

title: “Good Value-Good Price”
text: We stayed at the Residence Inn over Labor Day week end, and although it was very busy, the hotel handled the traffic just fine. Opt for a room rather than a suite if you would like, as it is huge with a kitchenette, et al. It's a better value than the one bedroom, unless you have more than two people staying there. Breakfast is included and you are walking distance to shopping and the Inner Harbor.

title: “Absolutely disgusting and dirty hotel! Go elsewhere!”
text: I booked into the Hyatt Islandia in order to attend a one-day seminar. Why did I book at a Hyatt--because it is a Hyatt! I thought I would have a little relaxation and treat myself; however, when I arrived the hotel was under MAJOR construction. The reception area appeared to be "make-shift"; I had to walk down the outside portside area about 200 yards to find a "hole" in the construction fence in order to access the elevator, which was by the service entrance. I went up to the 12th floor and arrived in my room. The room overlooked construction and rows of garbage dumpsters that were overflowing. I wanted to read--the light by the couch did not work. I turned on all of the lights in the room in order to do some written work I had to complete, and looked at the couch. It was FILLED with stains. I opened up the middle drawer of the dresser to put some clothes away, and found a dirty napkin and food in the drawer! My eyes were drawn to the carpet by the bed--it, too, was filled with large stains. That made me take a look at the bedspread (that had been turned down). The bedspread was not only covered in stains, it had large areas of encrusted chunky material embedded in it! I took all sorts of photos with my cell phone camera, stormed down to the manager, and demanded my money back. They were nice, although a bit hesitant--until I showed them the photos. Then they were willing to give me anything I wanted. What I wanted was to never stay in a hotel again. I drove the 2 1/2 hours home, arrived at 3:15 in the morning, and was soooo happy to be away from that filthy place. I have sent a letter and a copy of the photos to the Hyatt Corporation, and the Health Department in San Diego. Even though I prepaid through Priceline, my money was refunded in full; according to Priceline, it was due to the extenuating circumstances" of my visit. I have NEVER experienced anything like this in a hotel before, and there is NO excuse for it.

title: “Great hotel right at the airport”
text: This hotel is so convenient, especially if you have an early morning flight out. The rooms are very clean! A very nice place to stay. I would definitely return again! The only problem I had was that the cokes in the vending machine are $3.75. The pool was very cold but the hot tub was just right!

title: “Good for the price.”
text: Room was clean, small- cozy. Can't say much bad because the location was perfect! The price was half of those around us (using Priceline name your price) so I would come back. Downsides.... Rooms were small and a little out dated so if your looking for your five star huge room this is not it, if your looking for a clean place to sleep at night- perfect. Walls were thin so we did hear more then we wanted from the neighbors, I may bring ear plugs next time, and no refridgerator in room which was a downfall. Though overall good for the price and close to everything! The diner downstairs is one of the cheapest we found for breakfast - vs. some places next door being $50 + for breakfast for 2. Also they do provide shampoo, soap, hair dryer... Sum it up... Clean/cheap/location/small/old

title: “Best Hotel Experience”
text: I stayed at the Algonquin for 2 nights in December 2004. I love this hotel. I was expecting small rooms without a view, and I have no memory of its "better days" so I was not at all disappointed. Beautiful lobby, cozy and luxurious, helpful and friendly staff, convenient and inexpensive parking across the street. The place is drenched in modern literary history which appealed to me immensely. Perfect location for me, close to everywhere I wanted to go. I loved hanging out in the lobby lounge, drinking $15 cocktails (little steep) people watching and chatting with friends, or surfing the internet on my wireless laptop. I was a little out of place as a young guy, most guests were gentrified older couples, but everyone was friendly. Downside, our waiter was a little dismissive of me as he served my sister and I our delicious $150 dinner in the roundtable room. Perhaps I shouldnt have opened the sideboard cabinet to take a peek at what was inside, but it was right next to my seat, within arm's length, and I couldnt help myself. Huge stack of pressed white tablecloths, so you know.

title: “Good hotel, just a bit pricey”
text:
I haven't stayed in a NYC hotel in a while since my brother finally got an apartment of his own. No more roommates and frat-like atmosphere and hygiene - thank goodness. I just stayed here one night as we were evicted from my bro's apt when my parents arrived to squat in his apt for a couple of weeks.
Overall, a good hotel. It's actually right around the corner from my brother's apt and provides easy access to several train lines; in particular, the E train which will take you straight to the Air Train to JFK. The location may not be ideal for first -time NYC visitors as it's not in within walking distance to all the major sights, but for us it was perfect. The area actually does have a good number of restaurants nearby you just have to walk around or use Yelp to find the good ones. We went to a couple of cute French resturants that were nearby. Also close are Duane Read and a few other grocery stores.
The rooms were clean and large (by NYC standards). It's a very busy hotel and I paid more than I've ever paid for any hotel in my life! The shower did have mildew which is a huge peeve of mine. The best was so nice and comfy. I noticed lots of families coming in and out of this place so I imagine it's great for families - it was just me and the BF though.
The front desk staff were fine - not overly friendly or rude.
My main reasons for staying here were that it's close to my bro's apt and across the street from the E train so I was happy with my stay. I'd stay here again at a cheaper rate, but doubt I would stay here again paying the rate I did for one night. I'm just too frugal :)

title: “Good location but just fair accomodations.”
text:
Wife and I stayed for a week and although we found the location to be convenient to the Metro, Georgetown, and most of the sites, we were mixed about the rest of the hotel. My wife was attracted to the hotel based on the style of the building and reviews she read. We didn't have a problem with the elevator as some, but we found the maid service to be completely inconsistent. Turn down one night and none the next. Face towels and soap one day, none the next. Bed was a little uncomfortable for us and the street noise was loud enough to wake us several times a night, maybe 3 nights out of our 7. This really didn't happen until half way through our stay so we didn't bother changing. The room we had (9th floor) was on the smallish side. There was no in-room safe as we would have liked to have had since we had our laptop for the free wired internet, which came in very handy.
On the plus side, we had a nice experience with one of the hotel desk clerks. Very helpful in pointing out areas of DC to visit that were off the "tourist track" and even phoned his girlfriend to help us find her favorite sushi restaurant, which happened to be just down the street. We also had a good experience with ordering dessert via room service. Although we didn't try the hotel restaurant, if the desserts were any indication of the food being served, it would have been a nice place to eat. 
If we're to visit again, we'd probably opt to try somewhere else.

title: “Classy but with flaws”
text:
Why classy??
 * Great location: 
 * Just a couple of blocks from Central Park
 * Very close to the Metros which will get you anywhere you want to go
 * Staff was outstanding: always willing and able to take care of any needs. Very responsive.
 * Hotel room:
 * Room was quite large.
 * Bed was very comfortable
 * Kitchenette was nice plus
Why flaws?? 
Given the price of the hotel, I would have expected 5+ star quality in all areas and it was good but not great.
 * Rooms are somewhat dated and could use some upgrading.
 * Bathroom plumbing: drains in sink and tub were very slow to drain. Had to finally call maintenance to come and work on them. They finally got them to flow.
 * Hallway carpet: hallway carpet on at least two of the floors seemed to be dirty. Certainly not up to the standard expected.

title: “Great customer service!”
text:
Was stranded in Charlotte due to flight cancellation-very friendly front desk staff on check-in and esp. upon departure. 
Very comfy beds & pillows, blanket throw for the large sofa is a nice touch.
Very small shower area, didn't eat the breakfast but liked the Starbucks coffee.
Only complaint was the very high room cost since I checked in close to midnight and checked out at 7:15 am

title: “Wedding Weekend of Perfection!”
text:
When my husband and I started planning our wedding we had some definite ideas about the type of event we wanted. Our number one priority was for EVERYONE to have an amazing time. We knew we wanted it at a hotel so that our guests could be located in a central place for the entire weekend. We had lots of people traveling for the event and didn't want to burden them with lots of trips around the city, etc. Reasons we picked Doubletree Southpark:
- Their rates (for rooms and catering) were exceptional compared to others that we looked at.
- The location is amazing, literally steps from Southpark Mall. Very few people went anywhere in their car after arriving at the hotel.
- All of the rooms are suites. This was great for family to visit with each other without having to be draped over beds and crammed in together.
- The tent in the courtyard is gorgeous. Just the right ambiance for our simple ceremony.
- The whole hotel has lots of character and feels very upscale.
- The event coordinators (John and Natalie) were so attentive and thorough (especially compared to another hotel we looked at).
- Hotel bar, for the "after party." (We said we wanted our guests to have fun!)
So, it was a pretty easy decision to hold our wedding here. We decided to hold our ceremony in the Garden Pavillion (tent in courtyard) and the reception in the Ballroom.
After the fact:
- The staff went above and beyond for every aspect of the event. My friends, family and I didn't have to lift a finger the day of the wedding. The hotel did all decorating and even did more than I expected. The cake was even ordered through them so I didn't have to worry about that. (And a little shout-out to Ella, our private waitress during the reception...I've never seen someone that loved her job so much!)
- Natalie helped with the rehearsal and made sure everything flowed smoothly the night of the wedding. It was so great to have someone do all that so we could all have so much fun.
- The food (and cake) was delicious!
- They had two bartenders for our group. I don't think anyone had to wait long for a drink!
- Warm cookies at check-in. :)
- Gave my parents a much deserved room upgrade.
- Most people said they had no problem sleeping. (I was too pumped to sleep!)
- Other things I'm probably forgetting... Just filled with amazing memories from the weekend.
A few "negatives" (though nothing so bad):
- The hotel is HUGE and a bit confusing. It's a giant square with an interior courtyard. I think we could all find our way from the lobby to our rooms by the end of the weekend...
- The hotel is showing its age a bit, but I believe they are renovating. Beds were comfortable, flat screen TVs in the living rooms and bedrooms, everything seemed clean.
- Would be nice if they had a shuttle from the airport.
- A few issue with "mystery" charges on our credit card. They are all being resolved though.
Overall, I was totally blown away by the Doubletree. Truly made our day special and enjoyable.

title: “Awesome Experience!”
text: What a wonderful hotel! The staff were all friendly and helpful, the room was spacious (even though some reviews say rooms are small...we only reserved a basic size) and it was very clean and comfortable. The location was fabulous...within walking distance to much of Chicago. The Chicago Marathon happened the Sunday of our trip. Even though the hotel was very busy, the service remained great. I would definitely recommend this hotel to others and I will certainly be back. Loved it!!

title: “A light in the hurricane darkness...”
text:
Once grand now faded hotel which sadly needs a major facelift - rooms are large/beds comfy but the furniture is very spartan and old fashioned - not even a kettle. I was there in days following Hurricane Sandy and hotel very full and one day one no heat or hot water so lots of pressure on the service.... but no real excuse for the requests to concierge and housekeeping which just never happened....
That said the receptionists were exceptional and any hotel should be proud to offer the treatment I received - tired and tearful at 1am having found my hotel was closed by Sandy - despite being full Carolyn the night receptionist found me a room and the following day her colleague Elizabeth again worked to find two very nice rooms for me and friends all meeting for a 60th birthday weekend - they were wonderful and shining lights in the darkness of that particular hour - thank you both - and well done Park Central!

title: “Great value for accomodations in midtown Manhattan”
text:
We live nearby and occasionally stay in Manhattan to see a couple of shows, a museum or two and have a nice dinner. We prefer stay in the theatre distict.The room rates are quite expensive but if you shop well, you can find a bargain. The Fairfield Inn is on the cusp of the theatre district between 8th and 9th Avenune. Since we frequent Marriott hotels, this was a no brainer. 
We checked in at 11 AM on Saturday. If they didn't have a room available we could have checked our grip and be on our way. Room was small but normal for Manhattan. (We've stayed in some really small rooms in Manhattan but lets face it, you're here for the sights. You sleep in your room). The room was laid out well with everything you needed. Bedding was fine. The room was clean. The bathroom is small with a nice glass enclosed shower instead of a bath tub. The door to the bathroom has milk glass but is fine unelss you are extremely modest. This wasn't an issue at all. Towels were nice and fluffy for a Fairfield Inn. Elevators were a tad slow but again, this is NY. Our 31st floor room had a view of the Empire State Building if you leaned to the right. Again, this is NY with lots of tall buildings. In any hotel, you usually get a view of a building across the street or an air shaft. It's just the way it is in Manhattan. Breakfast was fine. In fact better than the usual Fairfield Inn breakfasts you find in other hotels. 
As for food, there is no restaurant in the hotel since Fairfield Inn's don't have restaurants but you won't go hungry. You are a couple of short blocks to the theatre district and restaurant row. However, my wife and I go to 9th Avenue and walk north where there are dozens of restaurants of every ethincity including Thai, Indian, Turkish, Italian, Greek, French and the list goes on. This is where the New Yorkers eat. You won't go wrong here. Face it. You didn't come to New York to eat in Applebys or Baba Gumps. 
As for location, you next to the Port Authority Bus Terminal, and a half a block from the 42nd St subway station. We came by public transportation but if you come by car they have a deal with a parking garage two doors away for around $28 for 24 hours. In this part of Manhattan, the norm is at least $40 and no garage offers in and out privliges. Remember, this is New York and not Omaha. Besides, if you go anywhere in Manhattan you use public transportation or a cab as there is no place to park.
Their breakfast room doubles as a bar after 5 PM that has all the appeal of an institution. If you want to have a cocktail before going out to dinner, take a walk and find your new favorite place and skip this place.
We'll be back in a few weeks. You won't go wrong here.

title: “Loved it”
text: Great room with a balcony and in in the heart of Venice. We walked down the boardwalk all the way to Venice, came back and had a drink on their great rooftop bar. The rooftop was slammed with a bunch of "cool kids" but after telling them we were staying in the hotel they moved us to the front of the line, drank some delicious margaritas and watched the sunset. 10/10 would stay again!

author.location: New York, New York, United States

title: “Constistently excellent”
text: I have stayed at this hotel many times and it always meets my expectations. The rooms are comfortable, the staff is helpful and friendly and the location is excellent. I will definitely stay there again.

title: “The Surrey – style over substance and service”
text:
After obsessively reviewing TripAdvisor, we chose the Surrey for the last leg of our four week US holiday - our first visit to New York. Six months prior we booked an Ultra Deluxe Salon with a king bed, for seven nights for late June. We checked out after four nights. 
When booking we’d selected the option of an eStandby Upgrade to an Ultra Deluxe Terrace Suite and hoped that this would be available. A day or two before arrival I sent an email request regarding reservations at Café Boulud and the Spa. At check-in reception seemed unaware of these various requests, so firstly I asked about the e-upgrade, which was airily dismissed as being highly unlikely. I was advised we could upgrade to a terrace-less suite, but I explained that we really wanted the terrace and the Ultra Deluxe Salon has a terrace. I was then told (I felt as a pressure to upgrade) that the Ultra Deluxe Salon I’d reserved might not have a terrace, at which point I became quite concerned and was then hastily advised that our reserved room DID have a terrace. Reception knew nothing about our other email requests, and these were referred to the concierge. Our room wasn’t ready, so reception suggested we wait in the bar. Having just arrived at the hotel I had to ask where it was. Overall check-in was not welcoming or helpful.
We had a drink in the comfortable bar, and were then shown to our room, which was gorgeous. On the 16th floor, the room was amazingly airy and light, with huge windows leading to our terrace with awesome views of the city and central park. The décor and design were really beautiful. The bathroom with a double sink, deep bath and spacious shower, also had plenty of storage space for cosmetics and skincare items, and a good make-up mirror. The water pressure to our room was quite weak, which diminished the luxury of the beautiful shower. The bed is very comfortable, and beautifully made up. Oddly, there is only one bedside control for room lighting so that one person cannot turn on their own bedside lamp. The minibar/wardrobe area is quite dark, you may need a torch to see into the wardrobe.
On arrival I unsuccessfully searched for a directory to the room/hotel, and rang guest services to check on this. I was dismissively told that the hotel had only opened in November 2009, and hadn’t yet put together a directory. I asked if it was possible to get an in-room electric kettle (to make tea) – the person seemed annoyed and exclaimed that they’d never had such a request, and she would get back to me (she never did). There was no in-room information about mini-bar contents or pricing, and no information/bags for laundry or dry cleaning. 
We found the biggest flaw is the hotel’s dining service (or lack thereof). For us ordering room service after a long day’s sight-seeing is part of our holiday experience. There seemed to be real communication problems between hotel staff and the Café Boulud regarding menu items and their timely delivery. 
There is a small room service menu based on Café Boulud’s current menu, perhaps 4 or 5 main courses. On our second night we ordered a room service dinner. Shortly after ordering 2 main courses we received a phone call advising that one of our choices wasn’t available, and so we chose an alternative dish. Thirty minutes later we received another call advising that our second choice wasn’t available either, so we ended up ordering two of the same dish. Another hour later we finally received our room service meal, which was unimpressive for the cost. The hotel acknowledged the inconvenience by not charging us for a half bottle of wine, but this did not make up for our ruined evening
When ordering breakfast the person taking the order was invariably unfriendly. I am not sure that the front desk people had a copy of the menu given the number of problems we had with ordering. For example, our last morning I ordered smoked salmon with a bagel from the breakfast menu, but no smoked salmon arrived. By then we had given up expecting professional service. 
Another night we visited the hotel’s rooftop garden for a cocktail and ordered a light meal. While the cocktail was great and the small garden delightful, our simple food took nearly an hour to arrive, the waitress apologizing profusely as we waited. Our meal was cold and lack-lustre. Further, our request for iced water on a hot New York night was politely repeated three times, but no water ever arrived.
Check-out was speedy and went without a hitch.
After we checked out, we waited in the lobby for a cab and overheard a detailed discussion between the front desk staff regarding storage of a new guest’s medication. She had asked that they refrigerate her medication pending her arrival the next day. Because the medication wouldn’t fit into her room’s mini-bar fridge, they decided to just put it in her room, with the air-conditioning turned down. Over-hearing this lack of care confirmed we were correct to check out early.
The Surrey is a good choice if your primary concern is a beautiful room and bathroom at a cost-effective rate compared to luxury hotels, provided that you down-grade your expectations regarding helpful or friendly service.

title: “great value!”
text: Two room layout works great for children, and everyone loves the breakfast. The staff was very friendly and helpful, and went above and beyond. The room was average (I would like to see more toddler-proof lock options) but the staff and extra amenities make it our top choice.

title: “Nice hotel but if youre after great service, dont bother!”
text: Stayed at the Barclay May 26 for 4 nights. Only two reception staff at check in, one of which was not exactly welcoming to say the least! Cant speak for the other. I asked for a room on a quieter side of the hotel (as per previous reviews) and we were upgraded to a king deluxe. Nice size room, smallish bathroom but nonetheless a good standard. We only had one dressing gown in the room and asked THREE times for another, when it finally arrived it was dirty. Also enquired about the limo service with concierge but the guy reluctantly gave us the information, he might aswell have said "you so cant afford it". Luckily we got a great rate from hotelanywhere but I would have been disappointed had I paid any more. All in all great base for exploring all NYC has to offer, a comfortable (bed v. comfy), smart hotel but just dont expect a hug when you arrive!. Stayed at the Radisson Lexington (over the street) previously and apart from the room and the lobby being nicer at the Barclay, no different really. Try Broadway Diner for breakfast, really nice food and cheaper and not as busy as Raffles can get across the street. (Out of hotel turn left onto Lexington, about 4 blocks on the left just past 51st st subway) Enjoy!

title: “Another disappointment”
text: Free internet access sessions in the lobby are limited to 45 mins; internet connection in the room is charged. Faster and unlimited free internet available at nearby coffee shop. Hotel charges to store luggage even for a few hours after check out. When my personal belongings were transferred by hotel staff to another room several items were lost & never recovered. Valet trousers returned with loose button that housekeeping provided a needle and cotton to fix as they would not sew it on securely. There were no envelopes, writing paper nor postcards in the room although there was a small notepad and pen provided. Not to mention the problem with the first room….Another disappointing experience.

title: “Beautiful Hotel”
text: My husband and I enjoyed a getaway weekend to the Adolphus. The hotel is absolutely gorgeous, the rooms are beautifully furnished, and it really is a magical place. The old world elegance is breathtaking compared to other modern looking hotels. We stayed in a very large junior suite.

title: “Don't Expect Much!”
text:
The Latham Hotel did not live up to it's reviews or the dollars spent. Our stay there was truly below average. If you're just looking for somewhere to lay your head with basic accomodations, this is the place for you. If you're looking to enjoy yourself away from home with a little luxury, this is not for you.
My husband and I visited Philadelphia for the 111th annual Penn Relays. We wanted to be near Franklin Field and close to shopping areas as well. So location was great, but the hotel is in need of serious renovations. Our plumbing was terrible and the rooms were tiny! 
Next year, we'll spend as much as we need to for a great hotel stay.

title: “Great Location”
text: Enjoyed our stay at the Edison Hotel. It is a great location, clean rooms and nicely renovated. The bathrooms are small but well equipped. The air condition did not cool the room as cool as we like it. The convenience of the cafe for breakfast is nice with quick service and a good breakfast menu.

title: “I've stayed in some great NYC hotels...this isn't one of them.”
text:
Ok, the hotel is cool and trendy, at least superficially. The decor is impressive; the deskclerk who checked me in was polite and professional; the bar was definately happening. Scarily though, the rooms are really, really small (and that's even by NYC standards! Hard to believe). There was a an asian fusion thing going on in the tiny room that was nice and I figured it would be fine for sleeping. 
Unfortunately sleep was the thing I didn't get. It was winter and the steam heat they use in the hotel makes a clanking that would wake the dead. When I called the front desk in the middle of the night they said I might have better luck with the heat off. It had been oppressively hot in the room and I had never turned the heat on. When I told them this they sent and "engineer" up to help. A half hour later when he came up the noise had stopped. He promised it would not be back. It returned about 15 minutes later. Since I wasn't sleeping I made my way to the vending machines. Apparently couples from the bar use the hallways as uh..."make out" spots to put it nicely. It was especially unpleasant as you could see the carpets were badly stained from some kind of leak, despite how DARK the halls are. Needless to say, I wasn't really in the mood for the atmosphere. I would have to recommend this hotel for very skinny party people who are either deaf or intoxicated enough to pass out despite the noise.

title: “Too far from centre”
text:
This hotel is in an area without restaurants or shops apart from one large supermarket about a quarter mile walk away. There is no restaurant in the hotel so you need to take the subway into town. Subway about a five minute walk away and four stops direct to Boston centre. The hotel itself has a Starbucks which also serves some food but it is very basic for such a large hotel. 
There is a small bar and nice lounge area in the lobby. Reception staff pleasant enough. The room we had faced the water which was nice. It was a fair size with two large queenbeds which were extremely comfortable. Coffee machine in room but no fridge or microwave. Room well serviced daily. The advantage of the hotel is that due to its location it is quiet and peaceful but be prepared to travel into town for restaurants and shopping.

title: “Two days ON THE BEACH”
text: I had a wonderful two days here, I agree with those who stayed longer...I wish I would have stayed an extra day, at least. The parking here is underground which is great-no street parking necessary. The desk personnel is very friendly and helpful. As a matter of fact the desk called shortly after I checked in to make sure everything was satisfactory. I believe his name was Matt. As it turned out I had done something plugging in the coffeemaker and the plug didn't work. He brought an extra coffee filter for me (since it was 4 or 5PM and I was already trying to make coffee); so that I would have a fresh pot for the morning and fixed the plug for me. I had a beautiful room on the beach (with a boardwalk in between) and a nice little patio so I could sit outside with coffee or a glass of wine & watch the spectacular sunsets along with the many, many surfers and of course skaters, joggers, bicyclists, and skateboarders. The room was spacious and clean & the bed was comfy with nice soft sheets. The lower patio areas have a fence all around which makes it very safe. I slept with the patio door open so I could go to sleep to the sound of the surf. and breathe fresh ocean air. The second night I was there it drizzled then rained all night. Still great. Continental breakfast was yummy, with a very nice wheat bread & little containers of peanut butter. I couldn't wait to get up have toast with peanut butter and delicious coffee and juice. The Firehouse restaurant & bar are a short walk across from the front door. There are a couple of pubs with outdoor eating areas and a 7-11 and a Ralph's within walking distance. One would never have to move the car.

title: “This was a great stay!”
text:
I recieved an E-mail from the customer service group at the Westin St. Francis. The best review I can give is to copy my response to their question about how our stay went.
Alison,
Very nice property, top notch staff and great location! We had a wonderful time. The front desk people were friendly and helpful with questions and the bartender on Saturday night mixed the best whiskey sour I have ever had and, without impugning my character here, I have had a few in my lifetime.
Thanks for checking!

title: “New Year's dud!”
text:
Our first room smelled bad, actually the whole floor smelled like a convalescent hospital. And, there was paint chipping off the ceiling! After switching rooms, we got something not much better. ( at least it wasn't smelly any more ) The ceiling in the bathroom was moldy and there was someone's hair stuck to the tile around the door which was there during our whole stay. (even though I mentioned it to the front desk - they never got back to me ) The room was extremely small with outdated furnishings & old carpet. We had asked for a king size bed but was told that the old tower didn't have any king size beds in it. We tried to upgrade our room, but was told they didn't have anything else available. Our stay was for 4 nights, but we wanted to go home after the first night as it was very noisy all night long. I guess the walls are really thin. The bathroom had no fan and no counter space. I had to put my personal stuff on the floor. There was a small window that was extremely hard to reach and open. I had to stand on the counter to budge it open. The heater also didn't work and just blew out cold air all night. To top it off, our key stopped working our last night there. Even after a replacement key, we had to keep calling security to open the door for us. I've stayed at westin hotels before and thought they were all very nice with the whole "heavenly" thing.
Basically, I think if you can't stay in the new towers which have renovated rooms, don't stay at all. The old towers is like a 2 star hotel.

title: “Great location, nice hotel, so-so service”
text:
My husband and I stayed at the Hotel Andra over Labor Day weekend. The location couldn't be better. 
The first night we were there, we stayed in the Andra Suite. The room was moderately spacious and well designed. The mini-bar was well stocked, but a price list was no where to be found. Room service was from Lola the restaurant in the lobby. The food was very good, and the prices were very high. Overall we had a great experience. 
We unexpectedly decided to stay at the hotel a second night. After our great experience the first night, we decided to save some money and get the smaller Andra Studio because we didn't think we'd mind a simple size change, we expected everything else to be of the same quality. I can tell you the room size was pretty much the only physical change, but the service the second night didn't reflect it's four star rating. First, the window didn't open. Now this isn't a big deal to us, but when we called the front desk to see if there was a trick to getting the window open (because the windows in the suite opened), the gentleman told us that it doesn't open because of fire code, and all the windows on that floor were sealed shut. I know that's not true because we had stayed on the same floor the night before. We didn't appreciate being lied to. Next, we went to turn on the TV. It didn't work. We checked the plug, it was fine.
