We called the front desk. They said they'd send someone up to check on it. Forty-five minutes later, a girl from the front desk arrived, announced that maintenance was unavailable and that she was going to check it out. She walked over to the TV, pressed the same power button we had tried and checked the same plug we had checked (just like we told her on the phone). After she was unsuccessful, she told us that she didn't know what was going on, and that she'd try to find maintenance. Another twenty minutes go by, and she calls to tell us that eminence wasn't working and wouldn't be until morning. I told her that was unacceptable because we had plans to stay in for the remainder of the night and were going to watch TV. I requested a new room with a working TV. She told me there were no rooms available and that we'd just have to wait until eminence arrived. I explained that I found it hard to believe that they were sold out all of a sudden, considering we had checked in two hours earlier and they had all kinds of other room options available (including the suite we had stayed in the night before and the mid-range Andra Room). She then told me she'd have to call me back. They ended up moving us and the new room was just across the hall, the Andra Room (and by the way, the windows opened in it, too). This was the second lie of the night. 
In the morning, we hit the valet key on the phone, to request our car. The front desk answered and said that she'd be happy to have the valet pull the car. We waited ten minutes and walked downstairs (that's about how long it had taken them the day before). When we got down there, there were two valets standing around having a personal conversation. After we stood there for ten minutes, holding the blue valet ticket and tip money in my hand, one of them comes over and asked if we needed our car. I explained that we had called and the front desk said they were going to call out and request the car. He said they hadn't and it didn't surprise him because "it had already happened a few times that morning". 
All in all, I can't say much bad about the hotel, the rooms or the restaurant. I don't mind little things like the window not opening or having to change rooms because the TV doesn't work. What I do mind is being lied to repeatedly and a supposed four star hotel dropping the ball on customer service in such a big way.

title: “Trendy and friendly, but extras and restaurant service disappointing”
text: We like this property and the staff is friendly. The rooms are comfortable, nicely designed and light. (We were in a King Deluxe on seven.) The prices for breakfast in Plein Sud are higher than the quality of the service, where most of the employees behave as though they are there to have their own breakfasts, chat about themselves and watch TV. Don't bother interrupting them for coffee refills either, because the effort is not worth the outcome. My only other gripe is the $10 per day per device internet charge. What a scam on its Apple-loving design-hungry punters! Otherwise a good location in a great neighbourhood with some enjoyable eating options.

title: “Great place to have a wedding reception!”
text: I just wanted to say thank you to the entire Holiday Inn DFW South staff. If was an absolute pleasure working with them. They provide excellent customer service. Thanks again for making my cousins special day so… special!

title: “Location a plus, room was a bust”
text:
First off, I am not the type of person that generally leaves a review, but this hotel definately deserved it. First off the location is amazing. As everyone has said it is a block from the magnificent mile. My husband and I drove to Chicago, but had the valet staff park our car (for $41 a day) and walked or took a cab everywhere. It is a $5 cab ride to most every place we went, and it isn't a bad walk if you want to do that instead. 
Now, on the down side. These rooms were rediculously small. I'm not saying it was a little cramped, it was TERRIBLE! The bathroom is the worst...there isn't a vanity and the shower is smaller than my kitchen sink. I was so disapointed. Chicago was just one of our stops on our 8 day road trip and with all of our luggage there wasn't any place to move throughout the room. I believe we paid $130 a night (booked it online) and this hotel was a terrible deal for the amount of space you are given. 
We looked at other hotels in the area, and if we are to go back to Chicago on vacation we will most defnately stay at the Marriott on Michigan avenue. This hotel is a block from the Inn of Chicago, is very decently priced, and even their smallest room has to outmatch the Inn of Chicago.

title: “Wonderful Getaway!”
text: Monica was a great help from the moment we checked in! She was the manager on duty. Since we were NY novices we did not know where to eat or any good comedy shows. She recommended a great movie, a hysterical Broadway Comedy stop and John's Pizza---all of which we LOVED! There also was delicious cookies offered in the evening (first come, first serve). We had a wonderful, and most accommodating stay in the Candlewood Suites, and the staff really made us feel at home.

title: “Great location! Great Hotel!”
text:
I stayed at this location 12-16 March 2012. If you are driving or will have a rental car, Hotel Circle is an ideal location right off I-8. The room was nicely decorated and extremely quiet. Since the room had a refrigerator, I called the front desk and asked if it was possible to get a microwave also, one was delivered within 5 minutes. The bathroom was large with lots of counter space. The room also had lots of lights and modern furniture.
The Bistro was well stocked with a great menu selection and the food and service was always outstanding. The sit-down tables had individual televisions which was a nice touch. There were also taller tables with bar stool style seats.
The Lounge area was modern and very comfortable. The business center was located in the same area. 
The front desk personnel were very professional and extremely helpful with any questions that I had. Housekeeping was also exceptional, when I got back everyday the room had been cleaned and looking like new. 
If you are going to visit San Diego and want to be located near the highway, I highly recommend Courtyard at Hotel Circle. I found everything that was talked about on Marriott's website to be true.

title: “Lovely Stay at the historic and beautiful Liberty Hotel!”
text: We went for a weekend getaway and the hotel was gorgeous. When you first enter the hotel, it takes you back to when it was once a hotel with their prison cells and the large open check in area. The rooms are very clean and the hotel staff was amazing! Our room wasn't quite ready but they offered us champagne and sitting in the lobby was great! you could take in the history as well as the elegance of the updated hotel. The atmosphere was great! Highly recommend!

title: “Is this the nicest HI ever?...No.”
text:
But, given its location on the bay and its reasonable price you'll probably be willing to stay there again.
The rooms need some work (Especially in the South Tower) but all-in-all it's not bad. Get the bay view room!!! The rooms on the backside over look a parking garage.... yuckl!

title: “lovely boutique hotel with nice touches”
text: Stayed in the Giraffe as an add-on to a business trip. it was lovely moving out of one of the more commercial, busy hotels, to the more intimate giraffe. The staff were very helpful and the free wine and cheese in the lobby on arrival was a lovely touch. My room (on the 9th floor) was beautiful, modern and quiet and had a lovely balcony, which makes a change in a city. Breakfast the next morning was also plentiful and free. All in all I could not fault the Giraffe. The part of town it was in was slighly non-descript, but an easy walk to the empire state building. I would definitely recommend this hotel.

title: “Great respite, multiple pools, jacuzzis, shopping, movies and restaurants near-by.”
text: I was looking for a place in Southern California during the rainy season where I could have a "stay at home" vacation in a hotel where others would do the daily chores. The Town and Country Resort Hotel was the perfect choice. Although a large hotel site with multiple buildings, its service was excellent. We had a room key mix up that was not the hotel's fault and an affable bellman, whose name I think was AJ, came immediately, not once but twice. Room service was excellent as well, rarely taking more than 20 minutes. The rooms were spacious - we had a suite which gave us plenty of room for different activities. Out of the back door of our building is a huge mall, accessible over a foot bridge, with all the major California department stores, including Nordstrom's and Macy's, a large movie theater, and multiple restaurants. I recommend Bing Crosby's Restaurant and Piano Lounge. Food excellent; music varies; not quiet on weekends. Also to the rear of the building where our rooms were located is the light rail system, which means a quick trip to downtown San Diego. Even though this hotel caters to large conventions, we did not seem to be affected in any way (rooms; service) by the various meetings.

title: “Average hotel, great location”
text:
My husband and I went to SF for a quick getaway weekend. We stayed at the hyatt because we had free nights there. The hotel location is great because it is right next to the Embarcadero building, downtown, and walking distance to North Beach, Chinatown, Soma, and Union Square. There are a lot of bus routes/bart in the vicinity to get to any other part of town. 
The hotel itself was average. The check in process was smooth. But I was surprised there was no offer to take up our bag to the room. The hotel lobby is nice but dark. I would recommend adding more lights to give it a little more liveliness. 
The room was on the 15th floor with a partial view of the bay and the rest of the view was of the buildings in the area. The bay view is incredible. The room itself was nicely furnished. However, there were a few details that needed attention. The carpet seemed a little dirty. Overall, I would give this hotel a 3.8 stars.

title: “Great Location and Good Value”
text:
This hotel is in a lovely leafy street just off 8th Avenue, is is close to the 23rd Street Subway which is useful for the E line which connects direct to JFK plus all the other lines.
The area feels safe day and night and has some good bars and resutrants nearby although some do close early compared to NYC standards. There is a supermarket on the corner and a couple of Starbucks nearby.
The hotel is very nice although I did feel the rooms were a little small once you opened up the large suticase it was all a little tight, a light over the mirror by the sink would also be useful. However we did not spend much time in the hotel and the bed was comfy, a reminder to other guests that closing doors can be done quietly!
It is within walking distance of several of the main attractions or areas.

title: “Great Hotel, Great Neighborhood”
text: We have stayed twice at Lyden Gardens. We love the neighborhood and the roomy suites - a nice to place to relax in between NYC activities! Not the most luxurious of hotels, but a great value and wonderful location. Staff is very helpful with restaurant recommendations, arranging car service, etc. Will definitely go back.

title: “Location,Location, large room!!!”
text: Stayed here Oct 2011 - the hotel is in an amazing location, just 1/2 block (barely) from Times Square!!!! Surprisingly not much street noise at all and I'm a very light sleeper!!! Very nice lobby, quick check in, helpful front desk! Had a dbl queen room - was huge by NY standards, great for 3-4 people!!! Our bathroom was very large-sink long enough for 2 to do hair/makeup, etc...had a wonderful view of the river -- room was clean, beds were comfortable! Breakfast buffet was great! Will definitely stay here again!!!

title: “Very Comfortable & Convenient”
text: We had a 2 night reservation, but cancelled the second night last minute due to the hurricane. There was no charge for the second night despite the late cancellation. The room was very clean and comfortable. This was a trip to drop off our George Washington Univ. freshman. The Double tree is very convenient both for the campus and sight seeing. This will probably be our "family hotel" in DC for the next 4 years.

title: “Girls Weekend”
text:
I had a fantastic time with my friends last weekend. We came to charlotte Center City
for a girls night out. The staff is so friendly and very helpful. The room was exceptional
and it felt like home. I loved the view of the rooftop and night, and the restaurant food and service was excellent. I will recommend this hotel to all my friends.

title: “we were not disappointed”
text:
We stayed at the Orchard for five nights, July 13th to the 18th. We chose the hotel based on the positive reviews and lack of negative reviews on Tripadvisor. 
We were not disappointed. It was everything everyone said it was. Our room was spacious and well appointed with tasteful furnishings. We made good use of the in room internet and safe. The king bed was extremely comfortable.
The breakfast had everything we wanted; lots of fresh fruit, cereal, variety of breads, sweat breads and croissants, many juices, good coffee. It was not the same every day and did vary to some degree. 
The location is excellent, just a short walk to many popular San Fran sights.
The staff was helpful & courteous, and always maintained their professionalism.
When we return we wil stay here!

title: “Absolutely Fantastic...”
text: The James is an excellent addition to Chicago.The rooms were incredibly spacious and well laid out with a impressive attention to details.The bed was so comfortable I wish it was my bed at home!We randomly chose the James-not realising it was new-so I was expecting it to be a bit of a gamble but I was very impressed.The location is excellent-right next to good food and the magnificent mile.Which can be either a good or bad thing depending on the state of your credit card!The staff at the hotel were attentive and helpful-the concierge was fabulous at getting difficult dinner reservations.I was most impressed by the david burke steakhouse within the hotel-I was expecting just an average meal but what we got was one of the best meals of our entire vacation with attentive service and beautiful food.My boyfriend vistis Chicago for work and we wouldnt hesitate to stay at The James again-in fact we look forward to it!

title: “Not your average hotel”
text: Stayed in the hotel Solamar for 2 nights. The staff in the hotel that we encountered were all very helpful and friendly - in particular the staff on the front desk. Our bedroom was great; loved the dressing gowns! There is a wine hour in hotel from 5-6pm each evening; I thought this was a great idea; never saw this in any other hotel! The hotel was very trendy and quirky; with a personal touch that you don't find in the big hotel chains; also the location was great. The only complaint I would have is the valet parking rates, think it was around $30 a night, we noticed a place only about 2 blocks away for a third of the price.

title: “Good location”
text:
Stayed at this hotel over 4th of July weekend. The location is very convenient as it's two blocks from the Inner Harbor. Our room came with a refrigerator, a decent sized bathroom and a view of an alley. 
There is a free continental breakfast each morning for about 2 hours which gets very crowded, and includes all of the basics (fruit, pancakes, sausage, muffins, coffee). Complimentary newspapers are also available in the lobby. There were a lot of kids at the hotel while we stayed there.
They have an average sized pool downstairs, which every time that I checked was usually filled with kids. There is also a business center with internet access (via 2 computers) although the connection is not very fast. The hotel also has a small fitness center, which consists primarily of cardio machines, so if you intend on lifting there, think again. 
Overall, if you're looking for amenities, I would not recommend staying here but if you're on a budget and want to be close to everything, then this is a good option.

title: “Trump SoHo is perfect”
text: We spent a long weekend @ Trump SoHo and is was difficult to leave. From the great location, fabulous room & view to the exemplary service everything was absolutely perfect. My wife & I agree it was by far our finest stay in NYC.

title: “Location is good..... and that's ALL!”
text:
We just got back from our trip and were extremely disappointed with the whole experience. 
Upon check-in, we waited for the hostess to get off her personal call to help us check in. 
We had a courtyard room that was extremely dark, even at 10:00 in the morning. So we had all the lights on all the time. The air conditioner didn't work well and there was only ice available upstairs. The only vending machine as down a long dark hallway and cost and arm and a leg for a coke. It's cheaper around the corner at the convenience store. 
We made plans... and reservations for high tea, and it was cancelled on us without any notification. However they still advertised it to others checking in. 
The worst part of this hotel is their customer service. very rude and will make YOU THE CUSTOMER wait while they talk to their friends on cell phones. Outrageous! 
Not recommended at all. Save your $200/ night and go elsewhere!

title: “Excellent position! Within walking...”
text:
Excellent position! Within walking distance to fisherman's wharf, ghiradelli square! A longer walk to china town but everywhere is close!
Nice comfortable rooms! Free wifi! Parking on expensive side! But it's like that everywhere in San Francisco!
All in all a nice, comfortable hotel

title: “Worth It!”
text: Super helpful front desk staff! We were able to check in early, as in before 12:30pm, and upgraded to a Grand Club room. They are currently renovating the club room in the east tower so they're using a suite in the west tower. Lots of space, beautiful views, again, helpful staff, nice snacks, happy hour, and breakfast. Our room was very clean, comfortable bed, and we were able to arrange for a late check-out. Wonderful!!!!!!!!

title: “A+++”
text:
My Family & i stayed at the Holiday inn right next door and figured we should try the 
This hotel was FANTASTIC. The staff was very nice and even printed us directions to the museums in the area. We had a great time. Stayed there 2 nights and loved the Continental breakfast. When my family and I visit LA again we are staying here
(Keep in mind though: Directions to this place are a little tricky so pay attention to the signs & as directions if you need to)

title: “Location, Location, Location”
text:
The Gaslamp is one of my favorite places for a quick weekend getaway and this hotel puts you in the perfect place to take it all in. We had no problem with noise from the guests or the rail. The room was small and the bathroom was tiny but both were modern and nicely decorated. The bed was comfy and the lighting was adequate. 
Now, on to why I only gave this place a 3 rating. Check In was easy but we were not supplied with any information on the hotel. The room was also sans information about on site dining or amenities. Just a couple of cute pairs of earplugs in case the train was too loud. We never did find the gym or pool. I am easy to give a little but there were a myriad of little things that added up. There was some porcelain damage to the tub that could have easily been fixed but was left ugly and staring at me when I took a shower. There were a few places in the shower that had black mold between the tiles. Again, another easy fix that was overlooked. The room and bathroom seemed fairly clean but the shower had black hair on the walls left behind from a previous guest. Ewww, The door to the bathroom had a broken closer at the top that just hung out dirty, rusted and useless. I'm not quite sure why it was there in the first place because even without it, the door would only stay in the closed position. Parking has gone up to $40 and for the money, I thought that the attendants were a little rude.(for $40 bucks you can open and close the door for me) 
So Hilton Gaslamp could have been good but it was just OK.

title: “Business or Pleasure - A Jewel!”
text: I love this Marriott, especially the friendly expert service, environment, and the clean rooms. It is tucked away and doesn't come up on AT&T Navigator, so you have to put in the address, 6330 West Freeway in Fort Worth to find it. Here's the deal guys, this hotel was chocked FULL of boy's baseball teams...and it was QUIET! Normally, boys teams are the worst and I was prepped for the same, but man, these guys know how to manage groups. From the front desk. Deidre is a spark of life behind the front desk and Eddie was very helpful and provided friendly service to us with our tv. Bottom line, folks, whether with family or Guard or business, it is rare to find a hotel so friendly and help. Look them up, you won't be disappointed!

title: “Mini-Hawaii. Fabulous cust. svc.We had a great time. Loved the views. Loved the amenities. Going back again this summer.”
text: Our family was in need of a extended weekend trip to get away from hustle and bustle of Las Vegas. We found Paradise Point on the internet and decided it looked like a nice place to go de-stress. It did not disappoint in any way. The staff was great, our room was great, and the other guests were great. We did smores at the firepit on the beach, played miniture golf and croquet. We ate on the patio at the Barefoot Grill and enjoyed the scenery as well. Their gift shop has everything, just in case you forget something. It is so close to Sea World you can walk over there. They really have something to do for everyone. We did have one afternoon of rain, but we did not let that get us down, we ordered pizza and watched the storm from our living room playing cards and dice. We decided we have found a new place to hang out this summer. We are definitely going back.

title: “More than i expected”
text: Amazing suite! My favorite thing about it was the bed it was so comfortable.They even gave you a choice in witch type of pillows you wanted to use. The staff was very friendly and there was no lazyness in between them if you had a problem they would go to it right away. The breakfast was also delicious and you had many things to choose from there was things like a Giant waffle, Muffins, Fruit and the main cource and there was also all types of drinks. There was even games you could play at the front desk all you have to do is go down there and ask and they will set them up for you. It clearly was a very good choice for me and im looking forward to coming back there soon.

title: “I would up this to a 10 star place to stay.”
text: This is our second stay at this facility and I cannot say enough about the staff and the oh so many extras. Have you ever heard of a hotel that gives you a wonderful continental breakfast,snacks whenever you want them or detergent to wash your clothes? The accommodations are wonderful and everyone is so helpful. The pools are so clean as are the rooms. We hope to visit again next year. A very enjoyable experience. Thank you Gretchen, Zeeshan, Lori, Justin, et al. A special thanks to Darren Ross. GM.

title: “A wonderful quick getaway”
text: We booked a room at the last minute for a weekend baseball getaway. We found a very fair price, beautiful room, a real attention to being green, and comfortable beds. The staff members were very gracious - especially Lily who was serving breakfast. She went above and beyond to be certain that all our needs were met.

title: “Great location, not luxury”
text: Smack in the middle of Times Square which is a mixed blessing. Quite a lot of street noise even on the 18th floor. Room was fine, decent size and seemed clean. No robes?! Not sure what the deal is with this trend to hip bathroom doors that are either peek a boo or are otherwise privacy challenged. The R wan't as bad as some places, especially in northern Europe, but what's wrong with just a regular door? Service was fine but my platinum status didn't seem to count for much here.

title: “Marri "Ought" to be Proud of this Property!”
text:
Late arrival with 5 yr old was a snap, thankfully! The courteous lone front desk agent even let me leave the check-in process to tend to my childs restrooms needs. 
Easy and simple check in. I used the sleep,park,fly rate. Ample parking in a mostly well lit parking lot, as this property shares parking with the Holiday Inn. 
Clean well maintained lobby. There is a work in progress, but it did not ruin my stay. Nice side lobby bar allows you to watch for your ride while you relax! 
Very clean room! I love the serene decor and the 6 pillows on the king bed! Bathroom is plenty big with nice amenities from bath and body works. Tv is new and in great working condition. Microwave, coffee machine, free internet, room service... This place has all of what I require for a great experience. (my first time at a Marriott I should add) I am a Starwood Hotel loyal, but needed the parking duration. I only spent $132+taxes and fees for this room which includes 5 days of parking and free shuttle service to Midway. By the way, this is the last stop for shuttle before going Midway, so no long rides across hotel row while you freak out about security lines at MDW!! 
Overall A+ for me and I will definately stay here again without doubt.

title: “I love the ULC of Chicago and their Valet team :-)”
text:
I have been going to the ULC of CHicago for many years now - a friend of mine is a member so everything is easy. The club is in a great location. I love using the valet team that is just more than nice - and respectful to your things.
The club is very old and a beautiful meeting location. It has the library upstairs which allows you to reserve a room and make phone calls. There is a fee of course.
It has also rooms for overnight stays which I have never used but heard of to be very comfortable a nice.
I would recommend the ULC for drinks and dinner and any meeting that you could possibly imagine. Lots of groups meet there and keep coming back. What is there more to say? Check it out!
Thanks Union League Club service people.

title: “For the money and location well worth it”
text:
me and a friend of mine, went to New York September 23-27, didnt want to spend alot on a hotel as we seen hotel prices in New York find this hotel on the internet worry alittle about the reviews on here, but figure for the price we would gamble a chance, got to the hotel little nervous, but was happy once got there, room was fine hotel smell of paint as the was fixing it up, the hotel is old but we never once felt out of place, room was clean not a 5 star hotel, but if you want a cheap hotel with a nice location, pick this place, trust me you wont be doing much other than sleeping and cleaning up, its New York a city that truly never sleeps, my only suggest would be to bring your own towel as the hotels are a little small and thin, kind like motel 6 towels, but basic hotel and great location
r

title: “Make sure you upgrade at the Wellington”
text: Standard room was dirty. The room was on the side of the building where the rubbish truck lined up at night. We were five fours up but the noise was beyond belief. The staff on the whole were most unhelpful although as always there were exceptions. Once we upgratded to a suite life improved. This hotel is in the very best location but remember never ever book a standard room. The worst experience I have ever had.

title: “Magnolia- a great place to stay!”
text: I can't say enough good things about the Magnolia: 1. Close proximity to the convention center. 2. Breakfast buffet was quite good and included more than the standard cold cereal and sweet roll. 3. Staff- always helpful and nice. 4. Clean. 5. Cost- you can't beat it. I really have nothing negative to say about my experience at the Magnolia

title: “Family and Friends”
text:
I have stayed at the Arizona Grand Resort 2 times in the last couple of years. Each time has been a great experience for me and my family. The Staff is great. Every employee was always helpful and curtious. The kids loved the resort and waterpark. The golf course is in great shape and the convienence to golf right at the resort is fantastic. The restaurants are also very convenient and we had a great time Rustler's Rooste.
I would highly recommend this resort to anywone looking for a great get away!

title: “A honeymooner's haven”
text: Cool, calm and charming - the Library Hotel was the perfect Manhattan base for the first leg of our honeymoon. Friendly, knowledgable staff made us feel so at home. And who can knock the complimentary cheese and wine that kick-started pretty much every evening of our stay?! We had the Love Room, which is worth the extra cost thanks to a small balcony that reminds you you're in one of the most exciting cities in the world. Great rooftop cocktails too! We loved it.

title: “The best hotel to stay in NY”
text:
I stayed at St. James Hotel three times with my family (four people) and we loved everything about it. The location in my opinion is the best feature of the hotel, a 5 minutes walk from Times Square. The staff were amazing, seriously they were always so attentive with our needs. The rooms are very simple but also very cozy. The bathrooms are quite small but well cleaned.
 Well in general I think the hotel it is a perfect and affordable option ! I will definitely stay there again for the fourth time and I also recommend this hotel! :)

title: “Good place to stay at airport”
text: We stayed here twice, at the beginning and end of our trip. Clean location and reasonably quiet.. Literally within a 10-minute walk of the El Paso Airport terminal building. The halls are a little run-down (wallpaper peeling off the walls) but the rooms are clean and the beds are comfortable. The first room they put us in had faulty air conditioning but I reported it to the front desk and they switched us to another room right away. Standard free breakfast with frozen waffles, cereal, etc. Lots of restaurants and other services within a 5-minute drive away.

title: “Location, location, location!”
text:
We stayed at Inn at the Market on May 29 and 30 on our way to Alaska. Prior to arriving I had made email contact with Taylor at the hotel and she was most helpful with our arrangements. The staff were very friendly and this hotel is truly boutique and has a lovely feel to it. Its location has to be one of the best right at the door of the Pike Place Market a world famous market and it's fascinating. Our room had a partial water view which was lovely. Bed was comfy, Wardrobe space good, tv in an amoire. Air conditioning very noisy and hard to control sadly.
Now ladies who have make-up...The bathroom has a pedestal basin and no cabinet area on which to place your make-up items as you need them. The shower is over the bath and the wc is in the same room. All in all extremely small-you could just shut the door. This is a pity because really this is the only negative aspect bar the aircon I want to highlight.
Apart from these two things this is really a great little property in an excellent location.
We dined at both Bacco and the new Asian restaurant. Both experiences were very good and we thoroughly enjoyed these. We also had room service once in the evening and this was good too.

title: “Kid Fest ruined our stay”
text: Our room was in middle of group from church/kid festival. The halls were constant noise, screaming, slamming doors. Why would we be put on floor where hotel knew there would be this large group of children. My sister and I are senior citizens. We needed rest from our travel and noise from pool went on until almost 11PM. Looked down at pool and there were more than 40 children in the water which must be against safety regulations. Is there a limit to number of people (especially children) in the water? Elevators impossible to use due to crowds of children in and out. We used the stairs. Only good part of our stay was price on priceline.com.

title: “Rooms are great, hotel is big!”
text: Never been somewhere that they give you a map of the place when you check in! Big hotel. Room in East Tower was very nice, very modern. I had a corner queen room. Very nice. Was in town for conference held in hotel. Visited fitness center, very, very busy at prime work out time, but usable. Big Bar in lobby, very expensive drinks ($12 for Makers/Diet), but very busy both nights I was there. Check in, Check out very helpful. Valet a little slow when leaving, but very good convention stay.

title: “vacation 2012”
text: My wife and I stayed 5/12 thru 5/19 and were treated like gold. The customer service at the desk was excellant and very helpful. The suite, breakfast and the other amenities were obsolutely great. We used the pool and hot tub almost daily along with your exercise room. The managers nightly cocktail time was a very nice extra. The suite was very clean and kept clean by your staff daily. The location worked very well as a central hub for all are vacation trips and needs daily and was very close to plenty of stores, restraurants and other places. The Jacksonville beach was not very far away and was very clean. We went to St. Augustine one day, Daytona racetrack & the beach another day, and Universal Studios another day during our week stay. Thanks again Mary & Joe Korn

title: “Nice Hotel, location, staff needs improvement”
text:
Pleasant hotel across divided street from Southcenter Mall. Rooms ok, bar nice, staff uncaring.
I am handicapped, with a cane. When I asked about another restaurant, they said there wasn't one (Outback Steakhouse is next door I found out later). I had dinner in the bar (burger and fries with no seasoning). I got burger and highly seasoned fries. Bartender took them off the bill.
Next morning I asked about seasoning on hashbrowns because I am allergic, then asked if I could get french toast without the eggs. The waiter couldn't care less, said if I'm allergic or don't want something, then don't order it. Since I would have had to pay for french toast, eggs and meat if I only wanted the 2 slices of french toast, I skipped breakfast.
When I pointed out to the front desk that their HHornors Benefits room flyer had a typo that said the hotel's restaurant was only open mornings (not lunch or dinner times) the receptionist was very nasty, said, "Don't leave!" when I turned to go, and insisted I stand there until he discovered I was right. Then, instead of saying I was right or apologizing, he said, "thank you for calling it to my attention," and turned away. Not very pleasant experience so I would suggest you do not point out any errors, mention any allergies, or ask for any omissions in their food service.

title: “what lovely views.....lacks a little for the family vacationers!!”
text:
Our family of five recently visited the JW for a few days upon
going to our destination in Sedona. Although, the hotel is
beautifully landscaped and the views are magnificent this one
lacks in service and is not very family oriented. Believe the 
reviews when people say this is geared more towards the 
business travelers with alot of conferences going on. It made
it hard to feel relaxed with all those corporate badges and 
people always doing business. The hotel definitely caters
to this and these people get the better service. They being the
business people also look at you like what are you doing 
bringing your small children here to vacation? What made a 
difference in our stay was that they do have a nice lazy river 
for children with a slide and my boys also enjoyed the 
basketball nets at the other pools. Also, we ate at Roy's on
our final night and they truly were wonderful! Kudos to their 
staff and their food was excellent. Thank you Roy's for letting
us end the trip on a remarkable note! Be aware also that this
is supposed to be a JW and the linens are not the best. Although, the room was clean the linens were awful (most of
the towels were not very white but dingy gray and the bed 
sheets were worn with even little tears). We went to the 
breakfast at Blue Sage one morning...I was very irritated that
the table was not clean and that the chairs were not wiped .
The booster seat they gave my daughter was disgusting also.
I hate to be picky but you can get this at an IHOP......and this is 
a JW! Do yourself a favor and if you are a family try the Camelback they are so much more service oriented and it 
has a much better feel for families. We have stayed at alot 
of Marriott's top resorts and also Ritz's and we were a little
disappointed with this one. We will definitely go back to the
Camelback with our next travels to the Phoenix/Scottsdale 
area and by the way, if your travels take you to Sedona don't
hesitate to stay at the Enchantment /Mii Spa Resort this is 
truly a fantastic resort and you will be amazed at
the views!!

title: “Good hotel nice location”
text: Really happy with hotel, price and location . If I had to be critical only bar is adjoining rare restaurant which is good but after walking shopping miles could have done with more relaxing bar / area.

title: “I hardly slept at all during my stay!”
text: My husband and I had a terrible stay at this hotel. It was in a convenient location and we found most of the staff to be pleasant, but the noise level coming from music at a nearby bar was so high, that we hardly slept a wink! The music was vibrating my bed it was so loud! When I complained to the front desk, they said that the police had been notified and the problem would be taken care of shortly. It never was. We were moved to a new room the next night, but A/C unit was humming noisily. I do not recommend this hotel.

title: “Outstanding Adventure!”
text: We had the opportunity to stay at the Alexander Inn in Philly, two weeks ago. The manager of the hotel, John, makes sure that everyone is happy by personally greeting everyone at breakfast. One feels like we were staying at a B and B with the niceness of a hotel. Christopher at the front desk is helpful as well. They are incredibly accommodating. The rooms are clean, albeit a bit small in the bathrooms, and the breakfast is outstanding! Everything is fresh and homemade. We will definitely stay there again!

title: “HYGIENE”
text: Worst hotel ever stayed in, back in home with bed bug bites. Would not recommend this hotel to a dog. But then again pets are allowed in the hotel rooms which is not hygienic at all. Apart from that San Fransisco is fantastic destination to visit.

title: “The Service makes the difference”
text: This hotel is not in as good a location as some of the others but the service more than makes up for it. The rooms are a good size and clean, a little dated and the a/c unit can be noisy if you need to run it at night. The concierge is fantastic and if you ask a few questions they will give you honest answers and always have alternatives for you. The buses stop right outside and you can either go to Santa Monica or downtown but make sure you have the right money as there is no change given or you can get a day pass for $6/person for the bus and train. Really enjoyed Hectors sense of humour when staying here but they are all fantastic. They also have a little shop for things you may have forgotten. Room service and Restaurant are prompt and more than adequate if you dont want to go out at night.

title: “Love it! Love it! love it!”
text: What can I say... We stayed here about 5 times and I just love it! Great staff, great location! All the rooms are different and have their own individual decoration. The first time we booked (travel agent forgot our request and) we got a queen bed room. Since we're used to two separate mattresses at home I went down to ask if there was some way to fix the 'problem', and without any trouble we we're switched to a double queen. Staff is more than willing to help and get you on your way in NY. Location is about 15 min. walk from Times Square so how much more central can you get. The hotel offers good value for money and I can recommed it to anyone. It felt like family away from home (and I mean the good kind :-)

title: “Good Value for Business Travel”
text: This hotel does a nice job of providing fine value for its business travelers. Attentive to their customers' needs, they are very responsive to any requests and have shown marked improvement since I relayed my concerns to their staff following a visit in early January. The location can't be beat by any other Hilton-network property in Center City....

title: “wonderful location”
text: Walking distance to everything good. Very nice hotel with a wonderful restaurant in the front courtyard. Staff is friendly and helpful. We especially enjoyed the roof top view. We would love to go back.

title: “Clean, comfortable and spacious”
text: Nice, spacious and clean rooms. Great location. Good customer service. Breakfast was average.

title: “Renovated rooms are clean, comfortable, and nice”
text:
The letter at the front desk and in the room warned that construction may be taking place after 7:00 AM. I saw few signs of this construction, except for the time I looked out my window and saw a construction worker hanging out of a seventh floor room working on the glass. The room I checked into, on the 8th floor, was fresh, clean, and pleasant. Like many hotels, guest noise from the hallway was frequent, but not annoying. 
Self-parking is a little inconvenient; it's a long way up to where parking starts on the 4th floor. Water pressure was solid, there was little wait at the front desk, and the bed was comfortable. The alarm clock is complicated to set right -- if you're the kind of person who had a VCR that constantly blinked 12:00, you're out of luck. I'm a computer nerd, and finally figured it out the second night, after an AM/PM mix-up (the staff had set the clock to be 12 hours wrong). Wifi was fast and stable.
My second night, I received a letter indicating that the water will be shut down for construction from midnight to 3:00 AM. I slept through it, so it didn't effect me.
The pizza in the restaurant was great, but I was both surprised and amused that the only beers on tap were Bud Light and Coors Light.
If I could be sure of getting a renovated room (and it sounds like they'll be done by fall), I'd definitely stay here again.

title: “Rough around the edges”
text: Room: compact; modern and slick; ample lighting; sufficient storage; desk and chair; comfy bed; very large flat-screen tv; deep bath tub. Elevator system: never waited longer than 15 seconds. Cons: Overall ambience was a negative. At no point was staff friendly and welcoming. Check-in was cold and business-like. Dowdy lobby. Room had no bath towels, no hotel directory. Room was hot. Shower was one degree from being cold. I called with regard to the ice machine location, and I was sent on a wild goose chase on another floor. Unless, I got an incredible deal, I would not stay at this place again.

title: “Perfect for short stays in NY”
text: Perfect hotel for a short stay in NY with most interesting places and/or connections within walking distance (We even went on foot with our luggage to Penn Station, would have taken us longer with a cab... an experience on it's own). Rooms aren't that big, but very clean and very good beds. Noisy airco (tip : leave it on all day, shut it down at night). Mostly recommended : very good breakfast with choice of everything to keep you going until late afternoon ! And if you have a problem : very friendly staff to help you out. Also the only hotel on our East Coast tour with free internet. Only one minor thing : try to stay away from the elevator(s) around checkout time... traffic is almost as heavy as on Broadway ;-) . We will definitely recommend this hotel to other people and the agency that booked our trip(s).

title: “Regular visitor”
text: We have been visiting NY for many years now and had stayed at several different hotels. For the past four years, we have stayed at the Edison. Actually, we couldn't be happier. Our rooms have always been clean and well supplied with fresh towels etc. The staff is friendly and helpful. Yes, the rooms are small and the decor is outdated, both of which add to the charm of visiting the city (at least for us). Sofia's is a great place for dinner and, the hotel bar has reopened. All this said, the best feature of the Edison is the location. Walk out the door and, in 50 yards, you're standing on Times Square. If you've never had your morning coffee on TS at 6:00 am, you owe it to yourself. I have reccommended the Edison to friends and we will continue to stay there.

title: “Great little hotel in a great location”
text:
I found a good rate at expedia.com, and my husband and I stayed at the Whitehall in August, 2001.
We really enjoyed it. The staff was very friendly and detailed. We arrived early, and we were able to get into our room. 
The location is excellent. It is on the northern end off the Magnificent Mile (Michigan Avenue) on a relatively quiet side street. It is just down the street from the Four Seasons. An El stop is just a few blocks away, and there was a small grocery store and a number of restaurants nearby (ranging from Thai food, a wine bar, and a diner). We found the restaurants and the grocery store on the way to the El stop.
The room was very nice. We had a room with a king bed. The bathroom was large and also very nice. The hotel also has a turndown service. The room also had a fully stocked mini-bar.
I would definitely stay at this hotel again.

title: “Location, Location, Location”
text:
We spent 3 nights at the Homewood Suites in downtown Chicago. When we arrived our room wasn't ready. They held our bags at the valet area and brought them up promptly when our room was ready..which only took about 30 minutes. 
Our room was very nice. The suites are great with kitchenette, living area, dining table, bedroom and separate sink area from the bathroom. Our room was very clean with the exception of mildew on the grout in the bathroom. With the products available now, there should be no mildew in bathrooms at hotels. It's just too easy to take care of these issues now. 
The hotel is right on the line for the free blue trolley to the Navy Pier. It's only about a 6 block walk so we didn't take advantage of the trolley...but we do tend to walk a lot. One block west of the hotel on E. Grand and N. State is the Grand Plaza Market. It's a small supermarket. We were able to get supplies for the room there. Prices were only about 5% higher than what we were used to at home, so not bad at all. They have a pharmacy, groceries, toiletries, etc. 
ESPN Zone is around the corner in the same building. Bloomingdales is around the corner as well. Easiest way to Michigan Avenue is to walk west on E. Grand, turn left on N. Rush then right on E. Ohio. Boom...Michigan Avenue in all it's glory.
The location is just unbeatable!

title: “Reasonable Hotel”
text: We stayed here as part of a holiday package. Hotel staff were friendly and reception staff were helpful apart from telling us the wrong bus to get one day! bit of a nightmare! Rooms were ok in size and we were happy with the space for 2 adults had it been 3 adults it would have been tight for space. Bathroom was a bit small - you could not close the door easily! Breakfast was a nightmare not enough tables and we tried a few different timings and every time the tables were filled with people waiting and the choice of breakfast was not great to be honest. Location was ok but would have been nicer to be nearer North Beach/Fisherman's Wharf. Would recommend providing you cannot get a similar priced hotel nearer the Wharf area. Good free wi-fi internet though!

title: “Great find in Boston”
text: My husband and I were looking for an inexpensive (relative to other Boston hotels) place to stay for one night in September. I found the Newbury Guest House on Hotels.com. You can't beat the location, right on Newbury Street. We could just walk out the door to stores and resturants. The hotel provides parking for a $20 fee which is reasonable for Boston. The Newbury Guest House has a European feel, with modern decor and simple furnishings. The rooms are not large, but the one we had was immaculate and the bathroom looked brand new. Across from the bed was a huge plasma TV. In the morning they have a continental breakfast which even included eggs and bacon. We will definately stay here again and will recommend it to our friends and family.

title: “Do Not Stay on Saturday Night”
text: Hotel is great, rooms are great, pool is great, location is great -- unless you stay on a Saturday night. The problem: The street directly in front of the hotel is a gathering place for extremely loud motorcycle riders who rev their engines and race down Meridian street all night -- apparently with the Indy police department's blessing. The noise is so bad that the hotel should have warned us in advance. What otherwise would have been a great stay was ruined because the hotel failed in its essential purpose -- we could not sleep.

title: “Lovely Hotel, Well Located with Amazing Service & Great American Girl Pkg!”
text: My daughter and I had the lovliest stay here for her first visit to both Chicago and the American Girl (AG) Store after years of collecting the dolls. I highly recommend Talbott's AG Package if you have interested daughters! They definitely give your child the royal treatment complete with special room service menu that's an incredible value in itself not to mention the scrumptious breakfasts included at Bice with outdoor dining next door, and the 30-minute horse-drawn carriage ride in the Magnificent Mile vicinity to the AG Store is wonderful. Beyond the AG bit and food, the staff are really personable and accomodating and the rooms spacious and equipped with cool coffee machines and free wi-fi access. And you can't beat the location in charming area right off Michigan Avenue (and I used to live in Chicago for almost 10 years so I know what I''m talking about here). The housekeeping keeps your room amazingly tidy (2-3X per day) and is very generous in replenishing towels and toiletteries. Only wish the rooms got more sunlight. Other than that, overall just splendid!

title: “Wonderful...”
text:
We loved our stay here… initially, after checking in, we asked for a change in our room… the first having several questionable stains on the carpet floor, any concerns however were quickly gone after the attentive service and getting settled in. Although we had a small corner room, the suroundings were comfortable and cozy. We loved the bathroom… and since I wasn’t feeling too well during our stay, it was great having such an awesome bed to rest in. It was cold/rainy during our stay, so we particulary enjoyed sitting in the lobby/bar area and enjoying the complimentary coffee in the mornings.
I agree with the hotel’s #1 ranking for DC… it’s in a great location, close walking distance to the metro and also to the main monuments.

title: “super friendly and helpful staff, so-so location”
text: I was in town on a business trip - asked for a quiet room and was told I had a 'city view' room. Corner of Bush and Grants streets. It was noisy and the hotel was booked so I was SOL. No fault of the front desk staff - they were always helpful and pleasant.

title: “The Happiest Hotel I Know!”
text:
Wow. What a place to stay. From the moment we arrived and were treated with little gifts for the children we felt  so welcome. Our room was a 2 room suite. 2 double beds and a sofa bed. Both rooms had large flat screen tvs. Hair dryer, fridge, microwave, safe, iron. Large shower - no bath . Pool was small and only 3.3ft deep but it was fine for the kids to splash around. Fitness suite was very well equipped. Lobby and reception were very well presented. Free flavoured water all day. Managers happy hour between 5.30/7.30 was busy but then alcoholic drinks and snacks were free so you'd expect this. Room service was pretty quick and food tasty. Breakfast was good quality and great quantities - but get there early as it gets really busy (the hotel does warn about this, so no need to moan), also mid week was a lot quieter than the weekend.  A nice surprise was the convenience shop in the lobby and the laundry in the basement - priced at only a dollar for wash and a dollar to dry and a fast wash and dry too.
Concierge, reception, porters and waitresses were always happy and willing to go the extra mile to help. We couldnt wait to get back after a days sight seeing to be in our little haven in hot and humid Washington DC 
I can not think of any way this hotel could better itself. Thank you for making our stay such a memorable  one.

title: “Excellent location. Rooms in need of renovation”
text:
The location of the Stephen F. Austin cannot be beat. The staff was pleasant and polite. Unfortunately, the rooms are in need of renovations. The furnishings are dated. Watching a bowl game on such a small 4:3 television with no high definition was painful. The rooms are small, but that is to be expected in a historic hotel. 
In order to compete with other downtown hotels Intercontinental needs to start upgrading their rooms ASAP.

title: “Come for the Food”
text:
Heads up, a $100/night deposit will be charged to your credit card. I wish check-in had explained that. Instead I got a shock when I checked my credit card balance. One phone call to the front desk later, it was resolved but I was plenty worried.
Other than that, come for the food. Norma' s and the Burger Joint are excellent.

title: “Dont sound ur money there, really not worth it trust me!”
text:
Hello,
My thoughts on the W city center is basically that up to now it is the worst W hotel I've ever stayed at. Thank god we didn't spend much time in the room because really the more I was in there the worst I felt about having paid so much for that kind of quality. One comment would be to redo ur bathtubs! The room we stayed in #1222 had a shipped bath tub I really didn't feel food about showering in there. Another complaint is that there was no complimentary coffee in the room. This is the first time I go to a hotel and no coffee or tea is offered in the room. Then we went to the gym and half the machines were out of order and the rest of them were being used so we couldn't do our workout. Finally when we came back from shopping on saturday our room wasnt even made we had to call front desk to request to house keeper to come. So my complaints aren't about the staff they are more about the quality of the hotel. Knowing the W hotel reputation and having stayed at the W in Montreal and in new York I expected a certain level of quality but didn't get that at all... Im really disappointed but thank god for Chicago being such an extraordinary city cause we still enjoyed our week-end. Just couldn't wait to leave the hotel. We will definitely not risk it again.

title: “A calm and welcoming port in the storm.”
text: My husband and I have just spent 5 nights at the Casablanca. We were very pleased with the cleanliness, comfort and service we received during our stay. After the hustle and bustle of times square entering the doors to the Casablanca were like entering a different time. We felt pampered and special. Special thanks to Peter on the front desk who made our arrival special and all the girls in Ricks cafe who assisted us with our breakfast and evening wine and cheese. Excellent champagne! We would definitely recommend staying here and hope to return in the future.

title: “Very quiet and relaxing!”
text: This hotel was totally booked, but we were able to get an early check in. Our entire trip, we did not hear other guests - it was so quiet and relaxing! Breakfast at the concierge lounge was nice every day although more variation in their menu each day would have been nice. Pool area was very unique and well kept. Overall, this hotel was a cool, quiet oasis after a hot day in downtown San Antonio!

title: “Palmer House Hilton please meet 2008. 2008 please meet the Palmer House Hilton”
text:
This is an absolutely gorgeous hotel. The lobby is immaculate and the French inspired decor was certainly not lost on you. However...Upon check in, you're a little turned off the by the confusion. Apparently you're supposed to wait in line at the bell desk only to be told that you should be heading upstairs with your own luggage. They finally point you to the elevators down a long hallway where when you step into the fabulous lobby and being the process of callousing your hands as you struggle with your luggage on the carpet.
You walk into a gorgeously decorated room that has this amazing lavender kind of smell that not too soapy or too flowery. Your smile starts to fade when you wonder why they would put a fainting couch so close to the door. And why would they make up a fainting couch like it's a bed. But it can't be your bed because well, it's small. You figure that maybe this is the precursor to the room and when you try to look for the rest of the room you realize that the wall stops. There's a window, but when you look out, you see the fire escape in extremely close proximity and beyond the black metal stairs is a brick wall.
You start to giggle uncontrollably (and check your makeup)because you're waiting for Allen Funt and the Candid Camera crew to come out of the tiny bathroom. After standing immobile with a picture perfect grin, you decide to call downstairs because you'd die of suffocation in a room so small. The staff mention that they know that the rooms are small - it being a historic hotel and all, and they agree to put you in a larger room that is not facing a brick wall.
When you arrive in your new room, it is larger (not much), but not as nicely decorated. But it is nice and has that same great smell and you're very appreciative. You go to take a gander at your view and it's not exactly facing a brick wall - it's facing a wall of windows where you can see into other rooms and vice versa. Great.
After unpacking, you go to set up your laptop and see that there is no wireless available in the room. Bummer. You then try to connect using the Ethernet cable provided, and learn that they want you to pay $13-$
18/day for Internet access. You get it free most places, but even when you have to pay, it's about half this price.
A little later you're tired, and instead of heading out for food you consider getting some overpriced room service. That's when you notice that they charge a $5 delivery fee to bring you a $10 bowl of soup.
You can't help but wonder if this joint hard up for money or what? I mean you know they're going through renovations, but according to your key packet, the renovations were scheduled to end in 2007.
Your stay ends (as planned), and you continue the second part of your trip at another Hilton in a Chicago suburb where you write this review from your large room with free wireless Internet. There's no lavender smell, but you revel in the fact that they'll bring you a $5.00 bowl of soup for free and you wish that one day these two Hilton's would meet.
Or maybe it's just me.

title: “Very Historic and nice hotel”
text: I stayed at the Copley for business recently and was pleased. It's a bit dated and the continual renovations were a bit of a headache, but the staff and facilities were very nice. I took advantage of the Gold level and was surprised to find charges for the offererings in the concierge loung, other hotels do not do this on their concierge level in my experience. The rooms were spacious and were nicely decorated though the heating unit in the hotel could not be moderated so the temps in the hotel were quite high throughout the stay. Nice hotel but not exceptional.

title: “Bed bugs-HORRIBLE”
text: The location is excellent. However the hotel staff/ facilities and quality of the hotel is totally unacceptable. Few of my collagues got bed bugs! Housekeeping keep banging on the doors, rush into your room without checking for the sign! Front desk staffs were not helpful!! Manager is such a GARBAGE!

title: “India 4 my Birthday”
text: I guess for the most part you get what you pay for. This place was clean and the exercise room was cool. Not the best location however we made the most of it. The only problem I had was the fire alarm with no explanation/evacuation. I was sitting in the lobby, and the alarm went off. No one moved or flinched. Except one lone house keeper who ran past me saying, "Baby run, its a fire, don't you smell that?" Hilarious actually.

title: “Excellent Hotel, great location and value”
text:
We stayed at the hotel New Years Eve 2011. We were in the north tower and had an amazing view of the Charles river on the 24th floor. Ask for a room facing the Charles river above the 20th floor or you may end up looking at the Hynes convention center! The rooms are quite small but very nice and at 3.5 star level at least. There's a coffee maker but no fridge. Very amazing bed! Front desk was friendly and efficient. Room was very clean and new looking. The view was BREATHTAKING. We turned off the lights to just gaze at the river. 
The hotel is connected to an upscale male called The Prudential Center Shops with tons and tons of shopping. You don't have to even step outside into the cold winter air...it's all via walkways. Lots of upscale shopping but regular shops too.
There's a Starbucks in the lobby of the Sheraton. No wifi for free except there. Just outside the hotel is the Copley square area and you are just 5 minutes walk from Newbury Street shopping and 15 minutes walk to the Boston Garden. There's a subway right down the street. Great area. Very safe and upscale area of Boston. Tons of restaurants. Sel de la Terre is incredible french food and very good value for money. 
The parking garage...well...terrible in terms of price. $45 a day. If you can park at the Boston Common Parking Garage for $11.00 per day and walk to the hotel (15 mins) you will save a bundle on the weekend but not weekdays. 
Don't pay $24 for breakfast at the hotel. There's a Duncan Donuts and an Au Bon Pain steps away from you in the Prudential mall. There's a fabulous foodcourt too with wonderful Indian food and a host of other foods. 
The pool is nice but was filled with rug rats so we passed. No hot tub. 
It's a big hotel (1100 rooms) but feels so much smaller! 
We paid $150 a night by doing Hotwire and chose the 3.5 star hotel with a pool and 95% recommended it and saved almost $75.00. We loved it and will do it again next New Years eve for sure!

title: “Nice rooms, fun touches and close to Moscone”
text:
I stayed here recently for business and a quick client trip out to Napa. Spacious W-designed rooms (much like W Union Sq and W Midtown Atlanta). Clean, staff seemed helpful.
When I'm away from home, I do appreciate the small things; W San Francisco seems to have figured this out. During this stay, in the mornings, I had iron my shirts and suit coats. I'm also typically in a hurry and have to dash out the door in the morning. The housekeeping staff at the W San Francisco put the ironing board away--while this may seem like a small thing, I really appreciate it. Nothing worse than coming home from a long business day and a hug ironing board filling up my living space.
Small negatives: Currently (Aug 2011) going through construction in lobby and XYZ restaurant--I got lost one morning going into the restaurant. Temporary lobby is tiny (no chairs, confusing queues).

title: “Attracts voyeurism”
text:
This hotel attracts young, successful, creative types who appreciate the high end design and want to be located in the trendy meat packing district of NYC. There is superb bar on the 18th floor which offers stunning views of the city and a roof garden which is a must see. 
Each room, while compact boasts a minimalist feel with all white furniture. You may also be surprised to see a glassed walled shower in the middle of you room. What makes The Standard's rooms so exceptional are the floor to ceiling windows which offer guests an wonderful panoramic view of the NYC skyline. Be warned, these windows allow office workers in the adjacent building a great view into your room, so don't get carried away and forget the blinds.

title: “Great Hotel and fabulous staff!”
text: We really liked the hotel, it's location and price, but the front desk staff really made us feel welcome and catered to our every need!

title: “Trendy Little Boutique Hotel”
text:
I have stayed at the Hotel 41 twice in the last month. I was very happy with both stays. It has a very hip, clean feel to it that appears to be recently updated. 
Key benefits. Great location, great price (for NYC), very helpful and knowledgeable staff. It reminds me of a european style hotel.
The beds were extremely comfortable (if not a little small). I am even going to call them to find out where they got their pillows. 
What didn't bother me, but may bother some people is that the rooms are small. The rooms aren't the size we have come to expect in the US. Considering in NYC you can pay a lot more for a little larger room which was last redecorated in the Carter Administration, this is a big upgrade from that. 
There wasn't a lot of storage room in my room. Which reminded me of traveling in Europe.
I would stay here again and will.

title: “Great place to stay in a great location”
text: We stayed here for two nights with our kids. The location is excellent and although you would think it would be loud in such a central busy place, it was not at all. The bed was so comfortable we all had great sleeps. The kids slept on the sofabed which was fine for them but I would not recommend it for an adult. It had no support at all.

title: “What a lucky find”
text: We stayed at The Kimberly to celebrate our Daughters 18th and 21st birthdays. What a fantastic and friendly hotel. We had a two bedroom suite it was massive large living area, balcony, two large bedrooms and two bathrooms. The beds were amazing so comfortable and the linen immaculate.The roof terrace "Upstairs at The Kimberly" was lovely and the breakfast such good value. The service was excellent and nothing was too much trouble especially for Harry the doorman so helpful. Really good location with good views of the Chrysler building and the Hudson from the suites windows and balcony. Would highly recommend this hotel.

title: “Five Diamond Property Image Fell Apart”
text:
I had extremely high hopes of this "Landmark" hotel and its reputed five diamond status
but unfortunately
All of the 5 diamond image fell apart in a 24 hrs:
 Some of the main problems that we had were:
- the room was very dusty. Under the cooling unit, you could see layers of dust
-the bathroom phone was so dirty you could see it from a distance
-the tap/faucet was leaking 
- our registration/payment was done through our conference agent and was never received.
-The room was VERY small
- If we asked for anything it look HOURS to arrive
- I asked for slippers and they arrived the next day and after 4 phone calls
- Restaurant in town recommended by Concierge was a bad one
Good Stuff:
-Friendly staff
-Nice House Car
-Excellent location and lobby
-Amazing fitness centre

title: “Great location”
text: We stayed at the Hampton Inn this past weekend to get away from Mardi Gras. Great location and free breakfast was really good. I found parking a bit high for what you pay for the room. Right around the corner from Beale Street and about a 10 minute drive to Graceland, which we really enjoyed. Elvis was in the building! I would definitely stay at this hotel again.

title: “Amalfi Hotel 3 night stay - Chicago”
text: What a wonderful boutique hotel. I had a suite that over looked the street. It was lovely. The bathroom was a great size. The bed was comfortable and to top it all off the hotel from 5:30-7pm the hotel holds a FREE cocktail and finger foods hour and half. It was a great relax and good start to a night on the town of Chicago. Our Bell man GREG is a great helpful, friendly and knowledgeable guy regarding the City things to do. Perfect place to walk to the Mile and show or over the river to visit the bean. All is walking distrance. The cab rides are only $5-$10 where ever you go and the city never sleeps. I loved Chicago.

title: “Great hotel but Queen Rooms are small!”
text:
I stayed here during Thanksgiving week, using a Travelocity discounted rate of $95/nt for a Queen Room. I loved the location, and thought the staff was gracious and efficient. I especially appreciated being offered a very early check-in at 8 AM, when I stopped in to drop off luggage in the morning. Overall, I enjoyed this hotel and would stay here again at this price, however on to the complaints and cautions: 
Rooms: Be careful if you are thinking of booking a QUEEN ROOM, they HAVE A SIZE ISSUE. There's only about a foot between the bottom of the bed and the dresser. Request a top floor room if you don't want everyone in the parking lot to have a great view of you in bed. I think all of the Queen Rooms face the parking lot. 
Noise: I didn't hear any outside noise at all. The P St. reconstruction is no longer obstructing the sidewalks or street, but there is still (loud) work going on. Be careful about taking a streetside room. I did however, hear a continuous light ticking sound. I have no idea what it was, and didn't ask for a room change (who wants to pack up and move after you've settled in).
The Plumbing: The faucet operations are not intuitive. For the sink, TURN the handle to get hot water, and LIFT it to turn it on! The splashing issue happens if you hold your hands too high above the sink. I think it has to do with the shape of the faucet, not the bowl design itself. Hold your hands down into the bowl and you will be okay. 
Toiletries. L'Occitaine two 50-gram bars of the Milk soap, and they did replace them. Shampoo etc 1 oz size, and also were replaced daily. I had NO problems at all with housekeeping.
TV etc. Sort of cheap selection of channels, No HBO. I could not get the CD/DVD player to work but didn't ask for help. They apparently have a free selection of DVDs at the desk. 
Linens and bedding very high quality. There is an in room safe, hair dryer, iron and ironing board provided. Also the two nice robes others mentioned. Locked Minibar, but didn't open it. 
Gym: Good cardio machines and free weight rack, balance balls, open 24 hours with room key on the 2nd floor. Not staffed.
EMail: If you don't travel with a computer, the business center has a minimum charge of $6. Go across and west down P street and use the computer at the coffee shop for $3/15 minutes.
Snacks/Food : As mentioned, free coffee/tea in the am (with a choice of soymilk!) and an evening wine hour from 5-6, with olives and crackerbread. There are free apples hidden away in the gym on the second floor (you'll need a room key to enter). There are several choices in the area for purchasing your own snacks, including the CVS near the Metro, and another market at the far end of the block. There's also a Starbucks right next door. No shortage of restaurants on P Street. Pizza Paradisio is excellent, they will make a takeout pizza in 10-15 minutes and they are just on the next block. 
Metro: Two and 1/2 blocks to Dupont Circle. When you leave the Q Street exit, turn left, walk down 20th street across Mass Ave to P Street, turn Right, walk 1 1/2 blocks and Palomar is on your right. Stationmasters.com is a great website to visit for info on Metro stops. I felt very safe walking from the Metro to the Hotel.
In the neighborhood: The Phillips collection museum is just down the street, and the Textile Museum is an easy walk. You are really between Dupon Circle and Embassy Row, the side streets are historic rowhouses with a few mansions throughout.

title: “Perfect location. Classy & Chic. Very comfortable & sparkling clean.”
text: Very modern inside. Valet parking very attentive as a first impression. Front Dest charming and helpful. Beds& pillows very comfortable. We got a gorgeous view. Loved walking out of the elevator and feeling like we were ouside. Very cool. Had drinks at the bar after visiting the Flower Show's Pre-Opening Dance Party. Expensive but generous sized drinks. Bathrooms perfect. Instant hot water that lasted for 4 of us. We definitely want to go back. If you're going to Philadelphia, you will not go wrong at the Le Meridien.

title: “Gouge City”
text: Other reviews accurately depict the poor quality of the rooms and service. I agree that this is a dumpy hotel with the Westin brand on it. What other reviewers have not mentioned is the exorbant prices for things like parking ($24), wifi ($12.96), etc. You are kind of stuck here without other options. I usually never spend on incidentals and I am SPG Gold. I picked the property due to the name and low rate but will never return. After reading the positive reviews it is clear that the management is somehow affecting those. No reasonable human being could look at this property and think it was good.

title: “Pier 39 with excellent restaurants”
text:
I stayed at the Hyatt Regency Embarcadero for four nights while I attended a conference.
The location is central to Fisherman's Wharf, Pier 39 and Union Square.
The BART station is right outside the door, as is the Embarcadero cable car stop.
My comfy room was overlooking the ice skating rink.
The hotel itself is huge, and the staff was attentive and hard-working. Christmas atmosphere was so excited ! You have to know - Internet access is $9.95 per day. There is Gym but unfortunately, no spa or swimming pool.
Anyway, I would definitely stay here again.

title: “Crossland experience”
text: My recent stay at crossland was supposed to be 3-4 days till I moved in with a friend. However , I decided to extend my visit for a week. This was solely due to the excellent customer services offered by the employees at crossland aswell as their overwhelming display of hospitality especially by the management. My first check in experience involved meeting Mr.Hassan the manager who personally accomponied me towards the room making sure I had everything I needed in order to improve my stay. I must say I was impressed by the professionalism. Mr.Hassan himself and his team are doing a great job and I hope to stay at crossland on my next trip.

title: “Great hotel and location”
text:
Room was luxuriuos! Location fantastic for shopping (walking distance). Underground 10 mins walk away. Loved the room.....recently refurbished.
Corridors a bit dingy. Main criticism - every morning woken up by the housekeeping staff who were very noisy constantly banging on doors!

title: “Over-rated closet”
text:
Location, location, location!!
Those would be the only 3 reasons why you should consider the Roosevelt. Can't complain about the rate cos they tell you that before you hand over your credit card. However, they really should be more realistic in their room descriptions!
I stayed in a traditional guest room for $299/night (and this was discounted). The room turned out to be dark, musty, and tiny with barely any artwork or furniture. Just a lumpy, platform bed with old sheets, a desk with office chair, an older model TV, a mini fridge and a wall mirror. I've stayed at the Sheraton for $199 with more luxurious amenities! My view?? I had a spectacular view of the Roosevelt's rooftop and air conditioning units! Lovely.
I would love to go on about the bathroom but that would bring on a claustrophobic attack.

title: “Misrepresented Hotel...”
text: When I called to make a change to my reservation, the hotel desk staff was incredibly rude and seemed totally confused. I travel quite a bit for my job and have stayed at many "boutique" hotels around the world. This service is what I would expect at a Motel 6, but not from 175/night "luxury" hotel. Needless to say, I am cancelling my reservation.

title: “Excellent Value for NYC”
text: My guess is that any one who writes a negative review of this hotel is used to staying at only the nicest hotels available. I am sure I could find a scuff on the wall or some peeling paint to complain about, but I think there are far more interesting things in Manhattan to think about! The hotel is a excellent value. You will be hard pressed to find any thing comprable for under $200.00 per night. It is right next to the 72nd St metro station and is comfortable. If you have any experience traveling in Europe you will most likely find these hotel rooms spacious and nictely appointed by compairison.

title: “NICE HOTEL - BUT NOT "LUXURY"”
text: They advertise the hotel as "luxury", but luxury hotels do not have torn and frayed curtains. Granted that did not interfere with our stay, but it does take the shine off the "luxury" claim. The room itself was spacious; the bed comfortable; and clean. But the room had a "funky" smell, like it had been on the smoking floor before the hotel became completely smoke free. They need to refresh the carpets to get more of that smell out. The bathroom was also nice and big, with separate shower. It is located in an ideal location within walking distance of everything downtown. On the whole, it was a comfortable stay. Parking is a bit steep, even with the self park around the corner. But it's still cheaper than NYC.

title: “Life Without a Care? Stay at Hotel Bel-Air.”
text:
A dreadful rhyme I know but frankly this hotel is a fairytale of exclusivity and enchantment. In one sense it is without rival the best hotel in Los Angeles. Let me explain. If arriving after dark you cannot beat the twinkling lights over the water as you cross the bridge to the lobby. Self check in is possible on the i-pads in the rooms but I was processed the traditional way by cheerful staff. My room was a delightful ground floor with a large sunny patio reached by a longish walk past the lozenge shaped pool and several playing fountains. I was totally satisfied with the room including the new technology. Very impressive was the log fire with a pile of logs in the room so you could light it yourself and enjoy the ambiance it leant.
However this hotel is QUIET. Monastery quiet. I felt I had the place to myself with a large staff. Rather like I was in a grand hacienda alone searching in vain for my host who never appeared. It wasn't unpleasant, just unusual. Come the weekend the inevitable wedding appeared. White seats by the pool outside and a ravishing bride swishing around the property all afternoon. I was rather glad to see other people there by this stage. The dining situation is a little too upscale for my tastes. that is to say food is gorgeous but very expensive. A casual cobb salad by the pool for lunch seems unattainable but this is not a criticism just an observation. 
I used the fitness room which was very well laid out if small, and the spa too was attractive. Zero points for the hair salon though which appeared to be smaller than my own wardrobe, claustrophobic and with no natural light. Just one girl working there made for a very dull appointment. I wont be going back there for my blow drys. 
I never got to grips with when the bar was busy during my 6 day stay - I'm sure it's very nice but wasn't appealing to me at the times I went there in the early evening.
Transportation is slow. One house car is available but given the distance to Rodeo it naturally takes longer than more central hotels to get back.
