They should have two really but it's a small price to pay to stay at this divine place. Waiting for a taxi when called can take 15 minutes so extra time must be allotted when going anywhere.
It's best to have a lover if you stay at this hotel as romance oozes from every corner. Honeymooners should beat a path to its door as should A-listers who like reclusivity. I was in none of these categories but nevertheless counted myself one of the luckiest people in the world to get to spend a week in this haven. 
If money is no object try one of the new canyon view suites which looked fabulous but really any room here is worth a stay if only to say you have been.

title: “Great hotel at a great location”
text: We stayed 6 days at Library Hotel and could not have asked for a better hotel. We loved the free wine and cheese after a long day of sightseeing and shopping. The only drawback was the somewhat noisy aircon and the hard mattress.

title: “Can't wait to go back!”
text: What a wonderful experience! This was my first time staying Seattle and could not have asked for more. The Edgewater is a must for anyone wanting to stay within walking distance of the best sights while experiencing clean, comfortable accommodations and impeccable service. The staff were helpful, courteous, and eager to make my stay as worry-free as possible. Six Seven was fabulous - I highly recommend their breakfast and enjoying a cocktail later in the afternoon in the bar area. I can't comment on their dinner menu as I ate out each night. My room was great, the bed was extremely comfortable, and the bathroom was gorgeous - impeccably clean with brand new appliances, stunning shower, and stone floor. There are trains that run by the hotel but they did not disturb me one bit. I didn't have to use them, but the hotel does provide earplugs in the room. All in all, it was a wonderful experience and I am definitely staying there again the next time I'm in Seattle.

title: “Great location - Mediocre service - Dogs in the elevator”
text: We picked this hotel solely because of its proximity to an athletic event we were competing in nearby. For our needs, the price was more than we wanted to pay so we thought we'd at least enjoy ourselves. Front door service was warm and friendly, but beyond that, service was pretty average (or less). We gave up on room service after we tried to order breakfast the night before, the delivery time for breakfast past, and a call to room service revealed they were running at least 45 minutes late because some staff hadn't shown up; no one had bothered to notify us. We went to a Starbuck's around the corner instead. When checking out, while seeing if we were charged for the room service that never came, the receptionist seemed not to be surprised by the event and did not apologize. We were also surprised the first time we encountered a large doberman (very friendly) as we entered an elevator. It didn't take us long to figure out this is a pet-friendly hotel. The room was clean and comfortable - no complaints there. Bottom line: Fantastic location, nice rooms, high price, average service, and pets.

title: “Not up to Marriott standards”
text: My company booked this hotel for 3 days at 240+++/night and I have certain expectations from Marriott hotels. This hotel is NOT worth the money. Hotel room was old, bathroom was small (could not use sink without having to first close the bathroom door), outdated and not that clean. There was no counter space in the bathroom and it took over 5 minutes for the shower to run "hot" water. The rugs in my room were "okay" but in the hall and elevator they were old, dirty and stained. The mini refrigerator was ripped out and there was no room safe. Bed was mostly comfortable and I was able to adjust the room temperature. These are my only 2 positives. I also had a problem with taxes added to my bill that I am still trying to resolve. Staff were "friendly" but no one could actually fix or explain the problem with my bill; they just keep sending me to someone else.

title: “Nice room & great location”
text: We stayed at the New York Marriott East side 9/3-9/5/06. The hotel location is GREAT - 6 blocks from the middle of Times Square or a $5 cab ride. It is an older hotel, in fact I think it said something about it being the tallest hotel in the world in 1920's. That translates to the room layout being somewhat awkward, our closet was tiny, and the elevators are small. They weren't slow to me, but only fit 5-6 people. Nothing in terms of decor looked old or outdated to me. The bedding is wonderful! The rooms are nicely decorated. I did notice some stains on the ceiling, but that didn't make or break my stay. The gym has a great view of the city. We ate the restaurant and the bar and both were good. The concierge was helpful with attractions. It is expensive, but not shocking for a hotel in downtown NYC.

title: “Mixed feelings”
text:
We chose this hotel because we knew we'd be staying in NYC for four nights and wanted room to spread out, and wanted to try to sleep of course. We're here for our daughter's 21st birthday and it's our first time to NYC. I have mixed feelings about the hotel. I know all the buildings here are old, and steam heat has its own issues and can be noisy. I grew up in an old home with radiators and steam heat. You do get used to the banging noise of the pump system and the clanging of the pipes and radiators after a while, but it's constantly there. We had to turn the radiators off (as much as possible, that is) to cool down the rooms to a temperature where we could actually sleep. The A/C units are window units, and I know they can be noisy as I've lived with those as well, so I'm not going to complain about the noise. Actually I sleep better with noise like that, and I need the room cool, so that worked out fine for me.
The kitchen is a full one which is very nice, but the surface light in the microwave is burned out and even when we brought it to the attention of the management it wasn't fixed. The light in the hallway was burned out and again a staff member even came up but it wasn't fixed. Not a very big deal since this is a penthouse suite with two bedrooms and we have plenty of light, but I'm still surprised the lights weren't replaced.
The bathrooms are seriously too small. Almost no counter space and little room to move around. The water pressure in the shower fluctuates, as does the water temperature, so be forewarned. There is no tub up here - only two full bathrooms with large showers. 
The bedrooms are interesting. One is barely large enough to move around the bed and there are only two nightstands. No dresser or chair to put a suitcase or other belongings off the floor. We took the clothes drying racks out of the closet in the other bedroom and put our suitcases on them. I don't put things on the floor of hotel rooms if I can help it. Speaking of floors, they're hardwood which is really nice, and there are rugs as well. The other bedroom is larger, but again only one nightstand and a stand for the TV. Not even a chair.
The TV's are nice - flatscreens and the reception is good. The Internet is blazing fast and very reliable - a plus for most of us. There is a safe but we had to get a staff member to come up and unlock it because some dolt before us locked it. DUH, people. Have some consideration and leave the safe unlocked for the next guest, okay? They don't know the passcode you set, idiot.
The breakfast is free but really poor. Two mornings in a row now sausage and rubbery poached eggs. The room is seriously too small to accommodate more than a few people at once comfortably, and it only took two obnoxious teens who seemed to be unaware there were others waiting in line to get to things, who were here both mornings now, monopolizing everything from the waffle maker to the milk dispenser for cereal, to ruin the experience.
I've read the other reviews about the street noise and the parking garage in the back of the property, but because we're up this high with a private, wrap-around balcony and a ten foot high concrete wall around it, we can't hear anything in the back (our penthouse faces East 49th Street) and the street noise would be preferable to the banging and clanging of the pump system and the steam heat. 
The staff has been great so far. Helpful and smiling. Housekeeping only freshened up one bedroom yesterday so we'll see what happens this morning. And they replaced our coffee maker with a smaller one and we still don't know why. On the other hand, we had complementary cookies and water upon arrival, and the coffee itself was replaced, and there is 24 hour free coffee and beverages down in the breakfast room.

title: “My 4-day weekend in San Diego ROCKED!”
text:
I traveled to San Diego recently for a 4-day weekend and my stay at the Hard Rock Hotel was brilliant!
In addition to being a beautiful property, the Hard Rock Team know the meaning of customer service! Being a Road Warrior (spending more than 120 nights on the road each year) it was refreshing to be surprised by customer care and a commitment to quality.
I highly recommend this hotel to anyone visiting San Diego, especially for those who enjoy great music, great food and a great time!

title: “Decent Place, Decent Price”
text:
This hotel is in an EXCELLENT location on Belt Line. There are so many restaurants to choose from, and all within a short drive or walk. The staff were extremely friendly and helpful, and although the room itself could have used a wee facelift, overall it was clean, and acceptable.
The only disappointment was the continental breakfast which I thought lacked freshness (bread and fruit wise), but otherwise was edible.

title: “Great Hotel-Staff was TOP Notch”
text:
The Hampton room was very spacious (studio) with comfy beds, chairs, kitchenette, etc. The staff went above and beyond to accommodate our needs. For instance, we returned our rental car the night before and they picked us up at the airport and brought us back to the hotel -NO QUESTIONS asked. And with a smile to boot. They were more than happy to map out the mall and route to the Hard Rock Cafe (which was also top notch food and service for a hard Rock-and we have visited our share of Hard Rocks-NYC, Tokyo, Cancun....). We mentioned to the Hampton staff that we had a very early morning flight and would miss the breakfast. They said--No worries, we'll pack a breakfast to go! Better yet, they said they'll set up early and we can help ourselves. We had great coffee, yogurt, fresh fruit, toast, etc. The night before, they had fresh large soft pretzels, nachos and cheese, tacos, etc. It looked good, but we passed because we just had dinner. But it was a nice gesture for those just checking in from a flight or long drive.
I would definitely stay there again and would recommend them to everyone! No REGRETS!

title: “Great Location, excellent service but bad gym!"”
text:
I stay here weekly for business and the location is great. Walking distance to the Inner Harbor, Camden Yards, Federal Hill, Fells Point and downtown Baltimore.
The rooms are standard rooms but the service is above average. People really care about helping you have a positive experience.
The one complaint is the gym. It is awful. There is 1 treadmill, 1 eliptical and 2 bikes. The space is smaller than a standard room. There are dumbells and a weight machine but it reminds me of the 80's.
Overall a pretty good hotel.

title: “Good hotel and location.”
text:
Stayed here with our 2 teenagers while visiting DC over Father's day weekend. Good location. Close to the subway and well within walking distance of national mall. It was busy this weekend but not a problem. Great breakfast. Valet service was great and very helpful!
We were in a suite. Nice having the bedroom in the back separated from the living area.

title: “Clean, Convenient, Great Stay!”
text:
Stayed here one night in a Queen room while on business in Austin. Great location to the downtown business area, State Capitol and Univ. of Texas. Very friendly staff, boutique feel, and upscale rooms made this a great place to stay. The bathroom was modern, with granite counters, newly updated shower and floors, and luxurious linens. Comfortable bed and lots of room to move around. Would loved to have been able to stay longer and take advantage of the restaurant and other services available. Felt much more like a bed and breakfast than a typical big-city hotel.
Will definitely come back next time I'm in Austin!

title: “Generally one of the better hotels in NYC”
text:
On the whole, Hotel Mela is a good bet if you want something decent in NYC. Having travelled to NYC every year for the last five years and stayed at different hotels, I must say Hotel Mela does provide good value for money.
1. Location, Location, Location
The best feature of this hotel is its location. It's right in the centre of all the action, Times Square. You will have no issue with food, transportation or shopping.
2. Free Wifi
The whole place has complimentary Wifi service (from the hotel lobby to my deluxe King room). This is great! 
3. The toiletries are magnificent.
The H2O toiletries are great. They smell really great. Much better than what some of the hotels are providing.
4. Room
The room is big! That's partly because I've got a corner room and it's a deluxe King. Enough space for my 4 huge luggages. And they do have a very comfy bed. The only complaint is that the service can be quite inconsistent (if I compare my experience with the other reviewers). I did not get any turn down service at ALL! No chocolates or what so ever. Hmmm.... have they shortchanged me?
5. My ONLY Complaint
I've requested for an early check-in because I had endured a 25-hour flight and arrived in NYC at 6am in the morning. Instead of trying to find me a room at the earliest possible time, the front desk staff insisted that I come back again at 3pm (the official check-in time). They did not even offer to call us if the room became available. The only helpful thing they did was to allow me to leave my luggages at the hotel while my partner and I roamed NYC in zombie-like state. No good for a first impression.

title: “Will Never Stay Here Again”
text:
I will never stay here again for the following reasons:
1) Reserved a non-smoking room and was given a smoking room. After complaining (nicely) for a long time a non-smoking room was "found" for me. When I reached the room, a bell-man was removing someone else's bags! I hope the guy that got kicked out was okay.
2) Internet was broken during my stay
3) Sink flooded all over the bathroom floor
4) No iron in the room - the first iron that was brought up for me was broken. A replacement iron was brought up 30 minutes later where I was asked if I new how an iron worked...
5) Room service food (a salad) was delivered without fork/spoon/knife. Another 20 minutes went by and then I got my flatware. Food was cold by that point.
6) Located next to Farragut West stop, but that entrance isn't open all day so it is actually deceiving. Most of the dining options nearby close around 5pm so the location isn't as great as advertised.
This time of year there are plenty other places for similar prices that have been better.

title: “Location only benefit. They charge for internet access!”
text:
This place has a great location but so do most hotels downtown. It is a typical conference/convention hotel. The rooms are small but I guess they have to be to fit 1000 of them in the place. The worst things are what they charge for. 12.95 daily for internet access but it is free on the first 2 floors which means it is free for everyone except those paying to stay there. Very bad idea. Even McDonalds has free internet! Come on people! You have to request a refrigerator for your room but it is free. Parking is 25.00/day. Really excessive but oh well. What are you gonna do. The people next to us had babies. You can easily hear them through the walls. They probably heard ours too.
 If we had to do it over again we would stay somewhere else.

title: “Scrupulously Clean and Stellar Service”
text:
I stayed at this hotel for over a month while accompanying my husband on business and we enjoyed every minute of it! This is an extremely clean hotel throughout and the rooms are in like new condition as the hotel is only a year old. The kitchenette in the room included a full size fridge, a mini-dishwasher, a full size sink, a full size coffee maker, and an electric cooktop (no oven). The overall soundproofing of the rooms was above average, the beds and bedding were exceptionally comfortable, and the free breakfast buffet was a delicious value. The laundromat area could be a bit larger--there are 4 washers and 4 dryers for over 200 guest rooms--but it was a much appreciated convenience having a clean and bright laundry in the hotel. The pool is definitely lacking here--it is very small, more like an oversized spa--and it is only 3 feet deep. The exercise facility was adequate; however, be advised that skilled photography on the website makes the gym appear larger than it actually is. There are 4 pieces of cardio equipment but only a tiny weight bench with a few dumbells. As an avid gym-goer, I got around this issue by joining a 24 Hour Fitness facility in Horton Plaza, about a 10-15 minute walk from the hotel.
The staff at The Residence Inn were truly professional and always courteous. It was a pleasure dealing with each and every employee here! Valet parking is mandatory (and expensive at $32/night), however, the valets were extremely prompt, polite, and attentive--on some occasions, they literally RAN to open the lobby doors for us. The dining room staff is extremely efficient and friendly as are the front desk and housekeeping staff. In addition, the maintenance department is equally attentive; I broke a coffee carafe and in under 5 minutes, a maintenance worker had removed the broken glass and thoroughly swept and vacuumed the room! The service here is truly exemplary.
The location, in the Gaslamp area of downtown, is a vibrant, exciting one. There are scores of restaurants and bars within easy walking distance, and although the area draws a young crowd of party-goers, we never heard any street noise inside of the hotel. 
I loved staying at the Residence Inn Gaslamp, and despite a few minor drawbacks, would recommend this hotel to a friend.

title: “Lovely hotel, great staff”
text: Stayed here the weekend of my hubby's funeral. What a beautiful hotel -- everything appeared brand new. Everyone was so wonderful to us. We were in room 338. Lovely eastern facing view, overlooking the swimming pool. At night we sat at the firepit by the pool, sipping our wine.

title: “Fairly priced in quiet neighborhood yet walkable”
text: Fully renovated older Hilton and typically small rooms for Manhattan yet nicely situated for quiet nights. There was an interesting view of the top floors of the Empire State building from the window. Staff at front desk were accomodating. My only complaint: I still don't understand why these major brands still charge for internet - it is almost like charging for a shower in the morning. Perhaps it is about losing revenues by not using the telephones in the room.

title: “Fine Hotel--Good Service”
text: I was very impressed by the InterContinental. The service was great from the minute my cab arrived at the hotel. No wait to get a room. And the room is very clean and well-appointed. If you are looking for a hotel in mid-town on the east side, this hotel is perfect. I have stayed at many other hotels in the same general vicinity (e.g., Grand Hyatt, W, Waldorf-Astoria), and I think the InterContinental is the best of the group.

title: “We should be more like Fernando!”
text:
My Wife, Daughter and I stayed at the Hilton SD Resort & Spa. We pulled up to the lobby and were greeted by Fernando. With a big smile he asked us where we were from. He proceeded to carry on a conversation about our home baseball team. If you choose to stay at this property, I hope Fernando is the bellman on duty, because he knows how to make you feel like family.
There was a small problem in getting our room ready for us to check in. In return for the delay, the front desk person upgraded us to larger room with a beautiful view of Mission Bay. I applaud the front desk staff for taking the initiative to keep our stay going in a positive direction.
This positive can do attitude was present over a majority of the property.
We ate breakfast every norning at the Acqua Bistro on property. If there was a place that didn't seem to keep the positive attitude that I saw in many other places on the property, it would be the Acqua Hostess' station at breakfast time. They need to spend time with Fernando, I'm sure his attitude is infectious.
Once you get seated for breakfast, things get much better. Carol was our server. She must be related to Fernando. She had a big smile and was also curious where we were from. She made us feel at home and gave us great service. She also was great at giving us tips of great places to see that were not your typical tourist destinations. She is also a great asset to the property.
The other person from the Acqua Bistro that was a stand out was Roberto, the busser. I'm guessing he is Fernando's brother. He was happy, smiling, gracoius, polite. He also made us feel like we were home. Keep up the great work Roberto.
The pool is great. It is clean, and what a view of the bay. The wait staff is there if you need anything. I did enjoy my time at the pool.
The other area that surprized me was the gift shop. The staff there was very helpful in getting us tickets to local attractions. They kept excellent hours so if you needed something at 8 or 9:00 they were open. They offer a good balance of merchandise for sale. A little food, a little clothing, some take home trinkets, fresh fruit and some cold foods as well. I thought it offered an excellent selection with out offering too much.
In closing, this is a GREAT property! Our family was sad to leave after our 6 night stay. It is easy to find. It is located in a place that makes it easy to get to many of the major attractions. The staff there is FANTASTIC. Did I mention Fernando? They make you feel welcome, at home and like you are welcome to return at any time. The pool is great and the on property services met all our needs. We look forward to our next visit. 
Thank you Hilton San Diego Resort & Spa

title: “Fun hotel, great location!”
text:
I enjoyed my stay at Dream - it was centrally located for walking/subway and the rooms were great! We had a gorgeous view of the empire state building from our room and everything was clean and modern. Plus, I loved the huge stuffed polar bear (and wolf) - definitely made a fun environment. 
Our first room did smell like smoke but I called right away and the bellman came right up and escorted us to another room very quickly! Good service! 
Would definitely stay here again!

title: “DO NOT STAY HERE, THEY OVERCHARE YOUR CREDIT CARD”
text: The Hotel WAY overchared my bank account and REFUSED to correct the issus, now I will have months of disputes and paperwork. The Hotel policy is that you sign a BLANK credit card slip, that they complete apparently at the staff's discretion. I was excited to find a place with a ood location (almost Riverwalk). Great peices, and nice rooms. I was traveling with friends and had 2 rooms. I gave the front desk one card for the first night and a second. When I called my credit card company to check the available credit, before final checkout, I discovered that I had been chared an extra $115 and $112.70 on the first card, I attempted to discuss the mistake with Assistant General Manager (Letty Ramos) who could not "find" the credit card charges within her system and therefore refused to acknowledge that they existed. She also said she is the only manager available and said that the General Manager is "out of the country" but that I can e-mail him. She was rude and uninterested in correctin the hotel's mistake. Ms. Ramos refused to discuss the chares with my bank (credit card company) and was very unproffessional. It is a shame that the billing pactices are so lax because were I billed correctly, this would have been a wonderful place to stay. It is unfortunant that now I will have months of paperwork and charge disputes when a reasonable issue could have corrected the problem before checkout. The housekeeping staff is great. The location was good, and prices were reasonable, but now all I will remember is being disrespected and disregarded by th Hotel GM. Sadly, we will not be back.

title: “Hotel Carlton, a Joie de Vivre Boutique Hotel”
text: This was my 8th trip to San Francisco and my favorite hotel experience. This time was a mother-daughter "bonding trip" and it couldn't have been better. Our room was on the 5th floor with two large beds. The room was very clean, the sheets were soft and there was plenty of room for two grown people who cannot figure out how to pack for a week. The staff was eager to answer questions and seemed happy to be there - smiling faces and all. Even the cleaning lady was fun to visit with. The location is good for using the MUNI system, though if you arrive from the airport via the BART, you may want to get a taxi unless you have packed light and have wheels on your luggage. I was happy to trade a "continental breakfast" for the wine time in the front lobby each evening. If you like to visit with people from all over the world, you are much more likely to strike up a conversation in the evening over a glass of wine than a sit in a break room early in the morning with a bagel. The restaurant "SAHA" within the hotel was excellent and my only regret is not eating more meals there. I write a food column for a LGBT magazine and needed to check out a number of places to eat, but even at one of the most strongly recommended places, I was wishing I were at SAHA. I will definitely return to the Hotel Carlton. Great experience! And did I mention it is a "green" hotel? - Bonus!

title: “This is the one!”
text: Just returned from 3 night NYC trip for our daughter's graduation gift. We loved the Doubletree. Great location!! We love the Olive Garden & it was right across the street. McDonalds is 2 doors down for those with small children. A NYC information center is right next door with free internet access. My daughters loved being able to IM friends from NYC! The rooms were very nice & clean. If I did it again with the 4 of us I would get a room with 2 beds instead of the king & sleeper I opted for to save $. The sleeper was not comfortable enough for 2 teenage girls but that was my fault. Small children would be fine. There were only 3 drawers for 4 people so that was a little tight but other than that it was wonderful. Staff was very friendly & helpful. We were able to store our luggage on the day we left until it was time for us to leave for the airport. Times Square Studios is just 2 blocks down for those planning on going to Good Morning America. And the ticket booth with 50% discounts to the plays is in the median directly across from the hotel. Like I said, great location! Subway stop going downtown to World Trade Center site and Statue of Liberty ferry is right across the street. Our original plan was to make this a once in a liftime trip but we will definitely go back & stay at the Doubletree!

title: “Great Hotel, Great Price, Good for exploring Hollywood”
text: This hotel is conveniently located around the corner from the Chinese Theatre. At the intersection is a Baja fast food burrito joint that was heaven to the palate after living in the UK for 2 years. While a car is highly recommended for getting around Hollywood to explore this was about as good as you could get for seeing the area without one. Staff were friendly and helpful (and magicians) and the room had a fantastic king size bed. I might be nit picking but the only thing keeping this hotel from an excellent review was the frigid pool.

title: “Classic Hotel Experience”
text:
The Adolphus is most definitely an "old school" hotel that earns its reputation with fine service and an elegant atmosphere. the public areas of the hotel are reminiscent of an English estate, the rooms, are very nice and well decorated but beginning to show a bit of age - nothing major - just an observation. The staff is knowledgeable, friendly and efficient.
If you prefer a classic, "old school" luxury hotel over the trendy, flashy type, you'll be very happy at the Adolphus. P.S. the free Internet is a nice feature as so many hotels charge an arm and a leg for access.

title: “Great relaxing stay before flight”
text:
We had a few things to do in Houston before departing after a US Road Trip. After staying at the Sheraton in LA and deciding we were impressed with the chain we booked in to this one near the airport.
 Very comfortable; friendly lady in the gift shop downstairs, nice swimming pools (an indoor and an outdoor so you have the option!) 
Definitely recommend the club levels - the lounge area has a very nice breakfast layout which is attended by a member of staff. The ones we encountered (we stayed 3 nights) we pleasant, friendly and helpful. 
We were on the top floor overlooking the airport with aircraft (sometimes two at a time!) taking off directly towards us; and barely heard a thing! Definitely no noise problems.

title: “Premium hotel in a prime location”
text:
This is one of the nicest hotels I have stayed in, possibly better than the Double Tree Hilton in Dubai.
Situated in lower Manhattan less than 2 minutes from Ground Zero and with the Irish Hunger Memorial (less depressing than it sounds) just outside the front doors, and Battery park easily accesible. There is plenty to see and do.
The room I had was spacious with a lounge, toilet and sink, separate large shower and a main bedroom. The bedroom and lounge both had large flat screen TVs. Wi Fi was available at $14.95 for 24 hours and was a good strong connection, though you could only have one device connected at a time. No good if you have a family staying.
I didn't use the onsite bar, restaurant or gym. Deciding to eat out during my stay, and far too lazy to hit the gym. Also in the interest of fairness, I didn't have to pay for my room either, so price wise it is whether or not its in your budget. (I have omitted these sections from my rating)
The staff were all polite and exceptionally helpful, not something you always experience at the higher end of the market.
For me it was the perfect starting point to explore lower Manhattan on foot and make my way up through the city, then crash out once my street weary legs shuffled me back.
Superb hotel.

title: “Top Notch Service and Good Accommodations”
text: On a recent stay we experienced excellent service from the hotel staff. They gave us an upgrade to a large suite without asking. In addition, hotel staff were pleasant and very accommodating on all requests. The room was very spacious, however it's in need of updating .... carpet, decor and especially the bathroom. Everything functioned well and it didn't detracted from our really good experience. I highly recommend this hotel based on price, professional staff and good location.

title: “Stayed for Just One Night, But it Was GREAT!”
text: My daughter and I stayed for just one night, but the location, service, and accommodations were excellent. The hotel was very quiet and extremely convenient to the airport, shopping, and restaurants. Highly recommend this Hilton Garden Inn.

title: “Great Hotel ! Clean - very modern and perfectly romantic!”
text:
Stayed at the Hilton Garden Inn Times Square from 5th - 9th December and it was fabulous! Was expecting it to be quite small and not very modern - (or clean for that matter!) But was very very impressed. The location is fantastic - we could walk everywhere and times square is right around the corner. 
Nice and close to a really good selection of restaurants - (We would highly recommend booking a table at Gallaghers Steak House which is not very far - Steaks like no where on earth!)And of course Broadway!
Room was very clean, modern and not small at all. Everything you could want in a room! Restaurant is more expensive than we thought, but very nice... especially breakfast (big!)!
Only comment is that it is very much a businessmans hotel - not very touristy.

title: “A very nice stay”
text:
My husband, 2 children and I stayed for 3 nights in early October while my husband attended a conference and had a lovely stay. The staff was very friendly and accommodating, from the reservationist, to the bellhop, to the front desk, to the concierge, to the maid service, even the maintenance guy at the pool was nice. As tourists, we received great tips on local restaurants and transportation. 
Our room was outstanding - I didn't find the decor or lobby "dated" or "tired" at all. It looked very updated to me - and our room furnishings, in fact, looked new. We had a corner room with fantastic views. Elevators were fast - no waiting. The pool was great for kids and the hot tub was awesome. We didn't eat at the hotel, as there are so many eating options around (Cosi is a great place to bring kids, and Pietro's was also very good). The location of the hotel is great. We walked all the way west to the Franklin Institute and east to the Liberty Bell. With two young kids, even - the Philly Phlash that so many recommended drove right past everyone waiting at city hall, (we didn't even see another one for over half an hour) and at Penn's Landing, an empty vehicle sat there forever, stranding a dozen tourists. So much for "pickups every 12 minutes." I don't think so.
It's hard to believe that from week to week people have such vastly different experiences at this hotel. How can the ultra-friendly people we encountered the weekend we stayed there change into surly, rude jerks the next? Maybe because the guests can also be surly, rude jerks? I'm just speculating.
As for parking, the garage is attached to the hotel - so it's very convenient. A lot of hotels downtown have parking A Block Away - which is lot more inconvenient than having to climb a few steps. If you don't want that hassle, you can pay a few extra bucks for valet service. At any rate, you can park your car at the door and the bellhop will unload your stuff and take it up to your room for you.
Free continental breakfast would be nice, but as far as in-room instant coffee goes, the Wolfgang Puck stuff was pallatable. And the warm cookies at check-in? YUM.

title: “Limited travel $$ = Clean, spacious, convenient, terrific guest service, quiet”
text: My friends and I were very surprised and happy with our impulse discovery! HUGE, CLEAN room, 2 comfy king size beds, quiet, convenient access for all our tourist adventures... Family owners on sight and so very pleasant and helpful. My/our first choice next trip.....

title: “Great Service all around!”
text: The service at the Westin Riverwalk is great. I came to San Antonio for a night and the staff was very helpful. Their Director of Front Office- Ronnie, was very accommodating with providing an early check in. After running into him in the lobby, I asked for some good running routes. He provided me with a small running map outlining a 3 mile loop- It was perfect! It was so nice for him to stop what he was doing just to help me out! Later that evening, I had for got my cell phone charger and the lady at the front Desk, Wendy I believe her name is so kindly let me borrow hers. The next morning at check out she was working there again and remembered who I was! Talk about feeling special! Ronnie and his staff made my short trip to San Antonio a great one! I will definitely recommend this hotel to others and cant wait to stay there again!

title: “Great inexpensive hotel”
text: 6 ladies stayed in 2 double rooms at this hotel for 2 nights before a cruise out of NYC. We had absolutely no complaints. 1 room overlooked the pool and was very quiet and the other on the 5th floor overlooked the street but we didn't find the street noise bad. Safe & clean. Walking distance to everything we wanted to see. Evangaline in gift shop made arrangements for a van to take us to our cruise and saved us about $50. Unless you really want to pay "big bucks" for a fancy hotel, stay here. We will again.

title: “Amazing Service”
text: I recently stayed at The MAve and had an experience second to none. The staff was amazing from the time we walked in until our final goodbye. The bed made in hard to leave the room, H20 products as well as the rain head showers are awesome, and the staff really sealed the deal. I felt like I had a personal assistant to the city, great recomendations in the area, and attention to deatail made my stay the best I have had in NYC.

title: “Lovely stay in style”
text: Just spent a lovely weekend night at the W New York. We were upgraded to fabulous suite and it was ...well, fabulous. Comfortable bed and attentive service made for another cool stay at what is quickly becoming my favorite hotel in NYC. Can't wait to try out the free ride in the new Acura on my next visit. We will be back.

title: “Great SD Location”
text: Great hotel with an amazing atmosphere. All the staff was very helpful and accommodating. Great place to stay when heading to a baseball game or wanting to be in the heart of all the downtown action. Had a great gym that I was able to use to work out all the toxins from the night before! A little bummed that the pool was closed for a private event but they concierge was super helpful in telling us that the Omni next door would take us!! Thank you HRSD for a great opening day experience!!

author.location: San Luis Obispo, California, United States

title: “Does the job”
text: A reasonable crash pad. Ok location - 7 minutes walk from 51st St. subway. Good views from roof terrace a bonus. Tiny rooms but beds were fortunately comfortable. Noisy AC so take earplugs. Bars and restaurants nearby. Es-a-bagel round the corner on 3rd is a great breakfast spot if you need a break from the claustraphobia and persistent Muzak of the Pod.

title: “Great, Fun Hotel”
text: This is a wonderful hotel, with friendly, helpful staff across the board; every staff person we encountered called us by name. The atmosphere is fun, and the hotel is very nice. The bar area is hopping in the evening. Our room was large, and although we booked a regular room, was actually a suite as a result of an upgrade.

title: “Just one night, but great hotel!”
text:
I selected this hotel because of the general proximity to the airport for an early morning (really, really early!) flight. It was a great choice! The hotel is clean, updated, serves a hot breakfast (which I missed because of my early flight), and a really nicely landscaped pool and patio area. 
I messed up my reservation by one day, but the hotel staff (Anthony, think) was very polite, helpful, and efficient. I will be back to Texas a lot because I have a new granddaughter in Corpus. Flight costs are best in/out of San Antonio. I will absolutely stay at the Antonian on future trips to ease the outbound flight process.

title: “Fabulous Hotel in DC!”
text: My husband and I went to Washington DC this summer and stayed at the Hotel Lombardy for a week. The hotel was better than I could've imagined! Very friendly staff and they were very accomodating throughout the entire week. The hotel was extremely clean and was located in great spot! We walked to the White House (just about 3 blocks down) every morning, along with other attractions that were very close by. Would definitely recommend this to a friend and will definitely stay again on our next trip to D.C.

title: “Awful...but awful service!”
text:
The stay couldn't be worse...one thing after the other. My fiance and I went to celebrate our first Valentines day together in this hotel...to begin with the valet parking guy is the bellboy, so you need to go into the hotel and ask so they can start the search for him...so we waited. The room that my fiancee had reserved was not available and the reason the hotel management gave us was that Expedia and Travelocity had overbooked the hotel, so they gave us a cheaper room. As we walked into the restaurant for dinner, no hostess or anybody to seat us...so we seated ourselves in. During dinner we had to wait for quite long periods of time to get each thing...starting with taking our order, up to my fiance had to stand up a couple of times to ask for things, and we weren't the only ones. There was only one waitress for all the tables, and she was also helping in the bar, so you can imagine the wait.....besides her manners of scratching the menu items with a pen, marking the ones that were no longer available, I thought things could get worse. And the food was terrible too...but the worst of it was the desert, two tiny Cosco brownie cupcakes with a vallina scoop and that was for the both of us. 
Once we walked into our room, we could hear all the humming and conversation of our next door neighbors through the vents...imagine, it was Valentines day. No roses were in the room either as my fiance was promised as part of the Valentines special. Almost no water in the shower, my fiance had to take a cup to collect the water and shower with it. Plus previously somebody had written "TE AMO" on the bathroom's mirror (and it was'nt us) , so we could tell it was never cleaned. Bad, bad experience...we were cut between laughing and the fact that we couldn't believe it!

title: “Unforgettable!”
text:
As I had a very poor experience at the Four Seasons Hotel in Boston in June I was hesitating to go to the FS in Philly, then I decided to and I had the surprise to find he FS I remembered back in full force: perfect service from the bell man and porter to waiters, room was well appointed and spotlessly clean.
 if i had to find a glitch was the cold unwelcoming check in and out and poor quality of coffee (same as in San Francisco!) whereas quality of food was superb from breakfast to brunch and dinner. 
 A perfect location and even if not a new hotel, as some other tripadvisor members pointed out, it has lots of charm and it is extremely well kept and run.
A must go in Philly!

title: “Perfect!”
text: Had a wonderful stay! The room was very nice, staff was very friendly and the location was perfect. I will stay here again!

title: “Business travelers beware”
text:
I stayed here for three nights with colleagues. We had a very important package delivered via overnight FedEx to the hotel on our second morning there. Despite noting both our name, room number and telephone number on the package, it was not given to us. Even after checking with the front desk, the package was not located. In fact, it was only after calling the hotel the week AFTER we stayed there, trying to track down the package, that they finally found it. 
Other frustrations:
- the area in front of the hotel that you must pass through in order to park your car is frequently blocked, leaving you waiting for upwards of ten minutes just to get into the parking garage at times
- the internet connection is not reliable and wireless is not available in the rooms
Plusses:
- location is good
- Starbucks nearby

title: “One thing after another...”
text:
1) Rooms are not clean, in my book anyway. The carpet in my room looked well worn, and smelled like a wet dog! The surface areas were clean, but I couldn't get past the carpet!
2) They failed to mention the $9 per day parking fee until after I was checked in! The thing that really griped me was that they left the "security" gate arm up during the majority of my six days staying there. What's the point? 
3) I posted a "no service" tag on my front door. They complied with that, however, when I did ask for housekeeping service, it was never done! When I returned to my room that evening and had NO towels and an over-flowing trash can I was irritated! The "electrical engineer" came up and brought me T.P. as well as changed my garbage. How embarrasing!
4) After we needed to extend our stay for several days (yes, we are glutons for punishment!) the staff failed to tell us our room key and gate key had to be re-activated! I only found out after trying to get into my room @ midnight and be denied. I don't want to talk about how bad I needed to use the restroom!
5) If you like the waters temp. near Alaska then this is the pool for you! My kids wouldn't go into the pool since the "heated" water was freezing! The manager agreeed that it was not comfortable for him either, and agreed to turn it up a bit. Yeah, right! It never happened!
6) Ice machine on our floor was broken for four of the six days we stayed. When reported to the front desk we were told that they had one on every floor. Who goes for ice in their pj's? I do and it's bad enough going across the hall in pj's never-the-less down the elevator! 
NOW THE GOOD THINGS...
1) Free USA Today M-F delivered to your room!
2) Most property staff is great.
3) Free shuttle to Universal Studios and City Walk seven days a week
4) Restaurant on-site stays open for breakfast, lunch and dinner.
5) Gift shop downstairs (gifs and food items)
6) Great pillows!
7) Lounge type chair w/ottoman in room/desk/two phones/coffee maker 
 had it's own counter, not kept on the sink like many properties/balcony/ tennis courts/ down the street from grocery store with many shops and Starbucks.
8) Travel coupon accepted from magazine. Room was discounted from 
 $105 to $89.
9) Had a Beverly Garland sighting our first day!

title: “Loved it”
text: The hotel was situated in a wonderful location -- surrounded by everything you want to see, do and eat while visiting a city.The room was comfortable room -- so much so I didn't want to get out of bed, but wanted to do the town. Was there for a conference -- meeting rooms were good and food was delicious. The hotel has the fastest, smoothest elevators that I have ever ridden in.

title: “Very quiet and confortable”
text: My husband and I had to come to San Antoinio for some emergency work. We found the Fairfield Inn & Suites to be very quiet and confortable. The rooms were large enough for us and the bed was quite nice with 5 feather pillows, which we really do like!! No problems with the breakfast they serve each morning. We would most likely return for a stay here.

title: “A Little GEM in the heart of Chelsea”
text:
As a former resident of Chelsea, it was a pleasure to see the blighted Allerton SRO Hotel turned into a charming little neighborhood GEM. Little, however, does not begin to describe the size of the rooms. Tiny is more appropriate, even by NYC standards. The queen bed room I had measured 10'x10'. Despite the tiny footprint, the room was completely functional, attractively furnished and immaculately clean. The bathroom was also very attractive and new--it lacked a bathtub but had a nice shower.
This appears to be a well managed, albeit a very new property. The staff encountered on the premises were all very friendly, professional, helpful and courteous--it really made a difference I believe for me and helped me overlook the things I didn't like about the hotel.
So, the upside of this hotel is that it is new, very clean, smartly yet simply decorated, has a great Chelsea location off 8th Av, attentive staff. The downside of this hotel are the tiny rooms--really best suited for one person or a very intimate couple with little luggage. Not meant for the traveler who needs to spread out, store lots of belongings, desires a window facing the street or spends much time in a hotel room. Very few rooms in the hotel have street views--most face a narrow airshaft. Check-out time is an early 11 a.m. but I had no problem getting a slightly later departure time when I stayed there. Bathroom lacks sufficient shelf space, bedroom lacks sufficient storage space.
All things considered, I would recommend this property at the right price. I paid only $105/night--a bargain in Manhattan, and was thoroughly pleased. I probably would only hesitate if rates were over $175, depending on what other comparable properties were charging at the time. As long as this property maintains its level of cleanliness and maintenance and its professional staffing, it will be easy to forgive the closet sized rooms and viewless windows.
Right now, the GEM Hotel Chelsea is a gem--I hope it stays that way.

title: “Excellent Service ,Great Location.”
text: The minute we walked in the staff was very attentive. Hotel was very clean everyone going out of there way to be helpful. The location was great we never had to drive while here. Everything with in walking distance or a $5 cab drive if you get lazy. We will definatly stay here again

title: “Great place to stay!!”
text: I visited new york for the first time in march, therefore i had no idea what kind of hotel i was getting into so i read users reviews and looked at many photos and found that the san carlos had very few low reviews so for the price i was sure i picked a great hotel, once i told many people i was going to new york and staying there no one had ever hear of this hotel therefore i got a little worried. Once i got to new york and got off the bus at grand central station, i ended up walking about 7 blocks to find myself walking into a very poor area, again i got a little worried that i paid a good amount of money for a low hotel, but once i turned the block and saw this hotel i was very pleased just by seeing the outside, this hotel is just about the nicest hotel in the area! The man at the front desk was very nice and helpful, the room was VERY clean and quite, it had everything it said it would, fridge, microwave, bathrobes, mini bar and lots of room for a new york hotel! the breakfast was great also! This hotel is located perfect to everything also, there is a subway stop on the same corner and its just up the street from rockerfeller center. Every time i return to New York i will be staying here again! I was very pleased!!!

title: “Excellent stay at the Fairmont”
text:
I spent a Saturday night at the Fairmont with 3 other friends (mid/late-20s), and all 4 of us thoroughly enjoyed the stay. 
We had paid very cheap internet-only rates for each of our two rooms (which made it all the more enjoyable), but I suspect we would still have been happy if we had paid full price.
The front desk were courteous and were happy to place us in adjoining rooms - each of which was well furnished with a large HD tv, couch, and elegant bathroom. 
My only minor complaint was the charge to use the internet, which I think is ridiculous for a 4-5* hotel (but seemingly most other hotels do this too). The staff at the hotel's sushi bar (where we had drinks but not food) were incredibly nice, as was the concierge who got us into priority seating at Ginos East Pizza. 
I would thoroughly recommend the Fairmont

title: “Nice Hotel”
text: My flight was cancelled out of SFO so I needed a place to stay for the night. I was in Union Square so I looked for something close. After looking through all the different funky hotels I settled on this one. One cause of price and the other location. It's right in Union Square. The staff was very friendly and helpful. The printer in the business center was out of ink so they let me print my boarding pass from one of the computers at the front desk. That was surprising. The rooms are quaint and clean. The bed was very comfortable. I see this hotel as a good base if your going to be out all day taking in the sights and dining. Overall a good deal.

title: “Excellent hotel, great location, bit noisy”
text:
Great, modern, clean hotel. Great views of Venice Beach. There is a roof top bar which can be a bit noisy if you are staying on the sixth floor (you can hear the music in your room) but as I was jetlagged this wasn't a problem, and am pretty sure it ends before 11 or midnight.
Apart from that great staff, good rooms. Wld recommend.

title: “Good all round and would use again”
text:
We stopped here for new year and had a great time. We enjoyed everything about it. Being in new york we hardly stayed in hotel but i was pleased with it. The main pro was the way in which staff helped me and my wife with probem we had, 1st class service. 
Would stay there again, loved the breakfast and the bar was nice but pricey!

title: “Beautifully updated hotel”
text:
Apparently, this hotel has gone through some recent renovations, and we found it to be quite nice. The hotel lobby was beautiful, our room was large and clean, and the hotel staff were extremely helpful 
Nice location in the heart of the city. I do wish we had the view from the other side of the hotel however.

title: “good location, beautiful historic building”
text: Historic building has been restored, beautiful lobby. Ceiling is amazing. Location is excellent, inside the loop, several subway stops around hotel. Walking distance to Grant Park, including the millenium park art museum and Buckingham Fountain. If you don't mind walking, we walked down to the aquarium and planetarium. We also walked up to the river for a boat tour an window shopped the magnificent mile.

title: “very nice”
text: We received excellent customer service at check in with a free upgrade. The room was lovely and large, the linens/bed was wonderfully comfortable. Everthing was quiet and the assistance from everyone quite nice. The only drawback was the breakfast in the lovely atrium. Service took forever and the food was just so-so. Otherwise the location is fantastic as far as going anywhere in the city.

title: “Great location; very friendly and professional staff.”
text: Everyone was very friendly and helpful. Loved the convenience to downtown shopping and restaurants.

title: “Very Nice Airport Hotel”
text:
I was here overnight between connecting flights. Upon arrival I called for the shuttle which arrived in less than 10 minutes, less time than I normally wait for rental car vans in Charlotte. The hotel is only a few minutes away. 
Courtyard hotels are in the midst of a national upgrade and this one had recently finished the upgrade. The very friendly hotel manager said about 40% of the Courtyards have been updated. The lobby is open, bright and welcoming. Checkin/out was quick and trouble free. My room was delightful. Instead of the basic cube the designers had created a cutout in one corner for the coffee machine and used bright colors to give the room a liveliness not often found in standard business hotels. 
The hotel is next to I-85 but the room was quiet. Since I was there just overnight I ate at the small restaurant in the hotel. The food is OK and the wine was fine. The shuttle will take you to local restaurants if you prefer to eat out but don't wish to use your own transportation.

title: “Excellent Service, Better than Expected!”
text: Loved the personal attention! Stayed for 7 days. Checked in and got 3rd floor right below a bus stop, which was rather noisy as the buses pulled away. Room was nice but decided that a higher floor would be better. Front desk called right after we checked in and we asked if they had a higher floor. He said that the hotel was sold out for the night but they would try to find another room for us tomorrow. We were pleasantly surprised when they called the next morning and moved us to the 15th floor. The room was much larger and very quiet. This particular room had a table for dining which we also used for our computers. What made this hotel stand out for us, besides the size of the room, was the friendly service we received. Everyone was very helpful and attentive to all our needs. They made our first trip to New York City a wonderful experience. We would, with no hesitation, stay at the Beekman again!

title: “Very nice!”
text: Descent room rate - comfortable bed - quiet room- clean bathroom - all employees very nice & helpful - good breakfast buffet - was charged incorrectly for in room movie but was assured it would be corrected when management arrived .

title: “Wonderful Place”
text:
We stayed at the Kimberly Hotel over the Memorial Day Weekend. We loved it.
I went down with two of my friends for a weekend of theatre, dinners and shopping.
Great location and most important a great staff. We had a beautiful room with a terrace and wonderful beds. The comforters and sheets were great.
I plan on coming back here in October.

title: “Excellent - Go there!”
text:
We headed over to New York at the beginning of May for a short break of just under a week. Having never been there before and therefore not knowing exactly what to expect, we did an awful lot of research to try to find the right place to stay. Even though we knew that most of our time was going to be spent sight seeing, we still wanted to stay somewhere spacious and comfortable. After having read an awful lot of hotel horror stories about tiny rooms, noisy locations, rodent infestations and worse, we opted for the Park South hotel which from all accounts seemed to be ideal. And we were not disappointed.
The location is perfect for sight seeing with all the major attractions within walking distance. If you're not feeling too energetic, the subway station is about 100 yards down the road and cabs are easily hailed from Lexington or Park Avenue. There were a few street traders down the street from the hotel but we didn't notice any "street walkers" as another reviewer mentioned. The area felt very safe (safer than London in some respects) and it was also surprisingly clean.
The hotel itself was modern, clean and comfortable. We had a room on the 7th floor at the back which although I was initially disappointed at not having a view of the Chrysler building - I was more grateful for the peace and quiet. New York is noisy and coming back to the tranquility of a quiet (and nicely air-conditioned) room after a day's sightseeing was a welcome relief. The room was enormous with a queen sized bed, armchair and still loads of room for our suitcases and shopping bags. It did lack a bit of hanging space as the wardrobe was bizarrely tiny but we managed.
We had local newspapers delivered every morning which was a nice touch and also the complimentary breakfast was fantastic. Rather than the usual dried up croissant and wrinked apple you normally see, the hotel laid out a full buffet including every type of bagel you could imagine (watch out for the onion ones - not good for breakfast!). Good coffee too.
The staff were very friendly but unobtrusive which was ideal - nothing worse than "in your face" service. If you needed anything they were there but you hardly saw them otherwise. 
We ate at the hotel restaurant, The Black Duck on just one evening which was very pleasant - the food was lovely and reasonably priced and the atmosphere relaxed. Apparently they also organise Jazz Sunday Brunches which, when we were there, appeared to have been brought forward a few hours to the Saturday night. We caught the tail end of it after a night out and had we wanted to develop hearing difficulties, we would have gone clubbing. Turn it down!
It think that covers everything - we would definitely go back there on our next visit and have already recommended it to friends who are flying out there in July.

title: “A wise decision.”
text: My wife and I stayed here on Valentine?s Night. We had a great experience. The staff was all nice enough, and our late night request for more pillows was answered with our choice of feather or synthetic fill, and there within minutes. The beds are great!! So many nights I've stayed in hotels with hopelessly unsupportive beds and woke up with a sore back. These beds are extremely comfortable, especially with the down comforter. Very conveniently located near Union Square. We had our car parked on arrival and relied on taxis to get around town. So much more relaxing in the city when you don't have to drive to an unfamiliar address and fight traffic and the consistently unavailable parking. The front door attendant was extremely helpful in getting us a taxi in a very busy area on a very busy night. The rooms are stocked with tons of goodies in the honor bar and at what I thought were reasonable prices. We did enjoy our half bottle of quaffable Champagne for only $20. The only part that left me a little disappointed was the free breakfast. They told us that a free breakfast was included with the room, but it was no big deal, it was just a continental breakfast. When they left out the part about it being continental, I had grand visions of choice omelets and French toast smothered in powder sugar and real maple syrup. No such luck. Oh well. Over all I thought that the accommodations were nice and reasonably priced. The rooms were adequately sized with a huge bathroom. It would be nice to have a spa tub for this price, but the water was hot, the pressure was good and the soaps smelled great, so the shower was enough. The thick terry robes are a nice touch.

title: “Another great stay at 414”
text:
This was my second stay at the 414 Hotel for a weekend trip to NYC. This has definitely become the hotel I will always stay in when I visit the city. Location is great with dozens of restaurant choices within walking distance. Short walk to Times Square/subway/Rockefeller Center/and other sights. They held our bags for us in the lobby after our checkout so that we could explore the city too. They accommodated us for a very late check-in the first night as well.
I could hear doors closing and people walking overhead but it wasn't bad. Normal hotel noise. Ask for a room on a high floor if that bothers you, just remember that there is no elevator so you have to walk steep stairs to upper floors. No bed bug issues at this hotel either.
One thing I noticed this time is that the free high speed wireless internet ran a little slow. It was faster for me to use the 3G on my phone instead of the internet. They may want to boost the speed in the future.
Overall, another great stay. At less than $300 a night, I definitely recommend staying here.

title: “Helpful Staff, Good Experience”
text:
OK, I have to admit that one star is probably due to the fact that we were upgraded to a 2 room suite, but I still have (mostly) good things to say about this hotel!
When checking in, I wanted to verify a King bed, and the kind woman who helped us mentioned we'd been upgraded. We sure had! The decent-sized bedroom was attached to a very large room with a dinner table for 6, chairs, a sofa, and a Murphy bed. There was also another closet/dressing area and a second bathroom. The decor I would describe as "1990s Conference Room", but it was the space that thrilled me.
Yes, the hotel is old. That is it's charm as well as it's problem. Walls were thin, but this was only an issue when other patrons felt the need to shout at each other like they were at Fenway when walking past our room at 2 in the morning. That is, if people behaved decently, you wouldn't care much about wall thickness.
The room was very clean, and the bed was quite comfortable, which are ultimately the most important things.
It was Marathon weekend, so the place was ridiculously packed. I was on the 8th floor, and it was impossible to get an elevator, so a very nice staff member brought several of us around to the service elevator so we could get downstairs.
Not at all thrilled to be gouged for wifi, but as they are primarily a business hotel full of people charging their employers for it, I can see why they do it.
Great to have Au Bon Pain, a pub, The Melting Pot (fondue restaurant) and other restaurants right in the hotel. The hotel is also close to Boston Common and the Public Garden, as well as amazing shopping on Newbury street. We crossed the Common to get a beer at Cheers (formerly Bull and Finch) a few times, since the walk was so pleasant (give me a break, I'm a child of the 80s)
To sum up- comfortable bed, friendly staff, clean, great location, thin walls, costly wifi. I would stay again, actually :)

title: “What do you Expect?”
text:
I have been staying at the Hotel Carter (formally Hotel Dixie Pre 1950) for the past 10 years. I stay as a last desperate attempt when no rooms are available in Midtown or when the prices are so high, its not worth the money.
 If you spend anytime in your hotel room besides sleeping or showering, this is not your place. There is no maid service to speak of (so save your towels), no cable TV, no desk, net access and you will be lucky to get a window A/C unit that works.
If you stay on a lower floor, the water pressure is so incredible. There are no watersavers here, just a huge Flow of high pressure water that can stip your skin off if your not carefule.
The beds are old used hospital beds, and well broken in. The sheets are clean once you arrive (I would not trust the comforter), but are not changed during your stay.
I would advise against unpacking your suitcases and putting anything in the closets or dressers. 
The rooms claim to be renovated, but I don't think nailing old carpet to the wall in back of the beds would be considered a full renovation. 
I did not see any bugs (I think they know better) and the rates are cheap $89, so you can't complain on that front. I have stayed at worse places.
If this is your first trip to NYC, please don't stay here, as this does not represent the USA very well. The hotel is for very cheap, frugal travelers (like me) who don't need frills and spend very time in the room.
If you get a high up room, the view can be excellent.

title: “Quick Response to Unsatisfied Customer”
text: I posted a review that I was unhappy that the hotel would not issue a refund for an unused night. I received a very fast response from the general manager. To make a long story short, a refund has been authorized and I am now a satisfied customer. Thank you.

title: “Not bad, good location”
text:
The room was clean and quite nice. Hotel is in a pretty decent location to get to the main San Francisco sights, easy walking distance to Fisherman's Wharf.
Had a bit of a problem with my credit card getting charged twice, the staff were quite unhelpful and flat out denied it could have happened - it's sorted out now.

title: “No problems for us!”
text: After reading the reviews it got myself and my boyfriend were pretty nervous and considered looking for somewhere else to stay. But the price and location were to good to give up. We stayed there for 7nights and I'm so happy we did. The location is fantastic. My room was spacious and clean. Housekeeping was always done on time. We didn't have one problem with the hotel, and I am quite fussy!! One evening I got talking to people in the lift and found out that their room was terrible. I think with this hotel you can be lucky, depending on what floor you are on! I guess we were one of the lucky ones! I would recommend this hotel if location and price are important.

title: “My Go-to Austin Hotel”
text: My friends and I travel to Austin pretty frequently to float the river and what not, and we ALWAYS stay at this Super 8. The staff at times isn't the friendliest, once when our room wasn't ready yet, I asked to use the bathroom, and the man working the desk ( I think he owns or manages the place) told me I couldn't use the bathroom even though we'd prepaid for our room! However, the prices are always spot on, and we can get a room with three queen beds! Not only that, the place is walking distance from 6th street. Yes you have to cross a bridge that crosses over the highway, but there IS a SIDEWALK for this purpose. I feel bad for the reviewer that too afraid to walk over a sidewalk.. but the world takes all types... The one time we were too intoxicated to walk back we hailed a cab and it cost us $5 dollars to get back. (Yep, it's that close). This place does in fact have a pool.. I'm not sure how that other reviewer missed seeing it. It's in front of the building, pretty much in the parking lot... I've only had the breakfast once, and it was what you would expect, some box cereal and fruit. Whatever its complimentary, I love cereal! All in all I'd recommend this place to anyone who doesn't need over the top bells and whistles. If you need a clean place to sleep, close to everything downtown, with extremely reasonable prices, this is it. If you want champagne service on a beer budget, you probably are not going to find that in Austin.

title: “Good Location”
text:
Good location...next to mall and several eating establishments close by. Valet was prompt and overall service was good. 
The rooms need to be updated a bit, specially the showers.
The only suggestion I have, is to make sure they guarantee the type of room you reserve. My reservation stated a king size bed. When I arrived, I was told the hotel had oversold those rooms and wanted to put me in a room with two doubles. When I complained, management stepped in and honored my original reservation.

title: “Your own castle by PHI”
text:
The Renaissance Hotel is located about a mile away from Philadelphia International Airport with shuttles to & from the airport every 20 minutes. It's part of the Marriott chain; so you can grab a few more points. There's a Concierge Lounge for Marriott members with light snacks if you don't need a large meal, but there is also a restaurant in the facility somewhere. 
They're renovating so there are lower rates available to business travelers during the work.

title: “Amazing service, great airport location”
text: We stayed at Four Points on 10/11 August 2012. Hotel is a short ride from the airport. I was really sick when I arrived and the lovely man at reception (name starts with M, I forget the rest) took one look at me and ordered complementary chicken soup and tea for my room. He then called to check on me and was an absolute star the whole time. The hotel is older in style and therefore rooms aren't completely sound proof and aircon is a little noisy. But I spent the whole time in my room and wasn't bothered and the service was so brilliant it makes up for it. Would stay again - it's hard to find this kind of service in a major hotel chain.

title: “Very nice, excellent value!”
text:
Hi! I just wanted to contribute to good overviews of the place. After reading tons of reviews on Tripadvisor I finally booked the Hotel at Times Sq. and stayed there for 10 days in the beginning of May 2009. 
The key thing to share is that it is a great location for visitors, clean rooms and friendly staff. I would not say the place is luxury, it is just nice and clean with nothing disturbing or annoying. I have a very pleasant impression of the place and would definitely recommend it to people who came to see the city and not stay in the hotel for long. 
However, I should admit that very often one of two elevators does not work, one of two PCs with free Internet access in the lobby does not work, the breakfast is the same everyday. But believe me it is not that crucial for the money you pay.

title: “Business and Leisure all in one”
text: This hotel is perfect for business or leisure. I had a tax conference, so I flew on a Thursday night to SFO; took BART to Embarcadero stop; took the short walk to the Hotel; quick check in; then had a fantastic dinner at the hotel restaurant and a great night of rest and awoke to a sun shinning on the Bay Bridge - what a great view from our room. My husband and I had tasty breakfast at the hotel restaurant with my latte perfectly prepared; he went to work and I went to the conference. Friday night we had another great dinner across the street at the Ferry Building at the Slanted Door. Saturday and Sunday we got to have fun with friends all day while our room was perfected with nice towels hung up, nice soaps lining the shower, and clean, soft sheets, and big pillows to flop onto at night. Can't wait to go back.

title: “Superb staff!”
text: Great hotel, convenient location. Everything was outstanding! But the best part of our five night stay was the hotel staff. They are the best we have ever encountered. You cannot find a better place to stay in San Antonio.

title: “Best Business Stay in DC”
text: Was in DC for a trade convention and had a great stay at Monaco. Very unique room with free Internet access(must sign up for rewards program first). Metro stop across the street and an easy 10 minute walk to the Convention Center. Dont miss the Portrait Museum across the street and National Archives are 3 blocks away. Spy and Crime and Punishment Museum's are also across the street. Cannot give a high enough recommendation. Stay here if you want to be in the middle of the action.

title: “Beautiful hotel, very accommodating staff”
text: This is a gorgeous little hotel, we stayed here for two nights last winter. It's a great area to stay in as well. We will be going back to Philly in August and the only reason we won't be staying there is that over three days, it's a bit costly for us. But for a special occasion, it's absolutely worth it. The staff is wonderful. We have recommended it to several friends.

title: “Good atmosphere”
text:
Just returned from spending two nights on business travel and I was very comfortable here. The staff were all very friendly and the rooms were nearly spotless, albeit a tad stark looking. I liked the open atmosphere - it felt more homey and safe that all rooms opened up to middle of the inside. 
The lounge/bar/lobby had plenty of room to hang out, drink a coffee or wine. Einstein Bagels was a plus and one woman who worked there was perhaps the friendliest service person I've ever come across so early in the morning.
While I didn't eat at their restaurants, the fitness center was very clean and enjoyable. 
I normally stay at the Omnipresent but I would consider this one while in Houston again.

title: “Stay every year for the St Jude Memphis Marathon”
text: This is the 10th year we have stayed here. nine of my family go and are very happy with the easy access to the trolly and easy walking distance to Auto Zone Park, Cook Convention Center, FedEx arena, Beale Street, Peabody Hotel to see the ducks and the beautiful Christmas decorations. The biscuits and sausage gravy are the best. It is nice to see the same staff year after year. Earlene and Christie at the registration desk are always very pleasant and the breakfast hostess Evelyn is so cheerful. Will keep coming back.

title: “Great family accommodation”
text:
This ranks as our favourite hotel so far on our vacation - according to our children and ourselves.
There were lots of holiday makers/ families staying here, but also business people.
The atrium is a huge hit - great to look at, and the opportunity to feed the fish twice per day is wonderful.
The rooms are spacious, having two vanities outside the bathroom is handy and having a door between the bedroom and living room is needed when you have children going to bed. (Beds are wonderful.)
The included breakfasts are great - lots of variety. Plenty of room to find a table.
The free evening nibbles and drinks are also great when you have kids - saves rushing out for an early dinner.
The laundry fees are only a dollar per wash, which is good value. 
Internet costs $9.95 per day, which is our only gripe.
Concierge and all staff were friendly and helpful. 
I definitely recommend this as great accommodation - including for families.

title: “Fine hotel”
text:
I stayed overnight after seeing a concert at the Wachovia Center. The hotel room was clean and tidy. The hotel staff was very courteous. My only complaint was that it's difficult to find as the directions from their website were incorrect.
There was free wireless internet and an indoor swimming pool, neither of which I used. The continental breakfast was average with the typical pastries, toast, box cereal, etc. 
I would stay again at this hotel. It is very convenient to the Philadelphia sports complex just a few miles away.

title: “excellent”
text: Great location, freindly staff, comfortable rooms - highly recommended.

title: “The Perfect Chicago Hotel”
text: Went for weekend getaway to Chicago and stayed at the Blackstone. It was the perfect hotel. Small but big, with great comfortable beds. The location was great for walking to everything we wanted to see. Our room looked out over Lake Michigan which was amazing. The staff was friendly and helpful. The restaurant in the hotel was also a pleasure. If I return to Chicago this is were I would like to stay.

title: “If you want rest- this is NOT a hotel for you-and I'm not one to write bad things unless they are pretty bad”
text:
Let me say good things so readers will know I m not being unilaterally negative. They have a nice view, the bellmen are sweethearts, the operator is super nice, the cleaning staff are very friendly. They have complimentary cranberry juice in the evening and the rooms are pleasant until you try to sleep in them.
Now on to the warnings. The reason this particular Hilton is not a 4 star hotel.
When you get to your room you may find a towel or too with yellow stains, oh yes, on checking in.
The doors are like lead and all make a smacking sound when they close - what that will mean for you if you are not dead to the world, your bedtime and waking time will be decided by the people above you, to the left, to the right and hell, across the hall. Oh and you'll love the cleaning staff cos they are there all the time so if you dare to try and make up sleep in the am, their vacumes will wake you up.
Thought you were going fancy and would be surrounded by people with manners?
 I have news for you. Many of your neighbors will come with their animals, 10 children, all of whom bark, yell and yes at all hours.
Some of the highlights of my stay were
:a group of teens screaming in a hallway we are in dc expletive expletive at 12:30 am
a family for 2 nights in a row having a 20 person get together in the room next to me replete with screaming babies, doting aunts and uncles, cooing grandparents...etc etc -Oh you wanted to just watch a movie and hear it? Well you cant at the Hilton. Oh and there is no option for close captioning on the tv so boo hoo to you if you want to go the subtitle route. Oh and come to think of it boo hoo if Hilton thinks its' complying with the ADA because people with hearing impairments or deafness I guess dont need or want to watch movies.
facing the back was awesome on friday night. Having been woken at 5 am FRI AM and just about ready for a nap at 8pm, I got to listen to a full on IMAX Blasting sound system from the terrace. I was told "we do it every friday for kids". Oh thats nice. And do you supply adults with earplugs or perhaps shuttles so they can launch themselves into out of space until you turn the volume down!!! 
And oh by the way. The Hilton will let you make a reservation and write a sweet note saying there will be fire alarms intermittnetly on all floor between 9-5 for 2 days in a row. OH and no, you wont get comped so much as a breakfast, you wont get offered anything for the inconvenience- just a sorry letter. 
So by day no 3 when you finally are at breaking point they will promise you another room at the top of the hotel saying we have one for sure tomorrow. And then the next morning you will be told you cant movr up in the hotel because they would have to charge you more. It doesnt matter that you were promised the change. It doesnt matter thatt you had 2 days of fire alarms for the whole day plus the imax movie at night blasted clear across dc. They aren't going to move you to the top because apparently all of this doesnt worry them.
