Oh and If you let them clean your room, thats fun. You can come back to a room like mine, where your bed was made replete with the same makeup stains you had on them last night (meaning NOT WASHED)
you can call in your requests for shampoo and conditioner cos whoever did your room for the first time in 3 days couldnt be bothered.
They will pick up your dirty towels off the floor and fold them with yellow stains facing forward. I think that was a special "we dont care about you touch" personally.
The long and the short of it is this hotel is a deal (and beware priceline bidders - thats where i found this) because they dont know how to treat people who paid to come rest. This is not a business hotel. Oh and get your walking shoes on because you have to walk like mad to get to anything

title: “worst hotel in Starwood chain”
text: My family has stayed in this hotel more than 4 times in the past. It was lousy each time, but centrally located. Never again! This hotel is horrible. On our last visit the staff was rude. Our room was not cleaned. The toilet wouldn't flush! We arrived late and stayed out all day for 2 days so issues were not addressed as they should have been because I was simply too tired to argue with the haughty staff. Trust me. This hotel is not worth 10,000 Starwood points!

title: “Awesome Hotel & Restaurant”
text: Great Location...amazing rest called Nage.....amazing...Hotel is in the middle of everything yet quiet enough that you can get away....this is my new favorite.......A+++++....our little secret

title: “Don't be worried”
text:
We read the reviews on this site AFTER we had booked and were pretty worried. The first room they gave us was dreadful (wallpaper pealing off the wall, holes in the carpet etc.) but having read the reviews about the 'refurbished' floors we went straight back down to reception. 
Without any arguments at all they gave us a room on the 9th floor which was absolutely fine. We were so happy, that we came back to this hotel a second time during our stay in the US!
This hotel is in such an unbeatable location (right opposite Madison Sq Gdn), it really can't be beaten on price.
Just go for it but demand a room on a refurbished floor! Good Luck :o)

title: “A Pleasant Surprise”
text: Stayed here and was pleasantly surprised. Looks like it has been overhauled and they did a great job. Help was friendly and the King room althouh a little small was very nice. Great value!

title: “Small, tiny, noisy rooms - even for NYC”
text:
The location is pretty convenient, but to be honest when you book a hotel in NY you usually pick a hotel near to whatever you need e.g. Shopping, business, sightseeing etc. just do a little homework before you arrive. So convenient for trendy TriBeCa - sure. 
The hotel entrance is small, but the staff were very helpful and super efficient. Checked in within 3 mins. Brilliant. 
However, the room was ridiculously small. I had to side shuffle round the ,albeit clean and comfortable, double bed. The ensure shower was efficient, but the ventilator sounded like an aircraft taking off and made me feel guilty about getting up early and having a shower, a it would have definitely woken up other guests nearby......but hang on....why should I feel guilty as they woke me up 5 times in the night! Who needs ice at 3am? Why can people not shut the door quietly at 12am. Do you really need to shout at your mate at 1am?
Ahhh!!!!
The rooms are so small and so close together you hear everything. Doesn't matter about the thickness of the walls.

title: “A beautiful historic hotel, but in need of a facelift”
text:
This is my second time staying at the Fairmont and I just don't know if it's worth it for the price, especially with all of the fabulous hotels in the city. It sits atop of Nob Hill which means there are great views of the city and the bay, but definitely not near the hustle and bustle of SF and you'll pretty much need to take a cab wherever you go. The food at Laurel Court left much to be desired. 
However, there is something to be said for the enormous marble pillars, fabulous crown molding, detail oriented wall paper, and what looks like original crystal chandeliers. The newly redone Swigg Suite Penthouse has a mind-blowing view of the Transamerica building and the bay (although most people probably wouldn't be able to step foot unless they ponied up a hefty amount). 
Like I said, the hotel is historic, code for old. It was a little musty when I arrived, although the smell seemed to disappear or I just got used to it as time went on. Maybe because I arrived on a very rainy day? There was no coffee bar, or water available in the room and the room service prices are exorbitant (and the food is mediocre at best)! There was no turn down service. The walls are thin, I could hear the guy in the room next to me blowing his nose (plus his yappy lil' dog) and I'm sure he could hear my very low volume TV in the am.
The saving grace is the great attitude by the staff. Everywhere I went, the staff was friendly and even greeted me and made polite conversation with me in the hallways and elevators. If they could not provide the assistance I needed, they were quick to call someone who could. When I complained about the unattended yapping dog, someone was there to follow up within 3-4 minutes, very nice!

title: “Very Good Choice...but TONS of kids over the 4th of July Weekend”
text:
We stayed at this hotel over the 4th of July long weekend. The location is fantastic! A short walk to: Navy Pier, Michigan Avenue, countless restaurants, and shops. There is a brand new Dominicks (supermarket) across the street...perfect for stocking up on groceries. 
The hotel is very new (2 years old?). Keep in mind that there are two Embassy Suites in Chicago...this is the newer and better one. The suites are very nice, quite new and some have wonderful city/lake views.
Due to the long weekend, the place was crawling with kids. My partner and I don't mind kids but this verged on ridiculous. Both the free (and very good) breakfast buffet and the evening cocktail hour were overwhelmed by the capacity crowds. 
Parking is steep ($36 per day self park)...but at least it is located in the same building. 
An elaborate movie theater and a bowling alley are also located in the same building. 
P.J. Clarkes (Burgers, pizza, pasta, steaks, etc) is a fantastic restaurant located on the street level of the hotel.
Would I stay here again? Yes!

title: “Pleasantly surprised”
text:
Having read the reviews, after we had booked, we were apprehensive about the hotel, as some of the reviews were offputting! We were pleasantly surprised, therefore, when we arrived at this lovely hotel, and enjoyed our 6 day stay very much. The bedroom was very clean comfortable and nicely furnished, and the bathroom had everything we needed. The staff were extremely helpful. It was our own fault that we arrived on Thanksgiving and everything was closed!!
We thoroughly enjoyed our stay in Boston, and in the Omni Parker Hotel, and would certainly stay there again.

title: “OK”
text:
This hotel was OK. The facilities were nice, but the amenities were bare bones for a 'luxury' hotel. You could tell that they were cutting costs. Expected a bit more from this class of hotel (no robes, mouthwash, only provided two towels per room, etc.)
Food was good. Breakfast buffet was excellent. Rooms were very soundproof and of adequate size.
Front desk was a bit disorganized and canceled our reservation that was prepaid for the night before we arrived in order to guarantee an early check in so that we could get ready for an event immediately upon arrival (actually they resold our room in order to make a little extra $$).

title: “Location and service was great!”
text: The hotel is located within walking distance of Union Square and Market Street. Being so close to these areas allowed us to explore the various transportation options that the city has to offer. The staff was always friendly and helpful with providing restaurant recommendations and with any other help we needed. For example, they provided an umbrella during the rainy days and also a map of the city. Overall, I felt welcome because of their outstanding service.

title: “Lovely Inn, lovely location.”
text: This scenic area has cobblestone streets and sidewalks and is full of cafes, restaurants, shops and bars. Half a block from the water and short ride to main harbor.

title: “Great stay at Days inn by graceland”
text: I had read mixed review about the Days Inn at Graceland. I was not sure what to expect, but it sounded fun with all the elvis decor. IT WAS GREAT. the gals at the front desk were very kind and the manager was so sweet. the room was clean and decorated with elvis all over! the bed was so comfortable!! there was elvis music playing in the courtyard, which also was fun. it was too cold to swim, but there was a guitar shaped pool. the continental breakfast was standard, nothing to rave about, but hey it was free. overall i would highly recommend this hotel. it is a great value. he only drawback is that it isn't in the greatest neighborhood, but i felt fine traveling through there alone.

title: “The hotel in the middle of the NYC shopping miles”
text: The Omni is just around the corner of New York Citiy's Shopping miles like Madison and 5th Avenue and that makes it a good place to stay. Rooms are newly renovated, clean and comfortable. The Omnia is child friendly and the staff is very friendly and helpfull. Altouhg the breaksfast rate is quite high it is from a good quality and you have a good choise what you would like to eat

title: “Not what was expected”
text: Booked an overnight at the Marriott this Saturday with the thought of enjoying the location and going to the Cubs game the next day. Location was good if you want to be near the shopping on Michigan Avenue and near Navy Pier. As usual the staff was very friendly and helpful. There was a teacher’s convention at the hotel so it was very busy and the elevators were running very slowly. Biggest issue I had was that the rooms were small and the bathrooms were very small. As a Marriott elite member I supposedly get upgraded to the best rooms available and if that was the best room available I would recommend going somewhere else. The pool that they show on the hotel website makes it look big...one of the reasons I picked the hotel. When we got there it ended up being a two lane lap pool at best. Also, just bought an iPad and brought it with us to use. The rooms do not offer wireless service so if you need to connect you need do it at the lobby or lower levels. Overall not happy with the value proposition at this property. Total cost of one night about $300.00 with valet service.

title: “Great location, attentive staff”
text: This was a one night stay for a business trip. Location is excellent with many shops and restaurants near by. Suites are very roomy, well equipment, and comfortable. Staff was very friendly and ready to help. Skipped breakfast when I stayed, but It seemed very popular. Served in a large dining room. Evening managers reception seemed a good value, too. All complimentary. And free internet. I could stay here again. For good eats nearby I recommend ENO and Purple Pig. Nordstroms is across the street!

title: “Unfriendly! (but clean)”
text:
I really like the location of this hotel--it's just a few blocks from Central Park (and, in my opinion, the most scenic part of Central Park--the Lake) so great for those that enjoy the park. It's also a short walk to some of the great Upper West Side restaurants, and a block from the subway. The rooms are clean, though tiny, and the bathrooms have been nicely remodeled.
The downsides: 1) The staff is really unfriendly, which for some reason just bugged me the whole time. 2) If you have a room that overlooks the street, it's quite loud. We had to buy earplugs. 3) For a better value, I'd go to the Milburn which is close, clean, and the rooms are huge.

title: “Nice hotel let down by historic layout”
text: This hotel has very nice public areas and is probably in the most central location you could ask for in Boston with a huge choice of nearby restaurants and other attractions. However, although clean with comfortable beds, the hotel's rooms are from a different era and let down by a lack of major renovation. Rooms are small with Victorian bathrooms and somewhat eccentric heating. Worst feature is the paper thin walls where you can easily hear next door conversations and the TV. I had to call my neighbor at midnight to ask her to turn the TV down. Make sure you bring earplugs if you stay here.

title: “Four Points......Minor complaint but great stay”
text:
We checked into the Four Points Sheraton on Thursday December 30th for a two night stay in Chicago. Upon arrival we were greeted with a smile by Bobby who gave us great directions for the parking as well as some tips on where to eat for the night. After parking Bobby met us back in the lobby and escorted us to our room which was 8424. Our room consisted of 2 double beds, sleeper sofa and then the micro/fridge. Once we entered the room we were greeted with a very odd smell, which Bobby noticed as well. We didn't alert the front desk about the odor until a few hours later. They were very understanding, professional and moved us to a new room (7344) on the 7th floor. I wasn't sure they were going to be able to move us because of the holiday weekend but it was not a problem. Our new room had no odor at all and was just as clean and well stocked as our first room. We did have to call down to housekeeping for an extra blanket which was brought to our room within 5 minutes.
My husband and I are sometimes very hesistant to stay at unfamiliar hotels. The Four Points Sheraton did not disappoint us at all. Every employee that we encountered (front desk, housekeeping, valet) were very professional,and helpful. We would definately stay here again in the future. Michigan Avenue was about 2 blocks away and we were surrounded by great restaurants. We walked to Rainforest Cafe, Eggsperience, TGIFridays, Giordano's and the Gran Lux Cafe. The farthest walk was to the Rainforest Cafe. The Hancock Observatory was about a 5-10 minute walk from the hotel.

title: “not bad at all”
text:
Sea Rock Inn, is a good place to stay. Clean,good bed,good service... and Terry was very helpful too. U have to pay for wireless 20$ for one week,unfortunately it had a weak connection.
For the rest its all good, i would come back to this hotel when i visit LA again!

title: “Right on the Cable Car Line...”
text: Very nice hotel with standard Marriott quality touches througout. Prime location in the middle of San Francisco's touristy shopping district. Small intimate lobby lacking thAT impersonal feel of large convention style hotels. The rooms are on the small side especially when comparing square footage to more limited service hotels like Courtyards, Very small bathrooms as already noted by other reviewers, but the quality furnishings and amenties make up for these small nuiansces. Very nice and capable staff. All in all, a great stay.

title: “great to stay”
text: is a great place to stay i recommend friend and family to stay at the double tree hotel

title: “Impressed Guest”
text:
I stayed in Hotel Andra for 5 days and just checked out yesterday. I was in town for a medical conference in Westin and the location of Hotel Andra was perfect.  
Being from Sacramento, I'm not very familiar with Seattle hotels but I must say that I was pleasantly surprised and extremely pleased with my stay in Andra. 
The hotel decor was to my liking and my room was adequately furnished and immaculately clean (I work in the Operating Room, I have an innate obsession over sterile things). I appreciate the careful thought and attention to detail made in the planning and infused in the ergonomics of the room. The hotel ambiance speaks of sophistication and comfort which extended outside the hotel premises like when we were offered an umbrella to use to forge through the afternoon Seattle rain yesterday.
From the valet crew to the front desk staff to housekeeping, everyone was hospitable and very helpful. We had brunch at Lola's on Saturday, the menu was superb. I loved their cauliflower anchovy spread with pita and the salmon kebab. It was so great, I ordered eggs Benedict for room service last Monday and was not disappointed. I had a falling out with Greek cuisine a few years ago but now, I remember why I fell in love with it in the first place.
What I was most impressed and happy with is the return of my friend's jade/ diamond/ white gold necklace which we left behind yesterday. It has great sentimental value and I'm ecstatic that Rachel, the Housekeeping manager was able to track it for me this morning. That's outstanding service.
Hotel Andra is definitely a rockstar of hotels in my book.

title: “Business trip - convienient lots of close”
text:
First the Hotel is under renovation - so, you have to give them room for that kind of thing. The decor in the new areas is great. HOWEVER, the one real problem is that the plastic is on the mattresses - it was muggy and the bed was "crinkley" noisey and hot becasue the bed didn't breath. The sheets did not want to stay on the bed. The hall is very well lit - the only problem with that is that the light comes through around the door...hopefully that will be completed and fixed as the renovation is complete.
I did really appriciate the security in the parking garage - the location is great close to lots of things that you might need in LA - close to Beverly Hills, The Grove Mall is like 4 miles away. There are lots of places to eat close (walking distance). Over all for what it is - I was pleased. Remodeled area we stayed was clean, and nice (aside from the plastic). Bathrooms were perfect - hair dryer, ironing board & iron, in our room there was a micro wave, coffee pot, and refrigerator - all worked great.

title: “Stupid hotel!!”
text: This hotel tries so hard to be hip that it's just annoying. The standard rooms are MINUSCULE, even for New York City (it's impossible to even reach the toilet tissue dispenser, your arm is jammed so close to the bathroom sink). And DARK (we had to use the light of the TV screen to be able to read the newspaper). You stub your toes on the bed because it takes up most of the room and is one big block instead of, say, a regular bed, or a mattress on a platform (which would make a lot more sense in such a TINY space). We were there for a special event and made that fact known to the management. Guess what we got? A note from the hotel manager with ONE can of Red Bull and some cheap-o snack. Plus we were put in a room right next to the elevator and the HORRIBLY LOUD ice machine. But maybe the worst thing was that we were supposed to have (not free, of course) Internet access in our room. It didn't work, so I called down to the desk and they told me to call the 800 number of Sprint, which I did -- twice, because we were disconnected the first time. They weren't able to do anything and I called down to report it to the front desk clerk who casually said, "Oh, we've been having a few problems with the server." No effort to help, no mention of when this "server problem" might be resolved. The capper: when we checked out, we discovered we'd been charged $2.00 each for the two 800 number calls TO THEIR OWN PROVIDER, FOR THE HOTEL'S PROBLEM. When I complained, someone said that because of renovation work, some of the rooms had been left without Internet service over the previous few days. I asked if we could have been moved to another room that hadn't been affected and the answer was, "Oh, probably -- if you had asked." Obviously, we will never stay here again!!!

title: “Watch out for wilting seafood and shady cab drivers”
text:
We were in LA to see a concert at the Gibson Amphitheatre and this was perfect for that. The room was clean and had a great view, and the staff were friendly and helpful. Overall, we had a great stay, but there were some issues:
- The hotel restaurant has a large buffet, most of which is left out in the open constantly. We were always walking past it, and I found it mildly disturbing that they left out shucked oysters and other seafood (covered in plastic wrap) when the buffet wasn't even open. 
- We had an issue with taking a cab from the hotel. I know that this isn't the hotel's fault, but I feel like I should point it out because it was a cab that the hotel arranged (and we tipped them for!). The cab driver tried to pull the tourist scam on us by basically taking the longest route possible, trying to turn a $20 cab ride into a $50 one. We caught him with the iPhone's GPS and he became tongue-tied and it was obvious that he knew what he was doing. I don't know if the hotel cabs are doing this to others, but just be warned!
Would I go back? If I was going to the Gibson Amphitheatre, yes. But I wouldn't eat at the restaurant or take a cab from the hotel without knowing where I was going.

title: “Amazing!”
text: Myself and my girlfriend stayed for five days, a 30th Birthday present for her! The Hotel is amazing, you really feel as if you are in the movies walking through the reception area, staff are very friendly and welcoming. We were on the 17th floor, room was large if a little dated but I suppose that's what you expect from this fine hotel. One negative would be there are no tea/coffee making facilities in the rooms and not even a bottle of water to be had!! Apart from that we had an amazing stay and would recommend this hotel to all looking for a memorable time in New York. If you're on a bit of a budget, DON'T eat in the hotel, Sunday brunch is 95 dollars per adult and 65 for a child, madness if you ask me, but as is the nature of New York you can make it as cheap or as expensive as you want.

title: “Very comfortable”
text: We stayed at The Mark because we wanted to be near the Metropolitan and the hotel was offering a special rate. It is a bright shiny place, with staff poised to help you at every turn. The bathrooms have deep solid marble baths and huge shower cubicles and, bizarrely, televisions embedded into the mirrors. The place is solid and plush and there are several places nearby for breakfast, plus the park just around the corner. Well-run, comfortable, a nice place to come back to after a day in the big city

title: “Wallingford Haven”
text: This is a nice spot near the University and many of Seattle's north neighborhoods. While it is not luxurious, it is functional and rooms include a microwave and small refrig. The bathroom has nice granite countertops. Breakfast is not included, but the cafe off the lobby has breakfast and other fare for a reasonable price. The underground parking at no charge is really a plus. The biggest negative is the bed linens. They don't use fitted sheets on the bottom, and the flat sheet they do use isn't quiet big enough to hold. So in the morning you are likely to wake up in a mess of sheeting!

title: “Good Location, Thats All!”
text: We stayed at this hotel with our two teenage daughters duing a part business, part family fun trip in July. We were very impressed with the location, within walking distance to great restraunts and shopping, inlcuding Water Tower Place (a great mall!). We were quite disappointed with the room cleanlinees and size. The bedspreads were filthy and so thin. The room decor is in dire need of an upgreade. The bathroom had no fan and it really smelled badly of mold and mildew. The shower actually had mold in the corners! This was a very tight squeese for 4 people. Especially the bathroom. The beds and pillows were quite uncomfortable. Even the elevators were tiny and could barely fit 6 people! Thank goodness there were a few elevators. Luckily we booked this room on priceline and would have never paid full price. The only upside was the great location. Also beware- its cheaper to take a taxi to the airport than the airport shuttle! Millenium promotes the airport shuttle but take a cab!

title: “Great mix of 2 worlds”
text: My husband and I just returned from a long weekend stay at this Ritz. It was all decked out for Valentine's day and we were impressed with the small touches. We enjoyed the welcome champagne and candy. On Saturday they had a chocolate fountain with fresh strawberries and again the same small candy bar for it's patrons. The staff here is all friendly and knowledgeable. We really couldn't find anything negative to say. To be honest the more we travel, the less we start to pick apart places and more just immerse ourselves in the experience. This hotel is in a lovely old building that used to be a bank. It has an old world feel to the rooms and lobby but the restaurant is more of a modern trendy place. We did have an early afternoon cocktail and snacks at the lobby lounge. The food was good but the drinks were even better. We would recommend the restaurant during that time. In the evenings on the weekends it gets quite loud and crowded. We stayed two nights on the 28th floor which had a very impressive view of the state house, with Ben Franklin on top. The room was quiet and spacious. The decor was simple but, clean and updated. We had no complaints and felt on top of the world in the evenings. We wouldn't hesitate to return.

title: “Great Hotel”
text:
Great hotel, great location, good restaurants in the area. Early check in, late check out (Hilton Diamond helps with both). Upon checkout, we were asked how everything was. I realized there was nothing to complain about; no suggestions. I travel for business every week, so I always have something to note. Not this time; it was perfect.
If you want a view, ask for a room on the street. There will be some abient noise. If you just want a quiet location, get a room in back. All you'll see is other buildings, but there is no street noise. 
Great breakfast, good restaurant recommendations. Try Stan's or Thai Tanic. 2 completely different experiences, both good.
I always like Homewood Suites. This was the best of the best.

title: “Nice Luxury Historic Hotel with Modern Touches in a Great Location”
text:
This is definitely a hotel where service comes first with staff that is friendly and attentive. The hotel is in a great spot near DuPont Circle and easy access to public transportation. The rooms were nice with period furniture and some luxury appointments that included a very comfortable bed. The Jockey Club restaurant was also good and would recommend for a nice occasion. 
As an SPG platinum member, they provided an additional free in-room amenity of Grand Mariner and little desserts. 
One extra bonus was the business center where computers with internet access and printing were free.

title: “Lovely Hotel”
text: We very much enjoyed our 3 nights here. It was in a great location near the centre of everything. Our room was comfortable and quiet, the only downside was the tiny bathroom which was barely big enough to contain the bath and toilet etc.! We were able to have a continenral breakfast in a small dining room in the tower as part of our stay which was very nice and an unexpected bonus as usually you have to factor in the cost of breakfast when staying in the states.There was another dining area if you wanted to splash out on the full cooked breakfast. All the staff we encountered were helpful and friendly. We would definitely stay there again.

title: “Brilliant Hotel! Will definitely be staying here again!”
text:
My husband and I stayed here from 28 Feb - 4 March 2011. We were really impressed with our room. It was very well presented and modern and was exactly what we needed after a long flight from Australia. The beds and pillows were super comfy! 
The Art and Soul restaurant downstairs is always busy and the bar is clearly a favourite for high powered local professionals. They have great happy hour specials too. 
We used room service a lot because we would come back to the hotel after long days of sightseeing. The food was absolutely delicious! It was high quality restaurant food and reasonably priced. 
The hotel staff were just wonderful. Especially the Concierge - she was very helpful and organised tours for us, gave us hotel recommendations and made reservations for us. 
The location of this hotel is brilliant too. Simply walk outside and you can see the Capitol Building. It is central to everything and is a great base for sightseeing, also only a few blocks from Union Station too. Also the West Wing Cafe diagonally across from the hotel is really cheap and a great place to get snacks, water, coffee, as well as light meals. We couldn't believe how cheap this cute little cafe/convenience store was. 
The hotel is located next to a fire station, but even staying on the second floor, we found the rooms to be really sound proof.
We will definitely be staying here again and won't even bother looking at other hotel options. The Liaison is where we will be staying in Washington from now on. 
I would recommend this to all my friends and family.

title: “Great Hotel!”
text: I booked our reservations through Hotrooms.com after The James Hotel would no longer honor my reservations due to a change in management [very last minute - I was NOT happy with The James Hotel!!]. I was originally bummed to be staying in a large chain instead of a small boutique hotel. The staff at the Sheraton, from the first person we met, were kind and fun and professional. The hotel has a 'small' feel, not a huge chain feel. They allowed us to get into our room early, the rooms were super clean and had a nice few. The location is perfect to walk to Michican Avenue or Rush Street shops and restaurants. I'd certainly stay here again.

title: “Good enough hotel in a great location”
text: This hotel is near bus and subway and close to the park and the Lincoln Plaza. Rooms are alright and service not bad. but the first room we got was terrible, so they changed it the next morning, moving us when we were out, but we had to leave the place packed up. the wifi is only free in the main lobby and business centre. The room was quiet and dark as we requested.The bathroom was small but fine.

title: “Thoroughly enjoyable downtown hotel”
text:
I booked a Premier Queen room (which has two queen beds) for a Saturday night stay. I have stayed at my fair share of downtown Seattle business hotels, and they are more or less about the same--except for this Hyatt. I was impressed. First of all, the room was advertised as 740 square feet, and indeed it was the most spacious hotel room I've been in outside of suites in Las Vegas. Beautiful corner location with rows and rows of windows, bringing in lots of natural light. Nice flat-screen TV and clean-as-a-whistle bathroom. Some trouble with noise from our next-door neighbors, but that's to be expected.
We had trouble with the room temperature, which got very cold and very hot when you turned the fan on, but somehow couldn't get "just right." Maybe a quirk of the "green" certification? Service was prompt and extremely friendly, and when I called down for extra shampoo it came within a half hour. I was also impressed by the call to the room from the gal who checked me in, just to make sure we had everything. Our room was on the 4th floor, so the view wasn't as sweeping as advertised on the corporate website. If you are paying full price and want a view, request a high floor.
Valet parking was a breeze, and, sadly, $39 is the norm for downtown Seattle. I've waited for my car for a half hour at other hotels on Sunday check-outs, but they had my car within 2 minutes. 
We had breakfast at the lobby restaurant, and that was the only disappointment. Food was overpriced and overcooked, and service was very slow with 3/4 of the tables full. Many patrons seemed to have free breakfast coupons. If you don't have a coupon, skip it.

title: “Great location, very comfortable”
text: Stayed at the Handlery for a conference in June. The room was compact but immaculate and very well set up for my needs. The location just off Union Square is ideal and the front desk staff were welcoming.

title: “Truly disappointing”
text:
Room was nice but not exceptional. Mayor disappointment was the poor quality of the service. Returned to hotel at 10:30om and found the room not cleaned and bed not made up. Faxes were not delivered timely and worst of all carrying a great deal of presents for a party and while I struggled to open the front door while the front door men saw me and did nothing to assist. Business center was frequently closed so again the hotel lacked service. 
This is not a 5 Star hotel.

title: “okay hotel”
text: The hotel was okay. It was in a good location directly across from the Ferry Terminal. The hotel itself is nothing spectacular. Internet in the room is rather expensive and works slowly, also you must pay per device. Television is horrible, most channels had static. Do not open the mini bar at all, you will be charged for it. It seems this hotel is lacking decoration. Very plain on the inside. Rooms were clean. It was nice that the sink and bathroom area was separate from the bedroom, and the sink was outside of the bathroom. Probably would find another hotel if I went there again.

title: “Another special trip to NYC - Thanks to Trump SoHo”
text:
We had another perfect stay at the Trump SoHo Hotel. Our room was not quite as well located as our 1st stay here last December, but the room was actually more ideal. I liked the cozier room and the bathroom seemed nicer. We had a direct 6th Avenue - Empire State Building view last time. 
It's nice to return to a hotel that is familiar, and the staff certainly makes you feel welcome. There is a sophisticated vibe to this hotel, and I would LOVE to lease one of these little jewel boxes of a room for a month or so. The location of the hotel is perfect - rather tucked away in SoHo, but right next to the subway line, with access to everything NYC has to offer. We were able to try many restaurants within walking distance, and the shopping was just a few blocks away as well.
Looking forward to my next visit to SoHo and NYC. Thanks Trump SoHo......See you soon!!

title: “Poor Service/ Hotel manager not available!”
text: Book reservation online Travel now .com . Arrive at Sheraton @ 10:30 pm with two young chrildren who wants to visit Sea world tomorrow. Hotel can't find rerservation, called Travel .com . Travel .com confirm reservation numbers. NO Mananger on site. Hotel try to send us down the street to another sub par hotel. Refuse! I asked them look for another Sheraton in the area. They said they found one. Travel fifteen mins. to new hotel to find out there is no rooms. Manager gave us a room from some one elses reservation. My kids finally went to sleep after 1:00AM . They didn't wake up after 10 am. Hotel mess up our vacation!

title: “Disappointing - can't understand rating”
text:
Granted, the hotel has history, but trying to get a good nights sleep is a whole different story. The windows are single pane - I think they built a building next to us during the night. It was soo noisy you could hear honking and noises the entire evening. The room was tiny even for New York standards. The lampshade was actually torn and stained and looked like it belonged in a shady hotel(looked worse than a salvation army lampshade). This was evidence of how clean the overall room was with black hairs in the bathtub...yuk. The beds were small hard and uncomfortable. We changed hotels for the remainder of nights. 
Extremely disappointed, especially after the good reviews here.

title: “Wound be awesome with an update”
text:
Very nice grounds, and friendly staff. But as others have noted, the rooms and furnishings are too dated. It seems like they are trying to improve the housekeeping, but the truths that with old (stained) furniture, linens, and carpets, it never quite feels clean.
Just because of the hotel design, you hear everyone pass your room. Not too noisy during normal sleepy hours, though.

title: “Good Hotel in Boston”
text: We stayed four nights at this hotel. The location is great-close to the airport, North End, Faneul Hall, and T access. The rooms are a bit small but for the rate it was fine and comfortable for two of us. We also enjoyed the Ruby Room bar that they had in the lobby for a pre dinner cocktail.

title: “Room not clean”
text: I recently stayed at the Dream New York. Due to a meeting, I arrived late. My room was small, but well equipped. However, it was not clean. Sheets didn't seem fresh and bath/shower had some mold around the caulking. But the capper was a disgusting booger smeared on the wall above the desk. Would not return.

title: “The best place to stay on Times Square”
text: We have stayed at the Novotel many times and have never been disappointed. It's close to Times Square and best of all within walking distance of many attractions. The staff at the Novotel are some of the kindest we have come across in our many travels. The hotel and its surrounding areas are immaculate. They have remodeled the rooms since our last visit and they are beautiful, for the money they are the best we have found in the city. If you need any recommendations for dinner check with Ian at the front desk, he has always given us remarkable places to try and we have always enjoyed the restaurants he has suggested.

title: “On business - stayed for a week - became home from home”
text:
Very friendly and efficient staff. 
location great for covering the value for meetings as so close to freeway intersections
Japanese restaurant across the road excellent.
Pool and Jacuzzi pleasant way to spend time if a few hours to kill
Great barman and creates an environment where quests talk to each other at the bar
Only flag - air conditioning in the rooms is loud and they should really try to address this

title: “Great Hotel in a Great Location”
text:
We recently spent four nights here on our first trip to Chicago and had a great time! The price was right for what we got and we had a very pleasant experience
Pros: Convenient to several CTA bus and train lines, including lines to O'Hare and Midway. Great restaurant and the bar has half price wine bottles Mon-Thurs. VERY helpful staff. Starbucks, Dunkin Donuts, CVS, 7-11 and ATMs are all within a block or two. Great pizza place across the street. Comfortable beds. Great location halfway between north and south tourist sights. Workout facility onsite.
Cons: Not all rooms have a city view. No bureaus or fridges (at least not in our room). The business center only had one computer so it was hard to find a time to use it when no one else was. The continential breakfast was pitiful. The sheets were stained with what looked like grease when we first arrived but the housekeeping staff took care of the problem quickly and professionally.
Overall we had a great experience and would definitely stay here again. It's in a great, safe location and the staff were all very helpful and friendly with suggestions of things to do and see. Our plane landed at Midway at 11:30 and we arrived at the Hotel by noon. They let us check in early so we didn't have to pull our luggage around the city for three hours, which was a huge relief.
Thanks Hotel Blake, we had a wonderful trip!!

title: “Great Boutique Hotel with great location”
text: Very good Hotel, great location, great staff. Boutique style with modern room. Very good Bed. I got a room in the high corner and was an amazing view.

title: “Stayed Before But This Time Was Special”
text:
I made Diamond status recently. I was upgraded to a huge one bedroom suite and a beautiful fruit plate with a card congratulating me on reaching Diamond status. I do not expect this level of upgrade, but the recognition was a very nice touch.
I have stayed in this hotel before and always had a nice room and a good nights sleep. The shuttle service has always been reliable, the sports bar food and service has always good and an exceptional value for both the burgers and beer.
As a gold, and this time as a diamond, I was provided a coupon for a free drink or appetizer at the sports bar and a voucher for the breakfast - both nice and appreciated perks.
I have read the "tired" comments and "needs updating" comments as well and frankly feel these are "parrotted" comments from others. Do not hesitate to stay here.

title: “Wonderful Experience”
text: From the valet to checkin to our room to the restaurant...EXCELLENT!! Everyone was gracious and accomodating. We only experienced quality while staying at the US GRANT. I was fastenated with the history and beauty of this hotel, and was always met with gracious, patient employees as I stopped them with my many questions. We stayed in a Grand Deluxe Room on the top floor. It was perfect, clean, quiet, and spacious. The food is wonderful, and served elegantly. The hotel is close to everything. Would definitly recommend the US Grant and will be staying here again. This was our first time, but will not be our last. :)

title: “Could have been better”
text: I am usually a fan of Omni hotels, but this one fell below my expectations. I reserved two rooms for two nights, one for me and my husband and one for his parents. The 2 queen beds room I requested for me and my husband was a nice size. However, the room with a king-size bed I had requested for my in-laws was half the size and had a horrible odor. I called the front desk, and they gave my in-laws another room that had 2 double beds, but more room. The tub in my room had rust all over the drain. I called housekeeping to remove the rust, and the maintence person reluctantly did so after I agreed not to take a shower until the morning so the paint could dry. No offer of another room was made. The free morning beverages is a nice perk of Omni hotels, but I did not get the soymilk I had requested for my coffee or the croissant I had ordered. Turns out they ran out of croissants, but couldn't be bothered to let me know by writing a note or calling to see if I wanted an alternative item. The following night we returned to the hotel @ 9 pm to take showers and rest. After I got out of the shower, I smelled smoke. My in-laws called our room and reported the same thing. The front desk informed us that an A/C unit caught fire and offered to allow us to change rooms, which we accepted. It would have been nice if they made the offer on their own rather than us having to ask. We moved 2 floors down, and my in-laws were disappointed that their replacement room was the same size as the small room they had initially received. The hotel did give us free breakfast coupons, which made the late night move a little more bearable, and allowed us to end our stay on a positive note. It was nice that I got to listen to my in-laws rave about the restaurant staff and food rather than how bad the accommodations were.

title: “Disappointing Doormen/Fabulous Concierge”
text:
My husband and I spent 3 nights at the Ritz, Battery Park last week. Typically we stay further uptown, but hubby was attending a conference at the hotel so we thought it would be easier to make it our home base. 
Other than the doormen, which I'll discuss later, the entire staff was gracious and attentive. A special note goes out to Concierge Jay, who landed us a reservation at Lamb's Club on a Friday evening and who tried everything to grab a last minute single ticket to La Traviata at the Met.
The room was enviable by NYC standards, but less than stellar compared to other Ritz properties we've had the good fortune to visit. The housekeeping staff was very accomodating, even having a dress pressed for me at the last minute, when an opera ticket materialized.
The restaurant has no ambience at all and really seems more like an open lobby. The lunch we had was good though, with a nice variety of soups, sandwiches, and other dishes on the menu.
The gym on the 14th floor has a nice round-up of equipment and a great view. My husband's meetings were all on the 14th floor as well, and he enjoyed the view of the Statue of Liberty each day. He remarked that the food brought in was better than your average hotel business luncheon rubber chicken.
Location wise, I would only recommend staying here if you have business in the financial district, otherwise you are a $20 cab ride or 6 block walk and 10 minute subway ride from all that NYC has to offer.
Now...the big downfall. I hate to sound pretentious, but when you're shelling out a certain amount of money for a certain type of hotel you have a certain expectation. In NYC, where even the small properties have doormen to assist with luggage, hail a cab, and greet you when you arrive, we certainly expected as much at a Ritz Carlton. Not so. Yes, there were 3 or 4 doormen. Yes, they hailed a cab for me at one point. However, they were never AT THE DOOR, but instead hanging by the front desk (where they couldn't see who was coming up the steps until they were already inside) or huddling in the luggage hold area. In fact, as the weather deteriorated, they were no where to be found. It may sound like a small smear for an otherwise good review, but the front door staff needs training at this Ritz property.

title: “Perfect Location for Authentic NYC Experience”
text: My sister and I took a 5 day trip to NYC, her first time and my fourth. I was trying to find a hotel that was within easy walking distance from the subway, restaurants and shops without being in a touristy area. WSH is perfect. Ronnie the doorman/concierge was a gem. From check in to check out he had helpful tips and information to make our stay better. The room was small, bathroom tiny, but we weren't in NYC for a rest; with everything to see and do we didn't spend much time in the hotel. However the time we spent there was comfortable. The continental b'fast was perfect, sometimes hard to find a seat but usually the guests were coming and going so we didn't have to wait long. We had drinks in the lounge one evening and found the other patrons were mostly locals, not guests of the hotel which made for an interesting evening of people watching. There is a safe, hair dryer and iron in the room; I am 5' 8" and found the twin bed comfortable. The room was clean so what else do you need?!

title: “Just What I Expected”
text: Family of 4 stayed at the Gaslamp Plaza Suites for 3 nights in late July in a Junior Suite (1 bedroom). Found the hotel to be what I had expected based on previous reviews. Excellent location for downtown without a car. Nice staff. Hotel is older but well kept. Breakfest is minimal. Very good value for the location. Noisy on Sat. night but I am a heavy sleeper so this was not a problem. My only complaint was that I found the beds to be way to soft. Other than that I would stay here again.

title: “Spacious and Friendly”
text:
I had such a busy schedule in Seattle, I barely got more than a few hours of sleep each night but the two nights I spent at the Maxwell Hotel were very nice anyway. The rooms are clean and large and the bathrooms even more so. They have free internet access and the location is great - not too far from the Space Needle and the staff are very friendly with calling cabs for you. 
I would recommend booking as soon as possible, as the hotel does seem to fill up fairly quickly. Also, I wasn't exactly pleased with the fact that they don't really serve a traditional hotel breakfast but the Citizen Creperie three blocks from the hotel is excellent (try their banana bread~!) so all-in-all it was okay. Also, they have a QFC three blocks from hotel, too, so, fabulous!

title: “Great hotel- wonderful views and luxury unique to this hotelier”
text: I love this hotel! The location was wonderful- right near the park, central to the city and right off of the river front. The staff were friendly, the spa was amazing, and the beds were divine. I would've liked to have a regular coffee maker in the room, but the espresso machine was a nice change. We ate at Aria as well- it was definitely well run and the cocktail menu was divine. Chicago is a great city and staying at the Fairmont just made it that much more memorable. Just watch out for the cost of valet parking ($50/night- ouch)!

title: “Excellent choice for auto show.”
text:
Stayed one night for auto show, very convenient location. Room was very clean and nice, used people mover to go to Cobo center. Front desk staff very friendly and helpful. Many plaeces around to get a nice dinner. Will come back again.
Stayed January 2012

title: “Great Hotel”
text: This is a wonderful hotel to stay in. The bathrooms are not anything like some people have stated. They are very private from the main room . I would rather have a glass door between the toilet area than an old hollow wood door. I stay in the major hotel chains but after the stay here, I will make it apoint to stay at this location. Very clean rooms!

title: “Mixed Reveiw”
text: My girlfriend and I arrived at the Omni on Thursday, August 30 for 5 days and thoroughly excited about being in NY for the first time. When we booked the hotel through Expedia we requested a room with double beds and followed through with a phone call to the Reservation desk at the Omni a week prior to arrival. Unfortunately, neither request was fulfilled and the front desk could do nothing to accommodate us – so we ended up sharing a bed. Upon speaking with the manager, a promise of some sort of amenity was given but the offer was never fulfilled. It was a very frustrating experience and makes one wonder if you book through a travel venue such as Expedia if requests are given second priority? The hotel itself was lovely although we could hear everything in the rooms next to us - including conversations of the occupants.

title: “Neat hotel with an awesome location...”
text: I really enjoyed staying at this hotel, the location was great with the 1 was at the corner, diners down the street and Starbucks next door. No elevator and you immediately have to walk up a flight of stairs just to check in. They have a bar with tasty drinks you can take back to your room. The room is a normal boutique size with "Moroccan" flair. My room had a very nice flat screen TV and a radio/cd player/ alarm clock. The bathroom was clean and big for the size of the room. No view, no restaurant and normal NYC noise. All of this was fine with me and I will keep this hotel in mind whenever I go back for a visit.

title: “Need Improved Customer Service”
text: I chose this hotel because of the low medical rate. I am working in the area and will be for some time. The cleanliness still needs to be worked on. The carpets are older and need vacummed. I have called on several occasions to try and get a room. Many times, even after 8PM, they put you on hold forever. Once I was put on hold for several minutes (long distance) and then told that they would take my number and call me back. They never did. There needs to be management in place to check the cleanliness of the rooms from a customer vantage point, and someone there to show the help what customer service should be like. Really needs major cleanup and change.

title: “Modern, comfortable and convenient city hotel”
text: The common areas of this hotel - entrance, desk, bar, lifts - are very W: dark, modern, full of music and design elements. The rooms are more standard, yet new, clean-cut and cleverly designed to fit all facilities and high-tech equipment into a relatively small space (given that this is in the middle of a very expensive city, one can't expect large rooms). The bathroom is particularly pleasant, with marble, large towels and great Bliss toiletries. The special W bed is a clear highlight, extra-comfortable and really plush. San Francisco town center starts only a few steps away and there are restaurants and cafes just around the corner. There is as much glass as possible so you can see the view, though in this part of town there is little more to see from above than high-rise buildings. All in all, it is a great city hotel - price aside - and I would very happily stay again!

title: “Fantastic Service”
text: Every person from the bellmen to the concierge that I encountered at the Westin Washington on M Street was gracious, acommodating, and engaging. Lynn Jackson, the Concierge, was so helpful and just as excited for us to enjoy our visit as we were to be there. Her advise and assistance made our stay delightful. There was another lady at the concierge desk on Sunday who was very helpful as well. The rooms were wonderful - fashionable decor, well appointed, fresh and clean. The only adjustment I had to make was the description ofwalking distances - in Oklahoma we drive everywhere so a 15 minute walk in OKC is rather different than a 15 walk in DC. It's good thing though because walking is much healthier for me and the environment!

title: “Would not stay here again.”
text: My recent stay on July 20, 21, 2012 was anything but nice. The hotel room carpet was filthy and the noise level was so bad from other guest that I checked out earlier than planned...I noticed that the iron was attached to the ironing board and was cumbersome using it. Also the bed comforters were soiled and the lighting was dim...one of the light fixtures was not working. Parking was ok but your sticker had to be posted in the window otherwise you would be towed from the premises.

title: “Happy once again!”
text: We just spent the weekend here (2 nights) 6/11 & it was just as good as the other 2-3 times we have stayed there. It is a little away from the center of the riverwalk, so a little walk, but we love that. We prefer being away from the hustle & bustle, so perfect location for us. We have no complaints and will stay again on our next visit.

title: “Good Stay”
text:
My Stay at the Mariott Beverly Hills was pretty basic but Good.
The rooms were very clean,and especially the Kitchen area.
the LCD T.V. was a plus for my son who enjoyed watching Cartoon Network while I took care of business.
The Location is pretty good, lots of resturants .75 miles north on Beverly Dr. Taxis always available but expensive, rent a car.
Universal City Walk is 9.5 miles away and a $40.00 cab ride each way. my 6 y.o. son enjoyed City Walk and we sipped on Frappachino's and counted the RR Phantom's on Rodeo Dr.
I stopped at 24 after about 30min. 
The FREE breakfast in the hotel is just that FREE. It's something to hold you til lunch. Eggs,French Toast,Sausage,Fruit, Sliced Peaches, and dry cereal for the kids. I tryed it once then was referred to Norms about a mile and a half west on Pico.
It was a greasy spoon joint with good home cooked breakfast
my son and I licked our plates. 
overall I will reccomend staying here again for Rates under $200.00 a night.
P.S. Front desk staff was very nice and courteous.

title: “Know What You're Getting - Not Much”
text:
The Braxton is definitely crap. And overpriced at that.
Most of the outlets in my room were not functional. I had to unplug the TV to plug in my laptop.
The air conditioner is actually a fan. I set it to high heat and it was just as cold as on high cool.
The shower has very little pressure, but the bathroom was reasonably clean. I've only seen one insect and it was pretty small.
Most of the furniture and facilities seem to be "second hand" goods from other hotels. The phone on my table says I'm in the Holiday Inn at Dulles. Not exactly. Their fax machine says they are a Gas and Power company.
The lock on the door was so flimsy I could pry it open with my hands and no tools. A screwdriver would probably make easy work of every door in the hotel. Needless to say, I checked my luggage in with the front desk every day when I left. I suggest you do the same. And lock it.
On top of all that, they screwed up my reservation. I got conflicting information from Orbitz and Sidestep about the availibility at the hotel, so I called to make sure that they had a room for all of the nights I needed. I was also VERY explicit with the woman who handled my call that I needed the room to be prepaid, as someone other than myself was paying. When I arrived at the hotel, I was informed that my reservation had been held but not prepaid and they had my departure date wrong. Turns out they were, in fact, sold out for the last night of my stay. Fortunately for me, my plans changed and I'm leaving a day early, anyway.
The Braxton was the only hotel with the nights I needed available for under $300/night within 1 mile of the place I'm working. I knew what I was buying, but it certainly confirmed my worst expectations. Stay elsewhere if at all practical. I highly recommend the nearby Beacon Hotel, which often has affordable rates.

title: “Very Classy Indeed!”
text:
We stayed here for 2 nights in early April while on our honeymoon. 
We had a spacious, elegant corner suite on the 24th floor with stunning views of St. Patricks Cathedral, Top of The Rock & Radio City Music Hall, both day & night. A huge flat screen tv, fabulous bathroom & large comfy bed, in an immaculate room. 
A great location, wonderful service & a trendy (but pricy!) bar results in a top stay in mid town New York. Recommended.

title: ““Excellent experience with conference staff””
text:
This was our first Board meeting at the Sheraton Gateway Los Angeles, it was very close to LAX, perfect for traveling members to fly in and out conveniently and the free shuttle was also a huge plus. Our personal attendant Estela Estrada was professional, attentive and excellent at her job, we were extremely pleased with her.
The only two things that we could offer suggestions for: Better signage directing people where our meeting was, some people had a had a hard time locating the room because there was nothing put up. Additionally the valet parking was not very well organized, one person on duty while two others stood by (apparently waiting for their shift to begin or on break). We waited 20+ minutes for our car.
The facilities were nice and clean, everyone was friendly and helpful, we would definitely consider using the Sheraton Gateway Los Angeles for meetings again in the future.

title: “Comfy, Cozy and good location”
text:
We spent 4 nights here in early August 2009 with a group tour from France. 
The staff were on their toes and very helpful. The lobby is tastefully decorated and well appointed - a comfortable place to "chill out". ATM right behind the lobby as well as a laundry room, which can come in very handy. Wifi in the lobby area. Coffee/tea bar tastefully hidden in a little nook in the lobby. Our room was clean and comfortable, featured high-speed internet connection (with RJ45 plug). 
The breakfast buffet was more than adequate (bread, bagels, raisin bread + big toasters), but closes at 9am. Unfortunately, this means that by 8:30am there's nothing much left to eat. Do as we did, gather up your courage and go downstairs before 8am, fix your breakfast and take it back to your room! We saw lots of people doing this...
If you miss your breakfast, there's always the diner next door (with a direct access from the lobby), or a bakery a block away from the hotel (exit right, leaving the hotel), with a huge array of donuts and hot breakfasts (eggs, bacon, pancakes). 
HOWEVER. Please do be careful with the homeless people in the area. Our tour guide had her suitcase stolen from the sidewalk in front of the hotel - but managed to get it back with the help of 3 guys from our group and a small "tip" to the homeless guy. This seems to be a recurrent problem in the area as there is a homeless shelter 1-2 blocks away from the hotel. Nothing to freak out over - just don't leave any bags unattended.
Convenient location. MUNI (bus) in front of the hotel - and on both streets north and south of the hotel. Get a 1 or 3 day pass and a map. 
I read the comment from a previous blog about "bed bug" problem and was very concerned about this. I checked the Bed Bugs Registry (www.bedbugregistry.com). This hotel is indeed on the list, as are most of the hotels in the area. I'm happy to say that neither we nor anyone else in our group of 41 experienced a bed bug problem.
Overall, the hotel was much better than expected.

title: “A skinny hotel with an abundance in service”
text: From the street you see the sign, and then you look up and notice the hotel is only two windows wide...but once inside the lobby is very inviting. Great design, Mac's in lobby, living art, bar/breakfast area very comfortable. The room was super clean, sleek design, very, very comfy beds. The guest services were great, everyone went out of their way to meet our needs. I will stay here again...and hopefully there will be a room available, after all these great reviews.

title: “Good for business”
text: Stayed four days in connection with a conference. Nice room and super service. The restaurant on 36 floor has great views but is apparantly closing in the near future. Ask for a room on a high floor! I was on third floor and there is a lot of noise from the street (people and construction). The location is perfect for business and shopping.

title: “In the middle of it all!”
text:
My husband and I stayed at this Hampton Inn for 2 nights. It is a high rise hotel and we were on the 14th floor. There are only about 10 rooms on each floor. The building is tall and narrow and has a lot of historical charm. I enjoyed seeing the old fashioned mail chute. This is clearly an older building that has been transformed into a hotel. It is clean and has been updated to Hampton standards. Our room had very high ceilings and was right next to the fire escape, which I found interesting. Being downtown, there was some noise from traffic but not enough to be disturbing. The breakfast was the same as all Hampton Inns. The staff members maintained it very well. There is no pool in this hotel which could be an issue for some but did not bother us.
The location is perfect, only a few blocks from the Magnificent Mile and the Theater District. The red line has a stop a half a block away which makes getting around town extremely quick and easy. You can buy passes for the red line at the Walgreens at the end of the block. We did all of our traveling by foot or on the red line or the bus, which are accessible from the same pass. Valet parking at the hotel is mandatory and pricey! We never used our own car but the valet men were very friendly. They always offered us advice on where to go and offered to make reservations or arrange transportation for us.
Overall, this was a nice place to stay. We did not spend a lot of time in the hotel because there is so much to experience in Chicago!

title: “Very clean and large room.”
text: We booked this hotel because of its proximity to back bay bus station (an easy walk through the Prudential Centre). Our room was very spacious and clean. Although it is a 15 minute walk to Boston Common, the location is still good. Lots of shops and restaurants on nearby Boylston and Newbury Streets are just around the corner. Jerry on the concierge desk was the best concierge we have ever dealt with.

title: “Great for families - ONLY”
text: Stayed at this hotel due to its proximity to Mission Bay where we were attending a wedding. For this, location was fine, we had a car, hotel was fine as were staff. Our only issue was that it was OVERRUN by families and children. Breakfast was like my worst nightmare. It was more like a zoo with children running over you and in every direction, like they had never been parented in their lives! Probably because it is close to SeaWorld, all the families stay here. For my husband and I, hoping for a bit of peace and quiet it was the absolute opposite. We ended up going out and paying for breakfast because we just couldn't stand that environment.

title: “good location, nice room”
text: I was pleasantly surprised by the quality of the room - nice renovation, modern touches, great bathroom and lighting. and we loved the location, just a block to hop on the subway

title: “The absolute closest hotel to Convention Center”
text: This is 1 block from convention center near train, famous Gaslamp District, wonderful running trail. The hotel is small in comparison to the others in the same 2 blocks. Omni, Hard Rock, Marriott, Embassy. It was just a tad cheaper than the others. The bed was very comfortable. Thats about the only good thing I can say about the room. There is no wi-fi in the rooms. They do have ethernet hook-up at the desk. I'm spoiled with wi-fi. There are so many restaurants in the area you are bound to have leftovers. After a $50 solo meal I am not leaving leftovers at the restaurant. Unfortunately when I opened the mini fridge cabinet there was NO fridge. For $200 a nite I want a freaking mini-fridge. My friends did have a room where the windows opened all the way and that was very nice -room 732. My window opened about 2 inches- room 338. It was a nice enough hotel but I wont be staying here again. I have stayed at the Omni and the Hard Rock across the street and would stay there even with the slight price increase.

title: “Decent Place and Location, but a Monument to Dreary 1970's Architecture”
text: Decent, clean hotel, if you need a room in a pinch, but drab, gray and gloomy, from the concrete entrance canopy to the Communist-looking hallways. The place lacks natural light everywhere, including the guest rooms, many of which overlook a dreary atrium. Bar area is not off the lobby, but is upstairs, making it hard to find and giving the lobby a dead feel with no energy. Rooms are small (although not unusual in DC), but are generally clean and comfortable. Hotel is centrally located within easy walking distance to many business centers, longer walk or Metro ride to tourist sites. When DC is booked up because of some big convention, check here and you’re likely to find a room available simply because there’s no charm or appeal to this hotel at all.

title: “Awesome family friendly resort”
text: My 8 yr. old daughter and I spent spring break week at the Biltmore, March 19th week. The resort is absolutely beautiful and the grounds are immaculate. I was surprised at how friendly everyone was, from the front desk to the gardeners. No request was too small and we were even upgraded to a bigger room with a walkout patio. The pools are heated and were plenty warm to swim comfortably. There were multiple family groups and the lawn chess and croquet were a big hit with the kids. If I had a criticism it would be the food and drink prices. $4 is a bit much for an iced tea. The breakfast buffet at $10 for kids and $16 for adults was well worth the price. I would highly recommend the hotel and look forward to returning for another visit.

title: “We LOVE The Churchill!!!!”
text:
Excellent service, warm and inviting staff, very comfortable rooms. 
The Churchill is where we stay when visiting the city. Working for a historic hotel myself, I know what to look for and what to expect. You want a clean room, in a nice hotel, in a great location, with employees who care about what they're doing. We have stayed many times with our friends at The Churchill and have never been disappointed. 
The location, just above Dupont Circle and a quick walk from the metro stop, is perfect for both the business and leisure parts of our trips. There are several restaurants located very nearby, and many more within a short walk. Shopping is great too, whether near the hotel, in Georgetown (a short/cheap cab ride away), or in the funky Adams Morgan district (also great for Ethiopian food). And a quiet walk around the gorgeous Kalorama area is really something to see...those great houses!!
I cannot say enough great things about the staff. They are at once elegant and sophisticated yet not at all stuffy or intimidating, as I find some city hotels to be. You get none of the attitude and all of the great service and attention to detail. 
The rooms are immaculately clean, and the beds are heaven after a day of walking around those city streets.
Those of you looking for the tourist-trap of a chain property should probably look elsewhere. Why stay in a room at the Marriott in THIS city that looks exactly like the one you stayed in at the Marriott in a different city??? I just can't understand that. If you want to feel like you're really doing the D.C. experience correctly, you'll be happy with The Churchill. 
We'll certainly be coming back for another visit soon!

title: “Downtown Fun”
text: We stayed here in August 2011. The positives about this hotel is that it is within walking distance 2-4 blocks to some really great restaurants and a cab ride to Navy Pier. The room was very nice with internet service, extra towels and fluffy pillows. The negatives about this hotel is the first room they gave us only had one queen bed, well this didn't work since we are a family of four, so we had to call the fron desk and arrange for another room , they appologized and sent us to a double queen, which had the view of a roof top and air conditioning eqipment. What we did not like was the price that had been quoted us changed when we checked out, we stayed three nights with the first night at the quoted price around $200 and the other 2 nights at a $150 increase in price per night, we flipped out!!! I asked why the increase since this was during the middle of the week Tuesday-Thursday and they said anytime a big concert series comes through rates increased to weekend prices. They did not change the rate to what we were originally given. We will not stay here again.

title: “Loved this hotel”
text: We picked this hotel because of previous reviews and we were not disappointed. First time in a Drury and it won't be the last. If you are coming to San Antonio stay here.

title: “Good Hotel”
text:
I stayed for 10 nights at Hotel 31 in November 2004, I had booked a hotel that was slightly more expensive but after reading horrendous reviews I switched to Hotel 31 (I booked through Expedia). I was glad I did I was very nervous as it was very as I did not want to pay a lot for the hotel; I wanted to spend my money enjoying my time in the city.
I was not disappointed, when we arrived I had booked a twin room they gave us a double (I was staying with my mum) The manager was very good said this happened all the time with Expedia they do not give out twin rooms only double. I had to pay extra $50 I thought that was ok.
Good Points 
Clean (All I wanted) Basic hotel
Friendly staff
Good location
The Neighbourhood
Atmosphere of the hotel
Felt safe
Comfy bed
Good shower
Shared bathroom was spotless and cleaned all the time
Bad points
The extremely strong smell (I think it was cleaning fluids) in the hallway
Our view from our window was a wall
Did not like the bed covers (not dirty) just weird and old fashioned
Noisy heating system
In summary I was glad I booked this hotel and had extra money to go to Broadway shows and good restaurants

title: “The Perfect Budget Hotel in NYC”
text: This hotel is the perfect budget hotel, brillant value for money, clean, efficent /friendly staff and in a nice area. We stayed in a bunk bed shared bathroom room, which after reading some reviews on here was actually more spacious than we thought!! The shared bathrooms were always spotless and we never had to wait to use them, there are little lights above the door in the bedroom so you can see when the bathrooms are in use. We had no problem with noise and there are some really nice restraunts close by, everything you would want to visit is in walking distance. We would definately use this hotel again.

title: “GREAT LOCATION! RIGHT IN THE MIX OF SAN DIEGO!”
text:
We stayed 5 nights at this hotel, it is right on the bay and next to the Core-Columbia district. At first glance I thought this place looked a little dated sitting right in front of all the new high rises, but the entire inside has been updated. We were looking for a bay view but alas all were taken so we went with the skyline view. I was glad we did! The city is absolutely stunning to see at night! The rooms all have balconies and the street noise isn't too bad, but the train can get a little annoying sometimes. 
So close to so much! Walking distance to the Midway carrier, Maritime museum, bay ferry, and trolley stop. (Highly recommend the trolley!),
Let me also add that I don't normally give hotel restaurants much cred, but the restaurant at this Holiday Inn is excellent. Oh yea, and its next door to Ruth Criss Steaks and across the street from the best seafood in town!

title: “Best Businessman's Hotel in Houston”
text:
This hotel (Hilton garden Inn, Houston Energy Corridor) is by far the most accomadating hotel in Houston. The people are very friendly and service is excellent.
I've stayed there well over 30 times in the last two years

title: “Not as bad as some say”
text: We checked in on 10/09 and checked out on 10/11/09, stayed in a non-smoking room with two queen beds with our two black labs. In a lot of other reviews people mentioned that the neighborhood that this hotel is in is a little scary and/or questionable but to us it seemed as though it doesn’t matter where you are in Memphis every area is considered questionable. The owners have posted signs that state the place is monitored by security cameras and we did see security cameras so that added a sense of security. There is a very large parking garage right across the street for the hospital that adds a lot of light to the area, don’t let that deter you though, the rooms have black out curtains and we thought it helped the security level of the area as well. By the parking garage there’s a long grassy area to take your pets. The hospital’s ER is about a block away but we’re surprised that we didn’t hear many sirens. We never got a chance to try the internet. Their breakfast is very small. It’s close to many downtown attractions and you have quick access to I-240 to get to others just as quickly. After entering the room we were overwhelmed with the smell of really bad, strong air freshener, it takes awhile to get use to; it’s best to air out the room for awhile. The rooms were large and ours included a small refrigerator (which was iced over) and microwave. The beds were clean and were made everyday however the tile floors needed a good cleaning and we did find many long black hairs in the bedding and on the floor. The owners were very friendly people and appeared to keep good watch over the area when someone came and gone and quickly came to change out the batteries in our chirping smoke detector. Pricing for hotels throughout Memphis don’t seem to match the quality that reviewers were posting online but this place appears to be making an effort with their given location and other circumstances to make this the better place to stay.

title: “Excellent”
text: The Crowne Plaza Times Square is in a very central location. We were easily able to access most things on foot and if we required a taxi, we didn't have any problems finding one. The hotel was perfect for our holiday. The beds are extremely comfortable, the rooms are spacious enought for 4 adults and very clean. The staff were very helpful and we had everything we needed at the hotel. Staying here made our stay in New York easy, I would thoroughly recommend it.

title: “very good, not quite great”
text: The bad news: the thermostat didn't work, 1 of 2 phones didn't either. The walls are a bit thin, the ceilings low, (7 1/2 foot). Now to the good news. This place has the cheeriest, most accommodating staff I've come across in ages; this was true of each and all of them from various shifts and days of the week. The place is attractive, rooms largish, beds exceptionally comfortable. Apparently every room has a large balcony -- ask for the city-view side as the touted view of the Rockies really overlooks the parking lot and the Rockies around Denver simply catch the pollution. Each bed has four pillows of differing composition and thickness, so that almost anyone can find one near to perfect. (Hey, howcum it took so long to think of that!?!) The decor is pleasantly understated classic, the bathrooms large and attractive. There is a hotel "car" (SUV) available to guests for places within 2 miles. The locations is terrific, right on the edge of central Denver, not right in the congestion, but not remote at all. It was a reasonably easy walk to the Denver Art Museum or the convention center even on a cold snowy day. If driving (we weren't) it is a remarkably easy location to getting into or out of Denver or to traverse the city on Colfax. The hotel is located on the edge of Capitol Hill, an attractive, urban-living area with a mixed gay/single/young couple old/young population. There are coffee bars, cheap-eats places mixed among the more fashionable and expensive restaurants. All in all the Warwick Denver was a find.

title: “Nice place!”
text: We stayed at the Tuscan for the last two nights of our holiday following our return from Las Vegas. Having spent the first week in a hotel closer to Union Square we had decided to be nearer to Fishermans Wharf. It was a good decision and we were not disappointed with the hotel. Very conveniently situated just a couple of blocks from Fisherman's Wharf. The hotel was very welcoming and efficient and the room comfortable and beautifully presented. Unfortunately the room looked out onto another building, but it was at least quiet and we didn't spend much time there. The bed was extremely comfortable. The wine tasting session in the early evening was a nice touch and extremely popular and the complementary tea and coffee in the morning was appreciated too. I wouldn't hesitate to stay at the Tuscan again!

title: “I would stay at the Wellington again”
text: We had reservations for 2 in a queen room for 4 nights. At check-in she told us we had a free upgrade to a king tower room on the top floor. It was really a suite, complete with a sofa, coffee table, desk, 2 chairs, 2 closets, a room with a sink, MW and fridge, decent size bathroom and 4 windows looking out over the city from the 27th floor. One window shade would not stay more than halfway down and the room was a little stuffy even with open windows and/or AC, but how nice to have a large room in mid-town Manhattan! It is a great location with nearby restaurants, delis, Carnegie Hall, Central Park and a couple blocks to our subway. A wonderful value for mid-town Manhattan.

title: “The service was amazing!”
text: My husband and I had our wedding at the AZ grand resort November 2010 and it was absolutely wonderful. Our guests could not get over how beautiful the view was and our wedding planner Melanie really kept things together making our wedding a night to remember! Our guests are still talking about it. The rooms were a bit pricey and they did charge us for more guests than we had which was a complete misunderstanding, but the overall atmosphere was so fun. Thank you AZ grand for making our wedding the best!

title: “Great Experience”
text: I was able to get a great deal on a two queen and sofa bed suite through Expedia. The room was large, decorated nicely, clean and quite. The rooftop pool was heated, and changed colors at night. The hot tub was very hot and a good size. Lots of lounge chairs and towels. The free breakfast was excellent. There was a hot buffet with eggs, bacon, sausage, grits and cubed potatoes that was very good. There was an amazing made to order omelet station, that also made eggs to order and I saw them make pancakes too. There were fresh melon and pastries. A coffee, juice, milk and tea station.
