In the evenings there was a manager’s reception that served free drinks and snacks. There was a Red Hot Chili Peppers concert that night, so we weren’t too fond of the type of crowd. Valet parking was very pricy, but the car was in a covered garage and not outside. There were several restaurants that were in walking distance, and the streets were very clean, even though there was a lot of construction. We had a relaxing and fun weekend thanks to Embassy Suites.

title: “Exceptionally helpful staff and great location”
text: It would be hard to beat this spot for convenience to transportation, shopping, the Space Needle, the Convention Center, the Pike Place Market, etc. The staff was among the friendliest and most helpful I have encountered; they even have stamps and envelopes if you have unexpected business to take care of. You wouldn't want to be too fussy about appearances, as there were some stains on the carpet, dirty windows, etc. But if your needs are more functional than aesthetic, this would be a good choice.

title: “A clean hotel with spacious rooms and friendly staff”
text:
I recently stayed at this hotel. It's located a few minute walk from Union Station and well located for DC sightseeing. All of the staff were friendly and the room was clean. Our view looked out on an office bldg that left its lights on all night and created a glare in our room, but that's somewhat expected in any downtown location.
We also ate at the restaurant. It was decent, not great, and predictably overpriced. While friendly the waiter was rather inattentive - I think we had to ask for ketchup three different times. Unfortunately there did not seem to be other restaurants nearby. 
Overall a nice place and as advertised on previous TripAdvisor reviews - wouldn't call it a luxurious hotel, but it's well run, clean and in a good location.

title: “Whatever, whenever? HORRIBLE experience”
text:
Attached is the letter that I sent to hotel management, that came back to me with, "sorry your experience fell short of your expectations and the hotel restaurant has taken steps to correct." No free night stay, no restaurant vouchers, no credits to our credit card, no real attempt at keeping customers. 
Quite honestly, I don’t even know where to begin. Every year, the second week in December my husband plans a downtown weekend for my birthday, which he has done for several years. This includes a minimum two-night stay, dinner and the theater. We live in the suburbs and love spending the weekend in the city. We enjoy shopping, holiday decorations and because of my birthday so close to the holiday, my husband takes special care to make it memorable. To date, we both immensely enjoy the weekend.
All except this last birthday at the W Hotel City Center. I will highlight the less desirable incidents as I feel awful that my birthday celebration was such a disappointment.
December 14, 2007
•Upon arrival in the room, we had to turn the thermostat up because the room was freezing, I don’t mean cold and uncomfortable but “see your breath” freezing.
•The bed was not a standard king, which was stated and the room extremely small.
•The sheet had a large stain which I am going to say was blood at the head of the bed between the pillows. I called the front desk immediately and let them know that we had reservations downstairs at the hotel restaurant at 7:15 p.m. and they could change the sheets while we were at dinner.
•We had dinner at the hotel restaurant (Ristorante We). Absolutely the worst service of any restaurant that we have been to and the food was mediocre at best. From the time we were seated, it took 10 minutes to get a glass of water and my husband had to wave someone down to ask for bread. It took another 10 minutes for the waiter to take our order. As we had plenty of time to look at the menu we ordered the appetizer and entrée initially. It took 25 minutes to receive our appetizer. At that point, we were in the restaurant 45 minutes before receiving an appetizer! The entrée arrived in another 20 minutes. My husband insisted we order a dessert, I told him that I was unwilling to wait 45 minutes for dessert but he insisted that it was my “birthday weekend” and he was equally upset with everything, but remained optimistic determined to have a good time. We ordered dessert. Not only did it 30 minutes to get to us, the order was wrong. My crème brulee was chocolate cake and then the waiter was indignant when I said, “I didn’t order this”. He said that he would put in the order for crème brulee. At that point, the tears started and I asked my husband for the key to our room and waiting another 30 minutes for my dessert was simply absurd. I left the restaurant and waited in the lobby until he was finished with the bill. We he left the restaurant, he then said, “you will NEVER believe this”, not only did he not remove the incorrect dessert from the bill, he haggled me when I told him that it needed removed from the bill and I didn’t even ask him to remove the dessert that I didn’t eat. My husband said, which even surprised me, “today is the first day in my entire life that I left NO tip, though the service was lousy until he hassled me about the dessert, I had every intention of leaving a tip.
•After that horrible experience, we return to the room only to find the sheets had not been changed. I told my husband that I have had enough of the W hotel and I was going to take a long shower, while he took a shot at getting some clean sheets. Sometime after 10 p.m. the sheets where finally changed.
December 15 – 8:00 a.m.
•We left the hotel to go downtown to shop (bought new fleece pajama’s because the room was so cold) and returned to our hotel at 3:30 p.m. to get ready for our 5:00 p.m. reservations at Everest then to the theater for Jersey Boys – Time was of the essence. It had begun to snow so we needed to leave by 4:30 p.m. Upon returning, our room had not been touched, we where gone all day and no one had cleaned the room. The cleaning lady showed up a 3:45 p.m. to clean our room, so we went downstairs to have a drink while our room was cleaned. At that point, my husband apologized for picking such a horrible hotel for my birthday. He said he was ashamed of himself for not doing more research and picked the room from a website because it had a contemporary eclectic style. He felt awful and I felt bad for him and bad that we were stuck there for another night.
•With 4+ inches of snow that we had overnight, the room was freezing when we returned. We thought the cleaning lady had set the thermostat back down, but we discovered she had not. We turned the heat up for the second night in a row.
December 16
•Packing up to leave the room, in adjusting the blinds and drapes realize the window was OPEN. The window was open about an inch and would not close no matter how hard we tried, it was broken open. Which explained why the sounds of the city kept us up every night. 
My husband has apologized with shame countless times, and ends with “I just wanted you to have a great birthday.” Isn’t your motto - Whatever, whenever? Based on the service we received, it sure didn’t feel like it to us. The next time we will spend time doing extensive research (to include on-line reviews) before choosing a hotel or simply stay home and drive to the city for dinner and the theater. We will certainly not recommend the W Hotel or the Ristorante We in the future.

title: “great hotel - centre of the action but without traffic/street noise.”
text: my husband and i chose this hotel for our 40th birthday treat, as it is close to the area we wanted. From past experience, I definitely wanted a "side street" hotel, slightly away from the constant sirens and horn honking of Broadway and Times Square area. This hotel seemed to fit the bill with a great location and reasonably priced room. When we arrived (early) our luggage was kept secure, and upon entering our room, we were amazed to be virtually under the empire state bldg. Couldn't have asked for better views! Close to Macy's, Times Square and the lovely Bryant Park. Short stroll to Grand Central,and Chrysler Bldg, so we couldn't have asked for better. Looking to return to NYC next year - but this time with our two children- and we will definitely book this hotel again. I've recommended it to everyone I know ! bed was really comfortable - definitely on par - or possibly even better than - the Marriott's. We were on the 28th floor and could not hear any traffic noise from the street below - slept well for all 4 nights. A feat in NYC ! Concierge service was very helpful with local info. Go ! Find out for yourself !

title: “Good value for budget travelers”
text:
The inn may not be located at the best location but I must say Sherman oaks was a lovely neighbourhood to live in. It takes us about an hour (or slightly less) to get to hollywood by the metro line. 
They have free breakfast (bread loaf and spread with coffee/milk/juice) and wifi. Staff were helpful and the rooms were big and spacious. Good value for budget travelers who don't mind living off the city.

title: “A gem of a hotel”
text: Found this via Expedia and were really pleased with our stay. there were five of us in total booked over two rooms and they were both excellently decorated and looked after. We stayed for four nights and were well looked after during our stay. Great location for all you want to see within new York and couldn't asked for a better hotel. Will definitely stay here again when we next visit New York. The kitchenette was great for making a quick cuppa for setting out for the day

title: “Recommended”
text: My wife and I booked this hotel on the basis of TripAdvisor reviews. Vacation. Three nights. Spacious and comfortably furnished room. Clean, comfortable and quiet. Adequate breakfast included in rate. High speed internet. All staff courteous and helpful. Location is convenient to Beale Street, Museum of Rock & Soul and shuttle services to other attractions. This new hotel and neighboring hotels are in an area in transformation with a number of building undergoing restoration. At night, we did not feel particularly safe walking to and from hotel because of loiterers and panhandlers on corners and near trolley stops. Note that many restaurants in area are closed on Sunday and Monday nights – not very tourist- friendly. As result, you might be forced to walk to Beale Street for dinner. Beale Street a real disappointment after visiting Bourbon Street. As development continues in the area, the “edginess” should lessen. The concerns expressed relate to Memphis generally rather than this hotel specifically. We recommend this hotel; it has much to offer at a reasonable price.

title: “Decent For a Four Star Hotel”
text: Great Location to most of the Attractions. Hotel was nice! Mini bar was expensive and having to pay $5 for water was a bit crazy. The hotel restaurant food was okay. For good food search around the neighborhood there are tons of great restaurants nearby. The pool is a spa pool and is small. Make sure you plan out where you are going cause parking in Philadelphia is expensive! Over all the stay at the hotel was good.

title: “Everything you need for a comfortable stay…great value”
text:
I stayed at the Touchstone on two business trips, each lasting approximately
10 days, in November and December 2009.
My stays at the hotel were very comfortable and I have nothing less than
positive to say about them. I stayed in two different rooms, and each room
was newly renovated, very tastefully decorated, clean, with fast and
reliable in-room internet connection. I looked forward to returning to my
cozy room in the evening after work.
The hotel staff was very nice and attentive, providing any extra amenities
one might (refrigerator, heater, water boiler). After returning home, I
discovered that I had left my new IPOD in the room.
They found it under the desk and sent it back to me.
The first room I stayed in was a Queen, which was standard size. The second
time I stayed in a Double, which was smaller. Both rooms were facing the
back, and thus very quiet. I recommended the hotel to three of my
colleagues, which ended up staying there as well and liking it.
And yes, the location couldn’t be better for someone who needs to get around
the city quickly, as was the case for me…2 minute walk to the BART and Union
Square, nice, safe neighborhood etc.

title: “WOW!”
text:
We had an awful experience at Nine Zero. My husband and I travel to Boston a lot, and we have never been treated SO rudely in our lives.
My husband has had brain surgery, and since his surgery in 2006 he tends to stutter a bit. 
We were in the hotel lounge and we got asked to leave because they assumed my husband was drunk when he went to order up a couple of beers. It was a complete embarassment, and totally uncalled for since he hadn't even had one drink yet. 
I would never recommend this hotel to anybody. Due to the reckless nature of the hotel employees...and it is completely over priced!
Good Luck

title: “Great find.”
text:
My wife and I visit New York City twice a year, and on this occasion we were looking for a reasonably price hotel near Times Square, with free Internet, free breakfast, and preferably near 47th Street. We read the reviews, and decided to take a chance on an eight nights stay. We were not disappointed; of all the hotels in which we have stayed, I cannot recall a friendlier staff. This is a very modern and elegant boutique hotel, and so we expected the rooms to be small, and so being upgraded to a Deluxe King was a wise decision. This is a small hotel and so the comfortable lobby is never crowded, and we enjoyed many interesting conversations with other visitors and staff while relaxing there and listening to the music. The location is ideal for all the Broadway shows, and Rockerfeller Center, we visited many, all within walking distance. Strangely, this is not a busy street, although restaurants and deli are just steps away. Their rooftop restaurant and bar is an exciting place to visit when the weather is fine, it was really jumping the nights we visited. Despite being the eldest couple there, we were treated like royalty. 
Thanks again to the staff; we will be returning in the future.

title: “Paradise in San Diego!”
text: My wife and I try to go to San Diego once a year. When we do go we have to stay at The Dana. They have a very friendly staff and you can't beat the views of Mission Bay. We look forward to next time!

title: “Oh yes!”
text:
I like it! Everything was clean, modern, and well cared for. Perfect for the business traveler, no fuss. You can check in on your own, love the location right off of MI avenue. Lots of restaurants and activities. Rooms are extremely large and accomodating.
Parking is $52!!!! WTF. I stayed here on business travel. I would NEVER stay here and pay that, it's ridiculous!
You can park in several garages around the hotel for $35; I found this on my own. When I called and asked the hotel the decided not to give me this information. They said the only thing around was the $52 valet. Good thing I checked! If it wasn't for the parking I would stay here on weekends w/ friends and family just to be in the city.

title: “My 5th stay at the W on Lex”
text:
I travel to NYC a few times a year on business and am now a regular at the W on Lex. The location is perfect, the staff are great (special mention to Sammy at check-in for sorting me out with a late check- out) and the rooms though on the small side actually have everything you need.
Add in a great option for breakfast at the restaurant off the lobby and free apples in reception and you have a great package.
Just one minor gripe - getting in and out with large bags is tough. The two revolving doors are hopeless with a big suitcase, and the other door is never staffed, so you too often end up struggling. Not a huge issue, but worth addressing.

title: “Low rates, great location - close to Pike Place Market”
text:
My partner and i decided to stay here for one night prior to our cruise and we are quite happy we did. This hotel was recently renovated, and is close to all downtown and Capital Hill attractions. 
One detail I loved about this hotel was the suite aspect, this provides two rooms just in case you are traveling with others or want some extra space. We did not visit the pool or bar area. 
Pike Place Market is a down hill, 10 min walk away. I think they also offer a shuttle, but there is really no need. You can also walk up hill (15 mins) to Capital Hill if you are looking for a bar scene. 
I highly recommend hitting Pike's Place if you can - check out Etta's and Elliot's happy hour! 
Oh, and this hotel provides a cruise shuttle for 7 a person. 
Be sure to ask for the quiet side of the hotel, the other side is on a highway.

title: “Could be my favorite hotel, but...”
text: We recently stayed here for the second time. Our first trip in August was wonderful-the room was huge and the staff fabulous. This time, however, we experienced all sorts of problems. We had booked our room (a king in the historic tower) over the internet-no deal ($349.00 per night)- but convenient. When we arrived, there was a large group of foreign tourists having all sorts of problems. After 15 minutes, the man behind me went to the assistant manager and demanded she help check people in. Naturally she was angry and after many heavy sighs, checked us in. The room was in the new tower and tiny with two small double beds. We immediately went downstairs to correct the room situation. My husband had written confirmation of our room, but this didn't matter-she insisted on arguing that this "wasn't in the computer." After advising her I was tired of her snotty attitude, we finally got the room we paid for. The luggage took forever to get to the room and the elevators were incredibly slow. The doormen were great though. The location is awesome and it's a shame that the management staff is so unresponsive. Our daughter is a student in the Chicago area and we will be visiting several times a year-we thought we had finally found "our" hotel. Prior to this trip, we had already booked a room for our anniversary in January-we'll see.

title: “Wonderful hotel but be CAREFUL with your events!”
text:
I had a hard time deciding between three or four stars...all of my guests probably found it to be a four or five star trip but the stress I went through definitely deserves the three star rating.
I was lucky enough to marry the love of my life at Loews this year. It is a gorgeous venue that manages to keep the historical art deco feel while still seeming very modern. I also couldn't get over how friendly everyone was; from the front desk to the maids, everyone seemed genuinely excited for me and tripped pver themselves to make our time special.
The one thing that turned this event from a happy event into a stressful one was the woman who was in charge of our event, Nickoletta. She,like everyone else, was very sweet and very lovely, but she was incredibly disorganized and bordering on incompetent.She was supposed to be helping with the planning and instead I found myself having to remind her several times of different things and even then they wouldn't get done. A front desk manager had to arrange for my bridal suite and my parent's room...they weren't in the system and obviously hadn't been arranged for ahead of time. She created more work and stress for me at every turn, and while everything was eventually worked out, I would be very careful in using Loews (or maybe just Nickoletta) for your events.
I would love to stay here again for a vacation, but I'll be taking my events elsewhere..

title: “We liked it very much and will return some day!”
text: Rather surprised this hotel is not ranked higher because we felt this hotel was excellent for several reasons: good value (although we used points), great pub-like place for breakfast that was very good and reasonably priced, excellent location for walking to the downtown shopping area, staff were VERY helpful, cabs were always easy to get. Made dinner reservations for us to eat at Salty's and had the restaurant's limo van pick us up and return us - excellent service! One of the top 10 in our book!

title: “Construction woes.”
text:
I reserved a 3 night stay at this hotel based in part on the good reviews I read. To the hotel's credit, I received an e-mail in advance of my travel telling me the hotel would be starting a lobby/restaurant renovation the week I was there, but that it would not affect my room. 
I arrived during lobby demolition and could not hear to check in. The room was okay but hardly worth the $229/night I paid. It was small and had an odor like old paint. The carpet was dirty and stained. There was a long black hair wrapped in the hair dryer's cord. There was something in the room that triggered my allergies. 
When I walked to dinner, the elevator to the lobby floor had been closed. I had to go to the lower level, walk into the basement of the parking facility, find the stairs and walk up (after I found them) to the new temporary lobby. It was inconvenient and a bit creepy for a woman traveling alone. 
The next morning I called the front desk to tell them I was leaving early. When I checked out, they didn't ask how things were or why I was leaving. I found a fabulous hotel nearby for $50 less per night. 
This hotel may be fine after the lobby renovation is complete, but because of the issues with the room, I won't be returning. On a positive note, the valet service was fast and super friendly.

title: “Good location”
text:
Hotel was well located. Rooms quite cozy and a comfy bed. Bathroom was fine, but as others have said...the toilet flush is really noisy and likely to wake up 'the other half' in the middle of the night.
We did find that the door to the adjcent room was really thin, so got
disturbed one night by next door's antics, but a quick phone call to reception at 3am and it was soon sorted. 
The only real grip I had was the attitude of the reception desk manager (whose name I forget) but had the charm of a brick. He was neither welcoming or terribly polite and, having just arrived in Seattle from Vancouver, I was shocked and disappointed at the welcome
to the city. My tip to the hotel management would be to send this guy
on a charm course...or maybe just get somebody else in. Other than that, an OK hotel in a convenient part of town.
Cheers!

title: “Great Stay”
text:
I was surprised to find this hotel so pleasant. Everyone was kind and very service oriented; ready to help in any way. We got there a bit early and immediately held our bags and asked if we needed anything (since our flight was a late one they also kept our bags until departure time). The room was comfortable; the maid wrote me a note each day wishing me a good day. The location was the only thing not great for me, but for anyone wishing to go shopping at canal street they would love it. I did love that we were walking distance to Soho as well as many great restaurants and subway.
Palm Beach resident

title: “INCREDIBLE SERVICE!!!”
text:
I booked this hotel because of the proximity to Discovery Place and other local attractions. My 4 year old son and I were meeting my husband (who is in military training in GA) halfway and I liked the reviews I read on a few sites.
I can't begin to tell you how incredible the service was from the second we checked in to the second we left. They gave my husband a second parking pass to the garage at no charge. They 'mapquested' and printed out directions for us when we asked about liquor stores or pizzerias in the area. When my son came down with a stomach virus on the second night, and we had to ask for another bed sheet, they called back to make sure he was OK. That in itself will make me come back to this hotel AND recommend it to anyone going to Charlotte. 
The food was good...the cookies were DELICIOUS!!..and the service was great! My son is a bit shy, but when the waitress brought out a Mickey Mouse pancake during our 'first' breakfast there, he completely warmed up to everyone! She told me she had a surprise for him, but I didn't know what it was. On the day we were leaving they gave us a couple of large Starbucks coffees to go and were as friendly then as they were when we first checked in.
Oh yeah...and the rooms were extremely clean (one of my pet peeves) and sooooo comfortable. 
I haven't had a stay like this in a hotel in a long time...and we do a lot of traveling.

title: “You'll pay for any and all extras.”
text:
Beautiful historic hotel with comfortable rooms, close to Millennium Park. Fantastic decor.
My only beef with the place is that they charge for items that really ought to be included for free: coffee maker, fitness center, and wireless internet. Really, who charges for these things these days? Well, The Palmer House, that's who.

title: “great for baseball fans”
text: The hotel is a great business hotel. We stayed a few nights with two adjoining rooms for my kids. The train wasn't an issue as others have posted. Breakfast is very expensive. Got a great rate through priceline. Free shuttle van drops you off wherever you need to go in the city. Not the best neighborhood. Very nice hotel.

title: “The standard for an American 5 star hotel”
text:
Everything about this hotel is amazing. It is not often that I stand in awe of a hotel lounge, but this one certainly did it for me. The Willard's design is of a period of American might and money that was only seen by the rich and the famous. Just walking into it wisps away any doubt about the cost of a room. The staff were quick to any needs, and had the concierge provided top notch recommendations of how to get around. 
We were in DC for the July 4th fireworks (a must see at least once) which causes the city to be flooded with droves of people. The hotel is only short walk from the National Mall, which allowed us to quickly return to our rooms once they were over instead of battling the hundreds of thousands of spectators. Keep in mind that they will need to check your key to let you into the building during major events such as July 4th. You will understand when you see the number of people on the streets. 
Our room was much larger than I even thought it would be. Perhaps I got upgraded and did not notice, but we had more room than some apartments have. I got to see into some of the suites, and they are well worth it if you have the extra money (but a bit too pricey for me). Expect to pay for internet (its an InterContinental... they all charge) and for parking if you bring your car. I recommend just flying into DC and taking the metro or a taxi. Its cheaper, and way more convenient then trying to find parking - then paying a lot for it.

title: “Excellent Business Hotel”
text:
Stayed here on a business trip. Loved the hotel. It's well situated on the west end of the downtown core. The view from my room was truly spectacular.
Excellent bed, desk and bathroom. 
Great lounge in the lobby and walking distance to many restaurants.

title: “Great rooms in excellent hotel”
text: We have stayed many times in New York and the rooms are always small, whatever the hotel, until we stayed here. The room was great - large, well equipped and comfortable - better than many much more expensive hotels. The service was also great - very friendly and helpful. Good complimentary breakfast and also free coffee and cookies in reception are a very nice touch. We would hearltily recommend this hotel.

title: “Safe Haven”
text: My Husband was having a complicated surgery at Mayo Hospital in Jacksonville FL. For the 1st week I stayed in a hotel nearer the Hospital at nearly double the price. Since I only slept for a few hours a night and only needed a clean bed and a safe place, I chose Red Roof Southpoint which filled the need nicely. Kim (Desk) helped find the best rate and was great. The room was clean, quiet and safe which was what I wanted. Coffee was always available and there is a Cracker Barrel in walking distance. It is also a quick trip from the Hospital by expressway.

title: “Thrilled to have such a great JDV choice at LAX”
text:
Loved everything about my stay. Decor, bed,room. Best of all staff. Helped me store my luggage for my next international flight, as I was able to pick up some food items at Ralphs next door for my friends in Chile. Very helpful with tips of things in area. 
I am so relieved to have such a great spot at LAX. Do not hesitate stay here!!!

title: “Still working out the kinks”
text: We stayed at the Wit for the city Marathon in October and mostly concur with the previous reviewers' comments. Little touches like the nature sounds in the hallways and the modern furnishings contribute to an overall positive experience. The rooftop bar and State and Lake restaurants are convenient services. However several gliches in service were poorly handled. Our shower had almost no water pressure and the shower head needed to be handheld because the bracket was broken. We called for repairs and when we returned to the room in the evening, the shower head had been 'rubber banded' to the bracket. We also never had room cleaned during our stay since we left at 9am and returned at 5pm and the housekeeping staff was still working in the hall. Rooms are small, similar to NYC hotels. Our 'river view' king spa room's description led us to think there was more that sufficient room for 2 parents and one tween. However we needed to majorly rearrange the room each evening so our son could sleep on the pull out sofa. It left no floor space so we needed to walk on the mattresses to get from one side of the room to the bathroom. A 'river view' meant standing on your tiptoes in the corner window to get a view.

title: “Awesome!!”
text: I traveled to NYC with 2 friends for shopping and a Broadway play. I checked online reviews as I searched for a place for us to stay. The Hampton Inn had excellent reviews so I made reservations. Now I am back to add another excellent review to the list. I cannot say enough good things. All the staff was extremely accommodating. Even after we checked out of our room, the bellboy let us leave our luggage there because we had a late flight out and wanted to do some more shopping. When we came back to pick up our luggage, the bellboy had a taxi waiting for us to take us to the airport. The hotel was immaculate. The breakfast was awesome! Great selection!! Everyone was extremely friendly. The location is great. Just a couple of blocks from shopping and Broadway. I could say so much more but I think you get the picture.

title: “Great for an escape!”
text: I loved staying here but there were a few Cons: The air conditioner didn't manage to keep the room as cool as we wanted it after coming in from the miserable August heat. Also, my boyfriend had an issue with the shower water being too hot (my shower was fine) as well as the $9.99/night charge for internet, if you want it. Oh, and factor into the price of your room $25-$30 for parking. There are, however, many redeeming Pros: It's within walking distance of the Alamo and Riverwalk. I enjoyed the ornate decor, comfy bed and other amenities (coffee maker, toiletries from Bath & Body Works, iron/ironing board, closet space!) and if you really need internet, there are two community computers on the ground level. The staff is also very friendly and helpful. I definitely recommend this place if you want to spend time with the people you're with on your trip without being distracted by the the internet or an enormous TV.

title: “Not for family, maybe if young single and on a tight budget”
text: Checked in and checked out within 15 minutes. The adjacent room was playing loud rap music with pounding bass. After complaining to fromt desk nothing was done, just given the option to move to a different room. That and the poor conditions, old bathroom and stained carpets, we repacked the car and got out of there to go to the renaissance hotel on nob hill.

title: “Not worth the price”
text: Hotel room was not cleaned the first day and had to tell the front desk to have someone clean the room. They only changed the towels and made the bed. These were the only things done for the 4 of the 5 days we stayed. No wash cloths were with the towels and had to request from the front desk. The A/C was not working properly and only response from repair was a note left saying tried his best but problem is the compressor. Breakfast and manager's reception was okay. Nothing special. Some of the exercise machines in fitness center were inoperable. Not worth the price paid.

title: “OK, but under renovation in May 2011”
text: Hotel was under renovation and reception, restaurant etc. were relocated in temporary locations. Room was OK, after they had fixed the aircon which weren’t working. Bad experience was laundry, which managed to loose a shirt of mine. Noise could be heard from the Airport and you could feel the cold wind blowing in through the windows – maybe they should change the windows instead of updating the lobby-area? There are a few restaurants in walking distance, and the Italian DiCicco’s I walked to 1½ block away was a good choice, recommended by the front-desk. Otherwise the area is hotels and only hotels, servicing DIA, so don’t go there for location. Shuttle service was very convenient and I didn’t pay for parking.

title: “nothing to complain about”
text:
since i came to washnigton to see the sights and monuments rather then going to a resort or a vactaion, all i needed was a nice hotel , close to the main attractions. 
this my folks is this hotel, small, comfy, serves tea and coffee in the lobby al day, and has good breakfast that is served in the lobby. around 0900 am the lobby is crowded with people eating that makes you feel your in a cheap lounge. 
the rooms are small and there is no elevator
, the view isn;t the hotels best features. the baths are clean and rahter big compaired to the room it self. the tv is in a closet. 
, but if your looking to a place to crash after a hard day of walking to the national mall and museums, it just the one you need.
p.s it's about 15min walk to washington monument and the white house.

title: “Great hotel for business travel”
text: We have been staying here regularly for business travel. The staff is outstanding. Very friendly, helpful and efficient. At the front desk, Latoya always makes the team feel welcome. The rooms are always clean and well cared for. Don at the lobby bar is terriffic and seems to know all the local Kearny Mesa history. The hotel recently started serving breakfast at 6:00 AM rather than 6:30. This is a very welcome change as we like to be at work no later than 7:00 AM. Thanks to the 6:00 AM breakfast, now our days are off to a better start.

title: “A pleasant surprise”
text:
I was in town for business and wanted to try somewhere new or different from the usual corporate hotel. St. Gregory's location, traveler reviews/photos and an excellent room rate of $119 on Expedia made for an appealing case. 
From reception to farewell, the multi-national staff was extremely courteous, professional, ready with answers to any questions I had and dedicated to ensuring that my (one night) stay was enjoyable. When the lock to my room's door was found to be broken, they graciously moved me to an upgraded suite with a kitchenette. The room was quiet, had excellent internet access and I was able to get a lot of work done. The doorman gave me several "insider's" recommendations for shopping and dining, all of which were perfect.
The one observation I have is that the bathroom was a bit dated and small, and overnight valet parking costs around $35, which is in line for DC (I personally find it money well-spent in the Foggy Bottom/Georgetown area, where free self-parking is rare but tow-away zones are not). But overall I enjoyed my experience at St. Gregory's and highly recommend it if you're looking for a nice gem of a hotel in the Foggy Bottom area that offers character, good value, great service and ambience.

title: “I Wasn't Going to Do This”
text:
It's not like the secret isn't out. I mean, for years people have been staying at The SoHo Grand. But I never did because when I went to Tripadvisor, I was some times scared off by the uneven reviews. 
Which lead me to stay in many different places: The Rivington, Hotel Gansevoort, The W, etc. But I must say, and I really am loathe to write this but feel a certain responsibility to like-minded individuals, The SoHo Grand is the best hotel I've stayed in in the city. Period.
First off, it's beautiful, and beautiful in a New York way. So while your personal tastes might be one thing or another, the SoHo Grand captures New York City (all the good parts anyway) and puts it into every single detail, large and small: the black and white photography adorning the walls, the dress code on the sleek and handsome staff, the large, glorious coffee cup waiting for you in your hotel room -- it's even present right down to the glorious Terrazzo floors you step upon when you first enter this stunning hotel. 
As far as the guest rooms go, each is so comfortable, even homey. The bathrooms have that lovely white brick-style New York'y tile, the bathtubs are deep, roomy, but not too large -- which I, a bath person, do not enjoy, the water pressure reminds one of why every New Yorker brags about New York plumbing. The lotion has a lovely vanilla aroma, and the shampoo actually WORKS! And even the hardware like the sink handles, etc. are that sort of white porcelain with black writing you'd think you'd see if you were staying in some grand hotel in the Manhattan of the twenties or forties.
Maybe the SoHo Grand is what the Algonquin was like in the day (I've stayed there too -- don't bother now, unfortunately). And let me say the views on the north side of the hotel are stunning (I can't vouch for the south, I didn't stay there). Picture postcard. You'll probably have a photographic view of the Empire State Building smack-dab in the middle of your large and spacious bedroom window. Can it get better than that?
Yes. Because the bed is the best in NYC. Or put it this way, it's right up there with The Hotel Gansevoort and I must say, better than my own. I'm thinking of buying the whole thing. And one thing I found considerate and unusual are the draperies. They have a thick heavy, cloth drapery you pull down that very efficiently blocks out much light and, I would venture to guess, noise as well. This is a commodity in Manhattan.
As far as the social aspect goes, the bar and lounge are hopping but with some interesting people and ACTUAL NEW YORKERS. Coming from NY myself, and having lived in the city about a decade ago, I love places that attract the real-deal people. And it's a sophisticated lot. You're not going to see Bridge & Tunnel people here. I think they'd be kicked out -- okay, that's mean, but you know, they just would feel uncomfortable. This is a high-caliber place. Not snooty, necessarily, but certainly a scene where taste, culture and a little bit of wealth and worldliness prevail. 
Like SoHo itself and that's another thing. Of course you have to evaluate what part of the city you'd like to be in, but for my money, SoHo is the most exciting, beautiful area and for some reason, right now, it's better than it's been in years. I can't quite pin it down. The whole city seems to be alive in a way it hasn't for years and SoHo is capturing that. That's pretty thrilling and certainly makes my heart swoon for all New Yorkers who've been through such difficult and tragic times.
But back to the hotel: Free WiFi in the Lounge for guests as well as a well-functioning Business Center on the 3rd floor are very helpful. So are the people. The doors were held open for me, if there were ANY problems Axl and the people at the front dest took care of it right away. And they were kind, remembered who you were and took care of you. In fact, the staff was much better than the models at The Rivington (my review, Nov. 14, 2005, is a little off. After this experience, I'd give it a 3 not a 4 rating). But I don't want to mislead. The employees at The Grand are also easy on the eyes, but unlike the Rivington's Abercrombie & Fitch runway concierges, in addition The SoHo's people are super-duper competent, friendly and efficient. Sorry, Rivington, but the truth is the truth. Perhaps you've improved in all this time, and if so, my apologies.
Oh, and before I forget, if you request it, they put luscious goosedown pillows in your room and a goldfish for a pet -- which I loved. Not as much as the girl I met in the elevator who requested to take hers back with her to Ohio. But they said no, he'd die. She looked so sad but they let her carry him around in a plastic bag for awhile. See, this hotel, in every respect, is the best place on the planet.
Which is why, fellow travellers, I thought I shouldn't tell you. Because I want to be Eloise and stay there myself all the time and always have my special room (the actual number I choose NOT to share with you) and just have the place to myself like a favorite restaurant before the word gets out. But you know, when something is so good, and people have treated you so well, I feel they must be rewarded as hugely as possible. And besides, I only get to go to NYC once or twice a year. With that said, and my desire is to always be able to stay there -- no ifs ands or buts, let's just keep this little note between us, okay?

title: “Great atmosphere with excellent customer service!”
text: We will definitely stay at this hotel again. Is great for adults and kids alike. Fast service when needed, speedy check in and check out - we were able to check in. 3 hours early.

title: “Great family hotel, excellent location”
text:
We wanted a central location but a family friendly one and were very happy with the Magic Castle Hotel.
Just one block from Hollywood Boluevard, the hotel is well located but wasn't noisy at all in the evenings.
We were travelling with our 16month old daughter and booked a 1 bedroom suite. The room was a little old, and had a few areas that could do with some attention, but all in all it met our needs.
Reception staff were excellent and really helped us with maps and recommendations on where to eat/visit.
The hotel had a complimentary DVD and in-room snacks menu when we were there which we used a few times. There is no room service though, but we ordered take-away's on the nights that we didn't want to cook for ourselves.
The rate was what you'd expect for such a central location, but I was generally very happy with the stay and would recommend it to others.

title: “Nice hotel in a questionable area”
text:
I spent 2 nights here this past week while traveling for work. My room was a little small but perfectly fine for a solo traveler. I had a comfy bed, large flat screen television, and everything was clean. My room was on the 3rd floor and overlooked the pool. The little interaction I had with the staff proved they were quite friendly. The complimentary breakfast is decent, offers a variety of options and I liked that each morning there were some different items to choose from. 
The area however is surrounded by multitudes of homeless people pushing their shopping carts and while I was waiting in the front parking lot for my sister to pick me up I saw a couple drive their car into the driveway, watched the woman get out and place something on the planter's brick wall then drive away. I was curious and went to inspect what she had left there only to find out it was a marijuana pipe, lighter, and a contact case...very strange. It is very close to Old Town but I certainly would not feel safe walking over there. I am happy that I did not have a room facing the freeway because I am guessing it would have been quite noisy. It is a shame that the area around is so lousy because if I felt safer I think I would make this my choice hotel for San Diego since I come here on a monthly basis for work. I would recommend this as a stopping through hotel and definitely not classify it as a family friendly place due to the area.

title: “Fabulous loved every minute in hotel”
text: We checked in all five girls for a 4 day shopping trip prior to Xmas. Totally loved the size of the rooms and the beds were very soft and comfortable,one room had one double bed and the other had two. Flatscreen t.v in each room and stereo. Bathroom was lovely but probably needed 2 being it was 5 females sharing but it was not a problem.The hallways are a little in need of an upgrade but you don't sleep in the hallway!! Staff very friendly and free safe deposit box at reception.Nearest tube/subway was 2 blocks away and a great place for breakfast just accross the street. We will be back again next December, not many hotels allow 5/6 persons to a room which makes for a cheaper stay, more money to spend on shopping.

title: “Our second stay celebrating another anniversary and it was spectacular”
text: Le Parker Meridien is an exceptionally wonderful hotel in NYC. The staff from top to bottom is wonderful, friendly and helpful. The hotel is located in the center of everything you want to do in Manhattan. It is a great home base to launch your activities from. Especially wonderful was the room we had and the assistance we got from Guest Relations Manager, Ms. Lisa Tharp. She made our second trip to this hotel even more special than our first. This is a great hotel for anyone who is visiting Manhattan and wants a clean, friendly and well located place to stay. The room was so quiet we slept way later than we planned. The room was also immaculate and the bed was extremely comfortable.

title: “Nice place”
text: Great value for the money - you get a whole suite! Kitchen, foyer, small sitting area, dressing area and bathroom. Comfortable bed, very clean and spacious, easy parking. Friendly and easy check-in and check-out and helpful reception. Free coffee in the lobby is nice too. Only bad thing is our room was right next to the elevator, so we heard some noise outside our room, so next time we are there, we will ask for a room further from the elevator.

title: “Convenient, friendly staff”
text: Right across the street from McPherson Sq Metro station, near attractions. I was there for business, alas. Hotel side: A+ cleanliness, friendly staff. Restaurant side: Staff A+++, food/menu, C. Good buffet in AM ($15), OK stuff for lunch/dinner. Kinda pricey. I'd stay here again in a heartbeat!

title: “Needs a lift but not too bad”
text:
There's not a lot to do downtown in Houston. 
Great pub around the corner though. Hotel features a small gym. Staff are a bit slow. 
Fantastic lobby area though offering coffee, water, fruit, tv, newspapers etc for travellers. Residences on the top 2 floors so handy to chat to locals.
Needs a bit of a facelift and appears dirty but overall the Hotel was nice.

title: “The room was very clean, the staff was very helpful and Acenar was delicious.”
text: This hotel is in a great spot on the river walk and close enough to fun hot spots on the street level. Our room was very clean but a bit dark, not enough lighting throughout the hotel. That would be the only "complaint" we had. Acenar food is great!

title: “More than we needed..paid less than advertised”
text:
Wanted to go to memphis for a saturday night but couldnt find a good price on a hotel. I had stayed here before and rooms were advertised starting at 109 + tax for four of us. We decided to just show up and get a room with no reservation. Great lady behind the desk offered us a walk-in special of 89 + tax. WE took it but was expecting very little for that rate and four twenty somethings carrying a cooler to their room! She directed us down the hall on the 1st floor. We passed through a doorway with EXECUTIVE SUITES on it. We get to our huge room with 2 queen size beds, big desk, fridge, microwave, and sink. There were also bottles of water and popcorn waiting for us. 
The room and rate were awesome here! I will look to them in the future for their rooms, rates, and service. It was a great place to begin our day and end our night.
Until we meet again Memphis....

title: “Funky & Fun Boutique Hotel!”
text:
We booked this hotel months in advance via Hotwire. We needed four rooms, and got them for $103 per night, for a pre-cruise stay. This hotel was listed as a 3 1/2 star boutique hotel, which I would say is exactly what we got. We arrived before 1pm from the East Coast, and were very happy that we had no problems checking in that early.
All eight of us loved the Hotel Max! Yes, the rooms are small, especially the bathrooms, but it's great preparation for the cruise bathrooms. This hotel has character! From the guys standing out front, to the front desk, they're young and friendly. Artwork throughout the hotel is unique and sexy. The bed was comfortable, and we got a kick out of the extra amenities in the room. (not that we used them...perhaps, if we hadn't stayed up so late in the hotel restaurant for late-night happy hour :) )
This hotel reminded me of unique boutique hotels I've stayed at in San Francisco and New York. It is NOT for anyone wanting a cookie-cutter hotel experience.
The location, by the way, is PERFECT. Less than a $10 cab-ride to Pier 66 and the boarding of our cruise. An easy walk to Pike's. It's very close to the Westin, and Il Fornaio (great Italian restaurant, if you're hungry for Italian).
We actually went back to the Hotel Max after our cruise to take a few pictures, as we had failed to do so when we were actually staying there.

title: “Perfect litte beach stop”
text:
I loved the views, the room, the experience! 
We were walkin guests and were shown two choices, one of the cabins over the ocean on the pier and one of the much larger rooms on land with full on facing of the ocean, same price.
We chose not to stay on the pier to get the full views offered by these rooms, a large private deck, living room, dining area, fully stocked kitchen, king bed in the bed room.... perfect!
The beach scene in the winter is wonderfully romantic, lacking the hordes of touring families and children one usually finds. We just adored this trip.
Outside our back windows was a little restaurant serving breakfast all day. All day it had a line to get in, so we decided to go first thing in the morning, no apparent line. When we got there the line was inside to keep the waiting warm. Alas, we aren't much for waiting and went elsewhere, but I imagine this breakfast joint is exceptional!

title: “Enjoyable stay, nice hotel”
text:
Rooms here are quite large by Boston standards (or really any large city in the Northeast/MidAtlantic corridor) and the floor plan sets the bed back quite a ways from the door, meaning very little hallway noise bleeds into the room. A major plus. Bed comfortable but not outstanding. Room decor is very muted, almost bland, kind of like they're going for the Colonial feel but took it a little too far. Room was nice, fresh and clean.
The breakfast buffet is underwhelming especially at that price, but surprisingly the hotel bar is one of the best bargains in Boston, with $6 pints of microbrews. The bar closes a bit early (11pm if I remember correctly, on a weekend) but you can carry your drinks to the "library" across the hall and relax there.
The room price is high but in line with other Boston hotels of the same caliber. It's a very expensive city. I would stay here again though!

title: “wow amazing !!!”
text:
it was nearly a year ago since we went but it was amazing then and can't see it changing that much... we arrived on black friday (night) the hotel was decorated for christmas, it was beautiful with a huge tree just by the restaurant. the view out of the window by reception ,of times square at night was breath taking. our room has two double beds so for just me and my husband it was great !!! very nicely decorated and clean. beds were also very comfy. the tv was big and useful as the news came on and told us about the black friday sales (which we didn't know about) !!!!
as we were still on english time we got up at 5 am and went out for a wonder, it was FREEZING !!!!! very windy. but star bucks is next door nearly and i remember it opening early so we grabbed some tea, coffee and cakes and had them for breakfast. SAME PRICE AS HOME REALLY !!! just under £10)
we went to toys R us which was just over the road and the sale was very good. take some extra bags with you !!!! and as we were in there so early we pretty much had the shop to ourself where as when returned a few hours later it was crazy !!!
if your sightseeing take the subway, we were a bit wary at first but for a few dollars you can go everywhere !!! just ask the locals people were always willing to help us, we got the hang of the map after a while anyway. we went to ground zero whilst there go into ( century 21) designer outlet (really cheap) just by st pauls. also the statue of liberty is within walking distance from ground zero, the boat trip to liberty island is a must !!! and really good value for money :) 
if your planning on catching a broadway show, right by our hotel is the famous red steps here is where you can pick up last minute tickets to shows at a discounted price.
all in all i thought the hotel was fab, i think mainly for it's location but i really enjoyed my stay reguardless. one warning, the hotel restaurant is very expensive !!! i can't remember how much breakfast was but when he told us the price we both thought OMG how much ??? lol 
we ate at mcdonalds a few times, starbucks and spalshed out on a few meals in times square. new york can be expensive but it depends on where you go like london. me and my hubby wanted some pancakes and fresh orange so popped to a lovely local cafe just off times square, i think its where all the locals go. but the pancakes were huge !!! one plate would have done us two but for breakfast there i think it cost £17 dollars, big difference from the hotel. so my best advice is get out there !!! and shop around :)

title: “Great location, great service”
text:
This is a nice hotel in an excellent location, near all the great attractions of Fisherman's Wharp, Pier 39, Ghiradelli, etc. Although I was on a business trip, I brought my family along (including 10 year old boy & 5 year old girl) and we stayed five nights.
Overall, the service was outstanding. The valet parking was always prompt, and the valet attendent knew me by name by the second day. The front desk was very helpful with driving directions and getting information on road conditions for the remainder of our travel through California.
The room was average size, sufficient for the four of us. The bathroom had an odd sink that was very shallow, causing water to spill over occasionally on my 5-year-old.
My only real complaint is that there was no refridgerator in the room. This would have been nice for storing left-overs from the wonderful restaurants in the area.
I would highly recommend this hotel for business travelers; at the same time, it is above average for tourists.

title: “Dated- but Good Place”
text: We usually go here or to the sister hotel next door anytime we go to 8 Seconds Saloon for a concert. They both offer free shuttle to and from the bar. That's better than $12 each way for a taxi! Yes, the place is dated, but that's just fine if you're staying the night after a long night of music. The bathroom was clean and the shower was great. I slept just fine. The bed was comfortable. The walls are very thin, so I did hear everytime somebody went to the restroom or opened or closed their doors. It was a little pricey for the hotel, but not for us, since we saved about $25 for a taxi!

title: “No troubles, at all”
text:
I stayed here with 8 girls for 3 nights. This hotel could not have been better suited for our needs. We had 2 rooms with 2 double beds so 4 girls to a room. I knew that NYC hotel rooms were small so I was a little nervous but it ended up being fine and comfy. The rooms are very updated and modern which we loved. One of our circuits blew in the room but they were quick to fix it and it didnt go out again. 
The hotel is very close to Times Square, 1 block and also close to 46th street which has some amazing restaurants. We ate on that street every night and had amazing food and service every single time. it is also close to all the theatres and the subway downtown is just 4 blocks down. 
I would definitely stay here again in NYC!

title: “Cheap parking, Unique Japanese style Hotel”
text: The rooms are nice and clean, uniquely decorated in modern Japanese style. Staff is very friendly and helpful. If you like Japanese cuisince, this place puts you right in the core of Japan town, although it is farther away from the Financial district, Downtown, Fisherman's Wharf area, which are a short bus ride or taxi ride away. I like the unique decorations and sometimes it offers special promotions. In a city where parking can cost an arm and leg, the parking garage next to the hotel is a bargain at the price of $15 per day. I would recommend this for both business and leisure travel, even though I only stayed here a few times for business. The only drawback - they don't have a frequent flyer program.

title: “Great hotel!”
text: Stayed here over a 2-night weekend in September with extended family. We all agreed the hotel was very nice. The Priceline deal made it all that much better. The rooms were clean, a little small, but not out of the ordinary for a bigger city hotel. I am still surprised to see older tv's in upper tier hotels such as this. The standard tv was fine, but hotels of this caliber should have HDTVs in all rooms by now. It would have been nice to watch some of the football on HD. Everything else was great. The staff here are likely some of the best I've ever encountered. There was a genuine quality about the staff that is hard to find. The concierge helped with directions, getting as detailed on how to get somewhere from where I was exactly standing. There is a Starbucks right by the elevator, but strangely my entire group all thought our drinks tasted "weak" and "different." They made mine twice but it still tasted off. Our group visited other Starbucks locations that weekend and the drinks tasted normal, so we aren't sure what was going on at the hotel Starbucks. The pool was closed when we went to look at it, but I heard it is nice. The king bed was fine, not fantastic but comfortable. I know bed bugs are exploding all over the country so it's hard to "blame" a hotel for it, but I did find one or two bumps on my legs after staying there. I'm not saying it was because of bed bugs at this hotel, but I'm also not sure where they came from. Our room was located on the inner side of the hotel (not facing a street-side) so we didn't have any problems with road or city noise at all. In fact, I don't recall hearing any neighboring rooms either. The windows opened slightly which was nice during the cool day. Bathroom amenities were great and the shower was warm. There was no exhaust fan in the bathroom. You can't beat the location. If you can do without a car I would recommend it. Parking across the street is $38 per day. The trains make everything we did incredibly accessible. My sister came from Midway Airport on a straight-shot, 35-minute train ride. We also went to Wrigley Field on a straight-shot train ride as well. Miller's Pub is a great place to catch a bite and beer right next to the hotel. I would definitely stay there again if I had the means to do so.

title: “Really Good!”
text:
My husband and I stayed in this hotel at the end of August. It is truly beautiful. We paid a little extra for an executive room. The room itself was a little disappointing with a small bed but we did enjoy an included breakfast and other snacks during the day which were very welcome. The staff were very helpful especially the concierge and the door staff.
Chicago itself is lovely and well worth a visit and the hotel is within easy walking distance of Navy Pier, Millennium Park etc. Would love to visit hotel again if in Chicago.

title: “Terrific staff”
text: My husband and I took our 9 year old grandson to DC for 3 days. The hotel turned out to be just perfect for us. Great location, a reasonable room for the price, the pool was wonderful after a long day of sightseeing, but it was the attitude of the staff that really impressed us. The restaurant was also a big hit with my family. They refused to eat anywhere else! Yes, the parking is expensive and the bathroom small, but all in all, we were very satisfied and will definitely go back on our next visit. One suggestion: book directly with the hotel, don't use hotel.com. You'll get a better rate.

title: “Location, decor, location”
text: We stayed at the Peabody in Memphis on an anniversary trip several weeks ago and we were quite pleased. The hotel is very close to the things we wanted to see...Beale Street, Civil Rights Museum, Gibson Guitar factory etc. We had stayed at the Peabody in Little Rock a couple of years ago, but this Peabody is much more of an experience. The decor is over the top, but harkens back to old style, grandiose hotels of the past. Our room was beautiful especially after we requested a different room from the one by the elevators. It was small but very comfortable. The biggest complaint about the room would be that noise traveled through the adjoining door to the room next to us as though we were all sharing the same room. The first night the room next door must have been empty, but the second night people arrived and we could hear every word of most of their conversations. Our room definitely would not be the room one would want if you were on your honeymoon!

title: “Amazing place”
text: I selected the Library Hotel based on the reviews I'd read on TripAdvisor and was not disappointed. The place really is amazing. I was travelling alone on business and this hotel was a high point in the trip. The friendly open spaces, the wine and cheese reception each evening and the staff for whom nothing was too much trouble were a welcome respite from the usual corporate hotels. The bedroom is small (in typical Manhattan style) but atypically there are so many places within the hotel where you can work or relax, and exchange a friendly word with other guests, that time spent in your room can be minimised. What more can I say? - I'll definitely return when next in the US and highly recommend the Library Hotel to any traveller. The hotel made my business travel a pleasure.

title: “The Best Value! A great hotel.”
text: This is by far one of the best values I have found in hotels! My husband and I stayed here for our 2nd anniversary, and found it a great romantic destination. The location was perfect - in the middle of Little Italy, downtown San Diego, just minutes from the zoo and seaworld and a trolley ride away from Petco Park and the Gaslight district. The rooms were ultra clean, which is always my number one priority. I read reviews on this site before our stay and was warned about the size being small, but we stayed on the southwest corner and our room was very well-sized and nicely arranged. The lack of air conditioning was no issue even in May; we enjoyed opening the windows to let in the ocean breeze. I will make a small comment about the train noise and the church bells that start about 7 am and go on about every half hour, but not a problem at all. The staff was very friendly, the lobby was like a living room, and the cute Italian coffee shop downstairs was our little kitchen. The garage was a little small, but it appears they are careful not to oversell it which makes it easier to get in and out. If you aren't into the big resorts and the costs/crowds that come with them, I HIGHLY recommend this hotel!!!!

title: “A second visit...”
text: I visited NYC , staying in the Affinia Shelburne for a second time. It is a nice hotel, with comfy rooms and beds, a very good localization, and a kind staff. There are many rooms with a small kitchen (suites), and they have a good size, for a NYC hotel. However, they urgently need to improve the cleaning, because my room was covered with dust. In the walls, table lightning, behind the furniture and the bed, behind the mirror, in the bathroom....Considering that Im allergic, this can be a great problem. They also need to remold the front desk area: it is dark and not very pleasant.

title: “Marwan T”
text: Lucky to have stayed there during our visit to NYC. Sad for the people that were affected by the hurricane. No electricity just 2 blocks away. Met by Ms. Cornelia Samara, the GM, upon arrival. Made us feel at home. A few goodies for the kids left in the room. A nice touch. We stayed in the suite. Good sized rooms for NYC. Lovely terrace with excellent views. Breakfast at the shop was great. The lemon soufflé pancake is a must. The eggs benedict too. Homey feel. Thank you to the general manager and team. Would highly recommend this hotel.

title: “Thought it was great!”
text: The service was great and the beds were soooo comfy ... I love feather beds/pillows!!!!! We got room service one night and it was also very good :) The maids even made a point to come see us upon checkout to say thank you for coming. We were very impressed. Only thing lacking is a pool/hot tub. It was chilly and we would have loved to go relax in the pool, but its an older building and we knew it didn't have one going into it. Its literally next door to the Hancock Tower, and blocks away from the beach. We walked to Gino's East, and Jake Melnick's Corner Tap *YUM* Valet guys were nice, but we've had better. There was a younger guy who was our favorite - can't remember his name but he was great!!!

title: “Feels like home!”
text:
We love this hotel! It's a boutique hotel with a terrific location. The staff makes you feel like family and they take great care of you. 
The room itself is spacious for NYC. It had a separate dressing area and is quiet and comfortable. The bathroom is updated and has nice amenities. 
The best part of the hotel is their club room that feels like a big living room. They serve a good continental breakfast and have drinks and snacks starting at 5pm. You can also stop in after coming in for the evening for late coffee and cookies. It gives you a chance to meet other guests at the hotels and make new friends. 
We love this place and would definitely return again and again.

title: “Disgusting Hotel”
text: You would think by the name of this hotel that it was in a good location near Sea World in San Diego. It was across the street from DeJaVu! The facility was dirty, uninviting. The room was questionable as to its cleanliness - we were afraid to touch anything. The breakfast was pre-made powdered eggs, pre-made pancakes, luke warm and not very good. There was a loud party going on in the next room into the wee hours of the morning so we got little sleep. It took two calls to the office to get it quieted down. We saw many Days Inn facilities in the San Diego area that looked newer and nicer. This one was not acceptable. We paid for 3 nights and left after the first night. Do not stay at this hotel!

title: “Great value, spotless rooms”
text:
This hotel is conveniently located in midtown, close to public transportation. My room, while small, had everything I needed and was immaculately clean. It was also quiet, a big plus. The staff was friendly, and helpful. 
A free bag check is available for visitors who arrive before check-in or who want to continue to tour the city after check-out. If you will be catching an airplane, check with the concierge for reservations on the shuttle bus. It's far less expensive than is a taxi.
Wifi was excellent. I look forward to staying here when I visit New York again.

title: “A slice of Vegas in Downtown San Diego!!!”
text:
An upscale hotel in downtown district that gives you the feel that you are in Vegas
and ready to live up the night life. Very friendly staff ready to help you in any part of the hotel. I was impressed by the choice of music you get to choose as you walk into the your room. At night this hotel transforms to the place to be for all party people. Great restaurants, bars, and night clubs. I would recommend visiting Float a roof top bar with a great view of downtown and fresh air. A great place to stay and party like a rock star!!!

title: “Comfortable stay with one major downside: noisy rooms.”
text:
Visiting LA for business and as my company has a contract with this hotel it was the obvious choice. Located in downtown LA the location is convenient for business. Checkin took a bit long due to the preferred guest line getting preference... he hotel itself is large and styleful with many facilities. Rooms are mostly OK, although a bight odd-shaped due to the cilindrical shape of the building. Bed's are great, one of the best I ever had. Bathroom was complete and good as well, apart from the shower head which was too low for me (1.85m). But that is a problem in many US hotels.
Biggest inconvenience was that the room was very noisy. Not sure if it was because of the thin walls or becuase of the face there was a (locked) door between the rooms, but you could hear everything from the neighboors room. Talking, television, even as it dod not seem to be exceptionally loud. First night that was not too much of an issue, but during the last night my neigbhours where clearly fighting a jetlag watching TV in the middle of the night.
Bit of a pitty as the rest of the hotel was very good.

title: “Beautiful rooms, great service”
text: If you have business or a meeting in NE Philadelphia, this is the ONLY place to stay. Rooms are refurbisshed and very comfortable. Service is outstanding!!!

title: “What a Nice Surprise!”
text:
I hate to admit it, but I had a lot of preconceived notions about the city of El Paso and was not expecting much in the way of hotels. Thankfully, I stumbled upon this gem of a hotel situated almost ON the University of Texas at El Paso campus (I was visiting there for work). The service at the Hilton Garden Inn was excellent, and the rooms were unbelievably nice. The beds/bedding were of good quality and the rest of the facilities were convenient. The aesthetics of the room (very modern) really made me overlook any of the cons I had for the hotel.
The area surrounding the hotel consisted of some fast food restaurants, convenience stores, and an Albertsons grocery store, which made it convenient when I was hungry. Parking was excellent, too!
I would DEFINITELY recommend this to anyone staying in El Paso.

title: “A for Accessibility!”
text:
I recently stayed at the Marriott Wardman for a conference (as it is mostly a convention hotel) and must ay I was not disappointed. However, for such an extravagent establishment, I found it odd that it was missing some of the simple basics. 
I believe my room may have been upgraded, or was just an accessible room. Originally I was supposed to only stay for 2 days then move in with a colleague for a meeting that occurred after the original conference, due to availability, but after talking to the kind people at check in, they assured me everything had been taken care of and I was escorted to a large room in the Park Tower.
I must give this hotel kudos, for it's ACTUAL accessibility. I have been in "accessible rooms" before that simply had a bar in the bathroom, but the size was hardly substantial enough for a wheelchair! This room had a large tiled foyer with a kitchenette, that was perfect to park my motorized scooter I use when I travel! the bathroom was also very accessible. It was very large, and had a hand held shower head that could be lowered.
However- although the bathroom was huge, the one thing it lacked was HOOKS. there was absolutely NOWHERE to even hang a towel. I happen to have hanging toiletry bags, and I couldn't put them anywhere. I ended up setting them on a counter, and things kept falling out and on to the floor. Very annoying.
Also, the fact that internet was $13 a day and was NOT wireless was very frustrating. Clearly when you travel on business you are going to need to access your email and the internet, and it was irritating to say the least to be tied to the desk to access the internet. Very circa 1999.
Either have it wired, and have it FREE, or have wifi and charge a little less...but still there is no need to pay such a rate daily to sit at a desk.
Room service was also out of this world expensive. We ended up paying $80 for breakfast for 2, and all we got was eggs benedict and coffee. A carafe of coffee for 2 was $17, and of course the delivery fee is ridiculous. The quality of the food was decent, but nowhere near $80 worth of amazing! The 2nd day we ordered breakfast, we noted there were 2 diners, and we did not receive a table. One of us had to dine at the desk, while the other just sat in a chair with their tray on the ottoman....not an ideal situation, especially for the cost.
On the up side though- the beds were very comfortable and our room was always cleaned sufficiently and in good time
Although the on site coffee was Starbucks brand, there was not a Starbucks location in the hotel, which I found to be disappointing, especially for the size of the establishment.
The size was definitely exquisite, and although it took me about our entire stay to start learning where things were (the entire hotel is like a maze, with 2 different towers) the hotel staff is very accommodating and helpful. there are staff members at every high traffic area to answer questions of where to go, so I didn't waste too much time getting lost after the first day.
The conference facilities were nice, but after the third luncheon I began to get sick of the typical salad, chicken and rolls. Luckily, both restaurants were wonderful with great food and service! For a nice change on the last couple of days. For our last dinner, the concierge also referred us to a delicious japanese restaurant that was within walking distance. The hotel was very close to lots of great places to eat and shop!
Overall not a bad place, in a great location, but I am not sure that I would stay here if I had my choice of hotels in the DC area...it misses the mark on simple things, and the $13 a day internet is definitely not conducive to teleworking.

title: “Great service, comfortable hotel, great location”
text:
We stayed at the Topaz from Sept 6 - 10th. This was our first visit to DC so didn't spend much time in the hotel except to sleep. The room was very spacious and clean, the bed very comfortable. Front desk was friendly and professional. On our last morning I verified what time check out was and they gave me the info, asked me if I needed to stay later and I told them we wld need to leave at noon so we could get the metro to the bus we were planning on taking to BWI airport. They suggested a different method of transportation and when we returned after an hour or so of exploring the neighborhood they had the train schedule printed out and hilighted with which time we should take to get there on time in addition to the price information. What a great help! 
The neighborhood (Dupont Circle) was wonderful. Funny thing - I kept telling my husband I wanted to see St Matthews church but I just didn't know where it was, little did I know we had been looking at it through our window our entire stay! 
The staff was wonderful, the hotel clean, the area safe, the room very spacious. We are planning on staying there again.

title: “Wonderful base for a visit to DC”
text:
We stayed at this hotel a few weeks ago. It was clean, comfortable and very well located to serve as a base for a visit to DC. It's a short walk from Dupont Circle where there is a wide array of shopping and restaurants and a Metro stop. It's also only about a 20 minute walk to the zoo. Best of all, it's surrounded by interesting neighborhoods where you can easily get off the beaten path. Adams Morgan is a vibrant neighborhood with lots of great restaurants that buzzes with energy at night and it's a five minute walk from the hotel.
During our week-long stay we found the staff to be friendly and helpful, the rooms to be very clean and meticulously maintained, and the hotel to be a comfortable and relaxing place to end long, hot days of sightseeing.
The only slight negative I would point out is that the walls are thin and you can hear people in adjacent rooms if they're loud at all. That's typical in hotels and the reason I always bring earplugs when I travel.
I would definitely stay at this hotel again.

title: “Good Location”
text:
The hotel is in a good location and the room was very cool with a jacuzzi bath. The hotel service was good but my only real complaint would be the time it took for the lift to arrive.
I would say this hotel is fairly good value for money and the central location should save you cash on taxis.

title: “Perfect Place to stay in D.C.”
text: The Madison was very affordable. We loved this hotel! The decor was very modern and posh. The customer service was extraordinary from the bell hops to the front desk staff. The location of this hotel is also wonderful. It is only a couple blocks from all major D.C. site. We definitely will be staying here again if we are in D.C.

title: “Great Resort”
text:
My wife and I stayed there for the third time. As usual the service was great. Very friendly people. The place is beautiful and clean. The afternoon tea was great. Only two issues. On our second day the room was not made up at 4:30pm. I had to go to the front counter and tell the folks that my room was not serviced at all (beds not made, towels on floor, nothing) even though the maid left a card saying they serviced the room. 
I came back two hours later and the room still had not been made at 6:30pm. Then the front desk person purchased a drink "on the house" and it showed up on my bill.
Look, we really like this place and will go back again. We really like the people and they really try hard. It is just that I did not expect this to happen at a 4 star establishment. Again, we will continue to go to this wonderful resort but we expected a bit more attention to detail with the housekeeping.

title: “The Only Choice For Pier 39 Or Fisherman's Warf”
text:
Second visit to Fisherman's Warf and this is now the ONLY hotel we will stay at. 
PROS: 
Easy access to spacious 3rd floor room. Situated CLOSE to EVERYTHING. Great value for price. VERY SECURE environment. Friendly and informed staff. DO NOT take a TAXI from or to SFO Airport. Instead book a Town Car & Driver for $50, save $10 after tip and ride in comfort. Available through Bellman. 
CONS:
Restaurant like every other hotel eating establishment is WAY over priced. No need to eat in Hotel - we didn't -everything from the best seafood within a five minute walk to having an iHop across the street. There were NO OTHER cons.
We have stayed at a lot of Hotels and this one is a safe bet.

title: “Very Satisfied Third Time Returning Guests”
text:
We have yet to be disapointed with our stays at this hotel. It offers quality guest services and amenities; reasonable room and parking rates; staff is knowledgeable and provides excellant services to its valued guests.
The parking rate is reasonable compared to other hotels in the area. It has not increased from the $26.00 daily rate which was offered last year with its in and out priveleges. Although parking is very limited; it can be quite a challege to park your vehicle depending on how full the parking lot is at the time.
