The hotels rooms were recently remodeled with newer furniture and choice bedding. The beds presently have feather topper bed covers. We have stayed on different floors during our three stays. Each time we have found our room to be clean and met the needs of our family. Despite the fact that the bathroom is small, it still met our needs.
Walls appear to be thin as voices can be heard from your neighbours as we have experienced during our stay(s). During this past stay, we encountered our neighbour's conversations but this could be in part due to our room being an adjoining room.
We have chosen this hotel in part to the fact that it allows five to a room which can be hardship when most hotels only allow 4 guests to a room even though some of those guests are children. We also like the idea, that children under the age of 12 years stay free when sharing a room with their parents as this is the norm for the Choice hotel chain.
Another concern is that there are 5 family members and that through out our stay, only 4 sets of towels were left in our room for our family to use.
We found it odd that despite the hotel be quieter than on our last visit, our room was not cleaned in a timely manner. We left our room at approx. 9:00 a.m. only to find that when we returned at 3:00 p.m., the room was only being cleaned at that time. We found this to be a bit of an inconvience as we had plans in a couple of our hours and needed to change our clothes to prepare for our outing within two hours.
The front desk staff is knowledgeable about the San Francisco area and gladly assists its guests with their requests. We found this to be true on each of our visits especially when it came to using the transit system. 
This hotel offers a complimentary breakfast daily with a good variety of hot and cold items. The staff that maintains the breakfast should be rewarded for their excellant service. They continually ensure that items are always on hand, dishes are available and that the tables are clean for the guests of the hotel.
The location of this hotel is close to many areas of interest: Fisherman's Wharf, Ghirardelli Square and Lombard Street and are all within a 15 minute walk from the hotel. If wanting to visit other areas such as Chinatown and AT&T park, transit stops are close by within a few blocks of the hotel.
We made reservations for a room located on the middle floors. After making our reservation, we had an inquiry and contacted the hotel. It was during the course of our conversation, that the front desk reservation staff discovered that we were returning guests to the hotel and due to the hotel having vacancies on the upper floors, much to our surprise the staff decided on its own to upgrade our room to a full view room located on the 10th floor in appreciation that we were returning guests at no extra cost to us.
The Comfort Inn By The Bay has yet to disappoint us during our stay(s) and we highly recommend this hotel to anyone that will be visiting San Francisco.

title: “Thoroughly enjoyed our stay while...”
text: Thoroughly enjoyed our stay while visiting our airman at Lackland AFB. Relaxing, rejuvinating, and loved the lazy river! Oh yeah, our airman had a good break also.

title: “Great place to stay for a week”
text: I stayed at the Double Tree from Sunday to Friday for a business trip. The room was wonderful - great view of the Capitol. Room service was incredible. Breakfast all day was a real treat! The front desk and valet staff were very friendly and always made sure they welcomed me back at the end of the day. The mini kitchen was a plus. We had one issue with service in the pool area, but they made amends immediately and were so apologetic that I would still rate them as excellent. My room was at the end of the hall and was so quiet! I would definitely stay there again.

title: “Elegant and comfortable”
text: When one travels on business and is staying at a large chain hotel, you know you'll get a good basic experience. This Hampton Inn in Happy Valley is WAY above expecations in all ways. My room was large, lovely, fancy bath (I think it's marble), very comfy bed. Just about anything you could want for breakfast, from the usual cereals and make your own waffles to western style egg burritos, etc. included in the room rate. A clean pool with sun and shade. I was sorry I only got to stay there one night.

title: “Really happy with our choice-thanks Trip Advisor”
text: We chose this hotel on the basis of Trip Advisor reviews and were not disappointed. In fact we highly recommend this hotel. We flew to JFK for a 5 night stay with Aer Lingus clearing US Immigration in Dublin! The Hilton Garden Inn is in an excellent location, close to Times Square. The staff were very friendly. The staff take great pride in their hotel. We asked for a quiet room which we got on the third floor. The beds were extremely comfortable. The restaurant affiliated to the hotel (Pagellis) was fantastic! It has a vibrant atmosphere and the breakfast portions were enormous! This hotel offers a really comfortable, straight-forward, value for money stay in the most exciting city in the world!

title: “BEWARE”
text: Rooms are nice, but the floors are thin, can hear stomping from above. Maids have no regard for personal belongings and will clearn the room as if you aren't returning, even if your checkout date is 3-4 days later.

title: “Great time in spite of condition of hotel”
text:
Our 4 days in Boston were fun and the Parker House Hotel was a joy to see in the lobby and restaurants and bars. All the staff were very friendly and helpful. Room service was always prompt. I am always happy to stay somewhere with history or a hotel with character rather than just a chain hotel that could be in any city or any town.
That said, however, the condition of the carpet in the hallway on the third floor and in our 1-bedroom suite was deplorable. The only way to describe the condition directly outside our room (306) is NASTY and in the room was not much better. It is inexcusable that the Parker House would let things get to this point. The furniture was also frayed (which I could live with) and stained and filthy (which I could not). We hated to sit on the sofa but had to sit someplace. I thought of asking to be moved but after walking the hallways on 2 other floors I decided it could not be much better in other rooms. After reading the other reviews on this site I have decided that decision was a mistake. Apparently not many others have had that problem and I'm happy for their luck. We must have been assigned the worst area of the hotel! I was in the room one day when the maid cleaned and she did an excellent job so none of my complaints are with her. When I did bring it up to the young lady at the front desk, she was very nice and told me the hotel is to be renovated soon. (When I don't know -- perhaps sometime between now and never?) At any rate she was very apologetic. Unfortunately, no apology could make up for that carpet. I have not seen anything that horrible in a hotel room in many, many years. Perhaps a token pass with a steam cleaner??
I was amused to hear the "haunted tour" near the hotel one night talking about the 3rd floor of the Parker House being the haunted floor. No wonder I never saw anything -- no self-respecting ghost would hang out on that floor very long! Mr. Parker must be twirling in his grave.

title: “Marvellous hotel in a marvellous location”
text: Have just returned from the Omni San Francisco hotel, San Francisco. Selected it because of the previous excellent reviews on TripAdvisor, and this one will simply add to that list. This is a marvellous hotel in a marvellous location. Staff uniformly polite, helpful and knowledgeable (particularly the concierge staff). Rooms spacious, clean and very comfortable. Restaurants excellent, with plenty of outside alternatives nearby. Great location, with east access to cable cars, Fisherman's Wharf, China Town and North Beach (Little Italy). Only minor negative comment is the lack of a business centre (only a tiny room with 2 PCs that charge at $5 per 15 minutes) - but hardly a major issue. Highly recommended!

title: “Rip off pet friendly”
text: Checked into this hotel only to find out I would have to pay a $100 pet deposit. I assumed that since it was a deposit I would get it back if there was no damage left to the room.the next morning received the bill with a $100 "miscellaneous fee". I spoke to the manager the next day to request my deposit to be refunded. He said it was not refundable. I argued it is not a deposit if it is not refundable. It is a fee and should have been disclosed on the website,which it was not. Do not stay here unless you want to get ripped off.parking was $40 per night and pet deposit (fee) is not refundable.the manager was a total waste of time and very unhelpful. Left this hotel feeling ripped off. Spend your money somewhere else. I will never go back to this hotel.

title: “Nice hotel, good service, dirty area”
text: I am partial to Marriott properties as a result of positive experiences so we chose this one due to the rate being $189/night on Labor Day weekend. The property itself is very nice but tight... the lobby is tight, the breakfast area is tight, elevators tight., the hallways tight.... we only had 2 small bags with us... I couldn't imagine getting on the elevator with larger pieces of luggage... having said this, while the king size room was small and.... you got it... tight, it was clean and the bed was comfortable. The breakfast is nothing special.. some instant hot cereal, cold cerea, apples and bananas each day, breakfast sandwiches for microwaving, standard breads with toaster... we always got a seat... sometimes had to wait but no big deal.... it would be nice if there were windows in the breakfast area... it appears that they might be working on this...I believe that there were 3 computers in the lobby area with free internet access and printing capabilities... It was nice having Pantene shampoo, conditioner and lotion. There is a nice hairdryer provided so don't bring one unless you are particular. Our view was of an office building but we didn't spend too much time in the room. If you plan to eat food in the room, this isn't the room for you... all we had was a king size bed and a chair with a desk... there was no other place to sit or an additional small table. There was enough room for our clothes for 4 days. The area is not the best.. while you are a few blocks from Times Square and the subway, you must walk by stores advertising peep show booths (even for buddies!!) and erotic merchandise/dvds etc.... there were always a few guys loitering about and police presence..the Port Authority is across the street..... if you walk 2 blocks to 7th street, the are changes dramatically. I would stay here again if the price is right; otherwise I preferred the Residence Inn on 6th Ave. Note that there are also 2 Courtyards on 42nd - one near 6th; the other near 5th.... the taxi driver did not believe us when we said that there was a hotel here.. it's THAT new. If you're going to Yankee stadium like we did, you can walk to Bryant Park station (at 6th and 42nd) and take the D train.... remember, NYC is a walking city.... what a place!! Can't wait to return!!

title: “Should be great but...no.”
text: I so wanted to be able to say wonderful things about our stay in this supposedly top hotel in my hometown, for which we uncharacteristically paid **rack rate.** There were some pros: the location can't be beat. The standard room was huge and, save for some scuffs on the walls, clean. The bathtub was deep and the shower was great. We were provided with a NY Times each morning, including Sunday. Bathrobes clean and comfy. Air-conditioning control accurate. Some really nice staff members. But mostly, things were just "off": email exchange ahead of time assured a feather-free room (allergies) yet down pillows were on the bed when we arrived; no Do Not Disturb tag, two requests to get one; some of the "luxury" towels stiff and frayed; morning room cleanup did not include water bottles in a city with notoriously awful tap water; evening turndown the last night (only time we opted for service) provided 1 water bottle and a floor mat next to my husband's side of the bed, with slippers marked "gent" on the bag, nothing on my side (weird). No yoga mats to borrow, even in fitness center (where the front desk attendant told me to go and check, rather than picking up the phone and checking for me). I could go on, but you get the picture. When visiting family in Philly, we normally stay at a Residence Inn, where a little bit of roughness around the edges is to be expected. At an expensive Center City hotel that boasts about its many awards, it is not. The hotel was recently sold. The new ownership certainly has its work cut out for it. In the meantime, if you decide to stay there, know what you're getting into.

title: “great hotel in perfect location”
text: From the concierge (Phillip) who set up our in room massages to the waiter who served our breakfast every morning, everyone at this busy hotel was on top of their game. It was great to be located super close to Dupont Circle, but just far enough way down the street where it is much more quiet. We walked everywhere from this hotel (Washington Monument, Lincoln Memorial, Georgetown). We took advantage of a deal they offer where you can get cocktails and continental breakfast included everyday for just a dollar more than your rate, it was a real bargain. The rooms were spacious and modern, but not stark, more cozy. The hotel also has nice Aveda products in the bathroom. Definitely a great find in DC,

title: “Not in the best shape”
text:
We had a nice penthouse room, well layed out close to the lobby. 
 Very good breakfast bar and area to eat. The hotel has some drawbacks though. Our room showed signs of wear it needs to have the carpets and curtians replaced we also had a few bugs in the bathrooms. The trains go by about every hour and shake the whole property and the parking lot is too small if you arrive late you'll have a very hard time finding a place to park.

title: “We're coming back!”
text: Love the happy hour, Albert is the man! lobby with the Killer whale statue, the decor thru out is beautiful, will ALWAYS stay at this location when in SD....

title: “Funky and a bit quirky”
text: I stayed at The Standard hotel for 3 days and whilst I found the location quite convenient to restaurants, public transport and the tour bus stop, I didnt really liked the room configuration. The shower is fully visible from the room, which means you are totally exposed to anyone else in the room. It was weird and not suitable if you are staying with a friend and not a spouse/partner. Also the vanity in the bathroom is too low, and so is the bed, which sits on a low platform. I think the hotelier is aiming for a funky look. The swimming pool on the rooftop is pretty cool, but as the bar there opens till 2am, make sure you dont get a room too high up or you will be kept awake till late with the noise.

title: “Value and Vitality”
text: Large room for a reasonable rate. The friendly and efficient staff are a plus. The location is excellent. Recommend Penelope at 30th and Lexington for breakfast. The hotel restaurant Rare seemed very popular and is reasonably priced.

title: “DC Weekend”
text: We selected this hotel because it is close to our daughter's apartment and because parking (in the underground garage) was included in the rate. The rooms are spacious (ours had two queen beds), clean and well appointed. Refrigerator was an overlooked bonus. Shower offered high pressure and plenty of hot water. I'm a runner and there are lots of route options (including park trails) in the vicinity. Staff was pleasant and helpful. We were able to check out at 11:00 and leave our car in the garage until 4:00.

author.location: Nags Head, North Carolina, United States

title: “Best place to stay to discover daily life in San Francisco.”
text:
Pros:
The staff (Rita and Jag) are fantastic!
The rooms are clean and the price is affordable.
Nearby Mall for shopping.
Quiet area.
Great Ocean Beach a few block away.
Easy access to downtown....great cental location.
Free Parking
Cons:
Parking spaces are small.

title: “My favourite place!”
text: EVERYTIME I hit NYC... I stay here. It is old glamour. The foyer, the ambience and the staff are truly wonderful. It is a great location, within ten strides to Grand Central. The Midtown area is safe for us girls, and clean, with plenty of great bars. The BEDS? I know that you don't go to NYC to sleep... but they are heaven, heaven, heaven. Some people say that the hotel rooms are slightly scruffy, but they are clean, and well cared for. You may see the odd corner of wallpaper unattached from the wall... But who cares! It is just charming. The breakfasts are yummy, and if you don't want to eat there... Grand Central has all you could want and more! MY only annoyance is that when you get there you have to lug your bags up quite a few steps. I am sure if you were to ask the concierge, they would help. but having stayed here five times this has never happened. It has always been tourists, or friendly silver haired gentlemen that have come to my aide. The Roosevelt... WONDERFUL!

title: “Not a 4 star!!!”
text:
We stayed here in November for 2 nights in 1bebroom suite. We booked the suite because we had 2 adults and 2 kids. At the time of booking I specifically requested pull out sofa and a king size bed. We got to the hotel around 8pm. Our room was not ready. Finally, in 20 minutes they gave us our keys. The room was big but dark, smelly, with very old and dirty carpet; with one queen bed and no pull out sofa. After few calls downstairs we finally got another room, which looked a little bit more close to what they had promised us. Still many amenities that were listed in the reservation were not there. We had to ask twice for the coffeemaker, and were given an attitude before it was delivered to our room. The only radiator that worked was in the kitchen. So it was chilly in the room even at 60 degrees outside.
The bottom line is that many things they claim is not true, including that they are 4 stars. Everything from the stuff’s attitude, an hour wasted at the check in, to no restaurant on premises, no gym and old and smelly rooms just doesn’t cut it as 4 stars. The only reason I gave it 2 stars is for their location.

title: “Very comfortable”
text: This motel has a comfy bed and is in a good area. The rooms are nice and neat. I would definately stay there again if going back to San Fransico. We stayed for 2 nights and found Geary Parkway Motel to be just what we needed as far as motels go.

title: “Excellent Anniversary Stay”
text: A great place for an anniversary. Beautiful view of the lake. Pillow-top beds were outstanding. The bar is excellent with very attentive service. Staff is outstanding - from the genuine interest shown at check-in to, to the suggestion that it would be faster & cheaper to take a cab rather than valet our car at the hotel and again at the restaurant, to the offer of a bottle of water for the trip home as the valet returned our car, service was first and foremost. Expensive, but worth every dime.

title: “The Holiday Inn Riverwalk is a pretty good hotel for the money.”
text: This hotel has a friendly staff. The staff will welcome you and try to meet any need that you have. This hotel is older, but has been renovated. The room is clean and spacious. The worst parts of the room are the bed(uncomfortable) and the television(just plain awful). The television was not that big of a deal because there is so much to do in San Antonio that we did not have much time to watch it, but the 11 channels that were offered only worked half of the time. Overall for the money this hotel is a good one because it gives you a room right on the riverwalk for about 70 to 100 dollars cheaper than most places.

title: “Great Boutique Hotel”
text:
Great hotel with a wonderful staff.
I wanted a hotel with a bit of charm and personality rather than the usual chain-megalith.
Hotel Giraffe was all I hoped it would be.
Charming rooms, friendly staff, great location.
Hotel is just far enough out to make driving and parking reasonable, yet easily walkable to great sites.
We look forward to visiting again.

title: “"Why would you want to go anywhere else?"”
text:
This is what friends who had stayed at the Novotel had said to us when we were planning our first trip to NY and now after our trip we couldn't agree more. Our five nights in the Novotel in Times Sq was brilliant right from the friendly, helpful reception staff when we arrived to collecting our bags from the doorman on the last day. Our room (2417) was spotless and spacious with a great view of the Hudson river and was kept clean throughout our stay. Requests were dealt with quickly and when we lost theatre tickets the hotel security and reception staff were extremely helpful and efficient in helping us get replacements. All in all we couldn't fault the Novotel and when we can manage another trip to NY will definitely stay here again. 
We loved Langan's on 47th St. - had a couple of meals there and the food, staff and atmosphere was great.

title: “Not Up To Expectations”
text:
My husband and I recently attended a 6 day professional conference in Charlotte and found this Westin not up to par with others. Rooms were clean upon arrival, though not cleaned to standard daily-not vacuumed, counters sloppily wiped down, etc. In addition, it became a daily annoyance to call down for amenities not replenished- one day ran out of soap, another no facecloths, another no bathmat left (safety hazard), had to ask for shampoo. In a highly rated, expensive hotel, this is unexpected! Had to be on a waiting list for 2 days for a refrigerator in room. Requested feather free because of asthma/allergies,-5 days later there were still feathers under bed.
Coffee shop had limited hours for working professionals ( closed 1:30 pm). Bed was comfortable, dining very good, though pricey, staff polite. Limited concierge services compared to other hotels. Limited electrical outlets in rooms for technology. Hope services improve before the Democratic Convention. Sadly, would not recommend this hotel.

title: “Gave Marriott a BAD NAME!”
text: Our family has always stayed at Marriott hotels for their high level of service, cleanliness, and quality of the room. However, this Residence Inn did not meet the standards expected of Marriott. The bathroom had black dirt/grease on the floor, the light in the bathroom did not work, half the TV stations were so fuzzy we could not see them, the phone only worked part of the time, the room had a mysterious odor & there were broken/loose boards underneath the carpet. When I called to complain to the front desk in hopes of maybe another room, I was told I'd have to wait for the manager on Monday. Our family is very disappointed with Marriott for allowing this hotel to be associated with them. Also, the pool is about the size of a normal hottub.

title: “Great View Room”
text: I used points for my stay, requested a view room, and was given a spectacular one. They do a great job here in all ways. The rooms are large and airy and have nice lighting. The bed was extremely comfortable, and the bedding supremely soft. The location is great--one block from Bryant Park. Highly recommended!

title: “Denver Delight!”
text:
Just had a FAB wedding wkend at the Westin with more than 150 guests from all over the world staying at the Denver Westin. All guests loved the ambiance,hospitality, spacious rooms...and the proximity to wonderful shopping!. Their expert chef customized a wonderful Sri Lankan dinner for our wedding guests. If you have an event where you want to dazzle your guests, stay at the Denver Westin. Ryan and Travis, the event mgrs will ensure that every detail will be well executed! Slight snag with long checkout but other than that couldn't be more pleased with our experience.
Deb and Tom B

title: “The hotel needs updated bad and the waterpark needs cleaned bad!!!”
text: my husband and i took our 16 and 19 year old girls and a friend 17 i paid extra for my one daughter and then they tried to charge us again at breakfast for her. the room was dirty the bathroom was gross and the sheets had blood on them so we complained they changed the bed clothes and that was it.I will never take my family there again we paid 250.00 and it was a waste of money,the people they let in from the outside who are only there for the water park,these people were dirty,nasty and not very nice..There lifeguards were to busy chatting to watch any of the kids in the pool...This place is nasty! We saw cockroaches out by the sauna,i was so glad to leave we will never go back ever,even if it was free!!! My advice is drive a little further and stay somewhere nice!!!They should close this place!!!!

title: “Brilliant team, wonderful hotel”
text:
We (husband and two children of 3 and 5) stayed in MO in October and were truly spoiled. From check-in to the moment we left the whole team looked after us. The lady who checked us in recommended that we pay extra for a suite since that would give us a bit more space and we agreed with her. She was very helpful and answered all our questions when she showed us around, being patient with us whilst we were weighing up the extra space vs extra costs. The staff in the hotel were very helpful: the airline lost our pram and the hotel offered us the use their spare pram ( without a charge), due to a business event we had to arrange room service on a few occasions and Caroline of the room service team arranged for a special meal to be made for my kids and myself. The concierge even offered to get some new DVDS in for the children as their collection did not have much for their age group. Last but not least, Monica and her team in the Tai-pan were lovely and looked after us whenever we visited the lounge. The lounge offered a nice relaxing atmosphere where we could all relax throughout the day when needed. Our room was spacious with great views, large bathroom and on the same floor as the Tai-pan which was convenient. 
We used the pool a few times where drinking water, fruit and towels are available for your use.
The hotel is a short taxi drive away from the shops in Georgetown but it is right on top of the National Mall with all the museum and sights on your doorsteps. My daughters enjoyed the sights ( as much as we could fit in) and simply loved the hotel with all the outdoor space around.
I struggled to find restaurants around the Mall so do some research as most Museum offer food; just plan what you are going to have especially if you are with children.
Great place for the whole family: it is pricey but it comes with the service that you expect from a MO hotel.

title: “Painful Experience”
text:
The Blake Hotel has a high amount of potential, but for now you are better off seeking other options.
While a renovation is underway, that doesn't excuse some of the service problems that exist today.
Let's talk about parking first, $15 is a little steep, but more importantly, the fact that it is two separate transactions with a different company just demonstrates that this hotel is not interested in working with or for the customer. Why can't the parking company and hotel work together so they bill each other directly? The hike from the parking to the lobby is extensive, so if you mind walking, use the valet (same price).
The Room. Imagine going back to the 1970's and opening a hotel room door at the Ramada or Holiday Inn. The decor can not be better described. The TV was nice, but it pretty much ends there.
I got this room through Hotwire and I will not trust Hotwire again for 3* hotels in Charlotte.
The gym is simple, the restaurant and pool were closed (both months from being usable.
Do yourself a favor, look elsewhere.

title: “Great Place to Stay in NY”
text:
Whilst not in the most "fashionable" part of town, the hotel is well located to get all around the city (only a few blocks from the Empire State). It is also very close to subway stations. The immediate area around the hotel seemed safe to walk around and you already feel is likely to quickly grow into a more bustling tourist area, with new hotels already under construction. 
The lobby area is fairly uninspiring, but is comfortable. It also has the benefit of a small business centre, where you have free access to computers, internet, printers etc. 
The rooms are a little small, but very clean and comfortable (especially the bed!). Complete with air conditioning, flat screen TV, fridge, hairdryer, wi-fi etc..everything you need after a hard day in the city.
The hotel has a small bar area and breakfast/ dining area. The buffet breakfast is excellent (cereals, fruit, toast, pastries, pancakes and a variety of hot food (incl. eggs & omeletes cooked to order).
The staff were exceptional. Nothing was too much trouble. We particularly found the Reception, bar and catering/ waiting staff were brilliant (and very knowledgeable)
All in all, Highly Recommended.

title: “Terrible”
text:
I CANNOT recommend this hotel and would suggest that you stay elsewhere. 
There were numerous problems- heat not working, phone not working, multiple phone calls to get a simple item, noise. When I complained to management, the response was rather cold with an unwillingness to take responsibility or to provide adequate amends. I even took the time to speak with the general manager, but he refused to be helpful and was not interested in knowing what the issues were and was hostile. Clearly quality and customer service are not important to this hotel’s management.

title: “Great Hotel!!!”
text: I stayed at this hotel with my best friend and my 11 year old daughter for a weekend of shopping. The room was very clean, location very close to shopping on Harwin, & value we couldn't beat. Best of all, the front desk clerk was very friendly and helpful with giving suggestions for shopping and restaurants.

title: “Really good value for money”
text: Stayed here with my son (12 yrs old) for 2 nights. Staff were very friendly & room was very nice and spotlessly clean. Location was good for the money I paid. Very close to cafe deluxe which is def well worth a visit and within staggering distance!!! I'd def stay here again.

title: “Good location and view but busy and noisy”
text:
The hotel was doing an offer where there were offering a Regency Club room for the same price as a standard room. We decided to take up this option and ended up with a room on the 34th floor (Room 3420) which had a great view out over the river and Navy Pier.
The room itself was exactly as the pictures on the website portrayed with a nice comfortable bed. There was a safe in the room which meant we could safely stow away our valuables and this was big enough to hold our cameras as well as cash etc.
The only criticisms of the hotel was it was extremely busy and noisy, we had heard it described as a railway station and this rang true. We were also in the West Tower and trying to get the lift to our floor took a long time as they were extremely busy.
We made use of the Regency Club lounge but as the promotion was being offered by the hotel it was extremely busy in the evening with nowhere to sit until other guests had finished. We spent our time in the adjoining business centre on the PC to kill a bit of time.
It was quieter in the morning but we were there fairly early as we didn’t get a good night’s sleep with other guests returning to their rooms at all hours of the night – and not being quiet about it.

title: “Conveniently located!”
text:
This hotel is conveniently located to many of Chicago's attractions, but not many within walking distance. I was there for a conference being held at Navy Pier, and was glad that shuttle service was provided for our group.
I was a little disappointed in the size of the rooms, and the lighting in the bathroom left much to be desired.
Internet service was expensive and unreliable.

title: “A Must Stay!”
text:
All hotels are not alike!! The Hampton Inn - Aboretum Northwest was exceptional, at least for me. What made it so good were the people. This property really trains their people well. For example, the next morning after I checked in and during breakfast, Sean Fitzgerald walked up to me and called me by my name. That has not happened to me in 30+ years of traveling. He was professional and asked me if there was anything he could do to make my stay more enjoyable. And when I checked in the night before, the same courteous attitude was extended to me. I aboslutely love the "people skills" exhibited by all the employees at the hotel. The rooms and breakfast were exceptional as well. 
I will return!

title: “3 1/2 stars”
text: The big advantage is that they have garage parking for cars. Check-in was cumbersome. The elevator required a card swipe each time you get in--a pain, but perhaps necessary due to security concerns in Washington. To use the garage, you have to call the front desk each time for access, which was also a bit of a pain. The garage spaces are tight--if you have a big car, watch out! The rooms have refrigerators and a coffee maker, and are spacious, but the heater wasn't on and you need to call the desk to ask how to operate it since the controls are hidden away. Location-wise it's great, although it's about a mile or so from Dupont Circle, so you are in a quiet neighborhood, which can be a pro or a con, depending. No big problems--just a few niggly issues. Overall, 31/2 stars.

title: “Wrong address and unrepentent!”
text: Apparently it is fashionable to have an address on Pennsylvania Avenue, but when you are carrying luggage and it is cold and you are tripping over snow drifts, you should be able to find a hotel based on the address provided by the hotel. The Lombardy Hotel is not located at 2019 Pennsylvania Avenue; only a strip of green grass is located at Twentieth Street and Pennsylvania Avenue in Northwest Washington, DC. Aside from that criticism, the hotel is acceptable; not old and elegant like the Churchill, but acceptable, and 2019 I Street is a very good location in its own right.

title: “Right place at the right time.”
text: I was booked here by the Broadway League for a business event. After reading the reviews here, I wasn't certain about staying there, but I thought if the League is recommending it, it must be OK. We found it to be delightful! The rooms are small - this is Manhattan and if you want a big room, you're gonna pay huge bucks for it. But, it had everything you needed and some nice perks too. The Bose Wave radio (it's not an Ipod dock as one reviewer expected... it's a radio!) has a great sound. Our room was toward the back of the hotel and overlooked rooftops, so we left the curtains down. A windowbox light made it appear that sunlight was streaming in, even though the drapes were closed. The TV remote has a sensor that is not attached to the TV so if you place things on the desk that block the sensor, the remote won't work. (Another problem cited by a different reviewer.) There is an expensive mini bar - typical. WIFI was iffy, but the in-room ethernet connection worked great. We had a "red" room which felt vaguely "Japanese" to me with clean lines, black furniture and no wasted space. Bathroobes to lounge in were fluffy.The huge shower had plenty of hot water and pressure. Everything was clean. Maids were wonderful about coming in when it was convenient for us. There is a parking garage right across the street. The hotel is about 1/2 block to the very top of Times Square and about 2 blocks to the heart of it. The play "Chicago" is at the theatre right across the street. They were loading out "Spring Awakening" from next door and "Mamma Mia" is just out and around the corner. There is a Food Emporium across the street and 1/2 block down - upstairs is deli food and basement had a grocery store great for families watching their $$. Lots of cool sidewalk vendors on 9th ave, just aroudn the block. Subway, shopping, theatre, it's all within easy walking distance. Everything was clean. The staff was wonderful. The door isn't well marked - look for the yellow signs for Sarafina's - so I'm glad I knew the lobby was on the second floor.

title: “Great Location”
text:
We stayed here December 21, 2004. The room was clean, spacious and comfortable. Bed wasn't too comfortable, but that's hotel life.
Everything was conveniently located and within walking distance - Fort Worth Convention Center, Sundance Square, Greyhound Bus Terminal across the street, etc. and felt the area was safe for a downtown area at night. The room service and restaraunts are expensive, but there is a Corner Bakery around the corner as well as a lot of eateries two or three blocks away. One annoying item: our room overlooked the lobby - windows faced inside as we were on the 5th floor. They have birds in a cage and I heard whistling all night until around 11pm. Not a big deal, but worth noting. They also wake up around 6am, so if sleeping is important, you might want to request a higher floor or one not overlooking the inside lobby.
I'd recommend the hotel to friends.

title: “Beautiful Views and Excellence Services”
text: I absolutely wonderful place to stay for get away but unfortunately I was there for business trip. I did not have enough time to enjoy the ocean views. It’s very convenience location 15 minutes to San Diego downtown( Gas Lamp) and airport. Spectacular room. very clean and very quite. The best conceirge services I ever had, also friendly staffs waiters, and waitress. I can’t says enough about the beautiful ocean view. My biggest regret is did not stay long enough but definitely I will return for near future.

title: “Fantastic hotel”
text:
This is the second time we have stayed at Park 79 and it is a fantastic hotel. Great location (we like to get away from the hustle and bustle of Manhattan) and super close to a subway stop. The restaurants around the hotel are fantastic as well. The room is small but who cares - I didn't go to NYC to hang out in a hotel room. We had our own bathroom which makes the stay even nicer. The front desk people are nice and helpful, the door guys are cheerful and go out of their way to make the stay enjoyable.
We will be coming back for sure - and although I have heard that the elevator is slow - we have the fortunate advantage of staying on the first floor.

title: “Lovely stay - would recommend - great location”
text:
We enjoyed our stay here. The location is great - central to all the attractions.
We loved the Diner - great food and service.
We booked a View Room and had a fabulous view of the Empire State Building and the New York skyline. 
The room was spacious and very clean and the service was great.

title: “Great location”
text: Excellent hotel in a wonderful location. We took brisk walks to the georgetown shops and enjoyed all of the dining options. Our tour to Mount Vernon picked us up right at the hotel!! Very conveniently situated. Clean and well appointed rooms. Would absolutely stay there again.

title: “I didn't want to leave!!”
text: I had a room with a beautiful view of the city. My room was spacious, clean and came with a kitchenette. The front desk staff was helpful. The wifi was free and worked wonderfully. It wasnt until my last day that the amenities section was on the first floor. There was a laundry mat on my floor. I wish I'd known about it, I wouldve packed less. I was a 10 minute walk from the convention center, restaurnats, library and shopping.

title: “The perfect proposal?”
text:
I recently celebrated both my birthday weekend and my engagement at the Four Seasons Hotel. My fiance went to great lengths to plan a romantic weekend that I wouldn't forget.
He booked the 'Romance Package,' which included flowers, champagne, and breakfast room service the following morning. For an additional $30 he requested that they place a single line of rose petals from the door leading up to the champagne on the table. He called in advance to make certain that everything would be set up upon our arrival. He even dropped by the hotel to give them an additional dozen roses to set up in the room and double check the arrangements. 
We checked in and noticed that several other guests were sent to the Swann because their rooms were not ready. The clerk was very nice to me but kept giving me this goofy smile once she saw my name. Obviously she was in on everything. ;)
We got up to the room, and I asked my boyfriend what was wrong, because he looked upset. The room seemed fine to me and had a lovely view, but here they never set up anything per his advance instructions. He went ahead and proposed despite things not being exactly as he envisioned. The best laid plans of Mice and Men! 
My fiance called downstairs and mentioned that none of the flowers were there (the petals he purchased, the flowers that came with the room, and the flowers he bought), nor was the champagne.
A few minutes later, we heard a knock at the door. The valet handed him vase #1 -- the flowers that came with the room.
Several minutes later, the champagne unceremoniously arrived. Still no dozen roses. At this point it was comical because now I was aware of everything that was supposed to be done in advance.
Finally, a second phone call resulted in the staff locating the dozen roses (the hotel was kind enough to provide a glass vase, which they let me keep).
We had a light snack in the Swann Lounge. Very good.
Later in the evening we went down to a late seating dinner at the Fountain, which was wonderful. We did the tasting menu, which I highly recommend. For dessert, the lit a candle and wrote "Happy Birthday" on my plate and "Congratulations" on my fiance's plate in chocolate sauce. Now this was the Four Seasons' service that I recall from past experience. The only downside was that there were two couples near us who were very loud, but it provided some side entertainment.
We returned to our room, and lo and behold -- rose petals everywhere. 
The following morning, we had a delicious breakfast, although the time of delivery got screwed up by half an hour.
The bed was comfortable, and we had a good night's sleep, but the overall quality of service was not what I would expect given the hotel's reputation and price range. 
I have other experiences with this hotel and have stayed here before. I was unimpressed with a banquet dinner held here, but I absolutely love the afternoon tea at the Swann Lounge. It's wonderful, and I try to attend one at least once or twice a year.
I would not stay at this hotel again given the other options in the city, but the food service and quality more than make up for the hotel's other problems. I will continue to enjoy the Swann Lounge and will take my fiance to brunch at the Fountain for his birthday.
And despite all of the things that went 'wrong,' my proposal was still perfect and a memory that I will always cherish. I'm a lucky woman to have a man who went to such great lengths on my behalf.

title: “Horrible, disgusting and haunted”
text: I had stayed in the Ramada Inn while auditioning for American Idol. Where I'm from Ramada Inn's are very classy hotels, but not very expensive. This one was HORRIBLE! Words can't even describe it. We were put in a room that they house Red Cross burn victims in and there were blood stains all over the carpet. The heat refused to turn off and the building was half falling apart. Not to mention having someone taking a shower on either side of us at 1 am and finding out no one was in the rooms beside us! The staff was kind, but that was where the good ends! The diner is falling apart and the food was terrible! The side of town it's on is very run down. DO NOT GO ANYWHERE AT NIGHT! Very, scary! We were so displeased with the hotel that we slid in at 30 seconds until check out time, checked out, and threw our clothes into our bags still on the hangers. We didn't have another hotel to go to, but we would have rather slept in our car. By the time we found another hotel, and unpacked it was 8 at night because when we went to unpack we had everyone else's stuff because we had packed in such a panic just to get out of there! Trying to find another hotel was a waste of a day off between auditions! If you stay here, you will regret it!

title: “Great location”
text: We stayed for two nights in mid July 2005. The location was great, and the room clean. We had requested a rollaway bed for our seven year old, and they gave us a sofa bed which was great. The linens for the sofa bed were not in the room, but the next morning when the maid made up the room she made up the sofa bed. It was no big deal as we had a sleeping bag for our son. Everthing was clean. The breakfast in the mornings was very nice. The only downside was the parking fee was this was only $15 compared to $25 at the Holiday Inn.

title: “I was worried after reading reviews but it was a good experience.”
text:
I read a few reviews saying the rooms were small and that people had other issues, but I had a positive experience overall. I booked the room through priceline (naming my price of $190 a night, which worked out to about $220 after all taxes and fees and for memorial day weekend, I thought that was a pretty good price).
The room was a little small but it's New York and that's what I would expect. We didn't spend much time in the room though (it was a beautiful weekend and obviously wanted to get out and see the city). The room was also modern and clean. And you can't beat the location- right off Colombus Circle and close to subway and central park.
The staff was nice and check in/out was a breeze. The garden bar was nice but prices were pretty high (gin and tonic and a Makers Mark were $31 for the two). We stayed on 10th floor and had no problem sleeping- couldn't even hear the noise from the club in the lobby. The club was bumping pretty good when we got back to our room at about 2 or 3 Saturday night.

title: “can't get the Bold 9900 yet but the rooms were nice”
text: Stayed @ the ATT Hotel and Conference Center a couple weeks back and was very pleased with the quality of the hotel and room. The location is great if you want to stroll the college campus and eat at some of the local "color" eateries. Not quite "downtown" if that's the experience you're looking for. Probably a better deal if you "bid" through one of the travel sites, otherwise it seems a bit pricey to me.

title: “Great Experience”
text: Great experience. The staff was wonderful. Valet quick, bar decent, location great, room nice and quiet. I would definitely stay there again.

title: “My first trip to Chicago”
text: The Swissotel is an amazing hotel. The staff was so pleasant and very helpful. Our view from the room was perfect. Our daughter loved the huge bed, which was very comfortable. The hotel is centrally located to all the hot spots of Chicago. We will definately stay here next time we visit Chicago.

title: “Modern hotel at a great price”
text: My husband and I stayed at this hotel for 2 nights in the summer of 2002. We loved it. We had one little problem with a double charge (we booked through **** but it was resolved quickly and efficiently. The location just can't be beat. The design/decoration of the room was top notch - very high end and classy. I thought it was small (which was fine because I hear that most NYC hotel rooms are small) but my friends from NYC stopped by to pick us up and they were surprised at the size, the price and the location. If you've never been to NYC and want a nice, centrally located hotel. This is the place!! I highly recommend it!

title: “A fantastic hotel with exceptional staff!”
text:
Stayed here for the first time and this is now one of my new favorite hotels in the world. The hotel - and the rooms - have great design, terrific views, perfect public spaces and is extremely welcoming. The fitness center is not large, but is adequate. Restaurant and bar are both very good. Really exceptional staff - they were extremely accommodating to our very early check-in (thank you Anna); Concierge was very helpful in providing information on getting around (example: asked if we should call a taxi to return from a location - "No, call me and I will have one sent to you."); overall everyone we encountered was great. 
This would definitely be my first choice for any stay in Seattle.

title: “Simply fantastic”
text: The staff is fun and pleasant. We loved it and will be back soon again.

title: “Our Favorite Hotel in Chicago”
text:
We have stayed at the Omni, once a year for a few years. Cannot believe the staff actually remembers us! This hotel for our family just cannot be beat!
The staff is first rate, so attentive!
The rooms are perfect for a family with a large bathroom and separate living area. The rooms are always spotless and the bathroom stocked.
Join the Omni rewards program, it is free and gets you lots of free goodies.
Will continue to stay here.
Check out Travelzoo for great rates too!

title: “Loved it”
text:
Stayed here for 5 nights and loved the Hotel and loved San Francisco.
Fantastic location and unable to fault the Hotel.
Great central location with everything needed close at hand. Stayed on the 6th floor over 
looking the street.
San Francisco was the highlight of my holiday and the Baldwin just capped it off.
I will return to San Francisco and I will being staying here again
Stayed on the 6th floor over looking the street.

title: “Pretty Expensive for what you actually get.....”
text: Good location, close to the Piers, the cable car line, many restuarants, tours and etc. We paid over $200 per night for a less than average room. Was clean the first night, but was left pretty dirty for our next couple of nights. Very small room and not a great view. There were 4 of us and only 3 towels left every afternoon. So overall, location was good, housekeeping sucked and it was over priced, but still enough to rate it 3 stars.

title: “Poor AT&T reception for cell phones (but still a nice hotel)”
text:
The hotel is very nice but the signal on my AT&T Iphone was very bad (other than in the lobby) - a lot of time had no reception at all. 
I was also plagued by Internet problems multiple times - the Internet help desk is just unreachable. Tried them three times and waited forever in the endless waiting queue (I guess a lot of other people had issues as well), never was able to reach anyone. Front desk was not capable to help with this.
$20 for a lost umbrella??? First time see I something like that at a Hyatt. At many other Hyatts umbrellas are complimentary during rain!
Other than that the hotel is very nice and service is the staff is very helpful and friendly.

title: “Better than expected”
text: We stayed here for one night after a late night arrival at the airport before we headed out for a ski weekend. The quality of the furniture was much better and the size of the room was much bigger than I expected. Definitely a cut above the usual "clean, but bare bones" road side motels. It was clean and the staff was nice, but I cannot say we had that much interaction with them.

title: “Holiday Inn Capitol offers a great location, value, and staff”
text: We arrived at the Holiday Inn Capitol a little after 9:00 am. Our plan was to leave our luggage with the bellman and then walk over to the United States Capitol for our scheduled tour. The front desk staff allowed us check into our room immediately -- six hours before the official check-in time. The hotel has a wonderful rooftop pool that was still open in September. The Holiday Inn's location is superb. It is a block or so from the Air & Space Museum. Conveniently, there is a CVS and a McDonald's nearby. However, the gift shop is well-stocked and even carries my wife's brand of contact lens solution.

title: “You pay for history. Don't expect more.”
text:
I was very disappointed. I am an adult male traveling with my mother making two beds a necessity. We are meticulous about making sure to book rooms with two beds or we don't book at all.
So I'm sure you can see where this is going. We showed the check-in staff our exact paper that specified our room was to have two separate beds. We were told there were none available. The staff, however, was very accommodating and told us they could get us a roll-away and then upgrade us to a Suite. Fine, I'll rough it for one night.
So we head up to the room after being told the roll-away is on it's way. 30 minutes pass, nothing. We call back. Another 30 minutes pass, nothing. Only upon the third call (1:30AM) do we finally get a roll away. We sleep.
So the next night we go to the front desk to get keys to our suite. "OK, now this suite is going to have two beds?" "Oh well, it has a couch that turns into a bed. Yeah, but I didn't pay $300 a night to sleep on the COUCH! "This is a four level upgrade, I'm sure you will find it satisfactory."
Ummmmmm...no, actually. I appreciate your effort and generosity on such a large upgrade, but if our problem is that our room has only a single bed, upgrading us to a nicer room with one bed doesn't solve the problem that needs to be solved!
So that was that. We paid $300 a night for one of us to sleep on a hide-away bed for a week. Lame.
The AC units in the rooms are useless and you're discouraged from opening the windows. It takes the strength of the Incredible Hulk to get them open anyway, at which point you're met with the loud buzzing of generators.
The bathroom is the (only) highlight. Our suite had a fantastic tile walk-in shower. Shower head was high and heated up plenty fast. Sink was granite with plenty of space to put your stuff. The usual fare was provided.
To cap off the trip, for some reason the very last night they decided to remake the sofa instead of just leaving the bed down. Around we went again. Called at 5:00, come back from dinner, no bed. Called at 7, nothing. Called again at 8...finally someone came to make the bed down.
Common areas are beautiful (you have to sneak your way into some of the ballroooms) and I did feel for them, that has to be expensive to maintain, but that shouldn't fall on us. Con your way in to take pictures of the common areas, but stay somewhere else.

title: “Bargain for the location”
text: Firstly if you are looking for luxury or modern large rooms, stop reading and move on. This is an older hotel in a super convenient location just off times square priced extremely well. yes as per other reviews the rooms are old, the fixtures have seen some better days and the wireless internet will drive you nuts but look past this to the wonderful staff, perfect location and clean rooms. I have stayed at newer hotels in New York in much worse locations at 50% more per night. if you are like me and are in New York to get out and do things from morning until late at night, you will appreciate the easy access, great staff and clean bed to pop your head on after a full day in the big apple. It is the perfect location to access Central Park, Times Square, 42nd street station, pier 81, the list goes on.......... I will stay here again and I recommend it to anyone.

title: “Great bar/lobby and good food in the restaurant, but that's about it.”
text: This hotel is a great place for a party, with its open, central, welcoming bar/lobby and second floor restaurant which is expensive but has good food and nice wait staff. Flat screen TVs are everywhere in the lobby, and the atmosphere is festive. (Note: When you arrive, don't come to the Michagan Avenue entrance; bellhops, etc., are all on the driveway side of the hotel, on Rush Street.) The rooms, however, leave something to be desired. We were there for three nights. Our 15th floor room, which had fabulous linens and mattresses but also floor-to-ceiling windows, was freezing when we got there, and on the thermostat there was a printed warning: "In some seasons, you may need the assistance of hotel staff to maintain a comfortable temperature in the room." So we called, and a cordial man came up and fixed the problem. However, this was not the only heat-related difficulty. On two of the three mornings we had no hot water and couldn't take showers. Also, the bathroom was teeny.

title: “Great hotel for the Money”
text: This hotel was great for the money. I would definitely stay here again. My only compliant is that the toilet seat was in very bad condition a $20 repair that would have made the bathroom appear much nicer.

title: “A cheap hotel in the center of the town”
text:
Great room, clean. Just a little noisy at night
Very near the peabody institute
Not very far from Inner harbor
OK for the breakfast

title: “A Really Nice Hotel....just a couple small problems.”
text: This hotel is in a really great location! It was very easy to find and so close to the National Mall-2 blocks. We started at the Capital and worked our way to the Lincoln Memorial and then back up on the other side hitting up the White House and museums on the way and back. The 2 problems were this-we arrived at 9am (I know WAY too early to get into our room and I didn't expect to, I just wanted to park our van, let them know we have arrived and stow our luggage) well, to my surprise they said they had a room! Yeah! We go up with our stuff and open the door and SURPRISE! Someone's stuff is in the room. Thank GOD there was no one running around naked-that would have shocked us all! I go down and let the front desk person know (BTW ALL OF THE EMPLOYEES WERE SUPER PLEASANT AND PROFESSIONAL) he gets us another room. EEEK! Another room with someone's possessions. Another apology and he doesn't have another room. We check our things and head out for a great day. When we get back around 5pm our room was on the 11th floor and it was just a regular room (nothing exciting or fancy)-our things were brought up promptly. The decor and furnishings in the lobby/bar/restaurant were definitely nicer. We checked out at 4am and the person couldn't give me a receipt. I know they swiped our credit card and I assume we're going to be charged for parking but I couldn't get a receipt for the charge. Strange. We'd probably try another hotel next time we're in D.C. just to try another one but I would highly recommend this hotel.

title: “Disappointed”
text: I was excited about this hotel after reviews. However, I was disappointed. Check in lady was not friendly . The outdoor roof terraces were closed and under renovation (had looked forward to having wine and cheese there as suggested in reviews). There was noisy construction across the street early every a.m.. I am assuming this was the former site of Manhattan Diner, as it was not across the street as indicated in reviews? Shower was nice and roomy but the bathroom itself very small. It was our anniversary trip and I had asked for a quiet location away from elevators , above 9th floor and request any upgrades that might could be given to make our stay special.. Got none of my requests.......Got a room directly across from elevator and on 6th floor. Very noisy with doors slaming shut constantly (automatic closers), outside traffic noises and across street from a fire dept! Also my request for only tea packets instead of coffee packets went ignored. Did not feel the price of this hotel was worth it. POSITIVES: Was near subway stops, markets and cafes. Loved Coppala's Pizzeria on 79th! Our best meal while in NYC! Liked Big Nicks and Cafe Frida nearby.

title: “A patchy experience”
text: The location is very convenient, the staff was very helpful and courteous but the hotel itself is definitely in need of upgrading. Our room on the 18th floor was large and would have been great except for the feeling that it hadn't been maintained or refurbished in years. I also didn't feel that it had been cleaned very well. The bathroom especially is in need of work. And a more modern air conditioner that lets you sleep wouldn't go amiss.

title: “Spent my birthday here”
text:
This is a beautiful hotel , located within walking distance of museums and restaurants. Fact is we spent the weekend and never moved the car. The room were grand , I liked the layout of the bathrooms so much that I designed my current master bathroom the same way. The staff was friendly and helpful. The concierge even called ahead to the restaurant to tell them I was coming and it was my birthday.
This is a first class hotel with a first class staff.

title: “Great place to stay”
text: Stayed June 2012. Second time staying here. Great place to stay, near everything but quiet. Excellent service from Cody & Angel - nothing too much trouble, helpful advice. Breakfast had a good range; dinner in the restaurant was lovely - only ordered an main/entree as the sizes are big (not different ot most of US!!)

title: “Excellent value, family suite was perfect”
text: Excellent value for a 2 bedroom suite - paid $240/night (plus tax), booked directly by phone through the hotel - 1 room with 2 double beds, the other with 1 queen, both good-sized with their own TV's and writing/sitting tables. Quiet hotel, great location, rooftop terrace/garden/happy hour a great feature, along with the comfortable off-lobby lounge where the continental breakfast is served. Staff was extrememly courteous and helpful; excellent deli across the street; great decor. Theater tip -- try the Hourglass Tavern on 46th Street for dinner before a show, it's all 'pre-theater' fixed price specials, lovely Italian/European restaurant, almost quaint inside, great seafood and pasta, cobbler for dessert warm from the oven(!), all less than $20/person complete.

title: “Huge disappointment ...way below Marriott's expected standards”
text:
Firstly I'd like to say that the previous reviews mention clean rooms and comfy beds...Well? so they should be for a 4 star Hotel, and of course if you want central NYC then the location is perfect.
I have always believed Marriott USA would be the ultimate experience in Hotel excellence. I have stayed in Marriott Hotels around the world from Sydney to Dubai to Singapore to Toronto and the UK to mention a few... I have news for the Marquis management...you need to get out more! 
Hotel staff we dealt with were usually efficient . On check in we decided to upgrade to a suite for an extra US$200 per night. The 'suite'' needed a total re-furb, the furnishings were very tired. The bathroom had 3 little cheap toiletries, no tumblers. There were no drinking glasses in the room at all. There was a corkage charge of $US35. No mini bar and a useless little coffee machine. We had access to the Concierge Lounge, this facility is still a mystery to us, we expected an exectuive lounge such as other Marriott Hotels...in the Concierge lounge you could have free dessert and coffee ( in paper cups) each night....there was a very expensive bar where you could buy your drinks...that was it!?
Now here comes a WARNING...if you require tickets for a show, and approach the Concierge, you will be directed the TICKET TEK desk across the Lobby. This was my experience...The clerk at TICKET TEK quoted a price per ticket, silly me I didn't ask about the commission charge. I was charged 30% on top of the face value of $125...YES that's $US40 on EACH ticket. As fate would have it, this was the evening of the Times Sq bomb scare. The Hotel was barricaded off therefore making it impossible to get to the theatre next door! I'm still waiting on a refund! Leslie at Marriott's customer service has kindly tried to help, 5 weeks later I'm still hopeful. The Marriott Marquis should take better care of their guests and make sure they are not ripped off by TICKET TEK (Americana Tickets NY) 
 The management would learn a lot from other Marriotts such as the Sydney Marriott in Circular Quay. Efficient and Friendly staff... and THEY have a Executive lounge!
Will I be back to The Marquis?...NO

title: “A comfortable hotel, in a perfect location”
text:
We stayed at the Cassa Hotel from the 3rd May 11 to 7 May 11 and enjoyed our experience. We were on our honeymoon and were upgraded to better room by the guest services manager/concierge Eric Hall.
The room was of a good standard, a bit of a weird shape which made it feel a bit cramped but it was still a good size. The room was clean the bathroom was modern and of a good size. There wasn't a view which didn't bother us as we weren't sitting in our room looking out the window. We found the room comfortable and had a good quality sleep.
The hotel didn't have a restuarant although they did do breakfast and some sort of evening drinks and nibbles that we didn't try. They are in the process of putting in a restuarant but no works were being carried out during our stay.
The location was fantastic, the hotel was not on a buy street but close to times square, grand central station. There a numerous good restuarants around the area of the hotel.
A very big plus for the hotel was the guest services manager Eric Hall we went to him to ask a few questions about some things to see and when he found out that it was our first trip to New York he basically planned out the our trip on a map of all the things to do. We loosely followed these points of interests and had a great time.

title: “ABSOLUTELY GORGEOUS!!!!”
text: This was my first stay at the Hampton Inn and it was beautiful!!! As soon as you entered into the hotel u could smell the cleanliness. Everyone of their staff members were very professional and helped out as much as possible. The rooms are to die for, clean and comfortable. The location is great if u are looking for shopping and dining in walking distance. I would recommend this hotel for anyone in this area or traveling!!!!

title: “Meets Residence Inn Expectations”
text: The property is very centrally located and only a short walk from the Metro. Parking street-side can be challenging, especially due to alternate side regulations. That can be expected in any popular neighborhood in DC, however. Complementary dinner (served three nights per week) and breakfast (every morning) were excellent. I will definitely return.

title: “Disappointing”
text:
What a disappointing experience! For my money, I could have gotten a much better value at another hotel. First, even though it is only two blocks west of Michigan Avenue, it is almost in the middle of nowhere. No interesting restaurants, bars, or shops. Luckily, there is one good breakfast place on the same block - Tempo's. Eat breakfast there; you'll love it. Skip the hotel's breakfast offerings and head to Tempo's.
Check in was quick and uneventful.
Our room was on the 22nd floor and had a nice view of the Hancock. But the only downside of the room was this nasty noxious cleaning spray housekeeping uses - and they visit your room twice a day. Each time we'd enter the room, this poisonous cloud of orange smelling cleaning would attack our senses. If we had stayed longer, I would have probably called down and asked for our room not be to cleaned.
Oh, this is the reason I'll never stay there again: $9.95/day internet access. [-] T-Mobile access that you have to constantly log back in to.
The beds were comfortable, but the robes were not.
Turn down service was a nice touch, especially with the water bottles - but the staff turned the A/C off and our room was swelltering when we returned to it.
Two people cannot fit into the shower, so don't try it.
We won't stay there again, mostly because of the whole internet issue.

title: “Great Value, Location & Service”
text:
I booked this hotel as we were attending a conference at the JW Marriott. We had the option to stay there, but felt we didn't want to be right on top of it.
We were delighted with our stay here. From the moment we arrived the staff could not be more helpful.
The rooms are huge, and I mean huge! The beds are comfortable, and street noise is hardly there. Ocasionally you get the odd guest who might not respect that other people are sleeping, but to be honest what hotel doesn't.
Breakfast is a simple affair, cooked or continental. Though you can pour your own waffles!
Included in the price is an evening meal, although simple they are tasty and included is a selection on wines and beers, with soft drinks for those that choose. All in all great value!
Location, is perfect. You are within 5 minutes walk to all the best restaurants and bars. 
The Circle Shopping Mall is directly across the road and open till 9pm, so shopping available on tap.
The Indy Speedway is only 15 minutes drive away as well.
All is all I would recommend staying here and would have no trouble doing so again should I be in Indianapolis!

title: “Attentive Staff”
text: We stayed at the Empire for three nights, and found the experience very pleasant. Every staff person we interacted with, from the doorman to the people at the front desk, and the cleaning staff , was very pleasant and helpful. We requested a room with a view on a quiet floor, which was accommodated. The room was on the small side, but very clean and quiet. We reserved our room on Priceline, and found it to be an excellent value for the money. The bathroom was small, but workable. The location was great---just across the street from Lincoln Center, and a couple of blocks from Central Park. The weather was mild, so we didn't have issues with the heating or air conditioner. Would definitely recommend the Empire Hotel.

title: “Great hotel, great value, wonderful service!”
text: My wife and I had a very good experince staying at The Orchard. Probably the most impressive thing was the staff. While checking in, which went smoothly, I left my money clip laying on the counter and realised that I'd left it while on the way to our room. By the time we had got back to the desk, the doorman was already on his way to our room with the money clip. The staff's resturant recamendations were also helpful as was the shuttle service back to the airport. Overall a great experience with nice rooms and service!

title: “The best hotel we had in 25 day trip to west coast”
text:
What can I say about this hotel that has not been said yet. Probably nothing.
we were on a trip to USA for 25 days to the west coast ( San Francisco to San Diego) and stayed in many luxury hotels during that time , but Magic castle Hotel was the best, from several perspective.
First - is the great staff and their attitude to the hotel guest. Everything with a smile and a lot of patient.
The day we had to go to universal they guied us how to get thier and gave us a premade note which has an explaintion how to use the train , which station to take where to get down ect...
Second is the place itself , we had a 2 bedroom apartment which was fully occupied with everything we could think about , it was spacious enough for 5 people and very clean.
The hotel built as a small complex of apartment around the small pool. 
There is a laundry room and where ever you desire you can go to the front desk and get yourself a snack or something to drink.
Eventually the location is great 5 minutes walk to Hollywood boulevard and to the near market store.
One metro station from universal studio. 
we be more then happy to come buck to this hotel

title: “Great rooms and great location”
text: This is a comfortable and contemporary Embassy Suites. It is located right next to Westfield's UTC mall and steps away from PF Changs. We had 2 connecting 1 bedroom suites and then moved to a 2 bedroom suite. All the rooms were well appointed and spacious, with a microwave and coffee making facilities. There are laundry machines on each floor as well as vending machines for sodas etc and ice. Morning breakfast is v early and quite crowded so get up as early as possible if you are hungry. There is also a managers reception each evening with complimentary drinks and snacks. Kids will love the glass elevators and fish ponds. There is also a pool. I would def go back.

title: “Wonderful Story Time”
text: My children and I had a fabulous time at the Bedtime Story event. The staff were truly engaged with even the youngest kids! The pancake making instruction was terrific, too. Every child got to take part! We will return for years to come!

title: “Location, location, location”
text:
This hotel is all about the location. For a first time visitor to NYC it is amazingly close to about everything. We barely used public transport during our stay. Walking and a few taxi trips solved about all of the transportation.
The rooms are nicely appointed with a really comfortable bead, and a clean large bathroom. It is not overly large, but not small either. I would describe it as a good standard but not extraordinary.
Staff was both great and a bit of a miss. The concierge and the bell boys went above and beyond in helping us and really did a great job. I would recommend talking to them about restaurants, air port transfer, shopping etc. Though the fornt desk staff was more of a miss. They felt clueless in several requests and gave contradictory answers and did not feel that professional or knowledgable.
During our stay both the restaurant and the bar was being refurbished, something we were not notified of beforehand. And the breakfast was instead a box collected at the front desk consisting of yoghurt, a croissant and a banana. It was sufficient, but perhaps not something I would expect from a hotel such as this.
In summary, it is perfectly located and provides a good nights sleep. But it did not provide me with that feeling of a place that goes above and beyond, though the bell boys certainly do!

title: “Nice, warm and well appointed”
text: I liked this hotel. It doesn't have that corporate feel at all. The rooms are small but very comfortable and well appointed. The lobby is the same - small but warm. The location is odd but good. It is only a few blocks from the public library and 2 blocks from Grand Central. Times Square was a 10 minute walk. But you are on the "other side" of Park Avenue so it feels more residential and quieter. I was really pleased with my stay. It's not grand, or impressive. But it's warm, nice touches (like cocoa and hot toddies, water all day infused with citrus, and the "raid the mini bar" coupon) and a good-enough local.

title: “Not worth the money”
text: It was nothing buy avarage staff was unfriendly our aircon was broken, room wasnt ready at check in time booked it for the hostorical feel however for a few dollars more you can do allot better overall not whats advertised the location dis make up for the rest

title: “is crap!”
text:
Honestly I hated New York city because of this hotel! I remembered the movie derailed, stay away from this place! 
Pennsylvania hotel same or similar rate way better

title: “A weeks biz stay”
text: quiet and cosy room. average bar. car park - very hefty

title: “Fabulous”
text:
Love New York, love Tribeca, loved this hotel. 
Polar opposite experience here, compared with my stay at The Old Mill Inn in Toronto. 
There was a massive power outage that knocked out most of lower Manhattan, but the staff stepped up to the plate and delivered fantastic service with a smile. The concierge even sent someone in a taxi to pick up cheeseburgers and shakes for us!
The rooms are great, very clean and just an all round perfect place to stay.

title: “Excellent!”
text: My wife and I are having a wonderful stay at the Sofitel. Everyone from the concierge, to the people opening doors and wishing us bonjour, as well as the front desk staff, and the hardworking waitstaff, among them Bryan and Niakoba, have been exemplary and it has been a pleasure staying here.

title: “Bad service - customer comes last attitude”
text:
Clean hotel. Okay location. Definitely focused on Japanese business travelers. 
We booked about 3 weeks before our stay, and I specifically asked for a non-smoking room. When we arrived, they informed me we would be in a smoking room. I complained. They said they didn't get my "non-smoking" request. To get into a non-smoking room, we had to pay an extra fee. What?! The next morning, they found my email from 3 weeks before, requesting the non-smoking room. But they refused to refund my "extra fee." I couldn't believe it.
I won't stay here, again.

title: “okay...just okay”
text:
My husband and I decided to spend a weekend in Chicago for our birthdays the weekend of October 2nd and 3rd. The night before our stay, I called the hotel to make sure that we were NOT in a smoking room. I had read a previous post on trip advisor from someone who had gotten stuck with a smoking room. Since I am currently pregnant, I didn't feel like taking in some second hand smoke. The young lady who answered the phone assured me we had A NON-SMOKING KING ROOM. Well fast forward to check-in, guess what??? We were in a smoking room! I explained to the man at the front desk that I had called the day before to confirm and he said "that's what you get when you book through Hotwire." Nice. So we had to pay $60 for an "upgrade" of the exact same room we were going to be staying in to begin with. We just moved up 2 floors...wow. Our room by the way was definitely not equipped with a king sized bed. It was obvioulsy a queen.
The hotel decor was very modern but honestly not that impressive. The elevators were teeny tiny and you always had to wait FOREVER since they only had those two tiny elevators which had to make stops on like each floor. 
Room service was super expensive, but luckily I had read that the breakfasts across the street at E'leven were awesome. And they were! 
So overall, I'm very dissappointed with this hotel. Maybe it was because we "made the mistake" of booking through hotwire. And I still don't understand why we had to pay for an upgrade, yet we ended up in a smaller room two floors up?!!!

title: “A Must See in Phoenix”
text:
Just returned from 5 nights/6 days at the JW Desert Ridge Resort and we cannot say enough about this property. Not only are the grounds beautiful but the service is outstanding. We stayed Aug 15-20.
PROS:
It is not perfect in every way but it is so gorgeous and so well taken care of the pros far outweigh the cons. From the moment you drive up the grand entrance and the doorman opens the door as you enter you will be taken to another world--one of elegance and service.
I traveled with my wife and a teenager plus two small children so we upgraded to a suite and got an attaching room so we would have room to spread out. If you travel in August it is so hot the rates are affordable which allowed us to do this. I called three times to ask for a pool view and to be close to the pools since we knew our little ones would be back and forth. With each call I was moved closer to the pools and we were very satisfied with our room view and location and very satisfied that our request was treated with importance and that we were taken seriously. With small children we knew we would be back and forth from the pools to the room a thousand times so location was important to us.
Having a balcony was awesome as we sat outside almost every morning and evening and used it while the kids napped. And the view of the beautiful grounds was amazing.
My eldest son and I golfed the Faldo Course at Wildfire and had a blast! The course was in great shape and the drink gal that came around was prompt and very fast. The service at the course was phenominal and again the course was in great shape. The golf experience was definitely one of the highlights of our trip.
The slide was perfect for our 4 yr old and we all enjoyed many laps around the lazy river. We did use and enjoy the other pools as well.
