And the staff helped the kids make smores by the hot tub on Friday and Saturday nights which was a nice touch. The pool food and beverage service was prompt and very good. We used it often as well since the kids wanted to swim day and night!
The resort is just beautiful and the service makes the place even better. We will definitely be back which is the best compliment of all you can give a hotel.
CONS:
The only "bummers" we had were few and in comparison were far outweighed by the staff service and sheer beauty of the resort. The food selection at the Blue Sage was thin and the service was not great at this restaurant. The internet service really should be offered for free at such a fine hotel and it is painfully slow. My 3G phone was faster on the internet so we finally shut off the hotel internet. In this day and age charging you for internet at a 5 star hotel seems a little like nickel and diming. The entrance is so grand that the parking lot for self park is a pretty good jaunt from the resort. My children get up early and swim early AND late so we wished the slide would have opened before 10a.m. and stayed open past 6p.m.
All in all this is a fantastic property!!! We recommend you stay here on your next stay in Phoenix! We certainly will!!

title: “Nice Stay”
text:
I had a sweet experience at Westin..
Pros & Cons:
Pros:
Great location
Neat rooms
Movie theater inside the hotel!
Cons:
A bit expensive
Business lounge (for internet) closes at 10:00pm
Cheap breakfast

title: “Great addition to Charlotte downtown hotels!”
text: It was a nice Saturday so my boyfriend and I took the day to go in an exploring walk and ended up walking to downtown (I'm about a mile and a half from downtown). I've been wanting to check this place out so we walked through the lobby to see what it looked like and then over to the Epicentre to grab some lunch. I googled the hotel on my phone while at lunch just to see what all the amenities were and when I saw the $109 online rates, we decided it would be a fun get away to make a night of downtown dinner, movie, out... Very nice place and the "extras" are what make it a step up from the competition - nice kitcheonette with glasses, plates, silver and full size refrigerator. Very nice modern decor and spacious room with a wonderful view. It's a great location as well and depending on what is going on in downtown, you may be able to park in the lot directly next to the hotel for $5 - saves you the $22 parking and it's literally right by the hotel. Internet worked great, staff was very friendly and breakfast was exceptional for an included breakfast. I would definitely recommend this hotel to others!

title: “Nothing special on top of the hill”
text:
We reserved our room through SLH website, which as SLH club member should entitle you to one of those availability based upgrades. When we arrived, the front desk mentioned that we got an upgrade, but when we saw the room, one big disappointment: despite the respectable size, the room was dated, not well furnished and had no nice "touch & feel". Even a room at a chain hotel has more character.
bell staff however is outstanding, concierge lacks some interest in what guests ask for and does not seem to have the "contacts" one needs to get you reservation at the top restaurants.
Quite a disappointment for a SLH hotel ... but luckily there are other options like the Mandarin and even the Mark Hopkins Club floor rooms are much better!

title: “Great Room and Location But Pathetic Service”
text:
I stayed in YOTEL for 8 nights altogether during my trip to New York City.
The room was well designed for how small it is, making use of all available spaces. I liked the compartment below the bed where you could put your luggage. The adjustable bed was also delightful, makes lying on bed watching tv comfortable! I also enjoyed its fast WIFI service which i did not encounter any problems during my stay.
Overall the room was clean and morden!
I stayed in Yotel for 2 nights, before i went for a 4 day tour to DC and Niagara. Prior to arriving, i had emailed Yotel to asked if i could leave my excess luggage with them for 4 days. To which they replied no, as their YOBOT was only able to hold the luggage for 24hours. Fair enough. When i asked for RECOMMENDATIONS to where would be a good place near them to store my luggage for the days i wasn't around. Guess what? They replied that i should use GOOGLE. I am sure i did not thought about using google, but it would have been nice if they have recommended a place, as i would trust their recommendation more than a search from google.
I came back to yotel 4 days later and checked in again for the rest of my trip. There would always be missing towels everyday the house keeping keeps the room. Be it a floor towel, facial towel, it was hardly every a complete set.
I left yotel and to which it is my fault that i forgot to pack in 1 pair of my jeans and 1 pair of my pants. Upon reaching home and realising that i have left my pants in their hotel. I called their "Lost & Found" department. The person who picked up the call was unfriendly and uninterested to assist me. She simply said that there was no lost item reported. I probe further and told where where i placed my pants. She said she would call housekeeping to check and hang up on me, without taking down my details or making any indications that she would contact me once there is news. I had to call them again 1hour later to find out, and to which she said there was no lost item found and hanged up again.
What is the point of having a good room and location when your service just doesn't cut it. It is like a punch line of a bad joke that a service oriented company is providing bad services.

title: “Great deal for price”
text: Stayed here Memorial Day weekend. Basic King room on 13th floor was $179 a night. Great view. Only 4 rooms per floor. Light breakfast included, great way to start day. Quiet. Two long blocks and 2 short blocks to subway at 34th and 8th. 10-15 walking minutes from Times Square. Close to Penn Station if you want to catch train to Newark Airport. Room was clean and cleaned nicely each day, staff friendly. Held bags on last day after checkout. Free internet, free breakfast, it all adds up. Good location if you want to stop by room to clean up or rest before evening after day out. Not a great location if you don't want to walk some (but New York City is a walker's town). For the price, would be hard to beat in Midtown.

title: “Small Room, nice hotel!”
text:
Great history involved with this old hotel. Do your research and you will be happy to stay there! The upper floor pool old gangster style pool is wonderful! Great for kids! 
Make sure you get a room on the south side of the building. If you get a high enough room you will be able to see the chicago river, lake michigan and Michigan Ave! Great hotel for shoppers!!!

title: “Noisy and coffeeless”
text: I stayed in the hotel for 3 nights, having booked it through Expedia before leaving the UK. The reception was friendly, but the room was one of the smallest I think I have ever stayed in - though clean and tended by some pleasant Chinese chambermaids. The worst thing was trying to prepare a coffee! The coffee pot apparently did not fit the filter machine - which I only found out when the filter spilled water over the floor - oh, and all coffee, sugar and dried milk was damp and congealed in the packet. At night the noises in the corridor woke me twice after midnight, and it would appear that the room opposite mine was occupied by a hotel staff member (no swipe card machine on the outside, just a keyhole) who parked his bicycle in the corridor. I was put off (as were many English staying here) by the fact that the hotel locks its front door at 7pm (use your key to get in) to stop the vagrants getting in. A trip outside the hotel at 8pm meant running the gamut of large numbers of vagrants who continually ask for money, and can follow you down the street. I was only tempted to give money to one, who carried a board reading "Dollars wanted for alcohol research".

title: “Enjoyed our stay.”
text:
Excellent place to stay... No frills, clean, and free parking under your room in courtyard. Close to everything.
A classic, clean 1960's style motor lodge, in a beautiful city.

title: “Old, Tired & Dirty”
text:
We booked this place as a stop over - a place where we could rest after a long journey. This place is a dump. It's dirty, old and noisy. Our door faced a busy road, which was OK, except that there was such a big gap around the door that a giant could limbo dance under it! We listened to road noise all night. Take a look at the photos - the room was dirty, dark and old. The view out the window was "interesting" if you're interested in looking at a messy rooftop!
Lastly, the room cleaners are in the habit of mopping the water off the 2nd story balconies straight on to the path below. I was just about drenched as I walked back to my room in the morning.
Yes - it's cheap, but you barely get what you pay for.

title: “Excellent Weekend Trip”
text:
This is my second Kimpton hotel stay and I've had great experiences in both.
My wife and I celebrated our anniversary with a weekend trip to NYC and stayed here at Ink48. It's a fairly short walk to Times Square which was great.
We stayed on the 17th floor and had a fantastic view of the city. Beautiful accommodations - we were most pleased with our room. Plus, the concierge had a bottle of champagne waiting in our room on the first night. Nice touch!

title: “Good, but not great”
text:
We had a good experience at executive vintage hotel, but for the price we would have preferred to stay at the Holiday Inn at the wharf (which is where we stayed on the trip as well). The room was small, had a very strong musty smell when we arrived, and the window was small at best.
The pluses is the location is good (close to china town) and they do provide a nice wine tasting. The main desk people were nice as well. 
If you like wine or "an older feel" consider this place, otherwise look for an economy hotel instead.

title: “Nice place to stay.”
text: The hotel was clean. The staff was helpful. Very close to shopping and restaurants including two malls. It was a bit noisy after 6:30am because of construction around the hotel. The breakfast area is a little small. Overall, It was very good hotel for the money. If we choose to go back to San Antonio, this hotel will be on the top of our list.

title: “Love this hotel”
text: I have stayed in this hotel four times for a trip to the city. I loved it ,so elegant and friendly this hotel is underrated in my opinion. My granddaughter loved the fluffy beds and the ballrooms.

title: “$36 a night - you get what you pay for!”
text:
This was the worst hotel stay of my life. I had read reviews of this hotel on other websites and didn't read anything too negative, so I figured I'd give it a try. I got a special deal with my plane ticket on Priceline, and the room ended up costing me about $36 a night. I certainly didn't expect anything fancy, but I assumed that it would at least be clean and habitable - bad assumption!
I had made the reservation through Priceline about a month in advance, and the entire amount was charged to my credit card a few weeks before I actually traveled. My reservation was for two nights in a non-smoking room. I checked in at 5:00PM, and was told that the only room available was a smoking room. I reminded the desk clerk that my paid reservation was for a non-smoking room, and the desk clerk told me that I really didn't have any option, and that I wouldn't get any credit if I cancelled the reservation, as that was something I had evidently agreed to when I booked it through Priceline.
The room was filthy, it stunk of stale cigarette smoke, the air conditioner was disabled, and the temperature in the room probably didn't fall below about 90 degrees the whole time I was there. It nauseated me, and I didn't get a wink of sleep either night.
But shame on me, I guess. What did I expect for $36?

title: “Great Value, Great Service”
text: Hosted a small conference at this location largely to the excellent assistance from Tina Kindel the Best Western's Sales Director. Our associates were more than satisfied with the rooms and catering. Would do business with again in the near future. Service was extraordinary.

title: “Nice and Clean”
text: Stayed one night at the end of a business trip because of the close proximity to LAX. They also offer a free shuttle. The hotel looked recently remodeled, with very nice rooms and free wifi. Even got a complimentary snack bag for being a priority club member.

title: “Nice view”
text: Two nights in the big city. Fast elevators. Good food. Rooms were typical Hyatt,,upscale, clean and trendy. Property is quiet. Internet kind of sucked, but hey, they probably don't have business class cisco equipment. Garage was typical of a big city environment. Secure/large and easily accessible. I would stay here again.

title: “Loved the Palomar”
text:
Stayed in a beautiful 750 sq foot suite with a huge bathroom. Very comfortable. We also had another King room for our daughter. It was on the small side also quite beautiful.
Service at breakfast was not great one day. 
The bar is a hopping place.
Got a reat deal through travelzoo.

title: “A great place to stay”
text: The hotel was clean and had lots of amenities. The staff was friendly, especially Estela Estrada, who was efficient, charming and courteous.

title: “Kimpton Hotels never dissappoint”
text:
My husband and I fell in love with the Kimpton Hotels a few years ago in Washington DC. The Hotel Burnham did not disappoint us. The location is perfect - one block to the Blue Line, across the street from the Red Line. Easy train ride from O'Hare to the hotel. The building is gorgeous. The view was great. The bed was a little slice of heaven. The Atwood Cafe has excellent food, and our bar tender, Doug, was wonderful.
We are looking forward to visiting the newest Kimpton, Hotel Monaco, in Baltimore, and we are eagerly anticipating the opening of the Palomar in Philadelphia this fall.

title: “Delightful Hotel - Fabulous Location”
text: We found Hotel Indigo upon realizing that my old, cheap, fav, Days Inn on N. Clark, had closed... Indigo was more expensive, but considerably less than other Gold Coast locations, with a parking ramp next door, and located one block from the subway. What a great surprise! With decor based on aesthetics, the Golden Mean, and art symbolism, the Indigo was a treat for the senses - funky, comfortable furniture, unique wall coverings, interesting spaces, awesome colors. It was more like visiting the comfortable home of an artist than staying in a hotel. The staff were wonderful. We've found a wonderful place to go back to in Hotel Indigo!

title: “One Of The Best Embassy Suites We Have Stayed At”
text:
My husband, 7 year old son and I spent the night at this Embassy Suites and had a wonderful time. The hotel is located right off the highway and you have to park in a lower parking garage, but we never felt unsafe. The hotel just recently underwent a $12.3 million transformation and all I can say is WOW! It is very nice inside and it has a very relaxing atmosphere. There are flat screens everywhere, including booths where you can have your cooked to order breakfast in the morning, which by the way was very good.
We arrived just a few minutes after the Evening Manager's Reception had ended and the bartender was nice enough to allow my husband and I to have one cocktail before ending it. The hotel staff were all very friendly, which is very important to us.
The room was very nice and clean as well. There were two 37" flat screen tv's and it had one of the most comfortable beds that I have slept on at any hotel ever. 
If there was one thing that I would change about the hotel, it would be the size of the towels that they have at the swimming pool. We have stayed at quite a few Embassy Suites and usually you will find regular sized towels at their pools. At this Embassy Suites, they had very small towels and I did overhear a few people complaining about that. Other than that, it was a perfect stay and I am sure that we will be back again. 
I would highly recommend this hotel to anyone looking for a nice, comfortable and relaxing place to staff with friendly staff!

title: “Fantastic Hotel”
text:
We stayed at this hotel at the end of March while on our way to Vancouver. Check in was fast and the staff at the front desk were very helpful with maps and showing us places of interest that we may wish to visit. The hotel offered complimentry wifi for all guest which i think was fantastic.
The rooms we had were fantastic with large bathroom with a walk in shower and a large bath with sliding doors so you could watch the TV from the bath. The room was large and also had a queen size bed. 
The hotel offers guest free use of their town car so if your staying at the hotel before the crusie the hotel will take you down to the docks or if your travelling to the airport free of charge.
The hotel is only a short walk to the Space Needle, the hotel aslo has a super market under the hotel which you can excess from a lift in the hotel or a short walk out of the hotel down some steps.
Next time we are going to vist Seattle i will be deffintly staying at this hotel.

title: “We Love an Impeccably Clean Hotel”
text: We stayed here on Dec. 27, and as usual it was a great, relaxing experience! We have stayed here before, and you can count on the Westin Riverwalk to be consistent in every aspect, especially cleanliness. The hotel cleaning staff greeted us with a smile or hello whenever we passed them. There is nothing like walking into a clean hotel. The lobby floors are very impressive; not a smudge on them. My wife and I love the outside balcony areas. The lobby balconies are very clean and inviting. You can sit comfortably and watch the lovely Riverwalk, especially during Christmas. The city lines the Riverwalk with colorful Christmas lights; this year they used the new LED lights and they are spectacular. They turn them on the day after Thanksgiving and turn them off after the New Year. The Westin is the perfect place to sit and enjoy the Christmas lights. My wife noticed that there wasn't any dust on the tables, and that the trash cans were emptied regularly. Another thing, the elevators are impeccable; it isn't often that you find a hotel where the elevator walls and floors are polished. There wasn't a fingerprint on the elevator walls. You can see that great attention to detail is paramount here at the Westin. Our room was beautiful, and yes very clean. The bathroom was especially inviting. We got the room we wanted, the young lady at the front desk was very helpful and was attentive to our every need; we requested a room with a balcony, and got it. It was wonderful to stand out there and take-in the beautiful Riverwalk. There is no doubt that we will be back. Because of our experiences at the Westin Riverwalk; Westin is our first choice whenever and wherever we travel. Thank you Westin Riverwalk for another wonderful experience.

title: “Excellent!”
text:
I stayed at the Yotel while in NYC on business - while a little concerned that it looked like a yo sushi it in fact turned out to be a great experience, and an awesome place to stay.
Checking into the hotel was easy using the automated machinery, staff were on hand to assist you if needed. The rooms themselves were small - but this was expected. The beds were comfortable and automatic, so you can change them into more of a sofa than a bed. I am not old and do not suffer from a bad back, so messing with the bed was new to me, and good fun!!!
The 1st floor (check in area) also has the bar and food - at night this place becomes a mini bar/club and is convenient as I only had to fall into the lift to my room!

title: “In the middle of everything”
text:
The hotel has been recently renovated and it shows. The rooms are contemporary (in a pseudo Asian/bamboo way.)
You can see the old and tired portions of the hotel in the elevators, some hallways etc. 
Being that the hotel is embedded within Grand Central Staition, it is very conven

title: “Warm & Friendly Hotel - Great Location!”
text: This is a wonderful boutique hotel close to shopping, restaurants, buses, cable cars, streetcars & BART. It is nostalgically old with great character. Friendly staff who sincerely wanted us to enjoy our stay. We really liked the wine tasting hour in the lobby - met couples from Canada, Australia, Madison & Chicago; one night we had quite a party going when it ended at 6pm, so the server brought over a couple of opened wine bottles for us to carry on. We ate one breakfast in connected Jasper's Restaurant, food was good but a little spendy compared to neighborhood breakfast restaurants - but handy if you don't want to leave the hotel to eat. After reading about the bed bug outbreak in April, we brought along a spray that we used on the carpet surrounding the bed, but didn't see even one bug. Overall = A+, would definitely return.

title: “Beautiful Hotel, Beautiful Location!!”
text: The Copley Plaza Hotel is a beautiful hotel with the feel of real elegance. The Concierge and rest of the staff were very pleasant. Our room wasn't huge but very comfortable, the beds and linens were great. The bathroom was on the small size with very little room for personal toileteries for one person let alone two. The hotel is showing it's age and could do with a little sprucing up. But it is very obvious that it was once a very elegant and beautiful hotel. The lobby is amazing and looks like it has been kept in it's original form. The restaurant is lovely and has the feel of a gentleman's club. The hotel is centrally located on a beautiful square by the Library, Trinity Church and if you are a fan of Boston Legal the building is a couple of minutes walk away at 500 Boylston Street. Overall a very pleasant stay and would not hesitate to go back.

title: “Gorgeous Sheraton- probably best one I have seen”
text: Huge tall facility smack in downtown business district. Mind you downtown is DEAD after business hours and you have to trek to areas like Scottsdale or other parts of Phoenix to find something to do. The property is brilliant with huge lobby, all stone floors, nice large well furnished rooms, and a great workout facility. 4 diamond property and it shows for certain. Ample underground parking and a short drive from airport. Again not in a hot spot so if planning on bar hopping not the best location.

title: “A great place”
text: We stayed at The Westin for an overnight in Boston. We booked that day on Hotwire for $196. The room was great. We had a King size bed on the 35th floor with a spectacular view of Boston. We drank in the bar which was lovely. We ate in the fish restaurant which was very nice. This was a very nice hotel in a perfect location with a great many services on the premises and attached to a luxury mall. I highly recommend this place for business or pleasure.

title: “A week at Beck's Motor lodge”
text: I think it was a really ok place to live at, not so expensive and a good area. They cleaned the rooms every day and give you new towels each time. It is a bit loud, you hear easily people if they are talking outside the door or screams down at market street and the cars down the street. The room had a bit of weird smell. But altogether I would totally recommend it! And the bar Blackbird nearby!

title: “Nice Place If You're Headed to the Convention Center”
text:
My company sent me here for an expo. It's a cool hotel that's THE closest to the convention center you can get. That said, you still have to cross 2 busy streets and walk a 1/4 block to get to the center.
OK, I always break my reviews into Good News & Bad News.
The Good News:
The hotel passed my thorough bed bug inspection. Before even open my suitcase, I peel back all of the sheets, mattress covers, blankets and I lift up the mattress and box spring. Having done this I found no bugs but I was really tired and craving a beer - which was readily accessible in the hotel bar. 
The room smelled good and was very clean overall. My room was #1122 and it had a nice bathtub/shower combo. One of the best things is that they have AVEDA products. Not much in the world smells better than Aveda's rosemary mint shampoo, conditioner and lotion. And they refill your basket each day! 
The hotel bar & restaurant are nice -- there's a part of the bar that seems to be for the more businessey types and then another part that's connected to the restaurant that seemed to be more anything goes (even PJ bottoms and a t-shirt on one lady, but I digress).
Check-in was smooth as was getting to the room. The bellman and taxi guys are top notch and they have a killer conceirge called a "Navigator". There's a little over-priced gift shop onsite too (as found at most metro hotels) but they had all the major needs covered in terms of stuff people could forget.
It's in an OK neighborhood - good restaurants within a 10 minute walk. Chinatown nearby, Walgreens, Subway, etc. Don't make the mistake I did and let the hotel bartender tell you that the monuments are just a few blocks away - a good walk. I walked and it was at least 10 blocks or more. Grab a cab and have him drop you at the Washington Monument and from there you can walk to the WWII monument and the Lincoln Memorial on fresh legs. Then you can grab a cab at the cab stand outside the Lincoln Memorial and swing by the White House on your way back. 
If you're in town for a conference or meeting and you only have an hour or two to spare but you want to see a bunch of stuff, hire a cab for a rate of $25 for the hour and have him take you to the Washington, WWII, and Lincoln monuments and then swing by the White House and Capitol Building before heading back to the hotel. This was KILLER and we got great pics. Cabs-a-Plenty in front of the hotel for this.
The Bad News:
The bathrooms lack a fan for moisture so it gets pretty jungle-like in there after a shower. Add in a second person and you've got a tropical situation. Kind of challenging when getting ready for a business function. We propped our door to the hallway open and cranked the air in hopes of getting some flow and we had limited success.
As mentioned, the hotel is a bit of a hike from the convention center. About a 5-9 minute walk in all. Take it slow and easy so you're not all sweaty when you get to where you're going if you're in town for a show or expo.
This hotel doesn't appear to be overly handicapped accessible. I'm not handicapped but I have a family member who is so I always find myself thinking in terms of "how would my sister get around here". Lot of stairs and curbs. Not saying they're not ADA compliant, but just that it's not an optimal location for those who can't do steps.
Lots of construction in the area doesn't make for a nice view, but this is through no fault of the hotel. Actually, while I was there, they were doing some nice renovations to a portion of the building.
Last but not least, keep a close eye on your bags at the bell station when checking out. When we got to the airport, we had an "extra" bag in the trunk of our cab. We insisted the cabbie return it to the hotel and we even called the hotel to ensure they were aware of this and he did take it back, but it could've caused a real problem for some other poor unsuspecting person. It's always something...
Overall, I'd stay here again if I had an expo or convention to attend. It's not an A++ but it's a good place to call home for the time you're in town.

title: “Nice hotel, but had bed bugs.”
text: This is a nice hotel, in a good location for downtown Detroit events. Hotel looked nicely remodeled, looked clean above average. Hallways can be noisey as doors slam shut. We were happy with our stay until we woke up to find a bed bug on the comforter and in the bathroom. Management was professional and refunded our money. They denied any previous problems with bed bugs and stayed they would fix the problem.

title: “Hidden gem by SeaTac”
text:
I have now stated at the Cedarbrook Lodge five times in the last year while in Seattle for business. This hotel was formally the conference center for Washington Mutual, so it has a lot of great business features. It is surprisingly quiet even though it is just a few minutes from the airport. You do not feel like you are in the middle of an urban area, is there are some wetlands adjacent to the property. The hotel is just minutes from Interstate 5, so you can be in downtown Seattle or downtown Tacoma quickly. Even better, there is a light rail station just a few minutes a way that will take you to downtown Seattle in about 20 min.
The Copper Leaf restaurant is a small, intimate room with outstanding food. The hotel has a continental breakfast, and free snacks including Häagen-Dazs ice cream. I am not sure what more you could ask for in a business hotel.
My wife has also stayed there when traveling alone, and has been treated exceptionally and feels very secure on the property. This is our "go to" place when traveling to the Seattle area.

title: “Customer service A+”
text: This was my very first time in NYC. We took my son for his 16th birthday. I was so pleased with the staff. Everyone was so friendly & helpful. We were given an upgrade to accomodate my family of 4. The room was beautiful with a nice view of 5th Ave overlooking the New York Public Library. Mini bar drinks & snack + Wifi is complimentary excluding alcohol. Thank you Andaz for a wonderful 1st time! We will definitely be back!

title: “seattle”
text: we booked on the day of arrival and were upgraded to a room with a balcony, was lovely and pioneer square was a great area to be in with restaurants and shops and ferrries all easily accessible breakfast was great and staff friendly

title: “Great hotel, location just spoils it a bit”
text:
Our hotel room at the Silver Cloud Inn was one of the nicest ones I have stayed in for a long time. The hotel is brand new, which helps, but at the same time the room was planned and decorated really well. There was plenty of light (natural and electric), good storage, nice seating, great beds, flat screen TV (the favourite of my male travel companions) and the bathroom was great. Aveda toiletries were the icing on the cake. 
It took a little while to get used to the trains going past all night, but that was a minor nuisance and after the first night we got used to the sounds.
We only had drinks at the restaurant, which seemed like an upscale sportsbar. Which is natural as Safeco field is across the street. In a way I am happy we stayed at the Silver Cloud when Mariners were playing Away, the hotel and the streets around us would have been a lot tranquil with thousands of sportsfans wandering around.
We paid USD 169 per night for the room, plus parking. This is a very good price in Seattle in a summer weekend. I have to admit I was concerned when Hotwire gave me this hotel location after making my reservation. I still think the location is not great (except for Baseball fans), but it is walkable to downtown and the free shuttle makes life a lot easier. (Walkable is more like a city hike, so everybody might not be willing to do it.)
I would definitely stay at the Silver Cloud again, but at the same time I would be willing to pay a little more and stay truly downtown. I just wish I could take the hotel room with me, it was so great! Seattle Sheraton, pay attention...

title: “Great NYC hotel in Marriott chain”
text: I always like to try "smaller" boutique hotels, but I am a "Marriott tramp" and love, even more getting the Reward points! I will start looking more into Marriott Autograph Collection hotels because of our recent stay at the Carlton Hotel this past weekend. Great location between Midtown and SoHo - where we spend a good deal of our time: Midtown for B'Way shows and restaurants and SoHo for shopping and, well, restaurants! I was upgraded to a very nice room on the 11th floor (of 12 floors) with a king bed and a fairly large living room. The bath was very well-appointed and the place was very quiet - which I really appreciate, esp. in Manhattan. Everyone was friendly and helpful. Getting some work done was very easy - good wireless Internet connection, nice desk, did I mention how quiet is was?

title: “Great Event”
text:
I just had my birthday one the rooftop of Hotel Erwin and I can't say enough about the venue and overall experience. I worked with the events team, who were just amazing, to put together a party for 15 friends. The catering was wonderful, the hotel put together a specialty cocktail for my group that was delicious! 
If you haven't been to the rooftop, it's a must-see. From the outside of the hotel, you would never know what a gem sits on top, with the most breathtaking views of the ocean both to the east bay and Santa Monica, and Pacific Palisades. Definitely recommend the Erwin for any events.

title: “Just Fantastic from UK”
text:
My daughter and iIstayed at the palace from 22 oct for 6 nights
The trip was for my daughts 18th We stayed on the 38 floor overlooking St Pats just fantastic veiws and very large twin room
We checked in at 2 pm and the porter showed us to our room and explained how every thing works.
The large tv in our room had a message saying happy birthday and welcome to new york Jennifer 
The first night we went out for a walk ,close to everything 
On our return we found they had been in room and placed a birthday card and a plate of chocolate coverd straberrys on the table and a birthday cake on the dresser.
How many hotels round the world would do this (no cost )
We had breakfast and evening drinks and nibbles in the executive lounge ,will return to and recomend this hotel .

title: “Location and room excellent, but service makes it not worth the price”
text:
As a consultant, I have seen a large spectrum of hotels. To me the, St. Regis is a hotel that can go toe to toe with the four seasons. My experiences with this chain in NY, Dallas, and CA have all been very enjoyable. Their location, amenities, and service combined for some of the most memorable stays ever for me. Alas, this property fell short on one of those planks and that was service. Given my expectations for this brand going in, it made for a pretty disappointing stay. For what they charge, the shortcomings do not seem to make it worthwhile and I would be very reluctant to recommend this hotel to my friends and colleagues. 
Here is the breakdown of the experience:
Rooms
The rooms are very well appointed, they include two bottles of Fiji water complementary and the beds outstanding and incredibly lush. The bathrooms are well appointed, if a little small, and the bathroom mirror has a TV behind it which is both clever and nice. Being a shower person, this one gets two big thumbs up and has incredible pressure and flow for a very nice shower. 
Workout Room
Awful and basically looks like it was added as an afterthought. Small and not a lot of options. I have been in Marriott Courtyards with better gyms than this.
Location
Great location and I think the hotel gets a lot of its mileage based on this. You are basically right next to the White House and in the center of any business you need to accomplish in the city, both work and pleasure.
Service
For what you would expect, they fall very short. Basically, there is nothing unique about this crew. Special requests (and even regular requests) are met more with an attitude about why they can't or are reluctant to help, than a desire to help you out. The level meets the expectations I would have for staying at a Sheraton, Hilton or Marriott. If you are a little insistent, you can eventually get a resolution, but this is never enjoyable and you are left with the feeling of great hostility. 
Here is an example: We called the “butler” for a couple of Mount Gay and tonic rum drink. Not seeking any additional information they started off by saying they do not offer this? Surprised, because this was not too unusual of a request, we asked why they did not deliver drinks to our room. Finally realizing this was a room service request, they transferred us to the room service dept. The room service person took the order and we waited. Five minutes later, the person called us up and asked if “Mount Gay” was a Gin or Vodka drink? We explained that it was a rum, they thanked us and we waited again. Ten minute later the waiter appeared with three Bacardi Rum (a very, very different rum) drinks. We explained that this was not what we ordered and the server started arguing with us and said that we ordered rum drinks and these were rum drinks. After explaining the big difference, the server basically shot back "Well, what do you want then."
Now imaging 50% of your service interactions follow similar story arc. It is easy to explain away one bad experience as a fluke, but this is something that permeates every level of the organization. If your hotel stay is very typical and within their standard range of service, I am sure you will have a great stay. Go outside of those bounds, and prepare for a difficult experience.
Butler Service
If you book online, most of the room descriptions will indicate butler service as an amenity. In other St. Regis properties, this includes someone in white gloves offering to unpack you cloths, wake you up in the morning with fresh tea, provide you with a bowl of fresh fruit when you arrive. A real luxury and a great way to indulge on your stay. Here I was told that this service actually doesn't include any of this but really means that they "will bring up fresh towels and ice to your room." Not sure why you would brand that “butler service”, when this is something any hotel will do. In fact, unlike places like Westin where the person you talk to will take ownership of your request, the butler service here consisted of nothing more than someone acting like a telephone operator connecting us to the person who could help us like the room service or the valet. 
Starwood Preferred Guest
For business travelers who are SPG preferred elite, don't expect much. For the first time in nearly 5 years (and over 40 different hotels) of being a premium member, I was given a hard time for requesting a late check-out. The receptionist basically refused to acknowledge the option was even available and based on other feedback in this site, I think this is the norm. There were no upgrades, even though the person checking us in, mentioned it was a quiet weekend.
This is far from the worst place to spend your time and there is a lot going for this hotel. It just seems to me that when you have rooms that list for over $400 a night, you would get more than a typical hotel experience. If location and hotel caliber is key, I would recommend staying at the Willard for the price. Or you can save some money and stay at the Hyatt which has outstanding value for the price. Or if you do no need to be at that location, I would check out the Park Hyatt or Four Seasons. Both similar in price and much, much more worth the price.

title: “Great location”
text: This was at least our 5th stay - we celebrate our anniversary here from time to time when we want to stay in downtown Seattle. To start out, we had trouble trying to valet park, there were no places to pull over and we couldn't see a valet to help us if we double parked. We circled around the block and tried again and found a somewhat illegal spot to park. We love the lobby area and Oliver's is really nice. This stay I found things wanting that I hadn't noticed before: no fan in the bathroom, towels seemed a little thin, and the room fan was a little noisy when it clicked on and off during the night. That being said, we still love the hotel, its great staff, and its very central location.

title: “Very nice!”
text: We really enjoyed our 3-night stay at the Gansevoort Park Avenue. Modern decor, nice location, great service, clean rooms, large bathrooms, very comfortable beds, stocked mini fridge, beautiful outdoor pool on the top level. We would definitely recommend to friends and family and will return if the opportunity presents.

title: “Not the prettiest...”
text:
Look, if you've picked this hotel, you want cheap, in the right location and you'll get it here and you get what you pay for. 
The rooms are old, but they're clean, and have heat and really that's all you need. 
I very much liked having a bar fridge and microwave for my use when trying to reduce the number of meals out. Also, free in room wifi is a huge plus. 
The location is fab, easy access to Metro as well as walking pretty much anywhere if you prefer. 
If you're not looking for luxury, I highly recommend here.

title: “Great Value - Spoilt by attitude of Receptionist”
text:
We Stayed at the Grant hotel in March 2007.
The room we had over looked the street, and was very clean, the bathroom was especially good.
Location wise, for the price this hotel cannot be beaten, it is located close to Union Square, China town, Little Italy - all within walking distance. On arrival the guy at check in was very polite and helpful, the room was a good size, and very clean, we experienced some noise from the traffic outside, but this was not too bad.
Free Coffee and tea at reception was vey good, as there were not any in room facilities for making drinks.
Our only complaint is the attitude of a young female receptionist who was very off hand and arrogant, she also made a very rude and personal comment to a member of our party, which spoilt our overall enjoyment of our stay here.
I would recommend this hotel if you are on a budget, and want to be centrally located in San Francisco

title: “Don't miss this hotel!”
text: My flight out of Seattle after a convention was cancelled and I was lucky to get the last room available for one night at the Inn at the Market. My husband and I had stayed here before nearly 4 years ago. When I arrived, the front desk said, "Welcome back, Mrs. Adler. Do you still prefer the New York Times in the morning?" The location above the wonderful Pike Market is divine with those amazing $10 flower bouquets. And on a clear day you can buy wine, cheese and snacks in the market and then take them to the roof of the Inn for unparalleled views of Elliot Bay. The rooms are luxurious and comfortable and a bargain for what you get. I will always return to this lovely oasis in the remarkable Seattle!

title: “An unrefined hotel to say the least”
text:
The good
1. The beds are comfortable and the linens are nice. They have great pillows.
2. The room I was in was of adequate size. The bathroom was large and nice.
3. The hotel is in a central location. There are some good restaurants and bars around. The walk to Independence Hall is about 25 minutes. The drive to the Barnes Collection is about 30 minutes.
The Bad
1. Allot of the people who work there don't know what they are doing. For instance we had breakfast included in our room, but were told by the front desk people that it wasn't included. After about five minutes of waiting around the hotel realized that breakfast was included. At this point we were so embaressed and annoyed that we went elsewhere for coffee.
2. I lost my battery charger for my laptop. It was left in the room. When I called them a day later they said they would check and get back to me within an hour. I never heard back from them.
3. The lobby is pretty horrible, and lots of the furniture in the room was chipped.
Overall I would have been just as happy staying at a Courtyard Marriot or the Palomar accross the street.

title: “Great position, great place to stay”
text: We booked in at the Handlery just off Union Square in San Francisco on the strength of positive reviews from other TripAdvisor users - and we weren't disappointed. The position of the hotel, in Geary Street about two minutes walk from Union Square, is fantastic. The Cable Car to Fisherman's Wharf runs from the corner of the street (though our advice would be get up a bit early, and get on the Cable Car at the bottom of Powell Street. The earlier you get there the shorter the queue, and it's still less than a four minute walk from the hotel!). Great shopping nearby, a huge range of places to eat, Union Square is a brilliant place to people watch, and transport connections to this part of town are great. Our room wasn't huge, but plenty big enough for the two of us. Bed was comfortable, service was impeccable but still friendly and the hotel was spotlessly clean throughout. Nice pool but we didn't have time to use it. We've seen comments about car parking - but to be honest, why would you? We bought a Clipper ticket and loaded it with $40 when we arrived at the airport - and that got us absolutely everywhere we wanted to go, and the Handlery's central location gave us access to buses, cable cars, the BART and trolley buses which took us everywhere. If we're lucky enough to come back to San Francisco, we'll stay here again.

title: “Family visit to NYC”
text: We stayed at the Loews Regency in December 2011. What a lovely experience! Our children had just turned 3 and 6, so we wanted to stay somewhere that would be child (and adult!) friendly. This hotel really managed to get that right. The rooms were quiet and comfortable, the staff was efficient and friendly, the kids were greeted by name every time we arrived or left the hotel, the doorman was always ready to assist us getting into and out of taxis with a stroller. The location is excellent. It really made our stay in New York such a pleasant one. We will definitely stay at this hotel again whether our children are travelling with us or not.

title: “Great Location”
text: This was my first stay at this hotel. It was very nice and exceeded my expectations. It was only a 10 minute walk to the theatre district and other attractions. Considering it was right in noisy downtown Manhatten, you couldn't tell... it was quite. The gym facilities were excellent! I would definitely stay there again.

title: “Great mid-town base”
text:
Really impressed with this hotel - if you're looking for an upscale, deluxe hotel with all the add-ons this place isn't for you - but as someone who normally gives anything calling itself 'boutique' in New York a very wide swerve, fearing fashionista snobby staff and tiny, impractical rooms, this place is a revelation. 
First - location. Amazing. On business, I need to be in this part of town and it's 3 minutes walk from my office and numerous other great destinations. Great selection of restaurants on the doorstep - from walk in sandwich bars to high end. 
Second - The staff. None of the bowing and scraping and 'where's my tip' attitude of the big hotels. Wonderful warm, welcoming and helpful - people that really look like they're trying their best to make your stay a pleasure. If this is the new face of New York, I'll take more of this please!
Third - the room. OK ,not massive - but not tiny either. A little utilitarian/scandi functional for my taste but hey the wi-fi is free and fast (downloaded HD TV shows in minutes), the desk area cool, modern and spacious, great bed and fabulous shower. OK, no view and a little dark but a brilliant base. If I were staying with my wife I'd be more particular and ask for a bigger room with more light and a view, but in town for a couple of days business and needing a base to work from, brilliant.
There's no gym but there's a hook up with NY Racquet and Health down the street (3 mins walk) which I quite like - you get to walk down the road, pick up a juice on the way and an espresso on the way back. If they could expand the hook up to Equinox that would really make it for me!
Great place - I'm coming back to NY in a couple of weeks and will definitely be staying here..Four Seasons usually my place but Chambers has taken its place. Highly recommended! Look at it as your personal base in the city, almost like a serviced apartment with a great vibe. One happy customer.

title: “Great hotel.....”
text: I stayed in the King Suite at this hotel June 1-3 and it as very nice. Something different about this hotel - all the suites are on the first floor. Our window looked out to the sidewalk. I got a good deal directly through the hotel's website. Given that any hotel that had rooms nearby was much more expensive, I did not regret staying here. The location was excellent and easy to find. My only complaint (if any) was the terrible parking situation. There is parking for $5 a day in the garage, but walking out to the garage with all of our luggage was a total pain.

title: “Convinient, great location, great hotel”
text: We where greeted by the clerk in the reception, and where given an upgrade to a corner suite. The room was very spacious, and had all what we could wish for. The bed was very good, and it gave us the best sleep we have had on this trip around the world. All the personnel we where in contact with from room-maid to the front desk service and concierge was smiling and gentle. The breakfast was great too. With a variety of food to enjoy from the buffe. The only downside that we could pick on was the other restaurants in the hotel. There where nothing special buy the food they offered. We had both lunch and dinner there. The location is great if you visit LA buy car, and most people do. Parking was easy. You could choose from vallet parking or self parking. We had self parking. The car rental companies are close by, so there is no problem in returning your rental car. And there is a shuttle bus to the airport, it only takes 10 minutes. Overall we recommend this hotel, and we will definitely stay here again.

title: “Purgatory Point Would Be More Accurate”
text:
I would echo the previous review in every detail. "Prepare to be gouged" is spot-on. $20/day for a parking spot (see photo) -- not even for valet parking, but just to park yourself next to your room. $15/day for the tiny exercise room. Yes, that's per day, not per stay. You get one day's fee off if you book one of the overpriced "spa" packages. Big deal, since the spa services themselves cost many times what they would cost in the outside world. And the prices at their "casual" outdoor restaurant are what you would normally expect from a fine dining experience. My wife and I spent $73 for two appetizers, two soups (nearly inedible), one order of luke-warm, flavorless coffee, and two salads that we split -- no main course. Our room was nothing special, though the rate was what we normally spend in Hawaii. The bathroom paint was disintegrating and peeling off, the hinges on the door were completely rusted, and the furniture was shabby at best.
What the previous reviewer didn't mention is that this is one of those resorts where everything is inconveniently located -- it's all spread out over many acres. Your room is likely to be in a little building far from the main lobby, spa, exercise room, pool, meeting rooms, and restaurants. To do anything, you have to walk outside and walk or drive to the facilities. So if you want to be overcharged for the room, charged extra for every amenity, and inconvenienced in accessing any of them, this is the place for you.

title: “loved it..”
text: nice location,nice hotel,walk anywhere from it.nice and clean,,,a nice breakfast, nnice service.

title: “Great Hotel, Great Value, Great Area”
text: It was a great hotel for the price I paid. We mainly stuck to the Meatpacking District because it's where most of the shops, restaurants and bars we wanted to go to were located and this hotel was close to the action and convenient. It was located on a pretty quiet street (considering that it IS New York) although, I had to do a late night drugstore run and decided against it because of the amount of homeless people on the street, which didn't make me feel all that safe going alone. Again, it's New York and that notion is understood. My room was very clean and pretty spacious for NY standards. The only reason I did not give it a 5 was because one of the elevators was broken during our two night stay. They have either three or four elevators total and only one was operating to/from the rooms. The others were solely being used to take people up to the rooftop restaurant/deck/bar. That was a bit inconvenient but not a huge deal. Overall, great service, great room, great location and a great two night stay.

title: “In need of renovation!”
text:
Yes, the location is great for tourists but in the same general area is the Marriott Longwharf which is far superior.
The room wasn't as clean as I'd like, the carpets were indeed stained, the curtains dirty and the air conditioning unit was in need of repair as it's sputtering all night kept me awake. 
I didn't order room service food or eat in the restaurant for fear that the lack of cleanliness extended to the kitchen, but I did order a class of wine which set me back 22.00. Mind you, that was the least expensive wine on the list.
I come to Boston every 8 weeks for business and will never stay here again.

title: “Convenient but walls are paper thin”
text: The hotel is well situated if you need to stay in downtown LA for business. Be sure to ask for a renovated room - they are pretty nice, although the basic rooms are small. My primary complaint with this hotel is that the walls/doors are paper thin, even worse if you have an adjoining room - you literally can hear everything your next door neighbors have to say during normal conversations. Another annoyance for business travelers is the ridiculous surcharge for internet access - the fitness center is also getting outdated and had several broken machines. Room service was good, front desk helpful and pleasant, Lobby Court restaurant a good option for breakfast.

title: “Great Vacation!”
text: This was a great vacation! The front desk offered maps and driving directions to all the area attractions. They were there to answer all questions. They even helped me print my Sea World tickets for me on their computer.

title: “A nice weekend escape”
text: My husband and I stayed at this hotel on several occasions in Dallas. We are quite picky with our choices and were very pleased with this hotel. Our big "musts": cleanliness, location, ambiance, and as close to 5 star quality as possible. CLEANLINESS: This hotel was impeccably clean. Not one complaint. LOCATION: tucked in the beautiful downtown area of Dallas. There is a trolley that runs just outside of the hotel entrance, but we used personal transport. There are several high quality fine dining restaurants around this area. One in the hotel, a must! Chef Dean Faring’s creations are tasty. And others fine dining and casual restaurants just across the street. You can have access all of the major Downtown sites from this point with ease, taxis are quick and easy: the symphony, Dallas Museum of Art, Sixth Floor Museum, the America Airlines entertainment area, etc. AMBIANCE: my husband and I dislike fussy and overly ornate décor. The hotel is exquisitely decorated. Tones of gold and cream with touches of amber and chocolate. The outside of the hotel is very plain and unassuming. This small hotel is quiet and pleasant to return to after long days of site seeing. The staff were always pleasant to talk to and frequently asked for any way in which they could be of service. Friendly doesn’t do enough to describe the staff there, they made the experience top notch. The hotel bar is very nice and has been busy on both of our trips. Great food and drinks along with wonderful décor. ROOM: Both trips our rooms were very quit. One stay we had a separated living area from the bedroom and one we had a living area and bedroom all in one room. I think I prefer the more open larger feeling all in one floor plan. We had a medium sized flat screened TV, a desk and nice sized closet. The bed and linens were superior and comfy. The bathroom was wonderful. Marble countertops, huge step-in marble shower, large soaking tub and separate toilet room. The bath products were Bvlgari. There was also a TV screen in the bathroom mirror, unique technology that is a treat while getting ready. From the room I couldn’t tell which hotel I was in, no extraordinary factors (besides bathroom TV & bath products). Outside of the room it was first class to the extreme, a true Ritz experience. The hotel spa is a must. Best massage I have had in awhile! There is a patio bar and torch-lit sitting area with music each evening with a great view of Downtown Dallas. The hotel was a 5 star hotel and we really enjoyed our visits.

title: “Disappointment for the money, I have to say...”
text:
We planned Christmas and New Year's in New York City with our family, what could be better? Wanting to be near shopping, Rockefeller Center and Times Square on New Year's, we also had the challenge of finding a bigger space for a family of four. 
After some research, Flatotel arrived at the top of our list for location and that they had a larger suite with a kitchen that could accomodate us. We booked our trip, eventhough the price seemed rather high-but hoped it'd be worth it.
Let me say that the lobby is great, although small...however the elevators seem to have trouble accomodating the number of people that use them. The room was fair in appearance and cleanliness, but there were several days that we requested maid service more than once, and never got it. On one particular occasion, we had not left the room as of about 11 am, my daughter was still alseep and I was in the bathroom getting dressed, when there was a knock at the bathroom door. I assumed it was my daughter waking up and opened it only to find the maid staring at me. I must've looked rather shocked by her appearance in our room as she insisted that I tell her when I would be out so she could clean! I was infuriated! I didn't know maids can enter a room and see people there, only to knock on the door when they're in the bathroom getting dressed!
There was another incident with another one of the staff that I will not go into detail, but they actually threw a pen when they got upset with our conversation. Not professional, to say the least.
While I will say it is centally located, and the larger room with a kitchen is not easy to find, unless we were desperate, we would not return to this hotel. Our experience in New York is that good service is easy to find...just not here, I'm sorry to say.

title: “Good hotel, dismal service”
text:
I booked the Jr. Suite at Ink48 for a girl’s weekend away. We were in town to see a show.
We drove into town and got a great deal on parking at a lot that was only 1 block away; it was ½ the price of what we would have paid for the hotel valet.
Upon entering the hotel, there was nobody to assist us with our bags or open the doors for us which is unusual for Kimpton service (This happened twice when entering the hotel. The one time there were people to open the door, one of them was smoking). There was also no revolving door so getting into the hotel with all of our bags was a bit awkward. 
The two young gentlemen at the front desk were friendly but had to check to see if our room was ready even though we checked-in after 3pm.
We also weren’t given a mini-bar key but didn’t want to have to ask for it after we realized it.
The elevator situation is rather peculiar. There are four elevators available to go to the rooms (which fill up very quickly) but it can sometimes take up to 5 minutes to get one.
Additionally, the hotel staff and guests shared elevators. We had to wait additional time for elevators b/c they were full of service staff on a couple of occasions.
Upon entering our room, we were impressed. The Jr. Suite has an amazing amount of room. The living space is incredible with a fabulous bathroom to match.
However, the partial view of the Hudson is tainted by dirty rooftops and a fleet of telephone-service trucks parked in clear view. 
The hotel hallways were stifling and didn’t seem to be air-conditioned (or were just considerably hotter than the rooms). 
In the morning, we could smell cigarette smoke coming through the vents of the room even though it’s a non-smoking hotel. 
Once settled in the room, we decided to explore the hotel to see what else it had to offer. Surprisingly, there was no business center (although the hotel does have wireless capabilities so be sure to bring your laptop).
We were going to be out all night and just wanted to see the rooftop bar but it was closed and the staff said it wasn’t accessible so we missed probably the best part of the hotel.
We were contemplating dining at the hotel but arrived a little early. When asked to see a menu, the young lady seemed a bit miffed at us and stated that the menu wasn’t yet available because the chef hadn’t produced it even though the restaurant was slated to open in 15 minutes. The rest of the lobby was decent with a small “Living Room” section where the evening’s wine reception was hosted (which started late) and where there is some additional seating in front of the building.
The hotel’s surrounding area in HK is very convenient. We were able to walk to a great restaurant (44 ½ ) just a couple of blocks away. Additionally, it’s VERY close to the Lincoln Tunnel, the convention center and several other go-to areas in the city. For location alone, I wouldn’t totally write-off Ink48 and would possibly give it another try.
Overall, the hotel is decent but the service was seriously lacking (there were too many little things to list). Based on other reviews, I would like to think of our experience as a fluke. However, there are other nearby Kimpton hotels which I would book first before ever returning to Ink48. If this were my first Kimpton experience, I probably wouldn’t have been too excited to see what else they had to offer.
PROS: Location, convenience, newer hotel, clean/large rooms
CONS: Service, waiting for elevators, no business center

title: “Disappointing Conditions....”
text: High expectations relative to other Hawthorn Suites (Alexandria, VA), but proved to be disappointing. Hall carpet and room carpet appeared dark and dirty. Seemed to need cleaning badly. My room's daily housekeeping seemed limited to reshuffling my towels. While breakfast buffet selections were good, dinner snacks consisted of popcorn, pretzels, and chips. Really!! Grossly disappointing. Very close to the airport, with a friendly, customer-service oriented.

title: “Lollypop Guild Rejoice!”
text:
Ohhh yes! If you are one of the last remaining members of the famed Wizard of Oz "Lollypop Guild" (or the "Lullabye Lees" for that matter) the Alexander Inn IS FOR YOU! 
"But why?" you may ask in your funny little voice. Well if you are a member of the venerated Munchkin Land troupe you are no doubt short and because of your considerable age probably hard of hearing. 
Now, the twin beds MUCH too small for this ginormous 5'5'' AMAZON will be perfect for you little people. My feet hung way off the end and that's with my head butted right up against the lovely vynil padded headboard. (Foolish me for assuming The Alexander Inn would provide a bed that would actually FIT their guests.) 
Because of your age-related hearing issues the PAPER THIN WALLS at the Alexander Inn where you can hear every conversation, every door opening and closing, every television,every everything will not affect your sleep. It's gonna be a great place for you guys. I was thinking of you ALL NIGHT LONG!
Now, when you arrive at the Inn, be sure you brought along a flying monkey or two, because NO ONE HELPS YOU WITH YOUR BAGS. You are offered a DOLLY - not even a proper bellhop cart - a DOLLY, to haul your luggage up one, two, three, four stairs and through two doorways to get into the lobby. Two desk staff watched us struggle and strain with our luggage without once offering to help. If they only had a brain. 
Oh and one more thing, bring along that big bucket of water that Dorothy had at the ready 'cause you're gonna need it for the bathrooms. That's right, DIRTY! And dirty the NEXT DAY TOO. My little prettys, it wasn't so pretty to see the previous Scarecrow's straw still in the tub when we arrived.
Needless to say, there's no place like home.

title: “Nice hotel, very good location, but the service is hit or miss”
text:
As a long time road warrior (over 100 per year at a Hilton property fo the past 15 years), I have gotten to know the Hilton system very well. This hotel is relatively new and is nice appointed. The hotel is also well located to downtown, Inner Harbor, Little Italy and Fells Point. Cabs are easily gotten right at the hotel.
The "free" breakfast is adequate. Suggest Tea Evolve right around the corner if time and money are not an issue. Also suggest the Irish Pub accross the street. Good food, better atmosphere. You can start ... and end your night here.
Service at this Hilton is Hit or Miss. As a business traveler, my schedule often changes, and this location is sometimes difficult to work with when it comes to change. I have stayed at the hotel 10-15 times, sometimes great, sometimes not so much. Front desk is very much Hit or Miss. Suggest asking for the general manager when having a problem here, as she seems to actually get it. Front desk always seems to be under stress and often it shows in their attitude.

title: “Very good hotel- Great location!”
text:
Great and safe location, 2 minutes walking distance from Hollywood Bvd. Comfortable and big room, strongly recommend.
No free wifi, no slippers in the room, no shower cap. Bathrooms need renovation and should be more clean.

title: “Fantastic!!!”
text:
Just returned from a trip to New York with my daughter and niece. My daughter spent a long time researching hotels in New York - we eventually decided on The Lucerne and we were not disappointed. We had a Queen Suite on the 7th floor and it was perfect - plenty of room. The small kitchen area with a fridge, microwave, coffee machine, crockery and cutlery was an added bonus. The staff were extremely friendly and helpful - especially the doormen.
The location of the hotel is excellent - after the hustle and bustle of the city, it was lovely to get back to the hotel in the evening and have the choice of so many restaurants nearby. Because it is an area where there are lots of locals, the restaurants all offered really good food at reasonable prices. The restaurant attached to the hotel, 'Nice Matin' was also very good.

title: “Perfect for a Layover at LAX”
text: We needed a place to stay overnight before going to Honolulu and the Embassy Suites worked out great. The shuttle goes back and forth every 20 minutes or so and is only 10 minutes away from the aiprort. The service was fine and the drinks and snacks in the evening with the cooked to order breakfast the next morning was fine as well. We had dinner at the restauarant and if you like thin crust pizza, you should enjoy theirs. The suites were clean and roomy and our stay was very enjoyable.

title: “OK, but a bit strange...”
text:
Location is great if you have a waterside room - parking lot not so much. Loved the cruise liners moored next door, especially as they sailed in the mid-afternoon; when they docked at 5:00 am or so with horns blaring, not so much. Convenient to Pike Place Market, waterfront activities, and Bell Town (if you have police protection or a bodyguard) and a shuttle service is provided to within a reasonable distance of the hotel.
Decor is kind of weird for the Seattle waterfront - antlers everywhere and steel columns covered with bark and mechanically articulated brances to simulate trees... Really! The large LCD Panels in the elevators with underwater were interesting if a bit unnerving if a man eating shark or giant octopus happened to be showing as you entered. Room furnishings were also interesting - a chest of drawers that was probably intended as antique, but actually was way closer to the "garage sale leftover" genre. there was a footstool in front of the fireplace that was purportedly a bear - may have been at one time, but time had taken it's toll besides being butt ugly. The room was clean, but very cramped - not very comfortable for an extended stay.
In general, signs of ageing without timely upkeep were evident throughout. Door jambs and walls that had been run into by luggage carts leaving large gouges and scratches which had not been repaired were prevalent in the hallways. Lamps with loose sockets and inoperative switches are another example. Fire doors may be functional (one hopes), but are truly an ugly way to greet guests as they traverse the hallways - they are absolutely essential for safety, but could be way more attractively done.
We were part of a wedding party which included a buffet dinner. The food was good, plentiful and attractively presented, but the waiters hovered like flies around the guests as they went through the line. I'm not sure what their function was, but they seemed to be more of a hindrance than a help. Midway through dinner I asked one of the hoverers if I might have a cup of coffee and was told, "No, that comes with dessert." Makes for an interesting guest-server relationship...
We ate breakfast in the main didng room both morning of our stay. The food was excellent as was the service. The only fly in the ointment, so to speak, was the attitude of the host which was polite disdain at best. The fact that people wished to eat in his dining room almost seemed to be an unwanted distraction - from what I'm not sure, but he was obviously somewhere else - presumably in a "better place". 
The Edgewater is not what I would consider a value for the prices charged. One would expect first class accomodations and a welcoming attitude at every turn. The fake woodsy, lodge-like look and all the antler embedded furniture is a bad joke.

title: “FABULOUS FRIENDLY SERVICE & GREAT LOCATION!!!”
text: Just returned from a two-night stay at City Club Hotel. After having issues with a Priceline situation, upon arrival they upgraded us to a kind suite with two floors. The staff is extremely helpful & friendly. The location is awesome, two blocks from the center of Times Square. The room is trendy & modern with comfortable linens & very clean bathrooms. The Bigelow toiletries & abundance of towels are a great touch! They even bring you chocolate chip cookies with turn down service. Also, a nice feature for our teens was the free DVD rental from the front desk with many, many movies to chose from. The only downside I had was the noise from the street & other rooms, but we did have a great view with a balcony, so you have to take the good with the bad. After all, it is the city that never sleeps! Don't hesitate to stay here!

title: “Excellent stay”
text: We came into town to celebrate my fiance's daughters 14th birthday who lives in Fort Worth. We wanted to find a hotel where we could have an ajoining room, an indoor pool and a place that accepted pets. We got lucky and found this holiday inn express and it just happen to be less then 3 miles from their house. The ajoining room was a king suite and the other room had 2 queens. It was perfect for her and her friends. The pool was open 24 hours. The staff helped us by giving us forks and plates so the girls could have pizza and cake. The rooms were very clean and spacious. We were on the side facing I-35 and I did not notice any highway noise. The breakfast in the morning was good. There was ham, omlets, pancakes, biscuits and gravy and cinnamon rolls. There are plenty of places to eat around the hotel and the hotel was very convenient to get to. I will stay here again. Thank you!

title: “Wonderful place to celebrate.”
text: We spent 2 nights at the Vitale for my sweetie's birthday. We had a deluxe water view room the first night, and moved to one of the circular suites the next. Both rooms were beautiful and comfortable (and surprisingly quiet considering they overlook the Embarcadero) with great views and lots of amenities. When making the reservation, I mentioned to the hotel that this was a very special birthday celebration. They delivered free of charge, a bottle of champagne, plus a small Scharfenberger cake and birthday card to our room both nights. What a nice surprise! The staff was very friendly, attentive, and responsive. Pricey, yes, but for those special occasions, well worth it when compared with other high end places in SF. We felt very pampered and well taken care of. The only complaint I have is about the service at the Americano cafe in the hotel. We went there for breakfast and the food was very good, but service was slow and indifferent - a big change from the hotel staff. We decided not to go back since there are so many great restaurants in walking distance from the hotel. We had a great time at the Vitale and will definitely go back next time we have a special occasion to celebrate.

title: “Upper East at its very Best”
text:
We held our wedding ceremony, reception and party at The Carlyle - the day before Sandy arrived. It was truly magic. All arrangements were perfect, the rooms looked gorgeous, the staff was incredibly helpful (i.e. they managed to find a seamstress at 11 pm on Saturday night to help us out with an urgently needed alteration for a dress) and all very caring.
During and after "Sandy", the hotel continued to provide outstanding service with staff members working round the clock, looking after the wellbeing of their guests.

title: “Beautifully restored hotel.”
text:
If you long for a stay at a grand old hotel but worry that you will have to give up luxury and comfort, worry no more. The US Grant offers you the chance to capture the experience of a grand old hotel that has been enhanced with a modern touch that blends in very nicely with the original hotel.
Open for just a few months since its restoration, everything looks and feels brand new. The lobby is large and elegant. The elevator décor is dark wood and clubby. The foyer and hallways on each guest floor have blue silk panels within dark wood walls, different and nice. And the rooms, fantastic. The standard rooms may not be as large as other new five star rooms but our standard room had outstanding design features including: a high ceiling, raised braided paneling, three large windows, including one in the bathroom, and bold custom art work behind the bed. There is a frosted glass door to the bathroom, which is done in neutral marble with a cool modern sink area, and a great shower. Our bathroom did not have a bathtub - which was not an issue for us. Overall a very nice room, and a little different for once compared to other standard luxury hotel rooms. 
We did not use any of the restaurants but they looked very nice.
The gym is pretty good, in a front corner of the hotel with lots of windows. There is room for some more equipment which they could use. 
The staff was very friendly and always on top of things. 
The hotel is centrally located and an easy walk to all of the wonderful restaurants of the Gaslamp Quarter. The hotel is also across the street from Horton Plaza for shopping and entertainment needs. If you want to be in the heart of city in a classy hotel with a subtle cool edge, you should be very happy at the US Grant.

title: “Great Budget”
text:
The trip advisor board led us here,a good choice.Stayed here Jan.5-8 and again Jan 19-21. Both times in the older sections for $58 to $65 ,depending on room and day of week. 
 Nicely landscaped gardens and pool area(heated),good expanded continental brkfst.cereal,rolls,muffins,toast,bagels,waffles,h-boiled eggs,coffee,juice,hot choc,tea,milk. Didnt have my computer,so dont remember if all rooms have internet access,but there is a computer in the lobby for guest use which worked out fine.
 Great staff,especially,Mary and Maria,who seemed to be working most often when we were in the lobby,also always someone outside sweeping,cleaning pool,trimming,just keeping the place nice. Rooms very clean and pillow top beds comfy for hotel beds.Laundry available.
 Walk 2 blocks to Old Town or couple more blocks to the left for plenty of dining ,shopping options. (Guadalajara in OT or theres Sizzler on Rosecrantz that are decent choices.Dont forget a fish taco from Rubios while you're there)Driving easy also,but may have to cruise the parking lots in old town for a spot at certain times of the day. Desk has printed directions for both walking locally,or driving to most anything in San Diego. Commuter train,trolley,busses also right there at entrance to old town.Entry to I-8/I-5 or downtown on Pacific Hwy all convenient .Found driving SD quite easy from here.
 There is factory looking military (SpacWar) spacewar? complex across the street,but no noise or traffic problems resulted.
 Overall great place to stay

title: “Great place to stay”
text:
We arrived quite late at night from the east coast and were greeted warmly by the front desk. 
The room was large and very comfortable and the bathroom was huge.
There was free internet access beside the lobby. 
The complimentary breakfast was good. The indoor pool was also nice.
The courtesy shuttle bus was a useful addition.
All in all, a very pleasant stay, and we would definitely go back.

title: “Beautiful rooms, great location, fantastic staff but pricey”
text:
I attended a conference here but stayed over the weekend to see the city. Location is great. I took a cab to the airport (10 min ride) but walked or took the subway everywhere else. Out the front doors to the right about 5 blocks is a large wharf where you'll find land sight seeing tours, whale watching and other boat tours) along with restaurants. Walking away from the water a few blocks and you're in Quincy Market (street entertainers, shops, chain retail stores and lunch-type restaurants and many Irish pubs for drinks or dinner). One of the two main subway terminals (South Station) is to the left out the front doors of the hotel that will take you anywhere you want to go. I'm not "big city" but it was easy to navigate and I never felt unsafe even when it was packed to and from a Sox game. 
The rooms are beautiful and with an amazing bathroom for a hotel. There is a glassed in shower and a separate deep soaking tub. Everything was kept spotless. I only ate one meal at the restaurant/bar in the lobby but it was good and reasonably priced considering the type of hotel and the city. There are benches in the back of the hotel to sit and watch the harbor in the evenings. 
The one small weakness I found was the spa. The massage was mediocre at best and felt more like someone was just putting sunscreen on me than actually massaging.

title: “What's Up, Doc? Great for Howard and Eunice Bannister”
text: A very pleasant place to stay, especially for a conference replete with eccentric academics. The hotel is superbly situated near the Ferry Building. There is easy access to marvelous restaurants and to San Francisco's wonderful public transportation system. The polite staff offer thoughtful suggestions for tourists unfamiliar with the city.

title: “Pretty awesome for $69/night.”
text: Really clean, fresh, modern room. Great place to relax; worry free. Located in a nice, safe neighborhood with lots of food options nearby. Friendly service. The only things I can complain about was that 1) the noise privacy was not the best -- you could hear people in the hallway clearly and the guests upstairs were pretty heavy stompers, and 2) there was no refrigerator or microwave in the room. Other than those two things, I would definitely recommend staying at this hotel!

title: “Awesome hotel - I stay here every time I come to LA”
