text: First stayed here back in February 2010 and I've been very pleased with each of my stays at the Shelter Hotel (about 10 nights by now). The management & staff are very friendly and welcoming. The rooms are nice, comfortable, modern, and clean. I've introduced several of my friends to this hotel & they have all been very impressed. I highly recommend the Shelter!

title: “Great stay in San Fran!”
text: We really liked the hotel...when we arrived, they didn't have any non-smoking regular rooms available for us, so we upgraded to a suite with a bay view for another $15/night. We were there for 3 nights...parking was expensive, but we only had the rental car there for the first night before we returned it. It was a bit far of a walk to all the touristy things, but manageable. We ate at the restaurant on the top floor one night (reservations recommended) which spins to get a complete look at the city - good food and we had been given coupons at the front desk on check in, so all in all not too expensive of a meal...clean, nicely taken care of...we had a wonderful time!

title: “So much works”
text: The location and value is great (although I it really is in the tourist trap precinct). The rooms are adorable but have a little too much furniture in them and not enough mini bar (none). Happy hour is sweet and worth a dip. If I wanted to stay in this part of town I would come back

title: “Great Location and Value”
text: I am always second guessing myself when it comes to the perfect combination of Hotel and Location. The Omni fit both. You are walking distance to China Town and Little Italy. You also can walk to all three types of transit systems within 5-6 minutes. The hotel has a nice traditional feel and the staff is excellent. Everyone at the front desk was eager to answer my questions and offer suggestions on places to eat, things to do, and how to get there. Union Station is a great central location. I will stay here again when we return to San Francisco.

title: “Great Location, Okay Room”
text:
My husband and I took a much coveted overnight stay to Georgetown, our former stomping grounds. Sans kids we were able to travel freely and stay in places other than family-friendly places.
We are familiar with the workings of the city and traffic, especially the nation's capital as it was home for years. The level of expectation for this hotel was not met, in my opinion.
The hotel was located on a side street in the heart of Georgetown. Perfect for those wanting to be in the middle of it all without the sounds of the main drag.
The valet parking left a lot to be desired; there was no where to park easily (or without double parking and causing backup), there was no one waiting outside as promised. The front desk attendant, while friendly, offered up too much personal information (such as pointing out the owner's car out front, which could be moved for easier hotel access) and had unprofessional conversations with other hotel staff (more her tone and relaxed use of language in front of me - telling them to hurry up).
Our room was on the main floor and was an unexpected suite. The bath was nice and large but the refrigerator was in a hole carved out in the bathroom and was situated upon levels of plywood. The updates were nice but were overshadowed by some of the cheapness of other things, such as the loud fan in the bathroom and the jerry-rigged fridge.
Overall, it was an okay hotel and an okay experience. If you're traveling to Georgetown for leisure (or even business) though, this wouldn't be the place I recommend to experience it all.

title: “Beautiful hotel!”
text: This hotel is amazingly beautiful, and a great deal for the price. They have wonderful room service, and a car to take you to other places near downtown. Would totally stay here again!

title: “Do not waste your money!!”
text: I will never stay there again! I have never had such a horrible hotel experience. First of all we booked with a wedding party and we were supposed to get a special rate, we paid the same rate as on the website. Then our keys didn't work, we went and got new ones and those didn't work either! They said they were sending someone up, 15 minutes later someone finally comes up and moves us to a new room. There is a nasty, kind of moldy stain on the ceiling and no balcony like we were promised on the phone. The room is small, counter was dirty and there were no toiletries. Then we went to bring the car in, there was no one at the valet booth so we decided to park ourselves, the guy yelled at us, told us to go back around and he would park the car. The closest garage door did not open so we turned around and went outthe way we came in. The guy yelled at us again and told us he meant to go out the garage door, he told us to "exit the vehicle" and he would park it. The next morning we planned to go get breakfast because we got an email saying complimentary breakfast for two, it also said on the website that there would be complimentary breakfast for two. The rude guy at the front desk told us that since we were part of the wedding party we did not qualify. My friends getting married brought all the business here and we don't get the perks other people do? We are checking out days early!

title: “Excellent hotel”
text: This is an EXCELLENT hotel. We loved the environment, the people who work at the hotel, and the restaurant We are a very eco-friendly family and we loved this hotel. My husband and I traveled with our two children (6, and 9). We felt right at home. I can't say enough nice things about the people who work there, from the front desk, to the bellman and waitstaff. They were all very friendly and helpful. The rooms were spacious, very clean, and really nice. We loved the food at the restaurant. The food was delicious- it was local, sustainable, natural and fresh. A huge plus for us is that the restaurant was very accomodating with my son's food allergies. He has a gluten and dairy allergy. They took great care of him. My thanks to the Chef and restuarant staff. Another plus, besides the hotel, was that we loved Philly. This city seems like it is making a very concious effort to become more green. Kudos to Philly! We are coming back!!

title: “Great Stay at the Hilton Garden”
text: Very pleased with our three day stay at Hilton Garden. Staff extremely courteous, check-in took less than a minute. Both the room and bathroom were very clean. Room was not huge, just nice size with king bed, work table, sofa chair and ottoman. Room was quiet, only occasionally disturbed by noisy people in hallway and passing fire truck 20 floors down. Location is hard to beat; two blocks from Michigan Ave. Tons of good restaurants within a few blocks, not to mention the Weber Grill in the same building. Only minor complaint would be noisy fridge, but turning the fridge down from max to medium setting took care of the issue. Since I would not rate this hotel as "luxury", I would have hard time paying the $290 flat rate per night. If you can get the room at a discount like I did, it's defintely the top choice. Valet parking a little pricey if you are staying more than two nights, you can save a few bucks with self park.

title: “Clean...trendy....but LOUD. Good for biz traveling, but NO FREE WIFI!!”
text:
Check in was nice and easy.
Clean lobby and friendly staff upon arrival.
I was on the 26th floor. Room was clean and very comfortable.
The only negative (and for me it was a big one) the NOISE! I could hear people talking on the phone through both connecting doors to adjoining rooms. It was so bad I finally went and beat on the door to get them to be quieter after 11pm! THis is why I rated sleep quality low.
Seriously, get higher quality doors to block the noise. It was ridiculous!
Oh and there was no complimentary wi-fi. Come on it's 2011 who doesn't offer comp wi-fi?????

title: “Hip and Midtown coolness”
text: Love the new check in and seemless one person from door to room consistency. Bar in basement serving very well done drinks with taste and artful assembly. I was surprised how quiet it was in the room and how quickly the hustle bustle of NYC melted away in the ultra coolness of the room and super trick bathroom. I enjoyed the property and every one of the staff was helpful and extra friendly. The only thing I didn't like was the bagel served with killer smoked salmon. The "baker truly doesn't like bagels" said hotel staff. Hates them... so an english muffin with a thumb print plays 'bagel'. It just isn't what I expected... but in NYC you can have the best bagels in the world - just not at this hotel. That was my only complaint. The in house smoked salmon was epic and I quickly forgot the brick that it came with so BYOBagel. Boutique service with National chain points was a winner for me.

title: “Great hotel”
text: Great location, modern, clean, friendly staff and great view from the bar

title: “Perfect hotel in San Diego”
text: We stayed here for two nights -- just about everything about this hotel was perfect. The rooms were great, the bathroom is amazing, everything was spotlessly clean, and the staff was amazingly friendly and helpful. They recommended the best taco trucks to get awesome street food from, and were always ready with a smile and small talk. Great location in the Gaslamp Quarter as well -- one block off the main drag, so if you want to be rowdy it's in easy access, but we found the hotel to be perfectly quiet.

title: “Nice but poor breakfast”
text: We love this hotel but were really disappointed with the breakfast offered. They force you to order off a menu at an extra charge if you want anything hot to eat.

title: “What a pleasant unexpected surprise!”
text: Stayed there for a wedding last summer. Was not expecting much. Place was clean, modern, with plenty of conviences. The pool and terrace were very nice. The best surprise was the quality of room service - impeccable! Also, the restaurant on site was much better than the other outside places which were top of the Zagat list. Would stay there again without question.

title: “Great Service”
text: My wife and I love the Crowne Plaza at Union Station. It has a lot of character and is very relaxing. The pool and hot tub are also very relaxing. We highly recommend this hotel. The service is remarkable!

title: “Room was nice but the hotel is LOUD!!”
text:
Stayed one night in Charlotte with my kids and girlfriend. Chose the Embassy because it had enough room and wasn't too bad for redeeming some Hilton Honors points (30K).
It was ok, not great. A terrible nights sleep as will be explained below.
Check in was fast and easy. I got a room on the 6th floor that was spacious and well appointed. The room had a seperate living room along with a pullout couch and a bedroom (2 queens). Each had HD flat screen TV's. It was very clean and spacious. No complaints about the room itself. They offer a free breakfast buffet that was good but there is very limited seating and the lines were very long.
Unfortunately for us the hotel was packed with 10-13 year olds for the night. The indoor pool, not very large, had 30 or so kids already in it when we arrived. Of course they were having fun screaming, splashing, jumping, but it made for a bad experience for my 5 and 6 year old. They also stayed up all hours of the night running around slamming doors. I got very little sleep. In hindsight I should have called the front desk but.. they're kids. What can you do? Ultimately I decided that it was more of a sound insulation issue as EVERY noise from setting up the breakfast buffet could be heard clearly. The sound insulation is terrible. Typical for hotels with a huge atrium in the middle.
All in all I don't think I'd stay here again. It's well appointed but you really can't count on any sleep. I think I got very unlucky with the night I chose.

title: “Labor Day Weekend”
text: Just recently took a trip to the windy city over Labor Day weekend and stayed at the Intercontinental Hotel on Michigan Ave. While the front desk service and the room were mediocre at best (we had to wait in line for over 30 mins, just to be told our room wasn't ready yet), the wait staff was absolutely excellent. I've been to many hotels across the country and internationally and I have NEVER found a doorman as helpful as Will at the Intercontinental. He gave us great suggestions on breakfast, lunch and dinner each day we stayed at the hotel. And, when we had trouble locating our bags upon leaving, I knew who to ask - Will. And, of course he was the man who found them. All in all, the location of the hotel is great and we got a wonderful deal for staying over a holiday weekend, but if i were to rate the hotel without Will, it would have been significantly lower.

title: “One of the best hotels in NYC”
text:
It was our first trip to NYC and because of the excellent feedback from travellers at tripadvisor, we choosed the Distrikt Hotel. The hotel is perfect, because everything you´d like to see in Manhatten is really near. 15 Minutes to Empire and about 10 Minutes to Time-Square. As we got an upgrade to a better room category, our room was on the 30th floor. The room was very clean and the kingsize bed was excellent. As everything is new, we felt very comfortable.
Some wrote, that the street seems to be a little bit rough - but do not care, it is a quite normal street. We never felt unsecure. The staff of the hotel is very friendly and helpful. Every day you can take a free coffee in the lobby. All in all, we will come back!

title: “excellent hotel”
text: We spent 4 nights in this hotel at the start of jan 09 .We were allocated a corner room on the 26th floor with fantastic views of the city.Our room was huge with 2 queen beds and loads of room for myself, husband and two teenage sons.Once we found our bearings the location was excellent close to all major sights.The rooms were spotless and housekeeping were very discreet and unobtrusive.Dont be put off by the small Lobby.The staff were friendly and helpful..This is a great family hotel which I would gladly recommend and stay in again.

title: “Nice place, good value for flying out of San Jose Airport”
text: We booked through parksleepfly.com and got a great deal on our room and 14 nights parking while we were in Kauai. The room was very quiet and comfortable. The shuttle to the airport was great. One downside was that the restaurant was cold and they wouldn't change the air conditioning temperature. The bigger problem was that on our return after our trip, we waited at the airport for a half an hour for the shuttle after we called. If I'd known it was going to take that long I would have taken a taxi. Other than that, the Radisson was great and the San Jose Airport is really nice.

title: “I didn't want to leave”
text: We needed an extra night stay in Boston near Freedom Trail and liked the location. We loved it. Front staff was friendly and helpful. Room amenities are top notch. Shower was gorgeous. Bathroom was immaculate. Bed was comfortable and everything felt new and fresh - no stale smoke smell anywhere. We had to sign a no smoking agreement. Room layout user friendly. Especially loved desk and nightstand lamps which had on/off switch AND two electric outlets on the base to plug in your laptop or cellphone. The room overlooked the lively square so there was some local entertainment noise but that drifted away as the night ended. Great location.

title: “Can't Think of Anything Bad To Say About The Magnolia”
text: I was in Denver for a conference along with my wife. We have friends in town so it was a mixed business/pleasure trip. The Magnolia was just a couple of blocks from the convention center, and literally one block from the 16th St. pedestrian mall, so everything was within walking distance. There is even a major light rail hub a half-block away. The hotel has a lovely decor and the staff were always helpful and courteous. The free hot breakfast, though basic (scrambled eggs, sausage, oatmeal) was a big plus and we utilized it every day. We also enjoyed the cookies and refreshments in the evening, and even drank the bad wine at the evening receptions (what the heck -- it was free!). The bed was super comfortable and the room was just the right size. Nice size bathroom as well. Very nice fitness center, though it was often too warm in there. We opted for the "green" service, in which we had no maid service. This allowed us to get $5.00 off at Harry's (the hotel restaurant/bar). If you opt for this, the hotel will still provide any needed items like towels or toilet paper if you ask for them. I still tipped the maid at the end of our stay, in that the room was immaculate when we arrived. I would definitely return to the Magnolia for either business or pleasure!

title: “My favorite place to stay in Seattle”
text:
I've used the Mediterranean Inn many times for both business and leisure visits to Seattle. It's location on Queen Anne Hill makes it both convenient and out-of-the-way: it's within walking distance of downtown (or a quick bus ride) but quieter and more relaxed than a downtown hotel. The rooms are cozy, comfortable, and quiet with a refrigerator, coffee-maker, and microwave in each. There are plenty of eating options nearby including a Starbucks in the lobby and a grocery store across the street. 
The only warning to give is an extremely tight parking garage if you're driving a car: anything larger than a compact will be difficult to maneuver in the small confines of the underground space.

title: “An Absolute Gem”
text:
My husband and I are in our mid fifties and this was our first visit to New York. We found the Sofitel 44th Street to be everything that we required to make our holiday pleasurable. The location was perfect for the subway, Times Square , Train Station, Broadway , shopping , in fact for all needs. We were fortunate enough to have a Junior Suite and as we stayed for 16 nights this extra room was invaluable. 
The service was great, I had a birthday during the stay and our daughter arranged from Perth through Guest Services for me to receive flowers, champagne & chocolates first thing in the morning.This was followed by complimentary desserts delivered by the hotel to me in the evening. 
Our request for a coffee machine , a kettle and a small fridge were attended to without fuss.
We are fans of Sofitel and once again our trust in the brand was rewarded. If the flight was not so long we would be back!

title: “Fantastic renovated hotel in a great location”
text:
Having spent many hours and days researching accomodation (as I usually do) and reading alot of trip advisor reviews I am glad I took the time and chose the Shelburne. 
We arrived at 1230, not expecting our rooms to be ready (check-in is 3pm) so happily completed all the paperwork, had our bags stored and began exploring the city. It is only a 10-20minute walk to Times Sq/5th Avenue/Central Park.
The hotel has recently had a renovation, with tasteful furnishings throughout and is a pleasure to come home to every night. The rooms are spacious and come with a refrigerator stocked with mini bar items, hair dryer, Aveda bathroom amentities - shampoo/conditioner/moisturiser. No tea/coffee facilities in the room, however I'm sure you could get this from housekeeping. There is a Starbucks within 2 blocks anyway if you need it. The towels were nice thick too.
Our studio room #820 had great views of the Empire State Building. The neighbourhood is quiet for a big city and we had no issue sleeping with the window open and had no worries walking home at night.
Taking the advice of other reviewers we ate at Scotty's for breakfast a few times (336 Lexington, just past 39th Street corner). Great eggs, omelettes & pancakes.etc
Dinner - The hotel bar/restaurant RARE has nice burgers and plenty of drinks. It's a popular bar for locals too so gets busy from 7pm. Groovy atmosphere and well worth some time after a long day of walking.
Fagiolini's (Lexington & 39th) - great little Italian
El Rio Grande (37th Street between Lexington & 3rd) - nice tex mex with a huge choice of fantastic margueritas. They have a bar as well so you can just go for the drinks.
Third Avenue has alot of restaurants and convenience stores.
The hotel had very friendly staff throughout, including the bar staff and April in Concierge. She was knowledgable and assisted us with restaurant recommendations with great results. I would most definitely stay again and would not hesitate to recommend it to friends. The location was perfect with all the necessary shopping close by. If I could say one small thing that might let it down, is the "My Affinia" pitch. Having read several unfavourable comments about this part of the service on Trip Advisor I was prepared. We asked for a memory pillow and never saw it. It wasn't a priority so didn't bother chasing it up, and no explanation was provided by the hotel. There is a shortage of the walking kits as well, so perhaps tune up your own ipod. (This in no way made our stay a negative one though). We also used the hotel SUV car service (4 people) to JFK which was efficient and very comfortable and only $10 more than a yellow cab. Thanks for a memorable time in NYC. You will be happy you stayed here too.

title: “The Perfect Place to Stay ...................”
text: I live in Northern Arizona & make a point staying at this Hampton when ever I'm flying. A 24/7 shuttle service to & from Phoenix Sky Harbor. Very short drive from door to door. As far as I'm concerned this is an ideal location for anyone flying to or from a destination. Excellent for the 1st time visitor to our state. Have that hot breakfast before starting the day .... In my particular case this past weekend, I had an 8:30 am appointment at Arizona Heart for my annual checkup. Had my early wake up call, breakfast. It was roughly a 12 minute drive from the hotel to AZ Heart this past Monday morning. Also, I'd like to mention, I 've met Rachel several times and not only is she a delightful lady, she is very helpful.

title: “Affinia Chicago March 2012”
text: Stayed here for two nights in March (24, 25). Had a room on the 17th floor. Really enjoyed my stay at this smaller, boutique type establishment. The hotel staff were very accomodating and things ran smoothly from check in to check out. The location cannot be beat if you are interested in shopping or seeing some of the sights on Michigan Avenue. It is around the corner from all the most exclusive shops and right next to a popular pizza parlour called Ginos (didn't eat there but there were some long lines waiting to get in). The hotel is clean and up to date. I had breakfast in the restaurant attached and wouldn't recommend. Service was slow and the food was not a good value. There is a delightful rooftop bar but beware, it was closed the majority of the time I was at the hotel and seems to only be open Thur-Sunday. There is a great open roof top area but it's only accessible when the bar is open. I was disappointed that guests could not take advantage of this great area to chill out and relax. The only other common area is the small lobby so having this space would have been a plus (especially in light of the beautiful weather Chicago was having). If not for this, the hotel would have rated excellent in my opinion.

title: “4 day visit”
text:
Great experience, nice big room, quiet, slept great. The manager was very helpful with directions to get around. Great value for the money, a little inconvient for food but worth the trouble.
Will be staying again next week. Thanks to manager for all the help.

title: “A great place to get away, conference, and /or do the family vacay.”
text: The property is huge, serene, divided good, and has an amazing offering of amenities. I stayed for a several day escape and decompression and glad I came to the right place. It is ridiculously easy to get off property and visit mission beach, the gas lamp, old town or wherever. Sea World is a walk away. I had a snafu with a room and the staff handled it amazingly well. Sometimes fitness. Enters seem to be haphazard and run down, this one is sorta "mama bear" and just right. Outdoor heated pool, multiple pools, paddle boards, bikes, boats, great beach, just super nice stay.

title: “Fabulous!”
text: I stay frequently at the Affinia in Chicago. It is one of my favorites because the rooms are so large and the staff so attentive (without being stuffy). I had a chance to stay in Manhattan for one night of pleasure and choose the Affinia (by way of American Express travel). I was told it has recently gone through a redesign. I love a trendy looking room and this hotel does not disappoint. Very chic, spacious and so comfortable. The front desk staff was delightful and the check in was hassle free. For a New York hotel room, I was surprised how quiet things were. The modern design of the hotel and the room made for a really enjoyable stay that I wish I could have prolonged. Highly recommended.

title: “Park Hyatt Chicago is the tip-top”
text:
This review is a little late but now that I'm planning another trip I'm remembering just how great my stay at the Park Hyatt Chicago was. My boyfriend and I went to Chicago for a weekend get-a-away. I did quite a bit of research as to where to stay and made multiple reservations - The Peninsula, W. However, all reviews of the Park Hyatt were positive and from the photos on their Web site, it looked spectacular.
Everything went well on the trip. From the moment we arrived at the hotel, the staff was the epitome of professionalism. Our room was ready at 12:30 pm and our check-in was swift. The room met all expectations - it was roomy, on an upper-floor, with a stunning view of Water Tower Place and Lake Michigan. The best part of the room was the bathroom - spectacular. The soaking tub with the sliding doors providing a view to the city was heaven, especially at night. 
The facilities (gym, pool and whirlpool) were great. We lucked out because most of the time we were there, nobody was using them, so it felt like our own private gym and pool. 
We didn't eat at the restaurant, Nomi, but it looked lovely and it was crowed. We did have drinks and light fare one night at the lounge and it was great. The food was delicious and the atmosphere delightful. 
As for the location, you can't beat it. You are literally at the center of everything. 
I went to see the The Peninsula next door. I chose the Park Hyatt because it was cheaper. From what I saw, it was not worth the extra money and I was glad that I chose the Park Hyatt. 
All in all, the hotel is tip-top. I highly recommend it and will be returning.

title: “Pampered!”
text:
I spent over 2 weeks at the Palace on a corporate trip, and my lucky boyfriend tagged along. I checked in at 8am and tried to wrangle an upgrade to the Towers, but wasn't successful unfortunately! I did ask for a room on a higher floor and got one on the 13th floor which gave me a magnificent overview of the cathedral, away from the traffic noise below. I later found out that my colleagues ended up in rooms on the 3rd floor, ha!
My boyfriend tasted almost every item on the room service menu and he can attest to the great food served. Service is impeccable as you would expect from a luxury hotel - security was tight as well, and you need to show your room key to gain access to the lifts. 
The gym is spectacular for a hotel gym, very large, new and clean - and it is never full up so you don't have to wait for equipment. 
The clientele at this hotel is quite mature, and everybody was always dressed well. On my weekends off, it being in the midst of a sticky NY summer, I felt very out of place in my denim shorts and flipflops! But the service I received was the same thank goodness.
The Palace is in a brilliant location, about 3 blocks away from Fifth Avenue, and 1 block away from the subway. And if you're there for business, it's 4-5 blocks away from Park Avenue. Walking to Times Square took me about 15 minutes.
So if you want to pamper yourself but don't want to overly splurge on your accommodation, the Palace is the way to go! There's also a gourmet, top class, internationally recognised restaurant in the hotel - Le Cirque, which I unfortunately didn't get to try, but I have read great reviews of the food.

title: “Nice staff”
text: We booked another hotel in San Jose but when we got there we were afraid to stay here so we called up the Fairfield Inn by the airport. They were nice enough to give us a nice room right away. Since they did not have a room with two beds, the staff sent us a roll away bed for our daughter. The bed was already in our room by the time we got there.

title: “Top Notch J.W. Marriott - Don't know why we waited so long to visit!”
text:
This place is First Class all the way! From the moment we got there to the moment we departed. You never really have to leave the J.W. since they pretty much have everything on the property, from great dining choices, spa. golf and just a really fun pool, especially for kids. Although it was 100+ degrees outside, it was a really nice visit @ Desert Ridge. 
I would suggest that you valet your car, I can't imagine walking from the parking lot in this heat and it is quite a distance. The room was spacious, including the bathroom. We had a great view of the driving range and this huge pond. It was quiet and we were able to enjoy the sunrise and sunset. This resort is huge, but easy to navigate it through, by using the lobby as your middle point. It is pretty spectacular and well worth the price. 
Service is OUTSTANDING! We arrived after midnight and the valet was still working and got our luggage really quickly and it was brought to our room promptly after check-in. When we departed, we were able to take care of check-out, retrieval of our car and having them get our luggage. We are already planning our next visit!

title: “Elegant hotel”
text: I'm surprised by some of the negative comments. This was our first stay at the Pierre, and it was really an excellent experience. All staff we came in contact with were professional and courteous (check-in desk attendant escorted us to our suite, which was upgraded a notch through AMEX Platinum - elegant, spacious accomodations). Reservations are suggested for the bar off the lobby during the work week - it is difficult to get a table on the spur of the moment after 5. Location can't be beat. I'd definitely stay there on our next trip up. Pricey, yes, but a value. Didn't dine at the restaurant as our dinner plans were already set.

title: “Best of the Best”
text: Celebrated my 44 wedding anniversary by selecting the weekend speacility package. The price was extremely reasonable, the ambiance left little to be desired and the service was impecable. We ate two meals in their dineing room the meals merrited their rateing. I highly recommend this hotel especially if you can obtain their weekend package.

title: “Would stay here again!”
text: We booked The Westin Copley Place through the Starwood website; they had some great promotions - better rates than expedia, orbitz, etc. We lived in Boston for 5 years and went to visit friends. We booked the Westin at Copley because we knew it was located within walking distance to many of Boston's great restaurants and shops. Our room had a view of the Charle's River. The bed was VERY comfortable and the room was clean. We ate breakfast at the hotel one morning. It wasn't anything spectacular but it wasn't bad either. The staff was friendly and polite. We will probably stay here again when we visit Boston.

title: “Chic”
text:
Gorgeous design, love the bar, sexy reception area. Looks like they have the most romantic patio outside but not we were there is Dec so it was not for use. 
Rooms are toooooooo small, never seen a room the same width of a bed and that is not an exaggeration. Perfect for a bus traveler or couples in their honeymoon. Forget about spending time in room or ordering room service as the rooms are too small for that but in NY you want to get out and experience the city anyway. Also when there is a gorgeous bar downstairs why would you want to stay in your room.

title: “Good stay - but avoid Rm 912”
text:
We chose to stay at the Bellclaire with our 3 year son as we were looking for a hotel on the upper west side close to Central Park and the Natural History Museum. Overall, it’s a very nice hotel, with clean, good size rooms with great hardwood floors. The beds are also very comfortable. Staff were friendly as well and the neighbourhood was appropriate for travelling with our 3 year old – more residential and less hectic than the mid-town area. We recommend the Bellclaire, but please stay away from room 912. On check-in we were given this room, which at first seemed fine until the night when there was this horrible hissing and clanking noise coming from this peculiar vent (pipe) in the bathroom. There was noise also from the street however that did not bother me since this is New York City after all. My husband went down to the front desk to enquire about a room change and was told that because the Bellclaire is an older hotel, all of the rooms had this problem and they could not guarantee that if we changed rooms the noise would be any better. I decided it was worth the risk to stay in another room and we moved to room 511 the next day where I immediate check the bathroom to see if it had another one of those peculiar pipes. No pipe – no noise, and I had two very comfortable nights of sleep. So, stay at the Bellclaire if you are looking for a reasonable place in the upper west side, but avoid room 912 at all cost! 
Other tips – the hotel is also close to the subway (the 1 Train (local) on 79 street and the 1,2,&3 trains (express) on 72 street. There were also good choices for eating. We enjoyed Big Nicks Burger Joint just around the corner and had a lovely Italian meal at a bistro two blocks up on 79th between Broadway and Amsterdam – sorry can’t remember the name, but the fresh pasta special was delicious!

title: “So quiet-- excellent value and location”
text:
We have stayed in a variety of NYC venues over the years, including living here some time back, and this is one we would return to. We were on the 25th floor and the views are outstanding. We were pleasantly surprised by the utter soundproofing-- for a city that never sleeps it certainly sounded like it was asleep.
The Fairway across the street opens at 6 am with great fresh bakery items and fresh fruit (and everything else you need for groceries from olive oil to cereal to dried fruit and pasta).
The subway is a stone's throw from the hotel door complete with a gelato stand by the subway entrance.
An excellent healthful restaurant, Josie's, is right around the corner.
Central Park is a very short walk as are plenty of other restaurant choices and shops.
The room was clean and exceedingly comfortable. The tiny kitchenette was just perfect for storing basic breakfast items without taking up a lot of room and the decor was upscale, clean-- not stark-- a very pleasant place to put our feet after walking and look out on the city.
Very minor annoyances:
They charge for Wifi.
Guest concierge was rarely at the desk.
No parking-- we parked two blocks away in a garage for $35.
Some of the rooms are still owner occupied. So we found smoking on a non-smoking floor, but even with our sensitivity to smoke smell, we were not at all bothered once in our room.

title: “99% Perfect... Except for one Concierge...”
text:
My partner treated my to a once in a lifetime trip to New York, with all the bells and whistles (Limo from the airport, 5 Star Plaza etc). I have to say that the trip was an absolute joy. The Plaza Hotel was by far the best hotel I've ever had the pleasure of staying in. It was expensive but entirely worth it. 
1) Arriving
Our car was greeted by a friendly doorman who directed us to the front desk and arranged for a bell boy to deal with our luggage. When we arrived at the front desk, we were thrilled to be informed that we had complimentary use of the Rolls Royce Ghost (we used this once and it was an absolute pleasure). We felt we were getting a real 5 star personalised service. We were also offered a selection of complimentary newspapers each day. We were warned in advance of our holiday that we should tip tip tip, almost regardless of the service, but I will come to that shortly. The bell boy took us to our room with our luggage and we tipped him and he went on his way.
2) A short note on tipping
I must say that within the hotel (except for one Concierge whom I shall discuss later), tipping was necessary, however not "expected". We didn't experience any members of staff hanging around waiting for a tip which was nice (and what I was expecting). We tipped $5.00 a day to housekeeping (left in an envelope somewhere they will see it with Housekeeping written on the envelope), $5.00 to the bell boy and 15-20% to waiters for room service and a final $50.00 to the concierge on the last day.
3) The Room
Un-be-lievable! We stayed in a deluxe room with an enormous bathroom with top to bottom mosaic tiles and gold fittings. There was a walk in wet room waterfall shower, a separate toilet and a bath big enough for both of us (we are not small!) There was also a marble vanity with a small sink. Very opulent and beautiful. Each of the rooms had its own gorgeous chandelier.
The bedroom had a Super-Kingsize bed with clean crisp white cotton linens and a faux fur runner across the bottom. It was quite literally the most comfortable bed I've ever slept in. I've had a bad back for three months and sleeping has not been easy, but I slept well every night of our holiday.
There was also two very comfortable armchairs and a footrest, a writing table and a huge armoire with the mini-bar inside. I'll admit we didn't touch the mini-bar as it was very expensive, but understandably so, this is after all a 5 star hotel. Across one wall was a large wardrobe which had ample storage space for a long holiday (we were only there 5 nights). Located in one of the drawers was a large safe and on the last night we noticed that it had two power sockets inside for charging small electricals. The view overlooked a Manhattan street and the large windows let in a lot of light.
The room had a 42 inch flat screen television with over 30 channels for relaxing in the evening, and, most impressively, an iPad which could be used to precisely control the lights and heat and was also connected to the hotel's wireless internet for checking emails and Facebook. There were also the obligatory white Plaza robes ($150.00 to buy) and slippers.
4) Housekeeping
Housekeeping came to service the room twice per day. The evening housekeeper left a helpful weather information card on the bed each evening as well as turning down the bed and leaving a bottle of water on our bedside tables. The room was always immaculate.
5) Room-Service and a Nice Surprise
In all honesty, room-service was a very nice, but expensive treat. We found that the only place to get a decent cup of tea was in the hotel, and so we ordered room service most days at a cost of $10.00/pot plus tip. Prior to travelling, I arranged a room service breakfast for my partner as it was her birthday and ordered flowers from a NY florist which were delivered to the concierge. I must say that it was exquisite! Freshly baked parties and muffins, tea and coffee and orange juice, plus the flowers were in a vase on the table (see photos below). We also splurged on an in-room evening meal - it was absolutely delicious. The room-service was very prompt and easy to order. The nice surprise? Well, as we were checking out, we noticed that a $100.00 food and drink credit had been added to our bill! We were not expecting it, but it would appear that it was part of the package.
6) Concierge
There were two concierge's who served us during our trip. One concierge named John Powell was very happy to help, treated us like friends and made us feel like we were supposed to be there. We are not wealthy or monied. He arranged my partner's birthday breakfast for me and was incredibly helpful, taking time to come over and greet us when we walked past the desk and chatting to us.
Sadly, the other concierge whom I shall not name, made us feel incredibly awkward. When dealing with him, I felt as though he just wanted to get me off the phone and wasn't interested in helping me. When he did arrange things for us (such as a trip to the 9/11 memorial), it was with a curt attitude and no smile. I felt that he knew that we were not wealthy and so were not worth his time. This is the only negative aspect of the whole trip and although it didn't mar the experience too much, it was a real shame that on those occasions when we dealt with him, we were made to feel as though we shouldn't be in the hotel.
7) Location
The location of the hotel, within 2 minutes walk of Tiffany's and all that 5th Avenue has to offer was ideal. A 7 day Metro pass for the Subway and we good to go. Late at night Taxis are the best way to travel and the cost from Times Square to the Plaza is around $11.00. One night we decided to take advantage of the Rolls Royce Ghost which was a lovely car with a very nice driver. It is available to take you anywhere within 10 blocks (as far as the Radio City Music Hall but not all the way to Times Square).
8) Checking Out
We had a wonderful time in New York and took in all the sights and sounds. Leaving the hotel was hard (there were tears!) We called down and a bell boy took our luggage downstairs for us. Checking out was easy, and we were able to leave our luggage in the luggage room as our flight wasn't until the evening. We took the opportunity to have a cocktail in the champagne bar before our car arrived which was lovely.
I would most definitely stay there again, it was in short, the best hotel stay I have ever experienced. With regards to our ratings - the Service was sadly let down by that one concierge which is why I have awarded a "very good" rather than an "excellent".

title: “A bit disappointed”
text:
We selected Hotel Palomar because we had great experience with our other Kimpton Hotel stay.
My one complaint and disappointment has to be the bed. Having spent a long day flying in, we look forward to a comfortable bed for some much needed snooze. When I pulled back the sheets, I was shocked and appalled to see the mattress through the sheets (very thin) - like a motel bed. The mattress pad was strapped on but it was much too small for the king size bad. Honestly, it was also paper thin. As brought up by one of the reviews, I had expected more. If not a pillow top (which is what I would expect given this is considered a luxury boutique hotel), at least a pad that covers up the mattress. Even more disconcerting was that when house keeping (very cordial and helpful - bless their hearts) came to help remedy the situation, they could not locate a pad that would fit a king size bed. 
What made it all ok was that the two house keeping staff were very accommodating with my request to pad the mattress with several sheets, which by the way helped to create a nice comfortable padding. I just felt bad that they had to remake my bed at midnight.
Where's management in all of this. If this had been an earlier complaint, shouldn't management have already addressed this deficiency?
Bottom line, it is unacceptable that a hotel of this caliber is lacking in something so fundamental as the comfort of its beds.

title: “Pleasantly Suprised.........”
text:
I was hesitant to stay here because I am so spoiled I try to stay at the number one or two hotels whenever I travel. I couldn't find a lot of information on this hotel and knew it was pretty new and that it cost me very little points to stay there for a few days so I took the chance.
We had been traveling for much of the day hitting every kind of traffic. This trip was to drop my daughter at school and being miles and miles from home I arrived in Baltimore very sad. 
The hotel is on a narrow street that is not well lit. This worried me right away. I also noticed that the parking was limited to the sides of the street or valet parking was available at $25 per day. 
We entered the building and from the entrance to the desk we were greeted with smiling happy faces wishing us good will etc. Forgive me but I forget the woman helping us that first night. That would be Wednesday, 8/24/11. I think her name might have been Joyce. She was the sweetest, most helpful, friendly, talkative person. She was the reason I started to relax.
The rooms are all suites. They are newer with newer fixtures, dishes and all. Very nice value. The bed was comfortable but the first night we didn't have all of the sheets for the fold out bed. My daughter didn't care and was so tired she slept before we could call anyone. The only other not nice thing was how my husband had to run around for ice. He went to all applicable floors and was finally helped by the desk on the first floor. We were on the 8th or 10th. I can't exactly remember. 
The valet was so helpful on our day out he guided us to the highway. He was another helpful, nice person. 
I would recommend this hotel to any traveler but especially to those needing to stay for a while due to work.

title: “Don't stay here if you are afraid of the dark”
text:
I remember reading a review left by another member before my stay at this hotel, they said they felt like bats and now I can see why. This hotel is really dark, in the lobby, in the lifts, on the corridors, in the rooms, the bathrooms. If the hotel wants to create the dark, moody, contempory feel in the public areas then that's fine by me, but let me create my own atmosphere in the bedroom so I can see where my things are and I can put on my make up without looking like Aunt Sally!!!
We stayed in a penthouse suite and I have to say this is one of the most disappointing suites I have ever stayed in. The colour scheme was grey, dark grey and beige. No pictures on the wall, bland furniture, no curtains on the patio door in the living area. No handles on the sliding doors both from the bedroom to the living room or into the toilet.
The style of the bathroom resembled a mortuary, too much stainless steel, chrome and grey slate tiles both on the walls and floor. I can only imagine this room was designed by a man as there wasn't any dressing table area or mirror in the bedroom. Bearing in mind this was a penthouse we were missing slippers, we had one robe, there wasn't any complimentary fruit or water, no turn down service. 
A word of warning to anyone staying in a room with a fireplace....whatever you do don't ask for the fire to be lit. We made this mistake and throughout our entire stay our room and all our clothes smelt of smoke. 
On a positive note the hotel is in a good location but I'm afraid that really is all I can say that's good about it.

title: “lovely place”
text: We celebrated our 15th Anniversary - the hotel totally lived up to our expectations. We had a beautiful suite,the staff was more than gracious and when they heard it was our anniversary, they delivered a beautiful rose to our room. The room was beautifully decorated, i believe it is a historic hotel. It was recently renovated and we loved it. Loved the complimentary contienntal breakfast - muffins to die for. The Wales plus an evening at Jersey Boys made for a great get away weekend.

title: “Pedacito de Cielo!”
text:
My husband and I are from Ecuador, 
And we spent our anniversary in NY. We couldn't have chosen a more wonderful place for our stay. 
We practically didn't leave the hotel... spent hours reading in this cozy little library, where you could enjoy cappuccinos, muffins and scones all day long, while listening to soothing, great chosen music. We never missed their Wines and Cheese afternoons. 
Our room was located at the 11th floor. It was very quiet, tastefully decorated and incredibly comfortable. I loved the amenities! 
If I ever go back to NY I wouldn't doubt about my hotel's choice... although I hope next time I will dare leave the place and actually SEE the city! Yogini was very kind and efficient at taking care of our reservation.

title: “I would really recommend this hotel to anyone wanting to stay in central Boston”
text:
I did a lot of research/shopping around before booking this hotel and was a bit nervous as it didn't rate very highly on trip advisor however we absolutely loved it. Location is so central and less than 5 mins walk with luggage to the T station. Our room was gorgeous - had only paid for a standard room but ours was so good I think we may have been upgraded? It had a balcony/dressing room and great modern decor. 
We paid the advance purchase rate which made the hotel good value compared to other central hotels in Boston.
Staff all very friendly. Lobby slightly lacking in atmosphere but that wasn't at all important to us.

title: “I will always stay at this hotel”
text: as long as I remember to make my reservations way in advance. Everything was wonderful and the days I spent there were the best days of my trip.

title: “I love the location”
text: Before naming a price to bid a six-day stay in Philly, my bf and I were looking for a reasonable price with a comfortable room. Then, we planned to travel back and forth during our visit in Philly and fortunately we got a rather cheap price ($40/day) to stay in the hotel. Originally, I checked the review first on tripadvisor.com and we were horrified by the review. Nevertheless, after we arrived at the hotel at around 1am, we tried to reach the desk but no one was around. Therefore, we didn't enter our room till 30 minutes later--obviously the night shifter went to take a shower and our call was finally picked up. The room was not that dirty and the bed was satisfactory (if you don't use a five-star standard to examine it, it's worth the price paid.) So, my advice is that if you don't want to wait, go there between 7am and 11pm and you will be taken care of without too much hassle. Also, wireless internet is provided with a price of 4.99 per stay (that meant we only paid 4.99 for our six-day stay). So, 55 (40+tax and some fees) dollars a day are not that bad with the quality we got anyway.

title: “Nice place. Spot on location.”
text: The Jewel is great value. Not the best price around, but a great location, and nice rooms.
